DARS-NIC-00574-V2H1F.summary: Southampton City Council's agreement covers pseudonymised hospital data, including inpatient, outpatient, A&E and critical care records, for its public health work. The data is for analysing local health needs, inequalities and service demand, supporting needs assessments, health strategies and advice to NHS commissioners. The data have already informed drug and alcohol needs assessments, falls analysis, and neighbourhood health profiles used by clinicians to set priorities.

DARS-NIC-00656-V0Z4C.summary: University College London (UCL)'s agreement covers the use of hospital records (accident and emergency, admitted patient care, critical care and outpatients) together with national mortality data. The agreement allows study of how young people with long-term conditions fare when they move from children's to adult health services, looking at service use and missed appointments. The data is for informing Department of Health policy on transition and helping develop measures of good transition care.

DARS-NIC-00747-G8G0Z.summary: Cheshire East Council's public health team's agreement covers hospital and emergency care records (Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set) for meeting its public health duties. The agreement allows the data to be used to produce needs assessments, strategies and advice for NHS commissioners, helping the council find and respond to local health challenges, especially for disadvantaged groups. The council reports that the data informed its Crewe needs assessment, published in August 2023.

DARS-NIC-01189-Y2V3W.summary: Imperial College London's agreement covers the use of Office for National Statistics (ONS) birth data, specifically birth weight, for medical research. The data is to be linked with information already collected in the DELBYA study of young adults, which included lung function, height, weight, pulse, blood pressure and health questionnaires. The aim is to help explain differences in lung function between participants of different ethnic groups.

DARS-NIC-01207-V9G9P.summary: Compufile Systems Limited's agreement covers the use of pseudonymised hospital records (Hospital Episode Statistics for admitted patient care, critical care and outpatients) to provide analysis to NHS organisations and NHS suppliers, partly through its ESPRiT tool. The agreement allows analysis covering care pathways, benchmarking and service evaluation, aiming to help clients improve services and patient outcomes. Reported results include regular heart attack benchmarking for NHS RightCare, and a London workshop that led an NHS organisation to improve communication with GP practices about discharge coding.

DARS-NIC-02077-R7M9C.summary: Imperial College London's agreement covers the use of NHS registration data and cause of death reports for medical research. It allows follow-up of 54 people with COPD (chronic obstructive pulmonary disease) who had CT scans in 2003/2004, to see whether emphysema, bronchiectasis, airway inflammation, lung function decline and flare-ups predict death. The aim is to help doctors estimate life expectancy and guide treatment.

DARS-NIC-02292-T4P9N.summary: Herefordshire Council's public health team's agreement covers the use of pseudonymised hospital data, covering admissions, outpatient, accident and emergency, critical care and emergency care records. The data is for its public health duties, including needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, commissioning and advice to NHS commissioners. The aim is locally focused analysis of health outcomes and inequalities. The council reports that admissions data has already identified hotspots for targeted action, such as falls and cardiovascular disease.

DARS-NIC-02544-M7M7G.summary: The University of Birmingham's agreement allows it to use hospital records for accident and emergency, admitted patient care and critical care to carry out health services research. This covers hospital use and outcomes in the West Midlands, including maternity and child health, and the link between weekend specialist staffing and hospital deaths. The aim is to improve care and inform service planning. Published papers and a local emergency care report have already been used in discussions and decisions.

DARS-NIC-03075-X3M3H.summary: Somerset Council, a local authority, may use hospital and emergency care data (Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set) for its public health work. The agreement allows analysis of local health needs and inequalities to support needs assessments, commissioning and advice to NHS commissioners. Past uses include informing the council's response to violent crime and COVID, and a Director of Public Health report on COVID's impact on other conditions.

DARS-NIC-03398-N1D2C.summary: King's College London's agreement covers the use of pseudonymised hospital records covering accident and emergency, admitted patient care and outpatients. The data is for studying how air and noise pollution near airports, especially Heathrow, affect local people's health, so that airport policy and NHS planning can be better informed. A newspaper article reported that during a 2012 trial flight ban at Heathrow, spending on prescriptions for conditions such as insomnia and depression fell by 5.8% in the no-fly zones.

DARS-NIC-03422-Y7Y0Z.summary: University College London (UCL), through the Cancer Research UK and UCL Cancer Trials Centre, has an agreement covering mortality data (date and cause of death) for patients in the GALA-5 pilot trial who have been lost to follow-up. The agreement allows the data to be used to calculate survival in a trial testing 5-ALA and carmustine (Gliadel) wafers alongside standard glioblastoma treatment. The results are expected to guide a future phase III trial and inform a review of NICE guidance.

DARS-NIC-03429-L9Y1D.summary: Wirral Borough Council's agreement covers pseudonymised hospital and emergency care records (Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set) to support its public health duties. The agreement allows the data to be used to plan and assess local services, produce needs assessments and strategies, and advise NHS commissioners, with the aim of identifying and addressing local health inequalities. The data is for evaluating a local alcohol-sales scheme, informing drug and alcohol commissioning, and supporting NHS pathway redesign.

DARS-NIC-03452-G8Z1V.summary: The University of York's Centre for Health Economics agreement covers individual-level hospital records (including accident and emergency, admitted patient care, outpatient and critical care), mental health data and patient-reported outcome measures. The agreement allows analysis of the efficiency, productivity and performance of NHS providers and the impact of health policy. Only aggregated results will be published. The main intended benefit is evidence to inform Department of Health policy, resource allocation and NHS decision-making.

DARS-NIC-03519-X1P5B.summary: Northumberland County Council's agreement covers hospital records for admitted patients, outpatients, critical care and accident and emergency (Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set). The data is for its public health duties, such as needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, commissioning and advice to NHS commissioners. The aim is locally focused analysis of health and health inequalities. Reported results include detailed needs assessments, ward and primary care network profiles, and support for a falls pilot scheme.

DARS-NIC-03706-B8L8J.summary: The University of Cambridge's agreement covers hospital records from England covering A&E, critical care, inpatient and outpatient care, linked to maternity and birth information for women who have given birth. It allows study of whether women who had gestational hypertension or pre-eclampsia are more likely to develop cardiovascular disease later in life, including whether risk rises with more affected pregnancies. The work is expected to improve understanding of cardiovascular risk after gestational hypertension, with results published in open-access journals.

DARS-NIC-03716-R3W8Q.summary: The University of Exeter's agreement covers the use of Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care data, giving admission counts for cardiovascular disease, diabetes and obesity by small area, age band and gender. The agreement allows analysis of whether rural location and area deprivation affect hospital admissions for these conditions, alone or combined. The data is for helping clinicians and policymakers plan services for local needs. To date, the data has been used to validate the university's small-area model of comorbidity, which matched the observed pattern of admissions.

DARS-NIC-04641-R3Y5V.summary: The University of Leeds's agreement covers Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) reports on cause of death, cohort event notification and current status. The data is for long-term safety follow-up in the CE-MARC 2 trial, which compares two heart imaging strategies (CMR and SPECT) with NICE guideline-based care for patients with suspected stable angina. The main intended benefit is fewer unnecessary invasive angiograms, which could also save the NHS money.

DARS-NIC-05206-L1V6D.summary: NHS Midlands and Lancashire Commissioning Support Unit's agreement covers pseudonymised hospital, mental health, emergency care, diagnostic imaging, death registration and patient-reported outcome data. The data is for benchmarking services, modelling activity and supporting planning and commissioning for NHS and partner organisations, aiming to improve decisions about care. Reported results include a national report, "Making the Case for Integrating Mental and Physical Health Care", for NHS England, and work that informed responses to the 2021 spending review.

DARS-NIC-05429-H7X6R.summary: Device Access UK Ltd, a commercial company, is permitted to use Hospital Episode Statistics (HES) and Emergency Care Data Set records to produce bespoke, aggregated analysis of NHS patient pathways for medical technology companies and NHS organisations. The agreement allows this analysis to support their submissions to the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE), helping new devices be assessed and adopted by the NHS. Its analysis has been used in NICE applications that resulted in positive NICE guidance in 2022-2023.

DARS-NIC-05934-M7V9K.summary: Harvey Walsh Ltd, a commercial health data analysis company, is permitted to hold pseudonymised hospital, emergency care, diagnostic imaging, mortality, medicines and COVID-19 data from NHS England. The agreement allows the data to be used to give NHS bodies, universities, charities and life science companies services such as benchmarking, service evaluation and health economics studies. The aim is to help clients improve patient care and services. Reported results include published studies, conference presentations and a dashboard used to train clinicians.

DARS-NIC-06303-H3G5G.summary: The London Borough of Southwark's agreement covers hospital and emergency care data on admitted patients, outpatients, critical care and A&E. The agreement allows the data to be used for its public health duties, including needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, and advice to NHS commissioners. The data is for locally focused analyses of health and inequalities. Analysis of smoking and substance misuse admissions by ward, and of winter pressures, has already been carried out.

DARS-NIC-06381-N2B8J.summary: The University of Hertfordshire's agreement allows it to use pseudonymised Hospital Episode Statistics covering accident and emergency, admitted patient care, critical care and outpatients. The data is for building simulation tools that help NHS Trusts test changes to care pathways, such as for COPD, and assess their costs and effectiveness. The aim is faster, better-evidenced service planning. At Leicester Royal Infirmary, the cataract model led to approved changes and more surgeries each month.

DARS-NIC-06527-J1Q6T.summary: University College London (UCL)'s agreement covers linked hospital records and death registration data for England. It allows four studies on healthy life expectancy, meaning how long people live without significant ill health, and how this varies by factors such as deprivation, ethnicity and sex. The data is for giving policy makers and service commissioners evidence to address disparities. So far, UCL has reported published analysis tools, public training on using the data, and a research paper under resubmission to a journal.

DARS-NIC-06587-S1Q6N.summary: Wiltshire Council's agreement covers the use of pseudonymised hospital data covering admissions, outpatient, accident and emergency, and critical care records. The data is for its public health duties, including needs assessments, health strategies, commissioning and advice to NHS commissioners. The main intended benefit is locally focused analysis of health outcomes and inequalities. The data was used for the 2022 Joint Strategic Needs Assessment and analyses of alcohol-related and falls admissions.

DARS-NIC-06605-X1L9Z.summary: University Hospitals Birmingham NHS Foundation Trust's agreement allows it to use national hospital, emergency care and death registration data to run an online benchmarking platform and produce bespoke reports for NHS organisations. These help them monitor clinical quality, patient safety and efficiency, so they can improve services for patients. Reported results include one trust moving from special measures to a "Good" Care Quality Commission rating, and a new one-stop orthopaedic outpatient service.

DARS-NIC-06759-X5V7P.summary: The University of York's agreement allows it to use linked NHS England hospital, emergency care, cancer registration, death and demographic records for a matched comparison group of people without blood cancers. It compares their healthcare use, survival and other health conditions with those of patients with blood cancers in the Yorkshire and Humber region. The data is for improving understanding of blood cancers and informing care and policy. Published papers so far include one on rheumatological disorders and lymphoma.

DARS-NIC-07093-K5N3D.summary: Buckinghamshire Council's agreement covers hospital records for emergency care, admitted patients, critical care and outpatients. The data is for its public health work, including needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, the annual public health report and advice to NHS commissioners. The aim is locally focused analysis of health and health inequalities. The agreement allows the data to be used to build analysis tools and to produce the annual public health report, needs assessments and local area profiles.

DARS-NIC-07141-L2S0B.summary: Northern Care Alliance NHS Foundation Trust, through its hosted quality improvement body AQuA, is permitted to use hospital admissions data (Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care). The agreement allows the data to be used to analyse and benchmark hospital quality and safety, including mortality and re-admissions, for its member organisations. The aim is to reduce mortality and improve patient safety. Reported results include lower SHMI values at all six trusts given an in-depth mortality review, and a 2017 Greater Manchester stroke pathway review.

DARS-NIC-07173-T8S5M.summary: RAND Europe's agreement covers use of hospital records for accident and emergency, admitted patient care and outpatient care (Hospital Episode Statistics). The data is for two evaluations commissioned by NHS organisations: Southwark and Lambeth's Integrated Care programme for older people, and a study of telephone triage in GP practices. The aim is to measure the programmes' effect on hospital use and cost, helping providers and policy makers decide whether to adopt or expand these approaches.

DARS-NIC-07205-H2D1K.summary: Barts Health NHS Trust's agreement covers a Cause of Death Report from the Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) for 1019 women recorded as deceased by the Central and East London breast screening programme. The agreement allows the trust to audit women who were wrongly removed from screening, to check whether they have died, whether from breast cancer, or are still alive. The main intended benefit is offering screening to any women found to be alive and outside the programme.

DARS-NIC-07233-W1M2Q.summary: Neil Wilson Associates LLP, a consultancy, may use Hospital Episode Statistics admitted patient care and critical care data in its Financial Benchmarking System. The data is for NHS organisations to compare their costs and activity with national or similar-organisation averages and to plan service and financial changes. The intended benefit is more efficient, better-quality care. One CCG negotiated an invoice reduction of over £1 million with its local acute trust after using this evidence.

DARS-NIC-07289-G8J6C.summary: The Healthcare Quality Improvement Partnership (HQIP)'s agreement covers hospital admission, death registration and patient reported outcome data for the National Joint Registry, which tracks the results of joint replacement surgery. The agreement allows the data to be used to monitor outcomes by implant, hospital and surgeon, and to give early warning of patient safety issues. Reported benefits include outcomes data that led the MHRA to withdraw some devices, and changes to clinical practice such as guidance on hip implants.

DARS-NIC-07360-K4R9R.summary: The University of Southampton's agreement covers hospital, mental health, accident and emergency, and death registration records. It is for studying Community Treatment Orders, which let patients detained in hospital continue compulsory treatment in the community. The research looks at how their use varies between people and places, how they relate to outcomes such as readmission and deaths, and what they cost. It aims to give a stronger evidence base on whether and for whom they work. An advance summary of the research was cited by the Wessely Independent Review of the Mental Health Act.

DARS-NIC-07763-M5K6S.summary: Cambridgeshire County Council's agreement covers pseudonymised hospital data, including admitted patient care, outpatient, accident and emergency, critical care and emergency care records. The data is for its public health work, such as producing needs assessments, health strategies, the Director of Public Health's annual report and advice to NHS commissioners. The main intended benefit is locally focused analysis of health and health inequalities. Since February 2021, the data has been used to assess mental health admissions.

DARS-NIC-07787-Z1W1X.summary: Oxford University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers national hospital admissions data (Hospital Episode Statistics) linked to death registration records. The data is for examining whether reducing antibiotic use in acute and general medical inpatients is linked to higher death rates or other poorer outcomes. The aim is to help design ways of safely cutting antibiotic use, and so reduce antibiotic resistance. The analysis has already contributed to developing an intervention now being tested in a large trial.

DARS-NIC-08095-P4D0D.summary: NHS North of England Commissioning Support Unit's agreement allows it to use Hospital Episode Statistics, covering A&E, admitted patient care, critical care and outpatients, in its business intelligence service and RAIDR dashboard tool. The data is for benchmarking clinical commissioning groups against national peers, and for supporting service planning and savings programmes. Reported results include peer-group comparisons that led to discussions with "best in class" groups, and demand and capacity modelling for sustainability and transformation partnerships.

DARS-NIC-08472-V9S6K.summary: UK Biobank, a charity, has an agreement with NHS England covering health records, including hospital, cancer, mental health, death and medicines data, linked to its research participants. The data is for following participants' health over time so researchers can study the genetic, social and economic causes of illnesses, with the aim of improving prevention, diagnosis and treatment. Published research has already used UK Biobank data, including around 400 COVID-19 papers and a study linking blood proteins to cancer diagnosis years earlier.

DARS-NIC-08477-H7S0Z.summary: The Medicines and Healthcare Products Regulatory Agency (MHRA) runs the Clinical Practice Research Datalink (CPRD) with the National Institute for Health Research. The agreement allows pseudonymised hospital, mental health, diagnostic imaging, patient reported outcome and mortality data to be linked to GP records. The data is for approved researchers to study areas such as drug safety and disease patterns. The expected benefit is better public health and patient outcomes, including input to clinical guidelines and regulatory decisions.

DARS-NIC-09046-M7D4X.summary: London Borough of Wandsworth's agreement covers pseudonymised Hospital Episode Statistics data for accident and emergency, inpatient and outpatient care. The agreement allows the data to be used for its public health duties, including needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, the Director of Public Health's annual report, and advice to NHS commissioners. Results will be aggregated, with small numbers suppressed. The main intended benefit is locally focused analysis of health inequalities, so that local health challenges, particularly for the most disadvantaged, are identified and addressed.

DARS-NIC-09122-R1S1D.summary: The Department of Health and Social Care's agreement covers non-identifiable Hospital Episode Statistics covering accident and emergency, admitted patient care, critical care and outpatients, accessed through the NHS Digital Portal. The data is for analysis to support policy development, commissioning decisions, benchmarking, publications and answers to parliamentary questions. The main benefit is fast analysis of recent data when ministers need it. The department reports the data has informed national policy, including 7-day services policy, and ministerial briefings.

DARS-NIC-09217-Y6K2B.summary: Monitor, the regulator of NHS services in England, is permitted to use detailed hospital data covering A&E, inpatient, outpatient and critical care activity, without identifiers. The agreement allows the data to support its duties under the Health and Social Care Act: licensing providers, regulating prices for NHS-funded care, supporting integrated care, preventing anti-competitive behaviour and supporting continuity of services. Analysis covers activity and tariff reports, referral patterns and modelling of tariff changes.

DARS-NIC-09519-D5G0R.summary: Methods Analytics Ltd's agreement allows it to use pseudonymised national patient-level hospital, emergency care, mental health and death registration data. The data is for producing analysis, tools and reports that help NHS organisations and the Getting It Right First Time (GIRFT) programme understand variation in care and improve quality, safety and efficiency. Reported results include a GIRFT review that identified over £1bn of NHS savings, and an NHS Trust's improved patient flow.

DARS-NIC-09637-Y8T1N.summary: The University of Oxford's agreement covers a pseudonymised extract of hospital admissions data (Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care) that has been linked to birth registration records. The agreement allows its researchers to study how gestational age affects children's health and economic outcomes up to age 11. The aim is to inform clinical guidelines, services and support for families of babies born before full term.

DARS-NIC-09901-F6V6M.summary: Bracknell Forest Council's agreement covers pseudonymised hospital data, including admissions, outpatient, critical care and accident and emergency records, for its public health work. The agreement allows the data to be used to analyse the local population's health and to support needs assessments, health strategies, public health advice and commissioning of services. The main intended benefit is locally focused analysis of health inequalities, so that needs are identified and acted on. The council has built a data warehouse, and in 2022 hospital admissions data informed the relaunch of local Joint Strategic Needs Assessments.

DARS-NIC-09949-T4N3W.summary: Kingston Hospital NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers Hospital Episode Statistics data for A&E, admitted patient care, critical care and outpatients. The data is for the trust's planning team, which uses it for scenario modelling, strategy development and benchmarking productivity against peers, to support evidence-based decisions and savings. The trust reports that benchmarking has already shaped its estates planning, challenged consultants' coding advice and supported a business case to expand endoscopy.

DARS-NIC-10029-G5R2H.summary: The Northern Ireland Clinical Trials Unit holds pseudonymised mortality data for people with acute lung injury who took part in the HARP2 trial. The data is kept securely for archiving, and the trial itself is complete. The trial tested whether simvastatin improves outcomes in acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS). The results were published in the New England Journal of Medicine and informed a Scandinavian clinical guideline and two systematic reviews, which recommended against statins for ARDS.

DARS-NIC-100546-M1J6C.summary: NHS Great Yarmouth and Waveney CCG's agreement covers hospital, ambulance, community, mental health, maternity and other local health service data, some identifiable by NHS number and some pseudonymised. The data is for risk stratification, which forecasts demand by identifying high-risk patients, and for supporting commissioning of health services for its local population. The main intended benefit is more targeted care and better-planned services.

DARS-NIC-100629-M8Y8B.summary: Tameside Metropolitan Borough Council's agreement covers civil registration data on births and deaths, plus primary care mortality data, which includes identifiable details. The data is for understanding local health needs, planning services, supporting suicide audits and prevention work, and producing aggregated, small-number-suppressed statistics for needs assessments and public health reports. The aim is to tailor local services and reduce health inequalities and premature deaths. Reported uses include producing the JSNA and PNA, a suicide audit and local life expectancy profiles.

DARS-NIC-10094-P6P4B.summary: City, St George's University of London holds a research database linking hospital admissions data (Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care) with birth registration and notification records. It is used to study how the day and time of birth relate to outcomes, to help inform maternity staffing and service planning. Reported results include a final report published by NIHR in 2019 and a 2023 BMJ Open paper finding that higher out-of-hours neonatal mortality was limited to babies born by emergency caesarean section without labour.

DARS-NIC-10104-T7C3J.summary: Hampshire County Council's agreement covers non-identifiable Hospital Episode Statistics (HES) data, accessed through the HES Data Interrogation System. The data is for its public health duties, including needs assessments, commissioning of services, advice to NHS commissioners and licensing responses. The main intended benefit is timely, local evidence for trends across age, gender and area. The release register also describes benefits already achieved, including commissioning decisions on an alcohol nurse service and informing a suicide prevention strategy.

DARS-NIC-10123-M5K5H.summary: The University of Oxford's agreement covers identifiable death records and demographic data for 470 English participants in ACST-2, an international trial comparing two stroke-prevention procedures: carotid surgery and carotid stenting. The data is for long-term follow-up of stroke outcomes, including disabling or fatal strokes, with a final report due in 2026-27. The intended benefit is to show whether the procedures give comparable results, so patients and doctors can choose between them. A major report was published in The Lancet in 2021.

DARS-NIC-10279-J8L3R.summary: The NHS Trust Development Authority (part of NHS Improvement)'s agreement allows it to access Hospital Episode Statistics (HES) data through the HES Data Interrogation System, covering critical care, A&E, inpatients, maternity and outpatients. The data is for monitoring and managing NHS Trust performance, and for supporting dashboards, a mortality toolkit and ad hoc analyses, with results shown only at Trust level. The main intended benefit is to spot problems early and improve patient care.

DARS-NIC-102794-Q4D1M.summary: NHS Leicester City CCG's agreement covers pseudonymised hospital, ambulance, community, mental health, maternity and other local provider data, covering both clinical and financial information. The agreement allows Midlands and Lancashire Commissioning Support Unit to analyse it to plan and commission health services for the local population. The main intended benefit is better planning of services and patient flow, including fewer avoidable emergency admissions.

DARS-NIC-102804-C2V0N.summary: NHS East Leicestershire and Rutland CCG (Clinical Commissioning Group) agreement covers pseudonymised hospital, ambulance, community, mental health, maternity and other health service data, covering both clinical and financial information. The data is for planning and commissioning health services for its local population, including analysing needs, modelling how services interact and identifying patients at risk of hospital admission. The main intended benefit is better planning of services and patient flows, helping to improve quality and access to care.

DARS-NIC-102825-Q3G3F.summary: NHS West Leicestershire CCG's agreement covers pseudonymised hospital, ambulance, community, mental health, maternity and other local provider data, which contains both clinical and financial information. The data is for planning and commissioning health services for the CCG area, including analysing population needs, modelling how services interact and redesigning services. The intended main benefit is better planning of patient flows and pathways, improving the quality of and access to services.

DARS-NIC-10328-S0H5J.summary: Cumbria, Northumberland, Tyne and Wear NHS Foundation Trust, through its North East Quality Observatory Service, is permitted to use pseudonymised hospital admissions, outpatient, A&E and emergency care data. The agreement allows the data to be used to measure care quality, benchmark services and evaluate service changes, producing aggregated reports for NHS and public-sector clients. The aim is to help organisations spot unwarranted variation and improve care. Reported results include reduced hospital stays and readmissions at several Trusts, and reports used in regional discussions on hospice services and children's asthma pathways.

DARS-NIC-103333-G9P5T.summary: London Borough of Sutton's agreement covers hospital admissions, outpatient, critical care and accident and emergency data. The agreement allows the data to be used in its public health work, including needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, advice to NHS commissioners and planning of local services. The data is for understanding local health and inequalities better. The data has already informed the Sutton Health and Care Plan and the Annual Public Health Report.

DARS-NIC-10343-Z3M1B.summary: The Royal College of Physicians of London's agreement covers the use of Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care data, linked to audit records on people treated for hip fracture in England and Wales. The data is for comparing hospital performance fairly, tracking outcomes such as readmission and return to independent living, and estimating how many cases the audit captures. The aim is better care and outcomes for patients. An independent evaluation reported that the database reduced deaths in the month after hip fracture.

DARS-NIC-10459-G9T3P.summary: The London Borough of Richmond upon Thames, a local authority, is permitted to use hospital and emergency care records (Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set) for its public health work. The agreement allows the data to be used to produce needs assessments, health strategies, the annual public health report and advice to NHS commissioners. The aim is locally focused analysis of health and inequalities. Reported work so far includes analyses of violence-related A&E visits, preventable admissions, Covid inequalities and leading causes of death.

DARS-NIC-104802-G2J0P.summary: The London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine's agreement covers contact details for British nuclear test veterans: NHS number, date of birth, GP practice details and whether each veteran was at the tests. The data is for identifying and recruiting veterans through their GP practices for a study of possible genetic damage in veterans and their children. The main intended benefit is clearer evidence for the nuclear community about possible health effects.

DARS-NIC-10496-Z3F9B.summary: The University of Oxford's agreement covers use of Office for National Statistics mortality data for a research study in Oxfordshire. The agreement allows the study to find what proportion of patients who die in a year were assessed by the Oxfordshire Out of Hours (OOH) service in the four weeks before death, and whether any patient subgroups face higher risk. The main intended benefit is better evidence for developing out of hours services that meet the needs of people at end of life.

DARS-NIC-10497-N0K9V.summary: University Hospital Southampton NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers the use of Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care data on children under 18 with inflammatory bowel disease. The agreement allows the Trust to study whether biological drugs have changed the rate of bowel surgery, and whether appendectomy affects the risk of developing the disease or needing a bowel resection. The Trust expects the findings to guide how paediatric surgeons and gastroenterologists manage these children.

DARS-NIC-106180-L3C4J.summary: NHS Lambeth CCG's agreement covers the use of pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, maternity, ambulance, primary care and other health and financial data, with processing carried out by NHS North East London CSU. The data is for planning and commissioning health services for its local population, including needs assessment, service redesign and identifying patients at risk of hospital admission. The main intended benefit is better-planned services, with improved patient flow, access and quality of care.

DARS-NIC-10620-V9D8R.summary: Nottingham University Hospitals NHS Trust, which hosts the East Midlands Academic Health Science Network, has an agreement covering Hospital Episode Statistics data on hospital admissions, outpatients, critical care and accident and emergency care, along with the Emergency Care Data Set. The agreement allows the network to produce aggregated reports on demand for services, variations in care and the impact of innovations. The intended benefit is better, safer and more efficient care for East Midlands residents.

DARS-NIC-107814-Z0J1Q.summary: NHS England's agreement allows pseudonymised, record-level hospital, emergency care, ambulance, mental health and talking therapy data to be used for routine and ad-hoc analysis and reporting. The data is for commissioning, contract and performance management, and data quality checks. Linking the datasets is intended to show full patient pathways, including how physical and mental health relate, so commissioners can plan care and meet statutory duties.

DARS-NIC-107979-X3R6Q.summary: Doncaster Metropolitan Borough Council's agreement allows the use of identifiable birth and death registration data, plus primary care mortality data, to measure local health needs, plan services and protect public health, including suicide audits and hotspot mapping. Results are published only as aggregated statistics. The aim is to tailor local services to reduce mortality and health inequalities. The data has already been used to produce community profiles and to monitor mortality rates ahead of national monitoring.

DARS-NIC-108067-P1C4R.summary: Worcestershire County Council, a local authority, has an agreement covering civil registration data on births and deaths, plus primary care mortality data, which includes identifiable details. The agreement allows the data to be used to measure local health needs, plan services and support public health work such as suicide audits and prevention. The aim is to tailor local services and reduce health inequalities. The council reported using deaths data during the Covid pandemic to target services, and the agreement allows work with the integrated care board (ICB) on ongoing health issues.

DARS-NIC-108098-D2L3V.summary: The Clinical Practice Research Datalink (CPRD)'s agreement allows linked health data, with identifying details removed, from GP records and NHS Digital sources. The data is for two studies for Cancer Research UK on bowel cancer screening. One looks at how people who do not respond to screening use primary care. The other looks at how patients and GPs respond to symptoms after a negative screening test. The aim is to help target support and promote earlier diagnosis.

DARS-NIC-10891-M2Y6Z.summary: CHKS Limited's agreement covers the use of Hospital Episode Statistics, Emergency Care Data Set and Summary Hospital-level Mortality Indicator data to provide benchmarking and analysis services to NHS providers, commissioners and some commercial organisations working with the NHS. The agreement allows the data to support performance comparison, mortality review and reports, with small numbers suppressed. The aim is to help improve patient care and efficiency. Reported benefits include Barnsley and Barts Health using mortality reports to guide action plans and reviews.

DARS-NIC-10912-D5Y1L.summary: Newcastle City Council's public health team's agreement covers hospital inpatient, outpatient, critical care and accident and emergency data, plus emergency care data. The agreement allows the team to use them to support its public health duties, including needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, the Director of Public Health's annual report and advice to NHS commissioners. The aim is locally focused analysis of health and health inequalities. The data has fed into a Drug Market Profile, alcohol admissions mapping and completed needs assessments.

DARS-NIC-10929-K8H5K.summary: The Royal Borough of Greenwich's agreement covers hospital records from NHS England's Secure Environment: Hospital Episode Statistics covering admitted patient care, outpatients, critical care and A&E, plus the Emergency Care Data Set. Its public health team may use them to produce needs assessments, health strategies and advice to NHS commissioners. The aim is locally focused analysis of health outcomes and inequalities. Reported use so far includes analyses of COVID-19, maternity, alcohol and falls admissions that fed into reports and service performance reporting.

DARS-NIC-10932-H7Y6B.summary: Suffolk County Council's agreement covers hospital records for emergency care, admitted patients, critical care, outpatients and A&E attendances. The data is for public health work, such as producing needs assessments and the Director of Public Health's annual report, advising NHS commissioners and planning services. The aim is local analysis of health inequalities, including for disadvantaged groups. Analyses already produced cover areas such as self-harm, falls and asthma admissions, and demand projections.

DARS-NIC-109867-M8S6B.summary: The University of Leeds's agreement covers the use of hospital records (Hospital Episode Statistics), death records and cohort tracking reports for women in the UK Women's Cohort Study. The data is for linking them with diet and lifestyle information to study how diet and lifestyle relate to cancer and other chronic diseases, with the aim of informing public health advice. The register reports published research from the study, such as papers on cancer risk and hip fracture, which it says has informed policy and NHS programmes.

DARS-NIC-10994-B8M6V.summary: Cheshire West and Chester Council's public health team's agreement covers the use of hospital and emergency care records (Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set) to support its public health duties, including needs assessments, health strategies, commissioning and advice to the NHS. The aim is locally focused analysis of health and inequalities. Reported results include published Starting Well and falls needs assessments and annual Children's Centre profiles.

DARS-NIC-110660-G9W6M.summary: NHS Greater Manchester ICB, acting for the former NHS Stockport CCG, is permitted to use hospital, community, mental health, maternity, ambulance and primary care activity data, with some identifiable by NHS number and some pseudonymised. The data is for checking provider invoices, identifying patients at high risk so GPs can target their care, and planning and monitoring health services. The main intended benefit is that providers are paid accurately and care is better planned for local people.

DARS-NIC-110691-Y1M3W.summary: Blackburn with Darwen Borough Council's agreement covers basic personal details from the NHS Personal Demographics Service (PDS), including NHS Number, name, address, date of birth, date of death and registered GP practice. The agreement allows the data to match adult social care records with the right individual, so social care and health staff can coordinate care, including hospital discharge. The main intended benefit is better joined-up, safer care, with fewer discharge delays.

DARS-NIC-11114-J5C4Q.summary: Devon County Council's public health team's agreement covers pseudonymised hospital records, covering admissions, outpatient, accident and emergency, critical care and emergency care data. The agreement allows the data to support its public health duties, including needs assessments, health strategies, commissioning, and advice to NHS commissioners. The data is for locally focused analysis of health outcomes and inequalities. Reported benefits include the data informing the 2025 Joint Strategic Needs Assessment refresh and its new chapter on inequalities.

DARS-NIC-11221-X6Y6N.summary: University Hospitals of Derby and Burton NHS Foundation Trust's agreement allows it to use Hospital Episode Statistics (HES) data on hospital admissions, outpatients, critical care and A&E through the NHS Digital Portal. The data is for studying acute kidney injury (AKI) in England and for supporting quality improvement, with the aim of improving length of stay, mortality and services. Earlier access led to published research papers on AKI and to changes in coding and AKI recognition at Queens Hospital, Burton.

DARS-NIC-112227-F5J0Y.summary: NHS Southern Derbyshire CCG's agreement covers hospital activity data (Secondary User Services, or SUS+, for commissioners), identifiable by NHS number. The data is for checking invoices from care providers and, with North of England CSU, for risk stratification that links the data with GP records to identify patients at high risk. The main intended benefits are accurate payments and better targeted care, planning and commissioning of services.

DARS-NIC-112231-L7J9X.summary: NHS Hardwick CCG's agreement covers hospital, ambulance, community, mental health and primary care activity data, including patient-level data identifiable by NHS number. The agreement allows the data to be used to check invoices from care providers before payment and to run risk stratification, which identifies patients at high risk so their care can be planned. The main intended benefit is more effective commissioning of services, with earlier intervention and better use of public funds.

DARS-NIC-112258-C9G8J.summary: NHS Erewash CCG's agreement covers pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other health service data, containing clinical and financial information. The agreement allows this data to be used to analyse and plan health services for people in its area, including contract monitoring, service redesign and identifying patients at risk of hospital admission. Arden and Greater East Midlands Commissioning Support Unit carries out the processing. The stated aim is better planning and quality of services.

DARS-NIC-112265-G2X3M.summary: NHS Erewash CCG's agreement covers hospital activity data from the Secondary Uses Service (SUS), including NHS numbers, linked with GP data. The data is for checking provider invoices before payment and identifying patients at high risk so their care can be planned. The stated benefits are sound financial control and better-targeted care, with fewer avoidable emergency admissions.

DARS-NIC-112267-W4G8W.summary: NHS North Derbyshire CCG's agreement covers hospital activity data (Secondary Uses Service, or SUS+) that can be identified by NHS number, along with local provider flow data and GP data. The data is for checking that provider invoices are the CCG's responsibility to pay, and for identifying patients at high risk so their care can be planned. The intended benefits are financial control and better-targeted care in primary care, with fewer avoidable emergency admissions.

DARS-NIC-112374-X0T4S.summary: University College London (UCL)'s agreement covers hospital admission records (Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care) and Patient Reported Outcome Measures linked to them. The agreement allows UCL to independently evaluate the Getting it Right First Time (GIRFT) programme, which aims to reduce variation in NHS orthopaedic surgery, focusing on hip and knee replacements. The intended benefit is evidence on what worked, so the programme and future improvement programmes can be refined.

DARS-NIC-112633-G0C0H.summary: The University of Ulster's agreement covers the use of Adult Psychiatric Morbidity Survey 2014 data on adults in England. It allows more detailed analysis of hazardous, harmful and dependent drinking, including how harm differs by social class. The aim is to give policy makers and health planners stronger evidence for targeting services at the drinkers at greatest risk of alcohol-related harm.

DARS-NIC-112910-R4X9X.summary: The University of Leeds's agreement covers the use of hospital admission records and death registration data to follow up patients hospitalised with non-ST elevation acute coronary syndrome (a type of heart attack or unstable angina). The study tests whether using the GRACE risk score increases use of guideline-recommended treatments and reduces cardiovascular deaths and hospital readmissions at twelve months, compared with standard care. Data received so far went to the trial's Data Monitoring and Ethics Committee in 2019, which used it to decide that the study should continue.

DARS-NIC-11302-Q1L1F.summary: The National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)'s agreement covers the use of Hospital Episode Statistics data on hospital admissions, outpatients, critical care and accident and emergency. The data is for scoping and reviewing guidance and standards, developing indicators and building tools that estimate the cost of putting guidance into practice. The aim is guidance based on the best available evidence. In 2021, the data informed a published resource impact report and template for prostate cancer guidance.

DARS-NIC-113025-X7Z3L.summary: The Clinical Practice Research Datalink (CPRD) is permitted, under its agreement, to use linked health records, supplied through bespoke Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) datasets, to support the PEARL study. The study looks at long-term health outcomes for women who have had assisted reproductive technology (ART) treatment and for their children, linking GP data with fertility treatment registry data. The main intended benefit is better evidence for couples considering fertility treatment, for families and for clinicians, and for NHS planning.

DARS-NIC-113074-D9M1C.summary: The Clinical Practice Research Datalink (CPRD), part of the Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency, is using bespoke Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) data. This supports a study of how air pollution affects health, with results reported to the study sponsors and published in journals. The main intended benefit is a clearer picture of health effects at the low pollution levels now common in the UK, to help shape pollution reduction policies.

DARS-NIC-113611-X2Y3H.summary: University Hospitals Coventry and Warwickshire NHS Trust's agreement covers Hospital Episode Statistics data on accident and emergency attendances and hospital admissions for patients with specialist palliative care needs. The agreement allows the data to be used to find out why these patients end up in emergency departments and acute hospitals. The findings are meant to help design services that support them at home and reduce hospital admissions.

DARS-NIC-113855-M5G7Q.summary: Isle of Wight Council's public health team's agreement covers hospital records on admissions, outpatient visits, critical care and accident and emergency attendances. The agreement allows the data to support its public health duties, including needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, the Director of Public Health's annual report and advice to NHS commissioners. The stated benefit is locally focused analysis of health outcomes and inequalities. The data has informed health needs assessments, prioritisation work and early analysis of COVID's impact.

DARS-NIC-113964-G3J0C.summary: The University of Oxford's agreement covers pseudonymised, record-level hospital, emergency care, mental health and death registration data about people taking part in The HOME Study. The data is for showing whether adding a new psychological care approach for older hospital patients reduces the time they spend in hospital, and what it costs the NHS. The results are expected to inform decisions about NHS investment in liaison psychiatry services.

DARS-NIC-113980-R8Z8K.summary: NHS Cheshire and Merseyside ICB's agreement covers the use of pseudonymised health, social care and civil registration data, including hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other services, to support commissioning. The agreement allows the data to be analysed to plan services around local needs, understand patient flows and risk, and manage contracts. The main intended benefit is better planning and quality of services for the local population.

DARS-NIC-114531-J1Q9G.summary: Trafford Metropolitan Borough Council's agreement covers civil registration data on births and deaths, along with primary care mortality data. The agreement allows the data to be used to understand local health needs, support public health work such as suicide audits, and produce summary statistics for health strategies and reports. The aim is to tailor local services, reduce premature deaths and tackle health inequalities.

DARS-NIC-114652-L3R2T.summary: NHS Blood and Transplant's agreement covers the use of civil registrations of death data to find out whether recruited trial patients were still alive one year after major trauma bleeding. It supports the CRYOSTAT 2 trial, run with Queen Mary University of London, which tests whether early high-dose cryoprecipitate, a fibrinogen-rich blood component, reduces deaths. The aim is to show whether it improves survival and is cost effective. Short-term results have already been shared with the trial team, and a manuscript is being prepared.

DARS-NIC-115298-L5X4V.summary: GlaxoSmithKline Research & Development Limited, a commercial company, is permitted to keep hospital records data (Hospital Episode Statistics covering A&E, admitted patients, critical care and outpatients) for people in the Extended Salford Lung Study. The agreement allows the data to be used to answer peer review comments on its asthma studies before they are published. The main intended benefit is helping doctors identify asthma patients with poor control or frequent moderate flare-ups. Findings were presented as abstracts at the ISPOR 2022 and CHEST 2022 conferences.

DARS-NIC-115405-P6X6Q.summary: The University of Nottingham's agreement covers hospital records from NHS England (Hospital Episode Statistics for accident and emergency, admitted patient care and outpatients) for people with familial hypercholesterolaemia (FH), an inherited cause of high cholesterol. The data is for examining treatment patterns, heart-related outcomes and NHS costs over the long term, and for building economic models of testing relatives of people with FH. The aim is to show which testing approach offers the best value for money, to inform NHS commissioners and national guidance.

DARS-NIC-11544-S1L0R.summary: Birmingham Women's and Children's NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers the use of pseudonymised (non-identifiable) Hospital Episode Statistics for accident and emergency, admitted patient care, critical care and outpatients, accessed through an online portal. The agreement allows the data to be used to benchmark care, plan services across the local health system and assess future population need for children and women. The aim is well-planned paediatric care. Reported benefits include data informing orthopaedic service planning in business cases and the placement of community maternity hubs.

DARS-NIC-11552-L0V6B.summary: Cheshire West and Chester Council's agreement covers hospital activity data from the HES Data Interrogation System for local public health intelligence. The data is for needs assessments, advice to clinical commissioning groups (CCGs) and requests for analysis of hospital activity. The aim is to help the council meet its public health duties and to identify and reduce health inequalities, such as in falls admissions.

DARS-NIC-115590-Q1C7Z.summary: The University of Surrey's agreement covers hospital records for children in England, including admissions, outpatient and A&E visits, critical care and death registrations. The data is for one part of the EU-funded MOCHA study, which looks at how individual and health service factors affect outcomes in eight childhood conditions, including asthma, epilepsy and rickets prevention, between 2003 and 2017. The aim is to show which structural factors matter for child health outcomes in England, and to help identify the best models of primary care for children.

DARS-NIC-115814-Q4T8Z.summary: NHS North Cumbria CCG's agreement covers hospital, ambulance, community, mental health, maternity and primary care data, some identifiable by NHS number and some pseudonymised, with North of England CSU doing the processing. The data is for risk stratification, which forecasts demand by identifying high-risk patients so GPs can target care, and to support commissioning of health services. The main intended benefit is more effective commissioning, with better planning, earlier intervention and improved patient experience.

DARS-NIC-115892-Y2C6D.summary: Bolton Metropolitan Borough Council's agreement covers pseudonymised hospital activity data (SUS for Commissioners), allowing its use to support public health and commissioning duties. The data is for analysing health needs, inequalities and service use, and for producing documents such as Joint Strategic Needs Assessments and the annual public health report. The aim is more locally targeted and responsive services. Reported uses include supporting commissioning of young people's health and drug and alcohol services, and informing violence reduction work.

DARS-NIC-115934-P8P0X.summary: NHS North East and North Cumbria ICB's agreement, acting for the former Hartlepool and Stockton-on-Tees clinical commissioning group, covers hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other health service data, some of it identifiable by NHS number. The data is for checking provider invoices, identifying patients at high risk of health decline, and planning and commissioning health services for the local population. The main intended benefit is more effective commissioning, with accurate payments and better patient care.

DARS-NIC-11613-B4J8Z.summary: Blackpool Borough Council's public health team's agreement covers the use of hospital and emergency care records (Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set) to meet its public health duties. The agreement allows the data to be used to plan and commission services, advise NHS commissioners and produce needs assessments and strategies. The main intended benefit is locally focused analysis of health and health inequalities. Work on children's dental extractions, falls, alcohol-related admissions and urgent care use has supported needs assessments and influenced commissioning decisions.

DARS-NIC-116377-L5J9M.summary: The University of Sheffield's agreement covers hospital admissions records (Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care) and a bespoke MRIS (Medical Research Information Service) dataset. The data is for linking with dental data to study whether invasive dental procedures are connected to infective endocarditis, heart attack, stroke, pulmonary embolus and spontaneous pre-term birth. The main intended benefit is stronger evidence for guidelines on antibiotic prophylaxis before dental and medical procedures.

DARS-NIC-116524-S2N2H.summary: NHS Bath and North East Somerset CCG's agreement covers hospital, ambulance, community, mental health, maternity and other health service data, some identifiable by NHS number and some pseudonymised. The agreement allows South, Central and West CSU (Commissioning Support Unit) to process it for invoice validation, risk stratification to identify high-risk patients, and analysis to support commissioning. The stated aim is more effective commissioning of services, leading to a better patient experience.

DARS-NIC-116548-M7Z5F.summary: NHS Frimley ICB (a sub-ICB location) uses hospital, ambulance, community, mental health and other local provider activity data, including NHS-number-level data for some uses. It uses the data to check provider invoices, identify patients at high risk of poor health, and plan and commission health services. The main intended benefit is that providers are paid accurately and services are planned to match local needs. The register says services have been delivered to match population requirements, but gives no specific example.

DARS-NIC-116560-R7F9J.summary: NHS Bath and North East Somerset, Swindon and Wiltshire ICB's agreement covers hospital activity data (Secondary User Services data for commissioners), which can be identified by NHS number, supported by NHS South Central and West Commissioning Support Unit. The data is for checking provider invoices so that only patients the ICB is responsible for are paid for. It may also be linked with GP data to identify patients at high risk of health deterioration. The main intended benefit is accurate payment and earlier, better targeted care.

DARS-NIC-116582-F2F2J.summary: NHS Buckinghamshire, Oxfordshire and Berkshire West ICB, working with Oxfordshire County Council, agreement covers pseudonymised health and adult social care data, including hospital, mental health, community, maternity, prescribing and death records. The data is for planning and commissioning health services for Oxfordshire's population, including population health management and service redesign. The main intended benefit is better decisions and improved quality of services and health outcomes. Reported results include a diabetes dashboard, which was used to improve diabetes care, and a new community gynaecology service.

DARS-NIC-116738-W8J8Q.summary: NHS Northamptonshire ICB's agreement covers the use of Secondary User Services (SUS+) hospital activity data, which can be identified by NHS number, and its linkage with GP data. The data is for checking provider invoices before payment and for identifying patients at high risk of health deterioration, so that care can be planned and targeted. The main intended benefit is that providers are paid accurately for treatment and that at-risk patients receive earlier, more effective care.

DARS-NIC-116829-C2B8N.summary: NHS Northamptonshire ICB's agreement, as a sub-ICB location, allows it to use Secondary User Services (SUS) data for commissioners, identifiable by NHS number. The data is for checking hospital and service invoices so that only activity for patients the organisation is responsible for is paid. It is also for risk stratification, which links SUS data with GP data to identify patients at high risk so that care can be planned and targeted. The main intended benefit is accurate payment and better-targeted care.

DARS-NIC-116883-L8W9Q.summary: Moorfields Eye Hospital NHS Foundation Trust's agreement with University College London covers the use of pseudonymised hospital, emergency care and death registration records for about 550,000 patients who had retinal scans. The data is for studying how changes in the retina relate to dementia and other neurodegenerative diseases, with the aim of developing a tool to detect dementia early. Published work so far includes a 2022 BMJ Open paper, research finding retinal changes in Parkinson disease about seven years before clinical presentation, and a dementia prediction model.

DARS-NIC-117514-V5D2N.summary: Sandwell Metropolitan Borough Council's agreement covers the use of hospital and emergency care data (Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set). The data is for its public health duties, such as needs assessments, health strategies, advice to NHS commissioners and annual reports. The aim is locally focused analysis of health inequalities. The council used the data for a Family Hubs needs assessment, which helped target support in areas with birth-related issues.

DARS-NIC-11809-H1Y3W.summary: The University of Leeds's agreement covers the use of cancer registration, hospital, mental health, radiotherapy and systemic anti-cancer therapy data to run the Yorkshire Specialist Register of Cancer in Children and Young People. The data is for research on hospital use, diagnosis pathways and long-term health risks among cancer survivors aged 0 to 39. It aims to improve care and treatment decisions. Reported results include peer-reviewed publications and evidence that supported risk-stratified follow-up care in Yorkshire and beyond.

DARS-NIC-118232-Z8V8B.summary: Sandwell Metropolitan Borough Council's agreement covers the use of identifiable birth and death records, including primary care mortality data, to understand local health needs, plan services and protect public health, including suicide prevention work. The agreement allows the main intended benefit of local services better targeted at areas of greatest need, helping to reduce health inequalities and premature deaths. Reported uses to date include analysis feeding into the Joint Strategic Needs Assessment and Annual Report, and the data has been used extensively in the council's suicide prevention work.

DARS-NIC-119910-K6W9Q.summary: The University of Bristol is using NHS England hospital, cancer registration, death and diagnostic imaging records for men in the CAP trial, which compares inviting men aged 50 to 69 for a PSA test for prostate cancer with standard NHS care. The data are used to follow up deaths and cancer diagnoses over the long term, to assess whether PSA testing reduces prostate cancer deaths and whether it is cost-effective. The results are intended to inform UK screening policy. Findings have already been published in JAMA, and results have been presented to the Department of Health and Social Care and used in the National Screening Committee's review.

DARS-NIC-120037-G1Z7C.summary: NHS Coventry and Rugby CCG's agreement covers pseudonymised hospital, ambulance, community, mental health, maternity and other local provider data, covering both clinical and financial information. The data is for planning and commissioning health services for the CCG area, including population health management, service redesign and contract monitoring. The stated aim is to match services to the population's needs and reduce duplication in analysis.

DARS-NIC-120057-H3L3B.summary: NHS South Warwickshire CCG's agreement covers pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other local provider data, including clinical and financial information. The agreement allows this data to be analysed to plan and commission health services, monitor contracts and understand the needs of the local population, with processing by Arden and GEM CSU. It allows the data to be shared with two neighbouring CCGs for joint reporting. The main intended benefit is better-planned services and patient pathways.

DARS-NIC-120064-Z5S8S.summary: NHS Warwickshire North CCG's agreement covers pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other health service data, including clinical and financial information. The data is for planning and commissioning health services for the local population, through analysis such as population health management, contract monitoring and identifying patients at risk. The main intended benefit is better planning of services and patient pathways, including fewer avoidable emergency admissions.

DARS-NIC-120105-F0K2L.summary: The University of Leicester's agreement covers the use of linked, pseudonymised hospital records (accident and emergency, admitted patient care) and civil registration death records, alongside audit data on children's intensive care. The data is for studying whether delays in reaching paediatric intensive care, and the care given during transport, affect critically ill children's survival. The agreement also allows analysis of the costs and value for money of different transport team models. The intended benefit is evidence to guide future standards of care and national policy for transporting critically ill children.

DARS-NIC-120519-J7H0T.summary: Bolton Metropolitan Borough Council's agreement covers civil registration data on births and deaths, plus primary care mortality data, including identifiable details. The data is for understanding local health needs, planning services and protecting public health, including suicide audits and hotspot mapping. The aim is to tailor services and reduce premature deaths and health inequalities. Reported uses include Bolton's Joint Strategic Needs Assessment, its serious violence needs assessment and strategy, and a licensing decisions tool.

DARS-NIC-120758-L4C3B.summary: NHS Bury CCG (Clinical Commissioning Group) agreement covers sharing pseudonymised hospital, ambulance, community, diagnostic and emergency care activity data with three other Greater Manchester CCGs. The data is for collaborative reporting and contract monitoring to support the commissioning of health services. The main intended benefit is better planning and monitoring of care for the local population, including reviewing demand and integrated care pathways.

DARS-NIC-120770-V1H9H.summary: NHS Manchester CCG, with NHS Bury, Heywood, Middleton and Rochdale, and Oldham CCGs, is permitted to use pseudonymised local provider data covering acute, ambulance, community, diagnostic and emergency care services. The CCGs and their data processors, Arden and GEM CSU, may use it for shared commissioning analysis and reporting, such as contract monitoring. The stated aim is to support commissioning of health services that fit the health needs of local people, including reviewing demand and integrated care.

DARS-NIC-120774-Y8L7S.summary: NHS Heywood, Middleton and Rochdale CCG's agreement covers pseudonymised local provider data across acute, ambulance, community, diagnostic and emergency care services. The agreement allows the data to be shared with the Bury, Manchester and Oldham CCGs to support commissioning, including contract monitoring, reporting and dashboards. The data is for understanding the health needs of the local population. The CCGs report that sharing acute financial data let them compare trends and coding behaviour, and helped standardise financial challenges across the area.

DARS-NIC-120805-F9Q4D.summary: NHS Oldham CCG (Clinical Commissioning Group) agreement allows pseudonymised, record-level data on acute, ambulance, community, diagnostic and emergency care services to be shared with three other Greater Manchester CCGs (Bury, Heywood, Middleton and Rochdale, and Manchester) and its data processors, Arden and GEM CSU. The data is for collaborative reporting and contract monitoring to support commissioning of health services. The expected benefit is better planning and monitoring of care for the local population.

DARS-NIC-120848-R6V4C.summary: The University of Warwick's agreement covers hospital admission and outpatient records (Hospital Episode Statistics) for patients who had total knee replacement surgery in 2003, linked to National Joint Registry records of tourniquet use. The data is for research into whether using a tourniquet during surgery is linked to complications such as blood clots in the leg or lung and stroke in the year afterwards. The main intended benefit is evidence on the safety of tourniquets, which could inform surgical practice and NICE guidance.

DARS-NIC-121483-R8P9F.summary: University Hospitals Birmingham NHS Foundation Trust manages the database for the Baby Biome Study, using hospital, outpatient, accident and emergency, critical care and death records for consenting mothers and their babies. The feasibility stage tests whether these records can be linked to the study's own data and checks their quality, to see whether early gut bacteria relate to later childhood health. The main aim is to support funding to expand the study and, longer term, to inform child health practice.

DARS-NIC-121849-W0T5C.summary: The University of Birmingham's agreement covers pseudonymised hospital admission records (Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care) for mothers and babies from births between 2005 and 2018. The data is for studying whether giving antibiotics before skin incision, rather than after cord clamping, in caesarean births is linked to children's later hospital admissions, mainly for asthma and eczema. The aim is to inform national guidance. The team reported finding no evidence of an association between the change in antibiotic timing and early-life illnesses in children.

DARS-NIC-121924-M1G3Q.summary: The Children's Commissioner's Office's agreement covers use of a pseudonymised extract from the Mental Health Services Data Set. The review examines how far children travel to reach Tier 4 Child and Adolescent Mental Health Services (CAMHS) inpatient units, and whether this varies by area or children's characteristics. The aim is to show where more hospital beds and services are needed, so children do not have to travel long distances from home.

DARS-NIC-121996-T2R7B.summary: The University of Bristol's agreement covers the use of civil registrations of death data, linked to information on people with learning disabilities who have died in England. The data is for identifying their exact causes of death, which cannot be seen in national mortality statistics, so that services can be improved and early deaths reduced. Benefits reported so far include a national NHS England "Learning into Action" group, a March 2019 conference and a 2018 annual report.

DARS-NIC-122737-X2Y7F.summary: NHS Manchester CCG's agreement covers health data from hospital, ambulance, community, mental health, maternity and diagnostic services. It also allows primary care data and, in linked form, adult social care data. Most of the data is pseudonymised, meaning identifying details are masked, though risk stratification uses NHS number-level data. The data is for commissioning health services, identifying patients at high risk of needing care, and understanding the care Manchester's population receives. The main intended benefit is more joined up, efficient, higher quality care and better-targeted help for patients.

DARS-NIC-123200-J0L4T.summary: The London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine's agreement covers hospital records (admitted patient and critical care) and death and follow-up records for 1,615 people aged 65 to 84 who took part in a vitamin D trial. The data is for a study testing whether a larger trial of vitamin D supplementation, to see if it reduces illness and extends life, would be feasible. It aims to set the procedures, costs and design for that main trial. A paper on the feasibility study has been accepted by the NIHR Health Technology Assessment journal.

DARS-NIC-12406-X5D0K.summary: University Hospitals of North Midlands NHS Trust's agreement covers Hospital Episode Statistics data on accident and emergency, inpatient and outpatient activity. The agreement allows the data to be used to understand patient flows between hospitals, benchmark against other trusts and inform its annual plan and service planning. The main intended benefit is for the Trust to benchmark and improve its own performance and plan service capacity.

DARS-NIC-125012-S7Z6Y.summary: The London Borough of Hounslow's agreement covers civil registration data on births and deaths, plus primary care mortality data, which includes identifiable details. The agreement allows the data to be used to measure local health needs, plan services and immunisation programmes, and protect public health, for example through suicide audits and needs assessments. The aim is to tailor local services to reduce deaths and health inequalities. Reported benefits are information supplied to the Public Health team, such as deaths by cause and births by ward.

DARS-NIC-125031-Z3D7S.summary: The Royal Wolverhampton NHS Trust's agreement covers hospital admission, critical care, outpatient and death records for babies born at 27 to 31 weeks of gestation in England. The agreement allows a study of the cost of care up to age two, comparing neonatal intensive care units with local neonatal units, to help decide the best place of care. The aim is to guide neonatal service provision. The study team reports finding more serious brain injury in 27-week babies at local units, which is informing discussions on service delivery.

DARS-NIC-125783-W2W3P.summary: NHS West Yorkshire ICB's agreement with Wakefield Council covers linked health and care data covering hospital, ambulance, community, mental health, maternity and death records. The data is for evaluating Population Health Management work with care home residents in Wakefield and for planning services, with the aim of reducing hospital admissions and emergency demand. Reported benefits so far include a clearer picture of deaths moving from community settings into hospital, and of causes of in-hospital deaths.

DARS-NIC-126117-S3Y1K.summary: NHS Shropshire, Telford and Wrekin ICB (a sub-ICB location) is covered by an agreement that allows it to use Secondary User Services (SUS+) data, which is pseudonymised but identifiable by NHS number, for invoice validation and risk stratification. Invoice validation checks that hospital and other provider invoices are the commissioner's responsibility and recovers overpayments. Risk stratification links the data with GP data to identify patients at high risk, so care can be planned and targeted earlier.

DARS-NIC-12629-B4N5K.summary: Queen Mary University of London's agreement covers the use of NHS England cancer registration, hospital, emergency care and death records for the long-term follow-up of women in the IBIS-I breast cancer prevention trial. The data is for studying how well and how safely tamoxifen prevents breast cancer, aiming to give women at high risk and bodies such as NICE better information. Results from this data have already been published, including a 2015 paper on the main trial outcome that was used to inform NICE's recommendations on tamoxifen.

DARS-NIC-126676-G1X4M.summary: University College London's agreement covers identifiable NHS England data, including hospital records, cancer registrations and death registrations, for 382 women who took part in the TARGIT-A breast cancer radiotherapy trial. The agreement allows UCL to extend the trial's follow-up and to check whether collecting outcomes directly from patients is complete and accurate compared with NHS England data. The main intended benefit is a better way to gather long-term follow-up data in clinical trials.

DARS-NIC-12706-T1K2Q.summary: Knowsley Metropolitan Borough Council's agreement covers hospital data on admissions, outpatients, critical care and accident and emergency (A&E) attendances. The data is for its public health duties, including needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, the annual public health report and advice to NHS commissioners. The main intended benefit is locally focused analysis of health outcomes and inequalities. The council has used the data to monitor flu admissions by age group and to look at emergency admission trends.

DARS-NIC-127189-R2K8F.summary: St. George's Hospital Medical School's agreement allows it to use Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care data, supplied as tabulated counts of hospital admissions. It is for use with air pollution estimates to study how long-term and short-term exposure to outdoor air pollution relate to hospital admissions for respiratory and cardiovascular disease. The aim is to give UK policy makers useful information for assessing health impacts and planning measures to reduce air pollution.

DARS-NIC-127332-G0J1N.summary: NHS Shropshire, Telford and Wrekin ICB (a sub-ICB location) has an agreement that allows it to use hospital activity data from Secondary User Services (SUS+), linked to GP data for risk scoring. The data is for checking that provider invoices are valid and payable, and for identifying patients at high risk so care can be planned and targeted. The main intended benefits are accurate payment and budget control, and earlier support that reduces avoidable hospital admissions.
