DARS-NIC-12784-R8W7V.summary: Genomics England's agreement covers the use of linked NHS hospital, cancer, mental health, diagnostic imaging and death registration data in its National Genomics Research Library, a secure environment holding genomic and health data. The agreement allows researchers to use the data to understand diseases, find disease-causing gene variants and develop new treatments. Reported results include new diagnoses for 25% of participants in the 100,000 Genomes Project using whole genome sequencing.

DARS-NIC-12828-M0K2D.summary: Imperial College London's Dr Foster Unit, an academic research group, is permitted to use hospital records (inpatient, A&E, outpatient and critical care) and civil registration death data. The agreement allows it to develop measures of healthcare quality and safety, including monthly hospital mortality alerts and studies of how COVID-19 affected care. The aim is to show variation between hospitals and help improve care. Its mortality alerts helped identify problems at Mid Staffordshire NHS Foundation Trust, and its work has appeared in NICE clinical guidelines.

DARS-NIC-128537-M2P7G.summary: The Royal College of Physicians of London's agreement covers a list cleaning report from the Medical Research Information Service (MRIS), which supplies GP practice codes for people aged 50 and over who have had a fragility fracture. The codes link patients to clinical commissioning groups (CCGs) so that the Fracture Liaison Service Database can produce CCG-level summary reports. The reports are meant to show where fracture prevention services are under-commissioned and help improve secondary fracture prevention.

DARS-NIC-12881-L1H2B.summary: The University of York's agreement covers the National Audit of Cardiac Rehabilitation, which allows it to use hospital inpatient records (Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care) to count patients with heart conditions who should have received cardiac rehabilitation. The data is for reporting on how well services are performing, so that commissioners and clinical teams can improve them. The audit has produced over 25 research articles and led to national certification of programmes and inclusion in NHS England quality reporting.

DARS-NIC-129507-J0H0D.summary: NHS North East London ICB's agreement covers a sub-ICB location covering seven former CCGs in the area, and allows pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, maternity, primary care and civil registration data, including clinical and financial information. The data is for planning and commissioning health services for the local population, including population health management, needs assessment, demand management and contract monitoring. The main intended benefit is better-informed commissioning decisions, improving the quality of services and health outcomes.

DARS-NIC-129819-V5P5Z.summary: The University of Sheffield's agreement covers NHS list cleaning data (mortality checks, current addresses and type 2 objection removals) for patients with bladder cancer in Yorkshire, Humber, North Derbyshire and South Tees. It supports a survey of patients' health-related quality of life, to understand variation in outcomes and identify unmet needs. The list cleaning aims to improve survey coverage and avoid mailing people who have died.

DARS-NIC-12983-Y3L3K.summary: The University of Sheffield's agreement allows the use of de-identified hospital admissions data (Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care) to compare the safety and quality of care across English hospitals. The data is for giving policy makers and hospital administrators evidence on which hospitals may need further investigation. So far, the university has developed two new mortality indices, one for safety and one for quality, and used them to compare 136 acute general hospitals between 2010 and 2015.

DARS-NIC-129836-D5F3W.summary: University College London's Centre for Longitudinal Studies agreement covers receipt of demographic data, in the form of updated addresses, for members of the 1970 British Cohort Study. The data is for inviting participants to the age 51 survey and keeping in touch between surveys. The aim is to re-contact people it has lost touch with and avoid contacting those who have died. In the 2012 survey, almost 800 interviews were achieved with participants newly traced through addresses supplied by NHS England.

DARS-NIC-129953-Y2H5J.summary: NHS Leeds CCG (Clinical Commissioning Group) is covered by an agreement that allows it to receive hospital, mental health, community, maternity and other local provider data, some identifiable by NHS number and some pseudonymised. The agreement allows the data to be used to check provider invoices, identify patients at high risk so their care can be prioritised, and plan and monitor health services for the local population. The main intended benefit is better-planned services and improved patient experience through more effective commissioning.

DARS-NIC-129961-P7T9Z.summary: NHS Leeds CCG's agreement covers hospital, mental health, community, maternity and other local provider activity data, some identifiable by NHS number and some pseudonymised. The stated aim is better-planned, more effective commissioning, which is expected to improve patient experience.

DARS-NIC-130034-N7D1F.summary: NHS Leeds CCG's agreement covers hospital, mental health, maternity, community and other local provider activity data, some of it identifiable by NHS number and some pseudonymised. DARS-NIC-130720-Y8S8G.summary: NHS West Cheshire CCG's agreement covers pseudonymised data from hospital, ambulance, community, mental health, maternity and other health service datasets. The agreement allows the data to produce intelligence for commissioning health services, including reports, dashboards and budget monitoring. The data is for supporting planning that meets the health needs of the local population, such as reviewing demand and care pathways.

DARS-NIC-130731-T6N7C.summary: NHS Cheshire and Merseyside ICB's agreement, for the former NHS Eastern Cheshire CCG area, allows pseudonymised (personal details removed) hospital, community, mental health, maternity, ambulance and other health and care data, including clinical and financial information. Midlands and Lancashire Commissioning Support Unit may analyse it to plan and commission health services, assess population needs and redesign services. The main intended benefit is better planning of services and patient flow for the local population.

DARS-NIC-130735-P4Q6M.summary: NHS Cheshire and Merseyside ICB's agreement covers pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, maternity, prescribing and births and deaths data for the former Southport and Formby CCG area. The agreement allows the data to be used to plan and commission health services, including population health analysis, spotting patients at risk of admission, and managing demand and contracts. The aim is for services to better match local needs, with Midlands and Lancashire Commissioning Support Unit doing the processing.

DARS-NIC-130743-V5C9T.summary: NHS Cheshire and Merseyside ICB's agreement, for the former NHS Halton CCG area, allows it to use hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other health service data, mostly pseudonymised, with some identifiable at NHS number level for risk stratification. The data is for identifying patients at high risk, and for planning, monitoring and redesigning health services for the local population. The main intended benefit is better-targeted care and more effective commissioning, including fewer avoidable emergency admissions.

DARS-NIC-130744-K8R9C.summary: NHS South Cheshire CCG (Clinical Commissioning Group) is permitted to use pseudonymised data about hospital, mental health, maternity, community, ambulance and children's services. The data is for analysing health care provision for its local population and supporting the commissioning of health services. Expected benefits include better demand management, integrated care and patient pathways, and monitoring of service quality, performance and outcomes.

DARS-NIC-130761-H9V5V.summary: NHS Cheshire and Merseyside ICB (for the former Vale Royal CCG area) agreement covers pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, maternity, ambulance, primary care and civil registration data, with clinical and financial detail. The agreement allows Midlands and Lancashire Commissioning Support Unit to analyse it to plan and commission health services, including population health management, service redesign and identifying patients at risk. The main intended benefit is better planning of care pathways and patient flow.

DARS-NIC-130779-P1H2C.summary: NHS Cheshire and Merseyside ICB's agreement covers pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, maternity, prescribing and births and deaths data for the former South Sefton clinical commissioning group (CCG) area. The agreement allows the Midlands and Lancashire Commissioning Support Unit to analyse the data to plan and monitor health services, understand local health needs and identify patients at risk. The main intended benefit is better commissioning decisions and improved quality of services and health outcomes.

DARS-NIC-130789-T3F8P.summary: NHS Cheshire and Merseyside ICB's agreement for its Knowsley area covers pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, maternity, primary care medicines and death and birth records, covering both clinical and financial information. The data is for planning and commissioning health services for the local population, including studying needs, predicting demand and reviewing provider performance. The main intended benefit is better-planned services that improve quality and health outcomes.

DARS-NIC-130796-T8T5F.summary: NHS Cheshire and Merseyside ICB's agreement, for the former St Helens CCG area, covers pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, maternity, prescribing, social care and births and deaths data. The data is for planning and commissioning health services, understanding local needs, modelling demand and identifying patients at risk. The main intended benefit is better decisions that improve service quality and health outcomes. Reported benefits include supporting the Covid-19 vaccination and testing programmes, hospital discharges and care home support.

DARS-NIC-13133-B7B3K.summary: The University of Bristol's agreement covers NHS hospital records (including accident and emergency, inpatient, outpatient and critical care), mental health data sets and death and tracing records for about 5,000 adults enrolled in the Avon Longitudinal Study of Parents and Children as babies. The data is for tracing participants, updating records and studying adolescent mental health, substance use, self-harm and sexual health. The main intended benefit is better evidence for public health policy. Studies using the wider ALSPAC data have already informed policy and guidance, including on fish consumption in pregnancy.

DARS-NIC-13172-S1S3F.summary: The University of Oxford's agreement covers the use of hospital admission records and death and status-tracking records for people who took part in the SHARP kidney disease trial. It allows comparison of events recorded in these routine datasets with the outcomes that trial clinicians confirmed by reviewing hospital notes. The data is for showing whether routine healthcare data could replace costly manual checking, making future clinical trials cheaper and less demanding for participants.

DARS-NIC-131964-Q6L1J.summary: London North West University Healthcare NHS Trust's agreement covers hospital admission records (Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care) and Office for National Statistics mortality data. The data is for a feasibility study within the National Clinical Audit of Specialist Rehabilitation following Major Injury. It tests whether these data can track the pathways and outcomes of major trauma patients who need specialist rehabilitation but are not admitted to it. The aim is to help improve specialist rehabilitation services.

DARS-NIC-132001-W7C3H.summary: Derby City Council's agreement covers civil registration data on births and deaths, plus primary care mortality data, which includes identifiable details. The agreement allows the data to be used to assess local health needs, plan public health services, and carry out work such as suicide audits and prevention. The main intended benefit is health and care services tailored to local need, to reduce health inequalities and premature deaths. Reported results include death data having been used to frame a new inequalities agenda, and birth data having informed school placement planning.

DARS-NIC-132395-Q4W9P.summary: NHS Hampshire and Isle of Wight ICB's agreement, working with other clinical commissioning groups (CCGs) in the Hampshire and Isle of Wight partnership, allows the use of pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, ambulance and related data containing clinical and financial information. The data is for planning and commissioning health services, including reporting, demand planning and identifying patients and groups with particular needs. The stated benefits include better planning of patient pathways, improved access and quality, and fewer avoidable emergency readmissions.

DARS-NIC-132869-R0D7F.summary: Trafford Metropolitan Borough Council's agreement covers hospital data on emergency care, admitted patients, critical care and outpatients. The agreement allows the data to be used in its public health work, including needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, the annual public health report, and advice to NHS commissioners. The intended benefit is local analysis of health outcomes and inequalities, particularly for the most disadvantaged groups. Outputs will be aggregated, with small numbers suppressed.

DARS-NIC-133307-F2J3G.summary: Havering London Borough Council's agreement allows it to use Personal Demographics Service (PDS) data, meaning NHS Numbers and basic details such as name, address, date of birth, date of death and registered GP practice. The agreement allows it to find or confirm the NHS Number for people receiving adult social care, and to record it on its case management system. The aim is to let health and social care staff identify the same person, work together more closely and improve care, including smoother hospital discharges.

DARS-NIC-134027-L9T9J.summary: King's College London, an academic organisation, is using death registration records and hospital accident and emergency (A&E) records. It is using them in an eight-year follow-up of adolescents who went to A&E for self-harm and received either a Therapeutic Assessment or an assessment as usual. The study will look at whether the earlier gains in treatment engagement last, and whether A&E visits for self-harm changed. The team hopes the findings will inform assessment protocols and training.

The agreement allows North of England Commissioning Support Unit to process it to validate invoices, identify high-risk patients for GPs, and support commissioning. The main intended benefit is better-planned services and more targeted care, improving patient experience.

DARS-NIC-134719-D5W2Y.summary: Bristol NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers hospital, emergency care, diagnostic imaging and death registration records for the CIPHER study, which involves people who have had a stoma formed during bowel surgery. The study looks at how often parastomal hernia develops within two years and whether surgical techniques, such as the use of mesh, affect that risk. It aims to inform future research and guidance that could reduce hernias and improve patients' quality of life.

DARS-NIC-134833-S0M1M.summary: NHS Birmingham and Solihull CCG (Clinical Commissioning Group) is permitted to receive pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other health service data, including clinical and financial information. The agreement allows the data to be used to plan and commission health services for its local population, through analysis, reporting and patient risk modelling. The stated aim is to improve planning, patient flow and access to services, and to reduce avoidable emergency admissions.

DARS-NIC-134865-Q2T7Z.summary: NHS Dudley CCG's agreement covers the use of pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, maternity, ambulance and other health service data, containing clinical and financial information. The data is for analysing the needs of the local population and for planning, monitoring and redesigning the health services the CCG commissions, including identifying patients at risk of hospital admission. The main intended benefit is better planning of services and patient flow, with improved quality and access to care.

DARS-NIC-134899-Z7C9G.summary: NHS Sandwell and West Birmingham CCG's agreement covers pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, maternity, ambulance, primary care and cancer waiting times data, covering both clinical and financial information. The agreement allows this data to be used to plan and commission health services for its local population, including population health analysis, service redesign and identifying patients at risk of hospital admission. The stated aim is to better understand patient flows and population needs, so services can be planned and improved.

DARS-NIC-134909-J5H7C.summary: NHS Walsall CCG's agreement covers pseudonymised (identifiers replaced) hospital, community, mental health, maternity, ambulance and other local provider data, with clinical and financial detail. The data is for planning and commissioning health services for the local population, including analysing needs, modelling how services interact and identifying patients at risk of hospital admission. The main intended benefit is better planning of services and patient flow, with improved quality and access.

DARS-NIC-135277-R8M3G.summary: The Regional Drug and Therapeutics Centre at Newcastle's agreement allows it to use pseudonymised hospital, emergency care and primary care dispensing data. The data may be linked to produce prescribing reports for NHS areas, comparing medicine use with hospital admissions. The aim is to help local NHS teams benchmark prescribing and use medicines more cost-effectively. In Greater Manchester, the reports led to a diabetes pathway being developed and formulary changes.

DARS-NIC-135294-P7L0F.summary: Oxford University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers NHS England mortality data, including death registrations and cause of death reports, for the OxValve cohort of people aged 65 and over screened for valvular heart disease in primary care. The data is for reporting how long people with and without the condition survive and what they die from. This aims to help patients, clinicians and commissioners understand outlook and plan care. The findings have been published in the journal Heart and in a blog advising GPs that mild disease is unlikely to affect long-term outcome.

DARS-NIC-136400-H5Y3X.summary: Solihull Metropolitan Borough Council's agreement covers hospital data, including admissions, outpatients, critical care and accident and emergency (A&E) or emergency care attendances. The data is for its public health duties, such as needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, and advice to NHS commissioners. The aim is locally focused analysis of health and inequalities. The council reported using the data to inform its clean air strategy, a falls needs assessment and a learning disability needs assessment.

DARS-NIC-136916-B7D5C.summary: University College London's agreement covers the use of linked hospital, death registration and cohort-tracking records to compare outcomes for first-time teenage mothers who joined the Family Nurse Partnership home visiting programme with similar families who did not. The data is for showing how well the programme works for different groups of families, helping commissioners and policymakers target support. Reported results include published papers on enrolment and data linkage, and findings shared with the Family Nurse Partnership National Unit.

DARS-NIC-137718-T4D1S.summary: Bedford Borough Council's core public health team's agreement covers identifiable births and deaths records, including primary care mortality data, for use on behalf of itself, Central Bedfordshire Council and Milton Keynes Council. The agreement allows the data to be used to assess local health needs, run public health work such as suicide audits, and produce aggregated statistics for plans and reports. The aim is to tailor local services and reduce mortality and health inequalities. The data has produced a mortality dashboard for each of the three councils as part of the Joint Strategic Needs Assessment.

DARS-NIC-137819-F5B2W.summary: NHS Castle Point and Rochford CCG's agreement covers pseudonymised (identifiers removed) hospital, ambulance, community, mental health and other local provider activity data, along with Secondary Uses Service data. The data is for supporting the commissioning of health services, including population health management, service redesign, health needs assessment and identifying patients at risk of hospital admission. The main intended benefit is better planning of services and patient flow, with improved quality and access.

DARS-NIC-137826-M4W1Z.summary: NHS Mid Essex CCG's agreement covers the use of pseudonymised (personal identifiers removed) hospital, mental health, community, maternity and other local provider data, including Secondary Uses Service data. The agreement allows this data to support commissioning, including population health management, service redesign, health needs assessment and identifying patients at risk of hospital admission. The main intended benefit is better planning of services and patient flow, so that the right care is available where and when people need it.

DARS-NIC-137829-Z1M7V.summary: NHS Basildon and Brentwood CCG's agreement covers pseudonymised hospital, ambulance, community, mental health, maternity and other activity data covering its local population. The agreement allows the data to support commissioning, including population health management, service redesign, contract management and identifying patients at risk of hospital admission. The main intended benefit is better planning of services and patient flow, so that people get the right care when and where they need it.

DARS-NIC-137832-J6D8D.summary: NHS Southend CCG's agreement covers receipt of pseudonymised (identifiers masked) hospital, ambulance, community, mental health, maternity and other local provider activity data. The data is for supporting commissioning, including population health management, health needs assessment, service redesign and predicting which patients are at risk of hospital admission. Processing is carried out by North East London Commissioning Support Unit and Mid-Essex CCG. The main intended benefit is better planning of services and patient flow.

DARS-NIC-137841-V5M7Y.summary: NHS Thurrock Clinical Commissioning Group (CCG) is using pseudonymised hospital, ambulance, community, mental health, maternity and other local provider data, including Secondary Uses Service (SUS) records. It uses them to support commissioning of health services, including population health analysis, service redesign, activity and finance reporting, and identifying patients at risk of hospital admission. The main intended benefit is better planning of services and patient pathways, with improved quality and access for the local population.
DARS-NIC-137841-V5M7Y.retense_draft: NHS Thurrock Clinical Commissioning Group's agreement covers pseudonymised hospital, ambulance, community, mental health, maternity and other local provider data, including Secondary Uses Service (SUS) records. The agreement allows the data to support commissioning of health services, including population health analysis, service redesign, activity and finance reporting, and identifying patients at risk of hospital admission. The main intended benefit is better planning of services and patient pathways, with improved quality and access for the local population.

DARS-NIC-137864-T1P9B.summary: University College London (UCL) is authorised to use identifiable NHS England demographic data, mainly current addresses, for the National Child Development Study, which follows people born in one week in 1958. The addresses allow its Centre for Longitudinal Studies to contact participants who have moved and invite them to take part in future surveys. Reported benefits include newly traced participants being interviewed in the age 55 survey, and the age 55 data being available to researchers through the UK Data Service.

DARS-NIC-138652-J2Q4S.summary: The London Borough of Barking and Dagenham, a local authority, has an agreement covering civil registration data on births and deaths, along with primary care mortality data, including identifiable details. The data is for measuring local health needs, planning public health work such as immunisation programmes, and producing reports such as Joint Strategic Needs Assessments, with only aggregated statistics published. The aim is to tailor local services to areas of greatest need and reduce health inequalities. It reports that the data helped identify suicide hotspots and risk factors, which informed the local suicide prevention strategy.

DARS-NIC-139035-X4B7K.summary: NHS England's agreement allows it to use pseudonymised health data, including hospital, mental health, community, ambulance and clinical registry records, in its NHS England & Improvement Data Platform. The data is for managing commissioned services, supporting quality and productivity programmes, checking data quality and evaluating service changes. The aim is to help it meet its statutory duties and commission effective services. Reported benefits include a service moved to a more accessible location, dashboards and reports, and data supporting a published paediatric critical care review.

DARS-NIC-13906-G0F3F.summary: The Private Healthcare Information Network (PHIN), appointed by the Competition and Markets Authority as the "Information Organisation", may use pseudonymised Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care data on planned hospital care. The data may be used to publish hospital and consultant performance measures and to compare NHS-funded and private care. The aim is to help patients make better-informed choices of provider. PHIN has published analyses and consultant data reviews, and GPs have used its website to support patient choice.

DARS-NIC-139074-D9N2C.summary: NHS Heywood, Middleton and Rochdale CCG's agreement covers pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other health service data, including clinical and financial information. The data is for planning and commissioning health services for the CCG's population, with processing carried out by Arden and Greater East Midlands Commissioning Support Unit. Its stated main benefit is better understanding of patient flows and population needs, to improve planning, service quality and access.

DARS-NIC-139079-M6P7X.summary: NHS Manchester CCG's agreement covers pseudonymised health and adult social care data, including hospital, mental health, community, maternity and ambulance records, with clinical and financial detail. The agreement allows Arden and Greater East Midlands Commissioning Support Unit to process it to plan and commission health services for the local population, including population health analysis, service redesign and identifying patients at risk. The main intended benefit is better planning of services and patient pathways.

DARS-NIC-139091-F3T3H.summary: NHS Greater Manchester ICB, together with the other clinical commissioning groups (CCGs) in the Greater Manchester partnership, is permitted to use pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, maternity, social care, prescribing and death and birth records. The data is for planning and monitoring health services, tracking provider performance and costs, and understanding demand across the area. The main intended benefit is better-planned, higher-quality care that meets the needs of the local population.

DARS-NIC-139146-W7C3P.summary: Royal Papworth Hospital NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers the use of hospital admission and civil registration of death data to follow up patients with chronic thoracic aortic aneurysm in the ETTAA study. The data is for checking that deaths, hospital admissions and resources used are recorded accurately. The aim is to give reliable evidence on the clinical and cost-effectiveness of treatments, to guide decisions and NHS policy. Published papers in 2022 have already reported findings on treatment and monitoring.

DARS-NIC-13925-Q7R2D.summary: IQVIA Ltd, a commercial company, holds hospital data from NHS England (Hospital Episode Statistics, Emergency Care Data Set and data quality reports) that feeds its Hospital Treatment Insights database on diagnoses, treatments and drug use in hospitals. Under this agreement it may only keep the data securely, not process it further. Earlier work produced published studies and conference presentations on high-cost drugs, plus drug-use feedback reports that hospital chief pharmacists used to benchmark their prescribing.

DARS-NIC-139340-L4N0F.summary: NHS North Hampshire CCG's agreement covers pseudonymised hospital activity data (Secondary Uses Service, containing clinical and financial information) for commissioning. The agreement allows the data to be analysed to plan health services around the needs of the local population, including reporting, risk prediction and budget monitoring. NHS South Central and West Commissioning Support Unit and CHKS Limited carry out the processing. The expected benefit is better-informed service planning, including support for business cases and demand management.

DARS-NIC-139477-V5D6Y.summary: NHS Stockport CCG's agreement covers pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, ambulance, primary care and other local provider data, including clinical and financial information. The data is for planning and commissioning health services for the people in its area, including analysing needs, modelling how services interact and identifying patients at risk. The main intended benefit is better planning of services and patient flow, with improved quality of and access to care.

DARS-NIC-139741-D9Y1C.summary: Bangor University's agreement covers the use of Hospital Episode Statistics data on hospital admissions and outpatient visits for the NERVES trial, which involved 163 patients with sciatica. The data is for costing hospital care in the trial and comparing the cost-effectiveness of surgery with steroid injections. The main intended benefit is to help the NHS and commissioners decide which treatment is most clinically and cost-effective.

DARS-NIC-140023-N1F1S.summary: NHS Heywood, Middleton and Rochdale CCG's agreement covers the use of pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health and other local provider activity data, with support from commissioning support and data processing partners. The data is for commissioning, invoice validation, risk stratification and a national long-term conditions test bed programme. The main intended benefit is better planned, more joined-up care and earlier help for people at risk.

DARS-NIC-140037-T3W0M.summary: NHS Cheshire and Merseyside ICB's agreement, for the former Knowsley CCG area, allows use of hospital activity data (Secondary User Services data for commissioners) that can be identified by NHS number. The data is for checking provider invoices are correct and the CCG's responsibility, and for identifying patients at high risk of poor health so their care can be planned and targeted. The main intended benefits are accurate payment for care and earlier, better-targeted support for vulnerable patients.

DARS-NIC-140059-P1J9L.summary: NHS Cheshire and Merseyside ICB, with the local CCGs and councils in the Cheshire and Merseyside partnership, may use pseudonymised health and social care data covering hospital, community, mental health, prescribing and death records. The data is for planning, monitoring and improving commissioned services for their population, including demand, costs and patient pathways. Liverpool CCG's agreement covers use of the data to meet national data collection and 2-hour crisis response requirements, improve ethnicity coding, and support diabetes and Telehealth services.

DARS-NIC-140981-R5N6Z.summary: University College London (UCL)'s agreement covers a pseudonymised extract from the Mental Health Services Data Set, linked with Child Outcomes Research Consortium data, on young people aged 2 to 25 in child mental health services. The data is for studying how young people's characteristics relate to treatment outcomes and resource use, so care can be better tailored. UCL reports that a region has already used its findings in its Joint Strategic Needs Assessment.

DARS-NIC-141410-W6H4Y.summary: University College London (UCL)'s agreement covers hospital, accident and emergency, outpatient and death registration records for children and young people aged 0 to 24 in England. The research looks at why the UK's child and youth death rate is higher than in many comparable countries, including how health service use relates to this. The data is for informing health policy and service reform. Findings have already been published in Archives of Disease in Childhood and contributed to the RCPCH Paediatrics 2040 report.

DARS-NIC-14170-X2G3L.summary: Clatterbridge Cancer Centre NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers the hosting of the National Clinical Analysis and Specialised Applications Team (NATCANSAT), which may use linked hospital activity (A&E, admitted patient care and outpatient), death registration and mortality data. It allows analysis of cancer and cardiac care for NHS and Department of Health bodies, producing anonymised tables, maps and online tools. The aim is to show variations in practice and outcomes so services can improve. Its only reported project compared survival in non-small cell lung cancer patients across radiotherapy regimes.

DARS-NIC-141755-M8J2J.summary: NHS Cambridgeshire and Peterborough ICB's agreement covers Secondary User Services (SUS+) hospital activity data, identifiable by NHS number, for two purposes. The first is invoice validation, checking that providers' invoices are for patients the commissioner is responsible for. The second is risk stratification, where the data is linked with GP data to identify patients at high risk of health deterioration. The main intended benefits are accurate payment for care and better targeted care.

DARS-NIC-142633-S5G3Q.summary: NHS Derby and Derbyshire ICB's agreement, working with the former Erewash, Hardwick, North Derbyshire and Southern Derbyshire CCGs, covers pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other health and care activity data, with financial information and birth and death records. The agreement allows the data to be used to plan and commission health services, understand local health needs and redesign services. The main intended benefit is better planning of care, so services meet the needs of the local population.

DARS-NIC-142671-B1V9J.summary: NHS North Derbyshire CCG's agreement covers pseudonymised (identifiers replaced) hospital, mental health, community, maternity and other health service data, including clinical and financial information. The data is for planning and commissioning health services for its local population, including analysing needs, monitoring contracts and redesigning services. Commissioning support units may process the data, and four Derbyshire CCGs may share it for joint reporting. The stated aims include better planning of patient flow and improved quality of and access to services.

DARS-NIC-142675-L3P6F.summary: NHS Hardwick CCG's agreement covers the sharing and use of pseudonymised (identifying details replaced) hospital, ambulance, community, mental health, maternity and other health service data. The agreement allows the data to support commissioning, including population health analysis, service redesign, contract monitoring and identifying patients at risk. It also allows the data to be shared with three neighbouring CCGs for joint reporting. The main intended benefit is better planning of services around local needs.

DARS-NIC-142711-G4X3F.summary: NHS Southern Derbyshire Clinical Commissioning Group (CCG) uses pseudonymised hospital, ambulance, community, mental health, maternity and other health service data, containing clinical and financial information. It uses the data to analyse and plan the health services it commissions for people in its area, including population health management, service redesign and identifying patients at risk of hospital admission. The main intended benefit is better planning of services and patient flow, with improved quality and access.
DARS-NIC-142711-G4X3F.retense_draft: NHS Southern Derbyshire Clinical Commissioning Group's agreement covers pseudonymised hospital, ambulance, community, mental health, maternity and other health service data, containing clinical and financial information. The data is for analysing and planning the health services it commissions for people in its area, including population health management, service redesign and identifying patients at risk of hospital admission. The main intended benefit is better planning of services and patient flow, with improved quality and access.

DARS-NIC-142790-C1J9J.summary: King's College London's agreement covers the use of survey data on adult psychiatric morbidity and data from Improving Access to Psychological Therapies (IAPT) services. The data is for comparing the mental health, needs and treatment outcomes of veterans and non-veterans in England. The intended benefit is to help NHS England and service providers identify effective, timely treatments for ex-service personnel with mental health problems.

DARS-NIC-14337-J4N1T.summary: The University of Liverpool's agreement covers Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care data, limited to age, sex, admission and surgery dates and hospital, for the British Orthopaedic Surgery Surveillance (BOSS) study. The data is for checking that cases of slipped capital femoral epiphysis, a rare adolescent hip disease, are fully captured in the study's own database. The main intended benefit is better evidence on surgical practice and outcomes, to inform NICE and the feasibility of a clinical trial.

DARS-NIC-14340-R7G1F.summary: Meditrends Ltd's agreement allows it to use Hospital Episode Statistics hospital records and linked death registration data. It covers running a web portal of aggregated, small-number-suppressed analytics and producing custom analyses for NHS-led projects. The data is for planning services, comparing care pathways and estimating the budget impact of new technologies. The NICE multiple sclerosis appraisal analysis and the heart valve tariff guide are reported results.

DARS-NIC-14342-Q8W0X.summary: NHS Blood and Transplant's agreement covers the use of hospital records (Hospital Episode Statistics covering accident and emergency, admitted patient care and outpatients) linked to the ATTOM study of people in England with kidney disease who are on dialysis or have a kidney transplant. It allows examination of how health literacy, socioeconomic status and other health conditions relate to hospital use, costs and survival. The aim is to build evidence for reducing inequity in access to kidney transplantation.

DARS-NIC-14360-S9G2Y.summary: Imperial College London Business School's agreement covers the use of Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care records to study how new surgical techniques spread among consultants. It looks at colorectal and breast cancer surgery, and cardiac surgery, asking whether formal hospital cancer networks or consultants' professional networks have more influence on following national guidelines. The aim is to help policy makers target funding to speed up proven, cost-effective treatments. Two peer-reviewed papers, published in 2021 and 2025, have so far come from the work.

DARS-NIC-143777-Q0Q1S.summary: NHS Airedale, Wharfedale and Craven CCG's agreement covers pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, maternity, ambulance and other health service data, with clinical and financial detail. The data is for analysis by North of England Commissioning Support Unit to plan and commission health services for the local population, including service redesign and identifying patients at risk of hospital admission. The stated aims include better patient flow, improved access and fewer avoidable emergency admissions.

DARS-NIC-143888-H0W2N.summary: The University of Leicester's agreement covers the use of national hospital admission and death records, linked with other health datasets, to study how heart disease and cancer affect each other. The research looks at questions such as whether heart attack patients with cancer are treated differently and how cancer treatments affect long-term heart health. The main intended benefit is better evidence on managing patients who have both conditions, which could improve treatment and clinical practice.

DARS-NIC-144057-G4S0Q.summary: The University of Oxford's agreement covers the use of pseudonymised hospital admission records and death registration data for about 900,000 people over 60 who had hip fracture surgery. The data is for evaluating all-cause and cause-specific deaths after hip fracture, including how rates vary between hospitals, to show where and in whom mortality could be reduced. Benefits reported so far: the work supported the justification and planning for the DIRECT trial, which is now fully funded by NIHR.

DARS-NIC-14440-Q2G4W.summary: Royal National Orthopaedic Hospital NHS Trust's agreement covers the use of Hospital Episode Statistics admitted patient care and critical care data for the Getting It Right First Time (GIRFT) programme. The agreement allows calculation of hospital and Clinical Commissioning Group level metrics to support clinician review meetings, research and coding quality checks. The aim is to reduce variation in surgical practice and deliver efficiency savings. Measured changes in practice, such as shorter hospital stays and fewer readmissions in orthopaedics, and estimated savings already realised, are reported.

DARS-NIC-14455-D2N8Z.summary: FTI Consulting's agreement covers national Hospital Episode Statistics data for accident and emergency, admitted patient care and outpatients. The data is for financial and economic analyses for NHS trusts, clinical commissioning groups (CCGs), Monitor and NHS England, including benchmarking against peers and forecasting demand. The aim is to help these organisations see where they can improve performance, plan services and make savings.

DARS-NIC-144568-D7G6V.summary: Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust, through Royal Brompton Hospital, is using hospital admission, death registration and COVID-19 surveillance data to study how common acute myocarditis is in England, what happens to patients afterwards, and how COVID-19 relates to it. It aims to improve understanding of this poorly characterised condition. Reported benefits include a 2022 Circulation genetic study, and the data are referenced in UK government guidance on myocarditis after COVID-19 vaccination.
DARS-NIC-144568-D7G6V.retense_draft: Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust, through Royal Brompton Hospital, is studying hospital admission, death registration and COVID-19 surveillance data to examine how common acute myocarditis is in England, what happens to patients afterwards, and how COVID-19 relates to it. The agreement aims to improve understanding of this poorly characterised condition. Reported benefits include a 2022 Circulation genetic study, and the data are referenced in UK government guidance on myocarditis after COVID-19 vaccination.

DARS-NIC-144761-Y3X9Y.summary: King's College London's agreement covers the use of hospital admission, A&E and death registration data. The data is for studying end of life care for adults with serious mental illness, looking at hospital use in the last year of life and place of death, and which demographic and clinical factors are linked to them. The intended benefit is evidence on whether these patients face inequalities in care, to inform practice and policy.

DARS-NIC-145260-G4Y0G.summary: The London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine is using hospital admissions data (Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care) to study asthma, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and coronary heart disease. The research looks at how respiratory viruses and environmental factors such as air pollution affect the timing of hospital admissions for flare-ups of these conditions. The main intended benefit is a better understanding of these triggers, to help design preventive strategies and reduce the burden of flare-ups.

DARS-NIC-145660-F3MJ6.summary: The Healthcare Quality Improvement Partnership (HQIP)'s agreement covers the use of NHS registration data for medical research. It supports an audit of the quality of care for patients with oesophago-gastric cancer in England and Wales. The audit collects data from NHS Trusts to report on patient characteristics, treatment planning, postoperative outcomes and palliative treatment. It aims to link treatment details to outcomes.

DARS-NIC-146909-L9Q3C.summary: Thurrock Council's agreement covers the use of pseudonymised (identifying details removed) hospital, mental health, psychological therapy and maternity data, processed by MedeAnalytics International Limited. The data is for supporting commissioning of health and social care services, including population health analysis, service redesign and contract management. The main intended benefit is more effective commissioning and better patient experience. The council has used the data to complete the first phase of an evaluation of an alternative approach to adult social care.

DARS-NIC-147034-XH3H2.summary: The University of Cambridge's agreement covers date and cause of death records and related demographic data for participants in the CFAS II and CFAS Wales studies of people aged over 65. The agreement allows the data to be used to work out survival and life expectancy, including for people who develop cognitive impairment, to support research on dementia and healthy ageing. The findings are intended to help plan services. Welsh Government may use CFAS dementia prevalence findings to calculate diagnosis rates across Health Boards.

DARS-NIC-14709-Z2H2R.summary: i5 Health Limited, a consultancy, is permitted under its agreement with NHS England to use hospital, emergency care and community services data to produce aggregated reports and data models for NHS bodies, local authorities and voluntary organisations. The data is for supporting commissioning decisions, such as identifying out-of-hospital services, care gaps and the value of community nursing. The aim is better use of resources and improved patient care. Reported results include a £500,000 rise in NHS investment in nurse prescribing training, and 76 more patients identified for atrial fibrillation registers in Haringey.

DARS-NIC-147156-5PPWY.summary: University Hospital Southampton NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers the use of NHS registration data and Office for National Statistics (ONS) mortality data for medical research. The data is for the REM-HF study, which compares care guided by weekly remote monitoring from implanted devices with usual care for people with severe chronic heart failure. The study aims to assess clinical and cost-effectiveness, and patient and carer satisfaction.

DARS-NIC-147204-CGWY5.summary: Barts and the London NHS Trusts and Queen Mary University of London's agreement allows the use of NHS registration data and Office for National Statistics mortality data for medical research. The agreement is for building a sample of all patients with diabetes in the Diabetes Research Network regions. With consenting patients' DNA and clinical information, the research is to look for interactions between genes and environment in the development of Type 1, Type 2 and other forms of diabetes, and their complications.

DARS-NIC-147740-G203C.summary: Oxford University Hospitals NHS Trust (John Radcliffe Hospital)'s agreement covers the use of NHS registration data along with Office for National Statistics (ONS) cancer and mortality data. The data is for comparing the short-term risks of a procedure (heart attack, stroke and death) and its long-term effect on preventing stroke, especially disabling or fatal stroke. It also allows comparison of procedure and stroke-related healthcare costs and evaluation of quality of life.

DARS-NIC-147743-W4JNH.summary: The Wolfson Institute of Preventive Medicine's agreement covers receipt of NHS registration data, cancer and mortality data from the Office for National Statistics, Scottish events data, and Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) cause of death and cohort event notification reports. The data is for only one approved medical research project, MR170 Women with Benign Breast Disease. The release register does not state an expected benefit or any benefits reported so far.

DARS-NIC-147745-KFJ4K.summary: Newcastle University receives data from the Medical Research Information Service (MRIS), specifically a Cohort Event Notification Report. The release register says the data will be used only for an approved medical research project, but it does not name the project or describe what it involves. No intended benefits or outputs are stated.

DARS-NIC-147747-KRTQ8.summary: Queen Mary University of London's agreement covers identifiable cancer registration, death registration, demographic and cohort follow-up records for about 2.7 million women eligible for NHS breast screening invitations between 1988 and 1994. The agreement allows evaluation of how the NHS Breast Screening Programme affects breast cancer deaths and overdiagnosis. The aim is to give decision makers precise estimates to inform screening policy, such as age groups and intervals between screens. Earlier analysis of about 40% of the cohort has been published in two papers.

DARS-NIC-147748-XD18S.summary: The Institute of Cancer Research's agreement covers holding cancer registration, death registration and demographic data on people with insulin-treated diabetes, with secure storage and no other processing, so that updated analyses can be run in 2028 for a long-running national cohort study of cancer and mortality. The aim is better information on long-term health risks, to support patient advice, follow-up and screening. Papers from the study have already been used in international clinical guidelines on cholesterol disorders, heart disease and complications in children with diabetes.

DARS-NIC-147749-3SSRF.summary: The Institute of Cancer Research holds cancer registration, death and demographic records for about 27,000 patients with chromosome or childhood hormone disorders. The data is kept only for a long-running cohort study of cancer and death risks, with updated analyses planned for 2028. The aim is better information for patients, families and clinicians on long-term risks and follow-up. Published papers from the study have already been used in clinical practice guidelines.

DARS-NIC-147750-8GS7S.summary: The University of Cambridge's agreement covers mortality and demographic records for about 39,000 people screened for type 2 diabetes in the ADDITION study. It allows follow-up to see how screening, and early intensive treatment of risk factors, affect long-term death rates and cardiovascular risk. The aim is to inform NHS policy on whether population diabetes screening should be offered. So far, the study has produced over 80 published papers, and its findings have been cited in international screening guidelines.

DARS-NIC-147752-KRV7S.summary: The University of York's agreement covers the use of NHS registration data and Office for National Statistics (ONS) mortality data for medical research. The study tests whether collaborative care is effective and cost-effective at reducing symptoms of sub-threshold depression in older adults, compared with usual GP care alone. It also aims to validate the Whooley questions as a depression screening tool for this group, and to assess how acceptable collaborative care is. The release register says there is no clear evidence on treating this condition.

DARS-NIC-147755-C5H4X.summary: The University of Oxford's agreement covers the use of identifiable NHS hospital, emergency care, death and demographic records to follow up patients in the Arterial Revascularisation Trial (ART) for 15 years. The trial compares bilateral with single internal thoracic artery grafting in coronary artery bypass surgery. The aim is to provide long-term evidence on survival and cardiovascular events to guide the best treatment. Earlier results were published in the New England Journal of Medicine in 2019, and a cost-effectiveness analysis followed in 2022.

DARS-NIC-147756-SMGHS.summary: Nuvia Ltd, a commercial organisation, is permitted under the agreement to use mortality and cancer follow-up data on about 22,000 people employed at the Atomic Weapons Establishment between 1951 and 1982. The data is for studying the health effects of low-dose occupational radiation exposure, with the aim of informing the regulation of exposure limits. A 2017 published paper has already reported a significant effect of inhaled plutonium and uranium on lung cancer rates.

DARS-NIC-147757-8SVGP.summary: The University of Oxford's agreement covers NHS England hospital, emergency care, death, cancer registration, demographic, prescribing and diabetes audit data on UK participants in the REVEAL trial of the cholesterol-modifying drug anacetrapib. It allows follow-up to be extended for at least 15 years to study long-term effects on cardiovascular events, deaths, cancers and other serious adverse events. The aim is to improve understanding of treatments for vascular disease. The main trial has already shown a 9% reduction in major coronary events.

DARS-NIC-147762-6F2WZ.summary: The University of Aberdeen receives NHS registration, mortality and Scottish event data, including cause of death and cohort event notification reports from the Medical Research Information Service (MRIS). The data is used only for an approved medical research project, the RCGP Myocardial Infarction Study. The release register does not state an intended benefit or any benefits reported so far.

DARS-NIC-147770-1WNFL.summary: Picker Institute Europe's agreement covers NHS registration data, mortality data from the Office for National Statistics (ONS) and a Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) list cleaning report. The data is for filling in missing NHS numbers, recording whether people have died and finding the latest addresses of those still living. This updates contact details before a supplier sends out questionnaires before and after operations. The release register says this is not a medical research study.

DARS-NIC-147773-9G6ZN.summary: The University of Bristol's agreement covers NHS registration, cancer, mortality and cause of death data, including Scottish records and Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) reports. The data is for evaluating the effectiveness and cost-effectiveness of population-based prostate cancer screening, comparing men who were screened with men who were not. The intended benefit is policy-relevant evidence on the potential impact of screening on the UK population.

DARS-NIC-147773-N7Z6P.summary: NHS Fylde and Wyre Clinical Commissioning Group (CCG) receives hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other health service data, some identifiable by NHS number for risk stratification and some pseudonymised. It uses the data to identify patients at high risk of needing care, and to plan, monitor and redesign local health services. The main intended benefit is better-planned, more effective services, including fewer avoidable emergency admissions.
DARS-NIC-147773-N7Z6P.retense_draft: NHS Fylde and Wyre Clinical Commissioning Group's agreement covers receiving hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other health service data, some identifiable by NHS number for risk stratification and some pseudonymised. The data is for identifying patients at high risk of needing care, and for planning, monitoring and redesigning local health services. The main intended benefit is better-planned, more effective services, including fewer avoidable emergency admissions.

DARS-NIC-147774-MZT95.summary: The University of Manchester's agreement covers the use of cancer registration, death and demographic data to add to its study of children with rheumatic diseases, such as juvenile idiopathic arthritis, who take biologic therapies. It allows this data to be combined with study data to check whether these drugs raise the long-term risk of cancer or early death. The aim is to help choose the best treatments in future. Study data has already been cited in a 2015 NHS England commissioning policy, which led to more consistent prescribing.

DARS-NIC-147776-69CX7.summary: The University of Manchester's agreement covers mortality and cohort tracking records (from the Medical Research Information Service) for adults with myositis who took part in the UKMYONET study and agreed to data linkage. The research looks at which cancers these people develop, why, and their causes of death. It aims to support evidence-based cancer screening recommendations for earlier detection. Published papers and conference abstracts have already informed the 2023 international cancer screening guideline.

DARS-NIC-147777-8LD11.summary: Ctsu is using NHS registration data, Office for National Statistics mortality data and Scottish events data for medical research. The study aims to assess how strongly known and proposed risk factors are related to deaths from specific causes and to cancer illness, and how risk factors interact with each other. The release register does not state an intended benefit.

DARS-NIC-147782-0D7TX.summary: The University of Oxford's agreement covers hospital admission records and mortality and status information from NHS England for 1,759 surviving participants in the SHARP trial, a large study of people with chronic kidney disease. The data is for analysing the longer-term effects of a cholesterol-lowering combination tablet (simvastatin plus ezetimibe). The aim is to clarify long-term effects, which could inform kidney treatment guidelines and clinical care.

DARS-NIC-147783-6T2MW.summary: The University of Nottingham, an academic organisation, holds Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) records on causes of death, cohort events, flagging status and cohort membership for the Gedling Lung Health Study. The agreement allows secure retention only, with no other processing, while a later extension is prepared. The cohort studies how diet and other factors affect lung disease, cancer and survival. Reported benefits include at least 10 peer-reviewed papers, student dissertations and 3 local dietary intervention trials.

DARS-NIC-147788-X0G5L.summary: University Hospitals of Derby and Burton NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers the use of hospital admission records and death and cause of death information for people with stage 3 chronic kidney disease who were recruited from GP surgeries. The agreement allows the study of their survival, cardiovascular events and acute kidney injury, aiming to inform national guidance on managing the condition in primary care. The study has already produced peer-reviewed papers, including a five-year outcomes paper in PLOS Medicine in 2016.

DARS-NIC-147793-R05H3.summary: University College London (UCL)'s agreement covers the use of personal demographics and Scottish NHS registration data from the Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) for the INFANT study. The study tests whether intelligent decision-support software can help staff interpret heart rate monitoring (cardiotocograph, or CTG) during labour and improve how labour is managed. It also looks at whether using the software affects the longer-term neurodevelopment of children born to women in the study.

DARS-NIC-147794-JDPT1.summary: Public Health England's agreement covers the use of Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) data, including cause of death, cohort event notification, flagging status and personal demographics records. The data relates to patients admitted to Addenbrooke's Hospital between 2005 and 2007, some with Clostridium difficile infection and some without. The aim is a survival analysis to determine whether C. difficile infection is associated with excess deaths from all causes.

DARS-NIC-147797-45YHZ.summary: The University of Birmingham is using NHS mortality and cancer registration data (from the Medical Research Information Service, MRIS), including cause of death and demographic records. It is building a database of about 170,000 to 200,000 people in England and Wales who were diagnosed with cancer aged 15 to 39 between 1971 and 2006 and survived at least five years. The database will be used to study risks of specific causes of death, later cancers and other health conditions, and to assess evidence for cure. It aims to identify groups of survivors at much higher risk of poor health outcomes.
DARS-NIC-147797-45YHZ.retense_draft: The University of Birmingham's agreement covers NHS mortality and cancer registration data (from the Medical Research Information Service, MRIS), including cause of death and demographic records. The agreement allows building a database of about 170,000 to 200,000 people in England and Wales who were diagnosed with cancer aged 15 to 39 between 1971 and 2006 and survived at least five years. The data is for studying risks of specific causes of death, later cancers and other health conditions, and for assessing evidence for cure. It aims to identify groups of survivors at much higher risk of poor health outcomes.

DARS-NIC-147800-19WWQ.summary: The University of Oxford's agreement covers NHS registration data, Office for National Statistics (ONS) cancer and mortality data, and Scottish events data. The agreement allows an audit of whether the age at which women are first invited for a routine mammogram through the NHS Breast Screening Programme affects deaths from breast cancer. The findings are intended to inform screening policy and practice, and could help reduce the risk of dying from breast cancer.

DARS-NIC-147805-HDHWM.summary: University of Warwick's agreement covers pseudonymised NHS England mortality and cohort records for 75,143 people who worked in the UK electricity supply industry between 1973 and 1982. The agreement allows the data to be used to monitor long-term health among these workers, including any effects of exposure to extremely low frequency electric and magnetic fields. The aim is to inform bodies such as the Health and Safety Executive in setting exposure levels. Study findings have been published in peer-reviewed journals, including papers in 2019 and 2022.

DARS-NIC-147806-M11MB.summary: The University of Bristol's agreement allows it to use mortality records and related personal and registration data from the Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) to evaluate the Integrated Drug Treatment System in English prisons. The study compares deaths, engagement with community drug services and re-offending between 10,000 people released from prison on opiate substitution treatment and 10,000 released after detoxification. It aims to show how effective increased use of opiate substitution treatment is at reducing overdose deaths and disengagement from services after release.

DARS-NIC-147808-3F9FR.summary: The University of Oxford's agreement covers NHS registration, cancer, mortality and Scottish events data, including cause of death and cohort event notification reports. The data is for relating deaths from a wide range of specific diseases, and the incidence of cancer, to smoking habits. The agreement also allows characterising the effects of stopping smoking.

DARS-NIC-147809-M6YZK.summary: The University of Birmingham's agreement covers the use of personal demographics data from the Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) for the ASTRAL trial. The trial looks at whether opening narrowed kidney arteries with balloon angioplasty or stents can safely prevent worsening kidney failure in people with atherosclerotic renovascular disease. The text does not state a specific intended benefit.

DARS-NIC-147809-X5N8G.summary: Manchester City Council's agreement covers civil registration data on births and deaths, plus primary care mortality data, including identifiable details. The agreement allows the data to be used to understand local health needs, plan services, and support work such as suicide prevention, with only aggregated figures published. The intended benefit is local services better targeted to reduce premature deaths and health inequalities. Reported results include use of the data in the Manchester Reducing Infant Mortality Strategy and the Manchester Suicide Prevention Plan.

DARS-NIC-147810-M4Q9X.summary: NHS Greater Preston CCG's agreement covers hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other health service data. Some of the data is identifiable by NHS number for risk stratification, and the rest is pseudonymised for commissioning. The data is for identifying patients at high risk of needing care and for planning, monitoring and redesigning local health services. The main intended benefit is better planning and more effective commissioning, including fewer avoidable emergency admissions.

DARS-NIC-147811-YTH88.summary: The University of Manchester, an academic organisation, holds mortality data from NHS England's Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) reports, including cause of death and cohort event notifications. The data was originally supplied for the Norfolk Arthritis Register, a long-term community study of inflammatory arthritis. This agreement only allows the data to be stored securely for an interim period, with no other use and no new outputs.

DARS-NIC-147812-77TZR.summary: The University of Birmingham's agreement covers the use of NHS registration data, Office for National Statistics mortality data, and cause of death and cohort event notification reports. The data is for a randomised controlled trial comparing extended warfarin treatment with routine warfarin treatment in patients treated for a first unprovoked venous thromboembolism (VTE). The trial aims to prevent recurrent clots and post thrombotic syndrome, and to identify which patients are at highest risk.

DARS-NIC-147813-6PGDT.summary: The University of Oxford's agreement covers NHS registration, cancer, mortality and Scottish event data held for medical research. The research aims to obtain reliable information on the risk of breast cancer linked to hormone replacement therapy (HRT). The release register notes that about a third of women aged 50-64 in Britain use HRT, so even a small increase in risk would affect many women.

DARS-NIC-147814-86GS4.summary: The University of Bristol's agreement covers identifiable NHS England Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) records on causes of death, cohort events and current status for men in the Speedwell heart disease study. The agreement allows the data to be used to follow the men's health and deaths over time and to study the causes of heart disease and other chronic illnesses. The aim is to improve understanding of risk factors and prevention. A published risk prediction algorithm, SCORE2, has already come from related collaborative work.

DARS-NIC-147815-X5CHM.summary: NHS Blood and Transplant, a special health authority of the NHS, holds mortality data from the Medical Research Information Service (MRIS), covering cause of death, cohort event notification, flagging status and members and postings. The agreement only lets it keep this data securely for an interim period, with no other use, while it prepares a new application. The original study used the data to check that dates and causes of death on the UK Transplant Registry are accurate, to support organ allocation.

DARS-NIC-147817-KPFRY.summary: University College London (UCL)'s agreement covers NHS registration data, cancer data, and mortality and cause of death data, including cohort event notifications and Scottish registration records. The data is for informing a decision about introducing population screening for ovarian cancer. The work looks at screening's effect on ovarian cancer deaths, the best screening strategy, and the physical, psychological and health economic implications.

DARS-NIC-147821-BZG4L.summary: St George's Hospital Medical School's agreement covers Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) reports on cause of death, cohort event notifications, and members and postings. The data is for a study that aims to update information on survival and causes of death, and on the health of survivors, including hospital admissions and independence in daily living. The study also aims to give participants an opportunity to discuss problems.

DARS-NIC-147825-S6P8G.summary: NHS Morecambe Bay CCG (Clinical Commissioning Group)'s agreement covers hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other NHS service data, some of it linked to GP data. The data is for risk stratification, which predicts which patients are at high risk, and to support planning and commissioning of local health services. Midlands and Lancashire Commissioning Support Unit carries out the work. The main intended benefit is better planned services and earlier, more targeted care, leading to fewer avoidable emergency admissions.

DARS-NIC-147827-NC2TC.summary: Imperial College London's agreement covers linking NHS England mortality records (the Medical Research Information Service) and National Disease Registration Service cancer registrations to hospital colonoscopy data. The data is for studying how often patients with low-, intermediate- and high-risk bowel adenomas need follow-up colonoscopies, to show who can safely avoid surveillance. The results contributed evidence to the 2020 UK surveillance guidelines and were published in journals including Gut.

DARS-NIC-147829-5K4QP.summary: The University of Cambridge, an academic body, is permitted to use death records, demographic data and mortality-related reports for people in the long-running Cognitive Function and Ageing Study (CFAS) and the ALPHA study of older people. The data is for confirming dates and causes of death, so that survival and life expectancy can be estimated in people with cognitive impairment. This supports dementia planning. Published findings on dementia prevalence and incidence have already been used by NHS England for GP dementia targets.

DARS-NIC-147830-XVK36.summary: The Royal Marsden NHS Foundation Trust receives data from the Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) and other sources, covering cohort event notifications, NHS registration, cancer, mortality and Scottish events. The release register says the data will be used only for an approved medical research project, and it gives no further detail about that project. No intended benefit is stated.

DARS-NIC-147833-FGBLJ.summary: Western General Hospital's agreement covers NHS registration data, cause of death reports and cohort event notifications from the Medical Research Information Service (MRIS), along with Office for National Statistics mortality data. The data is for a study that began in 2000 and follows patients at six months, eighteen months and then yearly. Its main outcome is death and dependency. The release register does not clearly state an intended benefit.

DARS-NIC-147834-LHQ2R.summary: Nuvia Ltd's agreement covers the use of mortality and cohort records from the Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) for the long-running MR110 study of UK Atomic Energy Authority employees. The study examines deaths and cancer in the workforce to understand the health effects of low-dose occupational radiation exposure, helping inform exposure limits in regulations. A 2017 paper from the study reported a significant effect of inhaled plutonium and uranium on lung cancer rates.

DARS-NIC-147835-C8J9S.summary: NHS Coventry and Rugby CCG (Clinical Commissioning Group)'s agreement covers pseudonymised hospital, community, ambulance, mental health and other local provider data, including clinical and financial information. The agreement allows the data to be analysed, with processing by a commissioning support unit, to plan and commission health services for the local population. The main intended benefit is better planning of services and patient flow, with improved quality and access to care.

DARS-NIC-147835-GSMX5.summary: The University of Aberdeen receives Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) reports on cause of death and cohort event notifications. The release register does not describe the people covered by the data. The university will use them only for an approved medical research project, the Oestrogen in the Prevention of the Re-Infarction Trial (ESPIRIT). The release register does not state an intended benefit or any benefits reported so far.

DARS-NIC-147837-RJMRN.summary: The University of Bristol's agreement covers mortality and cancer records, linked to school growth records, questionnaires and blood samples, for a study of former Christ's Hospital School pupils born between 1927 and 1956. The data is for testing whether growth and puberty timing are linked to later conditions such as cancer and heart disease. The aim is to improve understanding of how childhood development affects chronic disease risk. Reported findings include that earlier puberty is associated with higher IGF-I levels, a hormone linked to cancer risk.

DARS-NIC-147838-RCVPF.summary: Leeds General Infirmary's agreement covers the use of NHS registration data and Office for National Statistics mortality data for medical research. The data is for re-auditing the care of patients with acute myocardial infarction and acute coronary syndrome. It will also evaluate and compare how well different cardiac troponin assays predict and relate to patients' clinical outcomes.

DARS-NIC-147839-Y4RRC.summary: The Health and Safety Executive's agreement allows it to receive NHS Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) data, including cause of death, cohort event notifications, flagging status, demographics and Scottish registration records. The data is for maintaining its Mesothelioma and Asbestosis Registers and producing statistics on how common these diseases are. The aim is to inform workplace asbestos control policy and to model future mesothelioma deaths in Great Britain.

DARS-NIC-147840-N7W5C.summary: NHS Blackburn with Darwen Clinical Commissioning Group (CCG)'s agreement covers hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other health service data, some identifiable by NHS number and some pseudonymised. The data is for risk stratification, which identifies patients at high risk so their care can be prioritised, and for supporting planning and commissioning of local health services. Midlands and Lancashire Commissioning Support Unit carries out the processing. The main intended benefit is better planning and more targeted care, including fewer avoidable emergency admissions.

DARS-NIC-147841-1G36R.summary: Royal Free London NHS Foundation Trust's agreement allows it to receive Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) records, including cause of death, current status and demographic details, for patients with amyloidosis. The data is for establishing cause of death and prognosis, and for seeing how treatments affect survival. Being kept up to date on deaths also means staff can avoid distressing relatives by chasing follow-up for patients who have died.

DARS-NIC-147842-NL26D.summary: Sheffield Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust receives Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) reports on cause of death, cohort event notifications, flagging of current status and Scottish NHS registration. The release register says the data will be used only for an approved medical research project, numbered MR777. It does not state the research topic, the expected benefits or any benefits achieved so far.

DARS-NIC-147843-8NKTW.summary: City St George's, University of London's agreement covers cancer registration, death record, demographic and flagging data about people who joined a screening trial between 1997 and 2006. The study tests whether screening for H. pylori infection and treating it reduces the later risk of stomach cancer. The main intended benefit is evidence on whether population screening would prevent stomach cancers.

DARS-NIC-147847-P6MMR.summary: King's College London's Centre for Military Health Research's agreement covers the use of cancer registration, death registration, demographic and military cohort tracking data on UK Armed Forces personnel who served in Bosnia between 1992 and 1996. The data is for studying whether their rates of cancer and death are higher than expected. The main intended benefit is evidence that could either reassure veterans or lead to earlier diagnosis and better protection from harmful exposures.

DARS-NIC-147849-L7T7N.summary: NHS West Lancashire CCG's agreement covers hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other health service data, some identifiable by NHS number and some pseudonymised. The data is for risk stratification, which identifies patients at high risk of needing more care, and for supporting planning and commissioning of local health services. The main intended benefit is better-targeted care and more effective commissioning, including fewer avoidable emergency admissions.

DARS-NIC-147850-1BWPG.summary: Leeds Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust's agreement covers NHS registration and mortality data, including cause of death reports, cohort event notifications and Scottish NHS registration data, supplied through the Medical Research Information Service (MRIS). The data is for an approved medical research project at Leeds General Infirmary, called "The Value of H-FABP in Early Diagnosis and Risk Stratification of Patients". The release register does not state a specific intended benefit.

DARS-NIC-147852-RV70L.summary: The University of Newcastle upon Tyne's agreement covers cancer registration, death registration and MRIS (Medical Research Information Service) cohort tracking data. The data is for studying whether radiation from CT scans and heart procedures in childhood affects later cancer risk. The aim is to inform guidance on safer scanning of children. Published results have already led some clinical groups to change practice, and most children's hospitals now have dedicated paediatric CT protocols.

DARS-NIC-147854-S4S6V.summary: NHS Blackpool CCG's agreement covers hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other health service data, some identifiable by NHS number for risk stratification and otherwise pseudonymised.
