The data is for predicting which patients are at high risk and for planning and commissioning health services for its local population. The main intended benefit is better-planned services and earlier help, such as fewer avoidable emergency admissions.

DARS-NIC-147858-KGYSS.summary: Saving Faces - The Facial Surgery Research Foundation, a charity, is permitted under its agreement to use identifiable NHS England death registration, cancer and demographic data for 609 consenting patients in its SEND trial. The research tests whether removing neck lymph glands as a precaution (elective neck dissection) improves survival and cancer control in early mouth cancer. It aims to help patients and clinicians choose treatments using high-quality evidence. A published paper has already been cited in international guidelines and by other researchers, and has been linked to a change in surgical practice.

DARS-NIC-147860-0RSHN.summary: University College London's Centre for Longitudinal Studies agreement covers civil registration death records, demographic details and Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) mortality reports for about 19,000 members of the Millennium Cohort Study. The data is for updating contact details, avoiding contact with people who have died or emigrated, and studying causes of death, with sub-licensed access for wider research. Published MCS research has shown, for example, how breastfeeding and smoking in pregnancy relate to children's health, and has reported rates of teenage depression and obesity.

DARS-NIC-147863-CCGZN.summary: Royal Devon University Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers the use of death registration, demographic and cause-of-death data to follow up participants in the Diabetes Alliance for Research in England (DARE) study in the Exeter region. The data is for studying how diabetes develops and leads to complications, including mortality. It also keeps participant records accurate so the Trust does not contact families of people who have died. So far, DARE data helped develop a urine test for insulin production, and mortality data fed a published study on arm blood pressure differences.

DARS-NIC-147867-D8128.summary: The University of Aberdeen's agreement covers the use of cancer registration, death and demographic data to continue following women in the Royal College of General Practitioners' Oral Contraception Study, which began in 1968. The aim is to understand the long-term health effects of oral contraceptives, including on mortality and cancer, so the public can be given informed advice on their safety. The study has produced over 100 publications and has informed national and international clinical guidelines on prescribing combined oral contraceptives.

DARS-NIC-147874-HVBFB.summary: University of Cambridge's agreement covers NHS registration, death (mortality) and Scottish event data, supplied through the Medical Research Information Service (MRIS). The release register says the data will be used only for an approved medical research project, numbered MR490. It does not describe the project's subject, expected outputs or benefits.

DARS-NIC-147875-00SJY.summary: The Institute of Child Health's agreement covers holding mortality and cancer data, supplied through the Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) reports, about around 1,800 people treated with pituitary-derived growth hormone between 1959 and 1985. The agreement allows secure retention only, while a longer-term application may be prepared. The wider study is for tracking deaths and illness in this group to monitor the risk of Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease (CJD) and to support public health advice. Reported results included showing that the CJD incubation period exceeds 37 years.

DARS-NIC-147876-YSQFX.summary: Public Health England's agreement covers the use of Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) data, including cause of death, cohort event notification, flagging status and demographic records, for a register of healthcare and laboratory workers who have reported occupational exposure to CJD and other transmissible spongiform encephalopathies (TSEs). The register will standardise reporting, hold the information in a central database and allow long-term follow-up to monitor the risk of CJD in these workers. It is intended to help develop guidance for healthcare and laboratory workers.

DARS-NIC-147877-QXH0L.summary: West Hertfordshire Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust's agreement covers Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) data, including cause of death, cohort event notification, current status and demographic records. The data is for a long-term observational study of how patients with early rheumatoid arthritis are treated and how they fare across the UK. The study aims to build a database that could contribute to good clinical practice, guidelines and clinical governance, and help design further studies.

DARS-NIC-147880-8R2YM.summary: Imperial College London's agreement covers the use of NHS registration data, Office for National Statistics (ONS) mortality data and Scottish events data for medical research. The data is for the Endo-Vascular Aneurysm Repair (EVAR) trials, which assess how effective EVAR is in treating Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm. EVAR1 compares EVAR with open repair in patients fit for both, and EVAR2 compares EVAR plus best medical treatment alone in patients unfit for open repair.

DARS-NIC-147884-R7CBN.summary: The University of York's agreement covers linking hospital, cancer registration, death and demographic records to study the long-term health of people diagnosed with cancer as children, compared with people of the same age and sex who were not. It aims to examine hospital activity, reasons for admission and survival, to inform future healthcare planning. The study has already published papers on health outcomes of childhood leukaemia survivors and on the follow-up study's design.

DARS-NIC-147885-0TV66.summary: The University of Oxford's agreement covers the use of identifiable hospital, mental health, cancer registration and death records to follow up people who took part in the HPS2-THRIVE cholesterol trial. The data is for studying the long-term effects of lowering LDL cholesterol on health, including dementia, so patients and guideline bodies can better judge medicines. Reported results include the trial's findings that niacin/laropiprant brought no significant reduction in major vascular events, and its withdrawal from the European market.

DARS-NIC-147887-RJFZH.summary: Cardiff University School of Medicine holds pseudonymised death records, obtained through the Medical Research Information Service, for about 200 people in the SCOPE 1 oesophageal cancer trial. It keeps them so the trial analysis can be recreated and audited if needed. The trial tested adding cetuximab (Erbitux) to chemoradiotherapy. Findings from the trial have been published in journal papers, and it stopped recruiting in 2012 after cetuximab seemed unlikely to improve outcomes, so funds were reallocated.

DARS-NIC-147891-6J5NJ.summary: University College London's agreement covers the use of NHS registration data, plus Office for National Statistics (ONS) cancer and mortality data, for medical research on ovarian cancer. The study aims to identify genetic and epidemiological factors linked to higher risk of the disease. It also aims to find new biomarkers for early diagnosis, prognosis and monitoring of recurrence, and to explore whether recognising symptoms early could speed up diagnosis.

DARS-NIC-147893-ZFLWG.summary: The Society of Endocrinology's agreement covers the use of Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) reports on cause of death, cohort event notifications, and members and postings for the UK Acromegaly Database. The agreement allows study of long-term deaths and illness in people with acromegaly, a rare hormone condition, and of how different treatments affect them. The intended benefit is better day-to-day management of patients and centres auditing their practice. Reported findings include studies showing Gamma knife radiosurgery and conventional pituitary radiotherapy to be safe and effective, and surgeon experience to be important for surgical success.

DARS-NIC-147897-P4L75.summary: Cause Action Ltd receives Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) reports on cause of death, cohort event notification and Scottish NHS registration. It also receives NHS registration data and Office for National Statistics (ONS) cancer and mortality data. The release register says the data is to be used only for the approved medical research project MR188. It does not state an intended benefit or any benefits reported so far.

DARS-NIC-147900-4704M.summary: The Hillingdon Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust's agreement allows use of NHS registration data and Office for National Statistics (ONS) mortality data for medical research. The data is for comparing the effectiveness and safety of cabogen and nicotinamide combined with radical radiotherapy against radiotherapy alone in locally advanced bladder cancer. The release register does not state an intended benefit.

DARS-NIC-147901-2XMLG.summary: Bristol NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers the use of cancer registration, death and demographic records, plus cohort tracking reports, for the Head and Neck 5000 study, which follows 5,511 people diagnosed with head and neck cancer. The data support a 10-year follow-up, comparing outcomes and identifying factors that predict survival and long-term side effects. The aim is to improve outcomes and care for patients. The study has published peer-reviewed papers and contributed to the largest genetic study of head and neck cancer risk to date.

DARS-NIC-147905-V7Q0D.summary: NHS Chorley and South Ribble CCG's agreement covers hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other NHS activity data, some identifiable by NHS number for risk stratification and the rest pseudonymised. The data is for identifying patients at high risk of needing care, and for planning, monitoring and redesigning local health services, with Midlands and Lancashire Commissioning Support Unit doing the processing. The main intended benefit is better-targeted care and commissioning, including fewer avoidable emergency admissions.

DARS-NIC-147905-Y4P68.summary: St James University Hospital NHS Trust's agreement covers NHS registration, cancer, mortality and Scottish event data, including cause of death and cohort event notification reports from the Medical Research Information Service (MRIS). The data is for one approved medical research project, called MR1018 Melamona Follow-up and Case-Control Family Study. The release register does not state an intended benefit or any benefits reported so far.

DARS-NIC-147907-MLK7R.summary: Derbyshire Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers hospital records of people who attended the Royal Derby Hospital Emergency Department after self-harm, linked with death registration and cause of death data. The data is for monitoring self-harm and identifying risk factors for early death, including suicide, so that care and suicide prevention strategies rest on better evidence. The register reports that the findings supported the commissioning of a 24/7 Liaison Psychiatry service at the hospital and a liaison team for under 18s.

DARS-NIC-147908-CPCPG.summary: The University of Leeds holds mortality and cohort tracking reports for people in the CE-MARC study, which tested cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) scans for suspected coronary heart disease. This agreement lets the university keep data already received while it prepares a further application. The study's long-term follow-up aims to show whether CMR predicts later heart problems better than SPECT. Reported results include papers in the Lancet and Annals of Internal Medicine, and the study is said to be changing how suspected angina is investigated.

DARS-NIC-147910-HHGGZ.summary: The University of Oxford's agreement covers identifiable cancer registration, death registration and demographic data for about 7,000 women treated for subfertility in Oxfordshire and West Berkshire between 1970 and 1990. The agreement allows the study of their long-term cancer and mortality risks, and of the characteristics of the babies they conceived. The aim is to give policy-makers, doctors and patients better evidence on the long-term effects of fertility treatments, some still in use today. A draft paper has been produced, but it has not yet been submitted.

DARS-NIC-147912-5CDTL.summary: Gloucestershire Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers the use of Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) records, including cause of death, cancer event notifications, current status and demographic information, for a randomised trial of people with Barrett's Oesophagus. The trial tests whether offering an endoscopy every two years improves overall survival compared with endoscopy only when symptoms arise. Participants are followed for 10 years. The trial aims to inform future NHS and international surveillance policy.

DARS-NIC-147916-DPQ3Q.summary: The University of Manchester's agreement covers death registration and demographic data, including mortality records, linked to hospital self-harm records. The agreement allows the data to be used to study the risk of suicide and early death after self-harm and to identify groups at higher risk. The aim is to inform suicide prevention strategies and the allocation of healthcare resources. Its findings have already been reported as informing NICE self-harm guidelines and national suicide prevention policy.

DARS-NIC-147922-T7W2F.summary: University College London's Centre for Longitudinal Studies agreement covers identifiable death registration and demographic data on about 18,500 members of the National Child Development Study 1958 cohort. The data is for updating participant records, studying mortality outcomes and supporting further research. The aim is to inform health policy and healthy ageing. Death notifications have already stopped the study contacting relatives of people who had died, and research has fed into government briefing papers.

DARS-NIC-147923-P5DTX.summary: The Institute of Cancer Research holds cancer registration, death record, demographic and NHS-linked tracking data for a national study of cancer in twins. This agreement only allows the data to be stored securely until updated analyses in 2028. The aim is to give patients, families and clinicians better information about cancer risks. Published papers from the study have already added to scientific knowledge about the causes of some cancers.

DARS-NIC-147924-YHQZR.summary: The Medical School at Newcastle upon Tyne, working through its Institute for Ageing and Health, has an agreement that allows it to use Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) cause of death and cohort event notification reports, plus NHS registration and Office for National Statistics mortality data. The data is for one approved medical research project, MR802. The release register does not state the expected outputs or benefits, and no benefits have been reported so far.

DARS-NIC-147927-8K193.summary: The University of Birmingham's agreement covers hospital, cancer registration, death and related records for people with Parkinson's disease who took part in the PD MED trial. The data is for a 20-year analysis of which classes of Parkinson's medicine work best and are most cost-effective, including effects on care home admission and survival. The aim is to guide which medicines clinicians use. Earlier trial results were published in the Lancet and led to a 2017 NICE guideline update on treating early Parkinson's.

DARS-NIC-147929-T9S0W.summary: NHS East Lancashire CCG's agreement covers hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other health service data, including patient-level data that is identifiable or pseudonymised. The data is for risk stratification, which identifies patients at high risk so their care can be prioritised, and for planning and monitoring local health services. The main intended benefit is better planning and targeting of care, including fewer avoidable emergency admissions.

DARS-NIC-147931-DT25Y.summary: The University of Oxford's agreement covers identifiable NHS England data on cancer registrations, hospital admissions, deaths, cancer treatments and demographics for 4,553,604 women in the AgeX trial. The data is for assessing the benefits and harms of extra breast screening invitations at ages 47-49 and 71-73. The findings are intended to inform UK breast screening policy through the UK National Screening Committee.

DARS-NIC-147932-B9FG1.summary: The University of Birmingham's agreement covers the use of Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) data, including cause of death, cancer and current status records, for a study of rubber factory employees. The data is for describing deaths and cancer among recent entrants to the UK rubber industry. It will also check whether measures to reduce dust and fume exposure have removed the excess of lung and stomach cancer seen in recent years.

DARS-NIC-147936-1L3FD.summary: University College London (UCL) holds Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) records on deaths, cancer events and patient status for the HiLo thyroid cancer trial. This agreement lets UCL keep the data securely, with no other use, while it prepares a further application. The trial compared a low and a standard dose of radioiodine, and a later follow-up paper is planned. The trial's published results led to the low dose becoming standard care and being recommended in the 2014 British Thyroid Association guidelines.

DARS-NIC-147936-X6M4N.summary: NHS Lincolnshire ICB's agreement, for the former NHS Lincolnshire East CCG, covers the use of Secondary User Services (SUS+) data about hospital and other care activity, identifiable by NHS number, in a secure Controlled Environment for Finance. The data is for checking invoices from care providers, so that the CCG pays only for activity that is its responsibility. The main intended benefit is that providers are paid accurately and public money is used appropriately.

DARS-NIC-147940-WVXJF.summary: The University of Oxford holds identifiable NHS England data on deaths, cancer registrations and demographics for 1,405,340 women born in England or Wales between 1945 and 1948. It is used for a study of whether the age at which women are first invited for a routine breast screening mammogram affects their risk of dying from breast cancer. The findings are expected to inform national breast screening policy.

DARS-NIC-147941-XX4JP.summary: The University of Manchester's agreement covers linked cancer registrations, death records and hospital admissions data for the British Association of Dermatologists' register of people with psoriasis taking biologic treatments. The agreement allows the data to be used to track long-term safety, such as cancer, serious infections and death. The aim is to help clinicians and patients make better-informed treatment decisions. Published papers have already reported on drug survival, serious infection risk, cardiovascular events and skin cancer risk.

DARS-NIC-147942-N8J6Y.summary: NHS Lincolnshire ICB's agreement covers use of Secondary Uses Service (SUS+) data, which can be identified by NHS number, for commissioners. The agreement allows Liaison Financial Services to check invoices and review past payments for Continuing Healthcare, looking for overpayments and working with providers to recover the money. The main intended benefit is finding and recovering money that would otherwise be lost, while keeping control of the budget.

DARS-NIC-147943-C4Q5L.summary: NHS South Warwickshire CCG's agreement covers the use of pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, ambulance and other health service activity and financial data, with processing carried out by NHS Midlands and Lancashire Commissioning Support Unit. The agreement allows the CCG to plan and commission health services for its local population, including analysing needs, redesigning services and identifying patients at risk of hospital admission. The main intended benefit is better planning of care and patient flow.

DARS-NIC-147944-KJQBS.summary: Imperial College London's agreement covers NHS Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) data, including cause of death, demographic and cohort tracking reports, for the European Community Respiratory Health Survey III, a long-running study of about 10,000 adults. The data is for tracing participants, sending them questionnaires, working out accurate response rates and describing deaths in the cohort. The study aims to show how respiratory symptoms, allergy and lung function change as adults age.

DARS-NIC-147947-CGW0Y.summary: The Dudley Group NHS Foundation Trust holds Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) records, including cause of death, cohort event notification, flagging status and membership reports. The agreement allows the Trust only to keep this data securely for an interim period while it prepares a later application to extend it. The original study aimed to identify risk factors for heart disease in people with rheumatoid arthritis. The data has already led to published papers, theses, changes to national and international guidelines, and patient education material.

DARS-NIC-147948-6MSGP.summary: University College London's agreement covers the keeping of cancer and death registry records, including cancer type, diagnosis date and cause of death, for people who took part in the Lung-SEARCH lung cancer screening trial. The data is for further analyses of the trial's results, which could inform a national lung cancer screening programme for people who smoke and have COPD. Trial findings have been published, including the main trial paper in the European Respiratory Journal.

DARS-NIC-147949-WJKL8.summary: Breast Test Wales's agreement covers NHS Registration, cancer, mortality and cause of death data, including Scottish events, from medical research and Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) datasets. The data is for studying whether annual mammograms reduce late-stage breast cancer and deaths in women aged 40-49 with a significant family history of breast cancer, who are below the national screening age. The release register says services are urgently needed to manage this group.

DARS-NIC-147951-GXRLZ.summary: The University of Manchester's agreement covers the use of NHS registration data and Office for National Statistics (ONS) mortality data for medical research. The main aim is to investigate the role of patient choice, from both patients' and surgeons' perspectives, in surgical treatment decisions for older women with breast cancer. It also aims to find which health measures best predict outcomes after surgery.

DARS-NIC-147953-SXCMS.summary: University College London's agreement with the Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) covers cause of death and cohort event notification reports. These cover patients at the Whittington Hospital and University College London Hospital who had major elective surgery. The data is for a service evaluation of how well cardiopulmonary exercise testing predicts death and illness after surgery, compared with other risk tools. The aim is to refine how well the test predicts surgical outcomes.

DARS-NIC-147955-M8D2Q.summary: King's College London's TwinsUK research registry is permitted under its agreement to link NHS hospital, cancer, death, emergency care and mental health records to its long-running study of twins. The agreement allows the data to be used to study how genes and environment affect health and disease over a lifetime, and to track outcomes more completely, including for people who find it hard to attend clinics. The aim is to improve disease prediction, diagnosis and prevention. Earlier linkage work identified clinical and genomic risk factors for cancers.

DARS-NIC-147957-4444C.summary: The University of Oxford's agreement covers hospital records of people who presented at Oxford's John Radcliffe Hospital after self-harm, linked to death registration and cause-of-death data. The data is for studying risk factors for death, including suicide, and how hospital care relates to it. The aim is to help design better services that reduce self-harm and early death. Its findings have already informed NICE guidelines and national suicide prevention strategies.

DARS-NIC-147970-M0H6Z.summary: NHS Leicester, Leicestershire and Rutland ICB's agreement covers the use of pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, ambulance, maternity and other health service data, containing clinical and financial information. The data is for planning and commissioning health services for the population across the Leicester, Leicestershire and Rutland partnership area. The main intended benefit is better-designed services and patient pathways, with improved access and quality.

DARS-NIC-147978-LZDFC.summary: Cambridge University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust's agreement allows the use of hospital admission, accident and emergency, death registration and demographic data to follow people in the ERICA study of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). The data is for examining how heart, muscle and inflammation markers relate to later hospital admissions and deaths. The aim is to identify biomarkers that help predict outcomes and support more personalised COPD treatments.

DARS-NIC-147982-J7KGV.summary: The University of Liverpool's agreement covers the use of NHS England hospital, cancer registration, death and demographic records for the Liverpool Lung Project, a long-running lung cancer study. The data is for building risk models and biomarkers that identify people at high risk of lung cancer, so that diagnosis can happen earlier and screening can be better targeted. The reported benefits include the risk model being used to select people for lung cancer screening, and over 160 research publications.

DARS-NIC-147993-QY3ZL.summary: The University of Manchester's agreement covers mortality and cohort event notification data from the Medical Research Information Service (MRIS), including Scottish registration data. The data is for a trial of whether atorvastatin (Lipitor) can reduce heart attacks and strokes in people with rheumatoid arthritis. The trial also looks at whether the drug lowers joint inflammation in people with significant disease activity when they join.

DARS-NIC-147997-R8B9S.summary: The University of Leeds's agreement covers hospital records for accident and emergency, admitted patient care and outpatient care. The data is for a research project funded by the National Institute for Health Research, called UK-SAFE. The project looks at when, which and how patients present for revision surgery after joint replacement. The aim is to give evidence-based recommendations on how and when follow-up care should happen, reducing unnecessary appointments and tests.

DARS-NIC-148002-B0M0Z.summary: NHS Wolverhampton CCG's agreement covers Secondary User Services (SUS) data for commissioners, which can be identified by NHS number. The data is for invoice validation, checking that care providers' invoices relate to patients the CCG is responsible for. NHS Arden and Greater East Midlands Commissioning Support Unit carries out the checks and advises on payment. The intended benefits include financial validation of activity and better budget control.

DARS-NIC-148011-GM4F9.summary: Royal Free & University College Medical School's agreement covers the use of NHS registration, Office for National Statistics (ONS) cancer and mortality data, and Scottish events data for medical research. The data is for a study of civil servants from different government departments who attended screening examinations. The study allows examination of mortality and illness in the Civil Service, and of how social mobility, psychosocial and other factors relate to continuing social inequalities.

DARS-NIC-148019-SZSC9.summary: University College London (UCL)'s agreement covers the use of NHS registration data, Office for National Statistics (ONS) cancer and mortality data, and Scottish events data for medical research. The research aims to develop an optimised ovarian cancer screening procedure for women at high risk because of strong family history or genetic predisposition. It also examines the physical harms, resource implications, feasibility and acceptability of screening, and covers building a serum bank for future research on tumour markers.

DARS-NIC-148021-GNMPC.summary: Newcastle University receives NHS registration data, Office for National Statistics mortality data, and Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) reports on cause of death and cohort event notifications. The release register says the data will be used only for an approved medical research project, referred to as MR87. It does not describe the project's aims, expected benefits or any benefits reported so far.

DARS-NIC-148022-1MQBH.summary: The University of Newcastle upon Tyne holds mortality and cancer registration data for the Newcastle Heart Project, a study of heart disease, diabetes and risk factors in White and South Asian adults in Newcastle. The agreement only allows the data to be kept for an interim period, with no other use. The aim is to update earlier analysis of how risk factors relate to mortality in the two groups, to help inform targeted health interventions. Earlier work has been published in 2017 in the Journal of Epidemiology and Community Health.

DARS-NIC-148023-KVWYZ.summary: Royal Brompton Hospital's agreement covers the use of Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) data, including cause of death, event notification, current status and demographic records, for a pilot trial in patients treated with primary PCI after a ST elevation heart attack. The agreement allows a registry of these patients to be built, comparing complete revascularisation with treating only the infarct-related artery in those who also have multi-vessel disease. Deaths and major cardiovascular events are to be tracked for up to 12 months.

DARS-NIC-148024-P8GSC.summary: The Ministry of Defence holds mortality data on UK Gulf War veterans from 1990-1991, covering cause of death, postings and status reports. Under this agreement it can only keep the data securely for an interim period, while it prepares a further application. The original study looked at whether veterans' death rates, including suicide, were higher than the UK population's. Earlier analysis produced annual National Statistics and found no excess in deaths among the Gulf cohort.

DARS-NIC-148030-Q5N4D.summary: The UK Haemophilia Centre Doctors' Organisation, a society, has an agreement covering identifiable death registration and cause-of-death data for people with haemophilia and other inherited bleeding disorders. The data is for keeping the National Haemophilia Database up to date and for studying causes of death and life expectancy. The aim is to show which treatments are most beneficial and cost effective. Its annual reports to NHS England, Scotland and Wales have supported national healthcare planning, and its findings helped justify prophylactic therapy.

DARS-NIC-148033-FMST7.summary: The University of Bristol's agreement covers cause of death, cohort event notification and Scottish NHS registration data from the Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) for the Avon Longitudinal Study of Parents and Children (ALSPAC), a long-running birth cohort study. The data is for research by the wider scientific community, in a secure, non-disclosive form. It also allows the study to avoid causing distress by contacting families after a bereavement, and supports tracing of participants.

DARS-NIC-148034-SCKLL.summary: Royal Free London NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers the use of Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) death and flagging reports linked to records held by the UK Barrett's Oesophagus Registry. The agreement allows the data to establish all causes of death among people with Barrett's oesophagus, a change in the cells lining the lower oesophagus. The intended benefit is better management of patients and prevention of progression to cancer. A 2012 paper in Endoscopy has already been published and used in British Society of Gastroenterology guidelines.

DARS-NIC-148035-41S3L.summary: The University of York's agreement covers mortality, cause of death and NHS registration data, including Scottish records, for medical research. It allows examination of how long patients on the Yorkshire Haematological Malignancy Network (YHHN) register survive, in relation to their diagnosis, prognosis and treatment. The register covers people newly diagnosed with blood cancers in part of Yorkshire and Northern Lincolnshire. The findings are expected to have implications for the whole country.

DARS-NIC-148038-Y7M6H.summary: NHS Lincolnshire West CCG's agreement covers Secondary User Services (SUS+) data for commissioners, which can be identified by NHS number. The agreement allows the data to be used for invoice validation, checking that activity claimed by care providers is the CCG's responsibility to pay for. The main intended benefit is financial control, helping make sure public funds are spent properly.

DARS-NIC-148043-R1D0M.summary: NHS South Lincolnshire CCG's agreement covers Secondary User Services (SUS+) data for commissioners, which can be identified by NHS number. The data is for processing in a secure Controlled Environment for Finance, with Optum Health Solutions (UK) Ltd advising on payment. The data is for validating invoices from care providers, so the CCG can confirm that the activity claimed is its responsibility. The main intended benefit is financial validation of activity and budget control.

DARS-NIC-148044-RGS7W.summary: The University of Oxford's agreement, with University College London and the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine, covers pseudonymised cancer registration, death and demographic data on 19,019 London civil servants in the Whitehall Study. The data is for studying how lifestyle, social circumstances and cardiovascular risk factors relate to cancer and causes of death in old age. Reported benefits include results published in peer-reviewed journals and findings that have guided public health policy and clinical guidelines.

DARS-NIC-148050-WYFD5.summary: NHS Central Register Scotland receives registration, cancer, mortality and Scottish events data. These come from datasets including NHS registration data, Office for National Statistics (ONS) cancer data and ONS mortality data. The stated purpose is to provide data for Scottish research. The release register does not state an intended benefit or any benefits reported so far.

DARS-NIC-148056-T6T5Z.summary: Imperial College London's agreement covers linked NHS England data, including hospital, mental health, cancer, death, COVID-19 test and vaccination records, to follow the health of police force members in the Airwave Health Monitoring Study. It allows examination of whether use of the TETRA police radio system, and other lifestyle and workplace factors, affect their risk of cancer and other conditions. The main intended benefit is better evidence for health policy and for working conditions in police forces. The study has already supported over 80 publications.

DARS-NIC-148057-2763T.summary: The University of Leeds's agreement covers NHS registration data, death records from the Office for National Statistics and Scottish event data. These relate to children admitted to paediatric intensive care. The study looks at their longer-term outcomes after discharge, their causes of death on the unit and afterwards, and the overall burden of deaths from critical illness. It also examines these in relation to deprivation, ethnic group and location, to address health inequalities.

DARS-NIC-148059-8KY1S.summary: Gateshead Health NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) reports on cause of death, cohort event notifications, flagging of current status and Scottish NHS registration. The study looks at whether people with borderline (subclinical) hypothyroidism have a higher risk of cardiovascular disease and death over more than 30 years of follow-up. It also examines how borderline thyroid conditions develop over time, including outcomes for people with borderline hyperthyroidism.

DARS-NIC-148063-6YT63.summary: The University of Birmingham's agreement covers Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) data, including cause of death, cohort event notification, flagging status, membership and postings, and personal demographics reports. The data is for studying and improving the acute care of people with TIA (transient ischaemic attack) and stroke in Birmingham. The work aims to identify and reduce barriers to timely, effective treatment, so that patients reach specialist care sooner and care improves overall.

DARS-NIC-148066-2B6LS.summary: The Wolfson Institute of Preventive Medicine's agreement covers NHS registration, cause of death, mortality and cohort event data, including Scottish events, for a heart research study. The study tests whether also widening other significantly narrowed heart arteries, when treating the artery blocked in a heart attack, reduces coronary death, further heart attacks and severe chest pain. It also looks at safety, cost to the NHS and quality of life.

DARS-NIC-148069-ZB4GM.summary: The University of Oxford's agreement covers hospital records, cancer registrations, death records and mental health data on people who took part in the Heart Protection Study, a large trial of simvastatin and antioxidant vitamins. The agreement allows long-term follow-up of these participants to assess the lasting effects of lowering LDL cholesterol on major health outcomes. The intended benefit is better evidence to guide decisions about statin treatment. The trial's results have already influenced NICE guidelines and changed clinical practice.

DARS-NIC-148071-QHNM8.summary: Imperial College London's agreement covers the use of cancer registration, death registration and demographic data. The data is for extending follow-up of the UK Flexible Sigmoidoscopy Screening Trial, to test whether a single bowel screening test at age 55–64 keeps reducing bowel cancer cases and deaths into older age. The aim is to inform future screening policy. Findings were published in The Lancet in 2010, 2017 and 2024, and supported flexible sigmoidoscopy's inclusion in the English Bowel Cancer Screening Programme.

DARS-NIC-148077-M9HG5.summary: Leeds Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust's agreement covers Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) data, including cause of death, cohort event notification, flagging current status, members and postings, and Personal Demographics Service records. The data is for evaluating the clinical outcomes of patients who had percutaneous coronary intervention to the left main coronary artery at the Yorkshire Heart Centre.

DARS-NIC-148096-PT589.summary: The Institute of Cancer Research's agreement covers the use of identifiable cancer registration, death registration, demographic and hospital records for 113,766 women in the Generations Study. The data is for studying genetic and environmental risk factors for cancer, especially breast cancer, and for death, with the aim of supporting prevention and risk prediction. The study has produced over 190 peer-reviewed publications, including six in 2024, and has contributed to improved breast cancer risk models.

DARS-NIC-148098-9ZV2X.summary: The University of Leeds's agreement covers NHS registration data, ONS mortality data and Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) reports on cause of death, cohort event notification and current status. The data is for a medical research project on prognostic markers in patients with chronic heart failure. The release register does not state a specific intended benefit or any benefits reported so far.

DARS-NIC-148100-6RFK9.summary: University College London (UCL)'s agreement covers the use of hospital, cancer registration, death and demographic records for members of the 1946 National Survey of Health and Development, a long-running British birth cohort study. It allows these to be linked to the study's own data to understand how factors across life affect ageing, including heart health, physical and cognitive capability. The data is for informing health and social care policy. Published papers include one showing that early childhood chest infections were linked to premature adult death from respiratory disease.

DARS-NIC-148101-R7RSL.summary: University College London (UCL) holds mortality, cancer registration and demographic data for the British Women's Heart & Health Study, which follows women aged over 60 in England, Scotland and Wales. This agreement only allows UCL to keep the data securely for an interim period, with no new processing. The study aims to understand risk factors for heart disease and stroke. Its publications have contributed to fifteen clinical care and public health guidelines.

DARS-NIC-148103-QWGGH.summary: Aintree University Hospital NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers NHS registration data, Office for National Statistics (ONS) mortality data and Scottish events data, all listed as medical research datasets. The release register says the data will be used only for an approved medical research project, but it does not describe the project in more detail. No expected benefits are stated.

DARS-NIC-148106-PP9LS.summary: The University of Oxford's agreement covers death, cause of death and cohort status records for 24 people with Apert syndrome, a rare condition affecting the skull, fingers and toes. The data is for a long-term follow-up study of survival and causes of death, with improved statistical estimates of mortality. The aim is better evidence on long-term prognosis in adulthood for patients, families and health professionals. The findings have been published in the European Journal of Human Genetics (2026).

DARS-NIC-148118-VCXW9.summary: The Institute of Cancer Research's agreement covers identifiable NHS England death registration and cohort tracking data about men in the UK Genetic Prostate Cancer Study, who have prostate cancer or a family history of it. The data is for studying survival and finding genetic changes linked to prostate cancer risk. The aim is to help screen relatives and develop new treatments. The data helped build a genetic risk model that gives personalised predicted prostate cancer risks.

DARS-NIC-148119-WLQ4M.summary: Public Health England's agreement covers Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) records, including cause of death, cohort event notifications, flagging status and demographic details. The data is for following people identified by the CJD Incidents Panel as being at increased risk of CJD, and for finding any CJD-related deaths among them. The agreement allows the work to improve assessment of the risks these individuals face and to inform and evaluate public health measures.

DARS-NIC-148120-0Q51J.summary: King's College Medical School's agreement covers Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) reports on cause of death, cohort event notification and current status flagging, plus NHS registration data including Scottish records. The data is for determining mortality and early entry into care for babies and children up to 5 years old identified with sickle cell disease. It also looks at whether parents had timely, informed choice in earlier screening. The release register does not state an intended benefit.

DARS-NIC-148121-LZNC5.summary: The University of Birmingham receives NHS registration data, Office for National Statistics (ONS) cancer and mortality data, and two Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) reports, on cause of death and cohort event notification. The release register says the data will be used only for an approved medical research project, numbered MR792. It does not state the project's aims, an intended benefit or any benefits reported so far.

DARS-NIC-148128-815J1.summary: University College London uses mortality and cancer registration reports to follow up children born in England and Wales to women living with HIV. It is keeping previously supplied data for an interim period while it prepares a further application. The long-term surveillance monitors cancer and survival in children exposed to HIV and antiretroviral drugs before birth. So far, flagging methods have been established and 100 death and cancer notifications received for 8,877 children.
DARS-NIC-148128-815J1.retense_draft: University College London's agreement covers the use of mortality and cancer registration reports to follow up children born in England and Wales to women living with HIV. The agreement allows UCL to keep previously supplied data for an interim period while it prepares a further application. The long-term surveillance is for monitoring cancer and survival in children exposed to HIV and antiretroviral drugs before birth. So far, flagging methods have been established and 100 death and cancer notifications have been received for 8,877 children.

DARS-NIC-148129-FK1JJ.summary: The University of Cambridge, working with the University of Birmingham, is covered by an agreement that allows cancer registration, death registration and demographic data on a cohort of families of people with ataxia telangiectasia to be used. The data is for following them up to estimate cancer risks for people who carry an ATM gene mutation, so that their care can be better managed. A 2005 paper from earlier data led to breast screening starting at age 40 rather than 50 for obligate carriers.

DARS-NIC-148130-46N08.summary: The University of Oxford holds NHS England mortality follow-up records (cause of death, cohort event notification, flagging status and members and postings reports) for UK patients in the ISIS-2 heart attack trial. The agreement covers only secure storage and back-up, so the trial results can be checked or recreated if challenged. Published results showed that streptokinase and aspirin cut deaths, and a survey reported that these findings changed clinical practice.

DARS-NIC-148137-YQCFB.summary: The University of Oxford's agreement covers data from the Medical Research Information Service (MRIS), including a Cohort Event Notification Report and Scottish NHS registration data. The data is for an approved medical research project called MR240: Fertility Study. The release register does not state an intended benefit or any benefits reported so far.

DARS-NIC-148144-69CQ0.summary: Imperial College London's agreement covers the use of civil registration death records (age and cause of death) linked to the Wynn Database, a collection of metabolic health records from thousands of volunteers and clinic patients. The agreement allows study of how metabolic risk factors relate to survival time and cause of death, particularly for diabetes, heart disease and cancer. The main hoped-for benefit is a better understanding of chronic disease, which could inform prevention. The database has previously contributed to knowledge of diabetes and cardiovascular risk.

DARS-NIC-148146-KGGC9.summary: Royal Free & University College Medical School receives NHS registration, cancer, mortality and cause of death data, including Scottish records and cohort event notification reports. It will use them only for an approved medical research project called Haemostatic Factors of Coronary Heart Disease. The release register does not state an expected benefit or any benefits reported so far.

DARS-NIC-148150-D5TDH.summary: The University of Newcastle upon Tyne holds pseudonymised mortality and flagging records for participants in the Newcastle Heart Project, a study of White and South Asian residents of Newcastle. The agreement allows the records to be used to study how cardiovascular and diabetes risk factors relate to death rates in the two groups, including the "healthy migrant effect". The data is for informing targeted interventions. A 2017 paper in the Journal of Epidemiology and Community Health has already been published.

DARS-NIC-148152-FMXBG.summary: Strangeways Research Laboratory's agreement covers the use of NHS registration, cancer, mortality and Scottish events data for medical research. The agreement allows it to build a UK-wide group of people found to carry BRCA1 or BRCA2 gene mutations, combining this with epidemiological, clinical, pathological and genetic information. The aim is to estimate cancer rates in carriers and identify factors that change cancer risk, which the release register says will be important for managing carriers' care in future.

DARS-NIC-148153-TCLV1.summary: London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine, Royal Free and University College London's agreement allows them to use NHS registration data along with Office for National Statistics (ONS) cancer and mortality data. The data is for studying ovarian stimulation treatment for infertility, with particular attention to ovarian cancer. The agreement covers comparing women who had fertility treatment with an untreated control group to see whether treated women have a higher risk of ovarian or other cancers.

DARS-NIC-148155-K7P19.summary: The Institute of Cancer Research holds NHS mortality and cancer flagging reports (cause of death and current status) for people treated with growth hormone as children. The agreement only allows the data to be kept securely while the study moves to the University of Manchester, and in case questions arise about a paper under review. The study looks at long-term cancer and death risks after treatment, to reassure patients and the public about its safety.

DARS-NIC-148156-N8FNR.summary: Oxford University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers NHS registration and mortality data, including cause of death and current status reports from the Medical Research Information Service (MRIS). The release register says the data will be used only for an approved medical research project, referenced as MR174. It does not state the project's specific aims, expected outputs or benefits.

DARS-NIC-148160-G7YGJ.summary: The University of Leeds's agreement covers NHS registration data, cancer data, mortality and cause of death data, and Scottish events data. The data is for an approved medical research project, the UK Women's Health and Lifestyle Study. The release register does not state an intended benefit or any benefits reported so far.

DARS-NIC-148161-XXPS5.summary: The UK Health Security Agency uses identifiable NHS England demographic data and cancer registration data for about 43,690 servicemen, including those who attended UK atmospheric nuclear weapons tests between 1952 and 1967 and a control group. It uses them in a long-term study of whether test participants have had higher rates of cancer or other fatal diseases than controls and the general population. The study aims to give veterans evidence about their health. Four analyses have been published in scientific journals, and the Ministry of Defence uses the findings when considering veterans' concerns, such as War pensions.
DARS-NIC-148161-XXPS5.retense_draft: The UK Health Security Agency's agreement covers identifiable NHS England demographic data and cancer registration data for about 43,690 servicemen, including those who attended UK atmospheric nuclear weapons tests between 1952 and 1967 and a control group. The data is for a long-term study of whether test participants have had higher rates of cancer or other fatal diseases than controls and the general population. The study aims to give veterans evidence about their health. Four analyses have been published in scientific journals, and the Ministry of Defence uses the findings when considering veterans' concerns, such as War pensions.

DARS-NIC-148164-9PRJ0.summary: The University of Westminster's agreement covers the use of Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) records, including cause of death, cohort event notification, current status flagging, demographics and Scottish NHS registration data. The data is for studying whether changes in biochemicals (oligosaccharides) on breast cancer cells relate to how aggressive the cancer is, measured by the development of secondary cancers. It also allows assessment of whether patients who survive for long periods have natural immunity to these biochemicals.

DARS-NIC-148171-LGV0V.summary: The University of Oxford's agreement, through its Clinical Trial Service Unit (CTSU), covers the use of Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) cause of death and cohort event notification reports, plus NHS registration data and Office for National Statistics (ONS) mortality data. The data is for use only in an approved medical research project called MR200 Leukaemia Trials (CLL2). The release register does not state an intended benefit.

DARS-NIC-148172-C20B5.summary: CTSU is authorised to use NHS registration data and Office for National Statistics (ONS) mortality data for medical research. The data is for testing the effect of adding an intensive chemotherapy schedule early in treatment, and for establishing whether it is more beneficial given early, late or both. It will also assess the toxicity of the intensification schedule.

DARS-NIC-148175-1MJ42.summary: The University of Bristol's agreement covers mortality, cancer registration and demographic data from the Medical Research Council's Boyd Orr cohort follow-up, which tracks 4,999 children surveyed in 1937–1939. The data is for studying how early-life factors, such as childhood diet and family circumstances, affect adult heart disease, cancer and death. The aim is to provide evidence for health guidelines and policy. Research from the cohort has produced over 50 peer-reviewed publications and has informed national and international guidelines.

DARS-NIC-148194-QYCWF.summary: Barts and the London School of Medicine and Dentistry's agreement allows it to use Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) data covering cause of death, current status flagging and personal demographics. The data is for estimating the life expectancy of babies born in England and Wales with trisomy 13 or trisomy 18, a chromosomal condition.

DARS-NIC-148196-4WQRP.summary: The University of Southampton's agreement covers Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) records, including cause of death, cancer event notifications, current status and demographic details, for historical cohorts of workers exposed to styrene, phenoxy herbicides and formaldehyde. It aims to describe patterns of death and cancer over a longer follow-up period. The findings are intended to inform UK and international regulatory risk assessment and management of these chemicals.

DARS-NIC-148198-8KJMN.summary: Addenbrooke's Hospital's agreement covers the use of NHS registration data, Office for National Statistics (ONS) mortality data, and Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) cause of death and cohort event notification reports. The release register says the data will be used only for an approved study called MR634. It does not state the study's aims, any expected benefits or any benefits reported so far.

DARS-NIC-148202-4LQ9V.summary: Buckinghamshire Healthcare NHS Trust's agreement covers Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) records, including cause of death, cohort event notification, current status and demographic data. The study looks at life expectancy and leading causes of death in people with traumatic spinal cord injury (SCI) in the UK, and extends earlier UK research. It also examines trends over time and compares UK and USA results. The intended benefit is better preventative and therapeutic care, and better planning for life-long care.

DARS-NIC-148204-7B1XT.summary: University of Oxford's Early Breast Cancer Trialists' Collaborative Group agreement covers identifiable cancer registration, death registration and related mortality tracking data on women in early breast cancer trials. The data is for combining long-term follow-up from many randomised trials to assess the benefits and risks of breast cancer treatments, so clinicians, patients and policy makers can make better-informed decisions. Its published analyses have already changed practice, including wider use of aromatase inhibitors and bisphosphonates, and have been cited in guidelines.

DARS-NIC-148212-TPCFY.summary: CTSU's agreement covers NHS registration data and Office for National Statistics (ONS) mortality data for medical research. The data is for a study of treatment for children with Acute Lymphoblastic Leukaemia (ALL). It tests whether treatment can be reduced safely for a low risk group, whether extra treatment after remission improves outcomes for a high risk group, and how treatment affects quality of life. It also looks at how often children become sensitised to the drug asparaginase.

DARS-NIC-148215-CQWFM.summary: The University of Nottingham's agreement covers Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) data on cause of death, cohort event notifications, current status flagging, members and postings, and personal demographics. The data is for studying whether thrombophilia, an increased tendency of the blood to clot, raises the risk of developing idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF). It also asks whether thrombophilia changes the effect of environmental risk factors for IPF and whether it worsens prognosis for people with IPF.

DARS-NIC-148219-ZHB4Z.summary: The UK Health Security Agency's agreement covers identifiable demographic data and cancer registration data on past and present UK radiation workers in the National Registry for Radiation Workers study. The data is for combining with workers' radiation dose records to investigate how long-term occupational radiation exposure affects health, including cancer and death rates. The aim is to give public health planners more precise evidence on radiation risks. Results from earlier analyses have been published in peer-reviewed journals and found risk estimates consistent with those used by international bodies.

DARS-NIC-148220-FSJM5.summary: The University of Oxford's agreement covers NHS registration, cancer, mortality and cohort event data, including data on deaths and on events recorded in Scotland. The data is for the 3C Study, which investigates two ways of improving how long kidney transplants last. These are Campath-based induction treatment compared with standard basilixmab-based treatment, and sirolimus-based maintenance treatment compared with standard tacrolimus-based treatment. The data will be used to follow long-term outcomes of 5 to 20 years, including the safety of the treatments and later complications such as malignancy.

DARS-NIC-148227-4H7DT.summary: The University of Bristol's agreement covers the use of NHS Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) records, including cause of death, current status and demographic details, to trace 951 people. They were born to women enrolled in a dietary supplementation trial in South Wales between 1972 and 1974. The project will invite them to a follow-up clinical examination and questionnaire. It aims to understand how factors in pregnancy, infancy and early childhood relate to insulin resistance syndrome in early adulthood.

DARS-NIC-148229-QC5WK.summary: The Wolfson Institute of Preventive Medicine receives NHS registration, cancer, mortality and cause of death data, including Scottish records and cohort event notifications. The release register says the data will be used only for an approved medical research project, MR710. It does not state the project's specific aims or any expected benefits, and no benefits are reported so far.

DARS-NIC-148230-KHMHH.summary: Imperial College London's agreement covers NHS registration data, Office for National Statistics (ONS) mortality data, and Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) cause of death and cohort event notification reports. The data is for an approved medical research project, "High Risk Period for Patients with Heart Failure: A Population-Based Study". The release register does not state an intended benefit or any benefits achieved so far.

DARS-NIC-148232-CPHLL.summary: The National CJD Surveillance Unit, part of the University of Edinburgh, has an agreement covering death records and cause-of-death data for blood donors and recipients linked to CJD and variant CJD (vCJD) cases in England and Wales. The agreement allows the data to be used to check whether CJD or vCJD can pass on through blood transfusion, with the aim of informing policy on risk. The project has already identified four instances of probable transfusion-transmitted vCJD, and its findings have informed blood safety precautions.

DARS-NIC-148233-2MP49.summary: University of Nottingham receives Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) data covering cause of death reports, cohort event notification reports and personal demographics. It will use the data only for an approved medical research project called SNAP, which looks at nicotine replacement therapy in pregnancy. The release register does not state an expected benefit.

DARS-NIC-148239-M8RTP.summary: The University of Oxford's agreement covers mortality and event-notification data from the Office for National Statistics (ONS) and NHS Digital, linked to a register of children in four counties with cerebral palsy, vision loss or hearing loss. The data is for monitoring how common these conditions are, supporting research and planning services. The agreement allows the data to be kept as a unique resource for possible future survival analysis. Over 90 peer-reviewed papers have been published, and annual prevalence reports have been given to clinicians and service planners.

DARS-NIC-148247-CH0Z6.summary: The University of Manchester's agreement covers the use of cancer registration, death and demographic data to add to its long-running study of newer biologic therapies for systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). The data is for linking to existing study records to check whether these drugs raise the risk of cancer or early death compared with similar patients not taking them. The aim is to give a complete picture of long-term safety. The study's register was named as a condition for NHS England funding of rituximab in 2013 and for NICE guidance on belimumab in 2016.

DARS-NIC-148257-2ZLK2.summary: University College London (UCL) is using NHS registration data, Office for National Statistics (ONS) mortality data and Scottish events data. The data supports national heart audits covering myocardial ischaemia, adult cardiac surgery, congenital heart disease, heart failure and cardiac rhythm management. The release register says the data is for audit purposes only, not research. It does not state an intended benefit.
DARS-NIC-148257-2ZLK2.retense_draft: University College London's agreement covers NHS registration data, Office for National Statistics (ONS) mortality data and Scottish events data. The data is for national heart audits covering myocardial ischaemia, adult cardiac surgery, congenital heart disease, heart failure and cardiac rhythm management. The release register says the data is for audit purposes only, not research. It does not state an intended benefit.

DARS-NIC-148262-PR6G1.summary: The University of Nottingham's agreement covers Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) reports covering cause of death, cohort event notification, flagging of current status and Scottish NHS registration. The data is for the TARDIS trial, which assesses the safety and efficacy of intensive antiplatelet therapy compared with guideline antiplatelet therapy. The trial involves patients at high risk of stroke recurrence.

DARS-NIC-148264-XXC29.summary: The University of Manchester's agreement covers cause of death and cohort event notification reports from the Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) for the European Male Ageing Study. The study looks at symptoms and disabilities of ageing in men across EU regions and how they relate to hormonal decline and other risk factors. It aims to inform European policy-makers and industry and to shape recommendations on screening, prevention, diagnosis and treatment.

DARS-NIC-148267-W26RZ.summary: The University of Oxford's agreement covers cause of death and cancer notification records, which include identifiable details, for around 10,626 people in the Oxford Vegetarian Study. The data is for examining how vegetarian and non-vegetarian diets affect long-term cancer risk and death rates, to inform dietary guidance. The study's evidence has already been used in UK Government Scientific Advisory Committee on Nutrition reports on saturated fat and dietary fibre.

DARS-NIC-148269-0WSH2.summary: London North West University Healthcare NHS Trust's agreement covers the use of NHS England's Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) data, including cause of death reports, flagging status and demographic details, for the London Life Sciences Population (LOLIPOP) Study. The study follows about 30,000 Indian Asian and European white adults in West London to identify heart and circulatory events and deaths over 20 or more years. It aims to identify the genetic and environmental factors behind the higher cardiovascular disease risk among UK Indian Asians.

DARS-NIC-148284-T2GPT.summary: The University of Southampton's agreement covers hospital admission records, death registration records and demographic data for people in the Hertfordshire Cohort Study, which follows men and women born in Hertfordshire between 1911 and 1939. The data is for studying how factors across a person's life affect hospital admission, death and chronic diseases of ageing. The aim is to build evidence on risk factors that could later inform ways to reduce hospital admissions among older people. Earlier work from the study has been published widely and cited in national and international health policy.

DARS-NIC-148286-3RWRG.summary: University of Birmingham's agreement covers identifiable cancer registration, death registration, demographic and Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) data on the 8,861 women who joined the aTTom breast cancer trial. The data is for following them over the long term to see whether taking tamoxifen for 10 years rather than 5 improves survival and what side effects it causes. The aim is to help clinicians give individualised advice on extended treatment. Results have already appeared in published papers, and USA and European guidelines now recommend the Breast Cancer Index test.

DARS-NIC-148290-CJ1K6.summary: Leeds Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust receives Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) data covering cause of death reports, cohort event notification reports and Scottish NHS registration. The release register says the data supplied to the Cancer Research UK Clinical Centre will be used only for an approved medical research project. It does not state the project's details, expected outputs or intended benefits.

DARS-NIC-148292-HV9WG.summary: West Hertfordshire Hospitals NHS Trust receives Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) data: cause of death reports, cohort event notification reports and Scottish NHS registration data. The release register says St Albans City Hospital will use it only for the approved medical research project MR671. No expected benefits or benefits reported so far are stated.

DARS-NIC-148297-0XFP3.summary: Addenbrooke's Hospital receives medical research data covering NHS registration details, Office for National Statistics (ONS) mortality data, and Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) reports on cause of death and cohort events. The release register says it will use the data only for an approved medical research project, numbered MR835. No intended benefit or benefits already achieved are stated.

DARS-NIC-148298-N5HDR.summary: The University of East Anglia's agreement covers NHS registration data and Office for National Statistics mortality data, along with Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) cause of death and cohort event notification reports. The release register says the data is for an approved medical research project, numbered MR1017. It does not describe the project in more detail, and it does not state any intended benefit or benefits reported so far.

DARS-NIC-148313-G56YY.summary: The University of Birmingham's Centre for Childhood Cancer Survivor Studies has an agreement covering linked health records, including cancer registrations, deaths and hospital data, for people who survived cancer diagnosed in childhood, teenage or young adult years. The agreement allows monitoring of their risks of serious health problems and healthcare costs compared with the general population. The aim is to identify higher-risk survivors so follow-up care can match need. Its earlier published findings were used as key evidence in NHS England's review of its service specifications.

DARS-NIC-148321-ZPHJ3.summary: Liverpool University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers identifiable civil registration of death records (date and cause of death) for patients treated for ocular melanoma and other eye tumours. The data is for a service evaluation and audit of survival, vision and eye retention after treatments such as proton beam radiotherapy. The main hoped-for benefit is better information on prognosis and treatment choices, to improve patient counselling and care.

DARS-NIC-148322-TMFVQ.summary: The University of Oxford's agreement covers the linking of NHS England cancer registration, hospital admission, death and demographic records to its EPIC-Oxford study of about 65,000 mainly vegetarian men and women. The agreement allows the data to be used to examine how diet affects the risk of cancer and other long-term diseases. The aim is to give reliable evidence to inform dietary advice. Findings have been published in journals and used by the Scientific Advisory Committee on Nutrition in its reports.

DARS-NIC-148324-V6WWJ.summary: University College London Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) cause of death and cohort event notification reports, plus NHS registration, mortality and Scottish events data. The data is for a study of whether microbleeds and genetic factors can predict symptomatic intracranial haemorrhage (ICH). This is bleeding in the brain following anticoagulation given to prevent recurrent ischaemic stroke caused by atrial fibrillation (AF). The release register does not state an expected benefit.

DARS-NIC-148327-WKVYL.summary: Imperial College London's agreement covers NHS registration data and Office for National Statistics (ONS) cancer and mortality data for the SIGGAR trial. The trial compares three tests for diagnosing bowel problems in patients with symptoms of colorectal cancer: CT colonography, colonoscopy and barium enema. It looks at how well each test works, how long diagnosis takes, and the physical and psychological effects and costs of each pathway. ONS data is needed for the diagnostic efficacy and time-to-diagnosis aims.

DARS-NIC-148331-5F2FS.summary: St George's Hospital Medical School's agreement covers pseudonymised death, cancer registration and demographic records for about 22,000 men who attended a London BUPA medical centre between 1975 and 1982. The agreement allows the data to be used to study risk factors for cancer and death, especially smoking-related risks. The data is kept so past analyses can be recreated and future research can continue. Reported results include over 30 published papers, a 2022 prostate cancer screening study, and work that led the MRC to fund a pilot trial on aortic stenosis.

DARS-NIC-148332-V6CY3.summary: The National Centre for Social Research's agreement covers mortality, cause of death, demographic and Scottish registration records linked to participants in the Health Survey for England and the English Longitudinal Study of Ageing (ELSA). The agreement allows the records to be used to study links between social class, blood pressure and deaths from coronary heart disease, model causes of death, calculate response rates, and let other researchers account for deaths in their analyses.

DARS-NIC-148334-51PXR.summary: The University of Southampton's agreement covers identifiable NHS England data on a cohort of 2,888 breast cancer patients, including cancer registrations, hospital admissions and death records. The data is for long-term follow-up in the POSH study, which compares outcomes and recurrence in patients with and without BRCA1 or BRCA2 gene mutations. The aim is to help patients and clinicians make better-informed treatment decisions. Published findings have already contributed to changes in NICE testing guidance and in how often immediate bilateral mastectomy is recommended.

DARS-NIC-148336-V4SL1.summary: University of Bristol, an academic organisation, has an agreement covering the use of cancer registration, death registration, demographic and cause of death data to follow members of the Caerphilly Prospective Study cohort until they die. The aim is to understand what causes chronic disease and to let approved researchers use the linked data. The main intended benefit is better disease prevention and prediction. The study's data contributed to the World Health Organization's cardiovascular risk charts, published in 2019.

DARS-NIC-148341-TC6TD.summary: The University of Oxford's agreement covers identifiable hospital, cancer registration, death and mental health records for people who took part in the SEARCH trial of cholesterol and homocysteine lowering after heart attacks. The agreement allows long-term follow-up of these records to study how lowering LDL cholesterol affects chronic conditions such as dementia. The aim is to help guideline bodies and patients judge the effects of medicines like statins. Published results have already influenced statin labelling, treatment guidelines and recommendations on folic acid.

DARS-NIC-148348-XTNPJ.summary: University College London (UCL)'s agreement covers Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) data, including cause of death, cohort event notification, current status and demographic records. The data is for a randomised trial of women with screen-detected ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS). The trial compares surgical removal alone with surgery followed by radiotherapy and/or tamoxifen. It looks at how often invasive breast cancer later develops.

DARS-NIC-148353-G88Q7.summary: The University of Manchester's agreement, with the British Society for Rheumatology, covers the use of NHS England cancer registration, death and demographic data. The data is to be linked to the British Society for Rheumatology Biologics Register for Rheumatoid Arthritis to study whether newer rheumatoid arthritis drugs raise the risk of cancer or early death. Findings from the register have been used in NICE appraisals, clinical guidelines and patient information leaflets, and in published studies on biosimilar switching and JAK inhibitor use.

DARS-NIC-148355-ZLC7M.summary: Imperial College London's agreement covers the use of NHS registration data, Office for National Statistics (ONS) mortality data and Scottish events data for medical research. The study, called ASCOT, looks at the long-term effects of lowering blood pressure with two combinations of antihypertensive drugs. Its main aim is to compare their effects on non-fatal heart attacks (myocardial infarction) and fatal coronary heart disease.

DARS-NIC-148356-FTLV4.summary: The University of London's agreement covers Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) cause of death reports and cohort event notification reports. The data is for the feasibility phase of a study comparing vertebral angioplasty and stenting with best medical treatment for symptomatic vertebral stenosis. The phase aims to assess safety, recruitment feasibility, how often outcome events occur and restenosis rates in stented patients, ahead of a possible main trial.

DARS-NIC-148357-6N072.summary: Ctsu's agreement covers the use of NHS registration, cancer, mortality and Scottish events data for UK Biobank, a study of 500,000 people aged 40-69 from across the UK. The study is designed to look at how lifestyle, environment and genes affect health, and why some people develop diseases such as cancer, heart disease, diabetes and dementia while others do not. The stated aim is to improve prevention, diagnosis and treatment of illnesses and to help future generations avoid early death and disability.

DARS-NIC-148358-68V63.summary: Leeds Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust's agreement covers Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) data, covering cause of death reports, cohort event notification reports and Scottish NHS registration records. The data is for the Space Rocket Trial, an approved medical research project run through the BHF Heart Research Centre at Leeds. The release register does not state an intended benefit or any benefits achieved so far.

DARS-NIC-148364-RHMHS.summary: The Society for Endocrinology, working with the University of Sheffield, is permitted to use cancer registration, death registration, demographic and Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) records on UK adults with congenital adrenal hyperplasia (CAH). The data is for studying causes of illness and death in these patients and how other conditions and treatments affect outcomes. The aim is to improve day-to-day management of CAH. Earlier results from the study have been published, and centres report improved follow-up and transition care.

DARS-NIC-148369-8PPWK.summary: The University of Oxford's agreement covers identifiable NHS England data on hospital care, emergency care, cancer registrations, deaths and demographics for around 11,940 participants of the Oxford Vascular Study in Oxfordshire. The study follows people over the long term after stroke, mini-stroke and heart events, to measure outcomes and costs and to improve prevention and treatment. Study findings have already informed national stroke strategy and clinical guidelines on treating TIA and minor stroke.

DARS-NIC-148376-YBRWP.summary: Addenbrooke's Hospital holds Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) records, including cause of death, cohort event and demographic details, for participants in a study of how arteries stiffen with age. This agreement only allows the hospital to keep the data securely for an interim period while it prepares a new application. The original study followed about 1,200 healthy volunteers and kidney disease patients to measure how quickly arterial stiffness changes.

DARS-NIC-148377-0JTP9.summary: The University of Cambridge, through EPIC-Norfolk at Strangeways Research Laboratory, receives NHS registration data, cancer data, mortality data from the Office for National Statistics (ONS) and Scottish events data. The release register says the data will be used only for an approved medical research project. It does not state a specific intended benefit or any benefits reported so far.

DARS-NIC-148379-5VSG8.summary: The University of Birmingham is using NHS Digital's Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) reports on cause of death, cohort event notification and current status, along with NHS registration, cancer and mortality data.
