It is using them in FOxTROT, a multi-centre randomised controlled trial of chemotherapy given before surgery to patients with high-risk, operable colon cancer. The trial aims to find out whether this approach reduces recurrence within two years compared with surgery followed by chemotherapy, and whether adding panitumumab shrinks tumours more.
DARS-NIC-148379-5VSG8.retense_draft: The University of Birmingham's agreement covers NHS England's Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) reports on cause of death, cohort event notification and current status, along with NHS registration, cancer and mortality data. The data is for FOxTROT, a multi-centre randomised controlled trial of chemotherapy given before surgery to patients with high-risk, operable colon cancer. The trial aims to find out whether this approach reduces recurrence within two years compared with surgery followed by chemotherapy, and whether adding panitumumab shrinks tumours more.

DARS-NIC-148380-Q4H3D.summary: The University of Birmingham's agreement covers the use of NHS registration, cancer, mortality and Scottish event data, along with Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) cause of death and cohort event notification reports. The aim is to study overall deaths, and deaths from fractured femur and ischaemic heart disease, in patients previously treated with radioiodine for thyrotoxicosis. It will compare those who later received T4 therapy with those who did not.

DARS-NIC-148382-7KTF1.summary: The University of Southampton's agreement covers NHS England's Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) data, which covers cause of death, cancer event notifications, current status flagging and demographic details. The data is for following up groups of workers who were exposed to styrene, phenoxy herbicides and formaldehyde. The aim is to describe patterns of death and cancer over time. The findings are intended to inform regulatory risk assessment and management of these chemicals in the UK and internationally.

DARS-NIC-148386-78PDC.summary: The University of Southampton's agreement covers Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) records, including cause of death, cancer event notifications, current status and demographic details, for people in historical worker groups. These workers were exposed to styrene, phenoxy herbicides and formaldehyde. The agreement allows analysis to describe patterns of death and cancer over a longer follow-up period. The findings are intended to inform UK and international risk assessment and management of these chemicals.

DARS-NIC-148389-JPMNM.summary: The University of Manchester's agreement covers NHS registration data and Office for National Statistics (ONS) mortality data for medical research. The study looks at how far increasing age predicts whether older women have surgery for operable breast cancer, once tumour characteristics, general health and patient preferences are taken into account. It also aims to find which health measures best predict outcomes after surgery.

DARS-NIC-148396-WK1L5.summary: The Institute of Psychiatry's agreement covers the use of NHS registration data and Office for National Statistics (ONS) mortality data for medical research. The work looks at first episode mania, aiming to find which factors predict death among a large sample of people with bipolar disorder. The sample is meant to represent the whole range of the illness, not just severe cases.

DARS-NIC-148399-BJ7GR.summary: The Ministry of Defence holds cause of death report data from the Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) for a study checking how deaths among UK Armed Forces personnel are coded. The study compares the Ministry's coding with national coding so that death rates can be compared fairly, and looks at how accurately suicides and related deaths are identified. This version of the agreement allows the data to be kept for an interim period only, with no other use. The main intended benefit is more accurate identification of suicides and related deaths.

DARS-NIC-148406-2YXPR.summary: London North West University Healthcare NHS Trust's Family Cancer Clinic agreement covers death and cancer-notification records from the Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) for patients with a family history of colorectal and other cancers. The data is for keeping clinic records accurate and evaluating the outcomes of colonoscopic surveillance. The intended benefit is surveillance tailored to each person's genetic and family risk. Published studies have already changed surveillance ages and intervals and are cited in national and European guidelines.

DARS-NIC-148407-LRP3M.summary: University College London's agreement covers identifiable NHS England data on hospital admissions, deaths, cancer registrations and demographics for 960 consenting participants in the SABRE cohort study. The data is for studying why heart, metabolic and cognitive health in older age differs between ethnic groups and between sexes, with the aim of informing prevention and treatment. Reported benefits include findings on diabetes in South Asian and African Caribbean people that informed NICE's BMI thresholds for preventing type 2 diabetes.

DARS-NIC-148411-Q64H8.summary: University College London (UCL)'s agreement covers the use of identifiable NHS England cancer registration, death registration and demographic data, plus Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) reports, for about 8,000 men in the British Regional Heart Study. The data is for following disease outcomes to research prevention of cardiovascular disease, heart failure, dementia and disability in older age. To date, the study has published over 600 peer-reviewed papers, which have contributed to UK and international clinical guidelines.

DARS-NIC-148412-BC33Q.summary: The University of Manchester's agreement covers Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) data, specifically cause of death reports and cohort event notification reports. The data is for use only in an approved medical research project called "Rates of Cognitive Changes Preceding Death in Later Life". The release register does not state an intended benefit or any benefits reported so far.

DARS-NIC-148413-JDKYG.summary: The University of Southampton's agreement covers Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) records, including cause of death, cancer event notifications, current status flagging and personal demographics, for people in historical groups of workers. The workers were exposed to styrene, phenoxy herbicides and formaldehyde. The data is for describing patterns of death and cancer over a longer follow-up period. The findings are intended to inform UK and international regulatory risk assessment of these chemicals, so workers are protected without unwarranted restrictions.

DARS-NIC-148417-FT2KY.summary: The University of Southampton's agreement covers Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) data, including cause of death, cancer-related event notifications, current status and demographic records, for historical groups of workers exposed to formaldehyde, styrene and phenoxy herbicides. The agreement allows the data to be used to describe patterns of death and cancer over a longer follow-up period. The findings are intended to inform regulatory risk assessment and management of these chemicals in the UK and internationally, so workers are protected without unwarranted restrictions.

DARS-NIC-148419-BR8Z4.summary: The Department of Public Health Sciences at King's College London's agreement allows the use of NHS registration data, Office for National Statistics (ONS) mortality data and Scottish events data for medical research on stroke. The data is for estimating how often stroke occurs in Lambeth, Brixton and North Southwark by age, ethnic and socioeconomic group, and for studying the different types of stroke and their outcomes. The data is also for examining how the use and cost of stroke care relate to outcomes.

DARS-NIC-148425-R38F2.summary: The University of Birmingham holds NHS mortality and cancer-related records for people who agreed to join the National Register of Radiofrequency (RF) Workers. Under this agreement it may only store and back up the data for an interim period while it informs those people how their data is used. The data was originally used to study long-term health effects of workplace RF exposure, which could lead to new exposure limits.

DARS-NIC-148435-2T54S.summary: The University of Oxford's Clinical Trials Service Unit (CTSU) receives Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) data. This includes cause of death, cohort event notification, members and postings, personal demographics and Scottish NHS registration reports. The data is used for an approved medical research project, ASCEND (Study of Cardiovascular Events in Diabetes). The release register does not state a specific intended benefit.

DARS-NIC-148436-W4NL6.summary: The University of Oxford's agreement covers NHS registration and death-related data from the Medical Research Information Service (MRIS), including cause of death and cohort event notification reports. The data is for a randomised controlled trial of iodine supplementation in extremely preterm infants, looking at whether it changes neurodevelopment at 2 years corrected age. If the trial shows benefit, the study expects it could lead to worldwide clinical support for iodide supplementation in preterm infants.

DARS-NIC-148437-C9YSC.summary: The University of Leicester's agreement allows it to use identifiable death registration, demographic and hospital admission records for men recruited to the United Kingdom Aneurysm Growth Study after abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) screening. The data is for following their health events and causes of death over the long term to understand what influences AAA progression and whether screening can improve wider health. The main intended benefit is better clinical management of men with small AAA. Data received earlier was used to avoid sending study materials to men who had died.

DARS-NIC-148456-2YZGZ.summary: University of Oxford receives mortality and NHS registration data. This includes cause of death reports, cohort event notification reports, NHS registration data and Office for National Statistics (ONS) mortality data. The register says the data will be used only for an approved medical research project, referenced as MR767. It does not describe the project in more detail or state an intended benefit.

DARS-NIC-148465-PJQ4L.summary: The UK Health Security Agency's agreement covers the use of cancer registration, death registration and mortality follow-up data on people in the national hepatitis C register, mostly people infected through blood transfusions. The data is for studying how hepatitis C infection and liver disease develop and for modelling future demand on health services. The aim is to inform efforts to eliminate hepatitis C by 2030. Its analyses have already fed into the Infected Blood Inquiry, compensation decisions and published annual England reports.

DARS-NIC-148468-KFJZ5.summary: The Ministry of Defence holds mortality data on UK Armed Forces personnel who deployed to the 1982 Falklands campaign. This agreement lets it keep that data for an interim period, with no other processing. The data was originally used to check claims of higher suicide rates among Falklands veterans by comparing death rates with other groups. Earlier data led to two Official Statistics, the last in 2014, which reported risks of dying lower than or the same as the UK general population for all causes, except transport accident deaths in 1989.

DARS-NIC-148471-FR43L.summary: The University of Newcastle upon Tyne's agreement covers mortality and cohort tracking data (MRIS reports, including cause of death) for the Newcastle 85+ Study, which follows people from age 85 to 97 in the North-East of England. The data is for identifying factors linked to healthy ageing, disability, frailty and use of health and social care, so that care for the very old can be planned better. The study has contributed evidence to government reviews and parliamentary inquiries, and over 90 articles have been published.

DARS-NIC-148473-G85HC.summary: Public Health England's agreement covers Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) reports on cause of death, cohort event notification and current status flagging. It also covers NHS registration data and Office for National Statistics (ONS) cancer and mortality data. The release register says the data is to be used only for the approved medical research project MR1045. It does not describe the project in more detail or state an intended benefit.

DARS-NIC-148484-PSL6Q.summary: The Wolfson Institute of Preventive Medicine, an academic body, has an agreement covering Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) records on causes of death, cohort events, flagging status and members and postings, previously supplied for the UK Breast Screening Age Trial. The agreement allows analysis of how screening from age 40-41 affects breast cancer survival and mortality, by cancer type and grade, to explain why the benefit seems shorter-lived. The aim is to inform screening policy for women under 50. The trial has already published results showing reduced breast cancer mortality.

DARS-NIC-149506-6C4GX.summary: The Institute of Occupational Medicine (IOM) agreement covers use of the Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) Members and Postings Report. The study looks at cancer risk among workers in the lead manufacturing industry, pooling UK data with Finnish and US cancer registration data. It aims to clarify whether exposure to lead at work raises cancer risk, and the results are intended to inform occupational health policy, including that of the Health and Safety Executive.

DARS-NIC-149576-G6M4B.summary: The University of Edinburgh's agreement covers hospital admission records linked to death registration records for the RESTART trial, which tests whether people who survived a brain haemorrhage should restart antiplatelet drugs. The data is for finding trial outcomes missed by other follow-up and checking how accurate each method is. This could show whether linked data alone could track outcomes in a larger future trial. Published trial results have already influenced guidelines in Canada, China and the USA.

DARS-NIC-149784-H9K6B.summary: The University of Oxford's agreement covers the use of pseudonymised hospital admission records (Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care) linked with National Hip Fracture Database data. The data is for a PhD project to build a better way of adjusting hip fracture outcomes for patients' existing health conditions, and to compare outcomes between the UK, US and Australia. The main intended benefit is fairer identification of hospitals with better or worse hip fracture outcomes.

DARS-NIC-150201-T3G7X.summary: London Borough of Tower Hamlets, a local authority, is authorised under the agreement to use pseudonymised NHS hospital, ambulance, community, mental health and children's data, linked with council and GP data. The data is for understanding health inequalities and service use across local communities, and for producing a one-off summary report. The stated aim is to inform local commissioning so the right services reach the right people in the right places.

DARS-NIC-150435-R7X1Q.summary: University Hospitals Birmingham NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers the use of hospital admission and outpatient records, plus death registration data, to support an evaluation of stereotactic ablative radiotherapy (SABR) for patients with cancer. The data will be added to the information collected for NHS England's Commissioning through Evaluation programme, which is analysed by King's Technology Evaluation Centre. The aim is to assess whether SABR improves survival, side effects, quality of life and cost-effectiveness, and so informs future NHS commissioning.

DARS-NIC-150521-F2Q1V.summary: The University of Liverpool's agreement covers hospital accident and emergency attendance records (Hospital Episode Statistics Accident and Emergency) for people with epilepsy who took part in the SAFE pilot trial of seizure first aid training. The agreement allows researchers to estimate the training's effect on emergency department use and to compare the records with participants' own reports of their visits. The main intended benefit is better design of a possible larger future trial.

DARS-NIC-150780-W6W3Z.summary: The University of Sheffield is using hospital admitted patient care and accident and emergency records to evaluate shared haemodialysis care, in which patients having dialysis at a centre learn to carry out some of their own treatment tasks. The study covers 12 dialysis centres in England and assesses the programme's effectiveness and costs to the NHS. It aims to show the benefits and savings so patients, clinicians and policy makers can decide whether to adopt it. A report to the funders found no significant quality of life benefit but potential cost savings.
DARS-NIC-150780-W6W3Z.retense_draft: The University of Sheffield's agreement covers the use of hospital admitted patient care and accident and emergency records to evaluate shared haemodialysis care, in which patients having dialysis at a centre learn to carry out some of their own treatment tasks. The study covers 12 dialysis centres in England and assesses the programme's effectiveness and costs to the NHS. The data is for showing the benefits and savings so patients, clinicians and policy makers can decide whether to adopt it. A report to the funders found no significant quality of life benefit but potential cost savings.

DARS-NIC-150856-G6P5R.summary: The University of Warwick's agreement covers NHS hospital records (Hospital Episode Statistics) and death registration data for 182 consenting participants in the PARAMEDIC2 trial. The data are for testing how safe and effective adrenaline is for people who have a cardiac arrest outside hospital. The data give survival, hospital and intensive care stays, and costs. The main results were published in the New England Journal of Medicine in July 2018.

DARS-NIC-150908-B9F4C.summary: The London Borough of Lambeth's agreement covers hospital and emergency care records from Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set. The data is for public health analysis, such as needs assessments, health strategies and the Director of Public Health's annual report, to understand local health and inequalities. Reported benefits include informing a suicide prevention plan, oral health services for young children and the serious youth violence strategy.

DARS-NIC-151212-B5Z3R.summary: Barts Health NHS Trust, through its National Institute for Cardiovascular Outcomes Research (NICOR), holds linked hospital admission and death registration records for about 1,965 patients who had MitraClip mitral valve repair, left atrial appendage occlusion or patent foramen ovale closure. The agreement allows the data to support an NHS England evaluation of these procedures, and is for archiving only once that evaluation is complete. The intended benefit is better evidence for commissioning policy. A report on patent foramen ovale closure was published in July 2018.

DARS-NIC-152228-DL5MK.summary: University College London holds mortality data from the Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) for the Clinical Cohorts in Coronary Disease Collaboration (4C), a study of 3,345 patients investigated for new-onset chest pain. The agreement only lets UCL keep the data for an interim period, with no other processing. The original study aimed to improve understanding of heart disease outcomes and to inform policy on stable coronary disease. The benefits section reports no benefits from earlier outputs.

DARS-NIC-15226-X7Z9R.summary: University College London's Centre for Longitudinal Studies' agreement covers the use of demographic data and Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) reports to trace members of the Next Steps cohort, who were born in 1989/90. The data is for finding addresses so it can invite people to its surveys and keep the study sample representative. The age 32 survey data is available to researchers through the UK Data Service.

DARS-NIC-152414-W3P6Q.summary: The University of Bristol's agreement covers linked NHS England health records, including hospital, mental health, maternity, medicines and death data, for the Avon Longitudinal Study of Parents and Children (ALSPAC), which follows families recruited in pregnancy. The data are added to a research database so approved researchers can study health and wellbeing across generations. The aim is to improve understanding of health and care needs. Reported results include published papers and an earlier ALSPAC study that contributed to UK policy change on infant sleep positioning.

DARS-NIC-152807-J9T1B.summary: The University of Birmingham's agreement covers Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) cause of death and cohort event notification reports. These reports are for the TASMIN-SR trial, which compares self-management of blood pressure with usual care for people who have had a stroke or have other at-risk conditions. The trial looks at whether self-management controls blood pressure better, is achievable and acceptable, and is cost effective.

DARS-NIC-15281-W8L6H.summary: Moorfields Eye Hospital NHS Foundation Trust, one of NHS England's acute care collaboration vanguard sites, is permitted to use Hospital Episode Statistics data on admitted patient care and outpatient appointments. The agreement allows analysis of patient flows and activity in ophthalmology (eye care) to inform planning and make sure capacity meets demand. The aim is to put the right eye care expertise in the right places. The work will also produce a report and an e-learning toolkit for other NHS organisations.

DARS-NIC-15283-X7W4K.summary: North Northamptonshire Council's public health team's agreement covers hospital and emergency care records from NHS England (Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set). The agreement allows the data to support the council's public health duties, including needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, the annual public health report and advice to NHS commissioners. The main intended benefit is locally focused analysis of health inequalities. The data is for a cancer deep dive, self-harm and substance misuse analyses, and work for Local Area Partnerships.

DARS-NIC-15293-R6V2H.summary: Health IQ Ltd, a commercial company, is permitted to use NHS England hospital, emergency care, diagnostic imaging and mental health data. The data is for producing benchmarking, service analysis and disease burden reports, and for running its Vantage dashboard, which shows aggregate figures with small numbers suppressed. The aim is to give health organisations evidence on regional differences in access to treatment. Its analysis has already featured in a published journal paper on aortic valve replacement and in a regulatory submission.

DARS-NIC-15335-H0D1F.summary: The Royal College of Surgeons of England's agreement allows the use of hospital records (inpatient, outpatient and A&E) and linked death registration data to study how care and outcomes differ across NHS providers, regions and over time. The work covers national clinical audits and academic research, aiming to help the NHS benchmark services and improve patient outcomes. Reported results include national audit reports used in Care Quality Commission inspections, and peer-reviewed papers on vascular surgery outcomes.

DARS-NIC-15336-S8W9K.summary: NHS England's agreement covers pseudonymised, record-level Diagnostic Imaging Data Set records, covering NHS imaging tests such as X-ray, ultrasound, CT and MRI, from 2012 onwards. The agreement allows the data to be used to produce official statistics, answer parliamentary and media questions, and analyse access, waiting times and cancer pathways. The aim is to monitor and improve imaging services and support earlier cancer diagnosis. The published statistics have been used by the Care Quality Commission, Public Health England and NHS Improvement in their work.

DARS-NIC-153720-N8K6X.summary: NHS Kent and Medway ICB (a sub-ICB location)'s agreement covers pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, maternity, cancer waiting times and birth and death registration data, covering both clinical and financial information. The agreement allows this data to be used to plan and monitor health services for the population of the former Ashford CCG area, including population health management, risk stratification and service redesign. The main intended benefit is better planned, higher-quality services that meet local needs.

DARS-NIC-15402-M9L6Z.summary: Rod Gibson Associates Ltd's agreement allows it to use Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care data to produce aggregate maternity indicators for each maternity unit. These are supplied to Which? for its Birth Choice website, which helps pregnant women compare maternity services and make informed choices about where to give birth. The site has reportedly reached 75,000 unique visitors a month and won a British Medical Association Patient Information Award in 2016.

DARS-NIC-15411-C9Z9L.summary: The Health Foundation's agreement covers Hospital Episode Statistics (covering admitted patient care, outpatients, accident and emergency and critical care) linked to civil death registrations. The agreement allows the data to be used for two projects: modelling future NHS funding pressures and how service changes could ease them, and an international comparison of the care, costs and quality for patients with long-term, complex conditions. The aim is to help policymakers target changes to cost and care quality. Work already completed includes a published joint report with the Institute for Fiscal Studies and papers on readmission rates.

DARS-NIC-154590-YG6QH.summary: Public Health England (PHE), a public body, is permitted under the agreement to use patient-level data on people recently diagnosed with diabetes, including demographic details and relevant clinical information from GP records. The data is for inviting them to annual diabetic retinopathy eye screening and supporting appropriate care for those who attend clinic appointments. The data is provided to the 72 NHS diabetic retinopathy screening programmes.

DARS-NIC-154880-M7G5Z.summary: NHS Kent and Medway ICB, acting for a sub-ICB location, may use pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other NHS service data, including clinical and financial information. The data is for planning and commissioning health services for the population of the former Dartford, Gravesham and Swanley CCG area. This covers analysing local needs, monitoring services and budgets, and identifying patients at risk. The main intended benefit is better planned, more accessible services.

DARS-NIC-154892-N5F9Z.summary: NHS Kent and Medway ICB's agreement covers pseudonymised health and care data, including hospital, community, mental health, maternity, cancer waiting times and birth and death records, with clinical and financial information. The data is for planning and commissioning health services for the population of the West Kent CCG area, including population health management, service redesign and identifying patients at risk. The main intended benefit is better-planned services and patient flow, with fewer avoidable emergency admissions.

DARS-NIC-15504-X5K0H.summary: Plymouth University's agreement covers Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care data, including details of providers, conditions, procedures and patient characteristics. The data is for analysing how non-NHS providers' share of NHS orthopaedic and ophthalmic services has grown since the 2003 Health and Social Care (Community Health and Standards) Act, as part of a Department of Health-funded research project. The aim is to give NHS commissioners and the Department of Health evidence on provider diversification and patient choice, and to strengthen commissioning.

DARS-NIC-155188-V0V7L.summary: NHS Kent and Medway Integrated Care Board (ICB)'s agreement covers pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, maternity, ambulance, cancer waiting times and birth and death records, with clinical and financial details. The data is for planning and commissioning health services for the Medway population, including analysing needs, service redesign and identifying people at risk. The main intended benefit is better-planned services and improved patient flow. The agreement reports the data has helped check the quality and efficiency of commissioned services.

DARS-NIC-155197-S3L3V.summary: NHS Kent and Medway ICB, acting for the former Swale clinical commissioning group (CCG) area, uses pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, maternity, ambulance and other health service data, plus births and deaths records. It uses this to plan and commission health services, understand local health needs, and manage costs and demand. The stated aim is to match services to the needs of the local population. Reported results include business cases presented, a forecast £3.3m of savings, and analysis behind changes to eye and skin services and an Urgent Treatment Centre.
DARS-NIC-155197-S3L3V.retense_draft: NHS Kent and Medway ICB's agreement covers the use of pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, maternity, ambulance and other health service data, plus births and deaths records, for the former Swale clinical commissioning group (CCG) area. The agreement allows the data to be used to plan and commission health services, understand local health needs, and manage costs and demand. The stated aim is to match services to the needs of the local population. Reported results include business cases presented, a forecast £3.3m of savings, and analysis behind changes to eye and skin services and an Urgent Treatment Centre.

DARS-NIC-155254-Y1H0S.summary: NHS Kent and Medway ICB, acting for the former South Kent Coast clinical commissioning group (CCG), is permitted to use hospital, community, mental health and other NHS activity data, including birth and death records. The data is for checking provider invoices are the CCG's responsibility and for planning and commissioning local health services. The main intended benefit is that providers are paid accurately and services are planned around the needs of the local population.

DARS-NIC-155278-D1D1J.summary: NHS Kent and Medway ICB, a sub-ICB location, is covered by an agreement allowing it to use pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, maternity, ambulance, births and deaths data, among others, covering the former Canterbury and Coastal CCG area. The agreement allows the data to be used to plan and commission health services, including population health management, service redesign and identifying people at risk of hospital admission. The stated aim is to direct health and social care resources more effectively and improve patient experience.

DARS-NIC-155287-C4K4G.summary: NHS Kent and Medway ICB, a sub-ICB location covering the former Thanet CCG area, has an agreement covering pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, maternity, ambulance, diagnostic and civil registration data, including births and deaths. The agreement allows the data to be used to analyse health needs, plan and redesign services, manage contracts, and identify patients at risk. The main intended benefit is better planning of services and patient pathways to meet local needs.

DARS-NIC-15530-P7L1F.summary: King's College London's agreement covers the use of the Improving Access to Psychological Therapies (IAPT) data set to evaluate whether lesbian, gay and bisexual people with common mental health problems have equitable access to, and experience of, IAPT services in England. The aim is to identify areas where services need to improve. If inequalities are found, the researchers will make recommendations to the National IAPT team.

DARS-NIC-155843-0MQMK.summary: The University of Leeds's agreement covers hospital admission and mental health records for the general population of Yorkshire under 65. It allows comparison with a register of people diagnosed with cancer as children or young adults. The data is for understanding their hospital use and long-term health effects, so that follow-up care and services can be better tailored. So far, the work has contributed to a completed University of Leeds PhD thesis on the long-term mental health of survivors.

DARS-NIC-15625-T8K6L.summary: The Clinical Practice Research Datalink (CPRD), part of the Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency, provides NHS England hospital, mental health, cancer, maternity, death and other secondary care records linked to GP records to researchers under its agreement. The data is for public health research and drug safety work, aiming to improve clinical care and public health policy. Published studies have already shown higher flu risks for cancer survivors, supporting UK COVID-19 vaccine priority groups.

DARS-NIC-156334-711SX.summary: The University of Cambridge's agreement covers linked NHS England health records, including hospital, cancer, death, GP and COVID-19 data, for blood donors in the INTERVAL, COMPARE and STRIDES studies. The agreement allows the University to follow their long-term health and how it relates to genetic, biological and lifestyle traits. The data is for improving blood donation services and donor health, and for supporting wider research on chronic diseases and COVID-19. Results have already led NHS Blood and Transplant to change its haemoglobin screening test and to use reminders to help donors keep appointments.

DARS-NIC-156407-5KJ0Y.summary: Leeds Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust's agreement covers Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) records, including cause of death, cohort event notification, flagging current status, members and postings, personal demographics and Scottish NHS registration data. The data is for studying whether the very small amount of heart muscle damage that can occur during angioplasty affects patients' long-term health, and whether the patients most at risk can be predicted. The aim is to allow steps before, during and after the procedure to reduce risk and improve outcomes.

DARS-NIC-156408-MJP0Y.summary: Sheffield Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust receives medical research data covering NHS registration, cancer and deaths. This includes Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) reports on cause of death, cohort event notifications and current status flagging, plus Scottish NHS registration data. The data is to be used only for an approved medical research project, referenced as MR1081. The release register does not state any expected benefits or outputs.

DARS-NIC-156409-W056Z.summary: University College London's agreement covers Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) records, including cause of death, cohort event notification, flagging status and demographic data. The data is for the SCORAD III trial, which compares one dose of radiotherapy with five doses in patients with metastatic spinal cord compression. The trial looks at whether patients keep or regain the ability to walk, along with quality of life, side effects and survival. The text says single-dose treatment could need fewer NHS resources and shorten hospital stays.

DARS-NIC-156412-QY9WM.summary: The University of Birmingham's agreement covers keeping death registration and cause-of-death records linked to participants in the ECHOES heart failure study. The data is for estimating long-term survival after a heart failure diagnosis, identifying the main causes of death and finding factors linked to survival. The main intended benefit is better information for patients and doctors about likely outlook. Earlier 5 and 10-year survival papers were published, and clinicians have used the figures when talking with patients.

DARS-NIC-15721-Y4V1G.summary: Warwickshire County Council's agreement covers hospital records for emergency care, admitted patients, critical care and outpatients, including Hospital Episode Statistics (HES) and the Emergency Care Data Set. The agreement allows the data to be used for its public health duties, such as Joint Strategic Needs Assessments, health reports and advice to NHS commissioners, to better understand local health and inequalities. Reported results include a report on childhood injuries and analyses used in two Joint Strategic Needs Assessments.

DARS-NIC-157211-T8B2M.summary: University College London's agreement covers the use of hospital, mental health, Improving Access to Psychological Therapies (IAPT) and death registration records to study whether psychological therapies in IAPT services affect the later risk of dementia. The agreement allows examination of access to and outcomes from therapy for people with dementia and other groups, aiming to inform policy, commissioning and clinical care. So far, it has published peer-reviewed papers, discussed findings with IAPT services and commissioners, and contributed to an Alzheimer's Society report.

DARS-NIC-15741-J6Y4L.summary: Queen Mary University of London's agreement covers pseudonymised civil registrations mortality (death) data, linked to cervical screening records. The data is for a study examining whether women in poorer health are less likely to attend cervical screening, and by how much, by comparing women who died with women of the same age. The aim is to show whether current estimates of screening effectiveness need adjusting, so that screening programmes and health inequalities can be improved.

DARS-NIC-157431-T3M4X.summary: Liverpool City Council's agreement covers hospital admissions, outpatient, critical care and accident and emergency data, including Emergency Care Data Set records. The data is for its public health duties, such as needs assessments, health strategies, commissioning of services and advice to NHS commissioners. The main intended benefit is locally focused analysis of health and health inequalities. Monitoring of hospital admissions for conditions including cancers, and identification of health disparities in child injuries across the city, have already been carried out with the data.

DARS-NIC-157949-43K23.summary: The University of Liverpool's agreement covers the use of NHS registration data, together with Office for National Statistics (ONS) cancer and mortality data, for a lung cancer screening trial. The trial aims to provide the evidence needed to decide whether to introduce population screening for lung cancer. It will look at the effect on lung cancer deaths, the best screening approach, and the physical, psychological and economic consequences.

DARS-NIC-158112-L0R5C.summary: University of Northumbria at Newcastle's agreement covers the use of Diagnostic Imaging Data Set records to study GP direct access to radiology tests for suspected brain, lung, pancreatic and sarcoma cancers in the North East and Cumbria. It allows a comparison of the costs and clinical process measures, such as time to diagnosis, of direct access with the urgent two-week-wait referral route. The main intended benefit is evidence on cost-effectiveness to inform commissioning decisions, service planning and guidance on referral routes for suspected cancer.

DARS-NIC-15814-C6W9R.summary: Monitor, which works alongside NHS England and NHS Improvement, has an agreement covering hospital, mental health, community, diagnostic imaging, cost and death registration data. The agreement allows the data to be used to set national tariff prices, oversee NHS providers and support programmes such as Model Hospital and Getting It Right First Time. The aim is to improve productivity, quality of care and payment. Reported benefits include Kettering Hospital releasing about £400,000 after reviewing its medicine stock.

DARS-NIC-158283-T2Q2D.summary: Cardiff University's agreement covers the use of National Diabetes Audit data, linked with education records, to study how children's and young people's schooling relates to their diabetes management, measured by HbA1c blood glucose results. The data is for giving clinicians evidence on how education factors affect diabetes-related health. A study was published in a leading diabetes journal, and findings presented to clinicians and patient groups were used to give practitioners a benchmark for expected absence.

DARS-NIC-158754-R5T3V.summary: The Brain Tumour Charity's agreement covers the use of hospital records (Hospital Episode Statistics), diagnostic imaging data and civil registration death data for people in England with a brain tumour. The agreement allows the Charity to build BRIAN, a research database and patient information system, to produce reports and research data extracts on diagnosis times, treatments and survival. The aim is to help patients make better-informed decisions and to support research. The Charity published three reports, on comorbidities, tumour incidence and surgeries per hospital, in its patient portal in September 2019.

DARS-NIC-159225-C9N9P.summary: King's College London, an academic institution, has an agreement covering use of data from the Adult Psychiatric Morbidity Survey (APMS). The study looks at how smokers with mental health problems can be helped to try quitting more often and to succeed. The researchers hope the findings will inform policy and clinical practice on stopping smoking for this group, and will publish the results in peer-reviewed journals.

DARS-NIC-159251-K4Y6Q.summary: King's College London's agreement covers use of the 2014 Adult Psychiatric Morbidity Survey (APMS) to study ethnic inequalities in health and in the use of health services. The data is for producing evidence for guidelines on training, practice and policy that reduce health disparities. Findings have already gone to policymakers and healthcare bodies, and a report produced with the Welsh Government informed its Race Equality Action Plan.

DARS-NIC-159399-K2M6H.summary: The National Centre for Social Research's agreement covers survey data from the Adult Psychiatric Morbidity Survey (APMS) 2014, which covers mental illness, treatment and service use in the adult population. The agreement allows analysis of the circumstances of adults with a learning impairment compared with everyone else, including physical health conditions and unmet needs for treatment and services. The findings will go into a short report for the Department of Health. The report aims to inform decisions on the design and targeting of services.

DARS-NIC-159523-F1C1P.summary: NHS West Yorkshire ICB's agreement covers the use of pseudonymised hospital activity data (Secondary Uses Service data for commissioners), linked with pseudonymised social care data, on behalf of Kirklees Council and the local NHS commissioners. The data is for understanding how social care and hospital use interact, and for producing reports and dashboards on falls, Better Care Fund measures and intermediate care. The intended benefits include fewer A&E attendances and emergency admissions, especially for older people.

DARS-NIC-159576-C0V1M.summary: University College London (UCL)'s agreement covers survey data from the Adult Psychiatric Morbidity Survey, covering adults under 65 in England. The data is for comparing rates of mental disorders and help seeking between sexual minority and heterosexual people in 2007 and 2014, and for looking at what predicts mental distress and wellbeing. The aim is to help address health inequalities. A first paper in Psychological Medicine has been published and received significant media attention.

DARS-NIC-16016-Y9H1D.summary: HSJ Information Ltd, a non-NHS provider, is permitted to use hospital, emergency care, diagnostic imaging and mental health data from NHS England. The agreement allows analysis of this data to raise awareness of diseases, support commissioning and service improvement, and produce long-term analysis of rare diseases. The main intended benefit is better diagnosis and patient outcomes. Its work has already produced a respiratory disease dashboard that a charity used to evidence health inequalities in discussions with NHS England, and it was covered in national press.

DARS-NIC-160361-NDZKG.summary: The University of Nottingham's agreement covers mortality and cancer registration records for about 550 consenting people with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF), taking part in the PROFILE study. The agreement allows the data to be linked to survival and to blood and other biomarkers, with the aim of predicting disease progression and guiding treatment. Reported results include several peer-reviewed papers, biomarkers used as endpoints in a clinical trial, and a successful NIHR Research Professorship application.

DARS-NIC-160394-Q0X1C.summary: NHS Bristol, North Somerset and South Gloucestershire Clinical Commissioning Group (CCG) agreement covers pseudonymised data covering hospital, ambulance, community, mental health, maternity and other services, including clinical and financial information. The data is for planning and commissioning health services for its local population, including population health analysis, service redesign and identifying patients at risk. The stated aim is better planning of patient flows, services and access to care.

DARS-NIC-16068-V9H0M.summary: North East Lincolnshire Council's agreement covers the use of hospital and emergency care records (Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set) for its public health work. The agreement allows the council to analyse local health patterns and inequalities to support its statutory duties, such as needs assessments, commissioning and advice to NHS commissioners. Admissions figures have been used to understand local activity levels, trends and geographic inequalities, including admissions for self-harm and substance misuse.

DARS-NIC-160958-K3J4W.summary: NHS North West London ICB's agreement, through its Brent sub-ICB location, covers pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, maternity, ambulance, primary care and death and birth records, including clinical and financial information. The agreement allows these records to be used to plan and commission health services for local people across the North West London Sustainable Transformation Partnership. The main intended benefit is better planning of care pathways, capacity and quality, based on a fuller understanding of the population's needs.

DARS-NIC-160981-S2D3K.summary: NHS North Central London ICB, acting as a sub-ICB location, is covered by an agreement that allows it to use pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, maternity, cancer, diabetes, and birth and death records, including clinical and financial information. The agreement allows these to be used to plan and commission health services for its local population, including population health analysis, service redesign and identifying patients at risk. The main intended benefit is better planning of services and patient pathways. North East London Commissioning Support Unit carries out the processing.

DARS-NIC-161143-S2S3Z.summary: NHS South West London ICB (a sub-ICB location) is covered by an agreement that allows it to receive pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, maternity, cancer waiting times and birth and death records, including clinical and financial information. North East London Commissioning Support Unit is permitted to process it. The data is for planning and commissioning health services, including population health analysis, service redesign and identifying patients at risk. The main intended benefit is better planning of care pathways and patient flow.

DARS-NIC-161339-RC2NB.summary: University College London's agreement covers the use of hospital admission and critical care records, linked to mortality data, to evaluate the reorganisation of acute stroke services in London and Greater Manchester, with the rest of England as a comparison. The analysis looks at deaths, length of hospital stay and cost-effectiveness. It aims to give evidence to guide future changes to stroke and other services.

DARS-NIC-161352-L1M9W.summary: NHS South East London ICB (a sub-ICB location, covering the former Bexley CCG area) is covered by an agreement allowing it to hold pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, maternity, diagnostic, cancer waiting times, diabetes, and births and deaths data. The agreement allows the data to be used to plan and manage health services, understand local health needs, identify patients at risk and monitor costs and quality. The main intended benefit is better-planned services and patient pathways for the local population.

DARS-NIC-161422-Q0K1M.summary: Royal Liverpool University Hospital's agreement covers hospital, emergency care, diagnostic imaging and death registration records for patients treated for juxtarenal aortic aneurysms, a complex type of aneurysm near the kidney arteries. The data is for a study that compares open surgery, endovascular repair and non-operative care to see which works best and costs the NHS least. It aims to inform national guidelines and commissioning. Results have been published in the European Journal of Vascular and Endovascular Surgery and have informed European aneurysm treatment guidelines.

DARS-NIC-162677-S1D8W.summary: NHS Surrey Heartlands ICB's agreement covers pseudonymised health and care data, including hospital, mental health, community, maternity, cancer waiting times and births and deaths records. The data is for planning and commissioning health services for its local population, including population health management, service redesign, budget monitoring and identifying people at risk of hospital admission. The main intended benefit is better planning of services and patient flows, with fewer avoidable emergency readmissions.

DARS-NIC-16274-J8H5T.summary: The University of Sheffield's agreement covers the use of pseudonymised hospital records (Hospital Episode Statistics) and linked death registration data to study vascular services in England. This extension examines socioeconomic, geographical and ethnic differences in who receives vascular surgery and how well they do, so policy makers can reduce those disparities. The project's findings on hospital surgical volumes contributed to the Vascular Society's 2021 revised policy document on vascular services.

DARS-NIC-162895-N9K8S.summary: NHS North Central London ICB's (Camden area) agreement covers the use of Secondary Uses Service (SUS) hospital data for commissioners, identifiable only by an encrypted NHS number. The data is for risk stratification, which forecasts future demand and identifies people at high risk of hospital admission or A&E attendance so GPs and commissioners can offer earlier support. The intended benefit is better planning and more effective commissioning of services, improving patient experience.

DARS-NIC-163747-X6Q5X.summary: NHS Berkshire West CCG's agreement covers pseudonymised hospital, ambulance, community, mental health, maternity and other health service data, including clinical and financial information. The agreement allows the data to be used to plan and commission health services for its local population, working with other CCGs in the Buckinghamshire, Oxfordshire and Berkshire partnership. The main intended benefits are better planning of patient pathways and services, and improved quality and access.

DARS-NIC-163816-G8W9C.summary: NHS Bristol, North Somerset and South Gloucestershire CCG (Clinical Commissioning Group) agreement covers the use of Secondary User Services (SUS+) data, which can be identified by NHS number, for commissioners. The data is for invoice validation, checking that the care activity providers bill for is the CCG's responsibility. The intended benefits include financial validation of activity, tighter budget control and avoiding misuse of public funds.

DARS-NIC-163830-B6X7B.summary: NHS Bristol, North Somerset and South Gloucestershire CCG's agreement covers use of Secondary User Services (SUS+) data, which can be identified by NHS number, within a secure Controlled Environment for Finance. The data is for invoice validation, checking that the care activity providers claim for is the CCG's responsibility. The main intended benefit is financial validation of activity and better budget control.

DARS-NIC-163839-T7M7M.summary: NHS Bristol, North Somerset and South Gloucestershire CCG's agreement covers Secondary User Services (SUS+) data for commissioners, which can be identified by NHS number, within a secure Controlled Environment for Finance. The data is for invoice validation, checking that the care activity providers claim payment for is the CCG's responsibility. The main intended benefit is financial validation of activity and better budget control.

DARS-NIC-163880-JTM70.summary: The University of Glasgow's agreement covers NHS registration, cancer and mortality data from the Office for National Statistics (ONS) for the SCOT Trial, a medical research study. The trial compares the cardiovascular and gastrointestinal safety of celecoxib, a selective COX-2 inhibitor, with traditional NSAID painkillers that patients already take, with or without ulcer-healing drugs.

DARS-NIC-164024-C3N9T.summary: King's College London's agreement covers the use of data from the Adult Psychiatric Morbidity Survey as a nationally representative comparison group. The data is for studying alcohol misuse and dependence among UK Members of Parliament. The main intended benefit is better mental healthcare and support for MPs. The study has already produced a published paper, which was widely shared and prompted national discussion.

DARS-NIC-164594-K4C5N.summary: University College London (UCL)'s agreement covers the use of pseudonymised data from the Adult Psychiatric Morbidity Survey to study how sensory and cognitive impairments relate to mental health, abuse and discrimination. The work is intended to build scientific understanding so clinicians and organisations can make better decisions about care for affected people. Several papers from this work have already been published in journals, including on sensory impairment and common mental illness, psychotic symptoms and suicidal ideation.

DARS-NIC-164830-L7L7C.summary: King's College London's agreement covers the use of hospital admission records and death registration data, linked to National Hip Fracture Database records, for people admitted with a hip fracture. The research looks at whether getting out of bed within 36 hours of surgery affects survival and recovery, and which patients are at higher risk of poor outcomes. The data is for informing better, more tailored rehabilitation. One paper has been accepted in Age and Ageing, finding early mobilisation was linked to better survival on discharge.

DARS-NIC-165012-9JHGZ.summary: The Royal College of Physicians of London's agreement covers patient records from the stroke audit (SSNAP) linked with national death records and hospital data. The data is for working out outcomes such as survival at 30 days, 6 months and 1 year after a stroke, and for identifying readmissions and further strokes. The aim is to compare quality of care with patient outcomes and to help teams arrange six-month follow-up appointments.

DARS-NIC-165460-G2C3R.summary: The Royal College of Surgeons in Ireland's agreement covers survey data from the Adult Psychiatric Morbidity Survey 2014 for a PhD project. It examines whether psychotic experiences, such as hallucinations or delusional beliefs, are risk markers for suicidal thoughts and behaviour in high-risk groups, including people with certain physical or mental health conditions. The aim is to improve understanding of suicide risk and inform clinical practice and suicide prevention policy.

DARS-NIC-165797-G5C7M.summary: NHS Doncaster Clinical Commissioning Group (CCG) uses pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, ambulance, primary care and other local provider data, containing both clinical and financial information. It uses the data to plan and commission health services for the Doncaster population, including population health management, service redesign and identifying patients at risk. The main intended benefit is better planning of services and patient flow, improving access and quality of care.
DARS-NIC-165797-G5C7M.retense_draft: NHS Doncaster Clinical Commissioning Group's agreement covers pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, ambulance, primary care and other local provider data, containing both clinical and financial information. The data is for planning and commissioning health services for the Doncaster population, including population health management, service redesign and identifying patients at risk. The main intended benefit is better planning of services and patient flow, improving access and quality of care.

DARS-NIC-165970-Q4Q8P.summary: West Sussex County Council's agreement covers Hospital Episode Statistics data on emergency care, admitted patient care, critical care and outpatients. The agreement allows the data to support the council's public health duties, including needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, the annual public health report and commissioning. The aim is locally focused analysis of health outcomes and inequalities. Reported benefits include analyses of mental health admissions that fed into a mental health needs assessment.

DARS-NIC-166391-W1S0Y.summary: Sunderland City Council's agreement covers hospital data, including emergency care, admitted patients, critical care, outpatients and accident and emergency (A&E) attendances, for its public health duties. The agreement allows the data to support needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, the annual public health report and advice to NHS commissioners, with the aim of making local analysis more targeted and responsive. The data is for ward-level analysis, a children's needs assessment on child injuries, and monitoring of its health visitor service.

DARS-NIC-16656-D9B5T.summary: The University of Liverpool's Place-based Longitudinal Data Resource covers Hospital Episode Statistics (hospital admissions, outpatient and A&E records) and Emergency Care Data Set records for the whole of England. The data is for building neighbourhood-level health indicators and studying how social, economic, environmental and policy changes affect health and use of health services. The aim is to help local agencies target resources at the neighbourhoods most affected. Reported results include published papers, a tool used by GPs across Cheshire and Merseyside, and evidence that informed government funding and welfare policy.

DARS-NIC-166879-K4Z0S.summary: The University of Bristol's agreement covers the use of NHS hospital records (admissions, critical care and outpatient care) and civil death registration data for a randomised trial of adults with end-stage kidney disease on dialysis. The trial compares high-volume haemodiafiltration with high-flux haemodialysis, mainly to see whether it affects non-cancer mortality. The intended benefit is stronger evidence on whether haemodiafiltration should be offered to patients.

DARS-NIC-167122-G6W8K.summary: King's College London's agreement covers the use of Adult Psychiatric Morbidity Survey 2014 data, which covers mental health in adults in England, in an Economic and Social Research Council funded project. The data is for studying how employment status relates to common mental disorders such as anxiety and depression, and how this has changed over time and by age group. The aim is to build the evidence base for public health policy. A paper from earlier survey years has already been published, and the researchers have presented findings at conferences.

DARS-NIC-167186-V7J4F.summary: University College London (UCL)'s agreement covers the use of hospital accident and emergency, admitted patient and mental health services data. It is examining how differences in local health and care services and in population needs relate to variation between clinical commissioning groups in A&E attendances and potentially avoidable emergency admissions, for people in contact with mental health services and those not. The aim is to show decision-makers where improvements could reduce avoidable emergency hospital use.

DARS-NIC-167794-K1P8H.summary: The University of Newcastle upon Tyne's agreement allows it to use Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care data to study whether patient choice of GP and hospital provider has affected fairness of access to planned operations such as hip and knee replacements and cataract surgery. The data is for giving NHS planners and policy makers evidence to reduce inequalities. A paper on private sector expansion and the NHS treatment gap between rich and poor has been published in Health Policy.

DARS-NIC-168692-Y5S4C.summary: NHS Coventry and Warwickshire Integrated Care Board (ICB), through its South Warwickshire area, has an agreement covering pseudonymised health and care data, including clinical and financial information from hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other services, along with birth and death records. The agreement allows the data to be used to plan and commission health services, assess population needs and identify patients at risk. The main intended benefit is a more joined up, efficient and higher quality care service. It reports that adding primary care data has allowed more targeted commissioning decisions.

DARS-NIC-168879-K2N8Q.summary: University College London's agreement covers the use of NHS England hospital, emergency care and children's mental health survey data to study how genetic disorders linked to intellectual disability affect the mental health of children and young people. The aim is to map how risks develop for people with different types of intellectual disability. The study hopes to give clinicians and families better evidence for care decisions and help healthcare resources be targeted more efficiently.

DARS-NIC-169866-G4Z6F.summary: NHS Frimley Integrated Care Board (ICB) uses pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, maternity, ambulance and other health service data, plus birth and death records, covering three former clinical commissioning groups (CCGs). It uses them to plan and commission health services for the local population, including analysing demand, service use and health needs. The main intended benefit is better planning of patient pathways and services, with care delivered in the right place.
DARS-NIC-169866-G4Z6F.retense_draft: NHS Frimley Integrated Care Board's agreement covers pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, maternity, ambulance and other health service data, plus birth and death records, covering three former clinical commissioning groups (CCGs). The data is for planning and commissioning health services for the local population, including analysing demand, service use and health needs. The main intended benefit is better planning of patient pathways and services, with care delivered in the right place.

DARS-NIC-169879-V6R4L.summary: NHS Bath and North East Somerset, Swindon and Wiltshire ICB's agreement covers pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, maternity, cancer waiting times and birth and death registration data, with clinical and financial detail. The agreement allows this data to be used to plan and commission health services for its local population, including population health analysis, service redesign and budget reporting. The stated aim is to improve planning, patient flow and access to services.

DARS-NIC-169933-S9N9J.summary: NHS Sussex ICB, a sub-ICB location, has an agreement covering pseudonymised hospital, mental health, community, maternity, social care and civil registration data, with both clinical and financial information. The agreement allows the data to be analysed and used to plan health services across the Sussex and East Surrey partnership, supporting commissioning and the redesign of services across boundaries. Reported results include a hospital discharge wellbeing checks pilot, which completed 1,441 follow-up checks, and health checks delivered with GP practices.

DARS-NIC-169971-Z9M1C.summary: The Institute of Occupational Medicine's agreement covers cancer registration, death registration and demographic data for about 1,800 UK workers from the glass-reinforced plastics industry. The data is for a study of whether workplace exposure to styrene, a chemical used in plastics and rubber, raises the risk of cancer or death, by comparing these workers with the general population and with each other by exposure level. The study aims to clarify whether styrene increases cancer risk, which could inform exposure limits and workplace practice.

DARS-NIC-170100-T1Q8C.summary: Cambridgeshire and Peterborough NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers the use of hospital inpatient, outpatient, A&E and death records, linked to its research database, to study people with dementia with Lewy bodies compared with other types of dementia. The data is for understanding how the condition presents and which modifiable factors affect survival, and for helping to develop a language-processing app that supports earlier diagnosis. The Trust reports that its first paper on mortality in this condition has been cited 49 times since 2017.

DARS-NIC-170211-Z1B4J.summary: The Newcastle upon Tyne Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers hospital episode, emergency care and civil registration (death) records, which are pseudonymised (identifying details replaced). The data is for the Northern Medical Physics and Clinical Engineering team's not-for-profit research on the safety, effectiveness and uptake of medical devices and procedures, and on patient pathways. The aim is to inform national guidance such as NICE's. Published studies have already contributed to updated NICE guidance.

DARS-NIC-170430-D2S8V.summary: NHS Kent and Medway Integrated Care Board (ICB), for the former Ashford area, is covered by an agreement that allows it to use Secondary Uses Service (SUS+) data about hospital and other care activity, which can be identified by NHS number. The data is for checking invoices from care providers, with Optum Health Solutions advising whether each should be paid. The main intended benefit is making sure providers are paid accurately and that the commissioner pays only for patients it is responsible for.

DARS-NIC-170444-L5Z2P.summary: NHS Kent and Medway ICB (Sub ICB Location, for the former Canterbury and Coastal CCG) has an agreement that allows it to use Secondary User Services (SUS+) data, which can be identified by NHS number, for invoice validation. A processor, Optum Health Solutions UK Limited, may analyse it in a secure Controlled Environment for Finance to check that invoiced care is the commissioner's responsibility and to advise whether invoices can be paid. The intended benefit is that providers are paid accurately and public money is properly controlled.

DARS-NIC-170461-D5B8V.summary: NHS South Kent Coast CCG's agreement covers Secondary User Services (SUS+) data for commissioners, which can be identified by NHS number. The data is for invoice validation, checking that the care activity providers claim payment for is the CCG's responsibility. Optum Health Solutions processes the data and advises whether invoices can be paid. The stated benefits include financial validation, budget control and protecting public funds.

DARS-NIC-170552-H5Q2X.summary: NHS Kent and Medway ICB's agreement covers the use of Secondary User Services (SUS+) data for commissioners, which can be identified by NHS number, for the former Thanet CCG area. The data is for invoice validation, checking that care providers' invoices relate to patients the commissioner is responsible for. The main intended benefit is that providers are paid accurately and public money is spent appropriately.

DARS-NIC-170564-P9F0D.summary: The London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine's agreement covers linked hospital records (admitted patient, critical care and outpatient) and civil registration death data, combined with National Chronic Kidney Disease Audit data. The data is for studying long-term outcomes, care pathways and the accuracy of GP coding for people with chronic kidney disease, aiming to improve diagnosis and care. Published results include a BMJ Open paper linking accurate GP coding of the condition to fewer hospitalisations.

DARS-NIC-170566-S0F6X.summary: NHS West Kent CCG's agreement covers the use of Secondary User Services (SUS+) data for commissioners, which is identifiable by NHS number, to check invoices from care providers. The agreement allows Optum Health Solutions to process the data in a secure environment and advise the CCG whether each invoice can be paid. The aim is to confirm that claimed activity is the CCG's responsibility, supporting budget control and avoiding misuse of public funds.

DARS-NIC-170580-K3W3H.summary: NHS Kent and Medway ICB's agreement covers the former Dartford, Gravesham and Swanley CCG area and allows it to use Secondary Uses Service (SUS+) hospital activity data, identifiable by NHS number, for invoice validation. Optum Health Solutions checks invoices from care providers in a secure Controlled Environment for Finance, so the commissioner can confirm that the patients billed for are its responsibility. The main intended benefit is that providers are paid accurately and public money is spent appropriately.

DARS-NIC-170585-V9Q4L.summary: NHS Medway CCG's agreement covers the use of Secondary User Services (SUS+) data, which can be identified by NHS number, in a secure finance environment. The agreement allows Optum Health Solutions to help check invoices from care providers, so the CCG can confirm that the activity claimed is its responsibility before paying. The main intended benefit is financial validation of activity and tighter budget control.

DARS-NIC-170589-L2W0Y.summary: The University of Glasgow's agreement covers linked hospital admission records (Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care) and civil registrations of death. The data is for following up patients in the FAMOUS-NSTEMI trial, which tested whether a pressure test during angiography (fractional flow reserve) should guide treatment after a type of heart attack called NSTEMI. The aim is to show whether this approach improves long-term outcomes, such as death or further heart attacks, and so inform NHS practice and guidelines.

DARS-NIC-170593-N0R4N.summary: NHS Kent and Medway ICB's agreement, for the former NHS Swale CCG area, allows Secondary User Services (SUS+) hospital activity data, which is identifiable by NHS number, to be used in a secure Controlled Environment for Finance, where Optum Health Solutions LTD checks provider invoices to confirm that the commissioner is responsible for the care claimed. The main intended benefit is that providers are paid accurately and public funds are used appropriately.

DARS-NIC-170647-Z0B6H.summary: Bristol NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers hospital, emergency care, diagnostic imaging and death registration data for the Sunflower Study, a clinical trial run with the University of Bristol and Leeds Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust. The study tests whether imaging the common bile duct before gallbladder surgery is needed for patients at low or moderate risk of stones there. It aims to inform national guidance and reduce unnecessary imaging. The data have reassured the independent data monitoring and safety committee that the trial is safe for participants.

DARS-NIC-170867-M5Q6W.summary: Liverpool University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers civil registration death data, linked to National Vascular Registry records of patients who had elective repair of an abdominal aortic aneurysm. The agreement allows the data to be used to develop and externally validate a clinical decision tool based on the Aneurysm Repair Decision Aid (ARDA). The aim is to help patients and surgeons make informed decisions about the best time to repair an aneurysm, or whether to keep observing it.

DARS-NIC-171083-Q8R4B.summary: The University of East Anglia's agreement, working with Public Health England, covers names-free records of addresses and ages for randomly selected GP-registered people in England. Those people may be invited to join a case-control study as healthy comparison participants, to find which routes spread Shiga-toxin E. coli (STEC) infection. The data is for identifying the most common sources so infections can be reduced. Recruitment has begun, with over 250 controls recruited.

DARS-NIC-171094-6GZMY.summary: Capita's agreement covers the use of Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) reports, covering flagging of current status and list cleaning, along with NHS registration data for medical research. The agreement allows the data to be used to distribute, collect, process and submit PROMs questionnaires. The release register does not state an expected output or benefit.

DARS-NIC-172121-G0Z1H.summary: The University of Oxford's Big Health Data Group's agreement covers the use of linked hospital admission records (Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care) and Patient Reported Outcome Measures data, alongside National Joint Registry data, for two studies of hip and knee replacement surgery. One compares partial and total knee replacement for patients with several health conditions. The other looks at follow-up care after joint replacement. The aim is evidence to guide patient decisions, NHS commissioning and surgeons' practice.

DARS-NIC-17218-B0W9X.summary: University College London's Centre for Longitudinal Studies has an agreement covering identifiable death registration, demographic and cause-of-death data on the 15,976 people in the 1970 British Cohort Study. The agreement allows the data to be used to update participant records, avoid contacting people who have died or emigrated, and research mortality and its links to health, behaviour and early life. The text says this should help inform preventative health policies. It reports that study research has already informed government briefing papers and gained media coverage.

DARS-NIC-172240-R4R0L.summary: The University of Oxford's agreement covers identifiable NHS England hospital admission records, demographic details and list-cleaning data, used to find and invite people with existing cardiovascular disease to join the ORION-4 trial. The trial tests whether inclisiran, a cholesterol-lowering drug, safely reduces heart attacks, strokes and cardiovascular deaths. Reported results so far: recruitment exceeded its target, with 13,190 UK participants, and a preliminary analysis of the invitation process was presented at a conference in October 2024.

DARS-NIC-172334-W0G2L.summary: Imperial College London's agreement covers pseudonymised hospital records (admitted patient care, outpatients, accident and emergency, and critical care) from 2012/13 to 2018/19. The data is for evaluating whether NHS England's Commissioning for Quality and Innovation (CQUIN) incentive payments for specialised services improve care and give value for money. The aim is to inform how future incentive schemes are designed. Findings have been reported to NHS England and the Department of Health and Social Care, and a journal paper has been published.

DARS-NIC-172821-S1X9K.summary: NHS Northern, Eastern and Western Devon CCG's agreement covers pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, maternity, ambulance and other health service data, containing clinical and financial information. The data is for planning and commissioning of health services across the Devon Sustainability and Transformation Partnership area, including population health analysis and reporting. The stated aims include better understanding of patient flows, improved services and reduced avoidable emergency admissions.

DARS-NIC-173508-F4X6P.summary: The Isle of Man Department of Health & Social Care, with Manx Care, has an agreement covering pseudonymised hospital activity and cost data (Secondary Uses Service data) for patients treated in England and Wales. The agreement allows the data to be used to plan and commission health services, with the aim of providing more care on the island and reducing travel for patients. The data has already helped justify a full-time plastics consultant for dermatology, bring the macular degeneration service back to the island, and support new CT scanning on the island.

DARS-NIC-173518-N4P7Y.summary: NHS West Norfolk CCG's agreement covers pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other health and care data, including clinical and financial information. The data is for planning and commissioning health services, including population health analysis, service redesign and identifying patients at risk of hospital admission. The main intended benefit is better planning of services and patient flow to meet the needs of the local population.

DARS-NIC-173530-W8D5F.summary: NHS Norwich CCG's agreement covers pseudonymised hospital, ambulance, community, mental health, maternity and other health service data, including clinical and financial information. The data is for planning and commissioning health services for people in its area, including analysing population needs, modelling how services interact, and identifying patients at risk of hospital admission. The main intended benefit is better-planned services, with improved patient flow and access to care.

DARS-NIC-173538-J5S0W.summary: NHS Great Yarmouth and Waveney CCG (Clinical Commissioning Group) agreement covers pseudonymised hospital, ambulance, community, mental health, maternity and other health service data, including clinical and financial information. The agreement allows this data to be used to plan and commission health services for the local population, including population health management, service redesign and identifying patients at risk of hospital admission. The main intended benefit is better planning of services and patient flow, with improved quality and access.

DARS-NIC-173542-R1B5F.summary: NHS North Norfolk CCG (Clinical Commissioning Group)'s agreement covers pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other local provider data, which includes clinical and financial information. The data is for planning and commissioning health services for its population, including analysing needs, modelling how services interact and identifying patients at risk of hospital admission. The main intended benefit is better planning of services and patient flow.

DARS-NIC-173549-H8J3R.summary: NHS South Norfolk CCG (Clinical Commissioning Group) agreement covers the use of pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other health service data, including clinical and financial information. The data is for planning and commissioning health services, understanding the population's needs, and identifying patients at risk. Arden and Greater East Midlands and North East London Commissioning Support Units process it. The main intended benefit is better planning of services and patient flow.
