DARS-NIC-174209-R8G8N.summary: King's College London's agreement covers five years of pseudonymised hospital admissions data (Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care), linked with NICOR heart disease registry data. The data is for research to find how many heart failure patients are repeatedly readmitted and which risk factors are involved. The intended benefit is to help clinicians avoid readmissions, improving patient experience and reducing costs for the NHS.

DARS-NIC-174337-X0N1L.summary: Kent County Council's agreement covers the use of pseudonymised health data, including hospital, community, mental health, maternity, diagnostic imaging and children's services data, together with data from local providers. The agreement allows the data to be analysed to understand the health and social care needs of people in its area and to support commissioning, service redesign and its statutory Joint Strategic Needs Assessment and annual public health report. The main intended benefit is better-informed commissioning and improved patient experience.

DARS-NIC-174486-Q8J1B.summary: University College London holds mortality, cancer registration and demographic data on women taking part in the British Women's Heart and Health Study, a long-running study of heart disease and stroke in older women. This agreement only allows the data to be securely kept while a further application is prepared. The wider study aims to identify risk factors for cardiovascular disease and support prevention. It has produced 218 peer-reviewed publications, fourteen of which contributed to fifteen clinical care and public health guidelines.

DARS-NIC-174557-H6J6Y.summary: NHS South Yorkshire ICB's agreement covers the former NHS Rotherham Clinical Commissioning Group (CCG) area and allows it to use hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other patient data, some identifiable by NHS number and some pseudonymised. The data is for checking provider invoices, identifying patients at high risk of health deterioration, and planning and commissioning health services. The main intended benefit is that providers are paid accurately and care is better targeted and planned.

DARS-NIC-174740-C0H0L.summary: King's College London's agreement covers the use of Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care data, which is hospital admissions data, for a PhD research project. The project studies how rates of self-harm differ between neighbourhoods and populations in London. The intended benefit is to help public health teams and mental health services target preventative support for self-harm in the areas that need it.

DARS-NIC-175120-W5G2X.summary: The Office for National Statistics (ONS) agreement allows it to use NHS England hospital, emergency care, psychological therapy and birth notification data to produce official statistics and statistical research. The data is for developing and improving statistics on births, population and migration, and health. The main intended benefit is better-informed decisions by government, local authorities and others. ONS has published analyses using these data, including articles on suicides, climate-related hospital admissions and carers' health outcomes.

DARS-NIC-175693-L5Y4K.summary: The University of Liverpool's agreement covers use of the Adult Psychiatric Morbidity Survey, a national survey dataset, for a PhD research project. The project will examine how social adversity, such as discrimination, bullying and trauma, helps explain the link between belonging to an ethnic or sexual minority group and psychosis, including paranoia. The intended benefit is better understanding, diagnosis and care for minority groups experiencing psychotic symptoms.

DARS-NIC-175989-M9T7B.summary: The National Centre for Social Research's agreement covers use of Adult Psychiatric Morbidity Survey data, which covers mental health among adults in England. The agreement allows analysis of trends, inequalities and risk factors in mental illness and self-harm, particularly for women and men, so government can plan services. It has already published papers, including one in Lancet Psychiatry on rising self-harm that received media coverage and was cited in policy briefings.

DARS-NIC-17649-G0X4B.summary: The University of Leeds's agreement covers Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care data, which are hospital admission records. The data is for its Cardiovascular Epidemiology research group's study of hospital stays and survival in people who survive a heart attack in England, including differences between areas. The main intended benefit is evidence to help NHS commissioners plan services and help clinicians improve care. The benefits have not yet been realised, so none have been reported.

DARS-NIC-176695-S5L5T.summary: The University of Birmingham's agreement covers use of survey data from the Adult Psychiatric Morbidity Survey, a general population household survey. The data is for analysing mood disorders and personality disorders to understand their causes, access to health services, inequalities and links to other disorders. The aim is to improve mental health care. A 2021 paper in the Journal of Affective Disorders has already been published, covering how common bipolar disorder is and who gets support.

DARS-NIC-177068-M1P0L.summary: The Office for National Statistics (ONS)'s agreement covers the use of pseudonymised Hospital Episode Statistics data on accident and emergency, admitted patient care and outpatients, accessed remotely. The agreement allows the data to be used to learn about data quality and test whether it is suitable for statistical purposes, before applying for identifiable data later. The main short-term benefit is helping ONS decide which data to request for work such as population, migration and health statistics.

DARS-NIC-177114-Y6W8J.summary: The University of Leicester's agreement covers the use of anonymised data from the 2014 Adult Psychiatric Morbidity Survey, a nationally representative mental health survey. The data is for studying how ADHD and autism relate to other psychiatric conditions and risk factors, checking an ADHD assessment tool, and looking at diabetes in autistic adults and trends in mental and physical health. The aim is to inform clinical understanding, health service planning and policy. The ADHD assessment validation has been carried out, but it has not yet been written up or published.

DARS-NIC-177392-B8T1Z.summary: The University of Oxford's agreement covers hospital records (admissions, A&E, outpatient and critical care) linked to death registration data. The aim is to study whether reorganising trauma care into Regional Trauma Networks and Major Trauma Centres has improved outcomes and cost-effectiveness, using open fractures of the lower limb as an example. The intended benefit is evidence to guide commissioning and service design. Reported findings so far show the burden of disease and the effect of the policy change and national standards on the process of care.

DARS-NIC-177523-N8J2S.summary: University College London (UCL)'s agreement covers use of the Adult Psychiatric Morbidity Survey, a survey of adults' mental health. It allows study of mental illness, loneliness and service use in people with borderline intellectual functioning compared with the general population. The aim is to improve understanding of this group's needs and help the planning of mental health services. A paper on loneliness and common mental disorders in this group has already been published in the Journal of Affective Disorders.

DARS-NIC-177734-XR2S6.summary: The University of Manchester's agreement covers the use of NHS registration data for medical research. The data is for the Childhood Arthritis Prospective Study (CAPS), which aims to benchmark the short and long term outcomes of childhood-onset arthritis, including physical effects, quality of life, treatment response and co-morbidity. It also aims to identify what predicts how arthritis develops in children.

DARS-NIC-178123-C4W3G.summary: NHS Bedfordshire, Luton and Milton Keynes ICB's agreement with its analytics supplier, Optum Health Solutions Limited, covers pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, maternity, cancer and other health service data. The agreement allows the data to be analysed to plan Milton Keynes health services around local needs, including population health management and service redesign. The aim is to understand population needs and unwarranted variation in care. Reported results include insights delivered to the CCG, local clinician workshops, and a noted change in clinical behaviour.

DARS-NIC-178135-HJSFF.summary: University of Birmingham's Birmingham Clinical Trials Unit's agreement covers identifiable data on date and cause of death, and cancer outcomes, for participants in the CReST colorectal stenting trial. The data is for archiving only, with no further processing, so the trial results can support evidence-based treatment of patients with bowel obstruction caused by colorectal cancer. The data has already helped change European guidelines on stenting as a bridge to surgery.

DARS-NIC-17824-V9F2B.summary: The Institute for Fiscal Studies, a research organisation, is covered by an agreement that allows it to use pseudonymised NHS hospital records (admitted patient care, A&E, outpatients), death registrations and patient-reported outcomes for joint replacement. The data is for economics research on the health and care system, to give policymakers evidence for better health policy. Reported results include published journal articles, and Sure Start findings that informed a decision in Northern Ireland to continue funding.

DARS-NIC-17875-X7K1V.summary: University of Bristol's Bristol Medical School's agreement covers pseudonymised hospital admitted patient and outpatient records, diagnostic imaging data and death registrations. It allows the measurement and explanation of geographic variation in hospital care and procedure use across England. The data is for helping the NHS use limited resources more effectively. Research using earlier data has produced published evidence on admission-reduction services, treatment costs and the effects of paused services.

DARS-NIC-178836-V1G3V.summary: Royal Devon University Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers the linking of hospital admissions records and death registration data with National Joint Registry data. The data is for studying how many total and revision ankle replacements fail within five years, including through further surgery, fusion or amputation, and what complications follow. The main intended benefit is that surgeons and patients get more accurate information on likely outcomes when deciding about ankle replacement.

DARS-NIC-178855-W0G7Z.summary: Oxfordshire County Council's agreement covers birth and death registration data, including identifiable details, and primary care mortality data. The agreement allows the data to be used to understand local health needs, plan services, and support work such as suicide prevention and immunisation programmes, with published outputs aggregated and small numbers suppressed. The intended benefit is local services tailored to areas of greatest need, reducing health inequalities and premature deaths. The council reports that mortality data supported suicide surveillance and helped plan its COVID response.

DARS-NIC-179115-S0R1W.summary: The Health Foundation's agreement allows it to use Mental Health Services Data Set (MHSDS) records to analyse trends and regional differences in mental health activity in England. It will build an economic model to estimate how spending pressures on mental health services may grow over the next 15 to 20 years, and how policies might reduce them. The main intended benefit is to help policymakers, commissioners and providers plan funding and workforce.

DARS-NIC-179285-7RS6G.summary: The University of Manchester's agreement covers the use of NHS Digital cancer registration, death and demographic data to add to its study of children and young people with juvenile idiopathic arthritis who take etanercept. It aims to check whether etanercept raises the risk of cancer or early death compared with the standard treatment, methotrexate. Published papers from the study have influenced NICE appraisals, clinical guidelines and a 2015 NHS England commissioning policy.

DARS-NIC-17931-M2B4J.summary: North Yorkshire Council, a local authority, is permitted to use Hospital Episode Statistics and Emergency Care Data Set records covering A&E, admitted patient care, critical care and outpatients. The data is for its public health duties, including needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, commissioning and advice to NHS commissioners. The aim is locally focused analysis of health outcomes and inequalities. The data has already been used to inform targeted work on older people's acute care, guide community service redesign, and contribute to the Director of Public Health's annual report.

DARS-NIC-179438-WCHHZ.summary: The University of Manchester's agreement covers the use of Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) reports and NHS registration data, which include mortality information. The data is for Tarn, a national audit of trauma care across England and Wales commissioned by the Department of Health. The aim is to assess the long-term outcomes of injured patients and give a better picture of the overall impact of traumatic injury.

DARS-NIC-179549-L8L1P.summary: The London Borough of Hounslow's agreement covers pseudonymised hospital data, including Hospital Episode Statistics for admitted patient care, outpatients, accident and emergency and critical care, plus the Emergency Care Data Set. The data is for analysis by the council to carry out its public health duties, such as producing needs assessments, health strategies, the annual public health report and advice to NHS commissioners. The main intended benefit is locally focused analysis of health inequalities, so that the needs of the most disadvantaged residents are identified and responded to.

DARS-NIC-179596-N1Q8X.summary: The London Borough of Tower Hamlets's agreement allows it to use hospital and emergency care records (Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set) for its public health work. The data is for producing needs assessments, health strategies and advice, so that it can better understand and respond to local health needs and inequalities. The agreement covers reports already produced using the data, including a diabetes needs assessment, locality profiles, and violence and mental health needs assessments.

DARS-NIC-180025-W6S0Z.summary: NHS Greater Manchester ICB, for the former NHS Tameside and Glossop Clinical Commissioning Group (CCG), is covered by an agreement that allows it to use Secondary User Services (SUS+) data, which is identifiable by NHS number, in a secure Controlled Environment for Finance. The data is for checking invoices from care providers, so the CCG can confirm it is responsible for the activity claimed and challenge any discrepancies. The main intended benefit is that providers are paid accurately and commissioners pay appropriately for the patients they are responsible for.

DARS-NIC-180665-GJMW5.summary: University College London's agreement covers the use of linked NHS birth registration, hospital and mortality records, including maternal age at birth, for children conceived through assisted reproductive technology (ART), their spontaneously conceived siblings and matched unrelated controls. The agreement allows study of whether ART-conceived children face higher risks of specific diagnoses, such as prematurity complications and cerebral palsy, to inform families, clinicians and health service planning. Findings have been published in BMJ Open and the American Journal of Obstetrics and Gynecology, which reported that ART-conceived children were more likely to be hospitalised.

DARS-NIC-18089-C7M8J.summary: Torbay Council's agreement covers the use of pseudonymised hospital and emergency care data (Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set) to support its public health duties, including needs assessments, health strategies and advice to NHS commissioners. The data is for locally focused analysis of health and health inequalities. Reported benefits include admissions analysis underpinning the Joint Strategic Needs Assessment and a two-page A&E profile that aided commissioning decisions.

DARS-NIC-181880-M8W1T.summary: NHS South Devon and Torbay CCG, with NHS Northern, Eastern and Western Devon CCG, is covered by an agreement that allows use of national Hospital Episode Statistics data on accident and emergency, admitted patient care and outpatient activity. The agreement allows benchmarking of local services against national and regional levels to inform commissioning plans and reduce unwarranted variation in care. The stated aim is to identify where care can improve, reduce inequalities and make the best use of NHS resources.

DARS-NIC-181948-L5P9K.summary: The London Borough of Barnet's agreement covers hospital records, including accident and emergency, admitted patient care, critical care and outpatients, accessed through NHS England's secure environment. The data is for public health work, including needs assessments, health strategies, the annual public health report and advice to NHS commissioners. The aim is to understand local health needs and inequalities. The analyses have already fed into its updated Joint Strategic Needs Assessment, joint projects with local hospitals on children's A&E admissions, and council strategies on child poverty and dementia care.

DARS-NIC-182098-Y4H0W.summary: The University of Cambridge's agreement covers the use of hospital, emergency care and death registration records, linked to its own clinical data on 152 patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) recruited from primary care. The agreement allows studying hospital admissions and deaths in this group to understand outcomes and the factors affecting them. The aim is to improve how HFpEF is diagnosed and managed. The project has already produced published papers and a research briefing, though these do not yet use the linked data.

DARS-NIC-182332-B2F4M.summary: NHS Gloucestershire ICB, a sub-ICB location formerly a clinical commissioning group, is covered by an agreement that allows it to use hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other health service data, including pseudonymised and NHS-number-identifiable records. The data is for validating provider invoices, identifying patients at high risk, and planning and monitoring health services for the local population. The main intended benefit is more effective commissioning of services, leading to better patient experience.

DARS-NIC-182736-Q2K7Y.summary: King's College London, working with Lancaster University, is using NHS England cause of death, current status and postings records for veterans who took part in chemical warfare agent experiments at Porton Down. It is updating earlier analyses of deaths and cancer with at least ten more years of data, to see whether exposure to nerve agents, vesicants or riot control agents is linked to long-term health risks. The aim is to improve understanding of low-dose exposure. A published cohort profile paper has already prompted contact from veterans and their families.
DARS-NIC-182736-Q2K7Y.retense_draft: King's College London's agreement with NHS England covers cause of death, current status and postings records for veterans who took part in chemical warfare agent experiments at Porton Down. The agreement allows the work to update earlier analyses of deaths and cancer with at least ten more years of data, to see whether exposure to nerve agents, vesicants or riot control agents is linked to long-term health risks. The aim is to improve understanding of low-dose exposure. A published cohort profile paper has already prompted contact from veterans and their families.

DARS-NIC-182801-H6R6R.summary: Bristol City Council's agreement covers civil registration births and deaths data and primary care mortality data, including identifiable details such as postcode. The data is for understanding local health needs, planning services and supporting public health work such as suicide prevention, with only aggregated figures published. The aim is to tailor local services and reduce health inequalities and premature deaths. The council reports that its analysis fed into the city's Joint Strategic Needs Assessment, a commended maternity care review and local suicide prevention policy.

DARS-NIC-183082-K3CPB.summary: The University of Oxford's agreement covers NHS registration and mortality data, including cause of death and cohort event notification reports, for the SIFT clinical trial. The trial compares fast and slow increases in milk feed volumes for very preterm or very low birth weight babies, looking at survival without moderate or severe disability at 24 months. The data is for avoiding sending the 24-month parent questionnaire to families who have lost a child or no longer live in the UK.

DARS-NIC-183359-N7P0D.summary: King's College London's agreement covers researchers studying the 2014 Adult Psychiatric Morbidity Survey to examine the mental health and wellbeing of military veterans and serving personnel compared with the general population. The studies cover employment, dementia, women's mental health, health service use and domestic violence and abuse. The data is for informing health services, support for veterans and charities' spending. Reported results include findings on veterans' job outcomes, higher rates of musculoskeletal disorders and a higher risk of homelessness among short-service veterans.

DARS-NIC-183465-X4D2Z.summary: NHS Surrey Heartlands Integrated Care Board (ICB), acting for the former East Surrey Clinical Commissioning Group (CCG), is permitted to use hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other health service data, including NHS-number-level Secondary Uses Service (SUS+) data. The data is for checking provider invoices, identifying patients at high risk, and planning and monitoring health services. The main intended benefit is accurate payment and better-planned, more effective services for patients.

DARS-NIC-183742-Z1J1B.summary: Oxfordshire County Council's agreement covers Hospital Episode Statistics and Emergency Care Data Set records covering hospital admissions, outpatients, critical care and A&E. The data is for its public health duties, including needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, commissioning and advice to NHS commissioners. The main intended benefit is locally focused analysis of health outcomes and inequalities, particularly for the most disadvantaged groups.

DARS-NIC-183842-H8L1J.summary: The Health and Safety Executive's agreement covers identifiable death, cancer registration and demographic data about asbestos workers who joined its survey after 2006 and gave consent. The agreement allows tracking of their deaths and cancers over time and comparison with the general population and between types of asbestos work. The main intended benefit is evidence on whether tighter asbestos regulation is reducing asbestos-related disease. Findings have already been published in HSE research reports and peer-reviewed journal articles.

DARS-NIC-184951-D1G8R.summary: The Intensive Care National Audit & Research Centre (ICNARC) holds pseudonymised hospital admission and death registration records for a completed study of anticoagulant treatment used in kidney replacement therapy in intensive care. The data is now kept for secure storage and for re-checking published findings. The study compared the clinical and cost-effectiveness of citrate and heparin anticoagulation. Its final report has been published in the NIHR Health Technology Assessment journal, and the NIHR selected it for an NIHR Alert.
DARS-NIC-184951-D1G8R.retense_draft: ICNARC's agreement covers pseudonymised hospital admission and death registration records for a completed study of anticoagulant treatment used in kidney replacement therapy in intensive care. The data is for secure storage and for re-checking published findings. The study compared the clinical and cost-effectiveness of citrate and heparin anticoagulation. Its final report has been published in the NIHR Health Technology Assessment journal, and the NIHR selected it for an NIHR Alert.

DARS-NIC-184980-J5B6C.summary: Cardiff University, an academic organisation, holds identifiable NHS England mortality, cancer registration and demographic data from the AML15 acute myeloid leukaemia trial. It is kept for secure storage, backup and regulatory audit, and previous analyses may be repeated only to verify published findings. The trial aimed to improve leukaemia treatment. Its results were published, informed later trial designs, and led to a change in the standard of care for a subgroup called APL.

DARS-NIC-185179-V0B0T.summary: The London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine's agreement covers the use of pseudonymised hospital admission, critical care and civil registration (deaths) data. The data is for comparing emergency surgery with non-operative care for people admitted as emergencies with common acute conditions, looking at effectiveness and cost. The aim is to inform changes to emergency general surgery across the NHS. Results already published include a final report to funders (January 2023) and papers, which found no overall difference in outcomes, but a benefit from non-operative care in very frail patients.

DARS-NIC-185897-R6T5S.summary: NHS Norfolk and Waveney ICB's agreement covers Secondary User Services (SUS+) hospital activity data, identifiable by NHS number, for two purposes. The first is invoice validation, run by Arden and GEM Commissioning Support Unit, which checks that care providers' invoices are the commissioner's responsibility. The second is risk stratification, run by Prescribing Service Ltd, which links SUS+ data with GP data to identify patients at high risk. The main intended benefit is better planning and more targeted care.

DARS-NIC-185910-D9W1Y.summary: NHS Norfolk and Waveney ICB's agreement allows it to use Secondary User Services (SUS+) data, which can be identified by NHS number, to check invoices from care providers. The checks are carried out by Arden and Greater East Midlands Commissioning Support Unit in a secure finance environment. They confirm that the activity claimed is the commissioner's responsibility before payment. The main intended benefit is that providers are paid accurately and public funds are used appropriately.

DARS-NIC-185930-B6N0H.summary: NHS Norfolk and Waveney ICB, through its former South Norfolk CCG area, is permitted to use Secondary Uses Service (SUS+) data for commissioners, which can be identified by NHS number. The agreement allows this data to be used to check invoices from care providers, so the ICB can confirm that the activity claimed is its responsibility before payment. Arden and Greater East Midlands Commissioning Support Unit carries out the checks. The main intended benefit is that providers are paid accurately for patients' treatment.

DARS-NIC-185937-D7J1Y.summary: NHS Norfolk and Waveney ICB, a sub-ICB location, may use hospital activity data (SUS for Commissioners), including NHS numbers, to check provider invoices, identify patients at high risk of poor outcomes, and understand local population health needs. The agreement allows invoice checking and risk scoring to be carried out by external organisations. The stated aim is accurate payment of providers and earlier, better-targeted care, including fewer avoidable emergency admissions.

DARS-NIC-185940-J1W0Y.summary: NHS Norfolk and Waveney ICB, through Arden and GEM Commissioning Support Unit, is covered by a data sharing agreement for Secondary User Services (SUS+) data that can be identified by NHS number. The agreement allows the data to be used in a secure Controlled Environment for Finance to check provider invoices and confirm that the care claimed for is the commissioner's responsibility. This lets the ICB challenge invoices, control its budget and ensure providers are paid accurately for patients' treatment.

DARS-NIC-186079-S6M6S.summary: University College London (UCL)'s agreement covers the use of NHS registration data and Scottish events data for medical research. The release register only partly describes the purpose. It discusses defining "time zero" as the point a patient presents to health care, and notes that a "biological time zero", when a patient first became unwell in the community, may be more relevant. No expected benefits are stated.

DARS-NIC-186250-L9C7M.summary: NHS South Eastern Hampshire CCG's agreement covers pseudonymised hospital activity data (Secondary Uses Service data for commissioners) containing clinical and financial information. The data is for planning and commissioning health services as part of a "vanguard" new care models programme with Fareham and Gosport CCG. The agreement allows population health analysis, service redesign and evaluation of local services. The main intended benefit is reducing demand for non-elective care and improving patient flow.

DARS-NIC-18646-P0R3M.summary: University College London (UCL)'s agreement covers hospital records (accident and emergency, admitted patient care, critical care and outpatients) and death and event notification reports for patients in the CROMIS-2 stroke study. The agreement allows UCL to track outcomes such as repeat stroke, bleeding in the brain and death in people taking anticoagulants for atrial fibrillation. The aim is to help clinicians make better decisions about anticoagulation after a stroke.

DARS-NIC-18674-W8Q8K.summary: The Nuffield Trust, an independent research group, is licensed to use Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care data. The agreement covers an evaluation of Age UK's Integrated Care Programme in seven areas of England. The evaluation is designed to compare hospital use by people who received the service with a matched group who did not. The main intended benefit is independent evidence for commissioners deciding whether to fund similar schemes.

DARS-NIC-186860-T7H5K.summary: The University of Manchester's agreement covers hospital admission records and death registration data for people aged 75 and over in Greater Manchester care homes. It allows the study of how different kinds of healthcare support for care home residents relate to emergency hospital admissions and place of death. The data is for helping commissioners and care providers plan more appropriate care and reduce avoidable admissions. Early findings were presented at local care home forums in 2019.

DARS-NIC-186881-Z9P9B.summary: NHS Buckinghamshire, Oxfordshire and Berkshire West Integrated Care Board's agreement covers hospital, community, mental health and other health service data, some identifiable by NHS number and some pseudonymised. The data is for checking invoices from care providers, identifying patients at high risk of health deterioration, and planning and commissioning health services. The aim is services that match local needs. The agreement reports that services have been delivered to match the population's requirements and that integrated care has been delivered.

DARS-NIC-186883-L6C8Y.summary: NHS Birmingham and Solihull ICB's agreement covers hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other NHS activity data, some identifiable by NHS number and some pseudonymised. The agreement allows the data to be used to check provider invoices, to identify patients at high risk of poor health so GPs and commissioners can target care, and to plan and monitor health services for the local population. The main intended benefit is more effective commissioning, with providers paid accurately and care better matched to local needs.

DARS-NIC-186885-Q1T3D.summary: NHS Bristol, North Somerset and South Gloucestershire ICB's agreement covers the use of hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other health service data, mostly pseudonymised, to validate provider invoices, identify patients at risk of poor health, and plan and monitor commissioned services. The aim is to pay providers accurately and to plan care that better meets the population's needs. The agreement has identified around £28.5m of savings and has been used to monitor the overnight closure of an A&E department.

DARS-NIC-186888-X2K6T.summary: NHS Buckinghamshire, Oxfordshire and Berkshire West ICB's agreement covers hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other health and care data, some identifiable and some pseudonymised. The agreement allows the data to be used to check invoices from care providers, to identify patients at high risk so their care can be planned, and to plan and commission health services. The main intended benefit is that providers are paid accurately and services better match local needs. The CCG reported that it had used the data to monitor in-year projects and publish an annual report.

DARS-NIC-186893-W6V1H.summary: NHS Frimley ICB, acting for the former East Berkshire clinical commissioning group, is covered by an agreement allowing it to receive hospital, community, mental health, ambulance and other provider activity data, including NHS-number-level and pseudonymised records. The data is for checking provider invoices, identifying patients at high risk of poor health so GPs can target their care, and planning and commissioning health services. The main intended benefit is that providers are paid accurately and care is better targeted and planned.

DARS-NIC-186896-Q5Q2G.summary: NHS West Yorkshire ICB's agreement, covering the former NHS Leeds CCG, allows the use of hospital, community, mental health, GP-linked and other health and social care data to check invoices, identify patients at high risk of poor health, and support the planning of health services. The agreement allows some data identifiable by NHS number, and some pseudonymised data. The aim is to ensure providers are paid correctly, target care for vulnerable patients and plan services around local needs. Benefits reported so far are contributions to the organisation's annual reports.

DARS-NIC-187228-X8C4G.summary: Derby City Council's agreement allows it to use hospital and emergency care data (Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set) to support its public health duties. This covers needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, the annual public health report and advice to NHS commissioners. The data is for locally focused analysis of health outcomes and inequalities. The council reports that the data helped it show the need to change its urgent care system and supported its Discharge to Assess model.

DARS-NIC-18798-V2J6C.summary: NHS England's agreement covers Hospital Episode Statistics (HES) data on hospital admissions, outpatients, critical care and A&E, plus the Emergency Care Data Set, which it downloads through the NHS Digital portal. The data is for commissioning, policy, finance and analysis, such as monitoring services and planning future care. The aim is to improve the quality and efficiency of NHS services. Published examples include a mixed sex accommodation breach rate and the Diagnostic Atlas of Variation.

DARS-NIC-188499-K4G0M.summary: King's College London's agreement covers the use of pseudonymised data from the Adult Psychiatric Morbidity Survey 2014, a national survey of adults in England and Wales. The researchers are studying how mental disorders relate to experiencing sexual violence and to carrying out domestic violence. They aim to give clearer evidence on how common and how likely these experiences are among people with mental disorders, to inform future research, practice and policy.

DARS-NIC-188901-P9M0S.summary: Great Ormond Street Hospital for Children NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers hospital admission, death registration and maternity records for children admitted to paediatric intensive care units (PICUs). The data is for research, part of a doctoral fellowship, that examines why girls admitted as infants have had higher death rates than boys, unlike in the general population. It aims to inform care and a possible revision of the Paediatric Index of Mortality score. One systematic review has been submitted to peer review.

DARS-NIC-189166-R0Y9Y.summary: The University of Southampton, an academic body, may hold cause of death report data from the Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) for the New EPOC cancer trial. The trial tested whether adding cetuximab to chemotherapy helps patients with operable colorectal liver metastases. The agreement allows the data to be kept only for back-up and storage, to meet research standards. Results from the trial have already been presented at cancer conferences and published in the Lancet in 2014.

DARS-NIC-189627-R3N8Y.summary: Sunderland City Council's agreement covers civil registration data on births and deaths, plus primary care mortality data, which includes identifiable details. The data is for understanding local public health needs, including suicide and drug-related death audits, and for producing aggregated statistics for needs assessments and health strategies. The aim is to tailor local services to areas of greatest need and reduce health inequalities. The agreement allows internal Power BI reports showing births and deaths trends by ward, and the council has already built such reports.

DARS-NIC-190086-F5Z7B.summary: St George's Hospital Medical School's agreement covers the use of hospital records (admitted patient care, outpatient and accident and emergency), death registration data and a list cleaning report. The data covers about 120,000 young people who had voluntary heart screening through Cardiac Risk in the Young. The study looks at outcomes for the whole screened group, including those with normal results, to estimate how often sudden cardiac death occurs. The aim is a more reliable estimate that could inform decisions on screening programmes and guidelines.

DARS-NIC-190996-C4P8G.summary: RM Partners, a cancer alliance hosted by The Royal Marsden NHS Foundation Trust, is licensed to use the National Cancer Waiting Times Monitoring Data Set, which records cancer patients' waits from referral to treatment. The agreement allows analysis of waiting times and patient flows across North West and South West London to find variation and delays. The aim is to improve cancer pathways, survival and patient experience. Earlier analysis compared provider performance, so support could be targeted at providers facing challenges.

DARS-NIC-191209-G3Z6Z.summary: NHS Greater Manchester ICB's agreement, for the former NHS Bolton CCG area, allows use of pseudonymised (identifiers replaced) hospital provider data and civil registrations of death. The data is for supporting the Greater Manchester and Eastern Cheshire Cancer Vanguard's evaluation of cancer care and outcomes, and for helping commissioners plan health services, including population health management and contract management. The main intended benefit is better planning of services and patient pathways.

DARS-NIC-191964-Y3Z1L.summary: NHS West Yorkshire ICB's agreement, for the former North Kirklees area, allows use of hospital activity data (Secondary User Services, SUS+) that can be identified by NHS number. The data is for checking provider invoices before payment and for running risk stratification, which links the data with GP records to identify patients at high risk of health deterioration. The main intended benefit is that providers are paid accurately for the care they deliver, and that patients at risk can be offered earlier, better-targeted care.

DARS-NIC-192020-Q9Q0W.summary: NHS Greater Huddersfield CCG's agreement allows it to use hospital activity data from Secondary User Services (SUS+), which is identifiable by NHS number. The data is for checking invoices from care providers before payment, and for identifying patients at high risk so care can be planned and offered earlier. The main stated benefit is more effective commissioning of services and better patient experience.

DARS-NIC-192032-K0J3X.summary: NHS West Yorkshire ICB's agreement covers pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, maternity, ambulance and other health and care activity and financial data, plus birth and death records. The agreement allows the ICB, a sub-ICB location covering former Calderdale, Greater Huddersfield and North Kirklees CCGs, to use this data to plan and commission health services across the West Yorkshire and Harrogate partnership area, including population health analysis, demand planning and contract management. The main intended benefit is better-planned services and patient pathways.

DARS-NIC-192218-L8R4C.summary: London Borough of Waltham Forest, a local authority, has an agreement covering hospital and emergency care data (Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set). The agreement allows the data to support its public health duties, including needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, annual public health reports and advice to NHS commissioners. The data is for locally focused analysis of health outcomes and inequalities. It has already produced JSNA chapters on cardiovascular disease, respiratory diseases and air quality, and informed council projects such as road improvements for air quality.

DARS-NIC-192305-X3T0Y.summary: NHS England's agreement covers national, patient-level cancer waiting times data, with identifying details removed, along with aggregate figures. The data is for producing official statistics, monitoring performance against NHS Constitution standards, supporting policy and service improvement, and giving Cancer Alliances local performance reports. The main intended benefit is to focus improvements on the areas that will best improve cancer waiting times. Reported benefits include published monthly and quarterly statistics, funding allocated to Cancer Alliances using them as a benchmark, and national timed pathways developed from them.

DARS-NIC-19237-R3T6S.summary: The University of Liverpool's agreement covers cancer registration, death registration, demographic and mortality-flagging data for people who consented to join the UK Lung Cancer Screening Trial. The agreement allows the data to be used to follow participants' cancer diagnoses, whether they are alive, and their dates and causes of death. The data is for showing whether low-dose CT screening reduces lung cancer deaths, to inform the UK National Screening Committee. Results have already been published in Thorax and The Lancet Regional Health - Europe.

DARS-NIC-192767-R0S9V.summary: NHS Suffolk and North East Essex ICB's agreement covers pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, maternity, ambulance and primary care data, along with birth and death records. The data is for planning and commissioning health services for the local population, including analysing demand, finding patients at risk of admission, monitoring providers and redesigning services. The main intended benefit is that commissioners can make better decisions and improve the quality of services and health outcomes.

DARS-NIC-193359-V6H2X.summary: NHS Heywood, Middleton and Rochdale CCG's agreement covers pseudonymised hospital and other health service data, including clinical and financial information, with processing carried out by Arden and GEM Commissioning Support Unit and Salford Royal NHS Foundation Trust. The data is for planning health services for the North West population, including population health management, service redesign and identifying patients at risk. The Advancing Quality Alliance also produces aggregate quality reports from it. The stated aim is consistent, improved quality of care across trusts.

DARS-NIC-193381-L9V3D.summary: NHS Salford CCG's agreement covers pseudonymised hospital, mental health, maternity and other local provider data, containing clinical and financial information. The data is for planning health services for the North West population, including population health management and service redesign, and for helping Advancing Quality Alliance produce aggregate quality reports on treatment pathways. The main intended benefit is more consistent, higher-quality care across trusts.

DARS-NIC-193396-Z2Q3C.summary: NHS Tameside and Glossop CCG's agreement covers the use of pseudonymised hospital, mental health, maternity and other local provider data, including clinical and financial information. The data is for planning and commissioning health services for the North West population, including population health analysis, service redesign and identifying patients at risk. It also supports the Advancing Quality Alliance's quality improvement reports. The main intended benefit is more consistent, equitable standards of care across hospital trusts.

DARS-NIC-193456-W3M0H.summary: NHS Greater Manchester Integrated Care Board, working with three other ICBs, is permitted to use pseudonymised hospital activity, local acute provider and death registration data. The agreement allows the data to be used to plan and commission health services and to produce aggregate quality reports through the Advancing Quality Alliance. The aim is more equal, consistent care across trusts. Two published papers (2012 and 2020) report reduced mortality, and one trust changed its antibiotic process after analysis of the data.

DARS-NIC-193518-T5K7C.summary: The Children's Commissioner's Office's agreement covers use of the pseudonymised 2014 Adult Psychiatric Morbidity Survey to estimate how many children live in households where an adult has physical or mental health problems, or alcohol, substance or domestic abuse issues. The agreement allows publication of aggregated statistics so local authorities and government can plan services for families with complex needs. Its earlier estimates have been used in central government dashboards and in local authorities' Joint Strategic Needs Assessments.

DARS-NIC-193754-H7S6H.summary: NHS Wirral CCG uses hospital activity data from Secondary User Services (SUS+), which can be identified by NHS number, and links it with GP data for one of its two uses. It uses the data to check that invoices from care providers are the CCG's responsibility to pay. It also uses it for risk stratification, which identifies patients at high risk so their care can be planned and GPs can target support. The main intended benefit is more effective commissioning of services.
DARS-NIC-193754-H7S6H.retense_draft: NHS Wirral CCG's agreement covers hospital activity data from Secondary User Services (SUS+), which can be identified by NHS number, and links it with GP data for one of its two uses. The data is for checking that invoices from care providers are the CCG's responsibility to pay. It is also for risk stratification, which identifies patients at high risk so their care can be planned and GPs can target support. The main intended benefit is more effective commissioning of services.

DARS-NIC-194340-D6F3B.summary: The Office for National Statistics (ONS) holds linked census and life events data on about 1% of the population of England and Wales, and this agreement is a short-term extension to keep that data. It maintains the ONS Longitudinal Study research database and gives approved researchers controlled access to it, so they can study topics such as health inequality and ageing. Its data has already supported government reports on health inequalities, National Statistics on life expectancy, and evidence submitted to the Dilnot Commission.

DARS-NIC-194387-K3H5K.summary: The University of Sheffield's agreement covers demographic data and NHS mortality list-cleaning reports, used to check whether bladder cancer patients in Yorkshire, the Humber, North Derbyshire and South Tees have died or moved address. This supports a survey of patients' own reports of their quality of life during the first year after diagnosis. The aim is to understand outcomes, identify unmet need and shape clinical care. The checks also help surveys reach the right people and avoid distressing bereaved families.

DARS-NIC-194629-S4F9X.summary: The Nuffield Trust for Research and Policy Studies in Health Services, a research charity, is permitted under its agreement to use NHS hospital, emergency care and community services data. The data is for the NIHR Rapid Service Evaluation Team's evaluations of new ways of providing care, so that findings reach decision makers quickly. Reported results include influence on the Care Quality Commission's special measures regime, national Covid oximetry at home services, and a final maternity advocate report shared with government.

DARS-NIC-195235-Q0B5T.summary: The University of East Anglia's agreement covers hospital records on accident and emergency, inpatient and outpatient care for care home residents in England who took part in the FinCH trial. The data is for working out the costs of a falls prevention programme for care homes, compared with usual care, as part of a cost-effectiveness analysis. The aim is to give decision makers evidence on whether the programme reduces falls and offers value for money. The team's findings have been submitted for publication but have not yet been published.

DARS-NIC-195377-M9L8Z.summary: The Nuffield Trust's agreement covers hospital data on A&E, inpatient and outpatient care, for studying how prisoners use secondary care services and how their care compares with non-prisoners. The data is for helping to fill a gap in evidence on healthcare quality in prisons. The Trust reports that its findings were cited in a Prisons and Probation Ombudsman report and used in a review that led the Ministry of Justice to publish figures on pregnant women in custody.

DARS-NIC-195618-N6T1R.summary: King's College London's agreement covers the use of Adult Psychiatric Morbidity Survey data in a doctoral research project, with support from the National Centre for Social Research. The data is for a project that looks at common mental disorders and access to psychological treatments among ethnic minority groups in the UK, including the reasons for the treatment gap. The project aims to build the evidence base on mental health inequalities to support better access to services. A presentation based on the analysis was delivered at a UK Data Service conference in July 2021.

DARS-NIC-195793-R5Y3H.summary: The University of Surrey's agreement, working with the Royal College of General Practitioners, covers hospital admission records linked to death registration data. The data is for studying how mandatory risk assessment for venous thromboembolism (VTE, blood clots) has affected VTE rates and outcomes after surgery in England. The aim is to help target preventive treatment to the patients most at risk. The team has developed a prediction model for VTE after hip and knee surgery, and an abstract on it was accepted for a 2022 international conference.

DARS-NIC-196211-N2W0D.summary: The University of Aberdeen's agreement covers hospital, emergency care, outpatient and death registration records for patients in the UK-REBOA trial. The trial compares standard major trauma centre care with and without REBOA, a balloon placed in the main artery to stop life-threatening bleeding after severe injury. The data is for measuring 90-day mortality and cost-effectiveness. The aim is to show clinicians how best to treat major trauma and whether REBOA offers value for money to the NHS.

DARS-NIC-196221-K4K3Y.summary: The University of Manchester's agreement covers National Diabetes Audit data, including records of people at risk of type 2 diabetes, linked to NHS Diabetes Prevention Programme participation records. The data is for evaluating how well the programme works and whether it is a good use of NHS funds, so that commissioning decisions can be informed. Several research papers and conference presentations based on the data have already been published.

DARS-NIC-196263-J9Q7Z.summary: University College London's agreement covers hospital records (admissions, outpatient and A&E), civil registration death records and cohort-tracing data on women who gave birth. These are linked to Cafcass family court records on care proceedings. The research looks at the health needs of mothers involved in care proceedings, comparing them with other women who gave birth. It aims to give policy makers and services evidence to guide support for vulnerable families.

DARS-NIC-197584-N4S9C.summary: NHS Southport and Formby CCG, working with KPMG, is covered by an agreement that allows the use of pseudonymised (personal details removed) hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other health service data covering its area. The data is for analysis to support commissioning and to help develop a service change proposal for Southport and Ormskirk hospital services. The intended benefit is a proposal setting out clinically sustainable, practical and affordable options for those hospitals.

DARS-NIC-197669-K8J6D.summary: NHS Mid and South Essex ICB's agreement covers pseudonymised hospital, mental health, community, maternity and other health and care data from five local CCG areas. The data is for planning and commissioning health services, including demand planning, reporting and identifying people at risk. The main intended benefit is better-planned services and patient pathways. Reported results include an urgent community response service and a single bed bureau for hospital discharge, plus published 2020/21 annual reports.

DARS-NIC-197745-T1B4G.summary: NHS Mid Essex CCG's agreement covers the use of Secondary User Services (SUS+) data from hospital activity, identifiable by NHS number and linked with GP data, for risk stratification. Optum Health Solutions (UK) Ltd carries out this work. It produces risk scores to identify patients at high risk of needing high levels of care, so the CCG can plan services and GPs can target interventions. The main intended benefit is better case management and more effective commissioning of services.

DARS-NIC-19805-M6T5R.summary: The University of Liverpool's agreement covers Hospital Episode Statistics data on accident and emergency, admitted patient care, critical care and outpatients. The data is for a research study assessing whether electronic medical records can measure outcomes in a randomised controlled trial, SANAD II, which tests epilepsy drugs, compared with standard methods. The main intended benefit is to improve how SANAD II is analysed and to inform the design of future trials.

DARS-NIC-198066-F4H9X.summary: NHS Mid and South Essex ICB (a sub-ICB location)'s agreement allows it to use Secondary User Services (SUS+) data for commissioners, identifiable by NHS number, for two purposes. The first is invoice validation, checking that provider invoices relate to patients it is responsible for. The second is risk stratification, linking the data with GP data to identify patients at high risk of poor health. The main intended benefits are accurate payment of providers and better targeted care.

DARS-NIC-198104-H9N9N.summary: NHS Mid and South Essex ICB, through the former NHS Castle Point and Rochford CCG, has an agreement that allows it to use hospital activity data from Secondary User Services (SUS+) for commissioners, identifiable by NHS number. The data is for checking provider invoices before payment and, with Prescribing Services Ltd, for risk stratification, which links the data with GP records to identify patients at high risk of health deterioration. The stated aims are accurate payment for care and more targeted, effective care.

DARS-NIC-198111-C2W4W.summary: NHS Mid and South Essex Integrated Care Board (ICB) uses Secondary Uses Service (SUS+) data, which can be identified by NHS number, to check invoices from care providers. With Liaison Financial Services, it confirms that the activity billed is the commissioner's responsibility and reviews past payments for overcharges. The main intended benefit is that providers are paid accurately and money that would otherwise be lost is recovered.
DARS-NIC-198111-C2W4W.retense_draft: NHS Mid and South Essex Integrated Care Board's agreement allows it to use Secondary Uses Service (SUS+) data, which can be identified by NHS number, to check invoices from care providers. With Liaison Financial Services, the agreement allows it to confirm that the activity billed is the commissioner's responsibility and to review past payments for overcharges. The main intended benefit is that providers are paid accurately and money that would otherwise be lost is recovered.

DARS-NIC-198115-L1P3P.summary: NHS Southend CCG's agreement covers the use of Secondary User Services (SUS+) data, which can be identified by NHS number, within a secure Controlled Environment for Finance. The data is for invoice validation, checking that the care activity providers bill for is the CCG's responsibility. The main intended benefits are financial validation of activity and better budget control.

DARS-NIC-198119-X9P3J.summary: NHS Mid and South Essex ICB (Thurrock area)'s agreement allows it to use Secondary User Services (SUS+) hospital activity data, identifiable by NHS number, for two purposes. It allows checking provider invoices to confirm that the CCG is responsible for the activity claimed, and, through Prescribing Services Ltd, linking the data with GP records to identify patients at high risk of health deterioration. The main intended benefits are accurate payment of providers and better targeted, more effective care planning.

DARS-NIC-198958-C9G0C.summary: Leicestershire County Council, working with other Leicester, Leicestershire and Rutland health and care partners, is permitted to use pseudonymised hospital activity data (SUS for Commissioners). The agreement allows the data to be used to analyse local needs and service use, and to plan, commission and redesign health and care services under the Better Care Together partnership. The main intended benefit is a more sustainable, better-integrated system, with improved patient flow, quality and access to services.

DARS-NIC-199574-S1W3N.summary: NHS Leicester, Leicestershire and Rutland Integrated Care Board (ICB)'s agreement covers the use of Secondary User Services (SUS+) hospital activity data, linked to GP data, for one purpose. The data is for checking that provider invoices are for patients the commissioner is responsible for, and for identifying patients at high risk so their care can be planned and managed. The main intended benefit is more accurate payment for care and better targeted support for at-risk patients.

DARS-NIC-199584-M8L6H.summary: NHS Leicester, Leicestershire and Rutland ICB's agreement covers Secondary User Services (SUS+) hospital activity data, identifiable by NHS number, for two purposes. The first is invoice validation, checking that the care providers bill for is the commissioner's responsibility. The second is risk stratification, linking the data with GP records to identify patients at high risk. The main intended benefits are accurate payment for care and better targeted, planned care.

DARS-NIC-199599-S0T5M.summary: NHS Leicester, Leicestershire and Rutland ICB (a sub-ICB location) is covered by an agreement allowing it to use mental health and hospital activity data (Mental Health Services Data Set and SUS for Commissioners). The data is for checking that provider invoices are for patients it is responsible for, and for identifying patients at high risk of poor health so GPs and commissioners can plan their care. The main intended benefit is more accurate payment and more targeted, effective care that improves patient outcomes.

DARS-NIC-199682-T1L7Z.summary: The University of Cambridge's MRC Epidemiology Unit's agreement covers the use of address details for participants in the WRAP weight management trial, taken from the Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) list cleaning report. The agreement allows the data to update contact records, trace participants who have moved and avoid contacting those who have died, so the unit can invite them to 5- and 10-year follow-up studies. The data is for giving policy makers and commissioners stronger evidence on which weight management programmes offer value for money.

DARS-NIC-199726-F4V3C.summary: King's College London's agreement covers the use of hospital admission and outpatient records, together with civil registration death data, for the National Early Inflammatory Arthritis Audit. The audit assesses how well rheumatology units in England and Wales follow NICE quality standards, aiming to reduce variation in care and improve outcomes. Reported results include the Care Quality Commission using audit-based metrics in its reviews, and a Best Practice Tariff linked to audit data.

DARS-NIC-200139-H2X2Y.summary: Kingston University's Institute for Leadership and Management in Health's agreement covers pseudonymised hospital inpatient and outpatient records from 2015 to 2018. The data is for estimating the direct medical cost to the NHS of nine major diseases caused by HPV (human papillomavirus) across the UK. The aim is to give policy makers evidence on resource use and possible savings as the HPV vaccination programme extends to boys.

DARS-NIC-201077-P0V6T.summary: NHS Sheffield CCG's agreement covers hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other health service datasets, some identifiable by NHS number and some pseudonymised. The agreement allows the data to be used to validate provider invoices, identify patients at high risk so their care can be prioritised, and plan and monitor health services for the local population. The main intended benefit is more effective commissioning, leading to a better patient experience.

DARS-NIC-201243-R7L2M.summary: The Department of Health and Social Care's agreement covers pseudonymised NHS Health Check records for adults aged 40-74, linked to hospital admission and death records. The data is for evaluating and monitoring the programme and for seeing how patients' health outcomes differ. The aim is to help local services improve delivery and target support. Findings have already informed the 2021 NHS Health Check review, published papers and an interactive dashboard, and the announced inclusion of menopause in NHS Health Checks.

DARS-NIC-202004-C5F6G.summary: Bedford Borough Council's agreement covers the use of hospital and emergency care records (Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set) to support its public health duties. The agreement allows analysis to produce needs assessments, health strategies, the annual public health report and advice to NHS commissioners. The main intended benefit is locally focused analysis of health inequalities, so the needs of disadvantaged groups are identified and addressed. No benefits have been reported yet.

DARS-NIC-203503-X7K8K.summary: The University of Surrey's agreement covers hospital records (accident and emergency, admitted patient care and outpatients) and mortality data linked to the LOLIPOP study of about 30,000 Indian Asian adults. The data is for building models and assessing the cost-effectiveness of a new cardiovascular disease risk estimator for British Asians. The main intended benefit is helping clinicians decide how intensively to treat this group, improving health outcomes and reducing healthcare costs.

DARS-NIC-203509-L9P1P.summary: Health Innovation Network - South London, an Academic Health Science Network, has an agreement that allows it to use Hospital Episode Statistics data on accident and emergency, admitted patient care, critical care and outpatients. The agreement allows the data to be used to produce aggregated reports on demand for services, variations in care and the impact of service improvements. The intended benefit is better, safer and more efficient care, with investment decisions informed by evidence about what works.

DARS-NIC-203730-Y4V0Z.summary: The University of Bristol's agreement covers linked hospital admission and death registration data for about 40,890 patients who had lower limb vascular surgery in the National Vascular Registry between 2014 and 2016. The agreement allows evaluation of patient outcomes, including re-admissions and deaths, in the 12 months after surgery. The data is for giving clinicians and patients better information to guide treatment decisions.

DARS-NIC-204228-D8J4D.summary: The Nuffield Trust for Research and Policy Studies in Health Services, an independent health research charity, has an agreement that allows it to use hospital records for children and young people. These cover accident and emergency, admitted patient care and outpatient care. The agreement is for studying the causes of variation in emergency admissions for under 5s and of poor child health outcomes. The aim is to give national and local decision makers evidence to improve services and outcomes for children and young people.

DARS-NIC-204376-Y0V5Y.summary: Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers linked hospital, emergency care, outpatient, critical care and death records for patients with remotely monitored heart devices. The data is for evaluating the Triage-HF Plus pathway, in which patients with a high heart failure risk score are phoned to check for symptoms. The aim is to assess hospital admissions, deaths and healthcare use, and to guide improvements to care. A 2024 paper reported an association with fewer hospital admissions, and the data were submitted to a NICE review.

DARS-NIC-204512-H4R8C.summary: The Northern Cancer Alliance, a network whose staff are employed by NHS England, is permitted to use National Cancer Waiting Times Monitoring Data Set records on the time from referral to cancer diagnosis and treatment. The agreement allows the data to be used to compare waiting-time performance across hospital trusts and CCGs, spot delays and outliers, and inform discussions on improving cancer pathways. The aim is to help meet national waiting-time standards and improve survival and patient experience. Earlier use of this data has already supported monthly provider reports, funding bids and clinical group discussions.

DARS-NIC-204517-W3N5Z.summary: West Midlands Cancer Alliance, a network hosted by NHS England (West Midlands), has an agreement covering National Cancer Waiting Times Monitoring Data Set records from the Cancer Wait Times system. The agreement allows analysis of waiting times across hospitals and clinical commissioning groups to find variation and delays in cancer pathways, aiming to improve survival and patient experience. Earlier access has already informed performance reporting, executive advisory group discussions and work on 104-day breaches.

DARS-NIC-204520-B1V2G.summary: West Yorkshire and Harrogate Cancer Alliance, a network hosted by NHS West Yorkshire Integrated Care Board, is permitted to use National Cancer Waiting Times Monitoring Data Set records. The agreement allows the Alliance to analyse waiting times across cancer pathways, identify variation and long waits, and inform discussions with hospitals and commissioners. The aim is to help meet waiting time standards and improve cancer survival and patient experience. The Alliance reports it has already built dashboards and tumour-specific data packs that were used to drive targeted improvement work with trusts.

DARS-NIC-204531-P5L8G.summary: Humber, Coast and Vale Cancer Alliance's agreement names NHS East Riding of Yorkshire Clinical Commissioning Group as the legal data controller. The agreement allows use of patient-level National Cancer Waiting Times Monitoring Data Set data. The data is for analysing waiting times and variation across hospital trusts and CCGs, to help improve cancer pathways, survival and patient experience. Reported results may include performance dashboards, and analysis used in bids that secured £780k of 62 day recovery funding.

DARS-NIC-204535-L4S1P.summary: Nottingham University Hospitals NHS Trust, which employs the East Midland Cancer Alliance's staff, has an agreement covering National Cancer Waiting Times Monitoring Data Set data from NHS England. The agreement allows analysis of cancer waiting times by trust, clinical commissioning group (CCG) and tumour site, to find variation and long waits and to work with providers on improving patient pathways. The intended benefit is better survival and patient experience through meeting national waiting time standards. Earlier access has already supported regional analyses of 2 week, 31 day and 62 day performance.

DARS-NIC-204544-H5L0S.summary: Peninsula Cancer Alliance, working with the Somerset, Wiltshire, Avon and Gloucestershire Cancer Alliance, is covered by an agreement to use National Cancer Waiting Times Monitoring Data Set data covering referral to cancer treatment. The data is for comparing waiting-time performance, finding variation and long waits, and informing cancer pathway improvements. The main intended benefit is helping meet national cancer waiting times standards. Earlier access supported monthly provider reports, pathway mapping and funding bids.

DARS-NIC-204548-T8H8P.summary: Greater Manchester Cancer Alliance, with the Christie NHS Foundation Trust as the lead organisation, is permitted to use National Cancer Waiting Times Monitoring Data Set data from the Cancer Wait Times system. The agreement allows analysis of waiting times across providers and tumour types to find variation and delays, and to guide investment in cancer pathways. The main intended benefit is better performance against national cancer waiting standards, supporting survival and patient experience. Earlier work with similar data included reporting on waiting-time targets and evaluating a shorter referral-to-first-seen period for lung cancer.

DARS-NIC-204550-N7M4D.summary: Kent and Medway Cancer Alliance's agreement covers use of National Cancer Waiting Times Monitoring Data Set records from the Cancer Wait Times system. The agreement allows analysis of waiting times for cancer diagnosis and treatment, identification of variation between hospital trusts and areas, and examination of patient flows and long waits. The main intended benefit is better cancer pathways, helping meet waiting time standards and improving survival and patient experience. Earlier analysis supported monthly reports for provider leaders, funding bids and clinical group discussions.

DARS-NIC-204554-Y7F3H.summary: South East London Cancer Alliance, hosted by Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust, has an agreement to use patient-level National Cancer Waiting Times Monitoring Data Set records. The agreement allows the data to be analysed for waiting times, patient flows and variation between providers and areas. The aim is to improve cancer pathways, survival and patient experience. The alliance reports that the data has helped improve performance in Breast and Head and Neck pathways.

DARS-NIC-204557-F0N1T.summary: Thames Valley Cancer Alliance, whose staff are employed by NHS England, is allowed to use Cancer Waiting Times data covering referral to treatment for cancer patients across the Thames Valley. The agreement allows analysis of waiting times, variation between hospitals and commissioners, and patient pathways to guide priorities and investment. The aim is better survival, patient experience and performance against national cancer standards. Earlier work included inter-trust referral analysis and a prostate cancer pathway analysis.

DARS-NIC-204559-J4H7T.summary: Lancashire & South Cumbria Cancer Alliance, whose staff are employed by NHS England, is permitted to use patient-level National Cancer Waiting Times Monitoring Data Set records. The agreement allows analysis of waiting times by tumour type, trust and treatment to find variation and long waits, and to inform cancer pathway improvements and investment. The main aim is to help meet cancer waiting times standards and improve survival and patient experience. Earlier work has produced monthly performance reports and used breach reasons to identify capacity and demand issues at trusts.

DARS-NIC-204562-J5W0T.summary: South Yorkshire & Bassetlaw Cancer Alliance's agreement covers its staff, who are employed by NHS Doncaster Clinical Commissioning Group, and allows use of aggregate Cancer Waiting Times data that includes small numbers. The data is for analysing local performance by hospital trust and tumour site, and for identifying variation in waits. The main intended benefit is better cancer pathways, helping meet waiting time standards and improving patient survival and experience. Earlier access to similar data has been used to inform service improvement.

DARS-NIC-204565-L5J5F.summary: North Central London Cancer Alliance, a cancer services network, is permitted to use National Cancer Waiting Times Monitoring Data Set data from the Cancer Wait Times system. The agreement allows analysis of waiting times along cancer pathways, including variation between hospital trusts, to guide priorities and investment. The aim is to help meet national waiting time standards and improve cancer survival and patient experience. Earlier use of similar data supported funding bids, capacity and demand analysis, and service commissioning.

DARS-NIC-204571-R1F4T.summary: East of England - North Cancer Alliance, whose staff are mainly employed by NHS England, is using the National Cancer Waiting Times Monitoring Data Set, which records patients' waits from referral to cancer diagnosis and treatment. It will analyse waiting times by hospital trust, tumour type and treatment, and look for delays and unusual cases. The aim is to help the alliance and local providers improve cancer patient pathways, survival and patient experience.
DARS-NIC-204571-R1F4T.retense_draft: East of England - North Cancer Alliance's agreement covers its use of the National Cancer Waiting Times Monitoring Data Set, which records patients' waits from referral to cancer diagnosis and treatment. The agreement allows analysis of waiting times by hospital trust, tumour type and treatment, to look for delays and unusual cases. The aim is to help the alliance and local providers improve cancer patient pathways, survival and patient experience.

DARS-NIC-204575-V7X8H.summary: Wessex Cancer Alliance's agreement, hosted by NHS England, covers the use of National Cancer Waiting Times Monitoring Data Set data from the Cancer Wait Times system. The agreement allows analysis of waiting times across Wessex providers and commissioners, identification of variation and unusually long waits, and informing discussions on improving cancer pathways. The main intended benefit is better delivery of national cancer waiting time standards, supporting survival and patient experience.

DARS-NIC-204580-F5B0C.summary: The Clatterbridge Cancer Centre NHS Foundation Trust, on behalf of the Cheshire and Merseyside Cancer Alliance, has an agreement covering the use of National Cancer Waiting Times Monitoring Data Set records from the Cancer Wait Times system. The agreement allows analysis of waiting times and variation between providers and tumour sites, and of waits beyond the national standards. The data is for guiding priorities and investment to improve cancer pathways and patient outcomes. Earlier access has already supported monthly reports for provider discussions and funding bids.

DARS-NIC-204646-B9G2N.summary: The University of Newcastle upon Tyne is using pseudonymised hospital activity data (SUS for Commissioners), linked to GP and Ways to Wellness records, to evaluate a social prescribing scheme in the West End of Newcastle. DARS-NIC-205004-D2F8N.summary: The NIHR (National Institute for Health Research) Bioresource's agreement allows it to use Personal Demographic Service data to check participants' identities and whether they have died. DARS-NIC-205466-T2F7N.summary: The University of York's agreement covers the use of Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care data on coronary stenting procedures, linked by the General Medical Council to its records on doctors' characteristics. It is a first step towards modelling clinical behaviour. If differences are found, they could support research on reducing unwarranted variation in medical practice.

DARS-NIC-206314-N1N7K.summary: Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers hospital records of accident and emergency attendances and admitted patient care for older people with implantable cardiac devices who have joined the PATTErn study. The main intended benefit is better understanding of this link, which could help clinicians use device activity data and inform future research.

DARS-NIC-206496-N2C9M.summary: Walsall Metropolitan Borough Council's agreement covers civil registration data on births and deaths, plus primary care mortality data, which includes identifiable details. DARS-NIC-207675-J4L7G.summary: King's College London's agreement covers use of the 2014 Adult Psychiatric Morbidity Survey, a nationally representative survey of adults, to study whether mental illness is linked to perpetrating domestic violence. The aim is to inform how mental health services respond to perpetrators. A paper on intimate partner violence perpetration among secondary mental health service users has been published in BJPsych Open.

DARS-NIC-207953-Q9H2M.summary: The University of Bristol's agreement covers Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) data, including personal demographics, cohort event notifications such as deaths and cancer registrations, and current status flagging.
