The data is for producing risk stratification scores, which GP practices can view for their registered patients to support team discussions about ongoing care. The CCG sees only a pseudonymised view. The main intended benefit is better case management in primary care, including fewer avoidable emergency admissions.

DARS-NIC-22520-J3P7F.summary: NHS Leeds North CCG's agreement covers hospital activity data from Secondary Uses Service (SUS) records for accident and emergency, inpatient and outpatient care, identifiable by NHS number. The data is for producing risk scores for patients, which GP practices can view through a secure portal to support care discussions. The CCG sees only aggregate or pseudonymised views. The main expected benefit is better case management in primary care, including fewer avoidable emergency admissions.

DARS-NIC-22525-D4K1B.summary: NHS Leeds South and East CCG's agreement covers Secondary Uses Service (SUS) hospital data for accident and emergency, inpatient and outpatient activity, including NHS numbers. The data is for producing risk scores for registered patients, which the CCG and GP practices can view through a secure web portal. GP practices can see identifiable data for their own patients, while the CCG sees only pseudonymised data. The main intended benefit is better case management in primary care, including fewer avoidable emergency admissions.

DARS-NIC-22526-R6K4D.summary: NHS Leeds West CCG (Clinical Commissioning Group) is covered by an agreement that allows it to use Secondary Uses Service (SUS) hospital data covering accident and emergency, inpatient and outpatient activity, identifiable by NHS number. The data is for producing risk scores for registered patients, which GP practices can view in a secure portal to support care discussions. The CCG sees only a pseudonymised view. The expected benefit is better case management in primary care, including fewer avoidable emergency admissions.

DARS-NIC-22537-H4J9R.summary: NHS North Kirklees CCG's agreement covers the use of hospital activity data (Accident & Emergency, inpatient and outpatient records from SUS), identifiable by NHS number. The data is for producing risk scores for registered patients, which GP practices can view through a secure web portal and the CCG can view only in pseudonymised form. The main intended benefit is better case management in primary care, including fewer avoidable emergency admissions.

DARS-NIC-22542-R0Q7P.summary: NHS Wakefield CCG's agreement covers Secondary Uses Service (SUS) hospital data covering accident and emergency, inpatient and outpatient activity, identifiable by NHS number. The data is for risk stratification, which gives GP practices a risk score for their registered patients through the eMBED CPM web-tool. The intended benefit is to support multi-disciplinary team discussions about ongoing patient care and enhanced service requirements.

DARS-NIC-225591-Z2B1C.summary: NHS Shropshire, Telford and Wrekin ICB's agreement allows pseudonymised (identifying details removed) health and care data, covering hospital, community, mental health, maternity, cancer, births and deaths records, with clinical and financial information. The agreement allows NHS Midlands and Lancashire Commissioning Support Unit to process it to plan and commission health services for the local population, including understanding needs, redesigning services and identifying patients at risk. The main intended benefit is better planning of services and patient flow.

DARS-NIC-225927-H5J7J.summary: Surrey and Sussex Cancer Alliance, through its lead employer Royal Surrey NHS Foundation Trust, is covered by an agreement that allows use of national Cancer Waiting Times data covering referral to cancer treatment. The agreement allows analysis of waits and variation between trusts, clinical commissioning groups and tumour types to guide priorities and investment, aiming to improve cancer pathways, survival and patient experience. Monthly data packs and dashboards are produced for trusts that have identified outliers and have prompted local improvement work.

DARS-NIC-226185-B6C2J.summary: The University of Hull's agreement allows the use of hospital records from England covering admissions and emergency department attendances. The data is for studying people with alcohol dependence and alcohol withdrawal, looking at what predicts readmission and repeat attendance, including length of stay. The aim is to inform better care pathways for people admitted with unplanned alcohol withdrawal. The data has supported a successful funding bid for an Alcohol Care Team at Hull Royal Infirmary.

DARS-NIC-226261-M2T0Q.summary: The Nuffield Trust's agreement covers hospital, emergency care and community services patient data from NHS England. The data is for researching the quality and fairness of health and social care and informing health policy, with the aim of improving services and care for NHS patients. Its reported results include a report on ethnicity coding that the Race Disparity Unit adopted, and a children's health analysis presented to a national council.

DARS-NIC-226296-S7T2Y.summary: NHS Mid and South Essex Integrated Care Board (ICB)'s agreement covers the use of Secondary User Services (SUS+) hospital data, linked with GP records, to identify patients at high risk of health deterioration or heavy service use. Prescribing Services Limited carries out the risk scoring. The data is for helping GPs target care and helping commissioners plan services, reducing avoidable emergency admissions and improving patient experience.

DARS-NIC-226323-X4L5B.summary: The Institute of Cancer Research's agreement covers the use of cancer registration, death and NHS registration data to follow up 24,510 women who had HPV testing in the ARTISTIC trial. The agreement allows the assessment of the long-term value of HPV testing as a primary cervical screening method. The data is for giving policy-makers evidence to improve the cervical screening programme in the UK and elsewhere.

DARS-NIC-226549-V6R5F.summary: NHS Somerset CCG's agreement covers hospital, community, mental health, maternity, ambulance and other health service data, linked to GP data at NHS number level. The data is for risk stratification, which applies an algorithm to identify patients at high risk of poor outcomes. This allows commissioners to plan services and GPs to target care for those patients. The main intended benefit is more effective commissioning and a better patient experience.

DARS-NIC-226588-V0F1Z.summary: NHS East Lancashire CCG's agreement allows it to use linked hospital (SUS+) and GP data about patients, identifiable by NHS number, along with other NHS datasets covering areas such as mental health, maternity, community and ambulance services. The data is for risk stratification, which applies an algorithm to predict which patients are at high risk, so the CCG and GPs can plan care and target interventions. The main intended benefit is better planning and fewer avoidable emergency admissions.

DARS-NIC-226603-C7K2R.summary: NHS Kent and Medway Integrated Care Board (ICB) uses SUS for Commissioners data, which is hospital activity data linked to GP data at NHS number level. It uses this for risk stratification, which gives patients risk scores to identify who is likely to need high levels of care. GPs and commissioners can then target care and plan services. The stated aim is better case management in primary care and more effective commissioning.
DARS-NIC-226603-C7K2R.retense_draft: NHS Kent and Medway Integrated Care Board's agreement covers the use of SUS for Commissioners data, which is hospital activity data linked to GP data at NHS number level. The data is for risk stratification, which gives patients risk scores to identify who is likely to need high levels of care. GPs and commissioners can then target care and plan services. The stated aim is better case management in primary care and more effective commissioning.

DARS-NIC-226613-D8S2N.summary: NHS Cornwall and the Isles of Scilly ICB's agreement covers the use of hospital activity data (SUS for Commissioners), linked with GP data, to run risk stratification. This is to identify patients at high risk of health deterioration or heavy use of services, so GPs and commissioners can plan and target their care. Prescribing Services Limited carries out the processing. The main intended benefit is better planned and more effective care, including fewer avoidable emergency admissions.

DARS-NIC-226652-N1G2N.summary: Barts Health NHS Trust's agreement covers mortality records, including cause of death and current status, for 1,019 women recorded as deceased who had been removed ("ceased") from breast screening in central and east London. The agreement allows checks on whether they have died, whether any died from breast cancer, and whether any recorded as dead are still alive and not being offered screening. The main intended benefit is that any women found to be alive could be offered screening, and that families would know whether the removal caused harm.

DARS-NIC-228637-P6N0L.summary: Imperial College London's agreement covers hospital-level National Diabetes Audit data on young adults aged 16 to 25 with diabetes. The data is for the TOGETHER study, which evaluates group clinics for young adults. The analysis will compare study clinics with other services in England on patient make-up, treatment targets and care processes, and track changes over time. It aims to show whether clinical outcomes worsen where group clinics are introduced.

DARS-NIC-228903-Z0F4V.summary: Royal Free London NHS Foundation Trust, for the Transforming Cancer Services Team (London), is permitted to use national cancer waiting times data. The agreement allows the team to analyse it across London to compare performance, spot variation and support discussions on improving cancer patient pathways. The aim is shorter waits for diagnosis and treatment, and better survival and patient experience. Reported results include informing London recovery planning after COVID-19 and supporting a redesign of the sarcoma pathway.

DARS-NIC-230360-H3Y3C.summary: Erasmus University Rotterdam's agreement covers the use of civil registration death data to find out whether UK patients from the SYNTAX heart trial are alive or have died. The SYNTAXES study is for assessing survival of more than 10 years after patients had either a stent procedure (PCI) or bypass surgery (CABG) for coronary artery disease. The main intended benefit is long-term evidence to help doctors choose the best treatment.

DARS-NIC-230509-D4R8J.summary: The University of Birmingham's agreement covers the use of NHS registration data and Office for National Statistics (ONS) mortality data, including dates and causes of death, through the Medical Research Information Service (MRIS). The data is for a study of care home residents to find how often venous thromboembolism (blood clots in the veins) occurs, including related deaths and hospital admissions. The aim is to understand prevention and treatment and to improve risk assessment for residents with complex health needs.

DARS-NIC-230538-B9J9Z.summary: City of Wolverhampton Council's agreement covers the use of death registration records and hospital activity data for commissioners. It allows linking these with local health and social care data to show what services people use, and what is spent, in the last year of life. The data is for helping local partners redesign services so more people have a good death at home or in their preferred place, while using money sustainably.

DARS-NIC-231737-J7C6H.summary: NHS West Yorkshire ICB, acting for the Airedale and Wharfedale area, is permitted to use pseudonymised (identifying details removed) hospital, community, mental health, maternity, ambulance, primary care and births and deaths data. The agreement allows this data to be used to plan and commission health services, including studying population needs, redesigning services and identifying patients at risk of hospital admission. The main intended benefit is better planning of services and patient flow, with fewer avoidable emergency admissions.

DARS-NIC-233512-B7C4W.summary: NEC Software Solutions UK Limited, a commercial company acting for the Society of British Neurological Surgeons, is permitted to use pseudonymised hospital admission and death registration records for people who have had neurosurgery in England. The agreement allows the records to be used to run the Neurosurgical National Audit Programme, which checks surgical outcomes, including deaths, and identifies trusts or surgeons with outlying performance. The aim is to improve patient safety and outcomes. Reported results include published papers and trust reports that helped GIRFT direct resources to the trusts most in need.

DARS-NIC-23410-W8N9L.summary: The University of Manchester, an academic organisation, used hospital records covering admissions, outpatient and A&E care, patient-reported outcomes and death registrations. It used them to study how the Care Quality Commission's inspection and rating system affects hospital performance and quality of care, so the Department of Health and Social Care can improve it. The final report went to the department and the Commission, five journal articles were published, and the findings were presented to the Commission's board.

DARS-NIC-234297-P4M5G.summary: University College London (UCL), an academic organisation, is permitted to use linked hospital, national audit and death registration data on people with congenital heart disease. The data is for describing how patients use NHS services over time and for developing measures of long-term outcomes, so that commissioners and clinicians can improve services. Reported results include nine peer-reviewed papers from each of the two studies, and an updated risk model (PRAiS v4) adopted into clinical practice.

DARS-NIC-234656-C3J1D.summary: University College London (UCL)'s agreement covers linked hospital admission records and demographic data for children born in England between 2005 and 2014, along with their mothers' delivery records. The agreement allows study of how air pollution, housing conditions, and family factors such as parents' country of birth affect children's hospital admissions, especially for respiratory infections and preventable conditions. The aim is to give local authorities and NHS bodies evidence to improve child health and access to care. So far, findings have been presented at two conferences, and a paper has been submitted to a journal.

DARS-NIC-234915-J3K4V.summary: NHS Staffordshire and Stoke-on-Trent ICB's agreement covers working for six Staffordshire clinical commissioning groups, and allows the use of pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, maternity, prescribing and death and birth records, which include clinical and financial information. The data is for planning and commissioning health services, such as reviewing patient pathways, forecasting demand and monitoring providers. The aim is to match services to the population's needs. The CCGs have reported that the data helped them monitor in-year projects and deliver integrated care.

DARS-NIC-237669-T9W5N.summary: The University of Nottingham's agreement covers pseudonymised hospital admission records (Hospital Episode Statistics), linked to death registration data, for patients who had surgery between 2007 and 2017. The study looks at how earlier strokes and heart attacks affect outcomes after surgery, and how this varies by timing, treatment and type of operation. The intended benefit is better information to help patients and clinicians decide whether and when to operate.

DARS-NIC-238282-X0B6H.summary: NHS Coventry and Warwickshire ICB's agreement covers pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, ambulance and other health service data, linked with GP data, covering the Coventry and Warwickshire area. The data is for planning and commissioning health services, understanding local health needs and identifying patients at risk, with the aim of improving patient pathways and services. Under an earlier approval, South Warwickshire CCG used linked data to show which trialled services helped patients, supporting decisions to expand funding or adjust services.

DARS-NIC-238370-G8Z6V.summary: NHS Bristol, North Somerset and South Gloucestershire ICB's agreement covers hospital records for accident and emergency, admitted patient care and outpatient activity. The data is for building statistical models that produce growth projections and length of stay estimates by specialty, supporting local operational planning. The agreement allows national data to be used to make these estimates more accurate and reliable than local data alone. Initial length of stay work by specialty has already been used to update a length of stay fitting tool in open source simulation software built by the team.

DARS-NIC-238613-D3W0L.summary: The University of Oxford's agreement covers pseudonymised hospital admission records, patient reported outcome measures and death registration data, linked to National Joint Registry data. The data is for studying how implant choice, surgical approach and patient frailty relate to results after a first knee replacement, such as quality of life, mortality and revision surgery. The intended benefit is better-informed shared decisions for patients, clinicians and NHS commissioners.

DARS-NIC-239092-Q9Q3X.summary: Epsom and St Helier University Hospitals NHS Trust's agreement covers pseudonymised maternity records from the Maternity Services Data Set, covering 2017/18 to 2021/22. The agreement allows study of maternal and fetal factors linked to stillbirths, especially term stillbirths, and differences between ethnic groups. The data is for improving evidence on risk so that care for pregnant women and their babies, particularly from Black, Asian and minority ethnic backgrounds, can be better tailored and stillbirths reduced.

DARS-NIC-239975-C0K0X.summary: NHS North and East London Commissioning Support Unit's agreement covers Hospital Episode Statistics (HES) data for A&E, critical care, inpatient and outpatient care. The agreement allows named staff to analyse it to produce aggregate outputs for benchmarking across north and east London. The data is for supporting commissioning planning, service reconfiguration, weekend urgent care evaluation and a local COPD service review, aiming to find better outcomes and financial efficiencies.

DARS-NIC-240279-Y2V2N.summary: The University of Oxford's agreement covers linked hospital, emergency care and civil registration death records, which are linked to the QResearch database of pseudonymised GP records. The data is for medical research into causes of disease, drug safety and risk prediction tools, including urgent COVID-19 research. The aim is to give patients, the NHS and researchers a better understanding of disease. Its research has already informed NICE guidelines, and QRISK3 was implemented in the NHS from 2018.

DARS-NIC-241634-Z3F2L.summary: NHS West Yorkshire ICB, working with NHS North Kirklees and NHS Wakefield Clinical Commissioning Groups, is permitted to use pseudonymised hospital, ambulance, community, diagnostic and emergency care data that includes clinical and financial information. The data is for planning and commissioning health services, monitoring contracts, and understanding the needs of the local population. The main intended benefit is better planning of patient pathways and services.

DARS-NIC-242146-J2W3T.summary: The University of Birmingham's agreement covers hospital records from NHS England (accident and emergency, admitted patient care, critical care and outpatients), linked to GP data from The Health Improvement Network. The data is for epidemiology, health services, public health and health economics research, including studies of childbirth and maternal health. The aim is to produce findings that can change clinical practice and policy, for example by informing NICE guidance on antibiotics given during caesarean sections.

DARS-NIC-242415-V9T5D.summary: University College London's Medical Research Council Clinical Trials Unit's agreement covers the use of pseudonymised hospital admissions and accident and emergency records (Hospital Episode Statistics). The data is for comparing heart and circulation events in these records with those collected in the PATCH prostate cancer trial. The aim is to test whether national electronic records could supplement or partly replace manual trial follow-up, which could reduce costs and workload and mean fewer hospital visits for participants.

DARS-NIC-242486-R1G4D.summary: The University of Sheffield's agreement covers the use of survey data from the Adult Psychiatric Morbidity Survey, covering adults aged 16 or over. It allows study of how psychosis overlaps with conditions such as bipolar disorder, post-traumatic stress disorder and autism, and how childhood trauma and social factors relate to psychotic symptoms. The data is for improving understanding of mental illness and informing treatment and public mental health. A 2021 paper in Psychological Medicine reported a strong association between autistic traits and psychotic-like experiences.

DARS-NIC-243221-N3B9W.summary: Lincolnshire County Council's public health teams use Hospital Episode Statistics (HES) data on accident and emergency, inpatient and outpatient care. They analyse it to monitor disease trends, assess health needs, measure health inequalities and understand risks such as injury, self harm and cancer presentations. Results are intended to be published as non-identifiable summary reports and graphs, to inform health and care services, interventions and policy.

DARS-NIC-243359-X4T5M.summary: The Cambridge Centre for Health Services Research's agreement covers work with partner universities and RAND Europe on the BRACE NIHR Rapid Evaluation Centre. The agreement allows use of pseudonymised, record-level hospital data: emergency care, admitted patient, A&E and outpatient records. The data is for quick evaluations of new ways of organising and delivering health and care services. The main intended benefit is high-quality evidence that helps decide which innovations to adopt and which not to pursue.

DARS-NIC-243790-Y8K8C.summary: Carnall Farrar Limited, a consultancy, has an agreement covering record-level hospital, emergency care, outpatient, community and mental health data from NHS England. The agreement allows the data to be used to build analysis tools and reports for NHS organisations and other clients, covering forecasting, capacity planning, benchmarking and population health. The aim is to help the NHS find where performance, efficiency and finances can improve. Reported results include a Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust elective recovery plan and a south-east London mental health bed capacity model.

DARS-NIC-24422-R3W3S.summary: The University of Cambridge's agreement covers the use of NHS England hospital, emergency care, cancer registration and death records for a randomised trial of vitamin D (colecalciferol) supplementation in people with kidney failure on dialysis. The agreement allows the data to check the trial's main outcomes, including survival, and to follow participants over the long term without further contact. The aim is to show whether colecalciferol is a safe, cheaper alternative that improves survival. So far, the data has supported safety reviews, and aggregated results have informed trial committee decisions.

DARS-NIC-244278-F3V4X.summary: NHS Northamptonshire ICB, acting for the former Corby clinical commissioning group (CCG) area, is permitted to use pseudonymised health and care data, including clinical and financial information from hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other services. The data is for planning and commissioning health services, including population health analysis, service redesign and identifying patients at risk. The main intended benefit is better planning of services and patient pathways to meet local needs.

DARS-NIC-245768-V0N2T.summary: Queen Mary University of London's agreement covers the use of cancer registration, death registration and demographic data to study men with prostate cancer managed by watchful waiting. The aim is to build and test models that predict which cancers will progress, and to see whether biological markers improve on standard clinical factors. The main intended benefit is helping patients and clinicians decide who can safely avoid unnecessary radical treatment. Published papers, including a 2021 Cancer Reports validation of a cell cycle progression score, have already come from the study.

DARS-NIC-245962-Y6W3Z.summary: Walsall Metropolitan Borough Council's agreement allows it to use hospital and emergency care records (Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set) to support its public health duties. These include needs assessments, health strategies and advice to NHS commissioners, with the aim of analysing local health inequalities. Reported results include informing its air quality and suicide prevention strategies, and sharing analysis of violence-related admissions with West Midlands Police.

DARS-NIC-24629-X6B6N.summary: IQVIA Solutions UK Limited's agreement covers the use of hospital records (accident and emergency, admitted patient care, critical care and outpatients) linked to The Health Improvement Network (THIN) GP records. The data is for medical research, including drug safety, into how primary and hospital care relate. Published studies using the linked data include a smoking study featured in a NICE press release and a frailty index that NICE recommends in its multimorbidity guideline.

DARS-NIC-24688-J6W3F.summary: The Royal Borough of Kingston upon Thames, a local authority, has an agreement covering Hospital Episode Statistics and Emergency Care Data Set records on hospital admissions, outpatient, critical care and A&E activity. The agreement allows the data to be used for its public health duties, including needs assessments, health strategies, commissioning and advice to NHS commissioners. The main intended benefit is locally focused analysis of health inequalities. A new joint strategic needs assessment was released in 2023.

DARS-NIC-24810-Q6T3B.summary: The University of Birmingham holds hospital records (Hospital Episode Statistics covering A&E, admitted patient care, critical care and outpatients) and civil registration death data for people in its COPD cohort study. Under this agreement the data is only kept securely, with no new processing. The original study used it to build prognostic models predicting hospital admissions and death in people with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), to support better patient management and service planning.

DARS-NIC-248117-P2K4S.summary: St Helens Council's public health team's agreement covers hospital records from Hospital Episode Statistics (HES) and the Emergency Care Data Set, covering accident and emergency, admitted patient care, critical care and outpatients. The data is for supporting its public health duties, including needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, the annual public health report and advice to NHS commissioners. The intended benefit is locally focused analysis of health and health inequalities, so that local health challenges are identified and responded to.

DARS-NIC-249035-R2Z5Y.summary: Northumbria Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers hospital admission, accident and emergency, critical care and death registration records for patients ventilated during COPD (chronic obstructive pulmonary disease) flare-ups. The agreement allows the data to follow readmissions and deaths for a year after discharge and to validate a bedside tool that predicts death. The main intended benefit is wider use of lifesaving non-invasive ventilation through better clinical decisions.

DARS-NIC-250023-M6T9H.summary: Public Health Scotland's agreement covers the use of hospital admissions data for England (Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care), limited to alcohol-related conditions. The data is for comparing alcohol-attributable hospital admissions and deaths in Scotland with England, to assess the impact of minimum unit pricing for alcohol, introduced in Scotland in May 2018. The findings could help the Scottish Parliament decide whether the policy should continue.

DARS-NIC-25007-J9M9P.summary: Birmingham City Council's public health team's agreement covers hospital records (Hospital Episode Statistics) and mental health data from NHS England. The agreement allows the data to support its public health and commissioning duties, including needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies and the Director of Public Health's annual report. The aim is locally focused analysis of health outcomes and inequalities, benchmarked against similar areas. Reported results include a substance misuse needs assessment that informed the commissioning of drug and alcohol treatment services.

DARS-NIC-250100-R3W1G.summary: Glasgow Caledonian University's agreement covers a list cleaning report giving current names, addresses and whether people have died, for women in the ProLong study originally recruited in Birmingham. The agreement allows the University to use this to contact them accurately for ProLong20+, a follow-up study of pelvic floor problems after childbirth, such as incontinence and prolapse. The main intended benefit is a better response rate and better knowledge of how these problems change over time, helping to plan future NHS services.

DARS-NIC-250326-W3F1B.summary: NHS North East and North Cumbria ICB (Sunderland area)'s agreement covers the use of pseudonymised hospital and mental health data, including clinical and financial information. The agreement allows this data to be used to plan and commission health services, covering population health management, service redesign and identifying patients at risk. The main intended benefit is better planning of services and patient pathways. Population segmentation is intended to feed into commissioning decisions and service transformation.

DARS-NIC-252024-D7R9W.summary: The Royal College of Paediatrics & Child Health (RCPCH) agreement covers the use of Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care data for the National Paediatric Diabetes Audit. The agreement allows analysis of hospital admissions of children and young people with diabetes in a five-year comparative report, to show admission trends and support efforts to reduce admissions. Earlier analysis under a previous agreement was used by commissioners when deciding how to fund diabetes-related technologies.

DARS-NIC-252496-Z7M8H.summary: NHS Dorset ICB (a sub-ICB location) uses Secondary User Services (SUS+) hospital data, identifiable by NHS number, to check invoices from care providers and to carry out risk stratification. Invoice validation, done by Liaison Financial Services Ltd, confirms that charges are the CCG's responsibility and identifies overpayments to recover. Risk stratification, done by Prescribing Services Limited, links the data with GP data to identify patients at high risk so care can be planned and targeted. The main intended benefits are recovering money that would otherwise be lost and improved, more effective care.
DARS-NIC-252496-Z7M8H.retense_draft: NHS Dorset ICB (a sub-ICB location)'s agreement allows the use of Secondary User Services (SUS+) hospital data, identifiable by NHS number, to check invoices from care providers and to carry out risk stratification. Invoice validation, done by Liaison Financial Services Ltd, confirms that charges are the CCG's responsibility and identifies overpayments to recover. Risk stratification, done by Prescribing Services Limited, links the data with GP data to identify patients at high risk so care can be planned and targeted. The main intended benefits are recovering money that would otherwise be lost and improved, more effective care.

DARS-NIC-252902-C7C6P.summary: The University of Glasgow's agreement covers pseudonymised survey data from the Adult Psychiatric Morbidity Survey, which covers mental health in adults. The agreement allows a PhD project to study risk factors for suicidal thoughts and behaviour in men, and how these differ from those in women. The intended benefit is to help health and social care services recognise and respond to men experiencing suicidal thoughts.

DARS-NIC-253220-Q1X8H.summary: The University of Manchester's agreement covers the use of pseudonymised patient-level hospital admission, critical care and death records, linked to GP records from the ResearchOne database. The agreement allows evaluation of OptimiseRx, a software tool that alerts prescribers to possible prescribing errors, and of its effect on hazardous prescribing, hospitalisations and deaths. It also allows assessment of the tool's cost-effectiveness for NHS England. The intended benefit is evidence to support recommendations for safer prescribing.

DARS-NIC-25634-T2Z1Z.summary: MedeAnalytics International Limited's agreement covers monthly pseudonymised, non-sensitive Hospital Episode Statistics (HES) and Emergency Care Data Set records for admitted patient care, outpatients and A&E. The data is for an online analytics service that gives NHS and social care customers national comparators to prioritise service redesign. Benchmarking has already led one provider to correct A&E coding, with a £90k credit to the commissioner, and helped a CCG win about £190k for diabetes services.

DARS-NIC-25741-N1H1B.summary: Informatica Systems Ltd's agreement covers hospital records (admitted patient care, critical care and outpatients) and linked death records from the Office for National Statistics. The data is for the National CKD Audit and Quality Improvement Programme, which links GP data on chronic kidney disease (CKD) to hospital and mortality outcomes. The audit measures variation between practices in identifying and managing CKD. The main intended benefit is better diagnosis and care, with services able to compare performance and improve.

DARS-NIC-25780-T1F4G.summary: The Royal College of Physicians of London, an academic organisation, has an agreement covering linked hospital admission records, death registration data and national COPD audit rehabilitation data. The agreement allows it to study how pulmonary rehabilitation affects hospital readmissions and survival in people with COPD, and to publish only aggregated results. The aim is to improve how rehabilitation services are designed, commissioned and delivered. A national report on patient outcomes has been published, and local reports have been given to services and commissioners.

DARS-NIC-258079-G7W1Y.summary: University College London (UCL)'s agreement covers the use of pseudonymised NHS Digital birth and civil registration records for children born after assisted reproductive technology (such as IVF), and for their naturally conceived siblings. These would be linked with national school records to compare educational outcomes. The agreement allows this to show whether these children are at higher risk of learning problems, to inform fertility regulation, schools and families.

DARS-NIC-258494-J2Q5M.summary: The London School of Economics and Political Science (LSE)'s agreement covers the use of civil registrations of death data (fact, place and cause of death) for DETERMIND, a research study led by the University of Sussex that follows people recently diagnosed with dementia and their carers. The data may be added to the study's research datasets, used to manage participants' withdrawal from the study and to prompt a carer bereavement survey. The study aims to build evidence on inequalities in dementia care, costs and outcomes, to inform policy and practice.

DARS-NIC-258780-S9H7G.summary: The University of Cambridge, with the University of Edinburgh and Royal Brompton and Harefield NHS Trust, is permitted to use hospital admissions, diagnostic imaging and death registration data covering England. The agreement allows them to study how the 2016 NICE guidelines on investigating stable chest pain changed the use of cardiac imaging tests, and what happened to patients afterwards. The main intended benefit is evidence to guide future clinical practice, service planning and research.

DARS-NIC-25945-T8Q0Z.summary: The University of Cambridge's agreement covers keeping hospital records (Hospital Episode Statistics) and patient tracking data from the Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) for an interim period. The data is for following up consented BEST2 study participants, checking cancer outcomes to gather long-term safety and effectiveness data on the Cytosponge™ test for Barrett's oesophagus. The aim is to inform whether this less invasive test could replace some endoscopies. Reported benefits include informing the design of the BEST3 trial and a published paper on a methylation panel biomarker.

DARS-NIC-259538-Q4V0W.summary: University College London (UCL), an academic organisation, is covered by an agreement to use the 2017 Mental Health of Children and Young People survey, which covers children and young people aged 2 to 19. The research team will study how common body dysmorphic disorder is, how it varies with age and sex, which other conditions and environmental factors go with it, and what impairment it causes. The aim is to improve detection and diagnosis and to inform the design and commissioning of child and adolescent mental health services.

DARS-NIC-260281-Y6X5N.summary: University College London (UCL), working with Barts Health NHS Trust, is permitted to use identifiable hospital admission records (Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care) for people recruited to the MASTER study, who have had aortic valve replacement for severe aortic stenosis. The agreement allows tracking of hospital stays for heart failure and abnormal heart rhythms, to see how heart muscle scarring relates to these outcomes. The intended benefit is better identification of patients at highest risk, so treatment can be targeted earlier.

DARS-NIC-261216-Q1L2Q.summary: The University of Sheffield's agreement covers the use of Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care data, along with patient demographic linking data from the Medical Research Information Service (MRIS), in the PJI Study. The study examines whether invasive dental procedures cause late prosthetic joint infections, which occur three or more months after a joint replacement. Its results should give evidence to support or challenge existing UK dental guidance on giving antibiotics before such procedures, as well as guidance used elsewhere in the world.

DARS-NIC-261326-F9S5D.summary: The University of Cambridge's agreement covers hospital records (accident and emergency, admitted patient, critical care and outpatient) and a mortality list-cleaning report. These are linked to data from the Pregnancy Outcome Prediction Study, which followed 4,212 mothers and their children. The aim is to see whether pregnancy data can predict later health and educational outcomes, so that risks can be spotted and addressed early. Findings have already been published in peer-reviewed journals on children's long-term outcomes after common pregnancy complications.

DARS-NIC-262206-F1P5Z.summary: The University of Glasgow's agreement covers pseudonymised hospital admission, maternity and death records for women in England who had a pregnancy-related episode between 1997 and 2017. The data is for studying peripartum cardiomyopathy, a rare pregnancy-related type of heart failure, to describe how common it is and what outcomes follow in the UK. The main intended benefit is UK-specific evidence to help clinicians inform patients about their condition and about the risks of future pregnancies.

DARS-NIC-262908-X5F4Q.summary: The University of Leicester's cardiac surgery research group's agreement covers hospital, emergency care, diagnostic imaging and death records for patients with heart conditions in England. The data is for modelling surgical trials on a computer before they run, testing whether they are feasible and how to design them. The aim is to produce trial proposals on priority heart surgery questions. To date, it has supported the design and funding applications of four trials and published its method in the European Heart Journal.

DARS-NIC-263738-V6V9N.summary: The University of Bristol's agreement covers hospital records (Hospital Episode Statistics admitted patient care and outpatients) and Emergency Care Data Set data. The data is for comparing hospital and emergency service use and medication safety between GP practices testing an intervention for people taking multiple medicines (polypharmacy) and those giving usual care. The aim is to judge whether the intervention works and is cost effective, and to help improve medicines use in these patients.

DARS-NIC-263878-H2J7T.summary: Device Access UK Ltd's agreement covers Hospital Episode Statistics (HES) data on critical care, inpatient and outpatient care. The agreement allows the company to analyse patient pathways to show where medical devices could best be used in NHS care, and to provide aggregated results with small numbers suppressed to medical technology clients and government and NHS bodies. The aim is to help clients show NHS providers where devices can improve patient outcomes and reduce waiting times and hospital stays.

DARS-NIC-264102-D2X7J.summary: King's College London, an academic institution, is using pseudonymised hospital admission records and cancer registration data for patients in England. The research compares the risk of developing cancer after X-ray guided endovascular repair of aortic aneurysms with the risk after open surgical repair. The main intended benefit is giving clinicians and patients clearer information about radiation-related risk when choosing a treatment.

DARS-NIC-264169-J6F6T.summary: NHS Devon ICB's agreement covers identifiable hospital activity data (Secondary Uses Service data for commissioners) and Personal Demographic Service data. The data is for checking invoices from care providers, confirming that the CCG is the responsible commissioner before payment. It also allows hospital data to be linked with GP data to identify patients at high risk of health deterioration. The stated aims are accurate payment of providers and earlier, better targeted care.

DARS-NIC-265261-W7P8W.summary: The University of Oxford's agreement covers NHS England hospital records (admissions, outpatient, A&E and critical care) and death records for people who took part in the UK Prospective Diabetes Study, a trial of blood pressure and glucose-lowering treatments in type 2 diabetes. The agreement allows the records to be linked to see how the treatments affected dementia, major vascular disease, health service use and costs over the long term. The aim is better evidence for clinical guidelines and funding decisions. The original study has led to 122 manuscripts as of October 2023.

DARS-NIC-266008-T3S9D.summary: NHS England's Operations and Information directorate's agreement covers national patient-level cancer waiting times data, linked to deprivation, age and gender information. It is a one-off internal analysis to see whether deprivation, age and gender are associated with cancer waiting times. The intended benefit is a better understanding of how deprivation affects access to and effectiveness of cancer pathways, and whether adding these details to the data set routinely would be worthwhile.

DARS-NIC-266178-B3W1S.summary: Hartlepool Borough Council's agreement covers hospital records of emergency care, admitted patients, critical care and outpatient visits. The agreement allows the data to be used in public health work, including needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, commissioning and advice to NHS commissioners. The main intended benefit is locally focused analysis of health and health inequalities, so the council and its partners can respond to the needs of local people, particularly the most disadvantaged.

DARS-NIC-26646-M9Q0J.summary: The Public Service Consultants Limited (trading as 2020 Delivery Ltd), a consultancy, has an agreement that allows it to use a pseudonymised extract of Hospital Episode Statistics Accident and Emergency data. The data is for research into patterns of frequent A&E attendance for the British Red Cross, including what leads people to become high intensity users and how they can reduce their use. The main intended benefit is better support for these patients, and less pressure on emergency departments.

DARS-NIC-267223-D4Q3F.summary: Swansea University's agreement covers pseudonymised hospital records from Accident and Emergency and Admitted Patient Care (Hospital Episode Statistics) for twelve English emergency departments between 2010/11 and 2018/19. The data is for a study, funded by the National Institute for Health and Care Research, of how different models of GPs working in emergency departments affect care. The aim is to build stronger evidence on the effectiveness, safety and resource use of these models.

DARS-NIC-26815-F8H6B.summary: The Royal College of Surgeons of England's agreement covers the use of linked hospital records, patient-reported outcome measures, and death registration data to study access to and outcomes of elective hip and knee replacement for patients with long-term conditions. The research aims to show how these conditions affect who gets surgery and how well it works, informing care for patients. Papers and a PhD thesis have been published, and the study contributed evidence to a NICE guideline scoping workshop.

DARS-NIC-268750-B3T4W.summary: The University of Bristol's agreement covers aggregate, non-identifying Hospital Episode Statistics Accident and Emergency data on monthly attendances across Greater Manchester. The data is for evaluating whether the Communities in Charge of Alcohol programme, which trains local volunteers as alcohol health champions, reduces A&E attendances. The aim is to show whether the programme works. So far, the team has published open access journal articles, including in BMC Public Health.

DARS-NIC-27085-C5L5G.summary: Imperial College London's agreement covers the use of NHS England hospital, emergency care, diagnostic imaging, mental health, cancer, birth and death records for the SCAMP study of adolescents. The data is for examining whether mobile phones and other radio wave technologies affect young people's cognition, behaviour and mental health. The aim is to inform a review of UK advice on children's phone use. The study team has published papers on cohort profile, exposure validation, night-time screen use and sleep, and social network use.

DARS-NIC-272253-P9X9Y.summary: King's College London's agreement covers the use of hospital, emergency care and mental health service records for people treated for anorexia nervosa. The data is for the TRIANGLE trial, which tests whether online support for patients and carers after leaving inpatient care improves long-term wellbeing and affects the number of days spent in hospital. The researchers hope the findings will inform NHS care decisions and help address rising readmissions for the condition.

DARS-NIC-272668-H4M3S.summary: The Wolfson Institute of Preventive Medicine, an academic body working with Queen Mary University of London, is covered by an agreement for survey data from the 2014 Adult Psychiatric Morbidity Survey on mental disorder in the household population. The agreement allows the data to be used to study the link between mental disorder and violence in England and Wales, with the aim of informing policy and services. The team has linked key variables across the 2000, 2007 and 2014 surveys, and has been invited to join a London violence reduction advisory group.

DARS-NIC-272984-V0C5X.summary: NHS Greater Manchester ICB's agreement covers the use of pseudonymised hospital activity and cost data from the Secondary Uses Service (SUS) for commissioners. The agreement allows this data to be linked with GP and social care data to plan and commission health services, assess population needs, identify patients at risk and monitor contracts. The main intended benefit is better-planned, higher-quality services that meet local needs, including fewer avoidable emergency admissions.

DARS-NIC-273840-N0N0N.summary: City University London's agreement covers linking hospital inpatient records (Hospital Episode Statistics, or HES) with birth registration data from the Office for National Statistics (ONS). The data is for building a research database to study inequalities in pregnancy outcomes, including mothers' postnatal and babies' neonatal hospital care. The work is done in ONS's secure Virtual Microprocessor Laboratory, and other researchers may be able to use the database. The aim is to inform maternity service users about the outcomes of midwifery, obstetric and neonatal care.

DARS-NIC-27404-D5Z3F.summary: University College London (UCL)'s agreement covers linked hospital, accident and emergency, critical care, outpatient and death records for children and young people in England, combined with school data. It allows testing of how well health and education records can be linked, and study of how school outcomes relate to emergency hospital use, including for children with chronic conditions. The aim is to inform NHS and local policy. Results so far include a peer-reviewed paper on linkage error, published in September 2021.

DARS-NIC-274251-H0G6M.summary: King's College London's agreement covers linked hospital admission and death registration data on patients aged 60 or over who had hip fracture surgery in England or Wales in 2017. The data is for studying whether more frequent, longer or more comprehensive physiotherapy leads to better recovery, including discharge, readmission and survival. The aim is to inform quality improvement and reduce unwarranted variation in rehabilitation care. A published paper found that more frequent physiotherapy was associated with earlier discharge, and the results have been shared with physiotherapists and the Royal College of Physicians.

DARS-NIC-274291-Q5T1S.summary: NHS Nottingham and Nottinghamshire ICB, with NHS Bassetlaw CCG as joint data controller, is permitted to use pseudonymised health, social care, mortality and prescribing data covering clinical and financial information. The data is for planning and monitoring commissioned health services for the local population, including reporting, demand planning and patient stratification. The stated aim is better decisions and improved service quality. Reported results include a "safe today" quality dashboard and an infection outbreak dashboard.

DARS-NIC-276970-B8Y4H.summary: The Health Foundation's agreement covers analysis of linked Hospital Episode Statistics and civil death registration records that carry no direct identifiers. The data is for understanding demand for healthcare and how the quality of care can be improved, so that the NHS and policy makers can plan for the future. Outputs from this work were used with Imperial College London to model how to allocate elective care capacity during the COVID-19 pandemic, which helped NHS policy makers make resource decisions.

DARS-NIC-277499-D3D0X.summary: Optum Health Solutions UK Limited, a commercial health services company, is permitted under the agreement to use national hospital activity and payment data (Secondary Uses Service Payment by Results) to build four analytics products for NHS commissioners. These products produce benchmarks comparing organisations, to help commissioners find where care or spending differs and where savings or better care are possible. Reported results include a changed heart bypass pathway at one hospital, with £150,000 of savings written into the hospital contract.

DARS-NIC-27803-W8G1B.summary: University College London's agreement covers the use of Hospital Episode Statistics hospital admission and critical care data, linked to routine clinical data from patients in participating critical care units. The data is for building a research database to track the long-term outcomes of people who have survived critical illness. The main intended benefit is helping clinicians, patients and researchers make better-informed decisions. So far, the wider CC-HIC database has led to 2 published papers and 5 published abstracts.

DARS-NIC-278518-F3H0X.summary: Imperial College London's agreement covers hospital admission and critical care records from Hospital Episode Statistics for about 350 patients in the IMPROVE trial, which compared endovascular and open repair of ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm. The agreement allows the records to be used to check re-interventions and hospital re-admissions over three years, including at hospitals outside the trial. The aim is a more accurate assessment of the clinical and cost-effectiveness of the two treatments.

DARS-NIC-279476-Y8N7J.summary: University of Bristol's medical school's agreement covers NHS hospital, emergency care and mental health records for children and young people with chronic fatigue syndrome or myalgic encephalomyelitis (CFS/ME). The records are for a trial of FITNET-NHS, an online cognitive behavioural therapy, compared with activity management. The aim is to find out whether FITNET-NHS works and is good value for money in the NHS, so the findings can inform future NICE guidance.

DARS-NIC-28051-Q3K7L.summary: University College London (UCL)'s agreement covers the use of Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care data to build a classification of health needs for small areas, broken down by patient ethnicity. The agreement allows the work to show how health needs differ between areas and how stable they are over time. The intended benefit is to help clinical commissioning groups, local authorities and care providers set budgeting, commissioning and screening priorities.

DARS-NIC-280606-N9Z7W.summary: King's College London's agreement covers hospital, emergency care and death registration records for patients in the UK arm of the STARRT-AKI trial and a linked observational study. The data is for working out the NHS costs and outcomes of starting kidney replacement therapy earlier rather than at the standard time in acute kidney injury. The aim is to inform UK decisions and clinical guidelines on timing. Preliminary results were presented at a workshop in Paris in September 2023.

DARS-NIC-28095-S9N3P.summary: Imperial College London's Dr Foster Unit (ICL DFU) has an agreement covering Hospital Episode Statistics data for accident and emergency, admitted patient care, critical care and outpatients. The agreement allows the data to be used to develop and validate measures of healthcare quality and safety, including variations in performance by GP practice, consultant and NHS trust. It also allows a re-identification service so NHS trusts can investigate alerts about their own patients. The expected benefits include continued monitoring of hospital mortality and detection of outlying hospitals.

DARS-NIC-281073-Y5G3F.summary: NHS Derby and Derbyshire ICB's agreement allows it to use hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other health and social care data, some identifiable and some pseudonymised, for invoice validation, risk stratification and commissioning. This is for checking that providers are paid correctly, identifying patients at risk of poor health, and planning services to meet local needs. The register reports that the data has helped match services to population needs and monitor in-year projects.

DARS-NIC-281239-V4X7H.summary: Stockton-on-Tees Borough Council is using civil registration data on births and deaths, plus primary care mortality data, which includes identifiable details. The council uses it to understand local health needs, plan services and support public health work such as suicide audits and Joint Strategic Needs Assessments. The main intended benefit is local services targeted at the greatest needs, reducing health inequalities and premature deaths. So far, it has been used to examine COVID-19 coded deaths and improve understanding of local drug-related deaths and suicides.

DARS-NIC-281848-W3T5B.summary: The University of Bristol's agreement covers national hospital records (Hospital Episodes Statistics, covering inpatients and critical care) together with Office for National Statistics mortality data. The study examines whether socioeconomic position is linked to the likelihood of organ donation after death in England between 2008 and 2012. It compares people who could have donated with those who actually did, using deprivation rankings.

DARS-NIC-283774-B9Z6K.summary: Imperial College London's agreement covers linked hospital, emergency care, critical care, outpatient, mental health and death registration data for very preterm and surgical babies born in England between 2007 and 2020. The data is for studying long-term health and education outcomes and how care in neonatal units affects them, aiming to improve neonatal care and inform health and education planning. The register reports that the work has already informed and changed national guidance on survival of babies born extremely preterm.

DARS-NIC-28480-W2R8F.summary: Pharmerit International's agreement covers the use of patient-level hospital admissions and outpatient data from Hospital Episode Statistics to estimate what vulval and vaginal cancers, and their precancerous lesions, cost the NHS. The agreement allows results to be published in a peer-reviewed journal and presented at conferences. The main intended benefit is giving health funding decision-makers published cost figures, so NHS resources can be used more efficiently.

DARS-NIC-284866-L7K4D.summary: The University of Sheffield's agreement covers linking Yorkshire Ambulance Service patient records with pseudonymised Emergency Care Data Set and Hospital Episode Statistics Accident and Emergency data for adults taken to emergency departments. The data is for medical research to build risk prediction models showing whether an emergency department attendance was avoidable. The aim is a tool to help paramedics decide on scene whether to take a patient to hospital, so patients receive the most appropriate care first time.

DARS-NIC-28591-H5Q3X.summary: University College London (UCL), working with the University of Newcastle, is covered by an agreement that allows the use of identifiable NHS England hospital, emergency care, diagnostic imaging and mental health records for 4,123 consenting men in the British Regional Heart Study. The records are for adding detailed disease outcomes to the study, to research ways to prevent cardiovascular disease, heart failure, dementia and disability in older age. Findings from the linked data have already been published in peer-reviewed journals, including on healthy lifestyle, heart failure risk and dementia.

DARS-NIC-28604-N2L8W.summary: Blackburn with Darwen Borough Council's agreement covers hospital and emergency care records from Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set. The data is for its public health duties, including needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, the annual public health report and advice to NHS commissioners. The aim is locally focused analysis of health outcomes and inequalities. The agreement allows the data to support commissioning and service delivery, such as examining causes of accidental child hospital admissions.

DARS-NIC-286863-K7T5H.summary: The University of Keele's agreement covers the use of pseudonymised hospital inpatient and outpatient data (Hospital Episode Statistics) in reports and ad-hoc analysis for Clinical Commissioning Groups, Trusts and GP practices in England. The agreement allows the admissions figures to give wider context to prescribing and prevalence information. The main aim is to encourage the best use of medicines in patient care, though the release register says this is not always measurable.

DARS-NIC-287049-F7M1P.summary: NHS England, working with its evaluation partner Ipsos, is permitted to use cancer waiting times, cancer registration and death registration data. These are held in a secure NHS England research environment. The agreement covers evaluating the Targeted Lung Health Check programme, which invites people at higher risk of lung cancer for checks and scans. The aim is to measure its impact on cancer outcomes, such as stage at diagnosis, and to inform whether and how the programme should be expanded across England.

DARS-NIC-287229-D6F9F.summary: University College London's agreement covers survey data from the Adult Psychiatric Morbidity Survey, covering adults in private households across the UK, for a PhD project. The project examines whether the amount of alcohol people drink each week is linked to suicidal thoughts, suicide attempts and self-harm. The aim is to inform suicide prevention practice and policy. Initial findings were published in the journal BJPsych Open in November 2022.

DARS-NIC-28744-S4F8H.summary: The University of Cambridge's agreement covers hospital records (Hospital Episode Statistics for admitted care, outpatients and A&E) for 867 people whose type 2 diabetes was found through screening. The data is for testing whether early, intensive treatment of several risk factors lowers the long-term risk of cardiovascular events and death over ten years, and for informing the costs of care. The ten-year results have been published in The Lancet Diabetes & Endocrinology, alongside several other papers.

DARS-NIC-287601-K4P2V.summary: University Hospital Southampton NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers holding identifiable hospital admission and death registration data for about 20,000 patients from the CHARIOT study. The data is for examining whether raised high-sensitivity troponin blood test levels are linked to later deaths and hospital admissions. The aim is to help clinicians interpret the test. Results have been presented at cardiology conferences and published in the American Journal of Cardiology.

DARS-NIC-287804-H1T1R.summary: Imperial College London's agreement covers NHS registration, mortality and cause of death data, including Scottish events, for the IMPROVE trial. The trial compares endovascular repair with open surgery for patients with a ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm. The data allows complete mortality follow-up for at least three years, including whether deaths were aneurysm-related. The aim is to improve care for future patients, so that endovascular repair becomes available to all of them.

DARS-NIC-288807-P0R9B.summary: The University of Oxford, working with the University of Exeter, agreement covers pseudonymised hospital records (admissions, A&E, critical care and outpatients), emergency care data and death registrations for 5,409 people aged 65 and over. The agreement allows the data to be used to study back and other musculoskeletal pain in older people and to calculate the cost of their NHS care. The main intended benefit is a prognostic tool to help GPs spot when back pain threatens an older person's mobility.

DARS-NIC-290527-P5C0Y.summary: Northwest Ehealth Limited's agreement covers hospital admission, outpatient and diagnostic imaging records for patients with refractory chronic cough who consented to their records being used. The records are kept for archiving only, and other data has been destroyed. The data is for a study of how much healthcare these patients use and what it costs, to help understand earlier diagnosis. The analysis found that healthcare use and costs fall within six months of diagnosis.

DARS-NIC-29100-R2S2F.summary: The University of Sheffield's agreement covers the use of hospital accident and emergency (A&E) and admitted patient records from Hospital Episode Statistics. The data is for evaluating alcohol intoxication management services, sometimes called alcohol treatment centres, which treat intoxicated people who would otherwise go to emergency departments. The study compares six cities with these services against six without, looking at attendances, time spent in the emergency department and costs. It aims to give decision makers evidence on effectiveness and cost-effectiveness.

DARS-NIC-291482-X5N6H.summary: NHS Hampshire and Isle of Wight Integrated Care Board (ICB) is using Secondary User Services (SUS+) hospital data for commissioners, linked with GP data. It is used for risk stratification, which predicts which patients are at high risk of health deterioration so that care can be planned and GPs can target interventions. The main intended benefit is more effective commissioning, with fewer avoidable emergency readmissions and better patient outcomes.

The main intended benefit is more effective commissioning, with fewer avoidable emergency readmissions and better patient outcomes.

DARS-NIC-291736-N6J7Z.summary: Oliver Wyman Ltd's agreement covers hospital activity, A&E, outpatient, mental health and payment data that does not identify individuals. The data is for producing reports, population profiling and business cases for NHS clients, including CCGs and trusts, on new models of care. The stated aim is to help local health systems decide where to invest in care that improves quality and lowers costs.

DARS-NIC-291863-S9M0X.summary: The University of Birmingham's agreement covers the use of hospital admission records and death registration data for people taking part in the BASIL-2 trial, who have severe limb ischaemia caused by blocked arteries below the knee. The data will check the trial's main outcome, amputation-free survival, and extend follow-up without contacting participants again. The trial compares vein bypass first with endovascular treatment first, to find which works better and offers better value to the NHS and social care.

DARS-NIC-291938-R6V3V.summary: Barts Health NHS Trust's agreement allows the use of demographic data and Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) death and flagging reports to keep up to date the database of the Diabetes Alliance for Research in England (DARE) study in north east London. The database is for inviting people with diabetes to take part in research, with the aim of recruiting faster and speeding up evidence on diabetes care. So far, the database has helped recruit about 4,200 people to 32 approved studies, and the team has held a public event for members.

DARS-NIC-291940-S3D6R.summary: The University of Newcastle upon Tyne, an academic organisation, is permitted under its agreement to use data from the Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) and the Personal Demographics Service. The agreement allows this data to provide the register with statistical analysis from birth certificates, and to update and complete the registration of young people with a malignant disease in the North and North West regions of England. The text does not state an intended benefit.

DARS-NIC-291941-Z2Q1C.summary: Cardiff University, an academic organisation, holds NHS England Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) records on cause of death, cohort event notification and current status for patients in the FRAGMATIC lung cancer trial. It keeps them for secure storage and to repeat earlier analyses if the published results are challenged. The trial tested whether adding dalteparin to standard treatment improved survival. The results have contributed to international guidelines on preventing blood clots in cancer patients, and led to a new trial.

DARS-NIC-291953-M8M9V.summary: The Institute of Cancer Research's agreement covers the use of Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) records, covering cause of death, current status, members and postings, and personal demographics, for a breast cancer study. The agreement allows these to be linked to trial data to analyse relapse-free and overall survival, and to test whether bone marrow micrometastases at diagnosis independently predict outcomes. The aim is to identify women at high risk of relapse after surgery. Main results have already been published in the British Medical Journal and The Lancet.

DARS-NIC-291981-Y7J2F.summary: Imperial College London, an academic organisation, holds pseudonymised NHS England mortality and cohort tracking records (MRIS reports) for patients in the SIGGAR and SOCCER bowel cancer diagnosis studies, now kept for archiving only. The studies compared CT colonography with colonoscopy and barium enema, and examined which patients need a whole colon investigation. Results led the NHS Bowel Cancer Screening Programme to recommend only CT colonography as an alternative to colonoscopy, and symptom guidelines were updated.
DARS-NIC-291981-Y7J2F.retense_draft: Imperial College London's agreement covers pseudonymised NHS England mortality and cohort tracking records (MRIS reports) for patients in the SIGGAR and SOCCER bowel cancer diagnosis studies, now held for archiving only. The studies compared CT colonography with colonoscopy and barium enema, and examined which patients need a whole colon investigation. Results led the NHS Bowel Cancer Screening Programme to recommend only CT colonography as an alternative to colonoscopy, and symptom guidelines were updated.

DARS-NIC-292087-M7V9Q.summary: University Hospital Southampton NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers use of hospital admitted patient and outpatient records (Hospital Episode Statistics) for the FORECAST Trial. The trial involves adults referred to rapid access chest pain clinics. It compares a CT heart scan, with a computer-generated blood flow measurement (FFRct) where needed, against routine hospital tests. The main aim is to see whether this approach uses fewer NHS resources over nine months, which could inform national NICE guidance.

DARS-NIC-292279-Z2S5T.summary: South London and Maudsley NHS Foundation Trust's agreement allows hospital, emergency care, death registration and demographic records to enhance its de-identified clinical records research resource, CRIS. The data are for studying physical health, mortality and use of healthcare in people with mental health conditions, and for identifying health inequalities. Published research has already informed government policy and the Trust's smoke-free policy.

DARS-NIC-292300-H8K6G.summary: MedeAnalytics International Limited's agreement covers bespoke extracts of Hospital Episode Statistics (HES) data for accident and emergency, inpatient and outpatient care. The data is for giving its NHS and social care customers national comparators for quality and performance measures, shown as anonymised reports and dashboards. The release register says that linking data from different sources supports better operational, clinical and financial practices and, ultimately, better patient outcomes.

DARS-NIC-292304-J2W1T.summary: General Healthcare Group (BMI), a provider of NHS care, is permitted under the agreement to receive monthly extracts of Hospital Episode Statistics (HES) inpatient and outpatient data. The agreement allows the data to be analysed internally to look at closing services in favour of community settings, other ways of working, partnerships with other services, and the geographic footprint of services. The stated aim is to put patient experience and care at the centre of decisions.

DARS-NIC-294268-B3Q6J.summary: NHS Bedfordshire, Luton and Milton Keynes Integrated Care Board (ICB) uses hospital activity data (Secondary User Services data for commissioners), linked with GP data, to identify patients at high risk of poor health outcomes. This risk stratification, carried out by Prescribing Services Limited, helps GPs target care and helps commissioners plan services. The main intended benefit is better case management and more effective commissioning, including fewer avoidable emergency admissions.
DARS-NIC-294268-B3Q6J.retense_draft: NHS Bedfordshire, Luton and Milton Keynes Integrated Care Board's agreement allows it to use hospital activity data (Secondary User Services data for commissioners), linked with GP data, to identify patients at high risk of poor health outcomes. This risk stratification, carried out by Prescribing Services Limited, is for helping GPs target care and helping commissioners plan services. The main intended benefit is better case management and more effective commissioning, including fewer avoidable emergency admissions.

DARS-NIC-294304-Q1M0X.summary: NHS Bedfordshire, Luton and Milton Keynes ICB's agreement with Prescribing Services Limited allows the use of Secondary Uses Service (SUS+) hospital data linked with GP data. The agreement allows this data to be used for risk stratification: identifying patients at high risk, so GPs and commissioners can target care and plan services. The main intended benefit is better planning and more effective commissioning, including fewer avoidable emergency admissions.

DARS-NIC-294327-K1S3K.summary: NHS Nottingham and Nottinghamshire ICB (Sub ICB Location, formerly NHS Bassetlaw CCG) agreement covers the use of Secondary Uses Service (SUS+) hospital data for commissioners, linked with GP data, for risk stratification carried out by Prescribing Services Limited. The agreement allows this to identify patients at high risk, so GPs can target care and commissioners can plan services. The main intended benefit is better planning and fewer avoidable emergency admissions.

DARS-NIC-294590-B6V3F.summary: The University of Manchester's agreement covers civil registration death records, covering whether patients have died and the dates and causes of death, for 151 patients diagnosed with naevoid melanoma, a type of skin cancer, at Royal Surrey County Hospital. The study will compare the outlook for two subtypes, papillomatous and maturing. The intended benefit is more precise diagnosis and better-tailored follow-up and treatment for each subtype.

DARS-NIC-294605-F1P7F.summary: University College London (UCL)'s agreement covers the use of Scottish NHS registration data from the Medical Research Information Service (MRIS). The data is for developing an improved screening procedure for ovarian cancer in women at high risk because of family history or genetic predisposition. The work will also assess the health effects, resource needs, feasibility and acceptability of screening, and build a serum bank for studying new tumour markers.

DARS-NIC-295342-W3Z6L.summary: The University of Oxford's agreement covers the use of hospital admissions records linked to death registration data to study surgery for upper limb injuries and infections, and the complications that follow. The data is for showing trends, regional variation, outcomes and NHS costs, so that services can be better planned and patients and clinicians can make better-informed choices. Analysis of flexor tendon injuries of the hand has been presented internationally and used to support an NIHR-funded trial of surgical techniques.

DARS-NIC-296034-T4Y4K.summary: IQVIA Ltd's agreement covers hospital records from accident and emergency, admitted patient care and outpatient care. The data is for studying people in England with pulmonary hypertension and its subtypes, looking at the route to diagnosis, treatment patterns, outcomes and healthcare use. The aim is to fill knowledge gaps and support better diagnosis, treatment and care pathways. A study report has been produced, and a publication is being developed.

DARS-NIC-297783-V4P6H.summary: GlaxoSmithKline Research & Development Limited's agreement covers pseudonymised hospital records (accident and emergency, admitted patient care, critical care and outpatients) for 629 participants in its INTREPID trial of COPD inhaler treatment. The data is for testing whether routine hospital data can record and cost hospital use, reducing the data collection burden on research sites. An abstract presented at the ISPOR Europe conference in November 2022 concluded that the linked data gave more detail than patient recall.

DARS-NIC-29785-Q4Y2T.summary: Leicestershire County Council's agreement covers hospital and emergency care data (Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set). The data is for its public health duties, including needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, the annual public health report and advice to NHS commissioners. The aim is locally focused analysis of health outcomes and inequalities. The council has reported analyses on alcohol-related admissions, covid admissions and hip fractures.

DARS-NIC-29822-N0N7W.summary: The London School of Economics and Political Science (LSE) is using linked hospital, mental health service and death registration records for English participants with dementia in the IDEAL study. It aims to understand patterns of health service use and costs, and how these relate to people's ability to live well with dementia. The intended benefit is better evidence to help shape services, policy and support for people with dementia and their carers. So far, service use and cost variables have been calculated and linked to the study data, and manuscripts have been submitted for peer review.
DARS-NIC-29822-N0N7W.retense_draft: The London School of Economics and Political Science (LSE) agreement covers the use of linked hospital, mental health service and death registration records for English participants with dementia in the IDEAL study. It aims to understand patterns of health service use and costs, and how these relate to people's ability to live well with dementia. The intended benefit is better evidence to help shape services, policy and support for people with dementia and their carers. Service use and cost variables have been calculated and linked to the study data, and manuscripts have been submitted for peer review.

DARS-NIC-29827-Q8Z7Q.summary: The University of Oxford's agreement covers hospital admissions records (Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care) linked to civil death registrations. It is for studying how patient, surgical and hospital factors affect outcomes and NHS costs in treating upper limb conditions such as arthritis, shoulder injuries, Dupuytren's disease and nerve compression. The main aim is to give patients and the NHS evidence on outcomes and variation in care. Six peer-reviewed papers have already been published on complications and repeat surgery, and they are being used in clinical practice.

DARS-NIC-298631-R9Y3L.summary: The Healthcare Quality Improvement Partnership (HQIP)'s agreement covers Hospital Episode Statistics (HES) inpatient records and NHS registration data. The data is for National Bowel Cancer Audit analysis, including the 2014 Annual Report. The agreement allows three in-depth analyses covering the rectal cancer pathway, why some patients do not get surgery, and five-year outcomes, each published in a separate report.

DARS-NIC-300282-G9Q0Q.summary: University College London's agreement covers its register of people with familial hypercholesterolaemia, an inherited cause of high cholesterol, and allows linked hospital and death records to be used for the University of Nottingham and University of York study. The data is for evaluating ways of identifying and managing patients, to inform cost-effectiveness models of relative testing.
