The work has produced long-term risk estimates that supported charity advocacy, and has shown lipid specialists inequalities in care.

DARS-NIC-300343-D5G8J.summary: The University of Leeds's agreement covers the use of NHS registration data, Office for National Statistics (ONS) mortality data and Scottish events data for medical research. The data is for studying whether type 1 diabetes diagnosed in childhood or young adult life raises the risk of early death, and which factors, such as sex or socioeconomic status, may be linked to it. It also covers looking at early mortality in young people with type 2 diabetes and providing anonymised data for a European comparison study.

DARS-NIC-301834-K0S2Y.summary: Certara UK's agreement covers pseudonymised hospital, accident and emergency, critical care, outpatient and death records for adults with haematological cancers. The agreement allows the study of the clinical characteristics of patients who develop veno-occlusive disease, a rare liver disorder, and of the hospital resources and costs involved in their care in England. The aim is to improve detection and care, and to inform planning of NHS resources.

DARS-NIC-302473-K6R0Z.summary: The University of Cambridge's agreement covers the use of cancer registration, death registration and mortality follow-up records to study people who carry BRCA1 and BRCA2 gene mutations and their relatives (the EMBRACE study). It aims to estimate cancer risks and the effects of lifestyle factors and risk-reducing surgery, so that screening and counselling can be better guided. Published papers have already been incorporated into guidelines, including those from NICE (the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence).

DARS-NIC-302604-S7H2N.summary: Imperial College London's agreement covers identifiable NHS hospital records (inpatient, outpatient, and accident and emergency), mental health data sets and death and status reports for participants in the ASCOT heart trial. The data is for studying whether atorvastatin and different blood pressure treatments affect long-term risks of dementia, stroke and other vascular disease, and how blood pressure variability relates to them. Published findings have already fed into the QRISK3 risk model and hypertension guidelines.

DARS-NIC-302792-X4T6B.summary: The University of Warwick's Clinical Trials Unit may hold hospital records (Hospital Episode Statistics for accident and emergency, admitted patient care, critical care and outpatients) from the completed PreFIT falls prevention trial. The agreement allows them to be kept securely archived for 10 years, and earlier analyses to be re-run only to check published results if they are challenged. The trial compared ways to prevent falls and fractures in people over 70. The findings were published in the New England Journal of Medicine and were referred to NICE for consideration.

DARS-NIC-302994-C2Q2Y.summary: The University of Oxford's agreement covers the use of NHS hospital, death, cancer, mental health, medicines and diabetes audit records to follow people who took part in the ASCEND trial of people with diabetes. The data is for finding out whether low-dose aspirin, and omega-3 supplements, affect long-term risks of cancer, dementia, heart failure, heart attacks and strokes. Published results have already been cited in updated guidelines, including the February 2023 NICE cardiovascular guideline update.

DARS-NIC-303379-H4C8H.summary: University Hospital Southampton NHS Foundation Trust and Liverpool Heart & Chest Hospital NHS Foundation Trust's agreement allows them to keep identifiable hospital, accident and emergency, outpatient, critical care, diagnostic imaging and death records for 1,100 participants in the RIPCORD 2 heart trial. The records are for secure storage, so the trial analysis can be repeated if its findings are challenged. The trial's findings were published in the journal Circulation in 2022 and have helped guide clinicians on using pressure wire technology.

DARS-NIC-303776-B2X1W.summary: The Healthcare Quality Improvement Partnership (HQIP)'s agreement covers the use of ONS mortality data, including date and place of death, for the national audit of oesophago-gastric cancer care in England and Wales. The data is for linking to audit records from NHS Trusts to show survival and end-of-life care outcomes. The aim is to give national and trust-level results, published in the audit's annual reports.

DARS-NIC-303785-L3K3Z.summary: Norfolk and Norwich University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust's agreement allows the use of hospital admission, outpatient and civil registration (death) records for patients treated with percutaneous coronary intervention, a procedure to open narrowed heart arteries. The data is for comparing drug coated balloons with drug eluting stents, including in different patient groups, and for looking at outcomes such as mortality and rehospitalisation. The aim is to publish the findings and present them at medical conferences. This could help show whether drug coated balloons are a suitable alternative to stents.

DARS-NIC-304146-M5F6Y.summary: Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers hospital admission records (Hospital Episode Statistics) and civil registration death records for patients who attended an emergency department. The data is for updating the T-MACS chest pain decision aid with machine learning so it stays accurate over time, and for testing whether emergency department data can predict long-term cardiovascular outcomes, including death. The expected benefit is continued safe, accurate and quick diagnosis of heart attacks.

DARS-NIC-304758-V5Q9V.summary: The University of Nottingham's agreement covers Hospital Episode Statistics (HES) data on accident and emergency, critical care, inpatient and outpatient care. The agreement allows this pseudonymised data to be linked to its QResearch database of GP records for medical research. The research includes developing and validating risk prediction tools such as QRISK2, and the linked data should make studies more complete. Results are published in peer-reviewed journals.

DARS-NIC-30487-G4F4J.summary: NHS Great Yarmouth and Waveney CCG's agreement covers hospital, ambulance, community, mental health and primary care activity data, including SUS data, that can be identified by NHS Number. The data is for producing commissioning reports, dashboards, statutory returns and readmissions analysis. The aim is to support the planning, monitoring and commissioning of local health services for its population.

DARS-NIC-30493-Y0C0K.summary: University College London (UCL) is permitted to use hospital records (accident and emergency, admitted patient care, critical care and outpatients) and mortality data, with names, addresses and NHS numbers removed, linked to the English Longitudinal Study of Ageing. The data is for research into health, social care use and ageing in people aged 50 and over, helping to inform planning of services. Linked data have already contributed to the Centre for Ageing Better's "Boom and bust?" report (November 2021) and a World Health Organization review on arts and health.

DARS-NIC-30560-W4V1T.summary: The University of Bristol's agreement covers the use of Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care data on hospital care since birth for children who took part in the DRIFT trial of a treatment for premature babies with bleeding into the brain's ventricles. The data is for comparing the use and cost of hospital care between the two treatment groups, as part of a school-age follow-up study. The aim is to show whether the treatment is cost-effective for the NHS, so that NICE guidance could be updated.

DARS-NIC-305864-D0Y3W.summary: The University of Bristol's agreement covers hospital admitted patient and outpatient records (Hospital Episode Statistics) and death registration data for a long-term follow-up of men in the UPSTREAM trial, which tested whether invasive bladder pressure testing (urodynamics) helps decide on prostate surgery for urinary symptoms. The data is for establishing whether surgery rates were lower with testing. Phase I results have been published, but the Phase II analyses are still in draft.

DARS-NIC-30645-Z2Z2K.summary: The University of Bristol's agreement covers the use of hospital admission records and death registration data to study hip fractures in England and Wales. The study examines how social deprivation and region affect how often hip fractures happen, and what follows: death, recovery, return home, readmissions and their costs. The aim is to inform commissioning and reduce health inequalities. Several peer-reviewed papers have been published, and the work helped win further funding for a follow-on study.

DARS-NIC-306651-W7L4C.summary: Keele University's agreement covers the use of hospital admission, death registration and national heart attack audit data to study complications and unplanned readmissions after a heart attack. The data is for understanding how often these occur and what raises the risk, so that risk scores can help clinicians tailor treatment and reduce readmissions. Published papers so far include one finding that heart attack patients with cancer face higher short- and long-term risk of death.

DARS-NIC-306849-M2N0X.summary: Royal Free London NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers hospital records (outpatient, admitted patient and accident and emergency) and death registration data. The data is for a study of people who had a right heart catheter test at specialist centres between 2009 and 2016 and whose lung artery pressure was raised but below the current threshold for pulmonary hypertension. The study compares their deaths and hospital admissions with a control group. It aims to support earlier monitoring and updated guidance for this group.

DARS-NIC-307462-D6B9M.summary: Royal Surrey NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers the use of cause of death information from death certificates, held in the Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) cause of death report, for about 250 patients who had prostate brachytherapy and were lost to follow-up. The agreement allows the causes of death to be added to the Brachybase database and prostate cancer specific survival after treatment to be audited. The main intended benefit is to show how effective the treatment is and allow comparison with results from other centres.

DARS-NIC-308166-T2Z1J.summary: Warrington Borough Council's agreement covers identifiable patient details from the Personal Demographic Service, including name, address, date of birth and GP practice code. The agreement allows the council to use them to invite residents to take part in a Health and Wellbeing Survey. The survey is meant to give up-to-date information on local health and lifestyle, so the council and NHS partners can plan services and target resources at areas and groups experiencing health inequalities.

DARS-NIC-309029-P7H1D.summary: The London School of Economics and Political Science (LSE)'s agreement covers the use of Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care data, which covers hospital births, together with a linking identifier dataset. The data is for studying whether the Health in Pregnancy Grant, paid to pregnant women in England from 2009 to 2011, affected birthweight and prematurity. The research aims to show whether the grant achieved its aims, to inform policy debates on public health and early intervention.

DARS-NIC-309034-C7M7W.summary: The University of Cambridge, working with NHS Blood and Transplant, holds pseudonymised hospital records (admitted patient care and outpatients) and death registration data for about 200,000 blood donors. The agreement allows the data to be used to study the long-term health effects of whole blood and platelet donation, such as on heart disease and diabetes, and to test whether such linkage can support ongoing donor health monitoring. Findings so far include no link between platelet donation and health outcomes, and preliminary results presented at a European conference.

DARS-NIC-309246-L8C4C.summary: The University of Nottingham's agreement allows use of maternity, hospital inpatient, critical care, outpatient, emergency care and death registration data for the GBS3 trial. The trial compares two ways of routinely testing pregnant women for Group B Streptococcus with the current approach based on risk factors, to see whether testing reduces serious infection in newborn babies. It also assesses costs. The main intended benefit is evidence for the UK National Screening Committee to decide whether routine testing should be introduced.

DARS-NIC-309284-N4T2H.summary: Northgate Information Solutions (also referred to as Northgate Public Services) provides data services for the National Joint Registry (NJR), and the agreement allows it to use Hospital Episode Statistics (HES) inpatient and outpatient data, plus linked ONS mortality data. The data is for linking to NJR records to produce the NJR's annual report, related analyses and reports for stakeholders. The linkage lets the NJR study outcomes such as death and revision, supporting its aim of monitoring and improving patient safety and outcomes.

DARS-NIC-309328-R9V1C.summary: King's College London's agreement covers the use of a list cleaning report from the Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) to locate patients from an earlier first episode psychosis study, AESOP, and invite them to join a new study called STRATA. STRATA aims to explore the predictors of treatment-resistant schizophrenia, using blood samples and medication histories. The intended benefit is a test that helps clinicians choose suitable medication much sooner.

DARS-NIC-309500-F4X1B.summary: The University of Birmingham, through its Birmingham Clinical Trials Unit, has an agreement covering cause of death and current status records for the 1,440 people in the original BAFTA trial. The data is for the BAFTA 2 follow-up study, to see who has died, from what cause, and the overall death rate, to understand the long-term effects of anticoagulation (blood-thinning) treatment in very elderly people. The aim is to help clinicians and patients decide whether to continue treatment. The original BAFTA trial has already led to published papers and been included in national guidelines.

DARS-NIC-309509-L2G1J.summary: University College London's agreement covers the use of identifiable hospital inpatient records (Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care) for about 16,720 infants in a randomised trial of a diagnostic aid, a video tool and checklist, for GPs' 6-week hip checks. The trial will test whether the aid reduces unnecessary referrals to hospital and late diagnoses of developmental dysplasia of the hip. The aim is for infants who truly have the condition to be treated sooner, and for fewer families to face needless appointments.

DARS-NIC-309751-G8D4H.summary: King's College London's agreement covers use of Adult Psychiatric Morbidity Survey data from 2007 and 2014 for a PhD research project. The study examines how caregivers' reports of domestic violence relate to their health, compared with carers who report no violence and with people who are not carers. The main intended benefit is a better understanding of carers' experiences of violence, which could help inform support and future interventions.

DARS-NIC-311095-K1Q0B.summary: Imperial College London's agreement covers the use of cause of death and NHS registration data to follow up people first seen in the Nottingham study of neurotic disorder of anxiety and depression, begun in 1983. The data is for identifying who has died, so relatives are not troubled by follow-up, and for supporting analysis of whether personality status shapes long-term outcomes. The main intended benefit is better outcomes through early personality assessment and treatment. Reported results include published papers and a new World Health Organisation personality disorder classification the study helped shape.

DARS-NIC-311179-R5V5Y.summary: The University of Liverpool's agreement covers Hospital Episode Statistics data on accident and emergency attendances, admitted patient care and outpatient appointments. The data is for the Liverpool Lung Project, which will link it to questionnaire and Office for National Statistics (ONS) mortality data for its participants. The aim is to study how other health conditions affect lung cancer, and to improve risk prediction and early detection, so lung cancer can be found at a more curable stage.

DARS-NIC-311182-F5W4X.summary: The University of Oxford's agreement covers demographic data (name, address, gender and date of birth) for people aged 65 or over in the Thames Valley who have several long-term conditions. The data is for identifying and inviting people to join the ATEMPT pilot trial, which compares taking more with fewer blood pressure medicines. The intended benefit is to help plan a larger trial on managing blood pressure in older people with multiple health conditions.

DARS-NIC-311182-N0L1Y.summary: National Centre for Social Research holds hospital records and death-registration data linked to participants in the English Longitudinal Study of Ageing, a long-running study of people aged 50 and over. The data supports research on health, work, finances and social life in older age, and can be shared with study partners at UCL and the Institute for Fiscal Studies. Linked data has already fed into published analyses on dementia trends, loneliness and end-of-life hospital spending, and into a Centre for Ageing Better report.

DARS-NIC-311183-X5Q2F.summary: The Royal Society for the Prevention of Accidents (RoSPA) is using a bespoke tabulation of Hospital Episode Statistics (HES), covering hospital admissions for external causes such as accidents and injuries in each local authority area of England. It will analyse the scale, causes and trends of unintentional injury, including small numbers. RoSPA will use the findings to target and evaluate its accident prevention programmes and to inform public health professionals, policy and strategy.
DARS-NIC-311183-X5Q2F.retense_draft: The Royal Society for the Prevention of Accidents's agreement covers a bespoke tabulation of Hospital Episode Statistics (HES), covering hospital admissions for external causes such as accidents and injuries in each local authority area of England. The agreement allows analysis of the scale, causes and trends of unintentional injury, including small numbers. The findings are for targeting and evaluating accident prevention programmes and for informing public health professionals, policy and strategy.

DARS-NIC-312474-H5Q0T.summary: The Royal College of Physicians of London's agreement covers the use of hospital inpatient records (Hospital Episode Statistics), NHS registration data and mortality-related data linked to the National Hip Fracture Database. The agreement allows these data to be used to audit and research hip fracture care, including whole hospital stays, deaths, readmissions and return to independent living. The main intended benefit is more accurate comparison of hospital performance and better-informed commissioning of hip fracture care.

DARS-NIC-313490-W3X2D.summary: Wilson Solicitors LLP, trading as NA Wilson Associates, is covered by an agreement for bespoke extracts of Hospital Episode Statistics (HES) inpatient and critical care data. The data is for a Financial Benchmarking System that lets NHS trusts and commissioners compare costed inpatient activity and financial performance. The aim is to support financial turn-around, plan service changes for patients' benefit, and assure that financial transactions between NHS organisations are fair and compliant.

DARS-NIC-313531-L7P4C.summary: Barts Health NHS Trust's agreement covers the UK Immune Thrombocytopenia (ITP) Registry, which holds records of patients with the rare bleeding disorder ITP, and allows hospital inpatient data (Hospital Episode Statistics) to be used. The data is for updating and completing the registry's records, including hospital care and causes of death, and for studying risks such as blood clots, bleeding and mortality. The stated aim is better data quality, giving more reliable findings to support clinical, policy and regulatory decisions.

DARS-NIC-313754-G6X4Z.summary: Cardiff University holds hospital records (Hospital Episode Statistics for accident and emergency, admitted patient care and outpatients) from the completed Building Blocks study of the Family Nurse Partnership programme for first-time teenage mothers. The data is securely archived to meet good clinical practice rules and to allow published findings to be verified if challenged. Retaining it also preserves a database that could support future research on children's longer-term outcomes. The study's findings were published and used by the Department of Health to decide how best to support young families in England.

DARS-NIC-314187-M1D8Y.summary: NHS England's agreement covers the use of patient-level data from the Assuring Transformation monthly collection on learning disability services. The agreement allows analysts to produce aggregated performance and quality indicators, such as admissions, discharges and patient numbers, for each commissioner. The indicators are for operational managers to hold commissioners to account and to identify good and poor practice. The intended benefit is an evidence base for improving services and patient experience.

DARS-NIC-314399-K4J9S.summary: NHS Wales Informatics Service, on behalf of Wales's seven local health boards, has an agreement covering identifiable hospital activity data (Secondary Uses Service accident and emergency, episode and outpatient records) about Welsh residents treated in NHS England. The data is for planning and managing health services, direct care, and checking payments and quality of care. The main intended benefit is better management of patient pathways and care across the Wales–England border. The register reports general improvements in care, services and finances, but names no specific outputs.

DARS-NIC-314521-S8M1Q.summary: The Department of Health's agreement covers linked hospital records (critical care) and death records for chronically ill patients in their last two years of life. The data is for building a Hospital Care Intensity Index at hospital provider and clinical commissioning group (CCG) level to measure the intensity of end-of-life care. The agreement allows testing of how the index relates to capacity, patient experience and outcomes, and comparison of England with the US. The findings are intended to give insight into managing supply-sensitive care and to inform advice to the Secretary of State.

DARS-NIC-31491-V6Z9Y.summary: Calderdale Metropolitan Borough Council, a local authority, is permitted to use hospital records covering emergency care, admitted patients, critical care and outpatients. The agreement allows them to be used for its public health duties, including its Joint Strategic Needs Assessments, the annual report of the Director of Public Health, commissioning plans and advice to NHS commissioners. The stated benefit is locally focused analysis of health outcomes and inequalities, particularly for the most disadvantaged groups.

DARS-NIC-315134-L9Z6B.summary: IQVIA Solutions UK Limited's agreement covers the use of pseudonymised or anonymised hospital admitted patient care and outpatient records (Hospital Episode Statistics) for patients with chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps. The agreement allows analysis of treatment pathways and the burden of nasal polyp surgery, including repeat operations, for Sanofi Genzyme. The intended benefit is to help the NHS understand where surgery burden is greatest and support service improvement.

DARS-NIC-315175-P8X6Z.summary: The University of Sheffield's agreement covers linked hospital records (Hospital Episode Statistics), ambulance patient records and mortality data. The data is for two studies: PhOEBE, which develops and tests measures of how ambulance care affects patients, and VAN, which explores why ambulance services differ in how often they do not take patients to hospital. The main intended benefit is giving ambulance services evidence on patient outcomes to guide service changes and demand management.

DARS-NIC-315419-F3W7K.summary: The University of Oxford's agreement covers the use of pseudonymised, population-level hospital admissions and death registration data to research hospital admission trends, cancer, maternal health and the effects of COVID-19. The aim is to produce evidence that helps improve NHS services, care and policy. Reported results include a study of Covid-19 deaths among clinically vulnerable patients, reported to the Joint Committee on Vaccination and Immunisation, which helped inform early vaccine roll-out.

DARS-NIC-315716-L0F4M.summary: Imperial College London's agreement covers the use of pseudonymised Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care data to research care for frail and elderly patients with chronic conditions and the effects of government health policies. The data is for better planning of spending and identifying older people at risk of declining health. So far, a PhD thesis has been passed with minor corrections, and earlier work was presented to health leaders and used to evaluate a health information exchange.

DARS-NIC-315871-Z7S4M.summary: NHS Cheshire and Merseyside ICB (South Cheshire area)'s agreement covers pseudonymised health and care data, including hospital, mental health, community, maternity, cancer waiting times and death and birth records, with clinical and financial detail. The data is for planning and commissioning health services, understanding local needs, modelling how services interact, and identifying patients at risk of admission. The main intended benefit is better planning of services and patient pathways, with fewer avoidable emergency admissions.

DARS-NIC-315999-W2W4C.summary: The University of Leeds's agreement covers the use of hospital admissions data (Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care) for a sub-study of the LP-MAESTRO project. The study evaluates the cost-effectiveness and efficiency of different liaison psychiatry service set-ups, which provide mental health care in general hospitals, using routine NHS data. It aims to help commissioners evaluate such services. Preliminary results on effects on hospital length of stay were presented at a RAID network conference in April 2017.

DARS-NIC-316335-R5V1J.summary: Queen Mary University of London's agreement covers a bespoke extract of Hospital Episode Statistics (HES) inpatient data. The data is for a PhD study comparing age and sex standardised hip replacement rates for osteoarthritis in England, Brazil and Scotland between 1993/94 and 2012/13. The study also looks at regional and socioeconomic differences from an equity perspective. It aims to inform recommendations on access to care and the allocation of resources to reduce inequality.

DARS-NIC-316369-X4S6T.summary: The London Borough of Croydon's agreement covers Hospital Episode Statistics and Emergency Care Data Set records, covering hospital admissions, outpatient, critical care and A&E activity. The data is for its public health duties, including needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, commissioning and advice to NHS commissioners. The aim is locally focused analysis of health outcomes and inequalities. So far, self-harm admissions analysis informed a needs assessment and was presented to the local suicide prevention board.

DARS-NIC-316443-V5Z4Y.summary: The University of Oxford's agreement covers the use of hospital admission, death registration and patient-reported outcome records for people identified from the National Joint Registry. It allows comparison of cemented and cementless knee replacements, overall and for different groups of patients, including their costs. The data is for showing which fixation method works best so care can be tailored to patients. Research already published shows cemented total knee replacements had better clinical outcomes, while cementless partial replacements did better.

DARS-NIC-316558-W0T8G.summary: Cardiff University holds NHS England's Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) data, covering cause of death, status tracking and demographics, for the AML16 clinical trial in older patients with acute myeloid leukaemia and high risk myelodysplastic syndrome. It is used only for secure storage and back-up, so the trial analysis can be reconstructed if needed. Reported benefits include tracking patients lost to follow-up, and trial results informing NICE guidelines and later trials.

DARS-NIC-316704-Z1Z7T.summary: The University of Cambridge's agreement covers pseudonymised hospital admissions, death registration and National Diabetes Audit data for people who took part in long-running studies of children and adolescents with type 1 diabetes. The research looks at how childhood and adolescent risk factors relate to later heart, kidney, eye and nerve complications in adult life. The main intended benefit is better understanding of early risk factors, to help prevent complications and guide future care.

DARS-NIC-316705-C9F9J.summary: The Nuffield Trust, an independent research group, has an agreement covering bespoke extracts of hospital records linked to death records and patient-reported outcome measures. The agreement allows the data to be used to develop better indicators of good care for frail older people and to evaluate Comprehensive Geriatric Assessment, a process for assessing frail older patients. The aim is to help the NHS spot and adopt effective care and to learn which patients benefit most.

DARS-NIC-317048-N8P0R.summary: NHS Midlands and Lancashire Commissioning Support Unit's agreement covers pseudonymised health and care data, including hospital, community, mental health, maternity, ambulance and other services, with clinical and financial details. It supports the four Worcestershire and Herefordshire clinical commissioning groups (CCGs) in planning and commissioning services for their local population. The data is for reporting, population health analysis and demand planning. The stated aim is to improve patient pathways and the quality of services.

DARS-NIC-317612-V1Q3X.summary: The University of Oxford's agreement covers a bespoke extract of Hospital Episode Statistics (HES) outpatient data, grouped by small geographic area, age group and gender. The data is for a doctoral research project on whether internet use is associated with health outcomes in England. The agreement allows the data to be combined with survey and census data to look at health service use and population wellbeing.

DARS-NIC-317873-H3L1R.summary: The University of Manchester's agreement covers hospital records of accident and emergency visits, admitted patient care and outpatient appointments (Hospital Episode Statistics). Four academic projects are permitted to use them to evaluate how NHS financial and organisational reforms, such as non-payment for readmissions and pay-for-performance schemes, affected patient outcomes and hospital performance. The stated aim is to inform policy makers on designing incentives and allocating NHS resources.

DARS-NIC-318632-T0N3M.summary: The University of Leeds's agreement covers the use of pseudonymised hospital admission and death registration records, linked with National Hip Fracture Database data. The data is for comparing outcomes after a neck of femur (hip) fracture across ethnic groups and examining possible reasons for any differences. The main intended benefit is evidence on whether ethnicity data should be collected, so hospital trusts can allocate resources fairly. Preliminary analysis has shown variation in survival after this fracture by ethnicity.

DARS-NIC-31865-Z2Y1D.summary: Gateshead Metropolitan Borough Council's agreement covers hospital records of admissions, outpatient visits, critical care and emergency department attendances. The data is for its public health duties, including needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, the annual public health report and advice to NHS commissioners. The aim is locally focused analysis of health and health inequalities. Reported work includes analysis of alcohol-related admissions, housing and health conditions, and Covid-19 vaccine support.

DARS-NIC-318886-M1B9L.summary: The National Institute for Cardiovascular Outcomes Research, an academic body, is permitted under its agreement to compare hospital-level counts of admitted patient care records (Hospital Episode Statistics) for angioplasty (percutaneous coronary intervention) with the cases hospitals submit to the national audit, to check how complete the audit is. The agreement allows the main intended benefit to be publishing case ascertainment rates, which encourages hospitals to submit more complete data. Reported results include identifying centres below national benchmarks, with letters sent to centres performing fewer than 200 procedures for three successive years.

DARS-NIC-31911-S3Y6M.summary: Newcastle University's agreement covers records of children born with congenital heart disease (CHD) in England and Wales between 1985 and 2012, linked to death registrations and area deprivation scores. The data is for estimating survival up to 25 years and identifying factors that predict it. The main intended benefit is better information for counselling parents after a diagnosis and for planning health services.

DARS-NIC-319171-G7H8K.summary: The University of Bristol's agreement covers use of NHS England hospital, cancer registration, death and demographic records for the CAP trial, which compares inviting men aged 50 to 69 for a PSA blood test for prostate cancer with standard NHS care. The data are for following up men who did not consent, assessing whether PSA testing reduces prostate cancer deaths and whether it is cost-effective. Published results have already been presented to the Department of Health and Social Care and used by the National Screening Committee.

DARS-NIC-319738-F3W3L.summary: University Hospitals Bristol NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers linked hospital records (inpatient, outpatient, accident and emergency and critical care activity) and Office for National Statistics mortality data. It allows study of whether a UK-wide registry could record the use of cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (CMR) in patients with a suspected heart attack. The data is for describing patients, their other health conditions, resource use and changes in care. The aim is to inform a possible future registry and research on CMR's value.

DARS-NIC-320147-M9K6K.summary: London Ambulance Service NHS Trust's agreement covers linking hospital and emergency care records to its 999 call and patient records for women who called in April to July 2019. The agreement allows the data to be used to study how accurately the ambulance triage system (MPDS Protocol 24) identifies maternity emergencies and which questions and factors predict them. The main intended benefit is evidence to improve telephone triage questions, so women needing urgent help are identified more reliably.

DARS-NIC-320217-X8P0W.summary: King's College London's agreement covers the use of record-level data from the Adult Psychiatric Morbidity Survey to study how having several physical and mental health conditions at once relates to social class and to social exclusion, such as homelessness. The aim is to inform NHS care, public health policy and research on inclusion health. Preliminary results have already been shared at conferences and with clinicians, and a blog has been published.

DARS-NIC-321226-T4B8S.summary: NEC Software Solutions, a commercial organisation, is authorised to use Hospital Episode Statistics admitted patient care data for the National Joint Registry, which collects data on joint replacement surgery. The agreement allows it to check how fully NHS trusts and hospitals submit their joint replacement records, and to report on this. The aim is to keep data quality high so that patient safety and outcomes can be improved. Reported benefits include helping trusts monitor Best Practice Tariff targets and improving the recording of where surgery took place in HES.

DARS-NIC-321571-V5S9C.summary: Monitor, the health sector regulator, has an agreement covering detailed hospital records for A&E, critical care, inpatient and outpatient activity, with identifiers removed. The agreement allows the data to be used to carry out its duties under the Health and Social Care Act: licensing providers, regulating NHS prices, supporting integrated care, preventing anti-competitive behaviour and supporting continuity of services. The release register says detailed activity data over several years is essential for these functions.

DARS-NIC-321968-S4Q6L.summary: The University of Cambridge's agreement covers linked NHS records, including hospital, cancer registration, death, mental health and diabetes audit data, for 25,639 people in the EPIC-Norfolk health study. The data is for following participants' health over time and studying how diet and lifestyle relate to disease and healthy ageing. The aim is to help prevent chronic disease and support good health in later life. Reported benefits include research that fed into a Department of Health public health campaign and into clinical guidelines.

DARS-NIC-322051-S8N9N.summary: The University of Aberdeen, with the University of Oxford, has an agreement covering hospital admissions records, cause of death reports and cohort tracking reports for participants in the Knee Arthroplasty Trial. The data is for 20-year follow-up of how different knee replacement designs affect long-term safety, need for further surgery and cost-effectiveness. This should give stronger evidence for patients, clinicians and policy makers. Ten-year results have been published and are a key source for American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons clinical practice guidelines.

DARS-NIC-323026-N2R0B.summary: Hull City Council's agreement covers civil registration data on births and deaths, plus primary care mortality data, which includes identifiable details. The data is for understanding local health needs, planning services and supporting work such as suicide prevention, with the aim of tailoring services and reducing health inequalities. The agreement allows the data to analyse stillbirths, calculate ward-level mortality rates and life expectancy, and support the local alcohol and drugs needs assessment.

DARS-NIC-32317-W3C2K.summary: Telford & Wrekin Council's agreement covers hospital data on emergency care, admitted patients, critical care and outpatients. The agreement allows the data to be used in its public health work, including needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, the Director of Public Health's annual report and advice to NHS commissioners. The main intended benefit is locally focused analysis of health outcomes and inequalities, particularly for the most disadvantaged groups.

DARS-NIC-323223-Q6C3D.summary: Hull City Council's public health team's agreement covers hospital records for emergency care, admitted patients, critical care and outpatients. The agreement allows the records to support its public health duties, such as producing needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, the annual public health report and advice to NHS commissioners. The aim is locally focused analysis that helps identify and respond to health inequalities. Reported benefits so far include improved statutory reports, support for substance misuse services and asthma hotspot work.

DARS-NIC-323309-L2G9T.summary: The Institute of Occupational Medicine (IOM)'s agreement covers mortality and cancer-related records for about 40,000 people who worked in the UK rubber industry. The agreement allows the data to be used to find out whether chemicals used in rubber manufacturing raise the risk of dying from cancers such as lung, bladder and liver cancer. The expected benefit is better evidence on workplace risks, to inform occupational health policy and preventative measures in the industry.

DARS-NIC-323322-M3H0S.summary: RAND Europe's agreement covers bespoke extracts of Hospital Episode Statistics (HES) data for A&E attendances, inpatient admissions and outpatient appointments. The data is for evaluating the Southwark and Lambeth Integrated Care (SLIC) Older People's Programme, commissioned by King's Health Partners. The evaluation looks at the programme's effect on hospital use and its cost-effectiveness, comparing GP practices in the two boroughs with matched practices elsewhere in England.

DARS-NIC-323893-J8B4H.summary: The University of Dundee's agreement covers the use of hospital inpatient records (Hospital Episode Statistics), linked with death and cancer data, for a randomised clinical trial called SCOT. The trial compares the heart and stomach safety of celecoxib with traditional anti-inflammatory painkillers (NSAIDs) used to treat arthritis. The data is for confirming hospitalisations, deaths and serious adverse events among participants. The aim is to answer a European Medicines Agency request on celecoxib's safety.

DARS-NIC-323925-K0B9S.summary: London Borough of Haringey, a local authority, is permitted to use identifiable birth and death records, along with primary care mortality data. The agreement allows these data to be used to measure local health needs, plan immunisation programmes and protect public health, including suicide audits and prevention work. The aim is to tailor local services to areas of greatest need and reduce health inequalities. So far, it has analysed excess winter deaths, heatwave deaths, Covid-19 excess mortality and changes in birth rates.

DARS-NIC-324040-N7L9R.summary: Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust's agreement allows the use of hospital admission records and death registration data, including cause of death, for patients who had a cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) heart scan between June 2016 and May 2018. The data is for studying how well CMR findings, such as heart scarring, predict death and hospital admission for heart failure. The aim is to identify patients at risk earlier and guide treatment. The agreement has already led to a risk calculator, which has informed a primary care programme.

DARS-NIC-324116-W0K9R.summary: Swansea University's agreement covers bespoke extracts of hospital records for England (HES) covering accident and emergency, critical care, inpatients, outpatients and linked mortality data. The agreement allows the data to be used to study factors such as day of admission and hospital size that may affect outcomes after emergency admission, to supply injury data to a European injury database, and to develop a trauma mortality prediction model. It also allows the data to be used to estimate the burden of injuries from falls.

DARS-NIC-324170-J4P1J.summary: King's College Hospital NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers the use of hospital admissions data (Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care) and Maternity Services Data Set records, linked to kidney disease registries. The agreement allows the Trust to build a calculator that predicts how far pregnancy may worsen kidney function in women with chronic kidney disease. The aim is to help women and clinicians make informed decisions about pregnancy. The tool has been nearly finished, and a paper is about to be submitted.

DARS-NIC-324220-P6W9Y.summary: Queen Mary University of London's agreement covers identifiable hospital, emergency care, cancer registration and death records for about 3,000 participants in the IBIS-II breast cancer prevention and DCIS trials. The data is for long-term follow-up to study the effects of tamoxifen and anastrozole on breast cancer, other cancers, heart disease, fractures and deaths. The aim is to help patients and clinicians make better-informed treatment choices. Results have already been published and contributed to a licence variation for anastrozole in England.

DARS-NIC-324251-J9T5N.summary: NHS England's agreement covers linked hospital inpatient records (Hospital Episode Statistics) and patient-reported outcome measures, which are questionnaires completed before and after heart revascularisation procedures. The data is for a pilot run with the National Cardiac Benchmarking Collaborative and Liverpool Heart & Chest Hospital NHS Foundation Trust. The pilot tests whether these questionnaires can be collected routinely and whether clinicians find them useful for improving services. Its findings will inform whether trusts should be required to collect them.

DARS-NIC-324368-Q0H5T.summary: The University of Oxford's agreement covers the use of pseudonymised Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care data to check that its national study of children aged 5 to 16 with cerebral palsy who have multi-level orthopaedic surgery (SEMLS) has not missed any cases. The study aims to count how many children have this surgery across NHS Trusts in England and to show how surgeons choose which children to treat. The intended benefit is stronger evidence to help set standard guidance on care.

DARS-NIC-324388-L6C2Q.summary: The University of Birmingham's agreement covers mortality and cancer registration data on about 35-40,000 male UK oil refinery and petroleum distribution workers in England. The data is for checking whether these workers have higher rates of particular cancers and causes of death than the general population, which could point to workplace exposures such as benzene. The findings are intended to help regulators assess worker protection. Two reports have been published on the Energy Institute website.

DARS-NIC-324608-Q0G8L.summary: The University of Sheffield's School of Health and Related Research's agreement covers hospital records (admissions, A&E and critical care) and death registration data for adults taken to hospital by emergency ambulance with possible sepsis. The data is for linking to ambulance records to test how accurate and cost-effective early warning scores used by paramedics are for spotting sepsis. The aim is to identify the best score for the NHS, which could lead to better treatment and fewer deaths from sepsis.

DARS-NIC-325074-F0J3D.summary: The University of Leeds's agreement covers the use of hospital, mental health and mortality records for young people who took part in the SHIFT trial, which compared family therapy with usual treatment after self-harm. The data is linked to trial data to measure repeat hospital attendance and safety, and to describe services used. The intended benefit is to inform NHS practice and NICE guidance. Results have been published, and the trial helped lead to a commissioned meta-analysis of self-harm therapies.

DARS-NIC-325256-V6L1S.summary: Rod Gibson Associates Ltd's agreement covers a bespoke extract of Hospital Episode Statistics (HES) inpatient data. The data is for producing aggregate maternity indicators for each maternity unit, with small numbers suppressed. The agreement allows these indicators to be supplied to the "Which? Birth Choice" website and published on the BirthChoiceUK website. Both sites are free to use and help women choose where to give birth.

DARS-NIC-32537-Y2H2L.summary: The University of Warwick's agreement covers hospital records of accident and emergency visits, inpatient stays and outpatient appointments for people aged 65 and over. The data is for mapping the routes older patients with complex needs take through hospital and how those routes relate to their health outcomes and use of resources. The intended benefit is to help services plan and redesign care for this group.

DARS-NIC-325819-D6V9H.summary: University Hospitals Birmingham NHS Foundation Trust's agreement allows the use of pseudonymised Hospital Episode Statistics (HES) data covering A&E, critical care, inpatient and outpatient care, linked to Office for National Statistics (ONS) mortality data. The Health Informatics Department's use of the data is for producing quality and benchmarking analysis, through the online Healthcare Evaluation Data tool or bespoke reports, so that NHS trusts and commissioners can monitor clinical quality and organisational effectiveness. The stated aim is to help NHS organisations deliver better services for patients.

DARS-NIC-325899-B0C9B.summary: NHS Humber and North Yorkshire ICB (Sub ICB Location)'s agreement covers pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, maternity, ambulance, births and deaths data, including clinical and financial information. The agreement allows this data to be used to plan and commission health services for its local population, including population health management, service redesign and demand forecasting. The main intended benefit is better commissioning decisions and improved quality of care.

DARS-NIC-325964-L1W7R.summary: Imperial College Healthcare NHS Trust's agreement covers the use of record-level hospital inpatient data (Hospital Episode Statistics) for patients in the UK EVAR 1 trial. The data is for finding out whether deaths related to abdominal aortic aneurysm are higher over up to 15 years after endovascular repair than after open surgery. The aim is to inform the NHS about the best and most cost-effective way to repair these aneurysms.

DARS-NIC-326033-G1P7Q.summary: The University of Manchester, through its affiliated Trauma Audit and Research Network (TARN), agreement covers the use of Hospital Episode Statistics admitted patient care data. The data is for measuring how completely trusts and hospitals submit trauma cases to the TARN database, and for sending hospitals lists of eligible patients to help them identify missing cases. The main intended benefit is better trauma care, through more accurate analysis of hospital performance and correct Best Practice Tariff payments.

DARS-NIC-326062-R5P2C.summary: Wolfson Institute of Preventive Medicine's agreement covers the use of breast screening data and local authority data. The agreement allows the institute to produce annual aggregate tables and a report for the National Breast Screening Programme's radiology committee, which audits and evaluates the programme. The main intended benefit is spotting areas of poor performance so that remedial action, such as extra training, can be taken.

DARS-NIC-326404-L9K3Z.summary: MedeAnalytics International Limited's agreement covers bespoke extracts of Hospital Episode Statistics (HES) data covering A&E, inpatient and outpatient care. The data is for its online analytics service for NHS and social care organisations. The service is designed to provide customers with national comparators for quality and performance measures, shown as anonymised reports and dashboards. These are intended to support better operational, clinical and financial practice and, ultimately, better patient outcomes.

DARS-NIC-326736-Q0F3G.summary: The Nuffield Trust's agreement covers monthly Hospital Episode Statistics (HES) extracts for accident and emergency, inpatient and outpatient care. The data is for evaluating new models of care, tracking hospital admission patterns and costs across England, and studying the efficiency of health services. The stated aim is to help the NHS identify and adopt good practice in efficient, effective care.

DARS-NIC-327369-T1M7M.summary: The University of Nottingham, which manages the ATTACK trial for the University of Southampton, is permitted to use hospital admissions, emergency care, death registration and cancer registration records. These records are for identifying heart attacks, strokes and other outcomes in people with chronic kidney disease, so the trial can test whether low-dose aspirin prevents major vascular events. The main intended benefit is evidence on whether aspirin should be prescribed to these patients.

DARS-NIC-327653-J2T3C.summary: SSentif Intelligence's agreement covers a bespoke extract of Hospital Episode Statistics (HES) inpatient data. The agreement allows analysis of the patient-level records to produce aggregated indicators, such as average length of stay, with small numbers suppressed. These indicators are for NHS and local government subscribers, who use them to compare organisations' performance across England. The stated benefit is helping subscribers spot service areas that may need closer attention or redesign.

DARS-NIC-327824-F8N7T.summary: Health IQ Ltd's agreement covers monthly Hospital Episode Statistics (HES) data on inpatient, outpatient and accident and emergency care. The agreement allows the data to be fed into Vantage, an online tool that lets NHS bodies and some pharmaceutical companies analyse healthcare data and produce reports. The aim is to improve clinical outcomes and operational efficiency, through uses such as commissioning intelligence, benchmarking and service redesign modelling.

DARS-NIC-327960-M2P9M.summary: Swansea University's agreement covers the use of linked hospital records (outpatient, inpatient and A&E) and death registration data. The data is for evaluating whether multi-disciplinary case management for people who frequently call 999 is safe and effective, including whether it shifts demand elsewhere in the NHS. The aim is to help ambulance services manage frequent callers better. A final report was sent to the funder in June 2023, and preliminary findings were presented at the EMS 999 Research Forum.

DARS-NIC-32833-M3M9V.summary: The Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) agreement covers the use of Hospital Episode Statistics data on accident and emergency, admitted patient care and outpatients. The agreement allows analysis of how closely NHS Trusts that plan to merge compete, including where patients live, which services overlap and how GP referrals are spread. The data is for helping decide whether mergers would reduce patient choice and quality. The data has already underpinned most of the analysis in the CMA's reviews of two mergers, in Manchester and Birmingham.

DARS-NIC-328464-Y5Y8F.summary: The University of Kent holds survey data from adult social care users and from carers of people receiving adult social care in England. The original study, by the university's Personal Social Services Research Unit, looked at variations in quality and outcomes and at the efficiency and productivity of social care services. The work was intended to inform social care policy and practice, including the Adult Social Care Outcomes Framework. This agreement only permits the data to be kept for an interim period.

DARS-NIC-32854-Y8P8B.summary: The Institute for Fiscal Studies's agreement covers the use of hospital records (inpatient, outpatient, A&E and critical care) and mortality data, linked to the English Longitudinal Study of Ageing, which follows people aged 50 and over. The data is for studying the economics of health and social care use as the population ages, to help plan services and policy. Results have been presented to the Department of Health and Social Care and NHS England, and a paper was published in the Milbank Quarterly in October 2020.

DARS-NIC-329869-Q9Z2Z.summary: The London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine's agreement covers Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care data, covering hospital admissions in England from 1997 onwards. The agreement allows the data to be used to study how air pollution, heat, cold and pollen affect hospital admissions in small areas, and which groups are most vulnerable. The aim is to give policymakers detailed risk information to protect vulnerable people. The team has linked the data to local environmental measures and submitted articles on admissions for conditions such as asthma.

DARS-NIC-330126-N1W7H.summary: Methods Analytics's agreement covers receipt of hospital activity data covering admissions, outpatients, A&E and critical care (Hospital Episode Statistics and Secondary Uses Service data). The agreement allows the data to be used to build indicators, dashboards and reports that compare NHS organisations nationally and show variation in quality, safety and patient experience. These tools are for NHS commissioners, providers, surgical societies and, in some cases, the public, including the free Stethoscope quality variation tool.

DARS-NIC-330478-X4Y4R.summary: Advancing Quality Alliance (AQuA), a not-for-profit membership body hosted by Salford Royal NHS Foundation Trust, is permitted to use Hospital Episode Statistics (HES) accident and emergency, inpatient and outpatient monthly extracts. The agreement allows the data to deliver services to NHS and social care members, including analysis of trends over several years and in-depth mortality reviews that check whether a trust is an outlier on a range of indicators. The release register states that these services support quality improvement programmes for its members.

DARS-NIC-330769-C9Y8Y.summary: University College London (UCL)'s agreement covers hospital records (outpatient, inpatient, A&E and critical care) linked to death registration data. The agreement allows study of what happens to young people with long-term conditions when they move from children's to adult health services, and which features of transition work best. The data is for guiding Department of Health policy and helping to develop measures of transition quality. UCL has already given the Department of Health a briefing paper and presented findings at conferences.

DARS-NIC-330892-Q5J3T.summary: The University of Cambridge's agreement covers the use of NHS registration data, Office for National Statistics (ONS) cancer and mortality data, and Scottish events data for medical research. The work involves recruiting 350,000 people across nine European countries, with the Norfolk region covering the UK, and following their later health outcomes. It focuses particularly on cancer, and also aims to assess how cardiovascular risk and other chronic diseases are distributed.

DARS-NIC-331142-P5K6M.summary: The University of Bristol runs the National Child Mortality Database, using NHS hospital, maternity, mental health, community, cancer, medicines and death records on children who die in England before their 18th birthday. It links these to child death review data to study how and why children die and to support recommendations that reduce child deaths. It reports that its findings have contributed to policy change, guidance and safety notices, and that its Sudden Unexpected Death in Childhood report was debated in parliament.

DARS-NIC-331607-P4J8H.summary: The University of York's agreement covers hospital records (outpatient, inpatient, and accident and emergency) and death registration data. The data is for studying whether healthcare use, especially emergency care, rises when young people with life limiting conditions move from children's to adult services. The aim is to give commissioners and hospices evidence to adapt services and target support at the groups most affected.

DARS-NIC-331733-T2K1Z.summary: Sandwell and West Birmingham Hospitals NHS Trust's agreement covers civil registration death records and demographic data for 1,487 people in the Birmingham and Black Country Atrial Fibrillation study cohort. The agreement allows causes of death to be linked to blood test markers taken at recruitment, to build a model predicting which people with atrial fibrillation will develop heart failure. The intended benefit is helping doctors start preventive heart failure treatment earlier. Baseline study data has already contributed to combined analyses within a research consortium seeking new biomarkers and treatment targets.

DARS-NIC-331739-Y7B7X.summary: NHS England's agreement covers a bespoke extract of the Mental Health and Learning Disabilities Dataset (MHLDDS), which covers mental health services. The agreement allows the data to be used to understand commissioning patterns, prevalence, treatments and outcomes, and to analyse service use, diagnosis coding quality and restraint, and to update a mental health quality dashboard. The stated aim is to help commissioners ensure appropriate services are provided and to improve outcomes for people with mental health problems.

DARS-NIC-331952-D8S2S.summary: Barnsley Metropolitan Borough Council, a local authority, has an agreement covering Hospital Episode Statistics data on emergency care, admitted patient care, critical care, outpatients and accident and emergency. The agreement allows the data to be used in its public health work, including needs assessments, health strategies, the Director of Public Health's annual report and advice to NHS commissioners. The main intended benefit is locally focused analysis of health outcomes and inequalities, including for specific groups, so that local health challenges can be identified and responded to.

DARS-NIC-332038-N4Z8R.summary: BMJ (the publishing arm of the British Medical Association) uses Hospital Episode Statistics data on accident and emergency, inpatient and outpatient care, including consultant codes for its customers. It uses the data only to power "Hospital Insight", a web-based benchmarking tool for acute non-specialist NHS trusts in England. Trusts use it to monitor performance on quality, efficiency, the local market and clinician revalidation.
DARS-NIC-332038-N4Z8R.retense_draft: BMJ's agreement covers use of Hospital Episode Statistics data on accident and emergency, inpatient and outpatient care, including consultant codes, for its customers. The data is used only to power "Hospital Insight", a web-based benchmarking tool for acute non-specialist NHS trusts in England. Trusts use it to monitor performance on quality, efficiency, the local market and clinician revalidation.

DARS-NIC-332338-X1N2G.summary: The University of Leeds's agreement covers the linking of hospital admission records and civil registration death records to its consented EMMACE study cohort of heart attack patients. The data is for studying how changes in health-related quality of life relate to later outcomes such as stroke, repeat heart attack, heart failure and death. The aim is to help design interventions that improve quality of life and survival. Results have already appeared in peer-reviewed journals and at conferences.

DARS-NIC-33234-C0V1D.summary: The University of Oxford's agreement covers mortality data (cause of death, cohort event notification and flagging status reports) for 290 people who had a transient ischaemic attack (TIA), a temporary interruption to the brain's blood supply. The agreement allows linking this to an existing study to estimate long-term survival, main causes of death and factors linked to survival. The aim is to help clinicians and patients understand prognosis after a TIA. An earlier 2003 paper from the study has been downloaded 3,926 times and cited 177 times.

DARS-NIC-332566-K2H4G.summary: Public Health England (PHE) is using a bespoke extract from the Diagnostic Imaging Dataset (DIDS). The data is used for cancer registration and to support investigations into GP Direct Access and into the diagnosis, care and treatment of patients.
DARS-NIC-332566-K2H4G.retense_draft: Public Health England's agreement covers a bespoke extract from the Diagnostic Imaging Dataset (DIDS). The data is for cancer registration and to support investigations into GP Direct Access and into the diagnosis, care and treatment of patients.

DARS-NIC-332870-B6Z4R.summary: The London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine's agreement covers the use of hospital admission, critical care and death registration records to evaluate community-based multi-disciplinary teams that join up health and social care. The agreement allows comparison of patients who used these teams with matched patients who did not, to see whether outcomes differ between patients and between team models. The aim is to give policymakers better evidence on how to integrate services cost-effectively.

DARS-NIC-333021-B6W2C.summary: The University of Manchester, an academic body, holds pseudonymised Hospital Episode Statistics admitted patient care and critical care records from 1999 to 2017. Under this agreement the data is only kept securely for an interim period, with no other processing and no new outputs. The data was originally supplied for the Norfolk Arthritis Register, a long-term community study of the causes and outcomes of inflammatory polyarthritis.

DARS-NIC-33318-X4Q1B.summary: The University of Manchester's agreement covers the use of hospital records (Hospital Episode Statistics for accident and emergency, admitted patient care and outpatients) to study whether dementia training for hospital staff affects outcomes for patients with dementia. The data is for giving evidence to inform national and hospital Trust policy on dementia care. Results presented so far show that poorer outcomes for people with dementia are mostly explained by patient characteristics, and that no beneficial impact of training was found. A paper has been submitted to BMC Medicine.

DARS-NIC-333498-D1K7G.summary: Cardiff University's agreement covers NHS England hospital records (inpatient, outpatient and accident and emergency) and death registration data for mothers and children from the Building Blocks trial of the Family Nurse Partnership home-visiting programme. The data is for evaluating the programme's long-term effectiveness, mainly in reducing child maltreatment, and its costs and consequences. Results were published in journals and shared with government and local authorities, and early results influenced decisions on funding the FNP National Unit.

DARS-NIC-333880-G4H3T.summary: NHS West Yorkshire Integrated Care Board (ICB), through its Wakefield sub-ICB location, is covered by an agreement allowing it to use pseudonymised health and care data, including hospital, mental health, community, maternity and death records. The data is for planning and commissioning health services for the local population, with processing carried out by North of England Commissioning Support Unit. The main intended benefit is better-informed commissioning decisions that improve service quality and health outcomes. The agreement has allowed benchmarking of performance across West Yorkshire and easier sharing of insight between CCGs.

DARS-NIC-334459-R9H4C.summary: The University of York's agreement covers linked hospital records (emergency care, admitted patient care and outpatient data) for 180 children in the "Your Tube" study who are fed through a gastrostomy tube. The data is for comparing healthcare use and gastrostomy complications between children fed formula and those fed home-blended meals. It is also for checking whether routine data could support longer-term follow-up. The aim is to provide evidence to inform clinical guidelines.

DARS-NIC-334549-B1Y6X.summary: The University of Bristol's agreement covers hospital records (admissions, outpatient and A&E) and death registration data, linked to the National Hip Fracture Database. The data is for studying how differences between hospitals in organising hip fracture care affect patient outcomes such as death, hospital stay and readmission. The aim is to reduce avoidable variation and improve care quality. Published papers have already supported a free toolkit for hip fracture services, launched in February 2023.

DARS-NIC-334745-L4J6P.summary: University Hospital Southampton NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers the use of hospital, death registration, diagnostic imaging, maternity and demographic data to study unruptured brain aneurysms in England. The study aims to predict the risk of rupture, including during pregnancy and delivery, so treatment decisions can be better informed. Pilot results have already shown that hospital and death records identified ruptured aneurysms in a subgroup of patients with a detection rate above 98%.

DARS-NIC-334952-R5M7K.summary: University College London (UCL)'s agreement covers the use of identifiable NHS hospital, cancer registration, death and demographic records from women in the UK Collaborative Trial of Ovarian Cancer Screening. The agreement allows these records to be used to identify cases for follow-on studies that draw on the trial's stored blood samples, aiming to improve early detection of disease, especially cancer. The trial's main results were published in 2023, and further studies and publications have followed from the trial's data and samples.

DARS-NIC-33499-F9N8F.summary: Plymouth City Council's agreement covers civil registration births and deaths data, plus primary care mortality data, which includes identifiable details. The agreement allows the data to be used to measure local health needs, protect public health and support work such as suicide audits, with published results only as aggregated figures. The main intended benefit is local services tailored to areas of greatest need, reducing health inequalities and premature deaths. The data has been used to produce a 2020 to 2022 suicide audit summary and Joint Strategic Needs Assessment documents.

DARS-NIC-335133-K2Y2S.summary: The Institute of Occupational Medicine (IOM)'s agreement covers the use of bespoke Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) data, a list cleaning report, NHS registration data and Office for National Statistics (ONS) mortality data. The data is for comparing death rates among hard-metal industry workers with those of the general population, and between lower and higher work exposures. The aim is to clarify whether working in the industry raises the risk of diseases such as lung cancer, to inform occupational health policy.

DARS-NIC-336478-Z7Q9F.summary: The Nuffield Trust's agreement covers hospital data from accident and emergency, admitted patient care and outpatients (Hospital Episode Statistics). The data is for QualityWatch, a programme that monitors changes in the quality of NHS care through reports, blogs and online indicators. The aim is to give independent analysis that prompts improvements. Earlier QualityWatch reports were cited in an NHS England mental health plan and used by a commissioning support unit to change its approach.

DARS-NIC-336857-P6C9Q.summary: The University of Bristol, jointly with the University of Manchester, is using hospital inpatient and outpatient records and death registration data for adults in England who were admitted with a severe pressure ulcer. The study describes the care these patients received and compares outcomes, such as returning to hospital and death, for those who did and did not have surgery. It aims to inform the design of a future randomised controlled trial of reconstructive surgery. So far, results have been presented at several conferences, including a poster at the International Clinical Trials Methodology Conference 2022.
DARS-NIC-336857-P6C9Q.retense_draft: The University of Bristol, jointly with the University of Manchester, is permitted to use hospital inpatient and outpatient records and death registration data for adults in England who were admitted with a severe pressure ulcer. The study describes the care these patients received and compares outcomes, such as returning to hospital and death, for those who did and did not have surgery. It aims to inform the design of a future randomised controlled trial of reconstructive surgery. Results have already been presented at several conferences, including a poster at the International Clinical Trials Methodology Conference 2022.

DARS-NIC-337151-T2S2K.summary: The University of Leeds's agreement covers Hospital Episode Statistics (HES) data on accident and emergency visits, inpatient and outpatient care, plus patient-reported outcome measures (PROMS), including patients' home postcodes. The data is for an NIHR-funded doctoral fellowship studying adults with rheumatoid arthritis and osteoarthritis in West Yorkshire and Harrogate. The study examines how travel distance to hospital relates to health outcomes and health inequalities, so it can inform guidance on moving or centralising health services.

DARS-NIC-337801-K2N5Y.summary: The Health and Safety Executive's agreement covers cancer registrations, death records and demographic data on about 79,700 asbestos workers recruited before 2006. It allows tracking of their long-term deaths and cancers, comparing them with the general population and across types of asbestos work. The aim is to show whether tighter asbestos regulation reduces disease and to inform future policy. Findings have already appeared in HSE research reports and peer-reviewed journals, and previously published articles have been cited over 160 times.

DARS-NIC-337896-H4F8C.summary: The University of Oxford's agreement covers breast screening annual return data (KC returns), with the release register also describing cervical screening returns. The data is for building graphs and other analysis methods that improve how breast and cervical screening performance is evaluated in England, allowing for confounding factors and statistical ability. The aim is to enable better comparison between screening services, such as laboratories, through adjusted performance measures. Findings are to be reported to screening evaluation groups and possibly published in journals.

DARS-NIC-338242-C8Z8M.summary: NHS Blood and Transplant holds linked hospital admission and death registration data for people on the national kidney transplant waiting list. The research looks at what happens to patients suspended from the list, including their hospital admissions and causes of death. It aims to help build a model for allocating donor kidneys by clinical need, with the intended benefit of fewer waiting list deaths and a fairer allocation policy.

DARS-NIC-338303-P4G5Q.summary: Cambridge University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers the use of hospital admitted patient care and outpatient records (Hospital Episode Statistics) for a clinical trial called the DIvO study. The trial tests whether digital imaging with the Neocam device is better than the standard ophthalmoscopic red-reflex test at detecting congenital cataract in newborns. The main intended benefit is earlier detection, which could lead to better long-term vision and may inform national screening policy.

DARS-NIC-338773-H5J5S.summary: The University of Manchester's Trauma Audit and Research Network (TARN) agreement covers the use of Hospital Episode Statistics admitted patient care data and civil registration death data. The data is for checking how completely hospitals submit trauma cases, and for working out 30-day patient outcomes, so that TARN can improve the quality of its reports. The aim is to improve patient care. Hospitals that used the linked data reportedly improved case identification by 5 to 50%, averaging 20%.

DARS-NIC-338789-M0T3Q.summary: NHS Bedfordshire, Luton and Milton Keynes Integrated Care Board (ICB)'s agreement covers the use of pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other health and care data, including clinical and financial information. The data is for planning and redesigning local health services, understanding the needs of the population, and identifying patients at risk of needing hospital care. The main intended benefit is better-planned services and improved patient flow, access and quality of care.

DARS-NIC-338864-B3Z3J.summary: Barts and the London School of Medicine and Dentistry's agreement covers linking NHS England hospital, mental health, community, maternity, cancer, death and diabetes audit records for the Genes & Health research programme. The data is for combining these records with genetic data to study health and disease in British Bangladeshi and British Pakistani people, with the aim of improving their health. Reported results include 44 publications and 50 volunteers diagnosed with familial hypercholesterolaemia and referred for NHS treatment.

DARS-NIC-339853-V1G0K.summary: Monitor, the health sector regulator, is permitted to use detailed hospital activity data from the Secondary Uses Service (SUS), covering outpatient, inpatient, A&E and critical care records. The data is for its duties under the Health and Social Care Act: licensing providers, regulating prices, supporting integrated care, preventing anti-competitive behaviour and supporting continuity of services. The agreement also allows it to share cleansed data with NHS England to help develop the National Tariff.

DARS-NIC-341768-K2T6V.summary: The University of Birmingham, as sponsor of the BASIL-3 trial, has an agreement covering hospital admission and death records for 481 patients with severe leg ischaemia (blocked blood vessels between the hip and knee). The data is for extending follow-up of trial participants and checking main outcomes without contacting them again. The trial compares three treatments, with the aim of finding the most clinically and cost-effective one.

DARS-NIC-341915-Z7J0Y.summary: The University of Edinburgh's agreement covers hospital, emergency care, death registration and primary care dispensed medicines records for 733 consented participants in the DUAL-ACS clinical trial. The agreement allows the data to be linked to trial data to compare 3 and 12 months of dual anti-platelet therapy after a type 1 heart attack. The main intended benefit is clear evidence on the safest treatment duration, to guide clinical practice and reduce harm and costs.

DARS-NIC-342096-J4N8K.summary: Imperial College London's Dr Foster Unit's agreement covers hospital administrative data from Hospital Episode Statistics (HES): A&E, critical care, inpatient and outpatient records. The data is for measuring the quality of healthcare delivered by providers or areas and for showing variations between providers. The work also supports a management information function for the NHS. Results are fed back to hospital trusts, which can use them to start clinical audits and case note reviews.

DARS-NIC-342229-X7K0T.summary: NHS Gloucestershire ICB, a sub-ICB location, has an agreement that allows it to use identifiable hospital activity data (Secondary Uses Service for Commissioners) and the Personal Demographic Service. The data is for checking provider invoices and confirming it is the responsible commissioner, and for identifying patients at high risk so GPs and commissioners can plan and target care. The aim is accurate payment and better, more effective commissioning. An annual report has referenced achievements supported by this data.

DARS-NIC-342322-Q1N7M.summary: University College London's agreement covers linked health records for children, including hospital, emergency care, mental health, birth and death registration data, with the Office for National Statistics processing the data. The study compares health and educational outcomes of children who had a brain injury around the time of birth with two matched groups of children without one. It aims to give parents, clinicians, the NHS and policymakers better evidence to shape care, follow-up and educational support.

DARS-NIC-342809-H1V7F.summary: The Nuffield Trust, an independent research group, has an agreement to receive Hospital Episode Statistics (HES) monthly extracts covering accident and emergency, inpatient and outpatient care. The agreement allows the data to be used for research on hospital use and costs, including evaluating new models of care, tracking admission patterns across England, and studying NHS efficiency.
