The stated aim is to help the NHS identify and adopt good practice.

DARS-NIC-343042-X5T7Y.summary: NHS Gloucestershire ICB, a sub-ICB location, is permitted to use pseudonymised local provider flow data covering acute, ambulance, community, mental health, emergency care, primary care and other services. The agreement allows the data to be analysed, with support from South, Central and West Commissioning Support Unit and Optum Health Solutions, to examine clinical and financial activity so health services can be planned around the local population's needs. The main intended benefit is better-planned services and patient pathways.

DARS-NIC-343158-Z2L4D.summary: NHS Gloucestershire ICB's agreement covers the use of pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, maternity, prescribing, social care and births and deaths data about people in the Gloucestershire area. The data is for planning and commissioning health and care services, understanding local health needs and supporting population health management. The main intended benefit is better-planned services and improved health outcomes. The CCG published an annual report that referred to key achievements supported by this data.

DARS-NIC-343380-H5Q9K.summary: The UK Health Security Agency's agreement covers a wide range of NHS England data, including hospital, emergency care, maternity, prescribing, testing and death registration records. The agreement allows the data to be used to monitor, prepare for and respond to infectious diseases and other health threats, producing statistics, surveillance reports, dashboards and guidance. The aim is to protect public health. Covid-19 test results have already been used to estimate infection levels and the reproduction number, informing government decisions on restrictions and public advice.

DARS-NIC-344271-Q5X0S.summary: The University of Oxford's agreement covers the use of hospital accident and emergency and admitted patient care records, linked with other primary care and death data, to study how the mix of staff in general practice teams relates to quality of care, effectiveness and staffing costs. The agreement allows the study to show which staffing combinations work best and where tasks can move between different practitioners. The intended benefit is to help practices and commissioners make staffing decisions that treat more patients effectively at the same or lower cost.

DARS-NIC-344511-H6N5B.summary: The British Society of Gastroenterology's agreement covers linking Hospital Episode Statistics data on inpatient, outpatient and A&E care to its registry of people with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) in England. The data is for measuring health outcomes and use of care, and for producing hospital feedback reports, an annual report and research. The main intended benefit is better benchmarking and national planning to improve IBD care.

DARS-NIC-344986-Y3R8M.summary: University College London (UCL)'s agreement covers the use of hospital inpatient records (Hospital Episode Statistics) and mortality records from the Office for National Statistics (ONS), linked with National Joint Registry data on hip replacements. It is a patient safety study into whether people with metal-on-metal hip replacements are more likely to develop heart failure than people with other hip replacements. The results are to be reported to the MHRA, so it can be established whether patients with these implants need cardiac screening.

DARS-NIC-345760-Q0M2Z.summary: The University of Manchester's agreement covers a bespoke extract of Hospital Episode Statistics (HES) inpatient records. It is for a PhD project within the National Confidential Inquiry into Suicide and Homicide. The project compares people with schizophrenia who committed homicide with matched control patients who did not. It looks at their social, criminological and clinical characteristics and their clinical care. The findings are intended for publication in peer-reviewed medical journals.

DARS-NIC-345789-L9Q7J.summary: The University of Surrey's agreement covers the use of NHS England hospital, emergency care, mental health, patient-reported outcome and death registration data. The data is for studying what affects how well NHS hospitals and ambulance trusts keep their staff, and how staff retention affects patient outcomes such as mortality, readmissions and length of stay. The aim is to give policymakers evidence for improving retention and patient care. So far, the project has led to press coverage, presentations to NHS England, and funding extensions.

DARS-NIC-345991-H2F5N.summary: Imperial College London's Dr Foster Unit's agreement covers hospital administrative data for accident and emergency, admitted patient care, critical care and outpatients. The agreement allows the unit to develop and test measures of healthcare quality and safety by provider, show variations in performance, and support NHS management information. Planned analyses include readmissions, returns to theatre after hip and knee replacement, and NHS capacity pressures. The stated aim is to help understand and improve the quality and safety of care.

DARS-NIC-346122-J2J0K.summary: Harvey Walsh Ltd, an NHS informatics and healthcare consultancy, is permitted under its agreement to receive monthly pseudonymised Hospital Episode Statistics (HES) data covering A&E, critical care, inpatient and outpatient care. The agreement allows it to analyse the data and provide an online system called Axon to NHS commissioners and providers, and to pharmaceutical and device companies. The work covers areas such as benchmarking, pathway analysis and disease burden. The stated aim is to improve patient care and access to services.

DARS-NIC-346693-F2X1G.summary: University College London (UCL), an academic organisation, is permitted under its agreement to use linked NHS hospital, mental health, cancer, death and COVID-19 records for the Whitehall II study of ageing in a long-running group of participants. The agreement allows the data to examine how social, biological and behavioural factors affect late-life conditions such as dementia, chronic disease and physical functioning, aiming to inform health policy and prevention. Its findings have been cited in clinical guidelines, including a 2023 NICE guideline on cardiovascular disease.

DARS-NIC-346859-C9J6J.summary: The University of York, working with Hull University Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust, is permitted to use linked NHS records, including hospital, cancer registration and death data, for patients with blood cancers in Yorkshire and Humberside. The agreement allows study of the causes of these cancers, their effect on later health and healthcare needs, and real-world treatment outcomes. The data is for informing cancer policy and services. Its data have already been used in 49 NICE submissions on treatments.

DARS-NIC-347023-W4W4V.summary: NHiS, an information intermediary, is licensed to use record-level pseudonymised, non-identifiable Hospital Episode Statistics (HES) data, including a bespoke extract from the Diagnostic Imaging Dataset (DIDS). The agreement allows the data to be used to produce public Disease Insight Reports and to support NHS commissioning through a set of tools called Q-PASS. The release register states that the aim is to raise disease awareness, improve diagnosis and management, and support service improvement.

DARS-NIC-347200-H9G0Q.summary: University of Leicester's agreement covers mortality data from the Medical Research Information Service (cause of death and current status reports) for 719 consenting participants in its Walking Away from Type 2 Diabetes Study. Researchers will examine how objectively measured physical activity and sedentary behaviour relate to the risk of death from all causes and from specific diseases. The aim is to strengthen the evidence on sedentary behaviour and mortality, which could inform NICE guidance and lifestyle interventions.

DARS-NIC-347209-L2Q4S.summary: St George's Hospital Medical School (St George's, University of London) agreement covers hospital and emergency care records from NHS England, covering admissions, outpatient visits, critical care and A&E attendances. The data is for a randomised controlled trial of specialist physiotherapy for functional motor disorder, a condition causing symptoms such as weakness and tremor. The records will show whether the physiotherapy reduces health service use and costs compared with usual treatment. If it works, this could support rolling it out across the NHS.

DARS-NIC-347470-X0W7J.summary: The University of Leeds's agreement covers identifiable hospital data (Hospital Episode Statistics for A&E, inpatient and outpatient care, plus mental health records) linked to a regional cancer register for children and young people. The data is for researching pathways and time to diagnosis for those diagnosed with cancer under 30, and the risks and costs to the NHS of later hospital admissions among survivors. The release register says this research could help identify environmental risk factors and check for inequalities in outcomes and access to specialist care.

DARS-NIC-348357-W0P1W.summary: NHS Devon ICB, working with NHS Kernow and Cornwall Council, is covered by an agreement to use pseudonymised health and social care data covering hospital, community, mental health, ambulance, primary care and death records. The agreement allows the data to be used to plan and commission health services, support population health management and compare provider performance. The main intended benefit is services that match local population needs. The register reports that the data has already helped monitor in-year projects and shape service delivery.

DARS-NIC-348988-V6G1J.summary: The Healthcare Quality Improvement Partnership (HQIP)'s agreement covers the use of identifiable Hospital Episode Statistics (HES) inpatient records for the National Pregnancy in Diabetes Audit. The records are to be linked to the audit's consenting cohort to add details of mode of delivery and delivery outcomes. The aim is to assess how well pre-existing diabetes care in pregnancy meets NICE guidance and what outcomes follow. The main intended benefit is to help delivery units improve care for women with diabetes who are pregnant, while reducing the data collection burden on participating sites.

DARS-NIC-34907-D9R3N.summary: The University of Cambridge's agreement covers NHS hospital records (Hospital Episode Statistics for accident and emergency, inpatient and outpatient care) and a service that checks which participants are still alive. The data covers people with recently diagnosed type 2 diabetes in the ADDITION-Plus trial. The data is for following their heart and circulation outcomes and health service use over the long term, and for testing whether a behaviour change programme helps. The aim is to inform NHS treatment decisions. The study has published 10 peer-reviewed papers so far.

DARS-NIC-349273-T3L4K.summary: The Royal College of Physicians of London's agreement covers the use of pseudonymised hospital admission and death registration data for patients in the national COPD audit in England and Wales. The agreement allows linking this data to audit records to examine readmissions and deaths within 30 and 90 days, with the aim of showing how hospital care affects outcomes and improving COPD care. Reports published in 2023 and 2024 have been used by hospitals to compare their performance and plan improvements.

DARS-NIC-349486-Y3C3L.summary: Market and Opinion Research International Limited, a commercial research company, has an agreement covering data from two national social care surveys: the Adult Social Care Survey of service users and the Survey of Adult Carers in England. The agreement allows analysis of which groups are under-represented in the surveys, as part of a research project funded by the National Institute for Health Research. The data is for helping the Department of Health and Social Care, NHS Digital and local authorities improve how well the surveys represent people, so that their findings are less misleading.

DARS-NIC-34964-S2V0M.summary: The Royal College of Paediatrics & Child Health (RCPCH)'s agreement covers the use of Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care data, linked to National Paediatric Diabetes Audit data. The agreement allows production of a three-year report on emergency hospital admissions for diabetes-related complications in children and young people in England and Wales. The aim is to show whether improvements in care are matched by fewer admissions, and to support targeted efforts to reduce them.

DARS-NIC-349688-V6V0Q.summary: NHS Humber and North Yorkshire ICB's agreement covers pseudonymised health, social care and mortality data, including hospital, community, mental health, maternity and prescribing records, for planning and commissioning health services for the population of the former East Riding of Yorkshire CCG area. The data is for population health management, service redesign, demand forecasting and contract management. The main aim is to match services to local needs. The register reports that services have been delivered to match population requirements.

DARS-NIC-349877-M5P7D.summary: i5 Health's agreement covers patient-level hospital data, including A&E, inpatient and outpatient activity from Hospital Episode Statistics (HES) and Secondary Uses Service (SUS) extracts. The agreement allows the data to be analysed to evaluate the economic impact of non-medical prescribing for the Health Education Board of NHS England. It also allows support for clinical commissioning groups (CCGs) with commissioning decisions, identifying savings initiatives and gaps in care, and advice to voluntary sector organisations.

DARS-NIC-349889-Q7R7K.summary: University Hospital Southampton NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers the use of civil registration death records to follow intensive care patients for one year after they had a high-sensitivity troponin blood test. The data is for finding out whether raised troponin levels in critical illness predict longer-term death and cause of death. The expected benefit is a better understanding of how clinicians should interpret these results in intensive care. Two abstracts have been accepted for presentation at the European Society of Cardiology Congress.

DARS-NIC-350331-P9L1M.summary: Roehampton University's agreement covers the use of record-level hospital admission, maternity services and death registration data about women giving birth in selected London areas and hospitals. The pilot study will compare childbirth, interventions such as inductions, forceps and C-sections, and maternal deaths and illness across ethnic groups. It aims to test whether the standard model of "normal" labour, based largely on white women, contributes to the ethnic gap in maternal outcomes, with a longer-term aim of improving care for Black, Asian and minority ethnic women.

DARS-NIC-35107-B1P1X.summary: NHS Eastern Cheshire CCG's agreement allows it to use Secondary User Services (SUS+) data for commissioners, which is identifiable by NHS number and held in a secure Controlled Environment for Finance. The data is for validating invoices from care providers, checking that claimed activity is its responsibility, and producing budget and business intelligence reports. The main intended benefit is financial validation of activity and better budget control.

DARS-NIC-35140-S8F6W.summary: Halton Borough Council's agreement allows it to use identifiable birth and death registration data, including primary care mortality data, to measure local health needs, plan services and support public health work such as suicide audits and Joint Strategic Needs Assessments. The data is for tailoring local services to areas of greatest need and reducing health inequalities. In 2023, the council used the data to produce local life expectancy and mortality figures for ward profiles and council performance reporting.

DARS-NIC-35152-Y4T0D.summary: Devon County Council's agreement covers identifiable civil registration data on births and deaths, plus primary care mortality data, for understanding local health needs, protecting public health and supporting work such as suicide audits and hotspot mapping. The agreement allows results to be published as summary statistics to guide local services and reduce health inequalities. The council reports that this has informed its Annual Public Health Report, Joint Strategic Needs Assessment and suicide prevention strategy.

DARS-NIC-351522-Y6W3L.summary: The Health and Safety Executive's agreement covers cancer registrations, death records, demographic details and hospital admissions data for people who completed pesticide competence certificates between 1994 and 2003. The agreement allows the data to be used to monitor long-term health, including cancer, deaths and hospital admissions for neurological, eye, respiratory and skin diseases. The aim is to inform policy on the health risks of working with pesticides. Earlier analyses of cancer and deaths have been published in HSE research reports and a 2011 peer-reviewed paper.

DARS-NIC-35166-B5Y7P.summary: Civil Eyes Research Ltd, a commercial research company, is permitted to use pseudonymised hospital activity data (Hospital Episode Statistics, covering admitted care, outpatients, accident and emergency, and critical care, plus the Emergency Care Data Set). The agreement allows the data to be used to benchmark hospitals against their peers, with analysis shared in workshops, to improve efficiency and clinical quality. It reports that hospitals have used this to review children's testicular surgery, London neurology services and organ transplantation.

DARS-NIC-351722-W7D4N.summary: L2S2 Ltd's agreement covers the use of pseudonymised Hospital Episode Statistics for admitted patient care and critical care to develop and maintain CRAB, a tool that compares hospital quality and outcomes while accounting for patients' clinical risk. The agreement allows its reports to support Care Quality Commission inspections and help NHS Trusts benchmark their performance, with the aim of identifying avoidable harm early. Reported benefits include use in CQC inspection work, Trust improvements and inclusion in GIRFT guidance.

DARS-NIC-351761-F8Z6V.summary: NEC Software Solutions UK Limited, a commercial company, is permitted under the agreement to use patient reported outcome measures (questionnaire responses from hip and knee replacement patients) that can be linked to Hospital Episode Statistics (HES). The data is for its Beyond Compliance service, which monitors new or modified implants and produces monthly summary reports for surgeons, manufacturers and independent assessors. The aim is to spot implant problems early and make patients safer. The service has led to changes in product design, instructions for use and indications for use.

DARS-NIC-351810-N3G6N.summary: The University of Warwick's agreement covers civil registration death records, NHS demographic data and a mortality list-cleaning report. It allows linking them to its Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest Outcomes (OHCAO) registry to track long-term survival of people who survived cardiac arrest outside hospital. The aim is to fill a knowledge gap and support improvements to patient care and outcomes. Reported benefits include survival data informing NHS England policy and annual reports that ambulance services used for planning.

DARS-NIC-35216-D6G6M.summary: Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care data, which records hospital admissions. The data is for filling gaps in follow-up information for patients who had heart valve surgery for infective endocarditis, a serious heart infection, over ten years. The agreement allows checking whether the Trust's shorter antibiotic courses keep the one-year relapse rate low. If they do, the Trust expects shorter treatment to reduce costs, antibiotic side effects and antimicrobial resistance.

DARS-NIC-352291-Y7B1S.summary: The University of Leeds's agreement covers the use of pseudonymised hospital inpatient data (Hospital Episode Statistics), linked to cancer registration and mortality records. The data is for a research study into whether bariatric (obesity) surgery changes the risk of colorectal and other cancers. The study compares people who had the surgery with people admitted to hospital because of obesity. It aims to clarify the long-term cancer risk for a growing number of patients.

DARS-NIC-352298-S8K3P.summary: NHS Lincolnshire ICB's agreement, through its Lincolnshire West sub-ICB location, allows commissioners to use Secondary User Services (SUS+) data, which can be identified by NHS number. Its contractor, Liaison Financial Services, may use it to validate invoices, including Continuing Healthcare invoices, and to review past payments back to 1 April 2013 for possible overpayments. The main intended benefit is finding and recovering money that would otherwise be lost, while keeping patient confidentiality.

DARS-NIC-352300-D9R2G.summary: The University of Birmingham's agreement covers Hospital Episode Statistics (HES) data on accident and emergency, critical care and inpatient care. The data is for two purposes. The first is evidence work commissioned by the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence, assessing how new treatments and devices are adopted in the NHS. The second is applied health services research under the CLAHRC programme, which is funded by the NIHR.

DARS-NIC-352310-L8R7H.summary: King's College London's agreement covers the use of Hospital Episode Statistics (HES) data on inpatient, outpatient, critical care and A&E care, linked to its King's Centre for Military Health Research cohort study of serving and ex-serving UK military personnel. The data is for examining how alcohol misuse and mental health relate to physical health conditions, accidents and injuries. It is also for identifying predictors of hospital service use and costs. No specific benefit is stated.

DARS-NIC-352381-P0L2S.summary: Royal Brompton and Harefield NHS Trust's agreement allows it to analyse national hospital records from Hospital Episode Statistics (HES), covering A&E, critical care, inpatient and outpatient care, linked to mortality data. The analysis is to examine the causes of illness and death in patients with congenital heart disease and pulmonary hypertension. It covers hospital stays, procedures and trends after clinical guidelines were published. The aim is a fuller picture of outcomes for these patients, so that guideline recommendations can rest on better evidence.

DARS-NIC-35239-W2W9R.summary: Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers Office for National Statistics mortality data for patients who took part in a trial of home mechanical ventilation (HMV) for hypercapnic chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). The data is for confirming whether participants are alive and providing dates and causes of death, so the trial can examine long-term survival. The intended benefit is better information to help clinicians and commissioners decide when to offer HMV and to reduce hospital readmissions.

DARS-NIC-352414-W9M3F.summary: CHKS Limited's agreement covers Hospital Episode Statistics (HES) data for A&E, critical care, inpatient and outpatient care, held only in pseudonymised form. The data is for providing NHS trusts, commissioners and commissioning support units with benchmarking, market share analysis, mortality profiling, consultant appraisal and awards services. The stated aim is to support and indirectly improve patient care by healthcare organisations.

DARS-NIC-352725-V1X2R.summary: The University of Oxford's agreement covers the use of hospital admission, accident and emergency, and death registration records, linked to detailed intensive care data. The data is for finding which patients are at risk of heart attacks, strokes and related events after leaving intensive care, and whether treatments and events in intensive care add to that risk. The intended benefit is to identify risk factors that could be changed to prevent these events. So far, it reports building a research resource from two sites, supporting two PhD projects, and creating and testing two predictive models.

DARS-NIC-353126-Y1S5F.summary: The University of Oxford's agreement covers linking hospital records (accident and emergency, admitted patient, critical care and outpatient) and death registrations to GP records for people aged 50 and over. The data is for studying how frailty develops and how it affects the use of health services, to help plan and commission services for older people. Two published papers have reported that service use and costs rise with frailty severity, and have described how frailty progresses with age.

DARS-NIC-35323-Y2N7J.summary: Thurrock Council's agreement covers civil registration data on births and deaths, plus primary care mortality data, which includes identifiable details. The agreement allows the data to be used to assess local health needs, plan services, support suicide audits and protect public health, with the aim of tailoring services to local needs and reducing health inequalities. Reported results include births data helping redesign the Brighter Futures children's services, and deaths data feeding into suicide audits.

DARS-NIC-353691-D9Z9G.summary: NHS Lincolnshire ICB, through its South Lincolnshire sub-ICB location, is permitted to use Secondary User Services (SUS+) hospital activity data, identifiable by NHS number, for invoice validation. The agreement allows Liaison Financial Services to check Continuing Healthcare invoices and past payments back to April 2013 to find possible overpayments and recover the money from providers. The main intended benefit is recovering money that would otherwise be lost, while keeping budget control and protecting patient confidentiality.

DARS-NIC-353882-J5X9Q.summary: The University of Warwick's agreement covers the use of pseudonymised hospital admission data (Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care) and Emergency Care Data Set records for a PhD study. It examines how patients use out-of-hours and urgent care services that use the Odyssey digital triage tool over the phone, and what happens to their health and later service use afterwards, before and after COVID-19. The main intended benefit is evidence on the safety of digital triage, to help improve the tool and services.

DARS-NIC-35389-P6P2F.summary: Buckinghamshire Council, a local authority, is covered by an agreement allowing it to use identifiable births and deaths registration data, including primary care mortality data. The data is for measuring local health needs, planning services and supporting public health work such as suicide audits and prevention. The aim is to tailor local services and reduce premature deaths and health inequalities. The agreement allows the data to be reported in its Annual Public Health Report, Joint Strategic Needs Assessments, community board profiles and suicide and drug-related deaths audits.

DARS-NIC-354267-B4V2G.summary: The Children's Commissioner's Office's agreement covers the 2017 Mental Health of Children and Young People survey, which holds anonymous information on the mental health and wellbeing of children aged 2 to 19 in England. The agreement allows analysis of how mental health relates to social and economic factors, internet use and risky behaviour. The results are for its Vulnerability Framework and reports on children's needs. The aim is to give government and local authorities evidence on where children need more support.

DARS-NIC-354497-V2J9P.summary: The London School of Economics and Political Science (LSE)'s agreement covers the use of pseudonymised hospital, A&E, outpatient, patient-reported outcome and death registration records to study how NHS reforms since 2000 affected patient outcomes, waiting times and provider behaviour. The agreement is for giving policymakers stronger evidence for health and social care decisions, including by using deaths in any location as a measure of care quality. Its work has been cited by a Prime Minister, used by NHS Monitor, and its Hospital Frailty Risk Score has been added to an NHS England data portal.

DARS-NIC-35519-S2R9Y.summary: Stockport Metropolitan Borough Council's agreement covers civil registration data on births and deaths, plus primary care mortality data, which includes identifiable details. The data is for measuring local health needs, planning services and supporting public health work such as suicide prevention. The aim is to tailor local services to areas of greatest need and reduce health inequalities. In 2023 the council produced outputs including small-area life expectancy estimates, monthly mortality tracking and excess winter mortality analysis.

DARS-NIC-35531-X3Y7Q.summary: The London Borough of Enfield's agreement covers the use of hospital and emergency care data (Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set) for its public health work. The agreement allows the data to be used to plan and assess local services, produce needs assessments and advise NHS commissioners. The data is for understanding local health and inequalities. The borough reported using the data to monitor COVID-19 hospital activity, and to commission falls prevention and frailty programmes.

DARS-NIC-35562-V6G5W.summary: Bristol NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers hospital records (admitted patient care, A&E, outpatient and critical care) and death registration data for patients who had an out-of-hospital cardiac arrest. The data is for the AIRWAYS-2 trial, which compares tracheal intubation with the i-gel supraglottic airway device to find which is more clinically and cost effective. The aim is better evidence on how ambulance staff should treat cardiac arrest. Results have been published, and some UK ambulance trusts, including SWAST, have changed their resuscitation practices in line with guidelines influenced by the trial.

DARS-NIC-355818-H7T3C.summary: Cegedim Rx Ltd's agreement allows it to use hospital episode statistics, emergency care data and civil registration death records. It is to maintain a large research data resource for commercial research on behalf of clients such as academia, pharmaceutical companies and public health bodies. Studies cover disease epidemiology, medication safety and healthcare use. The intended benefit is evidence to improve patient outcomes, care pathways and NHS service planning.

DARS-NIC-355855-R4G6G.summary: The Royal College of Anaesthetists's agreement covers linked hospital admission, critical care, demographic and death records for adults who have had emergency abdominal surgery (laparotomy) in England. The data is for the National Emergency Laparotomy Audit, which produces annual reports comparing hospitals' care and outcomes, such as 30-day mortality, to drive quality improvement. Reported benefits include seven peer-reviewed publications and improvements in key care standards, such as shorter hospital stays.

DARS-NIC-355868-H2R2D.summary: Ramsay Health Care UK, which runs 31 acute hospitals and treatment centres in England, may use Hospital Episode Statistics (HES) inpatient and outpatient extracts. The agreement allows it to compare its own hospital data with national NHS and independent sector data. This would cover coding practice, length of stay, re-admissions and the mix of procedures. The aim is to improve efficiency, quality and patient experience, and to show it does not "cherry-pick" patients.

DARS-NIC-356125-G9Z7Y.summary: Stoke-on-Trent City Council uses identifiable births and deaths records, including primary care mortality data, to understand the health needs of people in its area. It uses them for public health planning, immunisation programmes, health protection work and suicide audits. Outputs are aggregated statistics that help tailor local services and reduce health inequalities.
DARS-NIC-356125-G9Z7Y.retense_draft: Stoke-on-Trent City Council's agreement covers identifiable births and deaths records, including primary care mortality data, to understand the health needs of people in its area. The agreement allows the data to be used for public health planning, immunisation programmes, health protection work and suicide audits. Outputs are aggregated statistics that help tailor local services and reduce health inequalities.

DARS-NIC-356234-W2K8R.summary: The University of Cambridge, working with Cambridgeshire and Peterborough NHS Foundation Trust (CPFT), is using hospital, emergency care and death records linked to CPFT mental health records. It is using them to study physical health problems and deaths in people with mental disorders compared with a control population. The aim is to help narrow the health gap these people experience. Work so far has identified the immediate causes of death in subtypes of dementia (2023) and found that cholinesterase inhibitor use in Lewy body dementia was linked to lower mortality (2022).
DARS-NIC-356234-W2K8R.retense_draft: The University of Cambridge, working with Cambridgeshire and Peterborough NHS Foundation Trust (CPFT), is permitted to use hospital, emergency care and death records linked to CPFT mental health records. The agreement allows these data to be used to study physical health problems and deaths in people with mental disorders compared with a control population. The aim is to help narrow the health gap these people experience. Work so far has identified the immediate causes of death in subtypes of dementia (2023) and found that cholinesterase inhibitor use in Lewy body dementia was linked to lower mortality (2022).

DARS-NIC-35642-F6J4F.summary: Newcastle City Council's agreement covers civil registration data on births and deaths, plus primary care mortality data, which includes identifiable information. The data is for assessing local health needs, planning services, protecting public health and carrying out suicide audits, with only aggregated statistics published. The stated aim is to adjust local services to reduce deaths and health inequalities. Reported results include a Drug Market Profile, a Drug Related Death Audit, Covid-19 death analysis and a 0-19 Service Needs Assessment.

DARS-NIC-356980-Z5B9G.summary: MAC Clinical Research Finance Ltd's agreement covers hospital records for admitted patient care, outpatients and accident and emergency (Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set) for volunteers who have consented. The agreement allows the records to be used to check whether volunteers are eligible for clinical trials, as part of recruiting people onto trials for its clients. The main intended benefit is faster, safer matching of volunteers to trials, and less record-request work for GPs.

DARS-NIC-35699-L3K3Q.summary: Hertfordshire County Council's agreement covers identifiable birth and death registration data, including primary care mortality data, for studying the health needs of its local population. The agreement allows the data to be used for public health planning, suicide audits and hotspot mapping, and for reports such as Joint Strategic Needs Assessments. The aim is to tailor local services and reduce health inequalities and premature deaths. The council has supplied aggregated births data for school forecasting and children's centres, and has analysed avoidable deaths and suicides.

DARS-NIC-357479-S6C7T.summary: The Royal College of Physicians of London's agreement, working for the Healthcare Quality Improvement Partnership and NHS England, allows use of pseudonymised hospital admission and death registration data for adults admitted to hospital with asthma attacks. The agreement allows linking this to audit records to measure readmissions and deaths within 30 and 90 days, to show whether hospital care led to good outcomes. The aim is to improve asthma care and outcomes. A 2023 outcomes report has been used to inform recommendations on service resourcing after the COVID-19 pandemic.

DARS-NIC-358185-N3R6Q.summary: The Royal College of Surgeons of England's agreement covers bespoke tabulations of Hospital Episode Statistics (HES), which count vascular surgery procedures at each NHS trust and nationally. The agreement allows the National Vascular Registry to use them to calculate how many cases each trust should be submitting, and to check that trusts' submissions are complete. The expected figures will appear in the registry's public annual report and be sent to trusts so they can improve their data submissions.

DARS-NIC-358191-T5P4G.summary: The University of Oxford's agreement covers use of hospital admissions data (Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care) and Patient Reported Outcome Measures (PROMs) data for a DPhil research project on missing data in PROMs. The agreement allows work on factors behind missing questionnaire responses and aims to produce guidelines on handling and reporting missing data. The main intended benefit is more reliable evidence to help the NHS choose effective, cost-effective treatments.

DARS-NIC-35820-Y3H1M.summary: The Health Foundation, an independent UK health charity, has an agreement covering Hospital Episode Statistics data on hospital admitted patient care and accident and emergency. The agreement allows it to study the "weekend effect" on death rates after emergency admission, and how this varies between hospitals and over time. The aim is to inform policy makers and the NHS about variation in quality of care, helping to identify priority areas for improvement.

DARS-NIC-359603-D2Q6M.summary: The Care Quality Commission (CQC)'s agreement covers identifiable hospital, mental health, community, maternity, emergency care and death registration data. The agreement allows the data to be used to monitor health and care providers, plan inspections, flag concerns such as high mortality, and support reviews and national reports. The aim is to protect people from harm and improve care quality. CQC reports that the data have informed inspection planning and published reports, including the 2025/26 State of Care report.

DARS-NIC-359651-H3R1P.summary: The University of Oxford, working with the University of Leicester, is covered by an agreement that allows birth notification data from NHS England to be used for the MBRRACE-UK programme, which monitors maternal, perinatal and infant deaths in England and Wales. The data is for calculating perinatal mortality rates adjusted for factors such as gestational age and ethnicity, so that trusts and health boards can be compared fairly. The aim is to improve care for women and babies and reduce deaths. Reported benefits include changes to national policy, clinical guidelines and maternity services.

DARS-NIC-359670-Y7L3F.summary: The University of York's Centre for Health Economics agreement covers individual-level hospital records (including A&E, critical care, inpatient, outpatient and mortality data) and patient-reported outcome measures. The data is for economic analyses of health and social care, covering efficiency, productivity, differences between providers and the impact of health policy. The aim is to give the Department of Health and other policy-makers evidence to inform decisions. Only aggregated results will be published.

DARS-NIC-359692-Q4X1C.summary: Lightfoot Solutions UK Ltd, a small company, may use Hospital Episode Statistics and Emergency Care Data Set records in its Signals From Noise analytics platform. The agreement allows NHS clients to view aggregated charts of waiting times, length of stay and demand, to help them plan services and winter pressures and improve patient outcomes. Reported results include a Wakefield pilot where a targeted approach cut hospital bed days, equivalent to 35 beds a year.

DARS-NIC-359940-W1R7B.summary: The National Institute for Cardiovascular Outcomes Research, an academic body, is permitted to use linked hospital admission, death registration and demographic data on patients in six national cardiac audits. The data is for measuring survival and comparing hospital and clinician care against national standards, aiming to improve care quality. Audit data has already been used by the NHS to support Best Practice Tariff, which rewards hospitals providing a high standard of care.

DARS-NIC-360208-K1T4F.summary: Cambridge University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust, with the University of Cambridge, is allowed to use hospital, emergency care, imaging, death registration and primary care dispensing records to check clinical data collected for the UK-PBC Genetics Study of primary biliary cholangitis, a rare chronic liver disease. The aim is to improve risk prediction and treatment choice for patients. Checking the data has already found discrepancies in the study database, and a preliminary study was published in the journal Gastroenterology in September 2022.

DARS-NIC-360432-Z1Q8K.summary: NHS Birmingham and Solihull ICB, with Birmingham City Council and Solihull Metropolitan Borough Council, is covered by an agreement allowing use of pseudonymised health and social care data covering hospital, community, mental health, primary care prescribing and population records. The data is for commissioning and planning health and care services and for public health duties, such as needs assessments and reports. The main intended benefit is better-planned services, improved quality and access, and reduced inequalities. The CCG's annual report describes developments supported by this data.

DARS-NIC-361343-G9Z4S.summary: Genomics England's agreement covers Hospital Episode Statistics (HES) data, including accident and emergency, critical care, inpatient and outpatient records, linked to participants' genome sequence data. The data is for building a genomic medicine service for the NHS and supporting approved researchers studying how genomics can be used in healthcare and the causes, diagnosis and treatment of disease. The stated aim is that patients may receive diagnoses and, in time, more effective treatments.

DARS-NIC-36151-L1R4H.summary: Wiltshire Council's agreement covers identifiable civil registration data on births and deaths, together with primary care mortality data. The data is for measuring local health needs, planning services, and running suicide audits and hotspot mapping, with only aggregated statistics published. The intended benefit is local services targeted to areas of greatest need, with fewer premature deaths. The data supported Joint Strategic Needs Assessments (JSNAs) in 2022 and 2023, health needs assessments and local suicide monitoring.

DARS-NIC-361864-N8P1S.summary: The University of Newcastle upon Tyne's agreement covers the use of hospital, emergency care and death registration records for patients in England in a trial comparing two heart operations to repair the mitral valve: a small cut on the side of the chest and a full breastbone cut. The data is for showing which gives patients a better recovery, to inform NHS guidance. Initial trial results were cited in the 2025 European guidelines for valvular heart disease.

DARS-NIC-362204-F4B2C.summary: NHS Cheshire and Merseyside ICB, with Arden and GEM Commissioning Support Unit, is permitted to use hospital activity data (SUS for Commissioners) linked with GP data, identifiable by NHS number, for risk stratification. This applies an algorithm to score which patients are at high risk of health deterioration, so GPs and commissioners can target care and plan services. The main intended benefit is better case management and fewer avoidable emergency admissions.

DARS-NIC-362208-G8K6D.summary: NHS Norfolk and Waveney ICB's agreement covers hospital, community, mental health, maternity, GP and other health and social care data, some of it identifiable by NHS number. The data is for checking provider invoices, identifying patients at high risk of health deterioration, and planning and monitoring local health services. The aim is to ensure providers are paid correctly and services match the needs of the local population. The data has helped it monitor projects and deliver integrated care.

DARS-NIC-362209-B8N9J.summary: NHS North East and North Cumbria ICB's agreement allows it to use health, social care and registration data, including hospital, mental health, community and GP-related records, some identifiable by NHS number and some pseudonymised. The data is for checking provider invoices, identifying patients at high risk of poor health, and planning and commissioning health services for the local population. The main intended benefit is that providers are paid accurately and care is better targeted and planned. The CCG has also published an annual report on achievements the data has supported.

DARS-NIC-362234-W6M0T.summary: NHS Herefordshire and Worcestershire ICB, a sub-ICB location, is covered by an agreement that allows it to use hospital, mental health, community, maternity and other health service data, some identifiable by NHS number and some pseudonymised. The data is for checking provider invoices, identifying patients at high risk of poor health so GPs can target their care, and planning and commissioning local health services. The main intended benefit is that providers are paid accurately and care is planned more effectively, improving patient experience and outcomes.

DARS-NIC-362236-D7W4M.summary: NHS Surrey Heartlands ICB's agreement covers hospital, community, mental health, social care and other health data, some identifiable by NHS number and some pseudonymised. The agreement allows the data to be used to check provider invoices, identify patients at high risk so their care can be prioritised, and plan and commission health services. The main intended benefit is accurate payment and better-targeted care. The CCG has published an annual report describing achievements supported by this data.

DARS-NIC-362236-V8R5S.summary: The University of York's agreement supports the National Audit of Cardiac Rehabilitation (NACR) and allows the use of pseudonymised hospital inpatient data from Hospital Episode Statistics (HES). The data is for reporting on cardiac rehabilitation services at clinical commissioning group (CCG) and local programme level, including performance against national clinical standards and patient outcomes. The aim is to help commissioners make informed decisions and to raise the quality of care and outcomes for patients.

DARS-NIC-362237-Y5K7L.summary: NHS Bath and North East Somerset, Swindon and Wiltshire Integrated Care Board (ICB)'s agreement allows it to use hospital, community, mental health, primary care and other health and social care data, including identifiable data for some tasks. The agreement allows the data to check provider invoices, to identify patients at high risk of poor health so GPs can target care, and to plan and commission services. The aim is accurate payments and better-targeted care. Reported results include a model of hospital patient flow and GP-led support for specific at-risk patient groups.

DARS-NIC-362239-F6V0N.summary: NHS South West London ICB's agreement covers health and care data from hospitals, GPs, community, mental health, ambulance and social care services, plus births and deaths records. The data is for identifying patients at high risk of poor health, planning and commissioning services, and understanding local health needs. The aim is to target care better and reduce avoidable hospital admissions. An annual report describes how the data helped the ICB monitor services during its COVID-19 response.

DARS-NIC-362240-M2L1B.summary: NHS Sussex ICB, acting for the former East Sussex Clinical Commissioning Group (CCG), may use identifiable hospital activity data (SUS+) and patient demographic data. The data is for checking provider invoices and confirming the CCG is the responsible commissioner, and for identifying patients at high risk so care can be planned. The main intended benefits are accurate payment for care and better-targeted care. The CCG reports that the data has helped match services to the population's needs and supported delivery of integrated care.

DARS-NIC-362252-M1X0V.summary: NHS Northamptonshire ICB's agreement covers hospital, mental health, community, maternity and other NHS patient data, some identifiable by NHS number and some pseudonymised. The data is for checking provider invoices, identifying patients at high risk of health deterioration, and planning and commissioning local health services. The stated aim is more effective commissioning, leading to better patient experience and health outcomes. The CCG published an annual report summarising benefits realised.

DARS-NIC-362253-J5V8L.summary: NHS North Central London ICB's agreement covers patient-level health and social care data, including hospital, mental health, community, maternity and GP-linked records, some identifiable and some pseudonymised. The agreement allows the data to be used to validate provider invoices, identify patients at high risk of ill health, and plan and monitor health services. The aim is accurate payment, better targeted care and more effective commissioning. Reported results include funding secured for health inequalities projects, such as a bid expected to bring in £670k over two years.

DARS-NIC-362254-Q6S4W.summary: NHS South East London ICB (formerly the Clinical Commissioning Group, CCG)'s agreement covers patient-level hospital, mental health, community, GP-linked and other NHS data. The agreement allows the data to be used to validate provider invoices, identify patients at high risk of health deterioration, and plan health services for the local population. The aim is accurate payment and better targeted care. The CCG reports that the data helped it introduce services such as a hospital at home service for children and young people.

DARS-NIC-362255-K5D1H.summary: NHS Kent and Medway ICB's agreement covers the use of patient-level hospital, community, mental health, primary care and other health and social care data, which is for checking provider invoices, identifying patients at high risk of poor health, and planning and monitoring health services for the local population. The aim is to ensure providers are paid accurately and to improve care through better targeted, more effective commissioning. The group's 2020/21 annual report highlights achievements that relied on this data.

DARS-NIC-362259-K6L0L.summary: NHS Sussex ICB, acting for the former West Sussex CCG, is permitted to use identifiable and pseudonymised hospital, mental health, community and other provider data to check invoices, identify patients at high risk of health decline, and plan health services. The aim is to make sure providers are paid correctly and that care is better targeted to local needs. The data has helped match services to the population's needs and monitor in-year projects.

DARS-NIC-362263-B4Y6N.summary: NHS North East and North Cumbria ICB (County Durham)'s agreement covers hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other health and care data, some identifiable by NHS number and some pseudonymised. The data is for checking provider invoices, identifying patients at high risk of poor health so their care can be planned, and supporting the commissioning of health services. The main intended benefit is that providers are paid accurately and care is better targeted and planned.

DARS-NIC-362265-C4M6N.summary: NHS Nottingham and Nottinghamshire ICB (formerly the CCG)'s agreement covers Secondary User Services (SUS+) data, identifiable by NHS number, for invoice validation and risk stratification. The data is for checking that provider invoices are correct and the CCG's responsibility, and for identifying patients at high risk of health deterioration by linking it with GP data. The main intended benefits are accurate payments and budget control, and earlier, better-targeted care for vulnerable patients.

DARS-NIC-362267-P1W2X.summary: NHS West Yorkshire ICB, acting for the former Bradford District and Craven clinical commissioning group, uses hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other health and care data. It uses it to check invoices from care providers, to identify patients at high risk of poor health using risk stratification, and to plan health services. The stated aim is to make sure providers are paid accurately and that services and care for vulnerable patients are better planned. The group's 2020/21 annual report describes achievements during the year, some of which relied on this data.
DARS-NIC-362267-P1W2X.retense_draft: NHS West Yorkshire ICB's agreement, acting for the former Bradford District and Craven clinical commissioning group, covers hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other health and care data. The agreement allows the data to be used to check invoices from care providers, to identify patients at high risk of poor health using risk stratification, and to plan health services. The stated aim is to make sure providers are paid accurately and that services and care for vulnerable patients are better planned. The group's 2020/21 annual report describes achievements during the year, some of which relied on this data.

DARS-NIC-362273-D4H7T.summary: NHS Humber and North Yorkshire ICB (formerly North Yorkshire CCG)'s agreement covers hospital activity data (SUS for Commissioners), identifiable by NHS number, for two purposes. The first is checking provider invoices so that only activity it is responsible for is paid. The second is risk stratification, which links the data with GP records to identify patients at high risk. The main intended benefit is accurate payment and better targeted care.

DARS-NIC-362275-P4S4T.summary: NHS Lincolnshire ICB's agreement covers hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other health datasets, including NHS-number-level Secondary Uses Service data for some tasks. The agreement allows the data to be used to check invoices from care providers, to identify patients at high risk of poor health so GPs and commissioners can plan their care, and to plan and commission local health services. The main stated benefit is that providers are paid accurately while services are planned around the population's needs.

DARS-NIC-36248-X5J1Y.summary: NHS Bassetlaw CCG's agreement covers hospital activity data from the Secondary Uses Service (SUS), covering accident and emergency, inpatient and outpatient care, including data identifiable by NHS number. The data is for producing risk stratification scores for the CCG and GP practices, with practices able to see their own registered patients' scores. The main intended benefit is better case management in primary care, leading to fewer avoidable emergency admissions and more suitable services for patients.

DARS-NIC-36253-D9W8D.summary: NHS Scarborough and Ryedale CCG (Clinical Commissioning Group) has an agreement covering hospital activity data (SUS accident and emergency, inpatient and outpatient records) that can be identified by NHS number. The data is for producing risk stratification scores, which show GP practices which of their registered patients are at higher risk. The main intended benefit is better case management in primary care, with fewer avoidable emergency admissions.

DARS-NIC-36260-X3J7Q.summary: NHS Hull CCG's agreement covers pseudonymised hospital activity data from the Secondary Uses Service (SUS), covering accident and emergency, inpatient and outpatient care. The data is for risk profiling to support the commissioning of health services. GP practices can see risk scores for their own registered patients. The main intended benefit is better case management in primary care, including fewer avoidable emergency admissions.

DARS-NIC-362650-W7M3Y.summary: Derby Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers bespoke extracts of hospital inpatient records (HES) and linked Office for National Statistics mortality data. The data is for studying acute kidney injury (AKI) across England, including how often it occurs, how many patients die, and what happens to them over the long term. The agreement allows the Trust to give a more accurate picture of the burden of AKI to help develop ways to reduce it and improve survival.

DARS-NIC-363140-V3X2W.summary: The University of Bristol's agreement covers hospital records (Hospital Episode Statistics admitted patient care and outpatients data) together with demographic data about women who had a mastectomy or delayed breast reconstruction in NHS England in 2008 to 2009. The agreement allows the data to be used to identify the study group and compare the long-term clinical and cost effectiveness of implant-based and autologous breast reconstruction. The main intended benefit is better evidence to help women, clinicians and commissioners choose between reconstruction options.

DARS-NIC-363259-M1X8F.summary: Methods Analytics Ltd's agreement allows it to use Hospital Episode Statistics (HES) data linked to Office for National Statistics (ONS) mortality data in a standard monthly extract. The data is for building tools and dashboards, including Stethoscope, that benchmark quality and safety indicators nationally and show variation between NHS organisations. The tools also support surgical commissioning work and reproduce the Summary Hospital Mortality Indicator. The stated aim is to help NHS organisations spot issues and improve care quality.

DARS-NIC-363464-J4F8N.summary: The King's Fund, a health charity, holds Hospital Episode Statistics data on hospital admissions, outpatient appointments and accident and emergency attendances. The agreement allows the data to be used to give the Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC) analysis and advice on national health policy, aiming to improve the evidence behind policy decisions. It has delivered a report to DHSC comparing England's emergency admission rates with those of other countries.

DARS-NIC-363469-Y5Z3J.summary: NHS England's agreement covers a bespoke extract of the Improving Access to Psychological Therapies (IAPT) dataset. The data is for developing and testing a payment currency model for IAPT services, based on treatment outcomes recorded in the data. The model is meant to reward good performance and improve quality, and to help money follow the patient.

DARS-NIC-363607-Y4N8Q.summary: NHS Central Midlands Commissioning Support Unit's agreement covers hospital activity, mortality and mental health and learning disability data from NHS Digital's register. The data is for benchmarking and analysing health services for clinical commissioning groups (CCGs) and trusts across the Midlands, Lancashire and beyond. Permitted uses include opportunity packs comparing performance, cost and activity, and decision support tools for hip and knee replacement. The release register states the aim as helping commissioners, clinicians and patients make better-informed decisions.

DARS-NIC-364403-N2R6Y.summary: Public Health England's agreement covers pseudonymised, bespoke Learning Disability Census data covering 2013 to 2015. The agreement allows analysis of what predicts patients moving between hospitals, why people are in hospital (particularly their legal status), and whether particular hospital providers are linked to more or fewer adverse experiences such as seclusion, restraint or self-harm. It also allows tracking of changes in the in-patient population over time.

DARS-NIC-36455-Y6H8W.summary: Kent County Council's agreement covers civil registration births and deaths data and Primary Care Mortality Data. The data is for measuring local health needs, planning services and protecting public health, including suicide audits and prevention work. The aim is to tailor services to local needs and reduce health inequalities. Reported results include analysis of excess winter deaths, suicide patterns, and deaths during heat waves.

DARS-NIC-364597-G1G7Q.summary: NHiS, an information intermediary, is permitted to use record-level pseudonymised, non-identifiable hospital data (Hospital Episode Statistics), plus diagnostic imaging and mental health datasets. The data is for producing public Disease Insight Reports on diagnosis, awareness and disease management, and for building Q-PASS tools that support the commissioning cycle. The release register says the aim is to improve patient outcomes through better service development.

DARS-NIC-365037-W6W2R.summary: The National Institute for Cardiovascular Outcomes Research's agreement covers tabulated Hospital Episode Statistics (HES) data on heart failure admissions, broken down by hospital provider. The data is for comparing these figures with the records each Trust and Health Board submitted to the National Heart Failure Audit, to measure how fully hospitals take part. The agreement allows results to appear as participation tables in the audit's annual report. The audit aims to improve the quality of heart failure diagnosis and treatment.

DARS-NIC-365132-V5S8H.summary: The Department of Health and Social Care's agreement covers pseudonymised hospital records (Hospital Episode Statistics for outpatients, admitted patient care, accident and emergency, and critical care, plus the Emergency Care Data Set) accessed through NHS Digital's Data Access Environment. The data is for analysis to support health and care policy decisions and ministerial requests, often at short notice. Reported results include analysis of 7-day hospital services that informed Ministerial decisions, and outpatient referral analysis that informed policy work.

DARS-NIC-365145-G2P9F.summary: The Department of Health and Social Care's agreement covers NHS England's Secondary Uses Service Payment By Results data on hospital episodes, outpatients and spells. The data is for analysing health and care activity, so that policy, briefings to ministers and responses to parliamentary questions are based on evidence. The expected benefit is better-informed decisions on planning services, allocating funding and understanding population needs. The reported benefits come from separate Hospital Episode Statistics data, which informed work on new models of care, outpatient referrals and 7-day services.

DARS-NIC-365354-R3M0Q.summary: The University of Oxford's agreement covers the use of NHS hospital, GP, death, testing, vaccination, cancer and prescribing data for the RECOVERY trial, which compares treatments for people in hospital with COVID-19. The data gives the trial reliable information on outcomes such as deaths, so it can show which treatments work and could change NHS standard care. Published results have shown that some treatments, such as dexamethasone and tocilizumab, improved survival, and the COVID-19 Public Inquiry cited the trial.

DARS-NIC-365492-H6D6V.summary: NHS Blood and Transplant's agreement covers use of civil registration of death data to follow up one-year mortality for patients recruited to the CRYOSTAT 2 trial, run with Queen Mary University of London. The trial tests whether giving high-dose cryoprecipitate, a fibrinogen-rich blood component, early to adults with major trauma bleeding reduces deaths. The main intended benefit is clear evidence on whether it improves survival, to inform treatment guidelines. Short-term results have been shared with the trial team, and a manuscript is in late preparation.

DARS-NIC-365602-V5H3Z.summary: King's College London's agreement covers linked hospital accident and emergency, admitted patient care and death registration records for people with dementia. The data is for a PhD study to examine how often people with dementia attend the Emergency Department in their last year of life, why they attend and which factors predict it. The intended benefit is evidence to help policy makers, commissioners and clinicians improve end of life care for people with dementia.

DARS-NIC-365623-T3W4S.summary: The University of Manchester's agreement covers Hospital Episode Statistics data on psychiatric in-patients who died, including identifiers, provider and consultant codes. The agreement allows the data to be used to count sudden unexplained deaths in England and Wales, and to ask responsible consultants about the circumstances leading up to each death, as part of the National Confidential Inquiry into Suicide and Homicide by People with Mental Illness. The main intended benefit is better knowledge of the causes of these deaths, to help prevent them.

DARS-NIC-365804-B3N1K.summary: Perspectum Ltd, a non-NHS provider, is permitted to use NHS England data on hospital care, emergency care, deaths, cancer registrations, dispensed medicines and the National Diabetes Audit. The agreement allows it to study how liver fibroinflammation, MRI measures and the severity and age of onset of eye disease and type 2 diabetes affect heart and other diabetes-related outcomes. The findings are expected to inform evidence-based decisions on care and treatment for people with diabetes.

DARS-NIC-366103-V5L5J.summary: IMS Health Ltd's agreement covers receipt of pseudonymised hospital data from NHS England's predecessor body: bespoke extracts of Hospital Episode Statistics (HES) for A&E, critical care, inpatients and outpatients, linked to hospital pharmacy dispensing records. The data is for maintaining Hospital Treatment Insights, a longitudinal database of hospital treatment in England, which may also be linked with primary care data. The stated aim is to give insight into how disease, treatment and prescribing interact.

DARS-NIC-366210-V2H5M.summary: Imperial College London, an academic institution, is authorised to use hospital records (admitted patient care, outpatient, accident and emergency and critical care), death registrations and patient-reported outcome data. The agreement covers research into how NHS staffing, local funding and cancer care pathways affect waiting lists, access to care and patient outcomes, to give policy makers evidence for workforce planning and funding decisions. Earlier work under the agreement produced a tool giving local authorities projections of NHS and social care costs from air pollution.

DARS-NIC-366216-Z9H9Q.summary: The University of Sheffield's agreement covers the use of Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care data, which records hospital admissions, to build models of alcohol and tobacco policy. These models estimate how policy changes could affect illness, hospital admissions and costs, to help policymakers reduce harm from smoking and drinking. Its modelling has already informed a Royal College of Physicians report on meeting England's 2030 smoke-free target, and evidence for a government consultation on alcohol duty reform.

DARS-NIC-36666-D1M2K.summary: Hampshire County Council's agreement covers the use of civil registration data on births and deaths, including identifiable details, along with primary care mortality data. The data is for understanding local health needs, planning services and supporting public health work such as suicide prevention and health protection monitoring. The main aim is to tailor local services to reduce deaths and health inequalities. So far, the data has enabled small area life expectancy calculations and has informed the council's Joint Strategic Needs Assessment.

DARS-NIC-366845-Q1F0Q.summary: The University of Oxford's Big Health Data Group's agreement covers the use of hospital admissions records and patient-reported outcome data, linked to National Joint Registry data, for two research studies on hip and knee replacement surgery. One study looks for factors after knee replacement that predict long-term pain. The other looks at how hospital organisation and surgical factors affect outcomes and NHS costs. The main intended benefit is better prevention and management of long-term pain after knee replacement.

DARS-NIC-366913-C2V5F.summary: The National Institute for Health Research's agreement with NHS England allows identifiable demographic data to be used to find out which people on the Join Dementia Research register have died. The data is for removing those records, keeping the register up to date and avoiding contact with bereaved families. Several hundred deceased volunteers have been removed from the register, as reported.

DARS-NIC-367152-K6Y1D.summary: The University of Leeds's agreement covers list-cleaning reports, Personal Demographics Service data (including fact of death) and NHS registration data for men with prostate cancer. The data is for confirming addresses and checking for deaths before Picker Institute Europe mails quality-of-life surveys for the Life After Prostate Cancer study. The study aims to show how prostate cancer affects men's lives, to help shape health services and policy that better meet their needs.

DARS-NIC-36716-S2S3Q.summary: Hampshire County Council's public health team agreement covers hospital and emergency care data from NHS England, covering admissions, outpatients, critical care and A&E. The data is for supporting its public health duties, including needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, commissioning and advice to NHS commissioners. The main intended benefit is locally focused analysis of health inequalities. The council reported using the data to inform health needs assessments and substance misuse commissioning, and to help define neighbourhoods with the Integrated Care Board (ICB).

DARS-NIC-36724-F3F7N.summary: North Northamptonshire Council's agreement covers the use of birth and death registration records, including identifiable details, and primary care mortality data. The data is for understanding local health needs, planning immunisation and public health work, and investigating local concerns such as suicide hotspots. The aim is to tailor health and care services to local needs and reduce health inequalities. Reported uses include the annual public health report, needs assessments and community-level health outcomes for Local Area Partnerships.

DARS-NIC-36767-G4H9Z.summary: NHS Cumbria CCG's agreement covers hospital, mental health, maternity, community and other local service data, some identifiable by NHS number and some pseudonymised. The data is for forecasting demand by identifying high-risk patients, and for supporting the commissioning of health services, including a joint review of services across the Morecambe Bay area. The main intended benefit is better-planned services and improved patient experience.

DARS-NIC-36794-M9N3S.summary: NHS North East and North Cumbria ICB's agreement, acting for the former NHS Darlington CCG area, covers hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other health service data, some identifiable by NHS number and some pseudonymised. The agreement allows the data to be used to check provider invoices, identify patients at high risk of poor health so their care can be prioritised, and plan and commission health services. The main intended benefit is that providers are paid accurately and services are better planned and targeted.

DARS-NIC-368020-R5L2K.summary: Dr Foster Limited, a supplier of healthcare analytics, is permitted to use pseudonymised Summary Hospital-level Mortality Indicator (SHMI) data, which measures deaths in and after hospital at non-specialist acute trusts. The agreement allows the data to be used in dashboards and bespoke reports for NHS clients, comparing SHMI with its own mortality measure, HSMR, to help trusts investigate mortality and improve patient care. Reported benefits include a May 2023 analysis that helped an NHS Foundation Trust understand a SHMI outlier.

DARS-NIC-36808-C2G1F.summary: NHS North East and North Cumbria ICB's agreement, through its sub-ICB location covering Durham Dales, Easington and Sedgefield, allows it to use hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other health activity data, some identifiable by NHS number and some pseudonymised. The data is for checking provider invoices, identifying patients at high risk of health deterioration, and planning and monitoring health services. The main intended benefit is more effective commissioning of services, improving patient experience.

DARS-NIC-368233-L2N0W.summary: McKinsey & Company, Inc. United Kingdom, a commercial consultancy, is permitted under its agreement to use hospital, emergency care, community services and diagnostic imaging data. The agreement allows the data to be used to help NHS clients benchmark performance, compare activity and spending, study trends and forecast future capacity. The aim is to improve the quality and efficiency of NHS services. Past work has included a business case for the National Hospital Programme that secured central government funding.

DARS-NIC-36826-Z4F4K.summary: NHS Hartlepool and Stockton-on-Tees CCG's agreement covers hospital, mental health, maternity, community and other local health service data, some identifiable by NHS number and some pseudonymised. The agreement allows the data to be used to validate invoices for non-contracted care, identify patients at high risk of needing services, and support commissioning decisions. The main intended benefit is better-planned, more effective commissioning of services, with public funds protected and patient care improved.

DARS-NIC-36827-N2X8Z.summary: NHS North Durham CCG's agreement covers hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other local provider data, some of it identifiable by NHS number and some pseudonymised. The data is for checking provider invoices, identifying patients at high risk so their care can be planned, and supporting the planning and commissioning of local health services. The main intended benefit is more effective commissioning and better patient experience.

DARS-NIC-36834-Q6R6F.summary: NHS Newcastle Gateshead CCG's agreement covers hospital, mental health, maternity, community and other local health service data, some identifiable by NHS number and some pseudonymised. The agreement allows the data to be used to validate invoices for non-contracted care, identify patients at high risk of future service use, and analyse local health services to support commissioning. The stated aim is more effective commissioning of services, with better planning, quality and patient experience.

DARS-NIC-368477-C9Q1X.summary: University College London (UCL)'s agreement covers the use of NHS England cancer registration, death registration and demographic data, linked to records of young people living with perinatal HIV (HIV acquired before or during birth). The data is for studying the risk of cancer and death as they move into adulthood. The expected benefit is evidence that could help tailor future HIV care and inform clinical guidelines.

DARS-NIC-36851-Y1C0W.summary: NHS North Tyneside CCG's agreement covers hospital activity data (Secondary Uses Service), local provider data and mental health, maternity, children's and other health datasets, some identifiable by NHS number and some pseudonymised. The agreement allows North of England CSU to handle the data for invoice validation, risk stratification to identify patients at high risk of future demand, and commissioning analysis. The main aim of the data is more effective commissioning of services, leading to a better patient experience.

DARS-NIC-368543-C3J4B.summary: CHKS Limited's agreement covers the use of pseudonymised Summary Hospital-level Mortality Indicator (SHMI) data on deaths in and within 30 days of leaving hospital. The data is for benchmarking and mortality profiling services that help NHS healthcare providers and commissioners analyse mortality, with the aim of improving patient care. Reported benefits include Shrewsbury and Telford and East Cheshire trusts using CHKS reports in mortality review groups, and one organisation planning services around local needs.

DARS-NIC-36866-Q9F5W.summary: Derbyshire County Council's agreement covers civil registration data on births and deaths, plus primary care mortality data, which includes identifiable details. The agreement allows the data to be used to measure local health needs, plan services and protect public health, including suicide prevention work, with only aggregated outputs published. The aim is to tailor local services and reduce health inequalities and premature deaths. Reported results include annual and quarterly suicide reports, a life expectancy report for the Director of Public Health and analysis of cancer mortality and birth rates.

DARS-NIC-368694-D8G4M.summary: The Medicines and Healthcare Products Regulatory Agency (MHRA), through its Clinical Practice Research Datalink (CPRD), is permitted to use hospital data from Hospital Episode Statistics covering A&E, critical care, inpatient and outpatient care. The data is linked to CPRD's primary care records and supplied in pseudonymised form. It is for research projects approved by an independent scientific committee, such as drug safety and disease studies. The stated aim is to improve public health and patient outcomes.

DARS-NIC-36874-J9G7D.summary: NHS Northumberland CCG's agreement covers hospital, ambulance, community, mental health, maternity and primary care data, including Secondary Uses Service (SUS) records and local provider data. Some of the data is identifiable by NHS number and some is pseudonymised. The agreement allows North of England Commissioning Support Unit to process it to validate invoices, identify patients at risk of high service use (risk stratification) and support the planning of health services. The main intended benefits are budget control, better targeted care in primary care and more effective commissioning.

DARS-NIC-36882-M3N5C.summary: NHS North East and North Cumbria ICB, acting for the former South Tees Clinical Commissioning Group (CCG) area, has an agreement covering hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other NHS activity data, some identifiable by NHS number and some pseudonymised. The agreement allows the data to be used to check provider invoices, to identify patients at high risk of poor health so GPs can target care, and to plan and monitor health services. The main intended benefit is that providers are paid accurately and care is better planned and targeted.

DARS-NIC-36889-T6P5F.summary: NHS South Tyneside CCG's agreement covers hospital, community, mental health, maternity, primary care and other local provider data, some identifiable by NHS number and some pseudonymised. The data is for validating invoices through North of England CSU, identifying patients at high risk of future service use, and supporting commissioning of health services. The main intended benefit is more effective commissioning of services, leading to better patient experience.

DARS-NIC-36890-W8W7D.summary: Southend-on-Sea Borough Council is using hospital and emergency care records (Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set) for its public health work. It will analyse them to inform needs assessments, health strategies, commissioning and advice to NHS commissioners, aiming to give locally focused insight into health inequalities. The council reports it has used the data to shape its Joint Strategic Needs Assessment and to support projects on falls prevention, children's injuries and harmful behaviours.
DARS-NIC-36890-W8W7D.retense_draft: Southend-on-Sea Borough Council's agreement covers the use of hospital and emergency care records (Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set) for its public health work.
