The data is for analysis to inform needs assessments, health strategies, commissioning and advice to NHS commissioners, aiming to give locally focused insight into health inequalities. The agreement allows the data to inform the council's Joint Strategic Needs Assessment and to support projects on falls prevention, children's injuries and harmful behaviours.

DARS-NIC-36892-P3B3F.summary: NHS North East and North Cumbria ICB (Sunderland area) uses hospital, community, mental health, primary care and other health and social care data, some identifiable by NHS number and some pseudonymised. It uses the data to validate provider invoices, identify patients at high risk of health deterioration, and support the planning and commissioning of health services. The main intended benefit is that providers are paid accurately and care is better targeted and planned. Reported so far, invoices were validated on time and reports fed into budget and contract management, and an annual report has been published.
DARS-NIC-36892-P3B3F.retense_draft: NHS North East and North Cumbria ICB's agreement (Sunderland area) allows it to use hospital, community, mental health, primary care and other health and social care data, some identifiable by NHS number and some pseudonymised. The data is for validating provider invoices, identifying patients at high risk of health deterioration, and supporting the planning and commissioning of health services. The main intended benefit is that providers are paid accurately and care is better targeted and planned. Invoices were validated on time and reports fed into budget and contract management, and an annual report has been published.

DARS-NIC-369348-H6H8B.summary: The University of Dundee's agreement covers NHS England data on hospital admissions, deaths, cancer registrations and demographics for the ALL-HEART trial. The trial tests whether adding allopurinol to usual treatment reduces strokes, heart attacks and cardiovascular deaths in people with ischaemic heart disease. The aim is to improve their treatment. The main results have been published in the Lancet and presented at international meetings.

DARS-NIC-369596-F6Q9V.summary: Ernst and Young LLP (EY) has an agreement covering hospital activity data from the Secondary Uses Service, including A&E, inpatient episodes and spells, and outpatients. The agreement allows the data to be used to produce aggregated benchmarks and performance indicators for NHS and international healthcare clients, supporting performance improvement, mergers, local health economy planning and pricing work. The aim is to help clients find efficiencies. Reported examples include a trust programme that identified £14.2 million of savings and a 23-bed opportunity.

DARS-NIC-37047-V8V0H.summary: Peterborough City Council's agreement covers civil registration data on births and deaths, plus primary care mortality data, which includes identifiable details. The agreement allows the data to be used to understand local health needs, plan services and support public health work such as suicide prevention, with the aim of tailoring services and reducing health inequalities. Death data has been used to monitor local death rates and inform prioritisation, and births data has fed into a children and young people needs assessment.

DARS-NIC-370530-K6B9K.summary: Isle of Wight Council's agreement covers civil registration data on births and deaths, plus primary care mortality data, which includes identifiable details. The data is for measuring local health needs, planning services and immunisation programmes, protecting public health, and supporting work such as suicide audits and hotspot mapping. The main aim is to tailor local services to reduce mortality and health inequalities. Reported uses include updating JSNA briefings, informing suicide audits, and monitoring excess deaths during and after COVID-19.

DARS-NIC-37060-F5M7B.summary: Cambridgeshire County Council's agreement covers civil registration data on births and deaths, plus primary care mortality data, which includes identifiable details. The agreement allows the data to be used to measure local health needs, plan immunisation programmes and protect public health, including suicide prevention audits. The main intended benefit is local services tailored to areas of greatest need, reducing health inequalities and premature deaths. The data has been used to monitor local death rates and causes and to inform a children and young people needs assessment.

DARS-NIC-370641-K0J0T.summary: The University of Leicester holds linked hospital records (Hospital Episode Statistics) and civil registration death data for men invited to the NHS Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Screening Programme. The agreement lets it keep the data only, so it can respond to journal requests to revise analyses. The research looked at cardiovascular risk and outcomes after screening to help improve the programme. So far, the work has produced three published conference abstracts and supported funded NIHR grant applications.

DARS-NIC-370701-M8F1H.summary: King's College London is using NHS registration data (names, dates of birth and current contact details) to trace people from a study of babies born very prematurely, who are now adults. The aim is to invite them to a 30-year follow-up assessing cognition, mental health and brain development. The study hopes to identify brain growth patterns linked to risk or resilience, to help develop future treatments.
DARS-NIC-370701-M8F1H.retense_draft: King's College London's agreement covers the use of NHS registration data (names, dates of birth and current contact details) to trace people from a study of babies born very prematurely, who are now adults. The agreement allows invitations to a 30-year follow-up assessing cognition, mental health and brain development. The study aims to identify brain growth patterns linked to risk or resilience, to help develop future treatments.

DARS-NIC-370749-W1R8Z.summary: NHS England's agreement covers hospital activity data from the Secondary Uses Service (SUS): accident and emergency, admitted patient care and outpatient records. The data is for modelling the relative need for healthcare in each Clinical Commissioning Group (CCG) area and for specialised services. The results set target funding allocations and help answer queries about them, including one from a CCG. The intended benefit is fairer funding, and so more equal access to NHS care for people with equal need.

DARS-NIC-370843-R6V8T.summary: Imperial College London, an academic organisation, is authorised to use linked hospital, cancer registration, death and demographic records for UK participants in the COSMOS mobile phone study. The agreement allows the data to be used to follow participants' long-term health and examine whether mobile phone use is linked to health problems. The main intended benefit is evidence to inform health policy and advice on mobile phones. A 2024 published paper on 264,574 participants found no association between cumulative phone use and brain tumours.

DARS-NIC-370861-N5H8G.summary: University College London's agreement covers the use of hospital inpatient records (Hospital Episode Statistics) and linked Office for National Statistics mortality data. The data is for evaluating London's hyperacute stroke system and 24/7 care, funded by NIHR. The analysis examines whether day of admission affects care and patient outcomes, including mortality and length of stay. The stated aim is to identify lessons that support high quality 24/7 stroke care.

DARS-NIC-371011-F4X5F.summary: NHS England's agreement covers linking hospital admissions data (Hospital Episode Statistics) with Assuring Transformation data, which counts inpatients with learning disabilities and/or autism. The agreement allows comparison of the two datasets to explain why they show very different numbers of admissions, and to identify any under-reporting. The intended benefit is greater confidence in the Assuring Transformation data and better reporting by commissioners, which should help improve quality of care.

DARS-NIC-371031-B8K6D.summary: The University of York's agreement covers the use of pseudonymised Hospital Episodes Statistics (HES) data on inpatient, outpatient and A&E care for children and young people aged 0-19 with neurological conditions. The agreement allows measurement of how many are seen in hospital and A&E, how admissions, length of stay and attendances change over time, and whether use differs by ethnic group or deprivation. The aim is to give accurate figures to help plan services and support equal access.

DARS-NIC-371228-Y7S6S.summary: UCL Institute of Education's agreement covers the use of NHS registration, mortality and Scottish events data to help trace members of the 1970 British Cohort Study, which follows people born in one week in 1970. The data would update their addresses so they can be invited to keep taking part in the study. The aim is to keep as many study members as possible in contact, supporting the study's continuing success.

DARS-NIC-37123-L4W1M.summary: West Sussex County Council's agreement covers civil registration data on births and deaths, plus primary care mortality data, which includes identifiable details. The data is for measuring local health needs, supporting immunisation programmes and protecting public health, including suicide audits and hotspot mapping. The main intended benefit is local services tailored to areas of greatest need, to reduce mortality and health inequalities. In 2023 the council reviewed mortality in COVID and non-COVID years and reported this to the Sussex ICB board.

DARS-NIC-371243-H1P5T.summary: NHS North and East London Commissioning Support Unit's agreement covers national Hospital Episode Statistics, emergency care and diagnostic imaging data for NHS England's commissioning support units. The data is for benchmarking hospital activity and outcomes, helping commissioners and local authorities compare areas and plan services. Reported benefits include analysis of GP referral rates across London CCGs, support for diabetes and respiratory improvements, and modelling of drivers of A&E attendance.

DARS-NIC-371828-D2W1R.summary: Norfolk County Council's agreement covers pseudonymised hospital data, including admissions, outpatient, A&E and critical care records, to support its public health duties. The agreement allows the data to be used to produce local health needs assessments, strategies and advice to NHS commissioners, with the aim of better targeting services and tackling health inequalities. Reported benefits include a falls dashboard, updated electoral division health profiles, and a tool to support alcohol licensing decisions.

DARS-NIC-371831-L7M1M.summary: Leeds City Council's public health team's agreement covers pseudonymised hospital data covering inpatient, outpatient, accident and emergency, and critical care records. The data is for its public health duties, including needs assessments, health strategies, the Director of Public Health's annual report and advice to NHS commissioners. The aim is to understand local health inequalities and the burden on Leeds hospitals. The data has already fed an area profile tool, an alcohol harm matrix used in licensing objections, and a performance report.

DARS-NIC-371832-J2L9K.summary: Lincolnshire County Council's agreement covers pseudonymised hospital records for admissions, outpatient visits, accident and emergency, critical care and emergency care. The data is for its public health duties, such as needs assessments, the Director of Public Health's annual report, commissioning and advice to NHS commissioners. The aim is locally focused analysis of health and health inequalities. Reported benefits include an updated Joint Strategic Needs Assessment, profiles for Primary Care Networks and analyses of self-harm, which informed local strategy and services.

DARS-NIC-37191-P5S9S.summary: University College London (UCL) is using death registration, cancer registration, demographic and mortality flagging data to follow up men in the RADICALS prostate cancer trial. It is used to capture deaths and cancer events that trial sites may miss and to check causes of death, giving more accurate survival estimates. Linking the data identified 33 deaths that sites had not reported, and trial results have already changed practice, sparing some men unnecessary radiotherapy.
DARS-NIC-37191-P5S9S.retense_draft: University College London's agreement covers the use of death registration, cancer registration, demographic and mortality flagging data to follow up men in the RADICALS prostate cancer trial. The data is for capturing deaths and cancer events that trial sites may miss and for checking causes of death, giving more accurate survival estimates. Linking the data identified 33 deaths that sites had not reported, and trial results have already changed practice, sparing some men unnecessary radiotherapy.

DARS-NIC-372269-N8D7Z.summary: University College London's agreement covers linking NHS England hospital, emergency care, death, COVID-19 test and vaccination records with its Virus Watch household study of 58,490 people. The data is for estimating community COVID-19 infections, hospital visits and deaths, and for seeing how social distancing affected routine health service use. It is intended to inform the NHS and public health response. Findings have been presented to national advisory groups and used in reports and briefings, including one referenced by Australia's Department of Health.

DARS-NIC-372677-H7S0S.summary: The University of Warwick holds Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) cause of death and flagging current status reports for a study of older people in residential and nursing homes. The study tested whether a programme to promote exercise and social interaction reduces depression among residents. Under this agreement the data may only be retained for an interim period, with no other use. The study has produced a final NIHR HTA report and a Lancet publication.

DARS-NIC-372684-X6Q3M.summary: The London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine's agreement covers NHS England's Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) data, including cause of death, cancer event notifications, current status and demographic details, for women in a cohort of about 25,000 breast cancer cases. The data is for a study of treatment effects and endocrine, genetic and cellular risk factors for a second breast cancer in the other breast. The agreement also allows the study to identify genes that affect breast cancer risk and assess their value in predicting it.

DARS-NIC-372791-X0H3Q.summary: NHS Blood and Transplant (NHSBT) uses NHS Digital data on people who have had COVID-19, linked to its blood donor database, to find and contact people who might donate convalescent plasma. The plasma contains antibodies and is being tested as a treatment for patients with COVID-19, including in the REMAP-CAP and RECOVERY trials. It aims to widen the pool of potential donors. By 15 November 2020, 33,994 donor attendances had led to 24,530 plasma donations collected.
DARS-NIC-372791-X0H3Q.retense_draft: NHS Blood and Transplant's agreement covers the use of NHS Digital data on people who have had COVID-19, linked to its blood donor database, to find and contact people who might donate convalescent plasma. The plasma contains antibodies and is for testing as a treatment for patients with COVID-19, including in the REMAP-CAP and RECOVERY trials. The data is for widening the pool of potential donors. By 15 November 2020, 33,994 donor attendances had led to 24,530 plasma donations collected.

DARS-NIC-372865-W5X1R.summary: NHS Suffolk and North East Essex ICB (a sub-ICB location)'s agreement allows it to use Secondary Uses Service (SUS+) hospital data for commissioners, linked with GP data, for risk stratification. This is intended to produce risk scores that identify patients likely to need high levels of care, so GPs and commissioners can target support and plan services. The main intended benefit is better case management and more effective commissioning, including fewer avoidable emergency admissions.

DARS-NIC-373042-Y8N7D.summary: NHS Suffolk and North East Essex ICB (a sub-ICB location, covering the former West Suffolk CCG) is permitted to use hospital data from SUS for Commissioners, linked with GP data and identifiable by NHS number. Prescribing Services Ltd is permitted to use it for risk stratification, which applies an algorithm to predict which patients are at high risk of health deterioration and heavy use of services. GPs and commissioners can then target care and plan services. The main intended benefit is fewer avoidable emergency admissions through earlier intervention.

DARS-NIC-373132-D3Y7P.summary: The University of Oxford's agreement covers NHS hospital, accident and emergency, outpatient, COVID-19 hospitalisation and death registration records for the PRINCIPLE trial, which tests treatments for COVID-19 in people over 50 with health conditions and those over 65. The data is for measuring how well treatments given early in the illness prevent hospital admission and help people recover. The trial reports twice weekly to Public Health England, and these reports feed into disease monitoring and help shape national policy.

DARS-NIC-373563-N8Z9J.summary: IQVIA Ltd's agreement covers the use of hospital records, emergency care data, death registrations and hospital mortality indicators. The data is for paid analysis services to health sector clients, including software dashboards, care pathway analysis, hospital benchmarking and clinical trial site identification. The intended benefit is helping clients find ways to improve patient care and experience. Reported results include an analysis of unequal access to CAR-T cancer therapy and a characterisation of Thyroid Eye Disease patients, both used to engage with the healthcare system.

DARS-NIC-374190-D0N1M.summary: Genomics England, a research organisation, is permitted to use NHS England hospital, primary care, cancer, death, vaccination and COVID-19 surveillance records. The agreement allows these records to be linked to whole genome sequences from people severely affected by COVID-19, to study how genes affect response to the virus. The aim is to find genetic variants and biomarkers that could inform new treatments and tests. Results so far include published papers in Nature identifying genetic variants linked to severe COVID-19.

DARS-NIC-374223-P4P4L.summary: The NIHR Bioresource's agreement covers hospital, emergency care, death registration and COVID-19 hospitalisation records for over 30,000 people with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) who volunteered for research. The records are for studying how IBD medicines such as immunosuppressants and anti-TNF therapies, and genetic risk factors, affect COVID-19 outcomes. The main intended benefit is to inform treatment recommendations and policy for vulnerable patients.

DARS-NIC-374485-Y2X9C.summary: The University of Exeter's agreement covers Hospital Episode Statistics data on hospital admissions and accident and emergency attendances. The data is for studying how exposure to natural environments, such as green space, pollen and harmful algal blooms, relates to health outcomes, and for developing ways of valuing the public health effects. The main intended benefit is scientific evidence to help Public Health England and other government departments plan public health interventions and environmental policies.

DARS-NIC-374630-G7W3K.summary: Leicester Royal Infirmary NHS Trust's agreement covers bespoke extracts of Hospital Episode Statistics (HES) accident and emergency and inpatient data. The data is for examining whether deprivation is linked to wrist fracture rates and to the type of treatment, by hospital region. The aim is to help providers cut costs by encouraging cheaper k-wire fixation over volar locking plates, and to target fracture prevention at high-risk patient groups.

DARS-NIC-374907-Q5W5W.summary: Cardiff University's agreement covers the use of linked hospital records (admissions, outpatient and accident and emergency) and death registration data to study the Family Nurse Partnership, a home visiting programme for young first-time mothers. The work examines how the programme produces its effects, including on child maltreatment indicators. The data is for informing the future development of home visiting in England and Germany. Earlier findings have already informed national and local decisions on continuing the programme and changing its content and delivery.

DARS-NIC-374924-C8S5Y.summary: The University of Sheffield's agreement allows it to use demographic data from NHS Digital's list cleaning service to check whether people with bladder cancer have died and to find their current addresses. The data supports a longitudinal survey of patient reported outcomes, which follows newly diagnosed patients in Yorkshire, the Humber, North Derbyshire and South Tees over their first 12 months. The main intended benefit is to avoid sending surveys to bereaved families, improve response rates, and identify gaps in care.

DARS-NIC-37497-DOD1Y.summary: NHS Doncaster CCG's agreement covers hospital, mental health, community and primary care data, some identifiable by NHS number and some pseudonymised (with identifying details replaced). The data is for checking invoices, identifying patients at high risk of needing care, and supporting the commissioning (planning and buying) of local health services. The main intended benefit is more effective commissioning, with better-targeted care and tighter control of NHS spending.

DARS-NIC-375354-G8V1H.summary: The University of Oxford's agreement covers linked hospital records (admissions, A&E, outpatient and critical care) and death registration data, joined to the QResearch database of GP records. The data is for COVID-19 research only, including linking to intensive care data held by ICNARC. The main aim is to help patients and doctors reduce the risk of severe COVID-19, for example by finding out whether common long-term medicines make the illness worse or better.

DARS-NIC-375669-J7M7F.summary: Barts Health NHS Trust's agreement with Queen Mary University of London allows the use of pseudonymised, patient-level Hospital Episode Statistics covering inpatient admissions, critical care and outpatient appointments. The agreement covers studying how COVID-19 disrupted surgery and other hospital procedures in England, how they are restarting, and what future waves might mean for care. The aim is to give policy makers and NHS planners evidence to plan surgical care and resources.

DARS-NIC-376141-W5D3L.summary: The London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine's agreement covers linked national hospital, mental health, psychological therapies and death records for women who gave birth. The agreement allows study of whether community perinatal mental health teams change mental health admissions, access to care, birth outcomes and costs. The data is for informing how these services are commissioned. Results have been published in peer-reviewed papers, including findings that the teams' national roll-out reduced the risk of acute mental health episodes after birth.

DARS-NIC-376184-B2F2K.summary: The University of York's agreement covers bespoke extracts of hospital inpatient records (Hospital Episode Statistics) linked to Office for National Statistics mortality data, covering date of death only. The research, funded by The Health Foundation, examines whether hospitals that keep sicker patients alive see more emergency re-admissions as a result. It aims to inform the debate on financial penalties for hospitals with rising emergency admissions.

DARS-NIC-376211-Y8B6R.summary: The University of Leeds's agreement covers Hospital Episode Statistics (HES) records for accident and emergency, critical care and inpatient care, linked to records from the Paediatric Intensive Care Audit Network (PICANet). It allows the university to study long-term outcomes for children admitted to paediatric intensive care, understand the pathways leading to admission, and develop clinical decision aids. The stated aim is to build an evidence base for improving healthcare for these children.

DARS-NIC-376367-M5V9H.summary: The University of Nottingham's agreement covers linked hospital data (Hospital Episode Statistics accident and emergency, admitted patient care, critical care and outpatients) with the QResearch database of GP records. The data is for studying disease causes, medicine safety and treatment outcomes, aiming to give doctors and patients better evidence for decisions. Its risk tools, such as QRISK, are used across NHS GP practices and are recommended in NICE guidance.

DARS-NIC-376374-F8D0M.summary: Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers Hospital Episode Statistics (HES) data on accident and emergency, inpatient, outpatient and critical care activity across England. The data is for comparing its clinical coding and services with similar trusts and for planning services for the population it serves, with the aim of improving patient care. Analysis has already shown gaps in recording of co-morbidities, prompting coding reviews and changes to records.

DARS-NIC-37647-J8W1M.summary: Leicestershire County Council's agreement covers the use of civil registration births and deaths data and Primary Care Mortality Data, including identifiable details. The data is for measuring local health needs, planning immunisation programmes and protecting public health, for example through suicide audits and hotspot mapping. The aim is for services to be tailored to local needs and to reduce health inequalities and premature deaths. Reported work to date includes the Director of Public Health's Annual Report and the Joint Strategic Needs Assessment.

DARS-NIC-376603-K2J9R.summary: NHS England, with the Healthcare Quality Improvement Partnership, agreement allows use of patient-level hospital, outpatient, emergency care, death registration and demographic records for adults diagnosed with bowel cancer in England and Wales. The data is for the National Bowel Cancer Audit, which assesses the quality of NHS care and outcomes. The aim is to help services compare themselves and improve care. The audit reports a rise in stage III colon cancer patients receiving adjuvant chemotherapy, from 54% to 61%.

DARS-NIC-37666-Z1C3M.summary: Queen Mary University of London's agreement covers NHS hospital, cancer registration, death and demographic records for women in the LATTE study, who took part in the earlier ATAC breast cancer trial. The agreement allows the data to be used to study the long-term safety and effectiveness of anastrozole compared with tamoxifen, including recurrence and survival. The aim is to help patients and clinicians choose between the treatments. Data received so far has provided information on deaths and breast cancer recurrence for the study's main endpoints.

DARS-NIC-377038-J7G7X.summary: NHS Midlands and Lancashire Commissioning Support Unit's agreement covers pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other health and care data, including clinical and financial information, for four Black Country clinical commissioning groups (CCGs): Dudley, Sandwell and West Birmingham, Walsall and Wolverhampton. The data is for planning and commissioning health services for the local population. The stated aim is to understand patient flows and population needs, so services can be redesigned and targeted more effectively.

DARS-NIC-377358-F3R2K.summary: Civil Eyes Research Ltd's agreement covers bespoke extracts of Hospital Episode Statistics (HES) covering A&E, critical care, inpatient and outpatient care, held in pseudonymised form. The data is for benchmarking hospital performance and quality, giving NHS and social care doctors, clinicians and managers aggregated analysis. This includes benchmarking clubs on medical productivity, pathology networks and specialist children's hospitals. The release register does not state a specific measurable benefit, but it aims to prompt discussion and action on efficiency, quality and access to services.

DARS-NIC-377644-X9J4P.summary: The University of Sheffield's agreement covers linked health records for people with suspected COVID-19 who used emergency care. These include GP data for pandemic planning, emergency care and hospital admission records, critical care records and death registrations. The PRIEST study is evaluating how well 111, ambulance and emergency department triage worked, and developing risk tools to identify patients likely to deteriorate. The intended benefit is fewer patients wrongly advised to self-care and less strain on services.

DARS-NIC-37789-N6J1N.summary: Leeds City Council, a local authority, is permitted under its agreement to use civil registration data on births and deaths, along with primary care mortality data, which includes identifiable details. The data is for assessing local health needs, planning services and protecting public health, including suicide audits and hotspot mapping. The aim is to tailor services to local needs and reduce premature deaths and health inequalities. The council used the data for its 2022 Director of Public Health annual report and a mortality dashboard.

DARS-NIC-378185-P4L5Z.summary: The University of Leeds's agreement covers hospital, emergency care, death registration and primary care dispensing records for 1,615 adults with heart failure who consented to take part in a trial. The agreement allows testing of the Medicines at Transitions Intervention (MaTI) toolkit, which aims to make medicines safer and more consistent when patients move from hospital to home. The data is for showing whether the toolkit reduces deaths and hospital readmissions within 12 months. The main intended benefit is better evidence for heart failure care and guidance.

DARS-NIC-378491-R6K9Y.summary: The University of Sheffield's agreement covers linked hospital records (accident and emergency, admitted patient care and critical care) and mortality data. The data is for updating an economic model of the cost-effectiveness of regional trauma networks in England, comparing the periods before, during and after their introduction. The intended benefit is evidence for NHS England on whether the networks are cost-effective and where practice differs between regions.

DARS-NIC-378523-Y5Q9L.summary: The University of Leeds holds hospital admissions and accident and emergency records (Hospital Episode Statistics) for residents of 12 Yorkshire care homes taking part in a feasibility trial. The data is used to check hospital attendance for safety and to measure health service use for a physical activity programme called REACH. This supports a decision on whether to seek funding for a larger trial. This version only allows the data to be securely retained.

DARS-NIC-378657-B8F3K.summary: The University of Birmingham's agreement covers the use of hospital, emergency care and death registration data, with the University of Oxford processing it. The data is for studying how hospitals' approaches to acute care affected their resilience for COVID-19 and for other conditions, such as heart failure and stroke. The aim is to inform policy and NHS acute services. The team has completed one study on how hospitals' recovery of elective activity after the pandemic varied, mainly by region.

DARS-NIC-37891-V3K0S.summary: London Borough of Sutton, a local authority, is covered by an agreement for civil registration data on births and deaths, plus primary care mortality data, which includes identifiable details. The agreement allows the data to be used to measure local health needs, plan services and immunisation programmes, and support work such as suicide audits. The aim is to tailor local services and reduce health inequalities and premature deaths. The figures have informed neighbourhood team locality profiles and the Sutton Suicide Prevention Strategy.

DARS-NIC-378964-S2X2T.summary: Stockton-on-Tees Borough Council's public health team uses hospital and emergency care records (Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set) to analyse local health needs. It uses them to support its statutory public health duties, such as needs assessments, health strategies and commissioning, with the aim of targeting services to local residents, particularly the most disadvantaged. The council reports using the data to break down COPD and hip fracture admissions locally and to inform weight management work.
DARS-NIC-378964-S2X2T.retense_draft: Stockton-on-Tees Borough Council's agreement covers the use of hospital and emergency care records (Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set) to analyse local health needs. The agreement allows the data to support the council's statutory public health duties, such as needs assessments, health strategies and commissioning, with the aim of targeting services to local residents, particularly the most disadvantaged. The data is for breaking down COPD and hip fracture admissions locally and for informing weight management work. The council reported, in a past report, that it had used the data to break down COPD and hip fracture admissions locally and to inform weight management work.

DARS-NIC-379653-W3G5Q.summary: The Royal College of Physicians of London's agreement covers the use of pseudonymised hospital admission and death registration records for children and young people admitted to hospital with asthma attacks. The agreement allows these records to be linked to National Respiratory Audit Programme data to study readmissions and deaths within 30 and 90 days. The data is for showing whether care has led to good outcomes and for improving standards of care. Reported benefits include a 2023 outcomes report that informed recommendations on how services are resourced.

DARS-NIC-379681-D6L7G.summary: The University of York's agreement covers hospital admission records for children with life-limiting conditions, linked to death registration data, to study how long these children and young people survive and how common these conditions are in England. The aim is to help plan children's palliative care and hospice services. The final report was launched in April 2020 and has been used by regional children's palliative care networks and NHS England for service planning.

DARS-NIC-379704-S6H6R.summary: NHS England's agreement covers use of the Diagnostic Imaging Dataset, linked to Cancer Waiting Times data, in pseudonymised record-level form. It allows analysis of the diagnostic stage of cancer pathways, including how many tests patients have and how long they wait for tests and reports. Only aggregate results with small numbers suppressed will be produced. The aim is to help distribute diagnostic resources more efficiently and shorten cancer waiting times.

DARS-NIC-379807-P3R7Z.summary: The Intensive Care National Audit & Research Centre (ICNARC)'s agreement covers the use of pseudonymised hospital admission, death registration and National Diabetes Audit data for patients in adult critical care or who had an in-hospital cardiac arrest. The data is for studying risk factors and longer-term outcomes of critical illness to improve the risk models behind national clinical audits. Results so far include a published report, journal papers on sepsis and atrial fibrillation, and a new Case Mix Programme dataset now used in all participating units.

DARS-NIC-38002-S3K0V.summary: NHS Cambridge and Peterborough CCG's agreement covers hospital, mental health, community, maternity and other local provider data that can be identified by NHS number. The agreement allows this data to be used to provide intelligence to support the commissioning of health services, including reporting, dashboards, readmissions analysis and budget monitoring. The aim is to analyse care across patient pathways for the CCG area's population, supporting demand management, needs assessments and the monitoring of care quality.

DARS-NIC-380256-R6K5L.summary: Northgate Information Solutions's agreement covers a bespoke extract of Hospital Episode Statistics (HES) linked with patient reported outcome measures (PROMs) data. The agreement allows this data to be linked to National Joint Registry (NJR) joint replacement records to produce the NJR's annual report and related analyses. The data is for monitoring and improving patient safety and outcomes, including identifying poor performance by hospitals, surgeons and implants.

DARS-NIC-380650-K4F6X.summary: The University of Oxford's agreement covers the use of linked hospital admissions, patient-reported outcome, and death registration data, combined with National Joint Registry data, to study results of revision hip and knee replacements. The data is for understanding outcomes, how they vary over time and place, and which factors affect them, so patients and surgeons can make better-informed decisions. The research has led to published journal papers on revision knee and hip replacement and a web application to support shared decision making.

DARS-NIC-380680-T6F4D.summary: The Medical School at Newcastle upon Tyne's agreement covers pseudonymised Hospital Episode Statistics (HES) data on children's A&E attendances, inpatient admissions and outpatient appointments. The agreement allows the data to be used to describe how common acquired brain injury is in children in England and how patients move through acute and secondary services. The aim is to improve the evidence for NHS commissioning of cost-effective neurological rehabilitation services and to inform a future research grant application.

DARS-NIC-381078-Y9C5K.summary: Health Data Research UK's agreement covers the use of linked NHS hospital, GP, prescribing, vaccination, testing, mental health, maternity and death records for the COVID-IMPACT-UK research consortium. The research looks at how existing health conditions affect COVID-19, and how COVID-19 and the response to it affect later health. It aims to inform public health policy and clinical care. Published papers have already informed vaccine safety reporting to national bodies and discussions with the Chief Medical Officer.

DARS-NIC-381383-Z9F2P.summary: The Department for Transport holds hospital records (Hospital Episode Statistics admitted patient care and accident and emergency data) linked to police road accident data. This agreement only lets it keep that data for an interim period while it applies to extend the agreement. The data has been used to understand road injuries and to identify seriously injured casualties more accurately than police judgement allows. HES analysis has appeared in the Reported Road Casualties Great Britain reports from 2016 to 2019 and fed into the STATS19 review, which produced recommendations on injury-based reporting.

DARS-NIC-381632-M4D9L.summary: The University of Oxford's agreement covers use of the Shielded Patient List, which here means a pseudonymised NHS Number and a COVID-19 risk code (high or moderate) for each listed patient. The agreement allows the University to use this to develop and validate a new tool that predicts which people in England are at high risk of severe outcomes from COVID-19. The aim is a widely used, validated tool that supports consistent shielding policy and clearer communication between policy makers, professionals and the public.

DARS-NIC-381633-K9Y2T.summary: The University of Oxford's Department of Paediatrics agreement covers holding COVID-19 test results from non-hospital (Pillar 2) antigen testing. The data is for a trial of the ChAdOx1 nCoV-19 vaccine to assess its efficacy and safety, and the agreement allows the University to keep the data so that regulators can audit the findings. The main aim is to show whether the vaccine protects people from COVID-19. Analyses have already looked at efficacy against asymptomatic disease, reduced likelihood of transmission after vaccination, and efficacy against new variants.

DARS-NIC-381634-X8H0H.summary: UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA)'s agreement covers the use of linked, pseudonymised NHS and COVID-19 testing, vaccination and hospital data to study how COVID-19 spreads between household members. The aim is to improve national surveillance of infections in England and show how vaccination affects transmission. Reported results include analysis showing household transmission was 40% to 50% lower where the first case had been vaccinated, published in The New England Journal of Medicine and used by government advisory groups.

DARS-NIC-381683-R6R6K.summary: The University of Oxford's agreement, working for the Royal College of General Practitioners (RCGP) Research and Surveillance Centre and Public Health England, covers pseudonymised GP records linked to hospital, emergency care, mental health, imaging and COVID-19 test data. The agreement allows the data to be used for studies and monitoring of COVID-19 in England, including community spread and the effects of lockdown on other conditions. The main intended benefit is better information for the national public health response.

DARS-NIC-381719-L6D2H.summary: Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust, with King's College Hospital, has an agreement covering Hospital Episode Statistics Critical Care data linked to its research data warehouse of clinical, laboratory and demographic records for patients tested for COVID-19 and other respiratory pathogens. The agreement allows the data to be used for research on disease progression, treatment and outcomes, including risk calculators and prediction tools. The stated aim is to support better-informed decisions about COVID-19 treatment and care.

DARS-NIC-381887-X5W2S.summary: The University of Warwick's agreement covers hospital inpatient and outpatient records and death registration data. The data is for studying why GP practices in England differ in how often they refer patients with suspected bowel cancer. It also covers how this affects diagnosis and survival, and the effect of the bowel screening programme. The aim is to help target care at the right groups and reduce inefficiency in primary care.

DARS-NIC-381948-L9M8Y.summary: Northumbria Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers the use of hospital admissions (Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care) and demographics data for the Bone and Joint Infection Registry (BAJIR), which it hosts. The agreement allows a feasibility study with 250 consenting patients, comparing NHS England data with registry records to check they are complete and accurate. The main intended benefit is a more accurate registry, and patients' care teams may also learn of details they did not know.

DARS-NIC-38197-Z4J4Y.summary: Torbay Council's agreement allows it to use identifiable births, deaths and Primary Care Mortality Data to understand local health needs, plan immunisation programmes, and protect public health, including through suicide audits. The data is for producing aggregated statistics for reports such as the Joint Strategic Needs Assessment. The aim is to tailor local services and reduce health inequalities. Reported benefits include the data informing the local suicide prevention strategy and the 2023 Joint Strategic Needs Assessment.

DARS-NIC-381972-Q5F0V.summary: University College London's agreement covers the use of linked, de-identified NHS hospital, maternity, mental health, community services and birth and death records, held in the ECHILD Research Database, to study how children's health, education and social care connect from childhood into adulthood. The aim is to give policy-makers evidence on improving outcomes for children and families. Reported results include published papers and studies commissioned by the Department of Health and Social Care.

DARS-NIC-381984-B7X3S.summary: University Hospitals Birmingham NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers pseudonymised patient-level Summary Hospital-level Mortality Indicator (SHMI) data, which covers deaths in hospital and within 30 days of discharge. The data is for use in its Healthcare Evaluation Data (HED) system so NHS organisations can monitor mortality, benchmark against peers and spot areas of concern or good practice. The aim is to support safer, better-quality care. Bolton NHS FT reported that its mortality metrics moved into the expected range after it used the analytics.

DARS-NIC-38231-Y7T5P.summary: The London Borough of Hillingdon, a local authority, is covered by an agreement that allows it to use civil registration data on births and deaths, plus primary care mortality data. The data is for understanding local health needs, planning services and supporting public health work such as suicide prevention, with the aim of tailoring services and reducing health inequalities. The data has informed needs assessments, including work by its suicide awareness panel and on low birth weights, and was used to test a claim about stillbirths.

DARS-NIC-382333-M5J9W.summary: The University of Bristol's agreement covers linked NHS hospital, emergency care and mental health service records for children in State care in England. The data is for studying how common mental health concerns are, and how these children move through mental health services compared with other children, before, during and after the COVID-19 pandemic. The intended benefit is new evidence to help policy makers and services identify the children most at risk and support them earlier.

DARS-NIC-382334-Y2B1C.summary: The National Audit Office's agreement covers hospital, emergency care, mental health and linked death registration data from NHS Digital, for producing value-for-money audit reports for Parliament. The agreement allows analysis of this data to examine how the Department of Health and Social Care and NHS bodies spend public money, to help Parliament hold them to account and help services improve. Its reports have led NHS England to change GP opening-hour payment rules, and cancer admissions analysis identified £9 million of savings.

DARS-NIC-382364-Y0F4F.summary: The University of York's agreement covers use of the Adult Psychiatric Morbidity Survey, a national survey of adults' mental health. The agreement allows the data to study whether socioeconomic factors are linked to psychiatric hospital admissions for people diagnosed with a personality disorder. The main intended benefit is stronger evidence to inform policy, clinical practice and interventions, with the aim of reducing hospital admissions.

DARS-NIC-382718-N1T4C.summary: The London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine's agreement covers the use of hospital admissions records and death registration data, linked to National Cardiac Arrest Audit data. The research examines how services for spotting and managing patients at risk of deterioration relate to ward-based cardiac arrest rates and outcomes. It aims to identify which service features are linked to the lowest arrest rates and best outcomes, to help the NHS raise standards of care and reduce avoidable deaths.

DARS-NIC-382794-T3L3M.summary: Queen Mary University of London's agreement covers linking GP, hospital, maternity, birth, death, cancer and COVID-19 records to support the QResearch database. The agreement allows approved UK researchers to use it for observational medical research on the causes, treatment and outcomes of disease, with results published in journals. The aim is better evidence for patient care and health policy. Its QRISK and QCOVID risk tools have been used in NHS care, and its vaccine safety studies informed regulators.

DARS-NIC-38314-C3P0Z.summary: The University of Cambridge's agreement covers the use of NHS England mortality data (death registrations and cause-of-death, event notification and current status reports) for the Oesophageal Cancer Clinical and Molecular Stratification (OCCAMS) study. The data is for studying clinical and genetic factors affecting oesophageal cancer, to help predict how it progresses and tailor treatment. Reported results include several published papers and a revised lymph node-based classification giving better prognostic information.

DARS-NIC-383203-Q8B9L.summary: Imperial College London's Dr Foster Unit's agreement allows pseudonymised hospital records linked to civil registration death data to be used to measure the quality and safety of healthcare. The aim is to show variations in outcomes between hospitals and to develop risk-adjusted indicators, supporting better quality and safety of care in England. Its mortality alerts helped identify problems at Mid Staffordshire NHS Foundation Trust, and its published research on junior doctor changeovers led to a new shadowing protocol.

DARS-NIC-383324-D6B8T.summary: The Nuffield Trust for Research and Policy Studies in Health Services's agreement covers the use of linked hospital admissions, patient-reported outcome and death registration data to study the care of frail older people. The data is for developing measures to spot areas giving good care to people over 65, and for evaluating Comprehensive Geriatric Assessment (CGA), a multidisciplinary assessment of frail patients. The aim is to help the NHS target services at those who would benefit most. A frailty risk score paper has been submitted to a journal, with a decision pending.

DARS-NIC-383345-W2D3J.summary: The Royal College of Surgeons of England's agreement covers linked hospital records (admitted patient care, outpatient and A&E) and death registration data for mothers and their children. The data is for studying how maternal factors before and during pregnancy affect children's use of health services and their outcomes, with the aim of informing NHS and policy decisions on maternity and children's care. Three papers have been published so far, including work that has led to other studies linking mother and baby records.

DARS-NIC-383356-N8J6Z.summary: Cambridge University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust, with the University of Cambridge, holds civil registrations of death data from a completed clinical trial called PROTECT-V. The data is kept for secure storage and back-up, and so earlier analyses can be repeated to check published findings if they are questioned. The trial tested whether a niclosamide nasal spray can prevent COVID-19 in people on dialysis or taking immunosuppressive medicines. The main hoped-for benefit is a preventive option for immunocompromised people.

DARS-NIC-38368-V3S5C.summary: The Competition and Markets Authority (CMA)'s agreement covers the use of Hospital Episode Statistics data on admitted patient care and outpatients. The agreement allows research into how patients choose and switch hospitals, including after events that affect a provider's quality. The aim is to test and improve the CMA's models for assessing mergers involving NHS Foundation Trusts. The expected benefit is helping to maintain quality standards in the NHS.

DARS-NIC-38410-S7X7G.summary: Somerset Council's agreement covers civil registration data on births and deaths, plus primary care mortality data, which includes identifiable details. The agreement allows the data to be used to understand local health needs, plan services and support public health work such as suicide prevention, with outputs published as aggregated statistics. The aim is to tailor services to local needs and reduce health inequalities. Reported results include a suicide audit report, an infectious disease needs assessment and analysis of excess deaths during the COVID-19 pandemic.

DARS-NIC-384136-J3N8Z.summary: NHS North East London ICB, a sub-ICB location, is covered by an agreement allowing it to use pseudonymised GP record data on diagnoses, medications, tests, treatments and vaccinations, collected during the COVID-19 emergency. The agreement allows the data to be used to plan local health care, including analysing missed appointments, identifying patients at risk of hospital admission and deciding where to allocate resources. The main intended benefit is helping manage demand and capacity and supporting better commissioning decisions for patients.

DARS-NIC-384137-V8F6H.summary: University College London Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers Hospital Episode Statistics data on admitted patient care, outpatient and accident and emergency care for the BRIGHTLIGHT study of teenagers and young adults with cancer. It allows refining a scale of how much specialist care they received, to test whether specialist services add value. The aim is to show which model of care is best for young people and cost-effective for the NHS. Published papers have already reported findings on care outcomes and on diagnosis timeliness.

DARS-NIC-384326-R9V7S.summary: The Nuffield Department of Primary Health Sciences, part of the University of Oxford, is using hospital admission, cancer registration and death records for 1,490 people aged 60 or over in the NewKI chronic kidney disease (CKD) study. It is studying which factors predict death, cardiovascular disease and other poor health outcomes, and whether screening for CKD in primary care is effective. The aim is to help doctors identify who needs closer monitoring. Publications from the study have already estimated how common CKD is in UK primary care.
DARS-NIC-384326-R9V7S.retense_draft: The Nuffield Department of Primary Health Sciences, part of the University of Oxford, is using hospital admission, cancer registration and death records for 1,490 people aged 60 or over in the NewKI chronic kidney disease (CKD) study. It is studying which factors predict death, cardiovascular disease and other poor health outcomes, and whether screening for CKD in primary care is effective. The aim is to help doctors identify who needs closer monitoring. Publications from the study have already estimated how common CKD is in UK primary care.

DARS-NIC-384504-N2V5B.summary: University College London's Centre for Longitudinal Studies has an agreement that allows the use of NHS hospital and emergency care records, linked to survey answers from the Millennium Cohort Study at age 17. The records are for checking and improving the survey data and for supporting health research. The aim is to help research that benefits health and social care. So far, a linked dataset and a user guide have been made available to researchers, and a webinar has been delivered.

DARS-NIC-384524-C7M2Q.summary: Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust, through University Hospital of South Manchester, is permitted to use Hospital Episode Statistics admitted patient care and critical care data. The agreement allows it to check that the National Burn Registry, which holds burn care data from providers, is accurate and complete. The aim is to help the burn care Clinical Reference Group advise NHS England on matching burn service capacity to demand across England.

DARS-NIC-384572-J7P6Y.summary: The Nuffield Trust for Research and Policy Studies in Health Services, an independent research group, is permitted to use Hospital Episode Statistics data covering accident and emergency, inpatient and outpatient care. The data is for evaluating new models of care and studying patterns of hospital use, costs and efficiency across England. The aim is to help the NHS identify and adopt good practice, and to inform decisions by commissioners, providers and policymakers.

DARS-NIC-384582-F4X9R.summary: NHS West Yorkshire ICB, a sub-ICB location, is permitted to use pseudonymised (identifiers replaced) GP record data, ethnic category data and COVID-19 vaccination status data. The agreement allows the data to be used to plan local health services for COVID-19, including analysing missed appointments, identifying patients at risk of hospital admission, allocating resources and monitoring vaccine uptake. The main intended benefit is better-informed decisions on demand, capacity and workforce. The CCG published an annual report on its COVID-19 response, which this data helped to support.

DARS-NIC-384608-C9B4L.summary: NHS England's agreement covers a range of COVID-19 related health data, including GP records, test results, death registrations, NHS 111, prescribing and shielded patient list data. The data is for analysing how COVID-19 is spreading, planning services and resources, and producing dashboards and reports. The main intended benefit is to help control the virus and reduce deaths. Reported results include letters and guidance sent to people at high risk, and analysis showing a fall in spirometry activity in general practice, which led to initiatives to restart it safely.

DARS-NIC-384618-N1H4Y.summary: The University of Sheffield's agreement covers NHS Digital cohort notification and current status reports from the Medical Research Information Service (MRIS). The agreement allows the data to be used to check whether children in the MERIDIAN fetal brain imaging study were still alive before families were invited to a 2-3 year follow-up. The data is for back-up and storage only. The study's results were published, including a final report in December 2017, and were used to produce improved information leaflets for parents.

DARS-NIC-384653-L3N2Q.summary: King's College Hospital NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers hospital records of admissions, outpatient visits and accident and emergency visits for patients who had bariatric (weight-loss) or other planned general surgery. The data is for comparing how much healthcare these patients use over the medium term, to help show how safe bariatric surgery is. The intended benefit is to inform commissioners and policy makers, which may make bariatric surgery more accessible to suitable patients.

DARS-NIC-384661-Z9H3W.summary: NHS Cornwall and the Isles of Scilly ICB, a sub-ICB location, is covered by an agreement that allows it to use pseudonymised (identifiers replaced) COVID-19 data from GP records, along with ethnic category and vaccination status data. The data is for planning local health care, including analysing missed appointments, identifying patients at risk of hospital admission, allocating resources and monitoring vaccine uptake. The main intended benefit is helping commissioners manage demand and capacity and make better decisions to support patients.

DARS-NIC-384722-W7Y8W.summary: The University of Aberdeen's agreement covers a list cleaning report from the Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) for use in the eTHoS trial, which compares two operations for haemorrhoids. The data is for finding out which operation is better for patients in terms of quality of life, clinical outcomes and cost, including long-term safety and recurrence. The expected benefit is robust evidence to help surgeons and NHS Trusts choose which treatment to offer.

DARS-NIC-384771-T2D4G.summary: NHS West Yorkshire ICB's agreement covers pseudonymised GP record data (coded details such as diagnoses, medications, tests and vaccinations) collected for pandemic planning and research. The agreement allows the data to be used to plan local health care during COVID-19, including analysing missed appointments, identifying patients at risk of hospital admission as groups rather than individuals, and allocating resources. The main intended benefit is better management of demand, capacity and resources.

DARS-NIC-384776-G1X0Y.summary: NHS West Yorkshire ICB's agreement covers pseudonymised GP record data, such as diagnoses, medications, tests, treatments and vaccinations, collected for pandemic planning and research. The data is for supporting the local COVID-19 response, including analysing missed appointments, identifying patients at risk of hospital admission as groups rather than individuals, and allocating resources. The main intended benefit is better management of demand, capacity and resources for local patients.

DARS-NIC-384781-J8H2K.summary: NHS West Yorkshire ICB, a sub-ICB location, uses pseudonymised GP record data, ethnic category data and COVID-19 vaccination status data. It uses them to plan local health care, forecast demand, allocate resources and identify patients at risk during the COVID-19 response. It also uses them to find areas of low vaccine take-up. The intended benefit is better commissioning decisions and a more effective response to the outbreak. The CCGs have published annual reports describing pandemic response work supported by this data.

DARS-NIC-38500-Q9K8G.summary: Dorset Council's public health team agreement covers civil registration data on births and deaths, plus primary care mortality data, which includes identifiable details. The data is for measuring local health needs, supporting immunisation programmes, protecting public health and carrying out suicide audits, with only aggregated figures published. The aim is to tailor local services and reduce premature deaths and health inequalities. Reported results include informing a health visiting service review, pupil place planning and the local suicide prevention strategy.

DARS-NIC-385032-K3N9S.summary: The Health and Safety Executive's agreement covers NHS England death, cancer registration and demographic records for people in its long-term study of pesticide applicators' health. The agreement allows the records to be used to track cancer and deaths among participants and to keep the study's mailing list up to date. The aim is to understand the long-term health risks of working with pesticides. The records have kept the mailing list current, and a 2021 paper on asthma has been published.

DARS-NIC-385396-J1Z4V.summary: NHS Devon ICB, a sub-ICB location, is covered by an agreement allowing the use of pseudonymised (not directly identifiable) GP record data, ethnic category data and COVID-19 vaccination status data. The agreement allows the data to be used to plan local health services, model patient risk, allocate resources and monitor vaccine uptake during the COVID-19 response. The main intended benefit is better decisions on demand, capacity and resources. An annual report for 2020-21 describes key COVID-19 achievements that this data helped support.

DARS-NIC-38545-F7M6M.summary: Bracknell Forest Council's agreement covers the use of identifiable birth and death registration records, together with primary care mortality data, to understand local public health needs. The agreement allows the data to be used for work such as suicide audits, needs assessments and health reports, with the aim of targeting services and reducing health inequalities. The council reports that the data has already produced statutory reports, including the Joint Strategic Needs Assessment, and informed Children's Centre planning.

DARS-NIC-385550-Y8T2M.summary: Worcestershire County Council, a local authority, has an agreement covering NHS community services, maternity, mental health and hospital activity data for building a COVID-19 model for adult social care. The model is for showing where demand for health and social care services is likely to rise during the pandemic, so the council can plan support and make better-informed decisions. Reported benefits so far include presenting the model to the local integrated care system and partners, and using it to start conversations with senior managers.

DARS-NIC-385700-J4X9H.summary: University College London's agreement covers a bespoke extract of Hospital Episode Statistics (HES) inpatient data, linked to other health records, for a patient safety study. The agreement allows comparison of patients with metal-on-metal hip replacements to a matched group with other hip implants. The data is for finding out whether heart failure, related medication use and deaths from heart failure are more common in those with metal-on-metal hips.

DARS-NIC-38593-Q6K1V.summary: Calderdale Metropolitan Borough Council's agreement covers civil registration data on births and deaths, plus primary care mortality data, which includes identifiable details. The data is for understanding local health needs, planning services, and supporting public health work such as suicide audits and prevention. The aim is to tailor local services and reduce premature deaths and health inequalities. To date, the data has been used for child death audits, suicide prevention, and small-area birth and death rates for the Joint Strategic Needs Assessment (JSNA).

DARS-NIC-386178-Y2S6V.summary: University Hospitals Birmingham NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers the use of death registration records and hospital admitted patient and outpatient records. It allows follow-up of 1,290 people from the earlier BALLETS study, who had abnormal liver blood tests, including people with and without fatty liver disease. The aim is to describe how often fatty liver disease progresses to serious liver disease. The team hopes this will show whether routine liver monitoring is justified.

DARS-NIC-386376-Z1H5J.summary: The Renal Registry, a charity, is permitted under its agreement to use hospital, accident and emergency, and death registration records for adults with idiopathic membranous nephropathy, a kidney condition with no known cause. The data is for evaluating whether rituximab and its biosimilars work and are safe for this condition, including how often re-treatment is needed, hospital admissions and cost. The aim is to help NHS England decide whether to routinely commission rituximab, and to inform NICE guidelines.

DARS-NIC-386685-K2B6G.summary: Royal Free London NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers Pillar 2 COVID-19 non-hospital antigen testing results, including names, telephone numbers and London postcodes of adults aged 18 to 70 with a recent positive test. The agreement allows the trial team to phone these people to invite them to join the FLARE clinical trial, which is testing two antiviral drugs for early COVID-19. The data is for recruitment only. The intended benefit is helping to identify effective early treatments for COVID-19.

DARS-NIC-386877-S2T6C.summary: CSL-UK (CompuFile System Limited) uses Hospital Episode Statistics (HES) data covering accident and emergency, critical care, inpatient and outpatient care. It turns this into aggregated, masked results, with small numbers hidden, for NHS bodies, medical suppliers and pharmaceutical companies. The results show how patients move through hospital care and how treatment compares with best practice and between trusts and clinical commissioning groups (CCGs). The stated aim is to support cost-benefit analyses that help commissioning and reduce treatment costs.
DARS-NIC-386877-S2T6C.retense_draft: CSL-UK (CompuFile System Limited) is permitted under its agreement to use Hospital Episode Statistics (HES) data covering accident and emergency, critical care, inpatient and outpatient care. The results show how patients move through hospital care and how treatment compares with best practice and between trusts and clinical commissioning groups (CCGs). The stated aim is to support cost-benefit analyses that help commissioning and reduce treatment costs.

DARS-NIC-387073-P2L5R.summary: NHS Humber and North Yorkshire ICB, a sub-ICB location, is permitted to use pseudonymised COVID-19 vaccination data, which includes patient demographics, vaccination appointment and outcome details, and vaccine batch details. The data is for understanding vaccine rollout in its area, supporting weekly reports to NHS England and the Cabinet Office, and identifying areas of low take-up so it can work with local communities. The intended benefit is helping to control the spread of the virus and maintain high vaccination uptake.

DARS-NIC-387074-L1X5J.summary: NHS Sussex ICB uses pseudonymised (identifying details replaced) GP record data, ethnic category data and COVID-19 vaccination data. It uses them to plan local health services during the COVID-19 emergency, including analysing missed appointments, identifying patients at risk of hospital admission, allocating resources and monitoring vaccine take-up. The main intended benefit is to help commissioners manage demand and capacity and make better decisions for patients. The three local clinical commissioning groups (CCGs) have published 2020/21 annual reports describing achievements, including pandemic response, that this data contributed to.
