DARS-NIC-387079-N9L6D.summary: NHS Hampshire and Isle of Wight ICB's agreement covers pseudonymised GP record data, covering diagnoses, medications, tests, treatments and vaccinations, collected for pandemic planning and research. The agreement allows the data to plan local health services during COVID-19, including analysing missed appointments, identifying patients at risk of hospital admission and allocating resources. The main intended benefit is better management of demand and capacity.

DARS-NIC-387112-D9S8C.summary: NHS Frimley ICB's agreement covers pseudonymised GP record data on diagnoses, medications, tests, treatments and vaccinations, collected for pandemic planning and research. The data is for supporting its local COVID-19 response, including analysing missed appointments, identifying patients at risk of hospital admission, and planning where to allocate resources. The main intended benefit is helping commissioners manage demand and capacity and make better decisions to support patients.

DARS-NIC-387291-B3M4Z.summary: Dudley Metropolitan Borough Council's agreement covers the use of pseudonymised GP record data on diagnoses, medications, tests, treatments and vaccinations, collected for COVID-19 pandemic planning and research. The agreement allows the data to be used to plan local health care, analyse missed appointments, model patient risk and allocate resources, with the aim of protecting public health and supporting vulnerable groups. The data has supported quarterly COVID performance reports and updates to the council's COVID-19 advice page.

DARS-NIC-387297-J5L7M.summary: NHS Humber and North Yorkshire ICB, a sub-ICB location, is permitted to use pseudonymised COVID-19 vaccination data, which includes patient demographics, vaccination appointment and outcome details, and vaccine batch details. The data is for understanding vaccine roll-out in its area, producing reports for NHS England and the Cabinet Office, and identifying areas of low take-up so it can work with local communities. The intended benefit is helping to control and prevent the spread of the virus.

DARS-NIC-387346-G3H3J.summary: London Borough of Havering's agreement covers hospital episode statistics for admitted patient care, outpatients, critical care and accident and emergency, plus Emergency Care Data Set records. The data is for its public health duties, including needs assessments, health strategies, advice to NHS commissioners and the annual public health report. The aim is locally focused analysis of health inequalities. The data has already informed the 2023 Joint Strategic Needs Assessment, the 2022 Pharmaceutical Needs Assessment and other needs assessments.

DARS-NIC-387358-H3Z2J.summary: NHS Birmingham and Solihull ICB's agreement covers pseudonymised (identifying details replaced) COVID-19 data from GP records, ethnic category data and vaccination status. The data is for planning local health services, assessing missed appointments, identifying patients at risk of hospital admission, allocating resources and monitoring vaccine take-up. The main intended benefit is better commissioning decisions and a more effective response to COVID-19. The CCG has published an annual report describing its COVID-19 achievements, which this data supported.

DARS-NIC-387462-R0L8Z.summary: Chelsea and Westminster Hospital NHS Foundation Trust, through its Neonatal Data Analysis Unit, has an agreement covering hospital records (accident and emergency, admitted patient care and outpatients) and mortality data, linked to a national neonatal research database. The data is for studying deaths, hospital readmissions and later health problems in babies born between April 2006 and March 2015 who were admitted to neonatal units. The aim is to show which babies are most at risk, so health professionals can target preventive care.

DARS-NIC-387526-Y0J4L.summary: London Borough of Hackney's agreement covers hospital and emergency care records from Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set, accessed through NHS England's secure environment. The agreement allows the data to be used for its public health duties, including needs assessments, health strategies, commissioning and advice to NHS commissioners. The aim is locally focused analysis of health inequalities, particularly for the most disadvantaged. Analysis of inequalities in hospital admissions for conditions including substance use, violence and mental health has already taken place.

DARS-NIC-387559-Y5P4P.summary: Redcar and Cleveland Borough Council's agreement covers the use of hospital and emergency care records (Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set) for its public health work. The agreement allows the data to be used to plan and assess local health services, and to produce needs assessments, health strategies and the annual public health report. The main intended benefit is locally focused analysis of health outcomes and inequalities. The data has already helped the South Tees Teenage Pregnancy Strategy Group produce a more up-to-date teenage conception count.

DARS-NIC-387580-W0W5T.summary: The University of Leeds's agreement, working with Bradford Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust, covers hospital admission, outpatient, critical care, A&E and emergency care records plus civil death registrations for about 700 older people with frailty who took part in the HERO trial. The data is for testing whether a 24-week home-based exercise programme after hospital reduces hospital stays and falls, and whether it is cost-effective. If it works, the findings could inform NHS commissioning of services for older people.

DARS-NIC-387635-C9Y0W.summary: King's College London's agreement covers the Sentinel Stroke National Audit Programme, which allows linked hospital admission and death records for stroke patients to be used to report on stroke care quality, case ascertainment and mortality, so clinicians, commissioners and patients can see where care needs to improve. Reported benefits include trusts entering more records after being targeted, outlier trusts being offered peer reviews, and a 2018 paper in The Lancet.

DARS-NIC-387749-B8Z3M.summary: Lancashire County Council's agreement covers its use of hospital and emergency care records (Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set) through an NHS England hosted environment. The data is for its public health duties, including needs assessments, health strategies, commissioning and advice to NHS commissioners. The main intended benefit is locally focused analysis of health and health inequalities. The agreement allows analysis of self-harm and respiratory admissions by district to inform local public health planning.

DARS-NIC-387811-M7J2B.summary: Gloucestershire County Council's agreement covers the use of pseudonymised hospital data, including Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set. The data is for its public health duties, such as needs assessments, health strategies, commissioning and advice to NHS commissioners. The aim is locally focused analysis of health outcomes and inequalities. Reported uses so far include a liver health needs assessment, a children's oral health analysis and a drugs and alcohol needs assessment.

DARS-NIC-387891-W3F3B.summary: Dorset Council's agreement covers pseudonymised hospital data, including inpatient, outpatient, accident and emergency and critical care records, for its public health work. The agreement allows the data to produce needs assessments, health strategies, the annual public health report and advice to NHS commissioners, aiming to analyse local health and inequalities. The data is for forecasting respiratory illness admissions, informing substance misuse commissioners and producing needs assessments for the ICB.

DARS-NIC-387965-T2B5D.summary: Swansea University's agreement covers linked records on deaths, emergency care, hospital admissions and critical care. The data is for studying 999 callers with suspected COVID-19 in four ambulance services during the first wave of the pandemic. The aim is to compare how safe and effective different triage models were at deciding who needs a response and hospital conveyance. The intended benefit is better evidence for triage decisions in future pandemics and periods of high demand.

DARS-NIC-387994-T3R5C.summary: Oldham Metropolitan Borough Council's agreement covers hospital data from accident and emergency, admitted patient care, critical care and outpatients, including Emergency Care Data Set records. The agreement allows the data to support the council's public health duties, such as producing Joint Strategic Needs Assessments, the annual public health report and advice to NHS commissioners. The main intended benefit is locally focused analysis of health inequalities. The data has improved the council's understanding of secondary care use and contributed to its Joint Strategic Needs Assessment.

DARS-NIC-388052-T8J4S.summary: Harrow Council's agreement covers hospital data on emergency care, admitted patients, critical care and outpatients, accessed through the NHS Digital Portal. The data is for its public health duties, including needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, the Director of Public Health's annual report and advice to NHS commissioners. The main intended benefit is locally focused analysis of health outcomes and inequalities, so that the needs of the most disadvantaged residents are identified and responded to.

DARS-NIC-388185-C4D6J.summary: NHS Norfolk and Waveney ICB's agreement covers the use of pseudonymised COVID-19 data on GP records, ethnic category and vaccination status. The agreement allows the data to be used to plan local health services, allocate resources, stratify patient risk and monitor vaccine uptake. The main aim is to manage demand and support better commissioning decisions. So far, the vaccination data has supported local planning and inequalities work, and has been used to check vaccination clinic cohorts.

DARS-NIC-388376-R4T5R.summary: Halton Borough Council's agreement covers receipt of pseudonymised Hospital Episode Statistics data on accident and emergency, admitted patient care and outpatient activity, including standard monthly extracts. The data is for supporting its public health duties, such as needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, the annual public health report and advice to NHS commissioners. The stated benefit is locally focused analysis of health outcomes and inequalities, so that the health challenges facing disadvantaged groups are identified and addressed.

DARS-NIC-388466-F2Z7Q.summary: The London Borough of Merton's agreement covers the use of hospital and emergency care records, including Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set, through NHS England's secure environment. The agreement allows analysis to support its public health duties, such as needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, the annual public health report and advice to NHS commissioners. The main intended benefit is locally focused analysis of health outcomes and inequalities, including for specific groups.

DARS-NIC-38847-G3Z7R.summary: City of Bradford Metropolitan District Council's agreement covers pseudonymised hospital data, including admitted patient care, outpatients, accident and emergency, critical care and emergency care records. The data is for its public health work, including needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, advice to NHS commissioners and the commissioning of local services. The aim is locally focused analysis of health outcomes and inequalities. The data has supported the council's district plan indicators, local area committee priorities and an update of the Joint Strategic Needs Assessment.

DARS-NIC-388486-D9M5N.summary: The University of Oxford's agreement covers the use of NHS hospital admission and outpatient records, cancer registrations, death records and demographic data to follow up participants in the 3C kidney transplant trial. It allows study of how different anti-rejection drug approaches affect long-term transplant survival, patient survival, infections and cancer. The aim is to show whether the treatments help transplants last longer. Published results have already led some kidney transplant units to adopt alemtuzumab as their standard treatment.

DARS-NIC-388494-W3L6K.summary: University Hospitals Coventry and Warwickshire NHS Trust's agreement covers Hospital Episode Statistics data on hospital admissions, outpatient appointments and A&E attendances. The agreement allows the Trust to compare its length of stay, emergency admissions, follow-up appointments, activity volumes and clinical coding with similar teaching hospital trusts, and to analyse its market share in the Midlands and East area. The data is for identifying variations in practice and efficiency opportunities, and for informing service redesign proposals to commissioners.

DARS-NIC-388748-Z6Q4Q.summary: Plymouth City Council's agreement covers the use of hospital and emergency care data (Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set) for its public health work. The agreement allows the data to be used to assess local health needs, plan and commission services, and advise NHS commissioners, with the aim of showing health inequalities in local areas and groups. The council has already used the data in an oral health needs assessment presented to the local health and wellbeing board, and in neighbourhood profiles.

DARS-NIC-388768-T5H3Y.summary: NHS Mid and South Essex ICB, a sub-ICB location, is permitted to use pseudonymised (de-identified) COVID-19 data from GP records, vaccination status and ethnic category. The agreement allows the data to be used to plan local health services, assess missed appointments, identify patients at risk of hospital admission and allocate resources during the pandemic. The main intended benefit is helping commissioners manage demand and respond to COVID-19 risks. The local clinical commissioning groups (CCGs) have published annual reports that include their pandemic response work supported by this data.

DARS-NIC-388786-H0Q8Q.summary: Nottingham City Council's public health team's agreement allows it to use pseudonymised hospital records, covering admissions, outpatient, accident and emergency and critical care data, to support its public health duties. These include needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, commissioning and advice to NHS commissioners. The data is for locally focused analysis of health outcomes and inequalities. Reported uses to date include alcohol admissions analysis, a Health Needs Assessment for adult women, and tuberculosis data informing a Joint Strategic Needs Assessment.

DARS-NIC-388794-Z9P3J.summary: The Office for National Statistics (ONS) agreement allows it to use pseudonymised Mental Health Services Data Set records, accessed remotely in NHS England's secure environment. The data is for exploring the data's variables, quality and suitability for statistical analysis, to decide what to request for future linkage projects. The intended benefit is requesting only the variables needed and carrying out future work more efficiently. Earlier access under this agreement produced briefings on long COVID that were used in government and NHS decisions.

DARS-NIC-388913-L5D5B.summary: NHS Greater Manchester ICB, a sub-ICB location, is permitted under its agreement to use pseudonymised GP record data about COVID-19, covering diagnoses, medications, tests, treatments and vaccinations, with no free text. The data is for planning local health care, including analysing missed appointments, identifying patients at risk of hospital admission, and allocating resources. The stated benefit is helping commissioners manage demand and capacity and make better decisions to support patients.

DARS-NIC-388922-L1S0K.summary: NHS Cheshire and Merseyside ICB's agreement covers pseudonymised coded GP record data (such as diagnoses, medications, tests and vaccinations) collected for COVID-19 pandemic planning and research. The agreement allows the data to be used to plan local health care, including analysing missed appointments, identifying patients at risk of hospital admission and allocating resources. The main intended benefit is helping commissioners manage demand and capacity and make better decisions to support patients.

DARS-NIC-389134-S8L1C.summary: The University of Oxford's agreement covers linked NHS England data on hospital admissions, deaths, cancer registrations and mental health, which allows the health of women in the Million Women Study to be followed. The data is for studying risk factors for common diseases, such as smoking, obesity and alcohol, and for giving evidence for public health guidance. Its findings on hormone therapy and breast cancer were shared with the Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency and helped change prescribing guidance.

DARS-NIC-389320-R4M6Z.summary: The University of Nottingham's agreement covers hospital admission records, death registration data and linked records for consented patients in the Helicobacter Eradication Aspirin Trial (HEAT). The data is for testing whether eradicating H. pylori reduces peptic ulcer bleeding in people taking aspirin. The aim is to inform NHS policy, cut hospitalisations and save costs. The data has helped estimate event rates and so work out how many patients the trial needed.

DARS-NIC-389495-J7Z8L.summary: Nottinghamshire County Council's public health team's agreement covers pseudonymised hospital records, covering admissions, outpatients, critical care and emergency care. The agreement allows the data to be used to analyse local health needs and to support its public health duties, including needs assessments, health strategies, commissioning and advice to NHS commissioners. The aim is locally focused analysis of health outcomes and inequalities. So far, the data has been used for work on alcohol-related admissions, drug overdoses, intentional injuries and children's teeth extractions.

DARS-NIC-389715-Y4S3N.summary: North Lincolnshire Council's public health team's agreement covers pseudonymised hospital data, including admissions, outpatient, critical care and emergency care records. The agreement allows the data to be used to produce needs assessments, health profiles and the Director of Public Health's annual report. The data is for targeting services at local health needs and reducing inequalities. Reported results include analysis of children's injuries, which led to a task and finish group, and a dementia needs assessment.

DARS-NIC-389767-B0C0M.summary: Derby Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers the use of cause of death data from the Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) alongside its own patient cohort. The study looks at diagnosis rates and causes of death in coeliac disease in Southern Derbyshire from 1958 to 2014. The aim is to help clinicians and commissioners judge how many diagnoses to expect and the health risks patients face, particularly cancer.

DARS-NIC-389823-P1P6B.summary: NHS England's agreement covers identifiable and pseudonymised data from the Assuring Transformation collection, which covers people with a learning disability or autism who are in inpatient care. The agreement allows the data to be used to monitor and manage commissioners' progress in moving people from hospital to community settings, and to help Transforming Care Partnerships plan services. The aim is to reduce reliance on inpatient care. NHS England reports that it has used the data to identify blockages to discharge and to follow up with commissioners over late oversight visits.

DARS-NIC-389914-N9R8R.summary: The Department of Health and Social Care's agreement covers demographic data from the NHS Patient Demographics Service, which allows Ipsos MORI to select a nationally representative sample of adults in England for the REACT 2 antibody study run by Imperial College London. The study is for estimating, through self-administered finger-prick antibody tests, how many people have had COVID-19, including by local authority area. The data is for informing the public health response. Results have been reported in the media and published on the REACT findings webpage.

DARS-NIC-390154-Z4M0F.summary: The Office for Health Improvement and Disparities, working with the Department of Health and Social Care, holds GP records data from the COVID-19 General Practice Extraction Service Data for Pandemic Planning and Research. It is retained for secure storage and for repeating earlier analyses, so that challenges to published COVID-19 findings, including from the UK COVID inquiry, can be answered. The wider aim is to understand COVID-19 and help reduce its spread. The data has been used in the Mortality Displacement Tool, which the department uses to monitor the pandemic's impact.
DARS-NIC-390154-Z4M0F.retense_draft: The Office for Health Improvement and Disparities, working with the Department of Health and Social Care, holds GP records data from the COVID-19 General Practice Extraction Service Data for Pandemic Planning and Research. The wider aim is to understand COVID-19 and help reduce its spread. The data has been used in the Mortality Displacement Tool, which the department uses to monitor the pandemic's impact.

DARS-NIC-390198-L6W9C.summary: NHS Coventry and Warwickshire ICB's agreement covers pseudonymised GP record data, covering diagnoses, medications, tests, treatments and vaccinations, collected for COVID-19 planning and research. The agreement allows the data to be used to plan local health care during the pandemic, including analysing missed appointments, identifying groups at risk of hospital admission, and deciding where to allocate resources. The main intended benefit is helping commissioners manage demand and capacity and make better decisions to support patients.

DARS-NIC-39036-P2D2D.summary: NHS Ipswich and East Suffolk Clinical Commissioning Group (CCG)'s agreement covers hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other local provider data, some identifiable by NHS number and some pseudonymised. The data is for risk stratification, which forecasts demand by identifying high-risk patients, and for commissioning health services. North of England Commissioning Support Unit carries out the work. The main intended benefit is better planning and more effective commissioning, leading to improved patient experience.

DARS-NIC-390531-R7S3D.summary: Brighton and Hove City Council's public health team agreement covers hospital and emergency care data: Hospital Episode Statistics covering admissions, outpatients, critical care and A&E, plus the Emergency Care Data Set. The agreement allows the data to support the team's public health duties, including needs assessments, health strategies, licensing responses and advice to NHS commissioners. The aim is locally focused analysis of health inequalities. The data has already informed a self-harm needs assessment for children and young people, safeguarding work, licensing work and primary care network profiles.

DARS-NIC-390662-Q9Q1N.summary: Kent County Council's agreement covers the use of hospital and emergency care records (Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set) through an NHS England hosted environment. The agreement allows the council to use the data for its public health duties, including needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, commissioning and advice to NHS commissioners. The aim is locally focused analysis of health outcomes and inequalities. The data is for monitoring population health and, with district councils, for summarising crime and safety issues.

DARS-NIC-390749-C4P0X.summary: University of York's agreement covers linked NHS England data, including cancer registrations, death records and hospital records, alongside its Yorkshire and Humberside Haematology Network patient cohort. The research aims to understand the causes of blood cancers, their effect on later health and healthcare needs, and real-world treatment outcomes. It is intended to inform policy and care services. YHHN data have already been used in 49 NICE submissions on blood cancer treatments.

DARS-NIC-39079-P2T7V.summary: London Borough of Bromley's agreement covers its use of civil registration births and deaths data and primary care mortality data, including identifiable details. The agreement allows the data to be used to assess local health needs, plan public health work such as suicide prevention, and produce aggregated, small-number-suppressed statistics. The aim is to tailor local services and reduce premature deaths and health inequalities. The data has fed into the JSNA, and into substance misuse and alcohol needs assessments that informed service recommissioning.

DARS-NIC-39089-Q7S0Q.summary: Bath and North East Somerset Council's agreement covers civil registration data on births and deaths, including identifiable details, and Primary Care Mortality Data. The data is for assessing local health needs, planning public health work such as suicide prevention, and producing aggregated statistics and reports. The main intended benefit is local services tailored to areas of greatest need, helping reduce premature deaths and health inequalities. Reported results include updated suicide audits and a local Suicide Prevention Strategy, and a published substance misuse needs assessment.

DARS-NIC-390964-G8W3R.summary: The Care Quality Commission (CQC), with Ipsos MORI running the survey for it, is permitted to use demographic data and hospital admission records (Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care). The agreement allows them to survey patients admitted to hospital with COVID-19 and those admitted for other reasons, to compare their experiences of care. The aim is to inform planning and care in any second wave of COVID-19 admissions, with results at national, regional and local health system level.

DARS-NIC-391119-T4J3R.summary: NHS National Services Scotland's agreement covers the use of pseudonymised Hospital Episode Statistics data on accident and emergency, admitted patient care and outpatients from England. The data feeds the NSS Discovery service, which gives Scottish NHS health boards monthly benchmarking and comparison figures, including English peers for boards with no natural Scottish peer. The intended benefit is to help boards spot where services can improve, learn from better performing peers and improve patient outcomes.

DARS-NIC-391230-T1S2Q.summary: MedeAnalytics International Limited's agreement covers Hospital Episode Statistics (HES) data on accident and emergency, inpatient and outpatient care. The agreement allows the data to be processed in its online analytics service to give NHS and social care customers national comparators for quality and performance measures, such as length of stay. These comparators are for comparing organisations' performance, redesigning services and assessing health needs, with the aim of supporting better decisions and patient outcomes.

DARS-NIC-391309-T4N4V.summary: Thurrock Council's agreement covers pseudonymised hospital data, including A&E, admitted patient, outpatient and critical care records, to support its public health duties. These include planning services, advising NHS commissioners and producing local health needs assessments and strategies. The main intended benefit is local analysis of health inequalities. The data has informed business cases for integrated care in Tilbury, better-targeted NHS Health Checks, the Well Homes programme and flu vaccination efforts.

DARS-NIC-391589-Q6Q1H.summary: NHS Buckinghamshire, Oxfordshire and Berkshire West ICB's agreement covers pseudonymised GP record data, ethnicity data and COVID-19 vaccination data, which do not identify individuals. The agreement allows the data to be used to plan local health services, allocate resources and identify patients at risk during the COVID-19 response. It also allows the data to monitor vaccine take-up, with the aim of managing demand and capacity. The CCG published an annual report on its COVID-19 response, supported by this data.

DARS-NIC-391590-M5D5Q.summary: NHS Bath and North East Somerset, Swindon and Wiltshire ICB's agreement covers pseudonymised (identifiers replaced) GP record data, ethnicity data and COVID-19 vaccination data. The data is for planning local health services, assessing risk and allocating resources in response to COVID-19. The main intended benefit is helping commissioners make better decisions to support patients. The CCGs have published annual reports describing their pandemic response, which this data supported.

DARS-NIC-391600-Q4Y2J.summary: NHS Gloucestershire ICB, a sub-ICB location, is permitted to use pseudonymised COVID-19 vaccination data, including patient demographics, vaccination appointment and outcome details, and vaccine batch details. The data is for understanding vaccine rollout and uptake locally, deciding whether new vaccine sites are needed, and identifying areas of low take-up to work with communities. The intended benefits are helping to control the spread of the virus and maintaining high vaccination uptake.

DARS-NIC-391618-M3X6R.summary: Pathway Communications Ltd's agreement covers record-level Hospital Episode Statistics data on admitted patient care and outpatients. The agreement allows it to build tools that forecast demand for ophthalmology (eye) services over the next 12 months and to simulate patient pathways. NHS Trusts, Foundation Trusts, clinical commissioning groups and commissioning support units would receive the reports. The main intended benefit is to let service managers plan ahead and test service changes in a virtual setting for the benefit of patients.

DARS-NIC-391733-S8V5J.summary: Derbyshire County Council's agreement covers the use of pseudonymised hospital data, including Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set, for its public health work. The data supports its statutory duties, such as Joint Strategic Needs Assessments, health and wellbeing strategies and advice to NHS commissioners. The aim is locally focused analysis of health outcomes and inequalities. Reported results include mental health profiles, a falls prevention strategy and needs assessment, and alcohol analyses for the Health and Wellbeing Board.

DARS-NIC-391959-Q3C3G.summary: University Hospitals of Derby and Burton NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers national hospital admission, critical care and death registration records for patients in England with COVID-19. It is for studying whether COVID-19 deaths and acute kidney injury differ between regions, and which factors, such as age, gender, ethnicity and other health conditions, are linked to them. The main intended benefit is helping NHS trusts and regions understand and reduce unwanted variation in outcomes.

DARS-NIC-392001-G1C3D.summary: Dudley Metropolitan Borough Council's agreement covers the use of pseudonymised hospital data, including Hospital Episode Statistics and emergency care records, for its public health work. The agreement allows analysis of local health needs, inequalities and demand for services to support needs assessments, health strategies, commissioning and advice to NHS commissioners. Reported uses include analyses that fed into a Mental Health Needs Assessment, a local commissioning strategy and commissioning policy for a medicine.

DARS-NIC-392012-L7T4Q.summary: Nottingham University Hospitals NHS Trust's agreement covers Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care data on about 2,900 of its patients who had a total hip replacement with a collarless polished taper stem. The agreement allows research to identify how many of these patients later suffered a fracture around the replacement, to give a clear fracture rate for this stem. The main intended benefit is helping clinicians and policy-makers decide whether to keep using this implant.

DARS-NIC-392106-F2M3L.summary: Hertfordshire County Council's public health team's agreement covers hospital records on admissions, outpatients, critical care and accident and emergency or emergency care visits. The data is for its public health duties, including needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, the annual public health report and advice to NHS commissioners. The aim is locally focused analysis of health and health inequalities. So far, the data has been used to give falls admissions data to a local charity and to analyse under 18 mental health admissions for a council panel.

DARS-NIC-392201-S6C3W.summary: Dr Foster Limited, trading as Telstra Health UK, is permitted under its agreement to use hospital admissions, outpatient, emergency care, critical care and death registration data to provide analysis and benchmarking tools to NHS and other health organisations. The data is for comparing quality, mortality, length of stay and efficiency, with the aim of improving patient care. Reported results include Trusts having used its analysis in mortality monitoring and care pathway improvement, and published reports such as one on COVID-19 and cancer surgery.

DARS-NIC-392244-H3M3G.summary: Hull and East Yorkshire Hospitals NHS Trust's agreement allows it to use Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) cause of death and current status reports for a study of people with Type 2 diabetes. The study examines how body weight relates to cardiovascular disease and death, including what patients died from. It aims to improve understanding and treatment of the risks linked to weight in diabetes.

DARS-NIC-392341-F3R0B.summary: NHS Bedfordshire, Luton and Milton Keynes ICB's agreement covers pseudonymised GP record data on diagnoses, medications, tests, treatments and vaccinations, collected for COVID-19 pandemic planning and research. The agreement allows the data to be used to plan local health care, including analysing missed appointments, identifying patients at risk of hospital admission and allocating resources. The main intended benefit is helping commissioners manage demand and capacity and make better decisions to support patients.

DARS-NIC-392342-C3Y7R.summary: The University of Sheffield, an academic organisation, is allowed under the agreement to hold hospital and civil registration (death) records on emergency care, admissions and deaths, and may retain them after its study ends. The study looked at how closing five Emergency Departments in England between 2009 and 2011 affected local death patterns and emergency care activity. The data is for giving the public, the NHS and policymakers evidence for future closure decisions. The findings have been published in a journal article and an NIHR research report.

DARS-NIC-39243-P6P6J.summary: Wigan Metropolitan Borough Council's agreement covers civil registration data on births and deaths, plus primary care mortality data, which includes identifiable details. The agreement allows the data to be used to understand local health needs, plan services, protect public health and support suicide audits, with published outputs limited to aggregated figures. The main intended benefit is local services tailored to areas of greatest need, helping to reduce premature deaths and health inequalities. Reported uses so far include aggregated analysis of where deaths occur, Covid-19 analysis, and work to enhance the local suicide audit.

DARS-NIC-392669-T1F8B.summary: The University of Oxford's agreement covers hospital, emergency care, death registration and national heart audit records on adults who had heart bypass or heart valve surgery and joined its Ox-HVF research cohort. The data is for identifying blood, genetic and imaging markers that predict heart disease outcomes, with the aim of spotting at-risk patients and improving survival. Reported benefits include published studies on a fat-based imaging marker for heart attack risk, which has been included in clinical guidance.

DARS-NIC-392678-N5J1S.summary: The Institute for Fiscal Studies (IFS) agreement covers a bespoke extract of Patient Reported Outcome Measures (PROMS) data. The data is for several research projects on NHS care in England. These cover patient choice of maternity hospital, a model for simulating future policies, healthcare spending over a lifetime, the effect of independent providers on joint replacements, and demand for NHS services in areas with many foreign-born residents. It also includes a comparison of heart treatment spending with the US.

DARS-NIC-392690-F7H2Q.summary: The University of Oxford's Big Health Data Group's agreement covers extracts of patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) data and linked Hospital Episode Statistics (HES) inpatient data on people who had hip or knee surgery since 2009. The data is for a National Institute for Health Research-funded study to identify scoring thresholds for selecting candidates for joint replacement. The main output is the ACHE tool, a clinical tool to help clinicians and patients decide about referral and surgery.

DARS-NIC-392904-Y8N1Y.summary: Beacon Consulting, whose work is described under the name Meditrends Ltd, is permitted to use Hospital Episode Statistics (HES) extracts covering critical care, inpatient and outpatient records. The agreement allows analysis for pharmaceutical and medical device clients, to help them anticipate demand and understand disease patterns, treatment pathways and costs. The data may also be used to update a free website of national-level analyses for patients and healthcare professionals. The stated aim is to help new treatments reach the NHS more effectively.

DARS-NIC-39315-W4J4J.summary: North Lincolnshire Council's agreement covers identifiable birth and death registration data, plus primary care mortality data, to understand local public health needs. The agreement allows the data to be used for measuring health needs, planning services, and work such as suicide audits and prevention. The aim is to target services and reduce premature deaths and health inequalities. The data is for producing population, ward, locality and health inequality profiles, and for informing its suicide prevention strategy.

DARS-NIC-393384-L9Z2J.summary: The Royal National Orthopaedic Hospital NHS Trust's agreement covers the use of Hospital Episode Statistics (HES) inpatient and critical care data for the Getting It Right First Time (GIRFT) programme. The data is for calculating activity and quality measures for 10 surgical specialties, at hospital and clinical commissioning group level. These measures support peer-to-peer reviews of clinical practice and surgical performance, and feed into a performance dashboard and reports.

DARS-NIC-393388-Y4J4G.summary: Northumberland, Tyne and Wear NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers a bespoke extract from the Mental Health and Learning Disabilities Data Set, which will not be linked to any other data. The agreement allows the Trust to carry out statistical analysis to see whether scores on the Health of the Nation Outcome Scales (HoNOS) and mental health cluster data are related to patient prognosis. The release register describes how people experiencing psychosis use a large share of mental health resources.

DARS-NIC-393510-D6H1D.summary: University College London's Children and Families Policy Research Unit's agreement covers the use of linked NHS hospital, community, maternity, mental health, birth, death and COVID-19 testing records to study how children and young people use health services and what outcomes follow. The agreement allows the data to inform policy and practice for children's health and to reduce future pressure on the NHS. So far, the work has produced published papers, including one on hospital admissions as young people with learning disabilities or autism move to adult services, and a policy briefing.

DARS-NIC-393518-S1R6D.summary: West Sussex County Council's agreement covers pseudonymised Hospital Episode Statistics data for accident and emergency, inpatient and outpatient care. The data is for its public health duties, including needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, the annual public health report and advice to NHS commissioners. The stated benefit is more locally focused analysis of health outcomes, including health inequalities, so that local health challenges, particularly for the most disadvantaged, are identified and responded to.

DARS-NIC-393650-B7J6F.summary: The Department of Health and Social Care's agreement covers demographic data, including names and contact details of people aged 5 and over, so Ipsos MORI can invite a random sample to take part in the Imperial College London REACT-1 COVID-19 testing study. The study estimates infection rates and the R value across England, regionally and locally. Reported results include informing lockdown and tier decisions, and being used in government briefings.

DARS-NIC-393853-V6F2F.summary: Bristol City Council's public health team's agreement covers hospital records (Hospital Episode Statistics covering admitted care, A&E, critical care and outpatients) and Emergency Care Data Set data. The data is for analysing local health needs and inequalities, supporting its statutory public health duties, such as needs assessments, strategies and advice to NHS commissioners. Reported uses so far include informing children's centre programmes, road traffic injury and self-harm work, and homelessness and school health profiles.

DARS-NIC-394183-K3Q7F.summary: Sefton Metropolitan Borough Council's public health team's agreement covers hospital records for admissions, outpatients, critical care and accident and emergency (A&E) or emergency care. The data is for analysing local health needs and inequalities, and for supporting its statutory public health duties, including needs assessments, strategies and advice to NHS commissioners. The aim is to make local services more targeted and responsive. The data has fed ward-level figures for the Substance Use needs assessment and reporting to the Combatting Drug Partnership.

DARS-NIC-394285-D0L6M.summary: Suffolk County Council's agreement covers pseudonymised GP record data on diagnoses, medications, tests, treatments and vaccinations, along with ethnic category and vaccination status data. The agreement allows the data to support the council's local COVID-19 response, including outbreak management, spotting health inequalities and analysing vaccine uptake. The main intended benefit is identifying people at highest risk and targeting action to control the spread of the virus.

DARS-NIC-39439-F6D6Y.summary: NHS West Suffolk CCG's agreement covers hospital, ambulance, community, mental health and other health service data, linked at NHS number level with GP data. The agreement allows North of England Commissioning Support Unit to use it for risk stratification, which identifies patients at high risk of needing more care. This allows the CCG to plan services and lets GPs target support. The stated aim is better commissioning and patient experience, including fewer avoidable emergency admissions.

DARS-NIC-394629-C5Z4P.summary: The University of Aberdeen's agreement covers the use of hospital admitted patient care and outpatient records (Hospital Episode Statistics) for the eTHoS trial, which compares two operations for removing haemorrhoids. The readmission data will help measure long-term safety, recurrence of haemorrhoids and costs to the NHS. The main intended benefit is robust evidence on which operation works best and is most cost effective, so surgeons and NHS Trusts can choose treatments.

DARS-NIC-395236-V3W9P.summary: The Department of Health and Social Care, through the Office for Health Improvement and Disparities, has an agreement covering Cardiovascular Disease Prevention Audit data, linked with hospital admissions and death registration records. The agreement allows the data to be used for detailed analysis to support government and NHS England policy, including the health mission to cut deaths from heart attack and stroke, and to support NICE guidance. The work is expected to strengthen the evidence on preventing cardiovascular disease. Earlier work produced a national report, published annually, and an interactive dashboard, published quarterly.

DARS-NIC-39553-K5V4H.summary: London Borough of Richmond upon Thames's agreement covers civil registration data on births and deaths, plus Primary Care Mortality Data, which includes identifiable details. The agreement allows the data to be used to understand local health needs, plan services and support public health work such as suicide prevention. The aim is to tailor local services and reduce mortality and health inequalities. Reported uses include Covid-19 death analysis for the Joint Strategic Needs Assessment and end of life care monitoring.

DARS-NIC-396095-H1P1D.summary: NHS Cheshire and Merseyside Integrated Care Board's agreement allows it to use pseudonymised, person-level health data from hospital, community, mental health, primary care and registration sources. The data is for COVID-19 analytics, including dashboards and reports that support recovery planning and target care to vulnerable people. The main intended benefit is better-planned services and improved patient outcomes. Reported results include an enhanced case-finding tool for clinicians and an elective recovery waiting list tool.

DARS-NIC-396113-N9L4L.summary: Imperial College London's agreement covers the use of GP records for pandemic planning and research, death registration records and virtual ward pilot data. The data is for evaluating whether monitoring suspected COVID-19 patients at home with remote checks, such as oxygen levels, can improve outcomes and reduce hospital use. The evaluation informed NHS England's Covid Oximetry at Home programme, including its 14-day monitoring period and oxygen saturation thresholds, and a pre-print paper has been published.

DARS-NIC-396119-C8W3W.summary: The University of Oxford's agreement covers NHS data on COVID-19 hospital admissions, first positive COVID-19 test results and civil registrations of death for its RAPTOR-C19 study. The study compares new rapid point-of-care COVID-19 tests with laboratory tests in GP practices, to see how accurate they are. Linking the data aims to give more accurate estimates of test accuracy. The university has already used the linked hospital data to build this improved reference standard.

DARS-NIC-396423-H4Z6Z.summary: The University of Oxford's agreement covers use of details from NHS Digital's Permission to Contact service, which holds information given voluntarily by people who agreed to be contacted about COVID-19 vaccine trials. The agreement allows the University to invite potentially eligible people to take part in its COVID-19 vaccine trial. The main intended benefit is faster, more transparent recruitment, helping speed the development of an effective vaccine.

DARS-NIC-39719-F8X6K.summary: Leicester City Council's agreement covers civil registration births and deaths data and primary care mortality data, including identifiable details. The data is for understanding local health needs, planning services and supporting suicide prevention, with published results being aggregated statistics. The aim is to adjust local services to reduce deaths and health inequalities. Reported results include updated needs assessments, targeted Covid-19 messaging and vaccination, and input to the 0-19s Healthy Child Programme service specification.

DARS-NIC-397618-T8L8Z.summary: NHS England's agreement covers the use of Community-Local Provider Flows data, linked to pseudonymised GP records inside the OpenSAFELY secure analytics platform, so that approved researchers can study COVID-19. The data is for examining how high cost drugs relate to COVID-19 outcomes and for helping identify who is at highest risk. Reported results include informing policy on shielding and vaccine prioritisation, and adding to the evidence on how several drugs are associated with COVID-19.

DARS-NIC-39782-Z8J2T.summary: London Borough of Newham's agreement covers its use of Hospital Episode Statistics data for accident and emergency, admitted patient care, critical care and outpatients. The data is for its public health work, including needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, the Director of Public Health's annual report, and advice to NHS commissioners. The main intended benefit is locally focused analysis of health outcomes and inequalities, so that the needs of the most disadvantaged residents are identified and addressed.

DARS-NIC-39816-L3W3Z.summary: Nottinghamshire County Council's agreement covers civil registration births and deaths data, plus primary care mortality data, which includes identifiable details. The data is for understanding local health needs, planning public health services, and supporting work such as suicide audits and prevention. The aim is to tailor services to local needs and reduce health inequalities and premature deaths. Reported results include monitoring excess deaths during COVID-19 and local analysis of life expectancy and avoidable deaths.

DARS-NIC-398405-S0M4K.summary: The London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine's agreement covers hospital admission records and death registration data for about 5,000 older adults in the CRASH-4 trial. The data is for testing whether an early tranexamic acid injection helps people with mild traumatic brain injury, by tracking deaths, dementia and other outcomes for one year after joining. The expected benefit is reliable evidence to inform clinical guidelines and the care of older adults with this injury.

DARS-NIC-39848-B4R9P.summary: Medway Council's agreement covers civil registration data on births and deaths, plus primary care mortality data, which includes identifiable details. The data is for assessing local health needs, planning public health services and supporting work such as suicide prevention, with published results limited to aggregated figures. The main aim is to tailor local services to reduce mortality and health inequalities. Reported results include local area and health inequalities profiles, which informed a population health needs assessment and the local Integrated Care Strategy.

DARS-NIC-398666-H2S4K.summary: NHS Leicester, Leicestershire and Rutland ICB's agreement, with three local clinical commissioning groups (CCGs) and three councils, covers the use of pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, social care and other health data. The data is for planning and commissioning health services for the local population and for supporting public health work. The stated benefits include better service planning, fewer avoidable emergency readmissions and reduced health inequalities. The CCGs have published 2020/21 annual reports describing achievements, some of which relied on this data.

DARS-NIC-399287-T3X7W.summary: The Intensive Care National Audit & Research Centre (ICNARC)'s agreement covers the use of NHS England death registration, emergency care and hospital admission and outpatient records for children in two randomised trials. The trials compare two kinds of breathing support, high flow nasal cannula and continuous positive airway pressure, in critically ill children. The aim is to give evidence on which works better and costs less as first-line support. Results have been published in the Journal of the American Medical Association for both trials.

DARS-NIC-39944-D4M0D.summary: Imperial College London's agreement covers the use of Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care data, which records hospital admissions. The data is for testing data science methods, such as artificial neural networks, to predict which patients are at risk of emergency admission more accurately than linear regression models. The aim is to help GPs target care at those who need it most, possibly through a software tool or manual for the NHS.

DARS-NIC-399787-Z7T4V.summary: NHS Bedfordshire, Luton and Milton Keynes ICB's agreement covers pseudonymised GP record data (coded health details, with no free text) collected for COVID-19 pandemic planning and research. The agreement allows the data to support the local COVID-19 response, including analysing missed appointments, identifying patients at risk of hospital admission, and deciding where to allocate resources. The main intended benefit is helping commissioners manage demand and capacity and make better decisions to support patients.

DARS-NIC-399791-K3C6F.summary: NHS North Central London ICB's agreement covers pseudonymised (identifying details removed) GP record data, ethnic category data and COVID-19 vaccination status data. The agreement allows the data to be used to plan local health services, model which patients are at risk, allocate resources and monitor vaccine take-up during the COVID-19 response. The main intended benefit is helping commissioners manage demand and capacity and make better decisions for patients. The CCGs' annual reports describe pandemic response work that this data supported.

DARS-NIC-399796-Z4Q9K.summary: NHS Northamptonshire ICB, a sub-ICB location, may use pseudonymised GP record data, ethnic category data and COVID-19 vaccination status data. The agreement allows the data to be used to plan local health services, assess risk and allocate resources during the COVID-19 response. The aim is to help commissioners manage demand and capacity and make better decisions for patients. The organisation reports that the data improved its understanding of demand, capacity and COVID-19 risks, and supported content in its annual reports.

DARS-NIC-399802-C7Y9D.summary: NHS North West London ICB, a sub-ICB location, is covered by an agreement allowing it to use pseudonymised GP record data on diagnoses, medications, tests, treatments and vaccinations, collected for pandemic planning and research. The agreement allows this data to plan local health care during the COVID-19 emergency, including analysing missed appointments, identifying patients at risk of hospital admission and deciding where to allocate resources. The main intended benefit is helping manage demand and capacity and supporting better commissioning decisions.

DARS-NIC-399806-Q4L9C.summary: NHS Surrey Heartlands Integrated Care Board (ICB)'s agreement covers pseudonymised COVID-19 data, including GP record data, ethnic category and vaccination status. The data is for planning local health care, forecasting demand, identifying patients at risk, allocating resources and monitoring vaccine uptake. The main intended benefit is better commissioning decisions and a more effective response to the outbreak. The CCG's annual reports describe pandemic response work supported by this data.

DARS-NIC-399808-H3X8Q.summary: NHS South West London Integrated Care Board (ICB) agreement covers the use of pseudonymised GP record data, ethnic category data and COVID-19 vaccination data. The agreement allows the data to be used to plan local health services during the COVID-19 emergency, including analysing missed appointments, identifying patients at risk of hospital admission, allocating resources and monitoring vaccine rollout. The main intended benefit is helping commissioners manage demand and capacity and make better decisions for patients. The CCGs' annual reports describe pandemic response work supported by this data.

The main intended benefit is helping commissioners manage demand and capacity in response to COVID-19. The CCGs' published annual reports describe pandemic response work that this data supported.

DARS-NIC-400304-S1P1B.summary: The Office for National Statistics (ONS)'s agreement allows use of identifiable NHS hospital, emergency care, GP, mental health therapy, birth and demographic records. It allows linking them to study how COVID-19 affected disadvantaged groups, including employment and benefits outcomes, and to answer COVID inquiry queries. The aim is to give government better evidence for its pandemic response. ONS reported a completed project on long-term conditions and employment outcomes, due to be published.

DARS-NIC-400790-V0Y8W.summary: The University of Leicester's agreement covers linked, pseudonymised hospital, emergency care and death registration records for children in England and Wales. It allows study of what happens to children in their first two years when they move between neonatal and paediatric care. The data is for preparing families for neonatal discharge and informing discharge policy and service planning. One paper on paediatric intensive care admission risk in very preterm babies has been published, and a national group is drafting discharge guidance using the findings.

DARS-NIC-400985-V3D1C.summary: Barts Health NHS Trust's agreement covers hospital, emergency care, death registration and COVID-19 surveillance records for surgical patients in England. The data is for studying how COVID-19 and delays to surgery have affected deaths and complications, including differences by region, ethnicity and deprivation. The agreement allows the findings to help policymakers plan the recovery of surgical services. Published papers have already described a fall in surgical activity and a higher risk of death for surgical patients with COVID-19, informing national health policy.

DARS-NIC-401171-F9Z8T.summary: The National Institute for Health Research's agreement covers the use of Permission to Contact data, which is contact and eligibility details from people who volunteered to hear about COVID-19 vaccine trials. The agreement allows the data to be used to invite potentially eligible people to join a Phase 3 trial of the Novavax vaccine run by St George's University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust. The main intended benefit is faster recruitment, helping a vaccine become available sooner.

DARS-NIC-401890-W6Q8W.summary: Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers pseudonymised hospital, emergency care and death registration records for patients with compatible Medtronic implanted cardiac devices who have consented to take part. The data is for studying the workload of the Triage-HF Plus pathway, where remote device risk scores prompt phone calls to patients at high risk of worsening heart failure. The aim is to help providers judge the effects of changing clinical workflows. Preliminary results have appeared in a peer-reviewed paper and contributed to NICE guidance published in 2024.

DARS-NIC-401935-N9W7P.summary: East Anglian Air Ambulance's agreement covers pseudonymised hospital admission, critical care and emergency care records for about 1,600 patients it treated in 2021/22. The agreement allows these records to be linked to its own patient records to evaluate its care across the whole patient pathway, including diagnoses and outcomes. The aim is to find ways to improve care for future patients. The linked data was used to quantify secondary hospital transfers, work that won a prize at the 999 EMS Research Forum in 2024, and to evaluate a new intracranial bleeding pathway.

DARS-NIC-402080-N3V5Z.summary: The University of Exeter, working with the University of Cambridge, is using the names and contact details of people who took part in the Mental Health of Children and Young People surveys in 2020 and 2021. They will invite parents and young people to follow-up interviews about how Covid-19 affected mental health, education, access to services, special educational needs and disabilities, and eating disorders. The aim is to produce reports and briefings to help plan services and prepare for any future pandemic. Early findings have been presented at talks and conferences and in a participant newsletter.

DARS-NIC-402116-G1T7V.summary: The Health & Social Care Information Centre's agreement covers ethnic category data drawn from GP records and hospital records (inpatient, outpatient and accident and emergency). The agreement allows this data to be linked to existing systems to support the NHS England national call/recall flu vaccination programme. The data is for identifying COVID patients at high risk and for reporting on vaccine uptake by ethnic category, to address health inequalities. The aim is to reduce winter pressure on the NHS and help coordinate flu and COVID-19 vaccinations.

DARS-NIC-404798-C1Z9R.summary: NatCen Social Research's agreement covers survey data on the mental health of children and young people in England, from the 2017 survey and a 2020 follow-up of the same young people. DARS-NIC-409610-J6L1F.summary: The University of Oxford's agreement covers NHS England hospital, emergency care, death registration, COVID-19 hospitalisation and dispensed medicines data. DARS-NIC-412777-Z2J9N.summary: NHS Hampshire and Isle of Wight ICB (Portsmouth area)'s agreement covers the use of hospital activity data (SUS for Commissioners), linked with GP data at NHS number level, for risk stratification. DARS-NIC-414067-K8R6J.summary: Our Future Health, a charity, may use, under an NHS England data sharing agreement, NHS England data that identifies potential participants so it can post them invitations to join its health research programme. DARS-NIC-414309-R7H4W.summary: University College London (UCL)'s agreement covers identifiable hospital, emergency care, outpatient, critical care, cancer registration and death records for 497 English patients who joined the EUROGOLF study in 1998 to 2000. DARS-NIC-41477-N2G4S.summary: NHS Lancashire and South Cumbria ICB's agreement, covering the former Blackburn with Darwen CCG area, allows use of hospital, mental health, community and other health service data, mostly pseudonymised. The data is for checking provider invoices, identifying patients at high risk of poor health so GPs can target care, and supporting planning of health services. The main intended benefit is more accurate payments and more effective commissioning, leading to better patient experience and health outcomes.

DARS-NIC-414909-M5W6W.summary: The University of Oxford's agreement covers the use of hospital admissions records and death registration records for a pilot clinical trial called ATEMPT. The trial would involve about 200 people aged 65 or over with several long-term conditions or many medicines. It compares having more or fewer blood pressure-lowering drugs, to see how well this works, how safe it is and how acceptable it is to patients. The main intended benefit is better understanding of blood pressure management in this group, helping to plan a larger trial.

DARS-NIC-415025-V8S5S.summary: The Somerset, Wiltshire, Avon and Gloucestershire Cancer Alliance, a network of local health leaders, is covered by an agreement that allows it to use national Cancer Waiting Times data, which tracks how long patients wait for cancer diagnosis and treatment. The agreement allows analysis of waiting times and variation between providers to improve cancer pathways, with the aim of better survival and patient experience. Reported benefits include reports on delays in referrals between hospital trusts and on compliance with the 28-day faster diagnosis standard.

DARS-NIC-41506-S6K3P.summary: NHS Staffordshire and Stoke-on-Trent ICB's agreement, for the former Cannock Chase CCG area, allows hospital activity data (SUS for Commissioners) to be used, with Midlands and Lancashire Commissioning Support Unit carrying out the work. The data is for checking that provider invoices relate to patients the commissioner is responsible for, and for identifying patients at high risk so their care can be planned. The main intended benefit is accurate payment and better targeted care, reducing avoidable emergency admissions.

DARS-NIC-41508-M6M3K.summary: NHS Staffordshire and Stoke-on-Trent ICB (North Staffordshire area) uses hospital activity data from Secondary User Services, which is pseudonymised for invoice checking and linked to GP data using NHS numbers for risk stratification. The main intended benefits are accurate payment for care and earlier, better targeted support for vulnerable patients.

The data is for checking provider invoices, identifying patients at high risk of poor health so their care can be managed earlier, and planning and monitoring health services. DARS-NIC-41537-D0P0M.summary: NHS Telford and Wrekin Clinical Commissioning Group (CCG) uses hospital, mental health, community, maternity and other health service data, some identifiable by NHS number and some pseudonymised. The main intended benefits are accurate payment for care and earlier, better-targeted support for vulnerable patients.

DARS-NIC-41541-S0F4G.summary: NHS Lancashire North CCG's agreement covers linked, pseudonymised hospital, mental health, maternity, community and other health service data about people in its area. The data is for producing reports, dashboards and analysis, including readmissions, budgets down to GP practice level, and monitoring of provider quality and activity. The aim is to support commissioning of health services that meet the health needs of the local population.

DARS-NIC-41543-R8Q9Q.summary: NHS Shropshire CCG (Clinical Commissioning Group)'s agreement covers hospital activity data (the Secondary Uses Service), mental health, maternity and community data, and local provider data, some of it identifiable by NHS number. The agreement allows Midlands and Lancashire Commissioning Support Unit to use the data to validate invoices, identify patients at high risk of needing care, and support commissioning of health services. The main intended benefit is better planning and more effective commissioning, leading to improved patient experience.

The data is for checking provider invoices, identifying patients at high risk of poor health, and planning and monitoring commissioned services. The main intended benefit is that providers are paid accurately, care is better targeted and services are commissioned more effectively.

DARS-NIC-41556-H6V2V.summary: NHS Lancashire and South Cumbria ICB's agreement covers hospital, mental health, community and other health service data, mostly pseudonymised, with some identifiable by NHS number. DARS-NIC-41576-W2B4Q.summary: NHS Thurrock CCG's agreement covers hospital, mental health, community and other health service activity data, including Secondary User Services (SUS+) data that can be identified by NHS number. DARS-NIC-41597-J6M1R.summary: City of Wolverhampton Council's agreement covers civil registration data on births and deaths, plus primary care mortality data, which includes identifiable details. The data is for understanding local health needs, planning public health services and supporting work such as suicide prevention audits. The aim is for health and care services to be tailored to areas of greatest need, helping to reduce health inequalities and premature deaths. The data informed the Director of Public Health's 2022 annual report and an analysis of causes and place of death after COVID-19.

DARS-NIC-41605-Q7C3C.summary: NHS Lancashire and South Cumbria ICB (a sub-ICB location, formerly West Lancashire CCG)'s agreement covers hospital, mental health, community and other NHS activity data, some identifiable by NHS number and some pseudonymised. DARS-NIC-416308-H6X4N.summary: NHS Bedfordshire, Luton and Milton Keynes ICB's agreement covers pseudonymised GP record data, covering diagnoses, medications, tests, treatments and vaccinations, collected for pandemic planning and research. The agreement allows the data to support the local COVID-19 response, including analysing missed appointments, identifying patients at risk of hospital admission and planning how to allocate resources. The main intended benefit is helping commissioners manage demand and capacity and make better decisions to support patients.

DARS-NIC-41632-C6X9D.summary: NHS Camden Clinical Commissioning Group (CCG) uses hospital, mental health, community and other local health service data, some of it identifiable by NHS number and some pseudonymised.
