DARS-NIC-41640-G0C5N.summary: NHS Enfield CCG's agreement covers hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other NHS activity data, some identifiable by NHS number and most pseudonymised. The data is for checking provider invoices and for planning and commissioning health services for the local population, with North East London Commissioning Support Unit carrying out the processing. The main intended benefits are better financial control and improved planning, access and quality of services.

DARS-NIC-41646-V9N9J.summary: NHS North East London ICB (Redbridge area) is permitted under its agreement to use Secondary User Services (SUS+) hospital activity data, identifiable by NHS number, for two purposes. The first is checking provider invoices, so that it pays only for care it is responsible for. The second is risk stratification: linking the data with GP records to score which patients are at high risk, so that GPs and commissioners can target care and reduce avoidable admissions.

DARS-NIC-416549-K7D3J.summary: NHS West Yorkshire ICB (a Sub ICB Location) is permitted to use pseudonymised GP record data, ethnicity data and COVID-19 vaccination status data. The agreement allows the data to be used to plan local health services, model patient risk, allocate resources and monitor the effects of COVID-19, including vaccine take-up. The main intended benefit is better decisions on demand, capacity and resources. The CCGs have published annual reports describing their pandemic response, which this data supported.

DARS-NIC-41691-F5D8L.summary: London Borough of Merton's agreement covers civil registration data on births and deaths, plus primary care mortality data, which includes identifiable details. The agreement allows the data to be used to understand local health needs, support public health work such as suicide prevention, and produce aggregated statistics for health assessments and strategies. The aim is to tailor local services and reduce health inequalities. The data has already fed Merton's health needs assessments, Joint Strategic Needs Assessments, ward health profiles and a suicide and self-harm profile.

DARS-NIC-41730-G3J5W.summary: Wakefield Metropolitan District Council's agreement covers civil registration data on births and deaths, plus primary care mortality data, which includes identifiable details. The data is for understanding local health needs, planning services and supporting work such as suicide prevention audits, with the aim of tailoring services to reduce premature deaths and health inequalities. Reported results include analysis of seasonal and extreme heat deaths, which led to proactive work promoting ways to deal with extreme heat.

DARS-NIC-418208-J1Y6J.summary: Valneva Austria GmbH, a commercial company, has an agreement covering Permission to Contact data: details of people who signed up on nhs.uk to be approached about COVID-19 vaccine trials. Under the agreement, NHS Digital, acting as data processor, is to invite potentially eligible people to join Valneva's trial comparing its VLA2001 vaccine with the AZD1222 vaccine in adults. The main intended benefit is faster, more transparent recruitment, helping speed the delivery of an effective vaccine.

DARS-NIC-418444-H4X4L.summary: NHS Greater Manchester ICB, working with Bury Metropolitan Borough Council, may use pseudonymised health and adult social care data, including hospital, community, mental health, maternity and death records. The agreement allows it to link this data to plan, commission and monitor joined-up health and care services across Bury, aiming to improve population health outcomes. Reported benefits include commissioning data used to plan a new Urgent Treatment Centre at Fairfield General Hospital, and NHS Digital data that informed the response to endoscopy waiting times.

DARS-NIC-419335-H5P8T.summary: The University of Oxford is using linked hospital, emergency care, maternity, vaccination and death registration records for patients treated in intensive care units (ICUs). It is studying the risk of death, emergency hospital readmission, heart attacks and strokes in the year after discharge for people treated for COVID-19, compared with those treated for other conditions. The aim is to help clinicians and patients understand long-term risks and how follow-up care might improve. So far, the study found that survivors of COVID-19 in the first wave were less likely to die or be readmitted than pre-pandemic ICU patients.
DARS-NIC-419335-H5P8T.retense_draft: The University of Oxford's agreement covers linked hospital, emergency care, maternity, vaccination and death registration records for patients treated in intensive care units (ICUs). The data is for studying the risk of death, emergency hospital readmission, heart attacks and strokes in the year after discharge for people treated for COVID-19, compared with those treated for other conditions. The aim is to help clinicians and patients understand long-term risks and how follow-up care might improve. The study found that survivors of COVID-19 in the first wave were less likely to die or be readmitted than pre-pandemic ICU patients.

DARS-NIC-419453-G3G1G.summary: University College London (UCL)'s agreement covers the use of pseudonymised Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care data. The data is for comparing methods for creating synthetic datasets, which are artificial data that resemble the original but contain no real individuals. The main intended benefit is evidence and guidelines to help data providers decide whether synthetic health data could speed up and streamline researchers' access to data.

DARS-NIC-41957-W5S6T.summary: The London Borough of Barking and Dagenham, a local authority, is covered by an agreement allowing it to receive Hospital Episode Statistics and Emergency Care Data Set records covering hospital admissions, A&E, outpatients and critical care. The agreement allows its public health team to use them to support its public health duties, including needs assessments, health strategies, and advice to NHS commissioners, so that it can analyse local health and inequalities. Previously, the data fed into locality profiles on emergency admissions, which were shared with the local Integrated Care Steering Group.

DARS-NIC-420105-M8Y5X.summary: Novavax, Inc., a private healthcare company, has an agreement that allows identifiable details of its UK vaccine trial participants to be linked by NHS Digital to non-hospital (Pillar 2) COVID-19 test results. The data is for matching each participant's self-swab PCR result to them accurately, so the trial can measure how well the Novavax vaccine prevents COVID-19. The stated benefit is faster, more reliable evaluation, helping bring another effective vaccine to the UK population.

DARS-NIC-420168-K4N1F.summary: The University of Bristol, through the UK Longitudinal Linkage Collaboration, agreement covers linked NHS health records, including hospital, GP, mental health, COVID-19 testing, vaccination and death data, alongside data from UK longitudinal population studies. The data is for Covid-19 research on the pandemic's effects on health and wellbeing. The aim is to give policy makers rapid evidence. Findings have already informed NICE long COVID guidance, an NHS enhanced service specification for GPs and SAGE reports.

DARS-NIC-420229-G9H9S.summary: The University of Bristol's agreement covers linked NHS health records, including hospital, GP-related, mental health, maternity, cancer, death and COVID-19 data, for the UK Longitudinal Linkage Collaboration. The agreement allows a secure research database that links records to long-running population study data, for health research that relies on section 251 support rather than consent. The data is for evidence to inform health and care policy. Published research from it has been presented to NICE and SAGE and has informed Health & Safety Executive policy.

DARS-NIC-420710-X0H1P.summary: The Office for National Statistics (ONS) is using linked hospital, GP, emergency care and COVID-19 vaccination records, combined with 2011 Census and death data. It is creating an anonymised version of this dataset for approved researchers to use in a secure environment for COVID-19 research. The aim is better evidence for public health decisions. Reported results include Cabinet Office findings on ethnicity and deprivation that informed pandemic service decisions, and research that led to policy recommendations.
DARS-NIC-420710-X0H1P.retense_draft: The Office for National Statistics's agreement covers linked hospital, GP, emergency care and COVID-19 vaccination records, combined with 2011 Census and death data. The agreement allows the creation of an anonymised version of this dataset for approved researchers to use in a secure environment for COVID-19 research. The aim is better evidence for public health decisions. Reported results include Cabinet Office findings on ethnicity and deprivation that informed pandemic service decisions, and research that led to policy recommendations.

DARS-NIC-421524-R0Y3P.summary: Imperial College London's agreement covers the use of patient-level pseudonymised NHS data on Covid-19 testing, hospital care, deaths and the COVID Oximetry @ Home (CO@H) remote monitoring service. The agreement allows the data to be used to evaluate how safe, effective and equitable CO@H is, to inform national policy on home oximetry. Monthly interim reports have guided the programme's rollout, and preprint papers and a conference presentation have been produced.

DARS-NIC-421528-J6S3N.summary: The Health Foundation, a charity, is licensed to use linked NHS data on COVID-19 tests, GP records, hospital and emergency care, deaths and the shielded patient list. The agreement allows it to evaluate the national COVID Oximetry at Home programme, in which patients monitor their own oxygen levels at home. The aim is to show the programme's health and safety outcomes and fairness of access, to guide how it is run and improved. Interim analyses have been shared internally with partners in NHSX, NHS England and NHS Digital.

DARS-NIC-421602-N3B0X.summary: Northwest Ehealth Limited, working for Novartis Pharmaceuticals UK Limited, holds hospital and emergency care records (Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set) for a primary care study of inclisiran, a cholesterol-lowering treatment given in a vaccine-like way. The records are used to analyse NHS costs and hospital use, and to check the published findings if they are challenged. The study aims to show the best way for the NHS to deliver inclisiran. Findings have so far improved understanding of point of care testing and its limits.

DARS-NIC-42177-M7K0J.summary: Nottingham City Council's agreement covers civil registration data on births and deaths, plus primary care mortality data, which includes identifiable details. The data is for measuring local health needs, planning services and supporting public health work such as suicide prevention and needs assessments. The aim is to tailor local services and reduce health inequalities and premature deaths. The agreement allows the data to be used in its Joint Strategic Needs Assessment dashboards and when commissioning a new integrated wellbeing service.

DARS-NIC-422044-Z5K5Q.summary: Health IQ Ltd, a commercial research consultancy, has an agreement covering civil registrations of death data linked to hospital records for patients diagnosed with beta-thalassaemia or myelodysplastic syndromes between 2015 and 2019. Funded by Bristol-Myers Squibb, the agreement allows it to describe patient treatment pathways, healthcare use, costs and survival, including cause and time of death. The intended benefit is evidence to inform treatment policy, resource allocation and a regulatory review of a drug.

DARS-NIC-422183-C3K9L.summary: NHS Bedfordshire, Luton and Milton Keynes ICB's agreement covers the use of hospital, community, mental health and other health and social care data, including identifiable NHS number-level data and pseudonymised data, to check provider invoices, identify patients at high risk of health deterioration, and plan health services. The main intended benefit is more effective commissioning, with accurate payments and better patient care. Reported results include a review of people with diabetes at highest risk during the Covid-19 pandemic and choosing the location of a new health centre.

DARS-NIC-422189-G8H5X.summary: NHS Hampshire and Isle of Wight ICB's agreement covers hospital, community, mental health, maternity, social care and other health data about patients in its area. The main intended benefit is that providers are paid accurately and services are commissioned more effectively. The CCG has also produced an annual report describing developments its data processing supported.

DARS-NIC-422195-G1Y7D.summary: NHS Frimley ICB, a sub-ICB location, is permitted to use hospital, community, mental health, social care and other health datasets, some identifiable and some pseudonymised. The agreement allows the data to be used to check provider invoices, identify patients at high risk of health deterioration, and plan and commission health services. The aim is accurate payment and more targeted, effective care. The CCG has produced an annual report outlining developments and achievements the data supported.

DARS-NIC-422200-Q1K7S.summary: NHS North East London ICB's agreement allows it to use patient-level hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other NHS data, some identifiable and some pseudonymised, for invoice validation, risk stratification and commissioning. The data is for checking that providers are paid correctly, identifying patients at risk of worse health so GPs can target care, and planning health services for the local population. The aim is more effective commissioning and better patient outcomes. Reported results include fewer undiagnosed diabetes cases in Barking and Dagenham and shorter hospital stays in Waltham Forest.

DARS-NIC-422205-F2Y2V.summary: NHS North West London ICB, which took over from the area's clinical commissioning group, has an agreement covering hospital, community, mental health, primary care, social care and civil registration data, some of it identifiable by NHS number. The aim is more effective commissioning and better patient outcomes. DARS-NIC-422207-N1D1V.summary: NHS Shropshire, Telford and Wrekin ICB, a sub-ICB location, is covered by an agreement that allows it to use hospital, mental health, community, maternity, GP-linked and other health datasets, some identifiable by NHS number and some pseudonymised. DARS-NIC-422221-W0P7K.summary: NHS West Yorkshire ICB (a sub-ICB location)'s agreement allows it to use hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other health service data, some identifiable by NHS number and some pseudonymised. The data is for checking provider invoices, identifying patients at high risk of health deterioration, and planning and monitoring the commissioning of health services for its population. The main intended benefit is more effective commissioning, with accurate payment of providers and better targeted care.

DARS-NIC-42272-S9J3L.summary: The National Institute for Cardiovascular Outcomes Research, an academic body, is permitted to use hospital-level Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care data. The agreement allows it to compare these figures with the records hospitals submit to the National Heart Failure Audit, to check how fully each hospital takes part and to support the audit's annual report. The audit aims to improve the diagnosis, treatment and outcomes of heart failure patients. NHS England already uses the audit data to support the Best Practice Tariff, a payment incentive for specialist heart failure care introduced in April 2015.

DARS-NIC-422971-B8P2V.summary: Imperial College London, an academic organisation, is authorised to use COVID-19 General Practice Extraction Service (GPES) Data for Pandemic Planning and Research (GDPPR). The work is a service evaluation for NHS England. It examines whether open invitations to book breast screening, introduced in London during COVID-19, affect attendance and widen inequalities compared with timed appointments. The aim is to help screening services tailor resources and decide whether to change their invitation policy.

DARS-NIC-42321-K7G1C.summary: Cardiff University's agreement covers linked hospital, mental health, psychological therapies and mortality data about children and young people in England. It is part of a national review with Swansea University, commissioned by the Healthcare Quality Improvement Partnership. The agreement allows the study to look at hospital use, the reasons for admission and the move to adult services for young people with cerebral palsy or adolescent mental health conditions. The main intended benefit is to highlight gaps in care so services can improve.

DARS-NIC-423551-K2C4H.summary: NHS Cheshire and Merseyside ICB, covering the former Halton and Warrington clinical commissioning groups (CCGs), is permitted to use pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, maternity, social care, prescribing and death and birth records. The data is for planning and commissioning health services for the local population, including identifying patients at risk of admission and reviewing service demand. The aim is better-designed services and outcomes. The CCGs reported using the data to find duplicated or missing services and published 2020/21 annual reports.

DARS-NIC-423553-H8D6H.summary: NHS Sussex ICB's agreement covers the use of pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, maternity, ambulance, primary care and civil registration data, containing both clinical and financial information. The data is for planning and commissioning health services for the population of the former Brighton and Hove, East Sussex and West Sussex CCG areas. This includes reporting on providers, predicting demand and identifying patients at risk. The main intended benefit is better-informed commissioning decisions that improve service quality and health outcomes.

DARS-NIC-423859-V7S0R.summary: NHS England, with the Healthcare Quality Improvement Partnership, is permitted to use pseudonymised hospital admission and death registration data for the National Gastrointestinal Cancer Audit, covering bowel and oesophago-gastric cancer. The data is for assessing the quality of cancer care in England and Wales, giving hospital trusts timely feedback and studying the impact of COVID-19. The aim is to improve care. Reported results include more bowel cancer patients receiving adjuvant chemotherapy and more high-grade dysplasia patients being discussed by specialist teams.

DARS-NIC-423900-L1L7X.summary: North Tyneside Council's agreement covers hospital data, including emergency care, admitted patients, critical care, outpatients and accident and emergency (Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set). The agreement allows the data to be used for the council's public health duties, such as needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, the annual public health report and advice to NHS commissioners. The main intended benefit is locally focused analysis of health inequalities. The council reports it previously used the data to help develop a Local Health Index with partners.

DARS-NIC-424336-T7K7T.summary: The University of Exeter, working with the University of Cambridge and NatCen Social Research, is permitted under the agreement to use survey data on the mental health of children and young people from 2017 and a 2020 follow-up. The data is for examining how mental health, and use of mental health services, changed during the Covid-19 pandemic. The aim is to give evidence to those planning and commissioning child and adolescent mental health services, and to schools, so they can target support at the groups most affected.

DARS-NIC-424723-D5Q9W.summary: The Clinical Practice Research Datalink (CPRD), part of the Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA), receives a minimal extract of hospital data from the Secondary Uses Service (SUS) for COVID-19 surveillance. It is used to monitor the safety and quality of COVID-19 vaccines until routine GP data flows can be used, and to produce reports for the Yellow Card scheme. The data has already supported assessment of myopericarditis and menstrual disorders after vaccination.

DARS-NIC-42507-N1M8Z.summary: South Gloucestershire Council's agreement covers the use of identifiable civil registration data on births and deaths, plus primary care mortality data, to understand local health needs and protect public health. It allows the production of aggregated, small-number-suppressed statistics for needs assessments, public health reports and suicide prevention work. The aim is to tailor local services and reduce health inequalities. Reported results include local analysis showing no excess deaths among residents, and a needs assessment already used in council planning.

DARS-NIC-42575-X8G6W.summary: Southend-on-Sea Borough Council, a local authority, uses civil registration births data, primary care mortality data and Vital Statistics Service data, including identifiable details. It uses them to measure local health needs, plan and monitor services, and protect public health, for example through suicide audits and needs assessments. The aim is to tailor local services and reduce health inequalities and premature deaths. So far, its Joint Strategic Needs Assessments are being used to develop pilots of community-based support.
DARS-NIC-42575-X8G6W.retense_draft: Southend-on-Sea Borough Council's agreement covers civil registration births data, primary care mortality data and Vital Statistics Service data, including identifiable details. The agreement allows the data to be used to measure local health needs, plan and monitor services, and protect public health, for example through suicide audits and needs assessments. The aim is to tailor local services and reduce health inequalities and premature deaths. Its Joint Strategic Needs Assessments have been used to develop pilots of community-based support.

DARS-NIC-42679-H5B1D.summary: Knowsley Metropolitan Borough Council's agreement covers civil registration data on births and deaths, plus primary care mortality data, which includes identifiable details. The data is for understanding local health needs, planning services, supporting suicide audits and protecting public health, with the aim of tailoring services and reducing health inequalities. The council has used the data to compile a report on Excess Winter Deaths.

DARS-NIC-426830-M1C1K.summary: The London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine's agreement, through its commercial arm ARCTEC, covers Pillar 2 (non-hospital) COVID-19 test results, including test outcomes, symptom start dates and PCR cycle thresholds, for about 900 study participants. The agreement allows the data to be used to check how accurately medical detection dogs identify SARS-CoV-2 infection, including with new viral strains, low viral loads and no symptoms. The intended benefit is a quick screening tool for places such as airports.

DARS-NIC-426970-Y8V6T.summary: NHS Herefordshire and Worcestershire ICB's agreement covers the use of pseudonymised COVID-19 data, including GP record codes, ethnic category and vaccination status, to plan local health services. The agreement allows the data to be used to analyse missed appointments, identify patients at risk of hospital admission, allocate resources and monitor vaccine take-up. The main intended benefit is helping commissioners manage demand and respond to the outbreak. The CCG's annual report describes COVID-19 achievements that this data supported.

DARS-NIC-427822-X5G6N.summary: NHS England's agreement allows it to test and evaluate a pilot collection of ambulance service data from across England, with the aim of improving its quality and consistency, as directed by the Ambulance Services Data Set Discovery Directions 2020. The pilot supports a Long-Term Plan commitment to follow patient journeys from ambulances into other urgent and emergency care. The intended benefit is better commissioning of emergency care services, leading to better outcomes for users.

DARS-NIC-427962-M3K1W.summary: The Intensive Care National Audit & Research Centre (ICNARC), a research organisation, has an agreement covering civil death registrations and hospital admitted patient care and outpatient records. The data is for outcome information for the UK-ROX trial, which compares conservative with usual oxygen therapy in adults on mechanical ventilation after an unplanned intensive care admission. The main intended benefit is stronger evidence on the best amount of oxygen to give, to inform national guidance and improve survival and quality of life.

DARS-NIC-42818-F4R1T.summary: Solihull Metropolitan Borough Council's agreement covers identifiable births and deaths records, including primary care mortality data, for understanding local public health needs. The agreement allows the data to be used for needs assessments, health protection monitoring and suicide prevention work, with aggregated outputs. The aim is to tailor local services and reduce health inequalities and premature deaths. Under the previous agreement, the data fed an updated Joint Strategic Needs Assessment, a substance misuse needs assessment and a Falls Needs Assessment.

DARS-NIC-428459-V7Q8M.summary: The University of Oxford's agreement covers the use of Permission to Contact data, which is contact and eligibility details given by people who have volunteered to hear about COVID-19 vaccine trials. The agreement allows NHS Digital, acting as data processor, to email potentially eligible people about the Com-COV trial, which compares different COVID-19 vaccine schedule combinations. The main intended benefit is faster, less burdensome recruitment of suitable volunteers, helping speed up the delivery of an effective vaccine.

DARS-NIC-430380-F7L4Z.summary: The University of Bristol's agreement covers the use of Maternity Services Data Set records from England to study inequalities in stillbirth and preterm birth, and the risk factors behind them. The data is for helping the NHS find units needing support, judge whether interventions work, and develop tools to identify high-risk pregnancies early. So far, the team has found risk factors for both outcomes among first-time mothers, but no stillbirth prediction tool.

DARS-NIC-43048-T5S9D.summary: The London Borough of Enfield's agreement covers civil registration data on births and deaths, including identifiable primary care mortality data. The agreement allows the data to be used to understand local health needs, plan public health work such as suicide prevention, and produce reports with small numbers suppressed. The data is for tailoring local services and reducing health inequalities. The agreement allows the data to be used to show health inequalities to the council and voluntary sector, and in Joint Strategic Needs Assessment and Pharmaceutical Needs Assessment reports.

DARS-NIC-43059-H1N6M.summary: Sheffield City Council's agreement covers civil registration data on births and deaths, plus primary care mortality data, which includes identifiable details. The data is for measuring local health needs, planning services and protecting public health, including through suicide audits. The main intended benefit is to tailor local services and reduce health inequalities and premature deaths. Reported outputs include an updated Joint Strategic Needs Assessment, Director of Public Health reports and several health needs assessments.

DARS-NIC-430963-R7T2B.summary: The University of Leeds, working with University College London, has an agreement covering identifiable hospital, emergency care, death and cancer registration records for 1,279 people who consented to take part in a trial. It allows a long-term follow-up of the ELUCIDATE trial, which tests whether the Enhanced Liver Fibrosis (ELF) blood test can give early warning of cirrhosis and reduce serious liver complications. The data is for informing decisions on whether wider use of the test would improve patient outcomes.

DARS-NIC-431352-G7F1M.summary: Imperial College London's agreement covers linking consenting participants in its REACT COVID-19 study to their NHS health records, including hospital, cancer, mental health, death, testing and vaccination data. The linked data is for studying the risks of COVID infection and reinfection and people's later health, aiming to help plan healthcare for conditions such as Long COVID. The register reports that earlier REACT findings fed into government policy and were published in journals such as Science.

DARS-NIC-431355-B1L8W.summary: The University of Oxford's agreement covers linked NHS data on COVID-19 tests, vaccinations, adverse reactions, hospital care, maternity and deaths. The data is for studies of COVID-19 vaccine safety and effectiveness, including vaccine uptake and the risk of adverse events after vaccination. The stated main benefit is better public health knowledge about vaccine safety and how well vaccines reduce COVID-19 infections.

DARS-NIC-431565-K9V9N.summary: University College London's Centre for Longitudinal Studies agreement covers identifiable civil registration death records and demographic data for the 15,770 people in the Next Steps cohort. The data is for keeping participant records up to date, avoiding contact with people who have died or emigrated, and researching mortality and its links to health behaviours and social factors. Reported benefits include 21 deaths notified, which prevented unwanted contact with families.

DARS-NIC-431736-X6C4F.summary: Kingston University's agreement covers pseudonymised patient-level records from emergency departments and urgent treatment centres in England, drawn from two NHS England datasets: the Emergency Care Data Set and Hospital Episode Statistics Accident and Emergency. The research looks at how different mixes of non-medical practitioners and other staff affect patient outcomes, care quality, activity and costs. It aims to inform workforce decisions by clinicians, managers and commissioners.

DARS-NIC-431881-N8B0N.summary: The University of Oxford's agreement covers linked NHS hospital, emergency care, mental health, COVID-19 test and death registration data, alongside GP records from the Royal College of GPs surveillance network. The data is for developing and validating an early warning score to help GPs assess COVID-19 in remote consultations, using hospital admission as a measure of deterioration. It also aims to compare recovered and long COVID cases. So far, two predictive risk scores and a long COVID phenotype have been developed, and manuscripts have been written and submitted to a journal.

DARS-NIC-432598-Q6S0C.summary: The University of Oxford's agreement covers the use of hospital admitted patient care and outpatient records (Hospital Episode Statistics), linked to death registration data, to study shoulder replacement surgery in England. It allows examination of trends over time, differences in access across areas, complications after surgery and the likely future demand on the NHS. The data is for helping NHS planning of services, costs and staffing. A paper on rising demand, unequal provision and varying outcomes was published in BMC Medicine in 2023.

DARS-NIC-433152-N2N7C.summary: NHS West Yorkshire Integrated Care Board (ICB) uses pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, maternity, prescribing and population data, containing clinical and financial information. It uses the data to plan and commission health services, including analysing population needs, predicting demand and monitoring provider performance. The main aim is to help commissioners make better decisions and improve services and health outcomes. So far, it has let the CCGs benchmark performance across West Yorkshire, starting with mental health, community and maternity data.

DARS-NIC-433156-Q9X6Z.summary: NHS Hampshire and Isle of Wight ICB's agreement allows pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, ambulance, prescribing and population data, containing both clinical and financial information. The data is for planning and commissioning health services across the Hampshire and Isle of Wight partnership area, including activity and budget reporting, demand planning and identifying patients and groups with the greatest need. The main intended benefit is better-planned services and improved patient flow.

DARS-NIC-433158-L7X7P.summary: NHS Lincolnshire ICB's agreement covers receipt of pseudonymised COVID-19 data covering GP record codes (GDPPR), ethnic category and vaccination status. The data is for planning local health care, predicting demand, allocating resources, identifying patients at risk and finding areas with low vaccine take-up. The main intended benefit is helping commissioners make better decisions and respond to the outbreak. The CCG published an annual report describing its pandemic response achievements, which the data supported.

DARS-NIC-433163-Y2V0K.summary: NHS Black Country ICB's agreement covers pseudonymised community, mental health and hospital activity data, which includes clinical and financial information. The data may be processed by Pi Limited (trading as Predict X) to plan and commission health services and to profile health and social care use across the Black Country and West Birmingham area. The purpose is to find where care can be improved, such as emergency admissions and transfer of care delays. Reported results include dashboards showing pressure points in the care system for Wolverhampton City Council.

DARS-NIC-433166-T6N9F.summary: NHS Bedfordshire, Luton and Milton Keynes ICB, a sub-ICB location, has an agreement covering pseudonymised (identifiers replaced) GP record data, COVID-19 vaccination data and ethnicity data. The main intended benefit is helping commissioners manage demand and capacity and make better decisions for patients. The CCG published an annual report describing its COVID-19 response, which this data supported.

DARS-NIC-433167-R3Q1Z.summary: NHS Frimley ICB, a Sub ICB Location, has an agreement covering pseudonymised COVID-19 data from GP records, ethnic category data and vaccination status. The agreement allows the data to be used to plan local health services, model patient risk, allocate resources and monitor vaccine uptake. The main intended benefit is helping commissioners manage demand and respond to COVID-19. The CCGs have published an annual report describing their COVID-19 response, which this data supported.

DARS-NIC-433176-J8Q2S.summary: AstraZeneca AB's agreement covers the use of death records, hospital admission records and heart attack audit data to run a trial of dapagliflozin, given daily alongside standard care after a heart attack. The trial aims to see whether the drug prevents hospitalisation for heart failure or cardiovascular death. The main results were published in NEJM Evidence in 2024, with further published analyses of patient subgroups.

DARS-NIC-433181-W6M0J.summary: NHS Hampshire and Isle of Wight ICB's agreement covers pseudonymised (identifying details replaced) GP record data, ethnic category data and COVID-19 vaccination data. The data is for planning local health services, modelling which patients may need hospital care, allocating resources and monitoring vaccine take-up during the COVID-19 response. The main intended benefit is helping commissioners manage demand and make better decisions for patients. The CCGs' annual reports describe pandemic response work supported by this data.

DARS-NIC-433257-K6Q2Y.summary: The University of Liverpool's agreement, working with the University of Cambridge and Cambridge University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust, covers identifiable NHS England data on hospital care, emergency care, deaths and medicines dispensed in primary care. The data is for a national trial, HEAL-COVID, which tests treatments for people after hospital discharge with COVID-19. The data helps measure survival, hospital readmission and NHS resource use. The main intended benefit is knowing how best to treat patients in the post-acute phase of COVID-19.

DARS-NIC-43354-B7P4H.summary: NHS Bristol, North Somerset and South Gloucestershire CCG (Clinical Commissioning Group) agreement covers hospital, ambulance, community, mental health, maternity and other patient activity data, some identifiable by NHS number and some pseudonymised. The agreement allows the data to be used to validate invoices, identify patients at risk of high future service use, and support commissioning of health services. The stated aim is to improve planning, budget control and the quality of services for patients.

The data is for checking provider invoices, identifying patients at high risk of deteriorating health, and planning and monitoring commissioned services. The main intended benefit is that services are paid for accurately and planned to meet local needs. The CCG's 2020/21 annual report describes achievements such as a diabetes advice service and a COVID-19 recovery service.

DARS-NIC-433629-H3M0G.summary: NHS England's agreement covers routinely recorded GP data on physical health checks for people with severe mental illness, covering alcohol, blood lipids, blood glucose, smoking, BMI and blood pressure. The agreement allows this data to monitor delivery of the NHS Long Term Plan ambition for 390 thousand people to receive a comprehensive check and follow-up. The aim is to reduce premature mortality by supporting local quality improvement and tackling inequalities in access to checks.

DARS-NIC-433923-Z0V8D.summary: The University of Glasgow's agreement covers NHS England cancer registration, death registration and hospital admission records for people in the IRONMAN trial, which involves 1,400 people with heart failure and iron deficiency. The data is for capturing hospitalisations, cancers and deaths, to test whether adding intravenous iron to standard care reduces illness and death and is cost-effective. The initial linkage has already identified previously unreported clinical events.

DARS-NIC-43405-T5C4G.summary: NHS Wandsworth CCG's agreement covers hospital, mental health, community, maternity and other local provider data, including patient-level records linked with GP data. The data is for risk stratification, which identifies patients at high risk so their care can be prioritised, and North & East London Commissioning Support Unit will carry out the work. The stated aim is to help GPs and commissioners target early support, improve planning and reduce avoidable emergency admissions.

DARS-NIC-43418-W0V0N.summary: NHS Greenwich Clinical Commissioning Group (CCG) uses hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other health service data, including some linked to NHS numbers for risk stratification. GPs and commissioners can use the scores to target care and plan services. The main intended benefit is more effective commissioning, with fewer avoidable emergency admissions.

The agreement allows the data to identify patients at high risk of needing services and to support planning, monitoring and reporting on local health services. The main intended benefit is more effective commissioning, leading to a better patient experience.

DARS-NIC-43431-N0G4J.summary: NHS South West London ICB's agreement, covering the former Croydon area, allows hospital activity data, linked with GP data, to be used to identify patients at high risk of health deterioration or repeated service use. The Sollis Partnership Ltd is permitted to carry out this risk stratification, which is intended to help GPs and commissioners target care and plan services for vulnerable patients. The main intended benefit is fewer avoidable emergency hospital admissions through earlier intervention.

DARS-NIC-43435-D8M8Z.summary: NHS North West London ICB (a sub-ICB location) agreement allows commissioners to use Secondary Uses Service (SUS+) hospital data, identifiable by NHS number, for two purposes. DARS-NIC-43454-T1L8J.summary: NHS Horsham and Mid Sussex CCG (Clinical Commissioning Group) is covered by an agreement that allows it to use pseudonymised hospital, mental health, maternity, community and other local provider data, where patients are not directly identified. The data is for risk stratification to identify patients at risk, and for commissioning analysis, reporting and monitoring of services. The main intended benefit is better planning and commissioning of services, leading to improved patient experience.

DARS-NIC-43466-P5J3F.summary: NHS Guildford and Waverley CCG's agreement covers pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other local provider data, containing clinical and financial information. DARS-NIC-434738-K7Z9L.summary: The Office for National Statistics (ONS)'s agreement covers the use of demographic data from NHS Digital to select and invite a sample of people aged 80 or over to take part in a COVID-19 vaccination survey. The agreement allows the results to go to the Department of Health and Social Care to help plan vaccination policy and increase uptake.

DARS-NIC-43487-T6V1S.summary: NHS Lambeth CCG's agreement covers hospital, mental health, community, primary care and other local health service data, some identifiable by NHS number and some pseudonymised, for its area. The main intended benefit is better planned and more effective services, including fewer avoidable emergency admissions.

DARS-NIC-43492-M8R1G.summary: NHS North West London ICB, covering the former Hammersmith & Fulham CCG area, has an agreement that allows it to use hospital activity data (SUS for Commissioners) that can be identified by NHS number. DARS-NIC-43499-C1H9Y.summary: NHS North West London ICB's agreement, for the former NHS Harrow Clinical Commissioning Group (CCG), allows hospital activity data (SUS for Commissioners), identifiable by NHS number, to be used for invoice validation and risk stratification. DARS-NIC-48149-B0V9M.summary: Wakefield Metropolitan District Council's public health team's agreement covers the use of hospital and emergency care records (Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set). DARS-NIC-482185-K8G0F.summary: University College London's agreement covers the use of birth notification, birth registration and demographic records to select and contact families for a feasibility study of a possible new UK-wide birth cohort. Public dialogue reports and a participant website have been published, and initial deliverables were submitted to the funder.

DARS-NIC-482271-S6S1V.summary: The University of Manchester's agreement allows linked hospital records, community services data and death registration data to be used for research on adult community health services. DARS-NIC-482394-D4Q4R.summary: Imperial College London's agreement covers pseudonymised hospital admission, death registration and primary care medicines data for about 31,500 patients who had planned repair of an abdominal aortic aneurysm (a swelling in the body's main blood vessel). DARS-NIC-483357-P5L8F.summary: NatCen Social Research's agreement covers NHS England emergency care, maternity and community services data, plus a PersonID bridge file, for the National Lottery Community Fund's evaluation of A Better Start. The aim is to give partnerships, commissioners and policymakers evidence on the programme's impact.

The aim is to spot implant-related problems earlier and so reduce unnecessary risk to patients.

DARS-NIC-589868-W0K1B.summary: The University of Sheffield's agreement covers linked NHS data on emergency care, hospital admissions, outpatient care, mental health services, dispensed medicines and deaths. The data is for building a research database, CUREd+, to study how patients use urgent and emergency care in England. The main intended benefit is evidence to make these services more efficient, safer and better for patients. Under the agreement, four research studies may be approved to receive data extracts, and no results have been reported yet.

DARS-NIC-58999-K6P8B.summary: IQVIA Ltd, a commercial company, holds hospital data (Hospital Episode Statistics accident and emergency, admitted patient care and outpatients) to check its published findings on pulmonary arterial hypertension if questions are raised. The research looked at how patients with this lung condition are diagnosed, aiming to support earlier diagnosis and better treatment. Findings have already been published in the Journal of Pulmonary Circulation and the European Respiratory Journal in 2018, and presented at two international conferences.

DARS-NIC-59012-K2Q5T.summary: NHS England, through its Temporary National Repository, is permitted to use mental health, Improving Access to Psychological Therapies, and hospital accident and emergency, inpatient and outpatient data. The agreement allows its use for routine and ad-hoc analysis and reporting to manage commissioned services, support quality and productivity programmes, and check data quality. The main intended benefit is helping NHS England meet its statutory duties and monitor progress against the Five Year Forward View, including for mental health.

DARS-NIC-594012-C9R9H.summary: The University of Newcastle upon Tyne's agreement covers the use of NHS hospital, emergency care, outpatient, mental health and death registration records. The data is for studying how disabled children's contacts with NHS services changed between April 2019 and September 2021, across different COVID-19 lockdown periods. The aim is to inform policy on recovering services and planning a minimum service for future emergencies.

DARS-NIC-594129-R0M3W.summary: University Hospital Southampton NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers contact details and screening information (such as age, sex, location, job type and health questions) from people who signed up to be contacted about COVID-19 vaccine trials. The agreement allows NHS Digital to process this data on the Trust's behalf to recruit volunteers to a phase I trial of the pEVAC-PS vaccine. The main intended benefit is faster recruitment, helping speed up the delivery of an effective vaccine.

DARS-NIC-595090-W5R3K.summary: The University of Oxford's agreement covers the use of NHS hospital, emergency care and death registration records for a health economic analysis for the FAME trial. The analysis compares close contact casting with surgery in younger adults with unstable ankle fractures. It looks at whether ankle function with casting is not worse than with surgery. The main intended benefit is evidence to update NICE fracture guidance and inform commissioning decisions.

DARS-NIC-59545-S2W0Q.summary: NHS Airedale, Wharfedale and Craven CCG's agreement covers pseudonymised hospital, ambulance, community, emergency care and mental health activity data. The data is for supporting Airedale Foundation Trust and its Vanguard partners, including four CCGs, in commissioning the Airedale Telemedicine Service for care home residents. The aim is better integrated health and care, including reporting, dashboards and planning to improve outcomes.

DARS-NIC-59558-T4S1Q.summary: NHS Bradford Districts CCG's agreement covers pseudonymised hospital, ambulance, community, emergency care and mental health activity data, linked from several sources. The data is for supporting the Airedale Telemedicine Service and Vanguard partners in commissioning and planning services for care home residents. The aim is better integrated health and care, in line with the Better Care Fund, and improved outcomes for residents.

DARS-NIC-595667-K4S9R.summary: The University of Bristol's agreement allows it, as an academic organisation, to use pseudonymised cancer registration, hospital, radiotherapy and chemotherapy-type records for about 300 consenting patients in the ROMIO trial. The trial compares combined keyhole and open surgery with standard open surgery for oesophageal (gullet) cancer. It looks at recovery, complications, survival, quality of life and cost-effectiveness. The aim is to help inform the best surgical practice in future.

DARS-NIC-596002-V3N9J.summary: Harvey Walsh Ltd, a supplier working on a University of Bristol study, is permitted under the agreement to use GP records from the COVID-19 GP data extraction (GDPPR) for people registered with GP practices in the Bristol, North Somerset and South Gloucestershire area. The data is for calculating population denominators by risk group for the Avon Community Acquired Pneumonia study of hospitalised lower respiratory illness. The intended benefit is accurate disease incidence figures to help guide healthcare resourcing and vaccination policy.

DARS-NIC-59602-K3Y6W.summary: NHS Bradford City CCG's agreement covers the use of pseudonymised hospital, ambulance, community, mental health and emergency care data. Together with Airedale NHS Foundation Trust and its Vanguard partners, the agreement allows the data to support commissioning of the Airedale Telemedicine Service for care and nursing home residents. This includes reporting, dashboards and planning to join up health and care services. The stated aim is to improve outcomes through integrated care, as set out in the Better Care Fund.

DARS-NIC-59621-M2K5Q.summary: NHS East Lancashire CCG's agreement covers pseudonymised local provider and hospital activity data, including maternity, A&E, inpatient and outpatient records. The data is for supporting Airedale NHS Foundation Trust and its Vanguard partners in planning and commissioning the Airedale Telemedicine Service for nursing and care home residents. The agreement allows the data to be used to monitor outcomes, target support at residents at high risk of emergency care, and improve integrated health and care.

DARS-NIC-596409-F0T3M.summary: The Royal College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists (RCOG) agreement covers Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care data on mothers and babies. The data is for working for the Department of Health and Social Care to estimate how many obstetricians and anaesthetists maternity units in England need, taking account of how complex each unit's births are. The results will feed an online workforce tool, a report and publications. The aim is to help plan staffing that supports safer maternity care.

DARS-NIC-59669-F6Y3W.summary: The Royal College of Surgeons of England is using patient-level hospital admission records and civil registration death records for the National Vascular Registry, an audit of NHS vascular surgery. The data will be linked to the registry's records to show longer-term outcomes, such as 90-day mortality and readmissions, and to check how complete the registry's case numbers are. The aim is to help NHS vascular units improve care and patient outcomes. The registry's outputs have already been used by surgeons for revalidation, by NHS trusts for quality improvement, and in the NHS England CQUIN process.
DARS-NIC-59669-F6Y3W.retense_draft: The Royal College of Surgeons of England's agreement covers the use of patient-level hospital admission records and civil registration death records for the National Vascular Registry, an audit of NHS vascular surgery. The data is for linking to the registry's records to show longer-term outcomes, such as 90-day mortality and readmissions, and to check how complete the registry's case numbers are. The aim is to help NHS vascular units improve care and patient outcomes. The registry's outputs have already been used by surgeons for revalidation, by NHS trusts for quality improvement, and in the NHS England CQUIN process.

DARS-NIC-597255-J9M1H.summary: The University of Manchester's agreement covers cancer registration and civil death registration data for about 500 people who took part in the RAPID clinical trial for early-stage Hodgkin lymphoma. The agreement allows the University to follow their survival, causes of death and second cancers, comparing those treated with chemotherapy alone against chemotherapy plus radiotherapy. The hoped-for benefit is better evidence on late effects of treatment, which could change how early-stage Hodgkin lymphoma is managed.

DARS-NIC-59807-V1B8W.summary: NHS Humber and North Yorkshire ICB (North East Lincolnshire area)'s agreement allows it to use hospital, community, mental health, maternity, primary care medicines and social care data, including identifiable and pseudonymised records. The data is for checking provider invoices, identifying patients at high risk of poor health, and planning and monitoring health services. The main intended benefit is more effective commissioning of services, leading to better patient experience and health outcomes.

DARS-NIC-59873-D8C6G.summary: University College London's Medical Research Council Clinical Trials Unit's agreement covers cancer registration, death registration and demographic data on men taking part in the STAMPEDE trial of added treatments for high-risk prostate cancer. The data is for following participants' survival over the long term and for checking how well death records match trial data. The aim is better evidence on which treatments help men live longer. Death registration data let the metformin comparison report its main result sooner.

DARS-NIC-60215-F1S2G.summary: Cheshire West and Chester Council's agreement covers civil registration births and deaths data, including identifiable records, along with primary care mortality data. The data is for understanding local health needs, supporting suicide audits and prevention, and planning public health services, with the aim of tailoring services and reducing health inequalities. Reported results include informing the Place Plan 2024, Children's centre dashboards, and the 0-19 JSNA published in 2024.

DARS-NIC-602345-C6S4M.summary: The University of Cambridge's agreement covers the use of NHS England cancer registration and civil registration of death data for the EMBED study. The study aims to develop sensitive blood tests that detect tiny amounts of circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA), so breast cancer can be found earlier in women at increased risk. The main intended benefit is a simple blood test that improves early diagnosis and may reduce the need for repeated scans, biopsies and preventive surgery.

DARS-NIC-604129-X4D1K.summary: The University of Bristol's agreement covers use of the 2014 Adult Psychiatric Morbidity Survey, a population survey of adults in England covering mental health and use of support services. The research looks at which social and demographic factors are linked to older men using community support groups for mental health difficulties. The main intended benefit is to help support services and community groups target help at particular groups of older men.

DARS-NIC-60414-C4F7W.summary: NHS Leeds West CCG (Clinical Commissioning Group) is permitted to use hospital activity data (SUS) and a wide range of local provider data covering acute, community, mental health, primary care and more. The agreement allows the data to be used to commission services, produce commissioner reports and dashboards, and monitor hospital activity against contracts. Processing is carried out by NECS and eMBED Health Consortium. The main intended benefit is better-informed commissioning of high quality, safe services.

DARS-NIC-60430-F1Q3B.summary: NHS Leeds North CCG's agreement covers the use of local provider data from acute, community, mental health, primary care and other services, together with Secondary Uses Service (SUS) accident and emergency, inpatient and outpatient data. The data is for commissioning reports, dashboards, contract monitoring and analysis, with support from commissioning support organisations. The stated aim is better-planned, higher quality and safer services.

DARS-NIC-60433-X9Z5B.summary: NHS Rotherham CCG's agreement covers hospital activity data (SUS) and local provider data covering acute, community, mental health, ambulance and primary care services. The data is for commissioning reports, dashboards, contract monitoring and analysis of hospital activity, with support from its commissioning support providers. The main intended benefit is better information for commissioning high-quality, safe services that lead to better outcomes for local people.

DARS-NIC-60434-Z8Y6W.summary: NHS Hambleton, Richmondshire and Whitby CCG's agreement allows it to use hospital activity data (accident and emergency, inpatient and outpatient) and local provider data covering areas such as acute, community, mental health and primary care. Commissioning support organisations may process it for the CCG. The data is for producing reports, dashboards and analysis that monitor hospital activity against contracts, support statutory returns and help plan and commission services. The stated aim is better-quality, safer services and better outcomes for local people.

DARS-NIC-60435-G2S3T.summary: NHS Hull Clinical Commissioning Group (CCG) uses local provider data covering acute, ambulance, community, mental health and primary care, plus Secondary Uses Service (SUS) accident and emergency, inpatient and outpatient data. Its commissioning support providers, NECS and eMBED Health Consortium, use it to produce activity and finance reports, statutory returns, dashboards and analyses of hospital activity. The stated aim is better-informed commissioning of high quality, safe services and better outcomes for local people.

DARS-NIC-60437-N4W6X.summary: NHS Harrogate and Rural District CCG's agreement allows it to use hospital activity data (SUS accident and emergency, inpatient and outpatient records) and local provider data covering areas such as acute, community, mental health and primary care. Commissioning support organisations may process it for the CCG. The data is for monitoring hospital activity and contracts, producing reports and dashboards, and analysing services. The stated aim is better-informed commissioning of high quality, safe services and better outcomes for local people.

DARS-NIC-60439-T6C6W.summary: NHS Airedale, Wharfedale and Craven CCG's agreement allows it to use hospital activity data (SUS) and local provider data covering acute, community, mental health, primary care and other services. The aim is better information for commissioning high-quality, safe services and better outcomes for the local population.

The data is for commissioning services, producing commissioner reports, dashboards, contract monitoring and analysis of hospital activity, with support from commissioning support organisations. The stated aim is to help commission high quality, safe services that lead to better outcomes for local people.

DARS-NIC-60444-L5T3W.summary: NHS Leeds South and East CCG's agreement covers hospital activity data (SUS) and local provider data covering areas such as acute, community, mental health and primary care. The data is for use, processed by commissioning support organisations on its behalf, to produce commissioning reports, dashboards, statutory returns and monitoring of provider contracts. The stated aim is better commissioning of high quality, safe services and better outcomes for local people.

DARS-NIC-60445-F1S4V.summary: NHS Vale of York Clinical Commissioning Group (CCG) uses local provider data and Secondary Uses Service (SUS) hospital data covering accident and emergency, inpatient and outpatient care. It uses them to support commissioning, including activity and finance reporting, monitoring hospital contracts and producing dashboards, with commissioning support organisations processing the data. The aim is better-informed commissioning of high quality, safe services and better outcomes for local people.

The agreement allows the data to be used to produce commissioning reports, dashboards, contract monitoring and analysis, with support from data processors. The main intended benefit is better-informed commissioning of high quality, safe services and better outcomes for local people.

DARS-NIC-60449-S4F7K.summary: NHS Scarborough and Ryedale CCG's agreement covers hospital activity data (SUS) and local provider data covering acute, ambulance, community, mental health and primary care services. Commissioning support organisations may process it to produce commissioner reports, dashboards, contract monitoring and analysis of hospital activity. The stated aim is better commissioning of safe, high-quality services, leading to better outcomes for local people.

DARS-NIC-60452-X5V8S.summary: NHS Bradford City CCG's agreement allows it to use hospital activity data (SUS) and local provider data covering areas such as acute, ambulance, community, mental health and primary care. Commissioning support organisations may process it for the CCG. The data is for commissioning reports, contract monitoring, dashboards, readmissions analysis and benchmarking. The stated aim is better information to commission high quality, safe services and improve outcomes.

DARS-NIC-60454-Q4L6Z.summary: NHS Calderdale Clinical Commissioning Group (CCG) uses pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health and other local provider data, plus Secondary Uses Service (SUS) records for A&E, inpatient and outpatient care. Commissioning support organisations process the data. The CCG uses it to monitor activity, finance and quality, produce reports and dashboards, and support service planning. The stated aim is better-commissioned, safer, higher-quality services.
DARS-NIC-60454-Q4L6Z.retense_draft: NHS Calderdale Clinical Commissioning Group's agreement covers pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health and other local provider data, plus Secondary Uses Service (SUS) records for A&E, inpatient and outpatient care. Commissioning support organisations may process it for the CCG to produce activity and finance reports, dashboards, statutory returns and analysis. DARS-NIC-60465-D4R5F.summary: NHS Bassetlaw CCG's agreement covers hospital activity data (SUS) and local provider data covering acute, ambulance, community, mental health, emergency care and primary care. Commissioning support organisations may process it for the CCG. The data is for commissioning reports, dashboards, contract monitoring and quality reviews. The stated aim is better-informed commissioning of high quality, safe services that lead to better outcomes for local people.

DARS-NIC-60466-Z1J8M.summary: NHS Bradford Districts CCG's agreement covers hospital activity data (SUS) and local provider data covering acute, ambulance, community, mental health, primary care and other services. The data is for commissioning services, producing commissioner reports, dashboards, contract monitoring and analysis of hospital activity. The stated aim is better-informed commissioning of high-quality, safe services and better outcomes for the local population.

DARS-NIC-60470-V4B7X.summary: NHS North Kirklees CCG's agreement covers local provider data and SUS hospital data covering accident and emergency, inpatient and outpatient care. The agreement allows the data to be linked with social care data through its contracted processors. The data is for producing commissioning reports, dashboards and contract monitoring, and for supporting integrated health and social care planning. The stated aim is better-informed commissioning decisions and better outcomes for local people.

DARS-NIC-60479-W7X3T.summary: NHS Greater Huddersfield CCG's agreement covers hospital activity data (SUS) and local provider data, including pseudonymised records linked with social care data. The agreement allows the data to be used to produce commissioning reports, dashboards, contract monitoring and analysis. The aim is to inform commissioning decisions and support integrated health and social care, leading to better outcomes for local people.

DARS-NIC-604847-S4B5L.summary: Grail Bio UK Ltd, a commercial company, and Queen Mary University of London's agreement covers the use of pseudonymised patient-level NHS data on cancer registrations, cancer treatments, hospital care and emergency care. The data is for following up people recruited to the NHS-Galleri trial, which tests whether a blood test that can detect many cancers finds them earlier than current NHS tests. The aim is to inform whether the NHS adopts the test to help detect cancer earlier.

DARS-NIC-604851-W0M3S.summary: Grail Bio UK Ltd, a commercial company working jointly with the University of Oxford, has an agreement covering linked NHS cancer registration, hospital, emergency care and cancer waiting times data for people who consented to the SYMPLIFY study. The study assesses how well the Galleri blood test detects many types of cancer in people referred with possible cancer symptoms. The main intended benefit is to show whether such a test could help diagnose cancer earlier and with fewer diagnostic procedures.

DARS-NIC-605115-L0W3V.summary: The University of Oxford (Nuffield Department of Primary Care Health Sciences) agreement covers NHS England data on COVID-19 test results, hospital care, emergency care, deaths and dispensed medicines. The data is for the PANORAMIC trial, which tests antiviral treatments for higher-risk people with COVID-19 in the community. The aim is to see whether the treatments reduce hospital admissions and deaths. The trial has produced four publications, including a 2023 results paper on molnupiravir.

DARS-NIC-606084-D1D6T.summary: University of Cambridge's agreement covers the use of NHS England death registration records and hospital admitted patient and outpatient records to follow up people with cerebral small vessel disease, a disease of the small blood vessels in the brain. The research aims to find genetic risk factors for the disease and to identify who goes on to develop dementia. The main intended benefit is better prediction of dementia after lacunar stroke and a better understanding of the disease's causes, which could support new treatments.

DARS-NIC-60624-B1R2Q.summary: IQVIA Ltd, a commercial company working with the National Amyloidosis Centre at the Royal Free, has an agreement to use hospital records (admitted patient care, outpatient and A&E) on people with amyloidosis, a rare disease. The agreement allows the data to be used to study how patients are diagnosed and treated, to support earlier diagnosis and a more efficient care pathway. One paper on cardiac transthyretin amyloidosis has already been published in the journal Circulation.

DARS-NIC-606839-V5X2P.summary: The Boston Consulting Group UK LLP's agreement covers pseudonymised hospital, emergency care, diagnostic imaging, mental health, community services and patient-reported outcome data. The agreement allows the data to be used to give NHS and public sector clients benchmarking, performance analysis, demand and capacity modelling and care pathway analysis. The main intended benefit is helping clients find improvements in patient care and experience. In 2025, hospital data was used for an integrated care system's productivity analysis and to build a productivity benchmarking tool.

DARS-NIC-60714-M4T1M.summary: University Hospital Southampton NHS Foundation Trust, with Queen Mary University of London, has an agreement covering hospital admission, critical care and death records for patients in the FLO-ELA trial. The trial tests a fluid treatment for people having emergency bowel surgery. The aim is to show whether it helps or harms patients and what it costs. Data have been used in four safety reports, and the 2019 report led the trial team to change the primary outcome.

DARS-NIC-608743-H5X9Z.summary: The University of Oxford's agreement covers the use of identifiable NHS hospital records, demographic details and death registrations for children with certain surgical conditions. The agreement allows it to build a research database to compare hospitals' observed outcomes with those expected from the children they treat. The data is for identifying unwarranted variation in care, with feedback to hospitals and a public dashboard. The intended benefit is better health outcomes and care for children with these conditions.

DARS-NIC-609893-N5P5L.summary: Imperial College London's Neonatal Data Analysis Unit's agreement allows it to use demographic data (names and up-to-date postcodes) to link records of very preterm and surgical babies in the National Neonatal Research Database with education and health records. The data is for understanding the long-term health and educational outcomes of these children, so that neonatal care and service planning can be improved. Reported results include a peer-reviewed paper on survival of extremely preterm babies that changed national guidance.

DARS-NIC-609903-V6Q7S.summary: NHS England's agreement covers supplying demographic data from the Patient Demographic Service for a cohort of adults with autoimmune diseases or cancers who are immunosuppressed. The data is for Imperial College London's MELODY study, so that Ipsos MORI can send invitations, confirm identities and post home antibody test kits after a third COVID-19 vaccine dose. The study aims to show how many immunosuppressed people develop detectable SARS-CoV-2 antibodies, to help inform health policy and targeted protection.

DARS-NIC-61042-K9Q3G.summary: Hull York Medical School's agreement allows the use of hospital admissions records linked to death registration data to assess how national head injury guidelines (from NICE) affected deaths from traumatic brain injury and hospital admissions for head injury. The aim is to judge whether the guidelines have been clinically effective and whether they added to NHS admissions and costs. Analysis found that only the guideline recommending specialist centre care was linked to lower mortality, limited to ages 16 to 65.

DARS-NIC-610798-N0G8Z.summary: The National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)'s agreement covers the use of NHS England hospital, death registration, mental health, maternity, cancer and primary care dispensing data in the Secure Data Environment. The agreement allows this data to be used to understand NHS activity and costs, and to develop and update its guidance. The aim is for guidance to reflect real-world patient care. NICE reports completing eight data requests for 2025/26, including hospital data to support resource impact tools for guidelines.

DARS-NIC-61090-T9Y0G.summary: The University of Oxford's agreement covers linked hospital admission records, death registration data and the National Hip Fracture Database. The data is for studying whether total hip replacement gives better outcomes than partial (hemiarthroplasty) replacement for independently mobile older adults with a hip fracture. It will also look at whether treatment that departs from NICE guidance leads to worse outcomes. The aim is to inform future updates of NICE and British Orthopaedic Association guidance.

DARS-NIC-612092-Q0Y6F.summary: The Home Office's agreement covers detailed, unsuppressed tables of hospital admissions data (Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care) for assault injuries in England. The agreement allows the data to be used to monitor serious violence, evaluate policies and decide where to allocate funding. The aim is to target money at the areas with most need and reduce serious violence. A published evaluation of Violence Reduction Units reportedly showed a statistically significant reduction in violence.

DARS-NIC-61265-Q4L9V.summary: Wirral Borough Council's agreement covers civil registration data on births and deaths, plus primary care mortality data, which includes identifiable details. The data is for measuring local health needs, planning services and protecting public health, including suicide prevention work and needs assessments. The aim is to tailor local services to areas of greatest need and reduce health inequalities. Reported results include analysis that found high COPD mortality in two deprived wards and led to joint work with the ICB and Community Trust on early intervention.

DARS-NIC-613522-Q7Z8N.summary: The University of Newcastle upon Tyne's agreement covers NHS hospital, emergency care, community and mental health service records, including psychological therapy data. The agreement allows study of how people from ethnic minorities in North East and North Cumbria used mental health services before and after the pandemic, and how this relates to their health outcomes. The data is for informing evidence-based decisions and services that better meet the needs of ethnic minority communities.

DARS-NIC-614954-G8P7P.summary: The University of Edinburgh's agreement covers the use of identifiable NHS England data, drawn from hospital admissions, demographics and dispensed medicines records, to find and invite people who survived a stroke caused by bleeding in the brain to join the ASPIRING study. The study tests whether starting antiplatelet drugs reduces later major cardiovascular events. The main intended benefit is stronger evidence on whether this treatment helps stroke survivors.

DARS-NIC-615890-Q8N9R.summary: NHS Hertfordshire and West Essex Integrated Care Board's agreement covers commissioning, invoice validation and risk stratification datasets, which include patient-level health and financial data. The data is for checking provider invoices, identifying patients at high risk of poor health, and planning and managing local health services. The main intended benefit is more effective commissioning, leading to better patient experience and health outcomes. Reported results include a frailty service evaluation that led the provider to refine the service, and an urgent and emergency care analysis that informed an approved strategy.

DARS-NIC-615897-K1Z9C.summary: NHS North East London Integrated Care Board's agreement covers invoice validation, risk stratification and commissioning datasets, some identifiable by NHS number and some pseudonymised. The agreement allows the data to be used to check provider invoices are correct, identify patients at high risk of health deterioration, and plan health services for the local population. The main intended benefit is better-targeted care and more effective commissioning of services. The board says its analysis has helped it identify unmet need and inequalities.

DARS-NIC-615958-F7Q7Z.summary: NHS Bristol, North Somerset and South Gloucestershire Integrated Care Board's agreement covers commissioning datasets, containing pseudonymised clinical and financial information, and invoice validation datasets. The agreement allows the data to be used to plan health services for its local population and to check that provider invoices are correct and the patient is its responsibility. The main intended benefit is that services are planned and paid for accurately and appropriately.

DARS-NIC-615960-G7W1L.summary: NHS Kent and Medway Integrated Care Board's agreement allows the use of commissioning, invoice validation and risk stratification datasets, some of which can identify patients, to plan health services, check provider invoices and identify patients at high risk. The aim is to commission services more effectively, control budgets and improve patient outcomes. The data is for board performance reports, contract monitoring, invoice queries and disputes, and an evaluation of social prescribing in Kent and Medway.

DARS-NIC-615969-D3K1X.summary: NHS Black Country Integrated Care Board's agreement covers commissioning and invoice validation datasets, including pseudonymised clinical and financial data about patients. The agreement allows the data to be used to check that providers' invoices are correct and the patients are its responsibility, and to plan and manage health services for its population. The main intended benefit is that providers are paid accurately and services are commissioned to meet local health needs.

DARS-NIC-615972-B8C0H.summary: North Tyneside Council's agreement covers civil registration data on births and deaths, plus primary care mortality data. The data is for understanding local health needs, planning services and supporting public health work such as suicide audits. The agreement's main intended benefit is local services better targeted to reduce premature deaths and health inequalities. Reported results include identifying clusters of disease and of suicide, and an end of life care needs assessment.

DARS-NIC-615974-Y3R7Q.summary: NHS North Central London Integrated Care Board's agreement covers the use of identifiable and pseudonymised data on invoices, patient risk and commissioned health services. The agreement allows the data to be used to check that providers' invoices are correct, to identify patients at high risk of health deterioration, and to analyse population needs so services can be planned. The main intended benefit is more effective commissioning, with better patient outcomes and accurate payment of providers. The reported benefits section lists general aims but no specific completed outcome.

DARS-NIC-615980-P3Y7N.summary: NHS Cheshire and Merseyside Integrated Care Board's agreement covers commissioning, invoice validation and risk stratification data, some of it identifiable by NHS number and some pseudonymised. The data is for checking provider invoices, identifying patients at high risk of poor health, and planning health services for the local population. The main intended benefit is more effective commissioning, leading to better patient experience and health outcomes.

DARS-NIC-615981-K2W5D.summary: NHS South East London Integrated Care Board's agreement covers commissioning data and invoice validation data, including pseudonymised patient-level clinical and financial information. The data is for checking that provider invoices are correct and for analysing population health needs, so health services can be planned, commissioned and redesigned. Some results may also go to health and care professionals for direct care. The main intended benefit is that providers are paid accurately and services better meet local needs.

DARS-NIC-615983-Y9Q5G.summary: NHS Bedfordshire, Luton and Milton Keynes Integrated Care Board's agreement covers invoice, risk stratification and commissioning datasets, some of which can identify patients. DARS-NIC-61864-C6X2R.summary: South Tyneside Council's agreement covers hospital data, including emergency care, admitted patients, outpatients and critical care, for its public health duties.
