DARS-NIC-656861-S5H3R.summary: The London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine's agreement covers the use of NDRS cancer registration data for people diagnosed with cancer in England and Wales between 1971 and 2018. The data is for updating the cancer survival index, a single-number summary of survival for all cancers combined up to 10 years after diagnosis. The work is commissioned by Cancer Research UK, which is a joint data controller. The index offers a simple measure for comparing survival over a very long period.

DARS-NIC-656862-L4M7T.summary: The University of Sheffield's agreement covers the use of National Disease Registration Service cancer registry data, linked to hospital, radiotherapy and chemotherapy records, for pancreatic cancer research. The data is for replicating earlier clinical trials and comparing the results, to test whether registry data can reliably show how well different cancer treatments work. The aim is better-informed healthcare decisions. The work has already produced the first Target Trial replication studies using NHS cancer registry data, and the analyses are complete.

DARS-NIC-656863-R0V6Q.summary: University College London (UCL) is using pseudonymised National Disease Registration Service cancer registration data and National Cancer Diagnosis Audit data for patients diagnosed with cancer in 2014 and 2018. The research looks at how often GPs use tests such as blood tests, endoscopy and imaging before a cancer diagnosis, and how this relates to the time taken to diagnose. It aims to identify opportunities for earlier diagnosis. So far, the findings have identified areas for quality improvement in managing and referring suspected cancer.
DARS-NIC-656863-R0V6Q.retense_draft: University College London's agreement covers the use of pseudonymised National Disease Registration Service cancer registration data and National Cancer Diagnosis Audit data for patients diagnosed with cancer in 2014 and 2018. The research examines how often GPs use tests such as blood tests, endoscopy and imaging before a cancer diagnosis, and how this relates to the time taken to diagnose. It aims to identify opportunities for earlier diagnosis. The findings have so far identified areas for quality improvement in managing and referring suspected cancer.

DARS-NIC-656866-V3H6X.summary: Health IQ Ltd, a commercial organisation, holds cancer registration, hospital, radiotherapy and systemic anti-cancer therapy data for men in England with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The agreement allows the data to be used to describe patients' characteristics, treatments, survival and NHS resource use, helping policymakers make informed decisions about care. Results have already been included in a NICE submission on Pluvicto and presented to clinical experts.

DARS-NIC-656867-F3Q3L.summary: Birmingham Women's and Children's NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers congenital anomalies data from the National Disease Registration Service. The data is for research with the British Paediatric Surveillance Unit to count new cases of congenital ichthyosis in newborn babies in the UK and Ireland, and to study how these babies are managed and how they fare in their first year. The main intended benefit is accurate information to improve care, reduce variation in practice and help avoid deaths.

DARS-NIC-656870-H0K0G.summary: The University of Warwick's agreement covers pseudonymised cancer registration, hospital admission, radiotherapy and systemic anti-cancer therapy data on women invited to breast screening in England. The data is for studying how screening age, interval and recall threshold affect benefits and harms such as false positive recalls, overdiagnosis and mortality. The aim is to inform the UK National Screening Committee and revisions to breast screening quality assurance guidelines. A paper on the dataset's quality has been published, and initial results have been presented to the Breast screening programme board.

DARS-NIC-656873-Q2C7L.summary: The University of Bristol's agreement covers pseudonymised national cancer, hospital, diagnostic imaging, radiotherapy and chemotherapy data. The data is for studying whether people with brain (intracranial) tumours have been diagnosed earlier and more often by hospital eye services since the 2016 Honey Rose court case, and how diagnosis time and route affect survival. The aim is to help design better referral pathways for suspected papilloedema. The results so far have supported two successful National Institute for Health and Care Research (NIHR) grant applications for guidelines and training.

DARS-NIC-656874-T3L9D.summary: University College London (UCL), an academic institution, is permitted to use pseudonymised cancer registration data, linked to hospital records, for people diagnosed with cancer who later developed cardiovascular disease. The research examines how well ethnicity is recorded in health data and how often cancer and cardiovascular disease occur together in different ethnic groups. It aims to inform better treatment, prevention and health service planning. A review of COVID-19's impact on multimorbid ethnic minority groups has been published in JACC CardioOncology.

DARS-NIC-656876-L4B0V.summary: University College London (UCL)'s agreement covers the use of pseudonymised national cancer registration data, including rapid registrations, for adults diagnosed with ten cancers such as lung, breast and bowel cancer. The agreement allows modelling of how delays to screening, diagnosis and treatment during COVID affect cancer stage at diagnosis, survival and demand for services. The aim is to inform policy and clinical decisions, such as waiting targets, to improve cancer care.

DARS-NIC-656877-H3Z0P.summary: Hampshire Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers the use of pseudonymised cancer registration, hospital, imaging, radiotherapy and chemotherapy data on people with neuroendocrine neoplasia, a type of cancer. The agreement allows study of how common the cancer is, how people are diagnosed, how long they survive and what their care costs, to inform policy and resource planning. The work has already led to published papers on incidence and survival in England, including sex differences in survival.

DARS-NIC-656879-L3Y5Z.summary: Evidera Ltd's agreement covers the use of pseudonymised hospital records, cancer registrations and systemic anti-cancer therapy data for adults in England diagnosed with kidney cancer between 2014 and 2018. The data is for studying treatment patterns and survival in renal cell carcinoma, and how they vary by factors such as stage at diagnosis. The aim is to help healthcare professionals better understand these patients and treatments. Results have already been presented as two conference posters in 2023.

DARS-NIC-656880-K7V7P.summary: Health IQ Ltd, a commercial organisation working for Novartis, is using pseudonymised, non-identifying national cancer registration, treatment, radiotherapy, imaging and hospital records. It is studying the treatment pathway of patients with hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer in England, including differences in access to treatment. The results are intended to support a NICE submission and a journal paper, so that policy decisions are better informed. So far, the results are guiding a future, more specific research project.
DARS-NIC-656880-K7V7P.retense_draft: Health IQ Ltd's agreement covers the use of pseudonymised, non-identifying national cancer registration, treatment, radiotherapy, imaging and hospital records. The data is for studying the treatment pathway of patients with hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer in England, including differences in access to treatment. The results are intended to support a NICE submission and a journal paper, so that policy decisions are better informed. Results already obtained have guided a future, more specific research project.

DARS-NIC-656881-X0G0X.summary: Norfolk and Norwich University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers national data on people in England diagnosed with merkel cell carcinoma, a type of skin cancer, between 2004 and 2018. The data is for examining how many people are diagnosed each year and how this varies by factors such as age, gender, ethnicity and region. It also allows examination of tumour location, stage at diagnosis, treatment and survival. The intended benefit is a better understanding of the disease's incidence, trends, risk factors and mortality.

DARS-NIC-656883-P3K5F.summary: Sandwell and West Birmingham Hospitals NHS Trust's agreement covers pseudonymised cancer registration, hospital and systemic anti-cancer therapy data on people diagnosed with oesophageal and stomach cancer. The data is for studying how well upper gastrointestinal endoscopy detects cancer and which hospital practices reduce the risk of missing it, with the aim of guiding quality improvement. Findings have already been presented at national and international conferences, won a British Society of Gastroenterology award, and appeared in a Gut abstract.

DARS-NIC-656884-R1N3C.summary: The University of Hull's agreement covers national cancer registration, cancer pathway, diagnostic imaging and linked hospital admitted patient care data. A single named researcher is studying whether people from different socioeconomic groups differ in how quickly they are diagnosed and treated for colon and ovarian cancer, and in the treatment they receive. The findings are expected to support decisions by policy-makers, clinicians and patients about cancer care. The team has published a paper on inequalities in ovarian cancer diagnosis and treatment in England.

DARS-NIC-656885-M7T5X.summary: The University of Oxford's agreement covers pseudonymised NHS England cancer registration, treatment, hospital and patient experience data on everyone diagnosed with bowel and anal cancer since 1997. The agreement allows the University to build the CORECT-R research database, which approved researchers can use to study care and outcomes, with the aim of improving bowel cancer care. One published study on post-colonoscopy bowel cancer rates helped providers improve their practice and informed a national audit.

DARS-NIC-656886-D8H1H.summary: Adelphi Group Limited, a consultancy working for Merck Sharp & Dohme (UK) Limited, is authorised to use pseudonymised national cancer registration, treatment, radiotherapy and hospital records for adults in England newly diagnosed with locally advanced head and neck squamous cell carcinoma. The agreement covers describing patient characteristics, treatments, outcomes, and healthcare use and costs. The aim is to inform health and social care planning and show where treatment could improve. Results have been presented as a poster at ESMO 2022 and an ASCO 2023 abstract.

DARS-NIC-656887-Q7M1C.summary: Adelphi Group Limited, a consultancy working with Merck Sharp & Dohme (UK) Limited, is permitted to use cancer registration, treatment, radiotherapy and hospital records for people in England with locally advanced triple negative breast cancer. The agreement allows them to describe patient characteristics, treatments, outcomes, and healthcare use and costs, to show where treatment could be improved. Results have already been published as an online abstract for the American Society of Clinical Oncology (ASCO) 2023 conference.

DARS-NIC-656890-V4L0D.summary: Genomics England, a research organisation, has an agreement with NHS England covering cancer data, including cancer registrations, treatment, radiotherapy, scan and patient survey records. The agreement allows the data to be linked to genomic and health data in its National Genomic Research Library for the 100,000 Genomes Project and NHS Genomic Medicine Service cohorts. The data is for researchers to study disease, with the aim of better diagnosis and new or more effective treatments. Reported benefits include the genomic database and support for setting up the NHS Genomic Medicine Service.

DARS-NIC-657032-T7Z5C.summary: The University of Oxford's agreement with King's College London covers NHS England hospital records (admitted patient care, outpatient and emergency care) and civil registration death records for people with motor neuron disease (MND) in England. The agreement allows these records to be linked to the MND Register's clinical data to estimate how many people have MND, study how the disease progresses and the care people need, and build a mathematical model of MND. The main intended benefit is better evidence for care planning and treatment decisions.

DARS-NIC-657422-S1K1C.summary: The University of York's agreement covers linked hospital records (emergency care, admitted patient and outpatient data) for 180 children who are fed through a gastrostomy tube and who joined the "Your Tube" study. It allows comparison of healthcare use and gastrostomy complications between children given formula feeds and those given home-blended food. The data is for providing an evidence base for national clinical guidelines and for parents' and clinicians' decisions.

DARS-NIC-658395-F0F9N.summary: The University of Essex's agreement covers school-level results from the National Child Measurement Programme, with a local authority identifier added. It is for studying whether universal free school meal schemes run by local authorities in England affect children's bodyweight, including at age 11. The main intended benefit is evidence on whether these schemes reduce childhood overweight and obesity, to inform decisions on funding them.

DARS-NIC-658720-R3V5Z.summary: The University of Warwick's agreement covers identifiable NHS England hospital, cancer registration and death records for women aged 50 or over who have had breast cancer surgery. The data is for the Mammo-50 trial and a linked observational study. They compare annual mammograms with less frequent ones, looking at survival, recurrence and hospital costs. The aim is to show whether less frequent mammograms are safe and cost-effective, which could inform national guidelines.

DARS-NIC-659282-H1F7C.summary: The Royal Marsden NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers the use of death records, hospital records and national cancer registry data on women treated for Hodgkin Lymphoma at young ages. The data is for studying their long-term risks of second cancers, other illnesses and death, so patients and clinicians can understand personal risk when choosing treatment and planning follow-up. Early results helped establish a national high-risk breast screening programme for these women.

DARS-NIC-659283-N1S1H.summary: The London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine's Cancer Survival Group's agreement covers the use of cancer registration, pathway, molecular and systemic anti-cancer therapy data for England. The data is for CONCORD-4, a programme that compares cancer survival trends between countries. The intended benefit is evidence for cancer control policy and for judging health systems. Results from earlier CONCORD cycles have already been used in OECD Health at a Glance publications, WHO reports and EU Country Health Profiles.

DARS-NIC-659284-W0T0H.summary: The University of Cambridge's agreement covers identifiable NHS England cancer registration, death, hospital admission, radiotherapy and chemotherapy data for people with oesophageal and junction cancer who consented to the OCCAMS study. The data is for identifying clinical, demographic and molecular factors affecting how the cancer develops and progresses. The aim is to better tailor treatment plans. The study has produced a revised lymph node classification giving improved prognostic information, and publications showing that circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA) levels after surgery can predict relapse.

DARS-NIC-659285-B3X8G.summary: The University of Newcastle upon Tyne's agreement covers pseudonymised National Disease Registration Service (NDRS) cancer registration data on head and neck cancers diagnosed in England between 2006 and 2014. The data is for studying the routes patients take to diagnosis and how these differ by socio-demographic factors and survival, aiming to show where inequalities exist. A published paper found that older age, deprivation and non-white ethnicity increased the likelihood of emergency diagnosis, and the team has secured further research funding.

DARS-NIC-659293-T1G7M.summary: South London and Maudsley NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers pseudonymised cancer registration, hospital, diagnostic imaging and systemic anti-cancer therapy data for people in Lambeth, Southwark, Lewisham and Croydon. The data is for studying whether people with mental disorders differ from others in cancer incidence, stage at diagnosis, treatment and survival. The aim is to identify inequalities in care so healthcare pathways can be improved. One study has so far compared cancer incidence with expected rates and confirmed earlier findings of lower-than-expected risk.

DARS-NIC-659581-D4B1S.summary: The University of Cambridge's agreement covers hospital records for children who took part in the Healthy Start, Happy Start study: Hospital Episode Statistics (admitted patient care, accident and emergency, outpatients) and the Emergency Care Data Set. The agreement allows comparison of NHS service use, and so costs, between families who received a brief parenting programme and those who did not. The aim is to assess the programme's long-term cost-effectiveness for young children at risk of challenging behaviour.

DARS-NIC-66034-M7B8W.summary: RAND Europe Community Interest Company's agreement covers the use of hospital A&E, mental health and talking therapies data to evaluate England's national Liaison and Diversion services, which support people with mental health, substance misuse or learning needs in the criminal justice system. The agreement allows examination of whether the services change people's use of health services, to help NHS England decide how to commission them. Progress reports and draft findings have been presented to the Department of Health and Social Care and NHS England.

DARS-NIC-660630-L4H3T.summary: Digital Health and Care Wales's agreement covers identifiable hospital activity data (Secondary Uses Service data for commissioners) and National Diabetes Audit data about Welsh residents, and people registered with Welsh GP practices, who are treated in England. The data is for direct care, service planning and commissioning, policy development, public health monitoring and service improvement. The main intended benefit is better management of patient pathways across the Wales-England boundary. The register lists improved patient care and joined-up health care as benefits achieved so far, without naming specific examples.

DARS-NIC-661406-H4V1B.summary: University College London Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers hospital, emergency care, outpatient, community mental health and death registration records for children and young people aged 5 to 18 in England. The data is for describing trends in mental health admissions, A&E attendances and outpatient care, and the financial cost of admissions to paediatric wards. The main intended benefit is better care for children and young people admitted in a mental health crisis.

DARS-NIC-661733-V0T9G.summary: The University of Leeds's agreement covers pseudonymised National Disease Registration Service cancer registration data and survey responses from about 34,000 people diagnosed with colorectal cancer who completed a quality of life survey. The agreement allows two PhD students to test whether patients' own survey answers improve machine learning predictions of cancer survival beyond routine healthcare data. The findings are expected to help inform care, treatment and policy decisions for cancer patients.

DARS-NIC-661736-Y2Q9R.summary: Grail Bio UK Ltd, working with the University of Oxford, is authorised to use identifiable contact details from the Personal Demographics Service for fewer than 6,240 adults who joined the SYMPLIFY cancer test trial. The data is for a mailout asking participants to agree to a further year of medical record follow-up, with a chance to opt out. The aim is to add evidence to inform care and treatment decisions for people affected by cancer. An earlier mailout reportedly enabled GRAIL LLC to complete its analysis of the test.

DARS-NIC-661742-Y2K8L.summary: The University of Leicester's agreement allows the use of pseudonymised hospital, mental health, community services, diabetes audit and death registration data for people aged 65 and over in England. The research looks at how many physical health conditions older people receiving mental health care have, compared with those who do not, and how these relate to outcomes. It aims to inform recommendations for improving physical health care for people with complex physical and mental health needs.

DARS-NIC-661854-W9V1H.summary: The University of Sheffield's agreement covers pseudonymised national cancer registry data linked to hospital, radiotherapy, cancer waiting times and systemic anti-cancer therapy records for adults with prostate or kidney cancer. The data is for testing whether this real-world data can reliably compare the effectiveness of treatments given in sequence, by replicating the results of two clinical trials. The main intended benefit is evidence on whether these data can support NHS treatment decisions where trial data are lacking.

DARS-NIC-662234-T6B7J.summary: The University of Leicester's agreement covers record-level pseudonymised NHS England cancer registration data, plus data on the quality of life of colorectal cancer survivors in England. The data is for developing new statistical methods to show how a cancer diagnosis affects survival and quality of life, and how interventions or the COVID-19 pandemic affect outcomes. The main intended benefit is better methods for future cancer survival research. To date, the team has extended methods for imputing missing cancer stage, which others will now use.

DARS-NIC-662451-S5L8J.summary: Milton Keynes University Hospital NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers pseudonymised hospital admission records and civil death registrations for 2,667 patients who had a stress echocardiogram for chest pain. The agreement allows the Trust to follow their outcomes for up to 15 years and to use machine learning to build a model predicting major cardiovascular events. The intended benefit is more accurate diagnosis, potentially reducing the need for invasive diagnostic procedures and freeing NHS resources.

DARS-NIC-662465-L3R5W.summary: Cambridge University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers identifiable hospital admission records and death registration data for a clinical trial of people receiving dialysis for end-stage kidney disease. The trial tests whether lowering blood phosphate levels towards the normal level reduces deaths and major heart and circulation events, compared with a more relaxed target. The findings are intended to inform clinical guidelines, including those from NICE.

DARS-NIC-663093-K1B0K.summary: Ipsos (Market Research) Ltd, working for the Department of Health and Social Care, is permitted to use NHS England maternity and demographic data to select mothers of newborn babies in England and send them the Infant Feeding Survey. The survey is for producing national estimates of breastfeeding and other infant feeding practices. The main intended benefit is an up-to-date evidence base to help government shape policy, guidance and support for infant feeding.

DARS-NIC-663381-C9W8N.summary: The London Borough of Bexley's agreement covers Hospital Episode Statistics and Emergency Care Data Set records, covering hospital admissions, outpatients, critical care and A&E. The agreement allows the data to be used for its public health work, including needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, commissioning and advice to NHS commissioners. The aim is locally focused analysis of health inequalities. In frailty profiling, the data helped build a business case with NHS and Adult Social Care partners to reconfigure frailty services in the borough.

DARS-NIC-663539-G7F9X.summary: The Royal College of Surgeons of England's Clinical Effectiveness Unit's agreement covers the use of national cancer registration, hospital, radiotherapy and systemic anti-cancer therapy data to run the National Lung Cancer Audit. The audit allows evaluation of the quality of NHS lung cancer care in England and Wales against standards, and highlights unexplained variation between hospitals. Its main intended benefit is helping NHS services benchmark themselves and improve care. Reports have already shown rising curative treatment rates and led to quarterly reporting from 2023.

DARS-NIC-664431-F3G8W.summary: The University of Birmingham's agreement covers hospital, outpatient, imaging, chemotherapy, radiotherapy and death records for 143 patients in the BladderPath bladder cancer trial. It allows the university to follow them for up to 24 months to see whether their disease progressed and when. The trial tests whether an MRI scan instead of a surgical procedure (TURBT) avoids unnecessary surgery and speeds up treatment for muscle invasive bladder cancer.

DARS-NIC-664530-K6Q5H.summary: Imperial College London's agreement covers the use of pseudonymised NDRS Cancer Registration data on women in England diagnosed with anal and genital cancer or high-grade precancerous lesions (HSIL). The data is for a PhD thesis that aims to establish how many women with anal cancer or HSIL have also had a genital diagnosis, and which sociodemographic factors affect risk. The intended benefit is to identify who would gain from closer anogenital surveillance, supporting earlier diagnosis and guidelines for early detection.

DARS-NIC-666525-M8L1F.summary: The University of Leeds's agreement covers the use of hospital, emergency care, mental health, medicines and death registration data to study people who attend emergency departments frequently. It allows study of their patterns of use and costs, and of how well services work. The main intended benefit is evidence to help plan better services for these patients. Findings have already been shared with NHS service teams and presented to the Department of Health and Social Care.

DARS-NIC-667040-B5T1X.summary: The Centre for Health Economics at the University of York's agreement covers NHS England hospital, mental health, community, cancer, death registration and medicines data. The data is for research on health economics, including evaluating health interventions, policy impacts, inequalities and healthcare performance. The aim is to give policymakers evidence on getting the best value from limited NHS resources. Reported benefits include evidence for policymakers on mental health crisis care services, and findings on how new heart attack care technologies affect costs and survival.

DARS-NIC-667506-N6Q9G.summary: The London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine's agreement covers the use of pseudonymised hospital, emergency care and death registration data on adults with chronic liver disease admitted to hospital as an emergency. The data is for research into how treatment and services affect care and outcomes, so that care can be organised and delivered better nationally. A method for identifying first emergency admissions has been published in JHEP Reports, and findings have been presented at a liver conference.

DARS-NIC-667559-J3L9G.summary: The University of Oxford's agreement, working with the University of Bristol, covers pseudonymised hospital admission, death registration and patient-reported outcome data for people who had hip, knee, foot or ankle surgery. The data is for studying how often complications and repeat operations occur, and whether outcomes differ with surgeon and hospital unit volume. The aim is to set benchmarks for monitoring care quality and to help patients and surgeons understand the risks of these procedures.

DARS-NIC-668928-L9N5F.summary: The University of Oxford's agreement covers linking hospital, emergency care, cancer registration and death registration records with lung health check data to develop artificial intelligence tools for diagnosing lung cancer earlier and to improve predictions of patient outcomes. The main intended benefit is more accurate and quicker lung cancer diagnosis, and better selection of people for lung cancer screening.

DARS-NIC-669808-V6T0M.summary: Cardiff University's agreement covers the use of demographic data to match identifiers so that National Paediatric Diabetes Audit records can be linked with education data in the Office for National Statistics secure research service. The data is for a study examining how diabetes-related health and educational outcomes are connected. The study aims to give evidence that could shape policy and support for children and students with diabetes. The team has presented findings to clinicians, patients and researchers, and a first paper was accepted by Diabetes Care.

DARS-NIC-669962-W1F6D.summary: Cardiff University, an academic institution, has an agreement allowing it to use National Diabetes Audit data on diabetes diagnosis, blood glucose levels and care checks for people in England and Wales. The agreement allows this data to be linked with education records to examine how diabetes-related health and educational outcomes are connected. The purpose is to give evidence that could inform changes to policy, guidance and clinical support for children and young people with diabetes.

DARS-NIC-670080-S6J0Y.summary: The International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC), the World Health Organisation's cancer agency, is permitted to use pseudonymised cancer registration data from NHS England's National Disease Registration Service. The agreement allows the data to be studied to understand how COVID-19 affected cancer diagnosis, stage, treatment and survival, as part of an international benchmarking partnership. The aim is to help countries plan ways to reduce the pandemic's indirect impact on cancer services and patients.

DARS-NIC-67135-G7D9V.summary: The University of Dundee's agreement covers linked hospital admission and death records, with pseudonymised data on trial participants, to find heart attacks, strokes and deaths in the TIME study. The study tests whether taking blood pressure medicines in the morning or the evening better prevents heart attacks and strokes. The main results found no clinically significant difference, and they have been included in international hypertension guidelines.

DARS-NIC-671668-B4T0T.summary: The University of Manchester's rapid evaluation teams (REVAL-GM and Rose-NET) are permitted to use NHS England hospital, emergency care, outpatient, community and maternity data. The data is for evaluating new ways of working in health and care services, chosen by the National Institute for Health and Care Research (NIHR), by looking at changes in service use before and after each innovation is introduced. The main intended benefit is evidence to help commissioners, policymakers and providers improve services and patient access and outcomes. No specific benefit has yet been reported.

DARS-NIC-671672-G6R6W.summary: The London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine's agreement covers pseudonymised, England-wide national cancer registration, treatment, hospital, imaging and patient survey data. The data is for developing and validating methods to identify when bowel cancer has come back after curative treatment, and for testing them on other cancers. The aim is to make recurrence routinely measurable, supporting research, monitoring of care and clinical trials. To date, the work has produced internally validated algorithms for identifying metastatic cancer and recurrence.

DARS-NIC-672111-H3R2T.summary: Imperial College London's agreement covers identifiable NHS England data on hospital admissions, demographics, mental health services, talking therapies and the National Diabetes Audit. The data is for 9,936 people in the ADDRESS-2 study, who consented to follow-up after a type 1 diabetes diagnosis. The university will study long-term health, including mental health and diabetes complications. The main intended benefit is identifying new risk factors and prevention targets to reduce long-term illness.

DARS-NIC-67398-K2Y3T.summary: Imperial College London's agreement covers record-level, pseudonymised hospital data for inpatient, outpatient and accident and emergency care in England from 2011/12 to 2021/22. The agreement allows the data to be used to study how connected hospital providers are and how fragmented patient care is between them. The data is for helping clinicians and NHS England understand patient transfers and identify hospitals vulnerable to rising demand or cyber-attacks. Published papers have already informed North West London care planning and a Royal College of Surgeons response to COVID-19.

DARS-NIC-674735-Z0H6K.summary: Cardiff University's agreement with NHS England covers the use of demographic data, with identifiers passed on for linkage in the Office for National Statistics, to study how diabetes-related health and education outcomes are linked in children and young people. The data is for building evidence that could inform changes to policy and practice, and to help clinicians support them better. The team has presented findings to clinicians, patients and researchers, and a first paper was accepted by the journal Diabetes Care.

DARS-NIC-674822-S2K9T.summary: The University of Oxford, with Oxford University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust, may use NHS England's DigiTrials Patient List Update Service to check whether very young children in the Children's Surgery Outcome Reporting (CSOR) study have died, and to get current contact addresses. This is intended to stop study communications reaching bereaved parents or guardians. The main intended benefit is to keep contact going with parents while avoiding distress. So far, hospitals have used the CSOR data to plan changes, such as a decision-making framework for infants with necrotising enterocolitis at Southampton.

DARS-NIC-674976-S4T1V.summary: University College London researchers' agreement covers use of the Adult Psychiatric Morbidity Survey 2014, a national mental health survey dataset, for a PhD study. The study examines how "complex emotional needs" (also described as personality disorder traits) relate to loneliness, self-harm and suicidal thoughts, and the role of discrimination. The main intended benefit is evidence to help develop interventions that target loneliness.

DARS-NIC-675446-G2S5Q.summary: The University of Hull's agreement covers pseudonymised cancer registration, treatment, hospital and patient survey data for adults in Yorkshire and Humberside and the North East. The agreement allows study of whether longer travel times and distances to care are linked to differences in cancer stage, treatment and survival, including for people in coastal communities. Findings could guide extra support for patients who travel further. Results have been presented at conferences and used in a PhD thesis, which informed local Cancer Alliance work on where to place mobile lung health checks.

DARS-NIC-67693-R7J5Y.summary: London Borough of Ealing, a local authority, is permitted under its agreement to use civil registration data on births and deaths, plus primary care mortality data, which includes identifiable information. The agreement allows the data to be used to understand local health needs, plan services and protect public health, including through suicide audits and hotspot mapping. The intended benefit is local services better targeted to reduce premature deaths and health inequalities. Birth information has already informed its Joint Strategic Needs Assessment, the Director of Public Health's annual report and commissioning plans.

DARS-NIC-678273-F2S0V.summary: University College London's agreement covers national cancer registration, treatment, hospital admission, radiotherapy, chemotherapy and tumour gene data for people diagnosed with lung cancer. The agreement allows the data to be used to develop and test models that predict survival and other outcomes, and to compare modelling approaches. The aim is a prognostic tool that helps clinicians and patients make treatment decisions, reducing uncertainty about outcomes. Risk prediction models have been developed.

DARS-NIC-680303-Y3X4W.summary: The University of Oxford's agreement covers identifiable hospital admission, emergency care and death registration records for about 3,000 trial participants aged 75 or over who take blood pressure medicines. The data is for comparing emergency hospital admissions and deaths between people who stop or reduce these medicines and those who continue. The aim is to show the longer-term effects of reducing blood pressure treatment, to inform clinical guidelines for older adults.

DARS-NIC-680546-S0V4K.summary: University College London's agreement covers pseudonymised hospital admission, emergency care and civil registration death records for adults in England with stroke or stroke-like symptoms. It is for studying how prehospital video triage, used since 2020 in four areas, affects patient transfer, care, outcomes such as length of stay and deaths, and value for money. The main intended benefit is to inform national guidelines and decisions on whether to roll out this triage for stroke patients.

DARS-NIC-680871-G5H4X.summary: The University of Newcastle upon Tyne's agreement covers NHS Business Services Authority data on medicines dispensed in primary care, linked to women recruited to the SWEET study. The data is for testing whether prescription records can measure how well women with early breast cancer take their hormone therapy after treatment. The wider programme aims to support women to keep taking this therapy, which could reduce the chance of breast cancer returning.

DARS-NIC-681645-M2G8X.summary: Swansea University's agreement covers pseudonymised hospital admission, accident and emergency, critical care and death registration data from NHS England. The agreement allows the University to study how introducing Emergency Admission Risk Stratification (EARS) tools affected emergency admissions, emergency department attendances, intensive care use, time in hospital, deaths and NHS costs. The intended benefit is evidence to help policy-makers decide on the future use of these tools in primary care.

DARS-NIC-681965-Y4H5P.summary: Cambridge University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers national cancer registry data on people diagnosed with cutaneous melanoma between 1995 and 2018. This includes registrations, hospital records, radiotherapy, systemic anti-cancer therapy and molecular data. The agreement allows the data to be used to build and test an online PREDICT Melanoma tool that estimates individual outcomes. The tool is intended to help patients and clinicians make better-informed decisions about investigations and treatment.

DARS-NIC-682048-S9P4H.summary: Certara UK's agreement covers the use of pseudonymised NHS England cancer registration, hospital, radiotherapy and systemic anti-cancer therapy records. The agreement allows Certara UK to study the healthcare use and costs of graft versus host disease in adults with blood cancers who have had a donor stem cell transplant in England. The aim is to show the unmet need and support better treatment, planning and use of resources.

DARS-NIC-68229-Y5J6V.summary: King's College London, an academic institution, has an agreement covering Hospital Episode Statistics data on hospital admissions, outpatient visits and A&E attendances. The agreement allows this data to be used in the CODES trial, which tests cognitive behavioural therapy for people with dissociative (non-epileptic) seizures. The data is for showing whether treatment reduces use of healthcare services. The intended benefit is evidence that could inform NHS care pathways and reduce NHS spending.

DARS-NIC-682461-D0Z7H.summary: Imperial College London's agreement covers the use of cancer registration data and linked hospital admitted patient and outpatient records. The data covers people with Lynch Syndrome, an inherited condition that raises cancer risk. The data is for a pilot registry study to understand how these patients are monitored and managed, including how common cancer diagnoses are and the quality of colonoscopy surveillance. The main intended benefit is better evidence to improve care and to support the national Bowel Cancer Screening Programme's management of Lynch Syndrome surveillance.

DARS-NIC-682529-F0V1M.summary: Royal Free London NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers the use of pseudonymised 2018 National Cancer Diagnosis Audit data from London GP practices, linked to National Disease Registration Service cancer registrations. The data is for identifying factors linked to late or delayed cancer diagnosis, by demographic group and tumour type, to support planning and earlier diagnosis. Analysis of pancreatic cancer data has already led to a wider age range for direct access abdominal CT scans across London.

DARS-NIC-682532-B4B5L.summary: Hull University Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust's agreement covers pseudonymised national cancer registry data on adults diagnosed with melanoma between 2016 and 2022. The data is for comparing how often people with head and neck melanoma are offered sentinel lymph node biopsy, a staging procedure, across England, and what treatment and outcomes follow. The study aims to show whether access should be widened. Findings so far show access varies by where people live and by area deprivation, and are being prepared for publication.

DARS-NIC-682551-T8V0S.summary: University of Southampton's agreement covers identifiable NHS England cancer registration data for 23,801 consenting patients who went to their GP with lung or colorectal symptoms. The researchers will link the data to patients' symptoms and test samples to build and validate prediction rules for lung and colorectal cancer. The aim is to help GPs quickly sort patients into those who can be reassured and those needing cancer investigations, potentially speeding up diagnosis.

DARS-NIC-682554-L6G6Q.summary: The University of York's agreement covers pseudonymised hospital, cancer registration, chemotherapy and radiotherapy records for around 4,000 children, teenagers and young adults who died from cancer in England between 2012 and 2020. The research aims to find out whether the use of high intensity treatments near the end of life varies with the model of end of life care a treatment centre provides. The findings are intended to inform NICE guidelines and the planning and funding of children's end of life care.

DARS-NIC-682565-F6C6T.summary: Queen Mary University of London's agreement covers identifiable NHS England cancer registration data (the NDRS Cancer Consolidated Data Set) for women with gynaecological cancers discussed at specialist team meetings at sites in the UK COVID and Gynaecological Cancer Study. The agreement allows the study to examine how COVID-19 changes to care and treatment delays affected long-term outcomes such as recurrence and survival. The data is for helping policymakers and clinicians plan better care during future health crises.

DARS-NIC-682571-Q6Z6Y.summary: The University of Leeds's agreement covers identifiable NHS England cancer registration, hospital admission, radiotherapy, chemotherapy and diagnostic imaging data for about 2,000 consenting bowel cancer patients in Yorkshire and the Humber. The agreement allows this data to be linked to the patients' questionnaire responses about their quality of life. The aim is to understand differences in outcomes across the region and to feed findings back to hospital teams, so that care and patient outcomes can improve.

DARS-NIC-682583-Z3V2H.summary: Adelphi Real World, a commercial organisation, has an agreement covering linked NHS England cancer registration, treatment, hospital, A&E, outpatient and diagnostic imaging data for patients with early-stage or locally advanced non-small cell lung cancer. The agreement allows the study to describe patient characteristics, treatment patterns, healthcare use, costs and survival outcomes. Its purpose is to highlight gaps in treatment and inform the use of new treatments, such as immunotherapy, to improve patient outcomes.

DARS-NIC-682587-K5N5K.summary: The UK Health Security Agency is using identifiable cancer registration data from the National Disease Registration Service for a long-term study of 43,690 UK servicemen, some of whom attended atmospheric nuclear weapons tests between 1952 and 1967. The study compares their cancer and mortality rates with those of servicemen who did not attend and with the general population. It aims to give test veterans evidence on whether their health was affected. Four analyses have been published in scientific journals, and the Ministry of Defence uses the evidence when considering matters such as War pensions.
DARS-NIC-682587-K5N5K.retense_draft: The UK Health Security Agency's agreement covers the use of identifiable cancer registration data from the National Disease Registration Service for a long-term study of 43,690 UK servicemen, some of whom attended atmospheric nuclear weapons tests between 1952 and 1967. The study compares their cancer and mortality rates with those of servicemen who did not attend and with the general population. It aims to give test veterans evidence on whether their health was affected. Four analyses have been published in scientific journals, and the Ministry of Defence has used the evidence when considering matters such as War pensions.

DARS-NIC-682588-Z0V8G.summary: The UK Health Security Agency's agreement covers identifiable individual-level NHS England cancer registration data, with linked demographics data, for people who have worked with radiation for participating employers. The data is for the long-running National Registry for Radiation Workers study, which examines how long-term occupational radiation exposure affects workers' health, especially cancer and mortality. The main intended benefit is stronger evidence on radiation risks for public health and emergency planning. Scientific papers from earlier analyses have been published open access, with plain-language summaries online.

DARS-NIC-683842-M6S8N.summary: Lane Clark & Peacock LLP, a consultancy, is permitted to analyse NHS hospital inpatient, outpatient and civil death registration data. The agreement covers analysis of delays in gynaecological care and ethnic inequalities in coronary heart disease treatment for clients including the Royal College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists and the British Heart Foundation. The aim is to help decision makers understand health needs and address inequalities. A public online dashboard on gynaecology waiting lists has been built.

DARS-NIC-683852-F5X4W.summary: The London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine, working with the University of Bristol, has an agreement allowing use of hospital admission, outpatient and critical care records linked to death registration data. The study looks at people having surgery for common vascular conditions, comparing urgent with scheduled operations, including before and during COVID-19. The main intended benefit is to show which patient groups should be prioritised for urgent surgery, to inform clinical practice and guidance.

DARS-NIC-684835-V0W0X.summary: The University of Oxford, working with Bangor University, is permitted under the agreement to use pseudonymised hospital admissions, emergency care, critical care and outpatient records for people who took part in the SuMMiT-D trial. The data is for costing hospital care and comparing the cost-effectiveness of supporting people with type 2 diabetes through brief text messages against usual care. The main intended benefit is to show NHS decision-makers whether this support offers value for money.

DARS-NIC-685917-H4X8G.summary: Imperial College London and NHS Blood and Transplant (NHSBT) are permitted to use pseudonymised hospital admission, critical care and COVID-19 treatment records for about 10,000 consenting solid organ transplant recipients. The data is for studying whether people with COVID-19 antibodies after vaccination are less likely to be hospitalised or die from COVID-19, to help guide advice for specific patient groups. The study's findings have been published in The Lancet, reporting that having antibodies was linked to lower rates of infection and hospitalisation.

DARS-NIC-686058-N9C5V.summary: The London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine's agreement covers hospital records (emergency care, admitted patient and outpatient data) for a consenting group of homeless adults in London. The agreement allows comparison of hospital use between people who had contact with a peer advocate from the Groundswell homeless health peer advocacy programme and people who did not, focusing on attendance at scheduled outpatient appointments. The data is for evidence to guide future peer advocacy services.

DARS-NIC-68697-R6F1T.summary: Dr Foster Limited, now Telstra Health UK, uses pseudonymised hospital, emergency care and death registration data. It uses them to build online benchmarking tools, bespoke analyses and published research that help NHS organisations compare quality, mortality, length of stay and efficiency. The aim is better decisions and, ultimately, better patient care. Reported results include a COVID-19 mortality dashboard, a homelessness report and analysis of admissions during the first pandemic wave, published in the Daily Telegraph.
DARS-NIC-68697-R6F1T.retense_draft: Dr Foster Limited, now Telstra Health UK, is permitted to use pseudonymised hospital, emergency care and death registration data. The data is for building online benchmarking tools, bespoke analyses and published research that help NHS organisations compare quality, mortality, length of stay and efficiency. The aim is better decisions and, ultimately, better patient care. Reported results include a COVID-19 mortality dashboard, a homelessness report and analysis of admissions during the first pandemic wave, published in the Daily Telegraph.

DARS-NIC-68703-R4Y6C.summary: The University of Oxford's agreement covers hospital admissions records (Hospital Episode Statistics) linked to civil registration death data. The data is for studying knee arthroscopy, knee replacement and foot and ankle surgery, looking at rates of surgery, complications, outcomes and variation across England. The aim is to help reduce unnecessary surgery and standardise treatment choices. Several journal articles have been published, including findings on complication risks and a 2018 guidance on meniscal surgery.

DARS-NIC-687052-V2Q0M.summary: University of Liverpool's agreement covers pseudonymised cancer registration, treatment, hospital, and diagnostic imaging data for patients in England who were diagnosed with breast cancer at 16 or over. The agreement allows auditing of survival, how often cancer spreading to the brain and spinal cord is seen, and how it is diagnosed and treated, to help inform NHS policy and treatment decisions. So far, analysis shows survival has improved over time and differs by breast cancer subtype.

DARS-NIC-687063-J3V2C.summary: The University of Exeter, working with University College London, is using pseudonymised cancer registration and National Cancer Diagnosis Audit data on people diagnosed with cancer in England. It is studying how GPs use tests, such as blood tests and imaging, for patients who later receive a cancer diagnosis, and why use varies between practices. The aim is to identify opportunities for earlier diagnosis. The study has so far identified areas for quality improvement in managing and referring suspected cancer.
DARS-NIC-687063-J3V2C.retense_draft: The University of Exeter, working with University College London, is studying how GPs use tests, such as blood tests and imaging, for patients who later receive a cancer diagnosis, and why use varies between practices. The agreement allows the use of pseudonymised cancer registration and National Cancer Diagnosis Audit data on people diagnosed with cancer in England. The aim is to identify opportunities for earlier diagnosis. The study has so far identified areas for quality improvement in managing and referring suspected cancer.

DARS-NIC-68740-X7R2N.summary: Barts Health NHS Trust's agreement covers hospital admission records and death registration data for 7,045 UK surgical patients who consented to linkage in the International Surgical Outcomes Study. The data is for studying long-term survival and hospital use after surgery, including how early complications relate to later death. The aim is to inform how surgery is planned and delivered. A published paper has already shown that socioeconomic deprivation is linked to poorer long-term survival.

DARS-NIC-687582-X2P3K.summary: The Department for Business and Trade, through its Office for Product Safety and Standards (OPSS), has an agreement covering record-level, pseudonymised Emergency Care Data Set (ECDS) data from April 2022 onwards. The agreement allows the data to be used to measure and track injuries from consumer products, spot emerging trends and understand who is affected and how. The main intended benefit is better policy, regulation and targeted communications to help prevent product-related injuries.

DARS-NIC-687619-P7W5V.summary: Middlesbrough Borough Council, a local authority, is permitted to use civil registration data on births and deaths, plus primary care mortality data, which includes identifiable details. The agreement allows the data to be used to measure local health needs, plan services and immunisation programmes, protect public health and run suicide audits. Results are to be published as aggregated statistics. The main intended benefit is local services tailored to areas of greatest need, aiming to reduce mortality and health inequalities.

DARS-NIC-68774-M1W6Q.summary: The University of York's agreement covers linked hospital admission records, civil registration death records and National Audit of Cardiac Rehabilitation data. The agreement allows the data to be used to study whether modern cardiac rehabilitation, as delivered in routine practice, reduces deaths, hospital re-admissions and repeat heart attacks over five years, by comparing people who attended with those who did not. The aim is to inform future NHS decisions on whether cardiac rehabilitation should continue to be funded.

DARS-NIC-687867-Y7L9P.summary: NHS Lincolnshire Integrated Care Board's agreement allows it to use hospital activity data (SUS for Commissioners), linked to information from wearables, smartphone sensors and online questionnaires completed by consenting participants. The data is for testing whether this combined data can predict demand for health services and adverse healthcare events. The intended benefit is to help the NHS step in sooner, target vulnerable patients before they need hospital admission, and redesign services.

DARS-NIC-688223-X1W4R.summary: The University of Nottingham's agreement covers identifiable NHS England cancer registration and death registration records for about 1,500 women in the POSNOC trial. The trial tests whether adjuvant therapy alone is no worse than adjuvant therapy plus axillary treatment (treatment of the armpit lymph nodes) for women with early-stage breast cancer and one or two affected sentinel nodes. The records are for following recurrence and survival over ten years. The main intended benefit is evidence to guide future breast cancer treatment guidelines.

DARS-NIC-688768-Y9Q9S.summary: The Institute of Cancer Research's agreement covers cancer registration, hospital admission, radiotherapy and systemic anti-cancer therapy data on patients treated with radiotherapy for oropharyngeal cancer in England. The data is for comparing their demographics with those of patients in the TORPEdO proton beam therapy trial, to see whether the trial represented the wider population. The intended benefit is fairer design of future proton beam therapy trials and better-informed commissioning decisions.

DARS-NIC-689512-S9R2Q.summary: Nottingham University Hospitals NHS Trust's agreement covers National Cancer Registration and Analysis Service cancer registration, treatment, hospital care, radiotherapy and chemotherapy data on people with T- and NK-cell lymphomas in England. The agreement allows study of how often these rare lymphomas occur, how patients are treated and how long they survive, including differences by deprivation, ethnicity and region. The aim is to support better diagnosis, outcomes and disease management. Two papers have been published, on hepatosplenic and enteropathy-associated T-cell lymphoma.

DARS-NIC-689987-Z6D2Z.summary: King's College London's agreement covers pseudonymised cancer registration data on men aged 65 to 79 in Sheffield, Rotherham and Doncaster who have been diagnosed with bladder cancer. The data is for calculating bladder cancer incidence rates and comparing them with a consented group of participants in YORKSURe, a feasibility trial of early detection through testing for non-visible blood in urine. The main intended benefit is to show whether a larger trial is viable, which could lead to earlier detection and better survival.

DARS-NIC-690385-R5D4B.summary: Lancaster University's agreement covers hospital, emergency care, mental health service, alcohol dependency and death registration data. The agreement allows researchers to study how treatment pathways and longer-term outcomes, including mortality, differ for people with mental health conditions who also have alcohol or substance use disorder, with a focus on bipolar disorder and inequalities. The findings are expected to inform screening, referral and treatment decisions and public health policy.

DARS-NIC-691697-K9L9B.summary: University College London's agreement covers NHS England records on deaths, demographics, and hospital, emergency and outpatient care for people who received pituitary-derived human growth hormone between 1959 and 1985. The agreement allows UCL to build two research databases: one to check whether recipients have higher rates of death or hospital care for neurological conditions such as stroke and dementia, and one listing people who agree to be contacted about future research. The main intended benefit is to confirm whether recipients are at risk of these conditions, so they can be monitored and cared for.

DARS-NIC-692254-N3J5W.summary: University College London (UCL), an academic organisation, is permitted under the agreement to use pseudonymised NHS England hospital, cancer registration and death records for men identified as subfertile through the Human Fertilisation and Embryology Authority register. The agreement covers studying their risks of long-term cancers, other health conditions and early death, compared with men from the general population. The main intended benefit is better evidence on the long-term health needs of subfertile men, to help with early detection and prevention.

DARS-NIC-692602-Q6P4F.summary: Neo Health Hub Limited, a commercial company, is permitted under the agreement to use linked hospital data (Emergency Care Data Set, Hospital Episode Statistics admitted patient care and outpatients) with medicines dispensed in primary care. The agreement allows it to build dashboards, reports and bespoke analyses on prescribing and its links to hospital activity, for NHS bodies and approved others, aiming to improve prescribing and patient safety. The agreement allows NHS medicines optimisation teams to use its free respiratory and insomnia dashboards, and it has produced requested custom analyses.

DARS-NIC-69431-K1K8R.summary: NHS England Direct Commissioning's agreement allows it to use pseudonymised hospital, emergency care, outpatient, mental health and other local provider data for the services NHS England commissions directly, such as specialised services, armed forces and health in justice. The data is for producing commissioning reports, checking invoices and analysing readmissions and budgets. The aim is to support commissioning and contracting, monitor quality and finances, and ensure public funds are spent properly on patient care.

DARS-NIC-694476-T3R6K.summary: The University of Aberdeen's agreement covers hospital admissions and outpatient records for 387 women in England who took part in the HEALTH trial. The data is for following them for five to eight years to compare two treatments for heavy menstrual bleeding: laparoscopic supracervical hysterectomy and endometrial ablation. The study looks at further treatment, late side effects and cost-effectiveness. It aims to help patients, clinicians and NHS decision-makers choose between the treatments.

DARS-NIC-694500-C0W0K.summary: The Medicines and Healthcare Products Regulatory Agency (MHRA)'s agreement covers pseudonymised data from the Surgical Devices and Implants Data Set, including its Pelvic Floor Registry module. It allows analysis of how many pelvic mesh or tape procedures, and alternatives, were recorded for stress urinary incontinence and pelvic organ prolapse. The aim is to test whether this data can support safety monitoring of pelvic mesh devices. The main intended benefit is better-informed regulatory vigilance and decisions on mesh use.

DARS-NIC-695075-J7Y2H.summary: The University of Manchester, working with the University of York, is permitted to use pseudonymised hospital admission, emergency care and civil registration of death data from April 2013 onwards. The research is to compare the quality and safety of care in NHS and independent hospitals and to look at how clinical governance works across both. The main intended benefit is better evidence for policy-makers, clinicians and patients choosing where to receive care.

DARS-NIC-696708-J3L1R.summary: King's College London, with Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust, is using civil registration death data (date and cause of death) for people in the South London Stroke Register. They will link it with existing register data to study the long-term outcomes, needs and care costs of stroke survivors. The main intended benefit is evidence to help policymakers and services plan future stroke care.

DARS-NIC-69707-G0Q7Z.summary: RM Partners, an independent sector healthcare provider running a cancer alliance in West London, uses Hospital Episode Statistics and Emergency Care Data Set records covering hospital, outpatient, critical care and A&E activity. It uses them to produce comparative performance reports on cancer services, to find areas needing improvement and variation between providers. The aim is better cancer care and less variation. Reported results include redesigned prostate, colorectal and lung pathways and published two-week-wait volumes.
