The agreement allows these to produce comparative performance reports on cancer services, to find areas needing improvement and variation between providers. The aim is better cancer care and less variation. Reported results include redesigned prostate, colorectal and lung pathways and published two-week-wait volumes.

DARS-NIC-69751-C0M8P.summary: Nottinghamshire Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers hospital admission records and death registration data for patients admitted to or discharged from Arnold Lodge Medium Secure Unit in Leicester. The research looks at deaths and readmissions to psychiatric care among these patients, extending an earlier study to cover admissions up to June 2013 and a longer follow-up. The aim is to improve understanding of outcomes after medium secure care, so that services can plan support for people who may be particularly vulnerable.

DARS-NIC-698157-B0L5B.summary: Certara UK's agreement covers use of National Disease Registration Service cancer registration data (the NDRS Cancer Consolidated Data Set). The data is for assessing whether it is good enough to support research into CAR-T cell therapy, a treatment for blood cancers, by checking its quality, completeness and reliability. The main intended benefit is more efficient, robust research that helps inform regulators, clinicians and patients about the safety and effectiveness of these therapies.

DARS-NIC-698171-K4M0B.summary: The Home Office, a ministerial department, has an agreement that allows it to use aggregated hospital admission counts from Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care. These cover people admitted to hospital in England because of drug misuse or poisoning, the mental and behavioural effects of drugs or alcohol, or assault by a firearm or sharp object. The data is for monitoring drug use, drug-related harm and serious violence, and for assessing policies such as the County Lines Programme and Project ADDER. The main intended benefit is better drug policy and fewer drug-related harms.

DARS-NIC-699963-K1C6T.summary: Queen Mary University of London's agreement allows it to use NHS England's recruitment service, which provides mailing details for adult women in England, to invite people to join the PROTECT-C study. The study is for testing a population-wide genetic testing approach to identify women at higher risk of breast, ovarian, womb and bowel cancer. It is expected to provide evidence on whether such testing could be offered nationally, helping to prevent cancers.

DARS-NIC-700125-B2Z7J.summary: Young Epilepsy, a charity, has an agreement covering identifiable demographics data about 112 children who took part in the EPIPEG study. The agreement allows it to find their up-to-date addresses and check whether any have died. This lets it send invitations to the Turning6 follow-up study at 60 months to parents and carers, and avoid contacting families whose child has died. The aim is to reach enough participants for the study to produce meaningful results.

DARS-NIC-700547-S2M9L.summary: Corevitas's agreement covers the use of national cancer registration, treatment, radiotherapy, chemotherapy and hospital records for people in England with hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer. The agreement allows study of how the disease progresses from early to metastatic stages, which treatments people receive, whether age, ethnicity or deprivation affect access, and how often CDK4/6 inhibitor doses are reduced. The study also covers hospital resource use. The main intended benefit is better-informed treatment decisions for patients.

DARS-NIC-701654-Q5Z9T.summary: The Newcastle upon Tyne Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers linked national cancer registration, hospital admission, radiotherapy and systemic anti-cancer therapy data. The data is for studying patients who received four chemotherapies that have left the Cancer Drug Fund. The work compares their real-world outcomes with clinical trial results, to test whether routine NHS data can support future National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) guidance. The main intended benefit is to inform national guidance updates for these treatments.

DARS-NIC-701727-S2X0Q.summary: Bristol NHS Foundation Trust's agreement, with the University of Bristol and Change Grow Live, covers pseudonymised hospital, emergency care and death registration records for adults prescribed methadone or buprenorphine for opioid dependence. The data is for studying how the suspension of supervised opioid treatment during the COVID-19 pandemic relates to overdoses, drug-related deaths and how long people stay in treatment. The findings are intended to inform future practice and policy on supervising this treatment.

DARS-NIC-70235-T6P9F.summary: The Met Office's agreement covers NHS England hospital data, including admitted patient care, accident and emergency and emergency care records, for its Health Programme. The agreement allows the data to be used to develop and evaluate health forecasting services and to research how weather, climate and air quality affect health and hospital use. The aim is to help warn people of environmental hazards and help plan health services. Published research papers and heatwave and cold weather planning have already drawn on this work.

DARS-NIC-705741-K8K9G.summary: The Office for National Statistics's agreement with NHS England covers demographic data for use in the ONS Longitudinal Study, which links census and life events records for about 1% of the population of England and Wales. The agreement allows the Office to maintain a pseudonymised research database that approved researchers can use under strict controls. The data is for research on topics such as health inequalities and ageing. The study has already supplied evidence for government reports on health inequalities and for National Statistics on life expectancy.

DARS-NIC-705821-P6J0H.summary: ModernaTX, Inc, a pharmaceutical and biotechnology company, is permitted to use contact details and basic health information from people who signed up to the NHS England COVID-19 Vaccine Research Registry. The agreement allows NHS England to use this information to invite potentially eligible people to take part in the NextCOVE trial of a COVID-19 booster vaccine. The main intended benefit is faster recruitment, which should speed up the development of effective vaccines.

DARS-NIC-705902-L2J0F.summary: King's College London's agreement covers the use of hospital admissions, accident and emergency, death registration and community prescribing data. The agreement allows the data to estimate how many children and young people up to age 25 in England live with a life-limiting condition, and how complex their conditions are, including their use of medicines. The main intended benefit is better planning and funding of children's palliative care and hospice services.

DARS-NIC-706399-T8V0C.summary: The University of Warwick's agreement covers the use of Civil Registrations of Death data for the ADAPT-Sepsis Trial. The trial tests whether daily blood tests for the biomarkers CRP or PCT can safely shorten antibiotic treatment in hospitalised adults with suspected sepsis. The main intended benefit is reducing antibiotic exposure while keeping patients safe, which could change NHS care and guidance.

DARS-NIC-706484-D0Y6F.summary: The University of Leeds, an academic organisation, is permitted to use identifiable hospital records (admitted patient care, critical care and outpatients) and death registration data for people who took part in a stroke trial. The agreement allows this data to be used to cost participants' hospital care and to compare this with what participants report themselves. The main intended benefit is to show whether routine data can replace self-reported data in future stroke studies, reducing the data collection burden on patients.

DARS-NIC-706945-F6W2C.summary: York and Scarborough Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust's agreement allows the use of pseudonymised hospital admission records and death registration data for about 98,000 people in England with hereditary haemochromatosis, an inherited iron disorder. The data is for studying how many develop cirrhosis (liver scarring) and its complications, and the risk factors involved. The aim is to help services and clinicians review care for these patients.

DARS-NIC-707577-H0F4Z.summary: The University of Leeds's agreement covers identifiable hospital, emergency care, death registration and dispensed-medicine data for patients in the ALABAMA trial of penicillin allergy testing in primary care. It allows comparison of patients who had testing with those who had usual care, looking at hospital stays, deaths, antibiotic use and costs. The main intended benefit is more selective use of second-line antibiotics, which would help limit antibiotic resistance.

DARS-NIC-707682-B4H2R.summary: The University of York's agreement covers the use of pseudonymised hospital admission, accident and emergency, emergency care and death registration records for children who died aged 18 or under. The data is for studying differences in emergency hospital care in the last 12 months of life and in place of death, including how these relate to 24/7 paediatric palliative care services. The findings are intended to inform the development of such a service in the Yorkshire region.

DARS-NIC-708052-S1L9J.summary: London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine, working with King's College Hospital NHS Foundation Trust, is using demographic data on adults with chronic liver disease admitted to hospital as an emergency. It is used to link patients to intensive care records held by ICNARC (Intensive Care National Audit & Research Centre). The aim is to study critical care use and regional variation in care, so that services for acutely ill liver patients can be made safer and more effective. A related project's method for identifying first emergency admissions has been published in JHEP Reports.
DARS-NIC-708052-S1L9J.retense_draft: London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine, working with King's College Hospital NHS Foundation Trust, is allowed to use demographic data on adults with chronic liver disease admitted to hospital as an emergency. The data is for linking patients to intensive care records held by ICNARC (Intensive Care National Audit & Research Centre). The aim is to study critical care use and regional variation in care, so that services for acutely ill liver patients can be made safer and more effective. A related project's method for identifying first emergency admissions has been published in JHEP Reports.

DARS-NIC-708642-D2Z8T.summary: The University of Hull's agreement covers the use of hospital admissions data (Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care) from NHS hospitals in England. The data is for studying how alcohol care teams affect hospital activity, including 30-day readmissions after alcohol-related admissions, and the costs involved, by comparing the 24 months before and after teams were optimised. The findings are intended to inform how NHS England and other bodies commission these services.

DARS-NIC-709342-K9Z8V.summary: Queen Mary University of London's agreement, working with University College London, covers pseudonymised national cancer registry data (the NDRS Cancer Consolidated Data Set) on men diagnosed with prostate cancer in England between 2013 and 2022. The agreement allows study of whether survival and treatment patterns, including first treatments and treatment intensification for metastatic disease, differ by ethnic group. The intended benefit is to help identify inequalities and guide interventions that improve treatment uptake and patient outcomes.

DARS-NIC-709746-N2T6T.summary: Cardiff University is using NHS England hospital, emergency care, outpatient, critical care and community services records to follow up women who give birth in 36 UK maternity units taking part in the Obstetric Bleeding Study UK trial. The trial tests whether a set of care steps for bleeding after childbirth reduces major bleeding and blood transfusion, and whether it is good value for money. The aim is to give decision-makers evidence to improve care for women who bleed heavily after birth. Benefits reported so far include the implementation of the care package across the participating units and the collection of trial data, but final results are still pending.
DARS-NIC-709746-N2T6T.retense_draft: Cardiff University's agreement covers the use of NHS England hospital, emergency care, outpatient, critical care and community services records to follow up women who give birth in 36 UK maternity units taking part in the Obstetric Bleeding Study UK trial. The trial tests whether a set of care steps for bleeding after childbirth reduces major bleeding and blood transfusion, and whether it is good value for money. The aim is to give decision-makers evidence to improve care for women who bleed heavily after birth. Benefits reported so far include the implementation of the care package across the participating units and the collection of trial data, but final results are still pending.

DARS-NIC-709865-W9X6H.summary: The Royal College of Surgeons of England's agreement covers the use of pseudonymised patient data, including cancer registrations, hospital records, treatment, imaging, emergency care and medicines data, for the National Cancer Audit Collaborating Centre (NATCAN). The data is for ten national audits of cancer care delivered by NHS providers, so services can benchmark performance and identify unwarranted variation. The main intended benefit is better care quality, outcomes and equity of care.

DARS-NIC-712819-X8G2J.summary: The University of Oxford's agreement covers hospital admissions, accident and emergency, and maternity services data. The data is for studying how changes in the way maternity care is delivered, such as continuity of care, visit and scan frequency, and staffing, affect care pathways and health outcomes. The aim is to inform NHS policy and reduce health inequalities in maternity care. The agreement allows preliminary models to be built to test some of the main hypotheses, and the team has already built preliminary models that tested some of them.

DARS-NIC-714765-G1P5S.summary: The University of Oxford's agreement covers pseudonymised hospital, emergency care and death registration data from 2016/17 to 2023/24. The data is for studying whether waiting times in emergency departments differ by socioeconomic status, and whether longer waits lead to worse health outcomes. The aim is to give evidence that helps reduce any inequalities in waiting times. Preliminary results have been presented to the Department of Health and Social Care and NHS England.

DARS-NIC-715080-X0J9J.summary: The University of Manchester's agreement covers pseudonymised cancer registration, hospital admission, outpatient, radiotherapy and systemic anti-cancer therapy data for patients in England. The agreement allows the data to be used to study how socio-economic status and other health conditions affect cancer patients' treatment and outcomes, and to map the cause-and-effect relationships between them. The main intended benefit is evidence to reduce health inequalities and improve the fairness and quality of cancer care across the NHS.

DARS-NIC-715599-M3G8T.summary: The University of Leeds's agreement covers the use of hospital admissions, outpatient and national cancer registration data for a PhD research project on people with cystic fibrosis (CF). The project aims to measure cancer risk and outcomes in this group and identify who is at higher risk. The main intended benefit is evidence to inform screening, surveillance and educational resources for people with CF.

DARS-NIC-71603-T8C0Q.summary: The London Borough of Islington, a local authority, is using pseudonymised hospital data, covering admissions, outpatients, critical care and accident and emergency (A&E) attendances. It uses this data for its public health duties, including needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, advice to NHS commissioners and the annual public health report. The aim is locally focused analysis of health outcomes and inequalities. Since May 2023 it has used the data for work on hypertension, alcohol licensing, a London-wide chemsex needs assessment and a review of the local Healthy Start programme.

DARS-NIC-717299-R5H5N.summary: The University of Oxford's agreement covers identifiable NHS England data on hospital admissions, deaths and demographics for children with six surgical conditions. The data is for identifying and inviting eligible children's parents to join the Children's Surgery Outcome Reporting research database, and for checking that all eligible cases are captured. The main intended benefit is spotting unwarranted variation between hospitals, so that feedback to hospitals can help improve children's care.

DARS-NIC-717428-M3S8H.summary: The University of Birmingham's agreement covers NHS England's emergency care hospital data, covering attendances at type 1 emergency departments from 2018 to 2023. The agreement allows research that applies process mining to map how patients move through emergency departments and compares these patient flows, waiting times, admissions and outcomes across NHS trusts. The aim is to help trusts and policy makers redesign emergency care services and use resources more efficiently.

DARS-NIC-717485-F8L6H.summary: Evidera Ltd, a research organisation working for Sanofi Pasteur, is covered by an NHS England data sharing agreement for hospital admissions, COVID-19 tests and vaccinations, GP records and deaths. The agreement allows the data to study how well the VidPrevtyn Beta® COVID-19 booster protects against hospitalisation with laboratory-confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection, compared with people not boosted in the same period. The intended main benefit is real-world evidence for regulators such as the MHRA and the European Medicines Agency (EMA) to inform future booster campaigns.

DARS-NIC-717493-V2R4K.summary: The National Institute for Cardiovascular Outcomes Research's agreement allows the use of identifiable civil registration death and demographic data to link with national heart audit and TAVI registry records for Welsh patients. The aim is to report patient outcomes and compare the quality of cardiac care between hospitals, so that care can improve. Reported benefits include annual patient reports, risk models for heart failure and heart attack audits, and findings on how COVID-19 affected cardiac services.

DARS-NIC-717832-F6F3H.summary: The University of Oxford's agreement covers the use of NHS England hospital, emergency care, cancer, death, diabetes audit, imaging and dispensed medicines records for people who joined the ASCEND PLUS clinical trial. The records are for following participants' health, including heart attacks, strokes, kidney decline, dementia and deaths. The data is for showing whether long-term use of oral semaglutide is effective and safe for people aged 55 or over with type 2 diabetes. The results could inform national and international treatment guidelines.

DARS-NIC-719601-J7Z2S.summary: Hull University Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust's agreement covers pseudonymised patient data from national heart audits, linked to hospital admission, emergency care and death registration records. The data is for studying how much diabetes affects survival, stent re-narrowing and repeat heart attacks in people with heart disease, using machine learning. The main intended benefit is finding new links between diabetes and heart disease, to help identify higher-risk groups and target preventative treatment.

DARS-NIC-719879-K6X3J.summary: Sandwell and West Birmingham Hospitals NHS Trust's agreement covers pseudonymised National Disease Registration Service cancer registration data on patients diagnosed with upper gastrointestinal cancer after an earlier endoscopy. The data is for studying why some of these cancers are missed at endoscopy, to help endoscopy units improve quality and reduce missed diagnoses. The study has identified the main reasons cancers are missed and the procedural risk factors involved, and reported these to endoscopy providers.

DARS-NIC-719923-Q5H1S.summary: Imperial College London's agreement covers linked hospital, emergency care, cancer registration, death registration and demographic records for participants in the LOLIPOP study of UK South Asians. The data is for studying how genetic, lifestyle and environmental factors relate to heart disease, type-2 diabetes, cancer and other chronic conditions. The aim is to inform prevention and health policy for this group. The study's resource has already supported over 225 peer-reviewed publications.

DARS-NIC-720122-Y6Q0Y.summary: The University of Essex's agreement covers hospital admission, outpatient and death registration records for people in England who have had a stroke. The research, part of a PhD, looks at how factors such as age, gender, ethnicity, deprivation and coastal or urban location combine to affect deaths within 30 days and one year of a stroke, and the care pathways patients follow. It aims to give policymakers evidence to make stroke care more inclusive and improve outcomes.

DARS-NIC-72064-V5V2X.summary: London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine's agreement allows the linking of national hospital, cancer and death records for people in England with liver cancer (hepatocellular carcinoma) and those who went on to have a liver transplant. The data is for studying risk factors, treatment choices and survival after transplant, including the use of donor livers after circulatory death, to help improve patient selection and donor liver allocation. Five papers were published in 2019 and 2020, and the study reports that these donor livers did not worsen survival.

DARS-NIC-721538-N6B1V.summary: King's College London's agreement covers the linking of identifiable civil registration death records to data on about 300,000 hospital-admitted stroke patients. The data is for the Sentinel Stroke National Audit Programme (SSNAP), which King's College London runs. The aim is to report 30-day and longer-term survival rates for hospitals and health boards so services can improve stroke care. Outlier trusts have been contacted and offered peer review visits, and a 2018 Lancet paper on socioeconomic disparities has been published.

DARS-NIC-72180-R2L5Y.summary: The University of Glasgow's agreement covers NHS England hospital admission records and mortality and cohort notification data for the FAST trial, which compared the heart safety of two gout medicines, febuxostat and allopurinol. The data is for finding serious adverse events and study endpoints that had not been reported. The main intended benefit is clearer safety information for patients, prescribers and regulators. The main results have been published in The Lancet and a final report has been submitted to the European Medicines Agency.

DARS-NIC-72318-M4W8J.summary: Imperial College London's Big Data and Analytical Unit's agreement covers the use of Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care data, linked to month and year of death, for a PhD research study. The study compares two ways of timing gallbladder removal surgery, immediate or after discharge and readmission, including their costs. It aims to show decision makers which approach offers better value, potentially saving money and improving patient care.

DARS-NIC-724508-B4V3Q.summary: Queen Mary University of London's agreement covers hospital, outpatient, mental health and death registration records for about 10,000 consenting participants in the PREDICT-PD study. The records are linked to the study participants to follow up who goes on to develop Parkinson's disease, related neurodegenerative conditions or who dies, because following participants directly is impractical. The aim is to refine predictive algorithms so people at risk of Parkinson's can be identified earlier.

DARS-NIC-726177-R0H8V.summary: The University of Newcastle upon Tyne's agreement allows the use of hospital admitted patient, outpatient and national cancer registry data to study head and neck cancer. It is examining how diagnosis, treatment and survival differ by area deprivation and region of England, including before and during the COVID-19 pandemic. The aim is to inform policy and services that reduce inequalities. So far, the work has led to new research collaborations and the basis of a further funding proposal.

DARS-NIC-72626-V4P9B.summary: Nottingham University Hospitals NHS Trust's agreement covers hospital, cancer registration, diagnostic imaging, death and demographic records for about 4,264 people with hepatitis C-related liver cirrhosis in a UK research cohort. The data is for studying which patients go on to serious liver complications, including liver cancer, and how outcomes change after a hepatitis C cure. The aim is to help clinicians tailor monitoring and care to individual risk. Published analyses include studies on liver cancer risk, mortality after cure, and uptake of liver cancer surveillance.

DARS-NIC-726391-M6D4Z.summary: The University of Oxford's agreement covers civil registration death records, linked to archived health records of about 3,000 veterans treated for head injuries at a Second World War military hospital in Oxford. The data is for updating the group's mortality information by 21 years. It aims to show the long-term effects of penetrating brain injuries on life expectancy and health. The main intended benefit is evidence on lifelong outcomes, to help shape traumatic brain injury management guidelines.

DARS-NIC-726539-S6T2F.summary: Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers identifiable hospital admission and death registration data for a consented group of 10,007 patients who had heart scans (cardiac magnetic resonance, or CMR) at Wythenshawe Hospital. The agreement allows the data to be used to study how CMR findings relate to survival, hospital admission and heart conditions such as heart failure and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. The main intended benefit is earlier detection and better risk prediction for heart failure.

DARS-NIC-727325-W4M7T.summary: NHS England and King's College London's agreement covers the joint use of national cancer registration, hospital, radiotherapy and chemotherapy data for the PRECISION study. The data is for examining the risk of breast cancer developing in the opposite breast after ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS), a non-invasive breast cancer, compared with invasive breast cancer, and which factors predict it. The intended benefit is to identify patients at higher risk, so that treatment can be tailored and overtreatment avoided.

DARS-NIC-727343-L3N2H.summary: The Royal College of Physicians of London's agreement covers the use of pseudonymised civil registration death records for adults admitted to Welsh hospitals with asthma attacks. The agreement allows these records to be linked to audit data to show whether hospital care led to good or poor outcomes, using deaths within 30 and 90 days. The aim is to improve care standards and reduce readmissions and deaths. A 2023 outcomes report has already informed recommendations on how services are resourced.

DARS-NIC-727507-W9V7H.summary: Queen Mary University of London (an academic institution) may use pseudonymised hospital admission and civil death registration data for people in the British Spine Registry, plus a comparison group who had routine spinal operations. The data is for checking the accuracy of the Registry and assessing outcomes of common spinal operations for low back pain, including the effect of patient and surgical factors. The aim is to help clinicians and patients understand the risks and benefits of each procedure.

DARS-NIC-727537-C3V4G.summary: The Royal College of Physicians of London's agreement covers the use of pseudonymised civil registration death records for adults in the Welsh COPD (chronic obstructive pulmonary disease) hospital audit. The agreement allows the records to be linked to audit data to measure deaths within 30 and 90 days of admission, to show whether hospital care led to good outcomes. The aim is better COPD care and lower mortality. Outcome reports published so far have been used by services to benchmark performance and plan improvements.

DARS-NIC-727610-S2V3N.summary: University College London (UCL) is using pseudonymised Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care data, covering hospital admissions in England from 1997/98 onwards. Researchers are studying how different ways of paying hospitals affect their efficiency, costs and quality of care, and why providers respond differently. The main intended benefit is evidence to help policymakers design payment models that lead to shorter waiting times and better care.
DARS-NIC-727610-S2V3N.retense_draft: University College London's agreement covers the use of pseudonymised Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care data, covering hospital admissions in England from 1997/98 onwards. The data is for studying how different ways of paying hospitals affect their efficiency, costs and quality of care, and why providers respond differently. The main intended benefit is evidence to help policymakers design payment models that lead to shorter waiting times and better care.

DARS-NIC-727732-M8C2N.summary: Norfolk and Norwich University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers pseudonymised national cancer registration data on melanoma in situ in England, covering 2013 to 2023. The agreement allows study of how often lentigo maligna occurs, how long patients survive, and how likely it is to progress to melanoma. The aim is to help patients and clinicians make better-informed decisions about managing the condition.

DARS-NIC-727954-G5X8B.summary: The Royal College of Physicians of London's agreement covers pseudonymised civil registration death records for children and young people admitted to hospital with asthma attacks in England and Wales. The agreement allows the records to be linked to audit data to measure deaths within 30 and 90 days and readmissions. The aim is to show whether hospital care led to good outcomes and to improve care. Outcomes published in 2023 for earlier patients informed recommendations on how services are resourced.

DARS-NIC-729128-M5N1F.summary: King's College London's agreement covers identifiable demographic data about people recruited to the South London Stroke Register, a long-running study of stroke in a defined area of London. The data is for confirming which participants have died and for giving current addresses of those still alive, so that a newsletter can update them about the study and how to opt out. The intended benefit is to maintain contact with survivors while avoiding distress to families of those who have died.

DARS-NIC-729560-F2F3S.summary: King's College London's agreement covers identifiable demographic data from the NHS Population Demographics Service, covering twins born in England and Wales in 1994 to 1996 who take part in the Twins' Early Development Study. The agreement allows the use of current contact details to send information about linking their medical records to the study. The aim is to make the study's health findings more representative, including of people who have lost touch with it. Addresses from an earlier agreement let over 11,000 participants be included in this information campaign.

DARS-NIC-72957-B6S3P.summary: NHS South Kent Coast CCG's agreement covers pseudonymised (identifiable details removed) mental health, talking therapies (Improving Access to Psychological Therapies) and children and young people's health data for its own area. The agreement allows the data to be used to monitor and evaluate commissioned services, including access against NHS Constitution targets, and to check that enough capacity is commissioned. The main intended benefit is better-informed commissioning, including support for service planning and early intervention.

DARS-NIC-72971-J6V4C.summary: NHS Ashford CCG (Clinical Commissioning Group) agreement covers pseudonymised mental health, talking therapy and children and young people's health data, covering both clinical and financial information. The data is for planning and commissioning health services for people in its area, including analysing population needs, modelling how services interact and identifying patients at risk. The main intended benefit is better-planned services that improve patient flow and access.

DARS-NIC-72982-T7F3W.summary: NHS Thanet CCG's agreement covers the use of pseudonymised, locality-limited data on mental health, psychological therapies, children and young people's health, community services and cancer waiting times. The agreement allows the data to be used to monitor and review commissioned services, including access against NHS constitution targets and whether enough capacity is commissioned. The main intended benefit is better commissioning, with improved planning, service quality and access based on a better understanding of local patient needs.

DARS-NIC-72994-C1X0P.summary: NHS Canterbury and Coastal CCG's agreement covers pseudonymised mental health, psychological therapies, and children and young people's health data, which includes clinical and financial information. The data is for analysing the needs of the local population and planning and commissioning health services, with processing carried out by NHS South Kent Coast CCG. The main intended benefit is better planning of services and patient pathways, improving quality and access to care.

DARS-NIC-730384-H8G0Q.summary: The University of Birmingham's agreement covers the use of NHS England data quality report records, which hold customer contact and mortality details, for the PRISM follow-up research study. The data is for checking whether women who took part in the PRISM trial of progesterone in early pregnancy, and their children, are still alive and confirming their postal addresses. This allows the study team to send consent packages for long-term follow-up without contacting families in upsetting circumstances.

DARS-NIC-730458-M8D6M.summary: Royal Papworth Hospital NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers the use of pseudonymised hospital admissions data (Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care) for people in England who survived a cardiac arrest and then had a defibrillator implanted. The data is for estimating how common idiopathic ventricular fibrillation, a rare heart rhythm condition with no identified cause, is in England. The main intended benefit is to guide resources towards diagnosing and managing the condition, and to support further research.

DARS-NIC-732228-T8Q0V.summary: Leeds Institute of Health Sciences, part of the University of Leeds, is permitted to use NHS England death registration and cancer registration data on 9,046 people who agreed to take part in the Yorkshire Lung Screening Trial. The trial tests whether inviting smokers and ex-smokers aged 55 to 80 to community-based low dose CT lung screening, compared with usual care, improves lung cancer outcomes. The main intended benefit is evidence to guide the design of lung cancer screening programmes in the UK.

DARS-NIC-733055-Y4J1B.summary: The London School of Economics and Political Science (LSE) agreement allows use of pseudonymised heart attack audit data (the Myocardial Ischaemia National Audit Project) and civil registrations of death for adults admitted to hospitals in England and Wales between April 2010 and March 2023. The data is for evaluating how hospital factors, including mergers, affect quality and safety of care, and whether treatment and care quality differ between patient groups. The aim is to inform policy and treatment decisions and improve outcomes after a heart attack.

DARS-NIC-733084-C6R1J.summary: The University of Warwick's agreement covers pseudonymised hospital, emergency care and death registration records for 5,945 patients who survived to hospital admission after an out-of-hospital cardiac arrest in the PARAMEDIC-3 trial. The data is for comparing survival, hospital and intensive care use, and NHS costs between two ways of giving adrenaline: into a vein or into a bone. The intended benefit is evidence that could shape national and international resuscitation guidelines.

DARS-NIC-733503-V0X9Q.summary: Genomics England, a research organisation, is permitted to receive linked NHS hospital, emergency care, diagnostic imaging, community, maternity and death records for babies in the Generation Study. The agreement allows the data to be used in its National Genomics Research Library to evaluate whole genome sequencing of newborns, looking at cost effectiveness, health outcomes and the impact on the NHS. The aim is to find out whether babies with treatable rare genetic conditions can be diagnosed and treated earlier.

DARS-NIC-734202-N9F7P.summary: Cardiff University's agreement with Velindre University NHS Trust covers identifiable Civil Registrations of Death data (date of death only) for about 900 consenting participants in the PATHOS clinical trial of reduced-intensity treatment for HPV-positive throat cancer. The data is for checking that NHS sites have reported all deaths, and reported them correctly. The intended benefit is accurate survival data, so the trial can answer its research question reliably.

DARS-NIC-734273-H8R3Q.summary: The Institute of Occupational Medicine's agreement covers the use of identifiable death registration and demographic records for a group of about 15,000 to 22,000 former professional footballers. The agreement allows the data to be used to study whether heading footballs during a playing career is linked to a higher risk of dying from neurological diseases, and how their mortality compares with the general population. The findings are intended to inform policy to protect players' health and could lead to a review of heading in football.

DARS-NIC-73469-F3B9N.summary: The University of Manchester's agreement covers the use of aggregated hospital admissions data from Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care, with no identifying details. The data is for studying whether general practice performance under the Quality and Outcomes Framework, a pay-for-performance scheme, relates to hospital admissions across England between 2006 and 2019. The main intended benefit is evidence for the NHS and policy makers on whether the scheme works and how resources can best be used.

DARS-NIC-734773-Y3P3J.summary: University College London's agreement covers identifiable NHS England records on deaths registered in England between 2021 and 2023, together with hospital admitted patient care and critical care records. The data is for measuring how many deaths were linked to antimicrobial resistance (when infections no longer respond to antibiotics) and how this changed over time. The study also aims to set up a way for public health authorities to calculate these deaths from routine data. The main expected benefit is better evidence for managing drug-resistant infections.

DARS-NIC-736273-V5T6V.summary: Adelphi Group Limited, a consultancy working for Pfizer Limited, has an agreement that allows it to use hospital admission, critical care and death registration records. The data is for studying how often hospitalised children in England (aged 0-17) are admitted with invasive fungal infections, how much hospital care they use and how many die, comparing those with and without a past infection-related admission. The aim is to improve understanding of the risks and the need for better prevention and treatment.

DARS-NIC-736310-S6T1Z.summary: The NHS Counter Fraud Authority's agreement allows it to use hospital, emergency care, death registration, demographic and primary care medicines data to look for fraud and other crime in the NHS. The data is for exploratory analyses to find cases for criminal investigation and to spot system weaknesses that policy changes could fix. Its analysis has already led to a payment tariff change, with £28m of savings recognised by the Public Sector Fraud Authority Prevention Panel.

DARS-NIC-73678-Y1T0Y.summary: The London Borough of Redbridge, a local authority, is using hospital and emergency care records (Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set) to study local differences in emergency admissions, especially cardiovascular ones, and their links to NHS Health Check outcomes. It will use the results in its public health duties, including needs assessments, health strategies and advice to NHS commissioners. The aim is to identify and address health inequalities in the local population. It reports using the data to support a combined needs assessment with the local integrated care board and to inform local programmes, such as the suicide equity audit and children's health work.
DARS-NIC-73678-Y1T0Y.retense_draft: The London Borough of Redbridge, a local authority, is using hospital and emergency care records (Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set) to study local differences in emergency admissions, especially cardiovascular ones, and their links to NHS Health Check outcomes. The aim is to identify and address health inequalities in the local population. It reports using the data to support a combined needs assessment with the local integrated care board and to inform local programmes, such as the suicide equity audit and children's health work.
