DARS-NIC-736873-X9F8V.summary: Imperial College London's Dr Foster Unit's agreement covers the use of pseudonymised civil registration death records, linked to the National Hip Fracture Database, for about 8,000 to 10,000 adults with a fracture around a hip or knee replacement. It will study death rates, time to death and causes of death by hospital and by treatment. The aim is to inform NICE guidelines and quality improvement, so that treatment is more consistent and outcomes improve.

DARS-NIC-737073-H1C6D.summary: The Institute of Cancer Research's agreement covers national NHS England cancer registration, cancer pathway, radiotherapy, chemotherapy and hospital records for women diagnosed with breast cancer in England. The agreement allows study of whether different radiotherapy, chemotherapy and hormonal treatments are linked to later health problems, such as second cancers and cardiovascular disease. The aim is to inform treatment decisions and follow-up care for breast cancer survivors.

DARS-NIC-737123-P6P6G.summary: The University of Oxford's agreement covers linked NHS hospital, cancer, medicines, imaging, vaccination and death records for the MyMelanoma study, which follows at least 20,000 consenting melanoma patients across the UK. The data is for building a research resource to study what causes melanoma and how patients respond to treatment. The main intended benefit is better prevention, diagnosis and treatment of melanoma.

DARS-NIC-737139-W2B7S.summary: Cardiff University's agreement covers hospital, outpatient, critical care and emergency care records from NHS England. The records are for a randomised trial (TIPTOE) of a personalised self-management support programme for adults with knee or hip osteoarthritis and other long-term conditions. The records will help measure the programme's effect on use of healthcare services and its cost-effectiveness. The aim is to inform how osteoarthritis care is delivered in the NHS.

DARS-NIC-737333-K2F1T.summary: Queen Mary University of London's agreement covers identifiable NHS hospital, emergency care and primary care prescription records for 1,964 primary school children in London and Luton. The agreement allows the records to be used to study whether London's Ultra Low Emission Zone improves children's respiratory health, and it will also assess healthcare costs and value for money. The main intended benefit is evidence to inform government, NHS and city planning decisions on clean air zones and children's health.

DARS-NIC-739358-R1C7S.summary: The University of Leeds's agreement covers identifiable hospital, emergency care, mental health, death registration and dispensed medicines data for a randomised trial called FReSH START. The trial compares a psychological therapy for people who repeatedly self-harm with standard care. The data is for measuring repeated self-harm, safety and cost-effectiveness. The aim is to provide evidence that could inform NICE guidelines. So far, the data has been used for safety monitoring of trial participants.

DARS-NIC-739463-H4P9N.summary: NatCen Social Research, with University College London, the Institute for Fiscal Studies and the universities of Manchester and East Anglia, is covered by an agreement to use hospital records (admitted patient care, outpatients, critical care and emergency care) linked to the English Longitudinal Study of Ageing. The agreement allows them to study ageing, health and hospital use, including dementia and social care, to inform health and care planning. Linked data analyses have already featured in the Chief Medical Officer's 2023 annual report and in a Centre for Ageing Better report.

DARS-NIC-739472-P2Y8X.summary: The University of Hull's agreement covers pseudonymised hospital admissions data (Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care) for about 8,000 women aged 50 to 70 in Hull and the East Riding of Yorkshire. The data is for a feasibility trial of free door-to-door transport to breast screening appointments, checking whether this could raise attendance and whether a larger trial is workable. The intended benefit is better access to screening, which could lead to earlier diagnosis of breast cancer.

DARS-NIC-73974-P0L1Z.summary: The University of York, with the University of Liverpool and University College London, is covered by an agreement allowing it to use hospital records (accident and emergency, admitted patient care and outpatients) and date of death data for babies in the PREVAIL trial. The data is for comparing two types of central venous catheter, one coated with antimicrobial and antifungal agents and one standard, in very preterm babies, looking at death risk and hospital care costs. The main intended benefit is evidence to help hospitals decide which catheter to buy.

DARS-NIC-739822-Q8R6Y.summary: The University of Manchester's agreement covers keeping pseudonymised NHS Talking Therapies (formerly Improving Access to Psychological Therapies) patient data from 2020/21 to 2022/23. The completed study examined how provider waiting times affect patients' employment-related outcomes. The data is held securely so the analysis can be repeated if the findings are challenged. The research aims to help improve how Talking Therapies services manage waiting lists and meet patients' needs.

DARS-NIC-740323-Y4T3F.summary: The University of Leeds's agreement covers the use of identifiable NHS hospital, emergency care, outpatient, dispensed medicines and death registration data for the PROSPER Trial. The trial tests whether personalised care planning for older people with frailty, compared with usual care alone, reduces hospital use and is cost-effective. The expected benefit is robust evidence on its clinical and cost-effectiveness.

DARS-NIC-740806-W2F6Q.summary: University College London (UCL) is using pseudonymised NHS England cancer registration, cancer pathway and somatic molecular testing data on adults diagnosed with primary lung cancer in England between 2015 and 2022. The data supports a PhD project that describes lung cancer in never-smokers and how factors such as age, gender and ethnicity relate to diagnosis, stage and survival. The aim is to improve understanding and support earlier detection. So far, the team has reported its public engagement work to the National Institute for Health and Care Research (NIHR) in an annual report.
DARS-NIC-740806-W2F6Q.retense_draft: University College London (UCL) has an agreement that allows it to use pseudonymised NHS England cancer registration, cancer pathway and somatic molecular testing data on adults diagnosed with primary lung cancer in England between 2015 and 2022. The data is for a PhD project that describes lung cancer in never-smokers and how factors such as age, gender and ethnicity relate to diagnosis, stage and survival. The aim is to improve understanding and support earlier detection. The team has reported its public engagement work to the National Institute for Health and Care Research (NIHR) in an annual report.

DARS-NIC-74145-R8B9T.summary: London Borough of Southwark's agreement covers civil registration data on births and deaths, including identifiable records, plus primary care mortality data. The agreement allows the data to be used to understand local health needs, plan services, run suicide audits and protect public health. The data is for tailoring local services and reducing premature deaths and health inequalities. Birth data has supported needs analysis and briefings for the Maternity Commission and Children's Services, and mortality data has been used to calculate local life expectancy.

DARS-NIC-741610-V3R1Z.summary: London Borough of Hammersmith & Fulham's agreement covers civil registration data on births and deaths, together with primary care mortality data, which includes identifiable details. The data is for assessing local health needs, planning immunisation programmes, protecting public health and carrying out suicide audits. Results are published as aggregated statistics. The main intended benefit is local health and care services that are better tailored and targeted to reduce mortality and health inequalities.

DARS-NIC-742629-H5M4F.summary: London Ambulance Service NHS Trust's agreement covers the use of identifiable ambulance records linked to Emergency Care Data Set (ECDS) hospital records. The agreement allows the Trust to evaluate and audit its services, including how resources are allocated and how clinicians' care relates to patient outcomes. The main intended benefit is better care for patients, through targeted clinician training and by helping patients reach the right care pathway.

DARS-NIC-742898-S7N0V.summary: NHS Blood and Transplant (NHSBT) is using hospital admission records, death registrations and cancer data on people in England with liver disease, as part of a UCL PhD project. It will examine whether a patient's age, sex, ethnicity, social background and cause of liver disease affect their access to liver transplantation, organ offers and outcomes. The main intended benefit is evidence to help make liver transplant access fairer.
DARS-NIC-742898-S7N0V.retense_draft: NHS Blood and Transplant's agreement covers hospital admission records, death registrations and cancer data on people in England with liver disease, for a UCL PhD project. The project allows examination of whether a patient's age, sex, ethnicity, social background and cause of liver disease affect their access to liver transplantation, organ offers and outcomes. The main intended benefit is evidence to help make liver transplant access fairer.

DARS-NIC-742907-Z5F3Y.summary: The University of Southampton, working with University Hospital Southampton NHS Foundation Trust, is permitted to use identifiable civil registration of death records (dates and causes of death) for people taking part in the BRITISH clinical trial. The data is for testing whether implantable cardioverter defibrillators reduce deaths in patients with non-ischaemic cardiomyopathy, heart muscle disease not caused by blocked arteries, and scarring on heart scans. The main intended benefit is evidence to guide national guidelines and treatment decisions.

DARS-NIC-743125-M0K1Y.summary: The Royal College of Anaesthetists' agreement covers NHS England hospital admission records (Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care) and civil death registration data. The data supports the National Emergency Laparotomy Audit's work on patients who need emergency abdominal surgery but do not have it (the "NoLap" group). The aim is to understand these patients' care and outcomes, and to reduce variation in care between hospitals. The overall goal is better care and shared decision-making for this group.

DARS-NIC-743571-K7X4R.summary: The University of Oxford's agreement covers the use of identifiable demographic data from NHS England to find and contact adults in England who have a record of melanoma. The data is for inviting them to join the MyMelanoma study, which builds a large melanoma data resource so researchers can answer questions about risk, treatment and quality of life. Reported so far: about 150,000 invitations sent and about 15,400 participants recruited.

DARS-NIC-743681-L8G9L.summary: The University of Oxford's agreement covers identifiable demographic data from NHS England for up to 1,133 people who joined the EMPA-KIDNEY trial in England and Wales. The data is for identifying participant deaths not already reported, as part of a two-year follow-up of a trial testing empagliflozin in people with chronic kidney disease. The main intended benefit is to show whether the drug's benefits last over the longer term, and to improve the accuracy of the trial data.

DARS-NIC-743987-M7B3P.summary: The Medicines and Healthcare Products Regulatory Agency (MHRA)'s agreement covers pseudonymised Breast and Cosmetic Implant Registry data on people who had breast implants in England between 2019 and 2023. The agreement allows the data to be tested for whether it can support monitoring of breast implant safety, including implants of different textures. The main intended benefit is to help MHRA decide whether the registry can be used in routine vigilance, and to improve how it identifies possible links between implants and systemic symptoms.

DARS-NIC-744761-P7S8L.summary: South East Coast Ambulance Service NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers linked ambulance and emergency department records (the Ambulance Data Set and the Emergency Care Data Set). The agreement allows the Trust to use them to evaluate and audit its services, including clinical supervision and comparing treatment patterns across clinicians and patient groups. The aim is to improve patient care, target training and identify gaps in local services. Results will be internal dashboards of aggregated figures.

DARS-NIC-744993-Z8K2K.summary: Methods Business and Digital Technology Limited, an IT supplier, is permitted under its agreement to use pseudonymised national cancer data covering breast cancer patients in England from 2016 onwards. The data is for studying how treatment for triple negative breast cancer, including chemotherapy, surgery and radiotherapy, varies with ethnicity and deprivation. The study aims to improve understanding of the disease and the care patients receive.

DARS-NIC-745735-D8M0S.summary: Lancaster University's agreement covers pseudonymised NDRS Cancer Registrations data, which records cancer cases, from 2021 onwards. It allows comparison of cancer incidence, prevalence and mortality across the North West and the rest of England, and examination of links with demographic, socioeconomic and environmental factors. The aim is to show where cancer inequalities are greatest, so that North West Cancer Research can target its strategy and funding.

DARS-NIC-74625-S1Q8X.summary: Cardiff University's agreement covers the linking of hospital records for accident and emergency, admitted patient care and outpatients with data on acutely ill children under five seen in general practice. The data is for the CLASSIC project, which aims to check an existing clinical tool and develop a new one to help GPs identify serious infections in children that lead to hospital admission. Earlier work from the LUCI study has already produced three published papers, which found that the tools tested were not accurate enough in general practice.

DARS-NIC-746266-S8M6T.summary: University College London (UCL)'s agreement covers the use of identifiable hospital admission and emergency care records for about 3,500 consenting mothers and children in the Baby Biome Study. The agreement allows research into whether air pollution exposure during pregnancy affects pregnancy, birth and child health outcomes, including respiratory infections. The findings are expected to inform policy on regulating air pollution and advice to pregnant women on reducing their exposure.

DARS-NIC-746522-Y4R7L.summary: The University of Glasgow's agreement covers identifiable NHS England hospital admission, outpatient, emergency care and death registration data for 139 people in England who joined a registry of microvascular angina, a heart condition affecting the small blood vessels. The data is for following their long-term health outcomes and healthcare use, to understand how the condition develops and whether the trial drug zibotentan relates to later outcomes. The findings are expected to inform treatment guidelines and future medicine research.

DARS-NIC-747046-T7C5C.summary: Imperial College Healthcare NHS Trust's agreement covers the use of cancer registry data and mental health services data for Imperial College London's Indigo trial, which studies people living with and beyond cancer. The trial tests whether patient-reported questionnaires completed online can be linked to national records. The main intended benefit is a practical evidence base on collecting patient-reported outcomes in the community, so care can better reflect long-term unmet needs.

DARS-NIC-747507-C5G6T.summary: The University of Oxford, working with the University of Leicester, is permitted to use hospital, emergency care, critical care, outpatient and death registration records for 1,522 babies in the SurfON trial. The trial compares early surfactant treatment with expectant management in late preterm and early term babies with respiratory distress. The records are for estimating NHS costs and one-year survival. The aim is to inform treatment decisions and reduce intensive care needs and hospital stays.

DARS-NIC-747531-J2Q0W.summary: The London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine's agreement covers NHS hospital admission, critical care, outpatient and emergency care records, along with death registrations, for a clinical trial called CHIP-BCIS3. The trial tests whether a device that unloads the heart's left ventricle during high-risk coronary stent procedures gives better patient outcomes, quality of life and cost-effectiveness than standard care. The main intended benefit is clearer evidence so patients, clinicians and commissioners can decide whether the technology should be used.

DARS-NIC-748004-M6G9X.summary: Evidera Ltd, a research company working for Takeda Development Centre Americas, Inc., has an agreement that allows it to use pseudonymised cancer registry, hospital, radiotherapy, systemic anti-cancer therapy and molecular test data on adults with advanced non-small cell lung cancer in England. The agreement covers studying who these patients are, the sequences of treatments they receive, and how long they survive and go before their next treatment. The aim is to give evidence that helps refine treatment strategies and healthcare planning.

DARS-NIC-748215-Z7K2V.summary: Leeds Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust's agreement covers pseudonymised data from the TAVI (transcatheter aortic valve implantation) registry, linked to civil registration death records, for around 43,000 patients treated in England and Wales between 2007 and 2023. The data is for evaluating whether right bundle branch block, a heart conduction problem, is linked to higher long-term mortality after TAVI, and whether a permanent pacemaker changes this. The findings are expected to inform whether pacemakers should be fitted beforehand.

DARS-NIC-748645-R5G3D.summary: The Office for National Statistics (ONS)'s agreement allows it to use NHS England's Diabetes Prevention Programme data, along with hospital and emergency care records, to produce official statistics and statistical research. The statistics will look at how health affects labour market participation, and the reverse. The main expected benefit is better evidence for government departments, which could help improve the design of the programme and help patients back into work.

DARS-NIC-748653-S9J4H.summary: The Office for National Statistics (ONS)'s agreement covers the use of NHS England waiting list data, along with hospital, emergency care and psychological therapy records, to produce official statistics. The agreement allows a first project looking at links between adverse health events, NHS waiting lists and employment. The aim is to give government departments better evidence on how health and work affect each other. A published analysis has already examined how waiting times relate to pay and employment after hospital treatment.

DARS-NIC-748729-Z8B3M.summary: The University of Bristol's agreement covers linked NHS health records, such as hospital, GP, cancer, mental health, maternity and COVID-19 data, for the UK Longitudinal Linkage Collaboration. It allows a research database linking long-running population study participants' data, relying on participant consent. The data is for approved researchers' health research to inform policy and care. Its reported results include published papers on Long COVID and on work-related COVID-19 risk, which informed NICE guidance and Health and Safety Executive policy.

DARS-NIC-748984-C7G9X.summary: Slough Borough Council's agreement covers hospital activity data (Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set, covering admitted patient care, outpatients, critical care and A&E). The data is for its public health duties, including needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, commissioning, advice to NHS commissioners and the Director of Public Health's annual report. The main intended benefit is locally focused analysis of health outcomes and inequalities, particularly for the most disadvantaged groups.

DARS-NIC-749150-S0M7G.summary: Evidera Ltd, a research company working for Takeda Development Centre Americas, Inc., has an agreement that allows it to use pseudonymised cancer registration, hospital, radiotherapy, systemic anti-cancer therapy and molecular testing data. The data is for studying the characteristics, treatments and survival of adults with metastatic colorectal cancer who have had at least three lines of therapy. The main intended benefit is a better understanding of how these patients are treated and how they fare, to inform clinicians, policymakers and future research.

DARS-NIC-749612-D9M1V.summary: Queen Mary University of London's agreement covers hospital admissions data (Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care) on children in England. The agreement allows the data to be used to study how the Soft Drinks Industry Levy affected inequalities in hospital extractions for tooth decay by area deprivation, ethnicity and urbanicity, and to assess its financial and health effects through an extended cost-effectiveness analysis. The findings are intended to inform policy decisions, including the government's obesity strategy and the continuation of the levy.

DARS-NIC-750163-K6F7T.summary: University College London Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers identifiable cancer registration data, limited to a study cohort, for calculating survival times for teenagers and young adults with cancer. The research compares outcomes for those whose care is wholly, partly or not at all in specialist teenage and young adult centres. The agreement allows the research to inform NHS policy and service design so these services can improve outcomes for young people with cancer.

DARS-NIC-75079-V7Y7L.summary: Bangor University, an academic organisation, holds Hospital Episode Statistics data covering accident and emergency, admitted patient care and outpatient records. The agreement allows the data to be kept for archiving only, because it is source data for the SANAD-II epilepsy drug trial and analysis is complete. The trial's economic analysis compared the cost-effectiveness of antiepileptic drugs, to help NHS decision-makers choose the most clinically and cost-effective treatments.

DARS-NIC-75133-N8S0N.summary: City of Westminster's agreement covers civil registration data on births and deaths, plus primary care mortality data, which includes identifiable details. The data is for understanding local health needs, planning services and protecting public health, including suicide prevention work, with only aggregated figures published. The agreement allows the main intended benefit of local services tailored to areas of greatest need, reducing health inequalities and premature deaths. The council has published annual public health reports and has used deaths data to examine inequalities and life-expectancy gaps between boroughs' more and less affluent areas.

DARS-NIC-752432-W7V5T.summary: The University of Leicester's agreement covers pseudonymised National Disease Registration Service (NDRS) cancer registration data for adults diagnosed with selected cancers since 2000. The agreement allows its research unit to study trends in early diagnosis, stage-specific survival and inequalities between patient groups, and to develop statistical methods and a monitoring toolkit for NHS England. The main intended benefit is better evidence to help improve early cancer diagnosis and outcomes for future patients.

DARS-NIC-752595-J7L6P.summary: The University of Birmingham's agreement covers civil registration of death data, covering the date and cause of death for consenting trial participants. The data is for PETNECK 2, a trial comparing PET-CT-guided, patient-initiated follow-up with standard clinical follow-up for advanced head and neck cancer. The death data allows the trial to measure overall survival, its main outcome. The aim is to add evidence to help decide whether this follow-up approach is effective and cost-effective.

DARS-NIC-752925-P6Y2W.summary: The Royal College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists (RCOG)'s agreement allows it to use a bridging file of person identifiers to link maternity data from the National Maternity and Perinatal Audit with neonatal data from the National Neonatal Audit Programme. The linked data will show neonatal outcomes of maternity care that have not previously been reported, through a snapshot audit and updates to annual reports and a neonatal dashboard. The main expected benefit is better care and experience for women giving birth and for babies.

DARS-NIC-753305-S9Y1C.summary: Cardiff University, working with Velindre NHS Trust, has an agreement covering civil registration death records for about 400 consenting participants in the SCOPE2 oesophageal cancer trial. The agreement allows the records to be used to check and verify deaths so that survival results, the trial's main measures, are accurate. The trial compares a standard and a higher radiotherapy dose, and two chemotherapy combinations. The expected benefit is reliable evidence to inform treatment and NHS policy decisions.

DARS-NIC-753801-J5B3X.summary: Queen Mary University of London's agreement covers NHS England's identifiable demographic data, limited to men aged 55-79 and women aged 65-79, for producing mailing lists. The data is for inviting people to join the Heartburn Health Programme and, through it, the BEST4 Screening Trial. The aim is to recruit enough participants to test whether a capsule sponge device can screen for Barrett's oesophagus, a precursor of food pipe cancer, and to build a resource for future research on heartburn.

DARS-NIC-754054-P3H3V.summary: King's College London's agreement covers civil registration death records for 282 people who joined the NalPORS study and were lost to follow-up after six months. The research checks whether these participants, who were current opioid users, died and whether an opioid overdose was the cause. It forms part of a study of take-home naloxone given to people who witness an overdose. The expected benefit is more knowledge on preventing accidental opioid overdoses.

DARS-NIC-754175-W2Z4T.summary: Imperial College London's agreement covers pseudonymised hospital admissions, outpatient and emergency care records for adults in England between April 2022 and March 2024. The data is for a PhD project, funded by the NIHR, studying how separating planned and emergency surgery, including through surgical hubs, affects health inequalities and access to planned surgery. It is intended to inform policymakers and guidance on how surgical hubs are used.

DARS-NIC-754519-V1T5M.summary: The Intensive Care National Audit & Research Centre (ICNARC)'s agreement covers NHS England death registration and hospital admission and outpatient records. The data supports the UK-ROX trial, which compares conservative and usual oxygen therapy in adults on mechanical ventilation in intensive care. The data provides outcomes such as 90-day mortality and length of hospital stay. The intended benefit is stronger evidence on the best amount of oxygen to give, to inform clinical guidelines and improve survival and quality of life.

DARS-NIC-75485-J3R9B.summary: The University of Warwick's agreement covers hospital admitted patient, critical care and outpatient records (Hospital Episode Statistics) for about 380 people in a trial of exercise after breast cancer surgery. The records will be linked to trial data to check the hospital use that participants reported themselves, supporting a cost-effectiveness comparison with usual care. The main intended benefit is to help NICE decide whether to recommend physiotherapy after breast cancer surgery.

DARS-NIC-755470-G7Y8N.summary: Westmorland and Furness Council's agreement covers civil registration data on births and deaths, plus primary care mortality data, which includes identifiable details. The data is for understanding local health needs, planning services and supporting public health work such as suicide prevention audits. The main intended benefit is local services tailored to areas of greatest need, helping to reduce mortality and health inequalities.

DARS-NIC-755472-Y7C7F.summary: The Care Quality Commission (CQC) agreement covers pseudonymised NHS England data on community services, emergency care, hospital admissions, critical care, outpatients and mental health services. The agreement allows the data to be used in a pilot of NHS England's Unified Data Access Layer and in the CQC's regulation of health and care providers. This includes inspection planning, monitoring the Mental Health Act and national reports such as the State of Care. The intended benefit is better care, treatment and experience for people using health services.

DARS-NIC-755603-Q8Y4Y.summary: Keele University's agreement covers hospital, accident and emergency, outpatient and emergency care records for about 2,000 adults with musculoskeletal pain and about 2,500 adults aged 35 and over registered with participating GP practices in North Staffordshire and Stoke-on-Trent. The data is for studying musculoskeletal health, inequalities and healthcare use. The main intended benefit is a local system of musculoskeletal health intelligence to inform policymakers, practitioners and the public.

DARS-NIC-756432-F0B1L.summary: The Institute of Cancer Research's agreement covers national cancer registration, hospital, radiotherapy, chemotherapy and cancer waiting times data. The agreement allows the data to be used to compare patients who joined its cancer trials with similar patients who did not, looking at their characteristics and overall survival. The aim is to find groups that may be systematically left out of trials. The main intended benefit is more inclusive future trials.

DARS-NIC-756799-M4K3V.summary: Liverpool University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust is using identifiable hospital admissions data (Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care) for 3,751 consented trial participants. It is used to check whether patients with chest pain were admitted to another acute hospital within 30 days, in a trial comparing a 1-hour and a 3-hour repeat blood test pathway for ruling out heart attack. The aim is to show whether the 1-hour pathway is safe and can allow faster discharge. The trial's main results have been published in a cardiology journal, and they led to a regional switch to the 1-hour pathway.
DARS-NIC-756799-M4K3V.retense_draft: Liverpool University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers identifiable hospital admissions data (Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care) for 3,751 consented trial participants. The data is for checking whether patients with chest pain were admitted to another acute hospital within 30 days, in a trial comparing a 1-hour and a 3-hour repeat blood test pathway for ruling out heart attack. The aim is to show whether the 1-hour pathway is safe and can allow faster discharge. The trial's main results were published in a cardiology journal and led to a regional switch to the 1-hour pathway.

DARS-NIC-756900-Q2J3K.summary: University College London (UCL)'s agreement covers the use of hospital admission, critical care and death registration records to evaluate the National Perioperative Screening and Optimisation Programme, which sets up teams to assess patients' health needs before and after surgery. The aim is to measure its effect on patient-centred outcomes, with the hope of showing whether it leads to fewer complications and better recovery. The agreement allows UCL to build a baseline of days alive and out of hospital, readmissions and deaths for three types of surgery.

DARS-NIC-757611-Y2B1J.summary: The University of Sheffield, working with University College London, under an agreement that allows use of pseudonymised NHS data on talking therapy referrals, hospital and emergency care, mental health services, prescriptions and deaths. The data is for two studies comparing how effective and cost-effective different talking and digital therapies are for anxiety and depression, including differences in outcomes between groups. The main intended benefit is better evidence to help match patients to suitable therapies.

DARS-NIC-757820-S7F8B.summary: The Intensive Care National Audit & Research Centre (ICNARC)'s agreement covers linked civil death registration records and hospital admissions data (Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care). The agreement allows the data to be used mainly for national audits of adult critical care and in-hospital cardiac arrest, and secondarily to support approved research. The main intended benefit is better quality, safety and equity of critical care and resuscitation, through audit reports that include longer-term patient outcomes.

DARS-NIC-757823-Y6Q1H.summary: University Hospitals Birmingham NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers pseudonymised national congenital heart disease audit records and civil registration death records for about 8,000 people who had a pulmonary valve replacement in England and Wales between 2003 and 2023. The agreement allows comparison of how often different valve types are used, how long they last before further intervention is needed, and survival. The main intended benefit is evidence on whether one valve type is better, to inform a future multi-centre clinical trial and reduce repeat operations.

DARS-NIC-758592-R3M5V.summary: The University of Nottingham, working with Nottinghamshire Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust, has an agreement covering identifiable hospital, emergency care, community service and mental health service records for children in the STADIA trial. The data is for following up 539 participants for at least 36 months to see whether a standardised diagnostic assessment at referral to children's mental health services (CAMHS) affects later referrals, self-harm presentations and hospital admissions. The intended benefit is better evidence on whether the tool helps identify and treat children's emotional difficulties.

DARS-NIC-758630-F8C7Y.summary: South Central Ambulance Service NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers the use of linked ambulance and emergency department records (the Ambulance Data Set pilot and the Emergency Care Data Set). The agreement allows the records to be used to evaluate and audit its services, including clinical supervision, reviews of treatments and how resources are allocated. The main intended benefit is better patient care, with improved care pathways and less pressure on busy emergency departments. Results will be shared as aggregated dashboards.

DARS-NIC-759062-F2L6B.summary: NatCen Social Research, with University College London, the Institute for Fiscal Studies, the University of Manchester and the University of East Anglia, is covered by an agreement that allows use of English Longitudinal Study of Ageing data linked to NHS cancer registration and death records. The data is for studying ageing and health in England, including hospital use, social care, health inequalities and dementia, to inform health and care planning. Its findings have already featured in the Chief Medical Officer's 2023 annual report and in NIHR alerts.

DARS-NIC-759203-S1P1T.summary: St George's University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers hospital admission records, death registration records and the National Heart Failure Audit dataset. The data is for studying how kidney impairment affects short- and long-term outcomes, such as death and hospital readmission, in people admitted with acute heart failure over the last 15 years. The agreement allows building a tool to predict adverse outcomes. The main intended benefit is service improvements for patients with heart failure and chronic kidney disease.

DARS-NIC-759280-N0Y4F.summary: Slough Borough Council's agreement covers civil registration data on births and deaths, plus primary care mortality data. The agreement allows the data to be used to understand local health needs, protect public health and support work such as suicide audits, health assessments and strategies. Outputs are aggregated statistics with small numbers suppressed. The main intended benefit is health and care services tailored to local needs, reducing mortality and health inequalities.

DARS-NIC-759355-H7B9S.summary: The Department of Health and Social Care's agreement covers NHS England data on adult social care, hospital activity, emergency care, cancer waiting lists, continuing healthcare, virtual wards and dental training posts. The data is for analysing and developing evidence-based health and care policy and for advising Ministers. The main intended benefit is better-informed decisions that improve patient outcomes. Reporting based on the specialist advice dataset has been automated and fed into elective modelling ahead of the spending review.

DARS-NIC-759654-D8H5M.summary: The Royal National Orthopaedic Hospital NHS Trust's agreement covers pseudonymised hospital admissions, outpatient, emergency care and diagnostic imaging data covering England from 2021 onwards. The data is for running Getting it Right First Time (GIRFT) reviews for NHS and independent sector clients, comparing their results against national benchmarks. The main intended benefit is helping providers check the quality of care and improve it, with learning shared with NHS England.

DARS-NIC-759706-Y0Y3S.summary: Wokingham Borough Council, a local authority, has an agreement covering pseudonymised hospital and emergency care data: Hospital Episode Statistics (admitted patient care, outpatients, critical care, accident and emergency) and the Emergency Care Data Set. The agreement allows the data to be used for its public health duties, including needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, the annual public health report and advice to NHS commissioners. The main intended benefit is locally focused analysis of health outcomes and inequalities, especially for disadvantaged groups.

DARS-NIC-761685-K1C1Z.summary: The University of Aberdeen's agreement covers hospital admissions and outpatient records for 839 women who took part in the FUTURE clinical trial on refractory overactive bladder. The records will show any further admissions, operations and bladder treatments after each woman joined the trial. The study tests whether routine urodynamics (invasive bladder pressure tests) improves treatment outcomes and is cost effective. The findings are intended to inform patients, clinicians and NHS policy makers.

DARS-NIC-761989-J2G4R.summary: University Hospital Southampton NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers identifiable hospital admission and death registration records for about 20,000 patients who had routine blood tests at the trust in 2017. The agreement allows study of whether raised troponin levels, a blood test designed to detect heart attacks, are linked to heart attacks, strokes, heart failure and death over five years. The main intended benefit is helping clinicians interpret troponin results and prompting research into reducing risk. An earlier phase of the study found the test was closely associated with mortality.

DARS-NIC-762732-L6B5X.summary: Queen Mary University of London's agreement covers bowel screening, cancer registration and death registration data held by NHS England. The agreement allows the university to analyse and model existing faecal immunochemical test and colonoscopy results to estimate bowel pathology at different faecal haemoglobin levels. The work is the first of six stages in a programme on risk-based bowel cancer screening. It is intended to provide evidence to support introducing risk-based screening in the UK.

DARS-NIC-764229-C0C7B.summary: The University of Birmingham's agreement covers identifiable hospital, emergency care, outpatient and death registration records for 160 people with permanent atrial fibrillation and heart failure symptoms who took part in the RATE-AF trial. The data is for following their long-term health outcomes to see whether beta-blockers or digoxin, used to control heart rate, lead to different results. The aim is to help clinicians choose the best heart rate control treatment for these patients.

DARS-NIC-764470-N9W3S.summary: The Office for National Statistics (ONS) agreement covers NHS England's Hospital Episode Statistics for accident and emergency, admitted patient care, critical care and outpatients. Approved researchers may use it in the Health & Labour Market project to study how long-term health conditions, risk factors and treatments affect employment and earnings. The aim is to give HM Treasury and NHS decision-makers better evidence on where to allocate public funds. Initial analysis has already examined the economic effects of bariatric surgery.

DARS-NIC-765236-C7C1B.summary: The University of Oxford's Nuffield Department of Population Health's agreement covers identifiable NHS England data on deaths, demographics, hospital admissions, critical care, emergency care and dispensed medicines. The data is for following patients in the RECOVERY trial who were hospitalised with non-COVID-19 pneumonia, to measure death, other outcomes and longer-term effects of the treatments being tested. The main intended benefit is evidence to improve care and reduce deaths for people hospitalised with pneumonia.

DARS-NIC-765257-H7B7S.summary: The University of Cambridge's agreement covers identifiable cancer registration and death records for 2,025 consenting trial participants aged 50 and over who take long-term acid suppressants. It follows their long-term outcomes in the BEST3 trial, which compares an invitation to the Cytosponge-TFF3 test with usual care for diagnosing Barrett's oesophagus, a pre-cancerous condition. The intended benefit is evidence on whether this less invasive test could be used in primary care.

DARS-NIC-765457-R1Z0N.summary: University of Bristol's agreement covers the use of hospital admission records (Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care) and civil registrations of death. The data is for studying how intensive care is used after vascular surgery for blocked or narrowed blood vessels in the neck and legs between 2014 and 2024, and for comparing outcomes for patients sent to intensive care with those sent to a normal ward. The main intended benefit is better evidence on which patients need intensive care, to improve outcomes and reduce surgical delays.

DARS-NIC-766571-T4Z2L.summary: The University of Leeds's agreement covers identifiable hospital records (admissions, outpatients, emergency care) and dispensed medicines data for about 1.5 million patients registered at GP practices in the 3i-o study. The agreement allows the data to be used to assess whether audit and feedback to GP practices, aimed at reducing prescribing of antibiotics, addictive painkillers and gabapentinoids, affects health inequalities, and to analyse cost-effectiveness. The main intended benefit is more selective prescribing across the NHS and evidence on whether the approach widens inequalities.

DARS-NIC-766604-V7D1W.summary: North East Ambulance Service NHS Foundation Trust's agreement allows it to use linked ambulance and emergency department records (the Ambulance Data Set and the Emergency Care Data Set). The data is for evaluating and auditing its services, including clinical supervision and checking whether treatment and resources match patients' needs. The outputs are aggregated dashboards for senior leaders. The main intended benefit is better patient care and pathways, with less pressure on busy emergency departments.

DARS-NIC-76770-F0J5W.summary: NHS Greater Manchester ICB's agreement for its Salford area allows hospital activity data (SUS for Commissioners) to be linked with GP data for risk stratification, which identifies patients at high risk of health deterioration or repeated service use. NHS Arden and GEM Commissioning Support Unit does the work. The data is for letting GPs and commissioners target care and plan services, improving patient outcomes. Reported so far: better understanding of patient flows and identification of high-risk patients who often attend or are admitted to hospital.

DARS-NIC-767874-H5W4P.summary: East of England Ambulance Service NHS Trust's agreement covers linked ambulance and emergency care data, which records the care patients received from the ambulance crew and in hospital. The agreement allows the data to be used for service evaluation and auditing, including clinical supervision, staff development and spotting patterns in treatment. The main intended benefit is better patient care, with improved care pathways that could reduce pressure on busy emergency departments.

DARS-NIC-767882-N1X4D.summary: South Western Ambulance Service NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers the use of linked Ambulance Data Set and Emergency Care Data Set (ECDS) records, which combine ambulance call and patient record data with emergency department data. The agreement allows the data to be used to evaluate and audit its services, support clinical supervision and compare treatments and outcomes. The main intended benefit is better patient care, including improved training for clinicians and changes to patient pathways that could reduce pressure on emergency departments.

DARS-NIC-768785-V7L6D.summary: East Midlands Ambulance Service NHS Trust's agreement covers the use of linked ambulance and emergency care records, which cover the care patients receive from the ambulance service and then in hospital emergency departments. The agreement allows the records to be used to evaluate and audit its services, including clinical supervision and training for crews, and to check whether treatments and resources are consistent. The intended benefit is better patient care and care pathways, which could also reduce pressure on busy emergency departments.

DARS-NIC-769062-G5F1K.summary: University College London (UCL), working with Care England and The Outstanding Society Community Interest Company, is permitted to link hospital, emergency care, death and prescribing data on care home residents. The agreement covers piloting surveillance of infection and antimicrobial resistance in care homes, producing dashboards and reports for providers and policymakers. The intended main benefit is fewer infections and outbreaks, with better-targeted quality improvement.

DARS-NIC-76968-B0H8X.summary: London Borough of Ealing Council's agreement covers hospital and emergency care records from NHS England's secure data environment, including Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set. The data is for its public health duties, such as needs assessments, health strategies, advice to NHS commissioners and the Director of Public Health's annual report. The aim is more locally focused analysis of health outcomes and inequalities. The council reported using the access in the last year for needs assessments and other public health analyses.

DARS-NIC-769782-X5C1F.summary: Digital Health and Care Wales's agreement covers pseudonymised NHS England hospital data for admitted patient care, accident and emergency, and outpatient activity from April 2019 onwards. The agreement allows the data to build a benchmarking dashboard that lets Health Boards in Wales compare their metrics, such as mortality, with others across Wales and England. The main intended benefit is improved services in Wales, as Health Boards see how they compare and make changes.

DARS-NIC-771073-N4R2G.summary: Swansea University's agreement covers the use of pseudonymised hospital admission, emergency care, critical care and death registration data for a group of people who had an injury and contacted emergency ambulance services or emergency departments. The data is for linking to survey answers from 250 ethnic minority and 250 white British people. The study allows comparison of their injuries, care and outcomes, and exploration of their experiences of seeking help. The main intended benefit is evidence to help policy makers and services improve care and access for ethnic minority people with injuries.

DARS-NIC-771170-Y3J8Z.summary: The University of Cambridge's agreement, working with Cambridge University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust, covers the use of pseudonymised hospital admissions and emergency care records from 2013/14 to 2024/25. The research is to look at how easily people can reach specialist surgical services, including differences linked to inequality and location, and which surgical pathways are under strain. The main intended benefit is national evidence to help plan specialist surgical services and improve care.

DARS-NIC-771303-G4V1M.summary: University Hospital Southampton NHS Foundation Trust is using linked hospital, emergency care and death registration records, along with major trauma registry data, for the Pre-hospital Research and Audit Network (PRANA). The registry follows patients who received critical care outside hospital, to research and audit that care and its outcomes. It aims to give the first national picture of this care in England and Wales. So far, the linked data is being used by the Department for Transport to assess the health effects of road traffic collisions, and PRANA is named in the January 2026 National Road Safety Strategy.
DARS-NIC-771303-G4V1M.retense_draft: University Hospital Southampton NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers the use of linked hospital, emergency care and death registration records, along with major trauma registry data, for the Pre-hospital Research and Audit Network (PRANA). The registry follows patients who received critical care outside hospital, to research and audit that care and its outcomes. It aims to give the first national picture of this care in England and Wales. The linked data is for use by the Department for Transport to assess the health effects of road traffic collisions, and PRANA is named in the January 2026 National Road Safety Strategy.

DARS-NIC-771368-F4G0V.summary: The University of Warwick's agreement covers pseudonymised hospital, emergency care and death registration records for 151 patients who survived an out-of-hospital cardiac arrest and consented to join the PARAMEDIC-3 trial. The agreement allows the data to be used to compare survival, hospital activity and NHS costs between two ways of giving adrenaline: into a vein or into a bone. The intended benefit is evidence to inform resuscitation guidelines.

DARS-NIC-77142-Q4D1D.summary: University Hospitals Birmingham NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers pseudonymised hospital, death, cancer registration, radiotherapy and systemic anti-cancer therapy records for people who have had a solid organ transplant in England. The study links these records to examine cancer after transplantation, including cancer risk, deaths and hospital care, to help guide care and counselling for transplant patients. Preliminary findings have been presented at two international transplant congresses and submitted to The Lancet as manuscripts.

DARS-NIC-771891-C7B5S.summary: West Midlands Ambulance Service University NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers linked Ambulance Data Set and Emergency Care Data Set records, which follow patients from ambulance care into hospital. The agreement allows the data to be used to evaluate and audit its services, including clinical supervision, staff training needs and patterns in treatment. The main intended benefit is better patient care and pathways, with less pressure on busy emergency departments.

DARS-NIC-772217-L9G2N.summary: London Borough of Camden's agreement covers identifiable civil registration data on births and deaths, together with primary care mortality data. The data is for measuring local health needs, planning and monitoring services, and protecting public health, including suicide audits. The aim is to tailor local services to local needs and reduce health inequalities. Under an earlier joint agreement with Islington, it produced mortality profiles for GP practices and informed needs assessments.

DARS-NIC-772232-C4K8W.summary: London Borough of Camden's agreement covers the use of pseudonymised hospital and emergency care records, including Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set. The agreement allows the data to be used for its public health work, such as needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, the annual public health report and advice to NHS commissioners. The stated benefit is locally focused analysis of health outcomes and inequalities, particularly for disadvantaged groups.

DARS-NIC-772510-Z1K7F.summary: Yorkshire Ambulance Service NHS Trust's agreement covers the use of Ambulance Data Set (pilot) data linked to Emergency Care Data Set records, which show what happened to patients after they reached hospital. The agreement allows the data to be used to evaluate and audit its services, including reviewing clinical care, supporting clinician supervision and training, and checking whether resources are used well. The aim is to improve patient care and to help change patient pathways in ways that reduce pressure on busy emergency departments.

DARS-NIC-772615-N4N1V.summary: Liverpool University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers identifiable hospital admission records (Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care) for 5,250 Merseyside patients treated with clopidogrel or ticagrelor after acute coronary syndrome. The agreement allows testing of how well tools that estimate bleeding risk on antiplatelet medicines work in this real-world group, and identifying the best-performing one. The aim is to help clinicians prescribe with more confidence, reducing major bleeding and further heart attacks.

DARS-NIC-772633-Y3K3T.summary: University College London's agreement covers hospital, emergency care, critical care, outpatient and death registration records for studying young people who move from paediatric to adult intensive care. The data is to be linked with national intensive care audit records to show how many young people make this move, what their characteristics are and how they use hospital services. The main intended benefit is evidence to improve care and experience for these teenagers and their families.

DARS-NIC-773525-N5H9R.summary: The University of Cambridge's agreement covers survey data on the mental health of children and young people (the Mental Health of Children and Young People 2017 Survey and its follow-up waves). The data is for linking to school attainment records. The research looks at how mental health, mental health service use and educational outcomes relate over time, including during the COVID-19 pandemic. The aim is to show which services work, for whom and why, so that services can be better targeted and improved for children and young people.

DARS-NIC-773720-X4Q2Q.summary: The University of Edinburgh's agreement covers identifiable NHS England data on deaths, hospital admissions and medicines dispensed in primary care. The data is for a UK-wide study of memory, thinking and mood problems, and vascular dementia, after a stroke, including the effects of COVID-19. The study aims to find who develops these problems and why. The hope is better risk prediction and earlier information, treatment and care for patients.

DARS-NIC-773953-N5L3H.summary: Tolley Ltd's agreement covers analysis of pseudonymised hospital admission, outpatient and national cancer registry data on adults in England with non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer that no longer responds to BCG treatment. The agreement allows Tolley Ltd to analyse their treatment pathways and outcomes for ImmunityBio, which is seeking a NICE appraisal of its treatment. The intended benefit is evidence on current care to inform NICE decisions and UK clinicians.

DARS-NIC-774097-J9J0C.summary: University College London (UCL), an academic organisation, is permitted under its agreement with NHS England to use demographic data, specifically addresses, for the Medical Research Council National Survey of Health and Development, which follows people born in Britain in 1946. The agreement allows the addresses to be used to re-contact study members who have been lost to follow-up and invite them to rejoin. The intended benefit is keeping the study sample representative of the population being studied.

DARS-NIC-774351-T6M3Q.summary: The University of East Anglia, an academic organisation, is authorised under the agreement to use NHS England data on hospital admissions, outpatient visits, emergency care, deaths and medicines dispensed in primary care. The data is for testing whether the CHARMER training helps hospital geriatricians and pharmacists stop unnecessary medicines for older people. The main intended benefit is to show whether this reduces unplanned hospital admissions and to inform national policy on overprescribing.

DARS-NIC-774448-Q4C6X.summary: Beamtree UK Limited, a consultancy, has an agreement covering hospital activity data (emergency care, admitted patient, critical care and outpatient records) and the Summary Hospital-level Mortality Indicator. The agreement allows the data to be used to run an analytics platform, developed with the NHS Confederation, for NHS acute trusts. Trusts can benchmark their performance against peers, track trends and see predictions up to a year ahead. The main intended benefit is helping trusts target improvements to the safety, quality and efficiency of care.

DARS-NIC-775419-R1N5L.summary: Quality by Randomization Limited (trading as Protas), a research organisation, has an agreement covering NHS England data, including a mailing cohort and an aggregate recruitment data quality report. The data is for identifying and inviting eligible people to join NATRIX-SBP, a clinical trial of REGN5381, a monthly injection for uncontrolled high blood pressure. The agreement says its sole purpose is recruitment, and the wider trial aims to show whether the treatment safely lowers blood pressure.

DARS-NIC-775420-M7D8Z.summary: Quality by Randomization Limited (trading as Protas), a research organisation, is allowed to use NHS England mailing-list data and aggregate data quality reports to find and invite people who may be eligible for the NATRIX-SBP trial. The trial tests REGN5381, a monthly injection intended to lower uncontrolled high blood pressure. The data is for recruitment only, so no direct health benefit is expected from this agreement; the trial itself aims to show whether the treatment works safely.

DARS-NIC-775459-B7S5G.summary: North West Ambulance Service NHS Trust's agreement covers the linking of ambulance and emergency care data (the Ambulance Data Set and the Emergency Care Data Set, ECDS). The agreement allows the data to be used to evaluate and audit its services, including clinical supervision, clinician training needs, treatments given and patient pathways. The main intended benefit is better patient care and less pressure on busy Emergency Departments. Results will appear as aggregated dashboards for senior leaders.

DARS-NIC-775504-H4Z5Q.summary: The University of Oxford's agreement covers pseudonymised hospital admissions, outpatient, emergency care and death registration data for patients who had cardiac surgery at three NHS hospitals between October 2021 and July 2023. The agreement allows the data to be used to study how atrial fibrillation (an irregular heart rhythm) after cardiac surgery relates to longer-term outcomes, and whether prediction models can estimate the risk of those outcomes. The intended benefit is to improve and target follow-up care for patients after cardiac surgery.

DARS-NIC-77560-T5P8Y.summary: East Riding of Yorkshire Council's agreement covers identifiable birth and death records, including primary care mortality data, for understanding local health needs. The data is for public health work such as needs assessments, suicide audits and monitoring deaths, with only aggregated figures published. The aim is to tailor local services to the areas of greatest need and reduce health inequalities. The agreement has been used to analyse premature deaths in a deprived coastal town and to inform the 2022/23 Director of Public Health annual report.

DARS-NIC-776114-J7Q9J.summary: University College London's agreement covers identifiable NHS England data on deaths, cancer registrations and medicines dispensed in primary care for 300 deceased participants of the AspECT trial. The data is for following up whether aspirin combined with a proton pump inhibitor (a stomach acid medicine) affects deaths, oesophageal cancer or high-grade dysplasia (precancerous changes). The aim is to inform guidance on preventing oesophageal cancer in people with Barrett's oesophagus.

DARS-NIC-776144-T4V1D.summary: The University of Bristol, an academic body, has an agreement covering civil registrations of death and hospital admissions data (Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care) for the ASPECT randomised trial. The trial tests whether aspirin reduces heart attacks, strokes and cardiovascular deaths within 90 days in people aged 50 and over admitted to hospital with pneumonia. The main intended benefit is evidence to guide treatment decisions and potentially reduce these events in England.

DARS-NIC-776147-F5N3V.summary: Queen Mary University of London's agreement covers identifiable demographic data, specifically NHS Numbers, for people who have consented to join the Heartburn Health Programme. The data is for the linked BEST4 Screening Trial, which tests a capsule sponge as a screening tool for Barrett's oesophagus and oesophageal cancer. The numbers are to label samples, make onward referrals and follow up cancer outcomes. The stated benefit is accurate NHS Numbers for each participant.

DARS-NIC-776195-H7W4D.summary: Imperial College London's agreement covers the use of hospital admitted patient care and outpatient records from Hospital Episode Statistics. The data is for studying how pelvic floor surgery for rectal prolapse, constipation and faecal incontinence has varied across the UK over the past decade, including outcomes and waiting times. The main intended benefit is to identify regions with limited access to specialist treatment, so that policymakers and clinicians can reduce inequalities in care.

DARS-NIC-77633-Y4X1L.summary: Sheffield City Council's agreement covers hospital and emergency care records (Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set). The agreement allows the data to be used for its public health duties, such as needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, and advice to NHS commissioners. The aim is locally focused analysis of health inequalities. The council has analysed health inequalities in admissions, outpatient "did not attend" rates by ethnicity, and Covid-19 admissions.

DARS-NIC-776600-D8P6R.summary: Observational and Pragmatic Research International Limited's agreement covers the use of NHS hospital, emergency care and death registration records to analyse a trial called PREVAIL. The trial tests whether CONQUEST, a quality improvement programme for GP practices, reduces flare-ups and serious heart or breathing events in people with high-risk chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). Practices receiving the programme will be compared with practices giving usual care. If it works, the main benefit would be earlier diagnosis and better-targeted treatment.

DARS-NIC-776952-Z3R9D.summary: The University of Manchester's agreement covers the use of pseudonymised hospital, accident and emergency, and death registration data for patients registered with GP practices that use the PATCHS online consultation system. The agreement allows research into whether the system's artificial intelligence (AI) triage changes rates of A&E attendance, hospital admission and death compared with practices using PATCHS without AI. The aim is to help the NHS, GP practices and software companies decide whether to use AI triage, so that urgent patients may be helped sooner.

DARS-NIC-777554-J2V4K.summary: University College London (UCL), an academic institution, is authorised to use pseudonymised NHS England cancer registration, consolidated cancer and National Cancer Patient Experience Survey data on patients diagnosed with 21 solid organ cancers in England since January 2013. The agreement allows study of the causes of inequalities in cancer survival, patient experience, stage at diagnosis, route to diagnosis and first-line treatment. The expected benefit is to identify unusual care patterns so health professionals can investigate them and improve patient care.

DARS-NIC-777868-Z9N1M.summary: The London Borough of Hammersmith & Fulham's agreement covers hospital and emergency care records from Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set. The data is for its public health work, including needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, the annual public health report, advice to NHS commissioners and health impact assessments. The main intended benefit is locally focused analysis of health outcomes and inequalities, including for specific groups, so that the needs of disadvantaged residents are identified and addressed.

DARS-NIC-777919-R7D2B.summary: The University of Leeds, with the University of Sheffield and Sheffield Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust, is covered by an agreement that allows identifiable hospital, emergency care and death registration records for about 200 trial participants to be used. The data is for estimating hospital resource use and costs, and the time to events such as melanoma-related hospital care or death. This supports the DANTE trial, which compares a 12-month course of anti-PD-1 treatment with standard-length treatment in advanced melanoma. The aim is to help clinicians choose treatment regimens and allocate resources more effectively.

DARS-NIC-778449-V2L5D.summary: University Hospital Southampton NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers identifiable hospital, emergency care and death registration records for patients in the FLO-ELA trial. The agreement allows the data to be used to test whether cardiac output-guided fluid therapy reduces deaths after emergency bowel surgery (laparotomy) and to assess costs. The aim is to show whether the treatment should be adopted nationally. Earlier data supported safety monitoring reports and led the trial team to change its primary outcome.

DARS-NIC-778499-F3Q4L.summary: South East London Cancer Alliance, hosted by Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust, is permitted to use National Cancer Waiting Times Monitoring Data Set records from the Cancer Wait Times system. The agreement allows analysis of waiting times and pathways across local hospitals and the ICB, to identify variation and delays. The main aim is faster diagnosis and treatment, supporting better survival and patient experience. Earlier similar analysis is reported to have improved performance and corrected treatment pathways at Guy's and St Thomas'.

DARS-NIC-778520-D7B2M.summary: East of England - North Cancer Alliance, a network of health organisations, is licensed to use the National Cancer Waiting Times Monitoring Data Set, which records patients' cancer pathways from referral to treatment. The agreement allows analysis of waiting times and patient flows across trusts and integrated care boards (ICBs) to find variation, long waits and reasons for delay. The main intended benefit is better cancer pathways, helping services meet national waiting time standards and improving patient survival and experience.

DARS-NIC-778539-F0L7F.summary: NHS England's agreement gives Cancer Alliances, starting with Thames Valley Cancer Alliance (accessing through NHS Thames Valley Integrated Care Board), access to the National Cancer Waiting Times Monitoring Data Set from the Cancer Wait Times system. The agreement allows them to analyse waiting times for cancer diagnosis and treatment and to look for variation between providers. The aim is to improve cancer pathways, survival and patient experience. Earlier access has already supported local service improvement work.

DARS-NIC-778853-K4R8H.summary: University College London (UCL)'s agreement covers pseudonymised hospital admission records, death registration data and the national congenital heart disease audit for children in England with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy who had surgery to relieve a blocked heart outflow. It allows study of how many such operations take place, how outcomes vary between centres, and complications, readmissions and survival. The aim is to inform service planning, including whether surgery should be centralised.

DARS-NIC-778927-P3D9Z.summary: Imperial College London's agreement covers hospital records for emergency care, admitted patient care and outpatients. The data is for a research project on how cyberattacks could spread between NHS hospitals and how A&E demand would shift if hospitals were disrupted. The agreement allows the team to build a prototype tool to simulate hospital closures and plan how to redistribute patients. The intended benefit is better NHS preparedness and response to large-scale cyberattacks.

DARS-NIC-779200-S6R2D.summary: University College London's MRC Clinical Trials Unit's agreement covers linked NHS England data on deaths, hospital admissions and outpatient visits, and cancer registrations for about 8,000 consenting participants in three cancer trials (PATCH, Add-Aspirin and RAMPART). The agreement allows tracking of long-term outcomes such as survival, cancer recurrence, new cancers and treatment side effects. It also allows testing of whether health records can replace extra trial follow-up visits. The aim is to make trials faster and less burdensome for patients and hospital staff.

DARS-NIC-779354-C7T9H.summary: Somerset, Wiltshire, Avon and Gloucestershire Cancer Alliance, hosted by North Bristol NHS Trust, has an agreement covering National Cancer Waiting Times Monitoring Data Set data from the Cancer Wait Times system. The agreement allows analysis of waits from referral to treatment, comparison of hospital trusts and areas, and identification of long waits and variation in cancer pathways. The data is for guiding priorities and investment so cancer patients are diagnosed and treated sooner. Earlier access to similar data supported prostate improvement plans and shorter oesophageal cancer treatment waits.

DARS-NIC-779400-J2J4Z.summary: The University of Plymouth's agreement covers linked hospital records (emergency care, admitted patient and outpatient data) and death registration data. The data is for studying end-of-life care in rural and coastal communities of the South West Peninsula, including place of death and how distance from services affects care. The intended benefit is evidence and policy insights to help integrated care boards (ICBs) reduce geographical inequalities in end-of-life care.

DARS-NIC-779433-Q9R8N.summary: The London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine (LSHTM)'s agreement covers hospital and emergency care records from NHS England, including Emergency Care Data Set and Hospital Episode Statistics data. The data is for the THERM-UK project, which measures health risks from heat, cold, air pollution and infectious diseases, and the health benefits of reducing heat exposure. The findings are intended to inform policy, hospital and care home practice, and public guidance on protecting health during hot weather.

DARS-NIC-77953-C4M3T.summary: The University of Leeds's agreement covers the linking of hospital records on A&E attendances, inpatient admissions and outpatient appointments with GP records, for patients at eight English hospitals without a liaison psychiatry service. The agreement allows the university to build patient pathways and calculate their costs to the health service, to assess the cost-effectiveness and efficiency of different liaison psychiatry service set-ups. The main intended benefit is reports to help local and national commissioners make decisions about hospital mental health services.

DARS-NIC-779746-L0Q9T.summary: Wessex Cancer Alliance, a cancer network covering the Wessex region, is permitted to use National Cancer Waiting Times Monitoring Data Set records from the Cancer Wait Times system. The agreement allows analysis of waiting times across hospital trusts and integrated care boards to spot variation, long waits and reasons for delay. The main aim is to help improve cancer pathways, so that patients are diagnosed and treated sooner, with better survival and experience.

DARS-NIC-780370-H0H7P.summary: The Office for National Statistics (ONS)'s agreement covers records of medicines dispensed in primary care, supplied by the NHS Business Services Authority. The agreement allows linking them with other data, including Census 2021, to produce official statistics on population, health and disability. It also allows studying how treatments such as weight loss drugs and menopause medication affect employment, earnings and benefits. The intended benefit is more complete health information to guide government and local decisions.

DARS-NIC-780518-Q7K4W.summary: The UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA)'s agreement covers identifiable NHS England Flag 4 data, which marks people registering with a GP after arriving from overseas. The agreement allows the data to identify who is eligible for latent TB (tuberculosis) infection testing and to monitor and report on the national testing and treatment programme. The main intended benefit is evidence to inform TB screening policy, supporting earlier detection and treatment and reducing TB in England.

DARS-NIC-780525-J4L3S.summary: NHS England and the Department for Health and Social Care (DHSC) will jointly analyse pseudonymised NHS data on elective care, cancer waiting times, diagnostics, urgent and emergency care, and costs. They will use it to give ministers and senior officials timely analysis on waiting lists, waiting times and unit costs. The main intended benefit is better evidence for policy and funding decisions, leading to improved, faster and more efficient services.

DARS-NIC-781290-Q2Q6F.summary: The University of Leeds, an academic organisation, has an agreement covering NHS England hospital, cancer registration, radiotherapy, systemic anti-cancer therapy and death records. The agreement allows linking these records with data from about 5,500 people who took part in completed multiple myeloma clinical trials. The aim is to test whether routine health data can accurately support long-term follow-up in trials, and to study frailty, bone disease and who takes part. The main intended benefit is faster, cheaper and more efficient blood cancer trials.

DARS-NIC-781704-X8W4H.summary: Bangor University's agreement covers the use of hospital and emergency care records from NHS England (Emergency Care Data Set, and Hospital Episode Statistics for admitted patient care, critical care and outpatients) in a clinical trial called COPE. The trial compares carboprost with oxytocin as the first treatment for postpartum haemorrhage, looks at their cost-effectiveness, and explores participants' experiences. The findings are expected to help policy-makers, doctors and patients decide on best practice in care.

DARS-NIC-782158-W5V8C.summary: Synapsys IQ's agreement covers medicines dispensed in primary care, hospital prescribing and administration, emergency care and hospital admitted and outpatient activity data. The agreement allows it to build dashboards, tailored analyses and publications showing prescribing variation across England, to support safer prescribing and planning in the NHS. ICBs have used its bespoke analyses to plan asthma and COPD work, and an asthma analysis supported a conference poster.

DARS-NIC-782177-G5W5G.summary: The University of Oxford's agreement covers NHS England data on deaths, diagnostic imaging, hospital admissions and outpatient visits, and national cancer records. The data is for the DeLIVER research programme, which follows people with cirrhosis or early liver cancer (hepatocellular carcinoma, HCC). The aim is to understand what predicts HCC and to build a risk score. The main intended benefit is detecting liver cancer earlier, when treatment is more likely to work.

DARS-NIC-782449-Z6G3F.summary: University College London (UCL) is using birth notification and civil registration birth records to recruit families to Generation New Era, a long-term research study of about 30,000 babies born across the UK in the mid-2020s. The data is used to select families in England and Wales, to target fieldwork and to check how representative participants are. The study aims to show how inequalities in early child development emerge over time.
DARS-NIC-782449-Z6G3F.retense_draft: University College London's agreement covers the use of birth notification and civil registration birth records to recruit families to Generation New Era, a long-term research study of about 30,000 babies born across the UK in the mid-2020s. The data is for selecting families in England and Wales, targeting fieldwork and checking how representative participants are. The study aims to show how inequalities in early child development emerge over time.

DARS-NIC-782954-Z6C8Z.summary: The University of Oxford is using identifiable hospital admission, emergency care and death registration records for a small group of people aged 75 or over who lack capacity to consent and are taking blood pressure medicines. The data supports the OPTIMISE2 trial, which tests whether stopping or reducing these medicines is safe, looking at emergency hospital admissions and deaths. The aim is to inform clinical guidelines on treating high blood pressure in older adults.
DARS-NIC-782954-Z6C8Z.retense_draft: The University of Oxford's agreement covers identifiable hospital admission, emergency care and death registration records for a small group of people aged 75 or over who lack capacity to consent and are taking blood pressure medicines. The data is for the OPTIMISE2 trial, which tests whether stopping or reducing these medicines is safe, looking at emergency hospital admissions and deaths. The aim is to inform clinical guidelines on treating high blood pressure in older adults.
