DARS-NIC-783876-K7N5S.summary: The Royal Borough of Windsor & Maidenhead Council's agreement covers civil registration data on births and deaths, plus primary care mortality data, which includes identifiable details. The data is for understanding local health needs, supporting immunisation and public health work, and carrying out suicide audits. Results are to be published as summary statistics. The main intended benefit is local health and care services that are better targeted, to reduce mortality and health inequalities.

DARS-NIC-78397-Z1F1Q.summary: The University of Oxford's agreement covers the use of hospital, mental health and mortality records to follow up people in the Asymptomatic Carotid Surgery Trial (ACST-1), who had narrowed neck arteries. The data is for studying long-term stroke risk and whether carotid surgery reduces dementia. The aim is to help patients and clinicians make better treatment decisions.

DARS-NIC-784100-W4B7T.summary: The University of Manchester's agreement covers the use of linked NHS hospital, emergency care, maternity, mental health, death and cancer registration records for the Childhood Arthritis Prospective Study, which follows children with juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA). The agreement allows study of what happens to them as adults, including ongoing arthritis, mental health, cancer and death rates. The aim is to give patients and families better information on what to expect in future.

DARS-NIC-784425-X2Y5R.summary: The Office for National Statistics (ONS)'s agreement covers the Mental Health Services Data Set, which covers mental health care, linked with Census 2021 and other administrative data. The data is for statistical research on disability and general health, on how mental health and services affect employment, earnings and benefits, and on mental health support for young people. The main intended benefit is better evidence to help target health services and policy decisions.

DARS-NIC-785335-G6D8R.summary: The University of Surrey's agreement covers National Disease Registration Service (NDRS) cancer registration data and National Cancer Patient Experience Survey data. The research looks at whether marginalised groups report different experiences of cancer care, and whether those differences help explain inequalities in receiving treatment and in time to treatment. The intended benefit is an evidence base to help policy makers reduce inequalities in cancer care.

DARS-NIC-785339-D9Q2D.summary: The Newcastle upon Tyne Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers cancer registration data and the National Disease Registration Service (NDRS) consolidated cancer data set for a research project on lymphoma in people with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). The project aims to identify which types of IBD carry the highest lymphoma risk, whether genetic factors are involved, and which medicines may raise the risk. The main intended benefit is reducing the number of people with IBD who develop lymphoma.

DARS-NIC-786257-W9C8P.summary: University Hospital Southampton NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers identifiable hospital, emergency care and civil registration (death) records for patients in the FLO-ELA trial. The data is for testing whether cardiac output-guided fluid therapy during emergency abdominal surgery reduces deaths and is cost-effective, with the aim of informing national practice. Data from an earlier agreement helped trial monitoring reports spot a fall in the death rate, which led the team to change the trial's primary outcome.

DARS-NIC-786264-W6R5D.summary: University Hospital Southampton NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers hospital admission records and civil death registration data. The agreement allows follow-up of participants from the FORECAST trial, which compared CT coronary angiography with computed fractional flow reserve against standard care for stable chest pain. The data is for comparing the two approaches over five years for health outcomes and NHS resource use. The main intended benefit is stronger evidence to guide how chest pain patients are diagnosed.

DARS-NIC-786702-B8R5P.summary: Sanius Health, a commercial health data and technology company, is licensed to use NHS hospital, emergency care and primary care prescribing data about people with sickle cell disease. The data is for describing how they use care and what that care costs across urgent and planned settings, including high-cost drugs and transfusions. The aim is a national costing index, published in a peer-reviewed paper and reports, to help the NHS and NICE plan services and assess new treatments.

DARS-NIC-786843-Y6V6G.summary: The Department of Health and Social Care will use adult social care data collected by NHS England, covering areas such as council spending, safeguarding, carers and user surveys. It will use the data to take over publishing official adult social care statistics, which were previously published by NHS England. The aim is to support monitoring of services, accountability and policy decisions based on current, complete information.

DARS-NIC-786978-Z6K4M.summary: Abiomed Inc's agreement covers use of data from the National Audit of Percutaneous Coronary Interventions run by NICOR. The data is for a descriptive service evaluation of how Impella and intra-aortic balloon pumps are used in high-risk heart procedures in the UK. The aim is to see how far practice follows NICE guidance and to help design future studies.

DARS-NIC-787003-B1G4C.summary: The University of Bristol's agreement covers hospital admissions, outpatient and emergency care data for a research trial called RADICAL. The trial looks at whether radiofrequency denervation, a treatment for moderate to severe long-term lower back pain, reduces hospital use and is cost-effective compared with placebo over 24 months. The findings are intended to inform clinical guidelines and healthcare spending decisions.

DARS-NIC-787006-N2H5C.summary: King's College Hospital NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers national adult cardiac surgery audit data from the National Institute for Cardiovascular Outcomes Research (NICOR). The data is for helping run a UK-wide service evaluation of temporary mechanical devices that support the heart in patients who are very unwell before or after heart surgery. The aim is to show how often and which devices are used and what outcomes follow, and so to help plan the size of the service needed.

DARS-NIC-787009-K8R3B.summary: Imperial College London's agreement covers pseudonymised patient records from the Myocardial Ischaemia National Audit Project (MINAP). These cover about 3,000 people discharged with takotsubo cardiomyopathy, a heart condition that can mimic a heart attack, plus matched controls. The data is for research to estimate how common the condition is and identify associated factors such as triggers and existing health conditions. The stated main benefit is better understanding of the condition, supporting more accurate diagnosis and personalised care.

DARS-NIC-787193-Y8W6D.summary: The University of York's agreement covers national audit data on percutaneous coronary interventions (procedures to open narrowed heart arteries). The research asks whether a doctor's exam and training appraisal performance relates to how they later practise and to patients' 30-day mortality after these procedures. The main intended benefit is evidence to guide cardiology training policy, including support for doctors who may need it, and ultimately better patient outcomes.

DARS-NIC-787195-R1H2P.summary: University College London's agreement covers pseudonymised national records for patients who have had heart rhythm procedures, including NHS hospital, emergency care, death registration and national heart audit data. The data is for finding which patients with pacemakers or defibrillators are at risk of problems such as shocks, stroke or heart failure, and for understanding differences in outcomes. The main intended benefit is better selection of patients for implants and improved care for those at high risk.

DARS-NIC-787209-F3W7J.summary: University College London's agreement covers the use of NHS England hospital, emergency care, mental health and death registration data on children and young people with visual impairment or blindness. The study will link this with education and cohort study data to examine their health, healthcare use and educational outcomes. It aims to give policy-makers, service commissioners, families and charities national evidence on what works well and what needs improving in care.

DARS-NIC-787477-W3G5Z.summary: The Renal Association's agreement covers linking hospital records (admissions, outpatient, A&E and critical care) and death registration data to its rare kidney disease registry, the National Registry of Rare Kidney Diseases (RaDaR), which the charity runs alongside the UK Renal Registry. The data is for studying risk factors, predicting outcomes, examining inequalities, estimating care costs and checking the registry's data. The intended benefit is better evidence to improve care and outcomes for people with rare kidney disease.

DARS-NIC-788212-W2D4D.summary: King's College Hospital NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers NICOR Adult Cardiac Surgery data on adults who had elective cardiac surgery between 2012 and 2022. The agreement allows study of how smoking affects outcomes around the time of surgery, such as in-hospital death, length of stay and complications, and how this differs by type of operation, region and socioeconomic status. The aim is to identify patients most at risk so that smoking-cessation support can be designed for them.

DARS-NIC-788281-L8X5B.summary: The Regional Drug and Therapeutics Centre, hosted by Newcastle Upon Tyne Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust, is covered by an agreement that allows it to use pseudonymised hospital records (Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set) and primary care medicines dispensing data. It links prescribing with hospital activity to help NHS bodies improve how medicines are used and reduce avoidable admissions. It reports that findings led Greater Manchester to change its diabetes formulary and pathway, and COPD and asthma pathways to be redefined.

DARS-NIC-788403-Y9M1G.summary: Leeds Institute of Health Sciences, part of the University of Leeds, has an agreement covering NHS England cancer registration and death registration data for the Yorkshire Lung Screening Trial. The trial compares inviting current and former smokers to community-based lung cancer screening with usual care, using cancer stage and outcomes data. The main intended benefit is evidence to inform the design of future lung screening programmes and increase uptake, particularly in deprived communities.

DARS-NIC-788591-Z8G5K.summary: The University of East Anglia's agreement covers NHS England hospital, emergency care, death registration and primary care dispensing data for the CHARMER study. The study tests whether training geriatricians and hospital pharmacists to stop unsuitable medicines for older people reduces hospital readmissions, deaths and costs. The intended benefit is to inform national policy on managing overprescribing and improve older people's health and quality of life.

DARS-NIC-788663-G4F2D.summary: The Office for National Statistics's agreement covers use of the NHS England Health and Growth Accelerator Programme minimum data set, which records who took part in the programme's interventions. The agreement allows the data to be linked to the Office's own employment and socio-demographic data to give a preliminary analysis of the programme, which aims to tackle health-driven economic inactivity in three pilot areas. The aim is to support a bid for multi-year funding and to show whether interventions keep people in work or return them to work.

DARS-NIC-788684-Y5P8C.summary: The National Centre for Stereotactic Radiosurgery's agreement covers cancer registration and death registration data. The agreement allows study of patients treated with Gamma Knife radiosurgery over the last 40 years to see whether they develop cancer afterwards, including in the treated area, and whether this is more common than in the general population. The data is for giving doctors, policy-makers and patients better evidence on the long-term risks of this treatment.

DARS-NIC-789345-S3W6T.summary: Milton Keynes City Council's agreement covers civil registration data on births and deaths, plus primary care mortality data, which includes identifiable details. The agreement allows the data to be used to measure local health needs, plan immunisation programmes, protect public health and support work such as suicide audits and prevention. Results are published only as aggregated statistics. The main intended benefit is health and care services tailored to local needs, helping to reduce mortality and health inequalities.

DARS-NIC-789702-M6C7G.summary: Liverpool Heart and Chest Hospital NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers hospital admission records and civil death registrations for England. The agreement allows a pilot research study on post infarction ventricular septal defect, a rare tear in the heart that can follow a heart attack. The study looks at how often it occurs, who is affected and how patients move through care. The aim is to give better information for planning future clinical trials and a patient registry.

DARS-NIC-789772-N6S1N.summary: The University of Bristol's agreement covers linked NHS England health records, including hospital, mental health, maternity, cancer, death and medicines data, for the Avon Longitudinal Study of Parents and Children (ALSPAC), known as "Children of the 90s". The agreement allows the data to be added to a research database that approved researchers can use to study health and wellbeing across generations. The data is for improving understanding of conditions such as depression, psychosis and self-harm. Past ALSPAC research contributed to UK policy change on the "back to sleep" advice to reduce cot death.

DARS-NIC-79018-W9T1D.summary: Halton Borough Council's agreement covers the use of hospital admissions, outpatient, critical care and emergency care data to carry out its public health duties. The agreement allows analysis of patterns of illness, access to care and health differences between groups, to inform needs assessments, health strategies, commissioning and advice to NHS commissioners. The data is for locally focused analysis, especially for disadvantaged groups. The agreement allows reporting of the data to internal boards on key indicators. A 2025 analysis of children's hospital admissions and accidental injuries has been published.

DARS-NIC-790414-L6R9T.summary: The Institute of Cancer Research's agreement covers identifiable death registration and cohort-tracking records for men with prostate cancer, or a strong family history of it, who joined the UK Genetic Prostate Cancer Study. The data is for studying survival and finding genetic changes linked to prostate cancer risk. The aim is to help identify who is at higher risk and to inform screening and new treatments. The data has helped develop a genetic risk model for personalised prostate cancer risk predictions.

DARS-NIC-791529-K1J8C.summary: The University of Leeds's agreement covers the use of NHS England mailing cohort data and an aggregate data quality report to help recruit people to the Digital- My Arm Pain Programme (D-MAPP) clinical trial. The trial is testing whether a digitally delivered self-management programme can be developed for people with musculoskeletal disorders of the arm, to help recovery, long-term function and pain. The main intended benefit is faster, more efficient trial enrolment from a wider pool of potential participants.

DARS-NIC-791694-D2J8T.summary: Cristal Health Ltd, trading as Akrivia Health, has an agreement with NHS England's DigiTrials Recruitment Service, which allows personal data to be used to identify and send invitation letters to adults in England with a diagnosis or treatment for major depressive disorder, bipolar disorder or schizophrenia. The letters invite people to join the Global Minds study, which looks at links between serious mental illness and dementia and human biology. The study aims to improve diagnosis and help develop better treatments.

DARS-NIC-791919-T4Y0Y.summary: NHS South West London Integrated Care Board's agreement covers hospital records for emergency care, admitted patients and outpatients across England. The agreement allows the data to be used for commissioning and risk stratification, benchmarking the Board against other areas to find inequalities in care, such as length of stay, waiting times and readmissions. The main intended benefit is better evidence for planning services and allocating resources more fairly.

DARS-NIC-792066-B5D2T.summary: University College London (UCL)'s agreement covers the use of demographic data from NHS England to recruit families to Generation New Era, a long-term research study of about 30,000 infants born across the UK in the mid-2020s. The data is for selecting families to contact, boosting the sample using ethnicity fields, targeting fieldwork and checking how representative participants are. The study aims to understand how inequalities in early child development emerge over time.

DARS-NIC-792991-W4Z6B.summary: Cambridge University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers hospital admitted patient care, outpatient and newborn screening data for a clinical trial called the Digital Imaging versus Ophthalmoscopy (DIvO) study. The data is for testing whether digital imaging with the Neocam device is more accurate than the standard red-reflex eye test for spotting congenital cataract in newborns. The main intended benefit is earlier detection of cataracts, which could lead to better long-term vision and help inform national screening policy.

DARS-NIC-793230-S7H9P.summary: The University of Edinburgh, working with NHS Lothian, has an agreement that allows it to use NHS England death registration, hospital admission and primary care dispensed medicines data for the ASPIRING clinical trial. The trial tests whether taking a single antiplatelet drug, alongside standard care, delays major cardiovascular events such as strokes and heart attacks in people who have survived a stroke caused by bleeding in the brain. It could show whether this treatment reduces those events.

DARS-NIC-793367-S9D4P.summary: The University of Sussex's agreement covers the use of linked NHS hospital, emergency care, mental health and death registration records for a research study. It looks at women who had an adult psychiatric inpatient stay in England between April 2021 and March 2023, comparing mothers with non-mothers on their characteristics, length of stay, readmission and A&E attendance. The main intended benefit is national evidence on inequalities and outcomes for hospitalised mothers, to inform NHS planning and support for parents.

DARS-NIC-793368-F6W8K.summary: West Berkshire Council's agreement covers civil registration data on births and deaths, together with primary care mortality data, which includes identifiable details. The data is for understanding the health needs of local people, supporting public health work such as suicide audits and immunisation programmes, and producing aggregated reports like Joint Strategic Needs Assessments. The intended benefit is local services that are better targeted to reduce premature deaths and health inequalities.

DARS-NIC-793437-Z3C1X.summary: Westmorland and Furness Council's agreement covers Hospital Episode Statistics and Emergency Care Data Set records for hospital admissions, outpatients, critical care and emergency care. The data is for supporting its public health duties, including needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, the Director of Public Health's annual report and advice to NHS commissioners. The main intended benefit is locally focused analysis of health outcomes and inequalities, so that the needs of the local population, particularly the most disadvantaged, are identified and responded to.

DARS-NIC-793709-R9M3D.summary: The University of Warwick, working with University Hospitals Coventry and Warwickshire NHS Trust, is covered by an agreement that allows use of NHS England's recruitment service, which draws on personal data to identify and write to adults in England who had a stroke and left hospital 6 to 36 months ago. The letters invite them to join the ReSTORe trial, which tests whether an online, home-based exercise and recovery programme improves well-being after stroke. The service aims to speed up and improve recruitment.

DARS-NIC-793895-J0F7F.summary: Queen Mary University of London's agreement covers NHS England data quality reports, which allow participants' contact details and life status to be checked, for the Heartburn Health Programme and the BEST4 Screening Trial. NHS England will check whether participants have died and update their contact information, so the study team avoids contacting deceased people and can reach participants reliably. The intended benefit is to prevent distressing contact with families and to improve recruitment and retention in the trial.

DARS-NIC-79434-P1T7D.summary: Cardiff University's agreement covers a list-cleaning report from the Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) to check a group of about 110 participants in the Building Blocks study who have been lost to follow-up. The report gives updated identifiers and any death notifications, so the team can confirm who is still eligible and match them to National Pupil Database records. The main intended benefit is that only eligible participants stay in the study, and that families are not sent unwanted contact.

DARS-NIC-79526-V8F2X.summary: The University of East Anglia's agreement allows the use of pseudonymised hospital admissions, A&E, outpatient, critical care and death records for asthma patients at participating GP practices in England and Wales. The data is for the ARRISA-UK trial, which tests whether flagging at-risk patients' records and training staff reduces asthma-related hospital admissions, A&E attendances and deaths. The aim is to show whether this approach is worth adopting in primary care. The trial's main results were analysed and submitted to a peer-reviewed journal.

DARS-NIC-795268-S1T4D.summary: The Lampard Inquiry's agreement covers a statutory investigation into mental health inpatient deaths in Essex between 2000 and 2023, and allows it to use Mental Health Services Data Set (MHSDS) data. Its appointed expert health statisticians will analyse the data in a secure environment and publish a report on failings in care, staff practice, and NHS trust culture and governance. The report is intended to support evidence-based recommendations to reduce avoidable deaths and improve patient safety.

DARS-NIC-795405-N6K0D.summary: Stoke-on-Trent City Council is using pseudonymised hospital data, covering emergency care, admitted patient care, critical care and outpatients, for its public health work. It will analyse this to support its statutory duties, including needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, commissioning and advice to NHS commissioners. The main intended benefit is locally focused analysis of health inequalities, particularly for the most disadvantaged groups.
DARS-NIC-795405-N6K0D.retense_draft: Stoke-on-Trent City Council's agreement covers pseudonymised hospital data, covering emergency care, admitted patient care, critical care and outpatients, for its public health work. The agreement allows analysis to support its statutory duties, including needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, commissioning and advice to NHS commissioners. The main intended benefit is locally focused analysis of health inequalities, particularly for the most disadvantaged groups.

DARS-NIC-795868-X8R6B.summary: The Royal Wolverhampton NHS Trust, which hosts West Midlands Cancer Alliance, has an agreement covering National Cancer Waiting Times Monitoring Data Set records from the Cancer Wait Times system. The agreement allows analysis of waiting times across cancer pathways to find variation, long waits and delays, and to inform service discussions and investment. The main intended benefit is better cancer survival and patient experience. Earlier access to similar data is reported to have informed service improvement work.

DARS-NIC-795871-J2G4K.summary: NHS Nottingham and Nottinghamshire Integrated Care Board, on behalf of East Midlands Cancer Alliance, has an agreement covering use of National Cancer Waiting Times Monitoring Data Set records from the Cancer Wait Times system. The agreement allows analysis of waiting times and variation in cancer pathways across providers. The data is for helping the Alliance plan improvements, meet national waiting time standards and improve cancer survival and patient experience.

DARS-NIC-796147-S7T1T.summary: The University of Nottingham's agreement covers the use of hospital admission records and death registration data for a study cohort of older surgical patients. The agreement allows the data to be linked to its SNAP 3 study, which looks at how frailty, multimorbidity and delirium affect outcomes after surgery, including readmission and mortality. The aim is to improve the care of older surgical patients, including through a tool that predicts the risk of postoperative delirium.

DARS-NIC-796202-M0L0X.summary: The University of Essex's agreement covers the use of Health Survey for England data for a research project on school holidays and children's health. The project aims to understand how circumstances during school holidays and local food environments contribute to childhood obesity and mental health problems, and how far holidays drive inequality in these outcomes. The findings are expected to help policymakers decide on holiday support, such as food vouchers and holiday clubs, and so reduce health inequalities.

DARS-NIC-796232-C6B3Q.summary: University College London's agreement covers the use of death registration records, hospital admitted patient care records and dispensed medicines data for a research project on severe aortic stenosis. The data is for testing whether cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) scan measures can predict long-term survival after valve surgery or transcatheter valve replacement better than current risk models. The aim is more accurate risk assessment and better patient selection, which could improve survival and quality of life.

DARS-NIC-796943-G2Q0P.summary: West Berkshire Council's agreement covers hospital and emergency care data on admitted patient care, outpatients, critical care and accident and emergency (Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set). The agreement allows the data to support the council's public health duties, including needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, advice to NHS commissioners and the annual public health report. The main intended benefit is local analysis of health outcomes and inequalities, particularly for the most disadvantaged groups.

DARS-NIC-797243-P7K9P.summary: University Hospital Southampton NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers hospital admission records and death registrations for people who took part in the RIPCORD 2 trial. The data is for following them for five years to see whether routine pressure wire assessment during heart artery investigations is safe and effective compared with conventional angiography. The aim is to inform clinical guidelines. The main trial paper was published in the journal Circulation.

DARS-NIC-79728-X2C2X.summary: Lancashire & South Cumbria NHS Foundation Trust, hosting the Innovation Agency, is permitted to use pseudonymised hospital activity data (SUS for Commissioners) covering the North West Coast. The data supports the Connected Health Cities programme, which builds analysis models and algorithms for alcohol, COPD (chronic obstructive pulmonary disease) and epilepsy care, to help commissioners and clinicians improve services. Reports have already influenced seizure services, and analysis identified COPD hotspots in Wirral where a GP practice intervention tool was offered.

DARS-NIC-797405-H6S8S.summary: Northumbria University, an academic institution, has an agreement covering NHS England emergency care, hospital admission and mental health services data. The agreement allows the university to study how mental health crisis response pathways in four areas of England changed after the police strategy "Right Care Right Person" was introduced, looking at service use, patient outcomes and costs. The aim is to give the NHS better evidence for planning and commissioning crisis care.

DARS-NIC-798519-F7X8X.summary: London North West University Healthcare NHS Trust's agreement allows it to use NHS England bowel cancer screening data on people with Lynch syndrome, with postcodes converted to deprivation scores and dates changed to ages or month and year. The data is for a service evaluation of how often these patients develop bowel cancer or polyps, how well colonoscopies detect them, and how many take part in screening. The aim is to inform evidence-based decisions on improving surveillance and care for people with Lynch syndrome.

DARS-NIC-798687-Z0Z8F.summary: University College London's Medical Research Council Clinical Trials Unit's agreement covers cancer registration, civil registration of deaths and demographics data for the STAMPEDE trial. The trial tests added treatments for men with high-risk prostate cancer starting long-term hormone therapy, and the data are for following participants' survival over the longer term. The aim is to give patients and clinicians evidence on which treatments improve survival. Death registration data let the metformin comparison report its main result sooner.

DARS-NIC-799985-H0F0G.summary: Reading Borough Council's agreement covers hospital data from NHS England, covering admitted patient care, outpatients, critical care, and accident and emergency (including the Emergency Care Data Set). The data is for its public health duties, such as producing needs assessments, strategies, the annual public health report and advice to NHS commissioners. The main intended benefit is locally focused analysis of health outcomes and inequalities, particularly for the most disadvantaged groups.

DARS-NIC-799986-S3L4Q.summary: Reading Borough Council's agreement covers the use of identifiable birth and death records, including primary care mortality data, to understand the health needs of its local population. The agreement allows the data to be used for public health work such as needs assessments, suicide audits, immunisation programmes and monitoring deaths, with only aggregated figures published and small numbers suppressed. The main intended benefit is health and care services tailored to local needs, helping to reduce mortality and health inequalities.

DARS-NIC-800347-F4P5X.summary: The University of Oxford's agreement covers hospital admission records (Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care) and civil death registration data. The data is for studying how often infections after fracture fixation and bone infections occur in England, who is most at risk, and how repeat surgery and outcomes vary between NHS providers. The main intended benefit is better evidence for patient counselling, trial design and commissioning decisions.

DARS-NIC-800961-W7P2T.summary: University College London's agreement covers the use of birth notification and civil registration birth records to recruit families in England and Wales to Generation New Era, a longitudinal study of about 30,000 infants born across the UK in the mid-2020s. The data is for selecting families to contact, boosting the England sample using ethnicity fields, and checking how representative participants are. The study aims to show how inequalities in early child development emerge over time.

DARS-NIC-800987-T2X1J.summary: NHS North East and North Cumbria ICB's agreement covers the use of Cancer Waiting Times data, which records how long cancer patients wait from referral to diagnosis and treatment, on behalf of the Northern Cancer Alliance. The agreement allows the data to be analysed to compare waiting-time performance across hospital trusts and ICBs, find variation and unusually long waits, and look at pathways beyond the national standards. The main intended benefit is to inform cancer service priorities and investment so that waits shorten, survival improves and patient experience improves.

DARS-NIC-801407-W1X9R.summary: The University of Cambridge's agreement covers National Disease Registration Service (NDRS) cancer registry data for England. The research looks at how delays in diagnosis affect stage at diagnosis, deaths and costs across the 12 most common cancers, and how this differs by ethnicity and other patient characteristics. It will also build models of breast cancer progression to test alternative screening approaches. The main intended benefit is evidence to guide diagnostic pathways, screening and more equal cancer care.

DARS-NIC-801590-G7D7B.summary: The London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine's agreement covers the use of hospital admission records (Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care) and civil registrations of death. The research project, ELATE, compares local and general anaesthesia for endovascular repair of ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysms, looking at effectiveness and cost-effectiveness for different patient groups. It aims to give clinicians and policymakers better evidence to guide anaesthetic choices.

DARS-NIC-801642-B0K2B.summary: The University of Southampton's agreement covers NHS England bowel cancer screening data from the Screening Research Office. The agreement allows study of differences in screening uptake across groups such as sex, socioeconomic status, ethnicity and disability, including changes since the FIT test was introduced in 2019 and the COVID-19 pandemic. The main intended benefit is evidence on which groups are underserved, so the screening programme can target efforts and reduce inequalities in uptake.

DARS-NIC-801643-G1K4H.summary: The University of Leeds's agreement covers NHS bowel cancer screening data from the Screening Research Office. The data is for a randomised trial, BENE-FIT, to test whether a motivation and planning leaflet, a suggested return deadline, or both together help more people complete and return their home screening (FIT) kit. It also looks at which groups benefit most. The main intended benefit is evidence on whether these low-cost measures raise screening uptake and reduce inequalities.

DARS-NIC-802018-Y0J1Y.summary: City of Wolverhampton Council, a local authority, is permitted to use hospital and emergency care data from NHS England: Hospital Episode Statistics (inpatient, outpatient, A&E and critical care) and the Emergency Care Data Set. The agreement allows the data to be used in its public health work, including needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, the annual public health report and advice to NHS commissioners. The main intended benefit is more locally focused analysis of health outcomes and inequalities, particularly for the most disadvantaged groups.

DARS-NIC-802558-Z3M1D.summary: The Office for National Statistics (ONS)'s agreement covers a wide range of NHS England health and social care data, including hospital, maternity, mental health, vaccination and demographic records. The agreement allows the data to be used to carry out its statutory functions, such as producing official and experimental statistics, research, methodology work and survey sampling. The main intended benefit is better-quality official statistics, including population figures that the Department of Health and Social Care uses to plan services and allocate funding.

DARS-NIC-80304-H6P6R.summary: Imperial College London's agreement covers the use of pseudonymised Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care records from 2006/07 to 2015/16, linked to surgeons' simulation-based skills assessment scores. The study examines whether performance in simulated assessments is associated with real-world clinical and patient outcomes. The agreement allows an honorary staff member to continue the analysis and write up a peer-reviewed publication. The intended benefit is evidence to improve surgical training and assessment, and so patient care.

DARS-NIC-803151-K2Q8V.summary: NHS West and North London Integrated Care Board's agreement covers commissioning, invoice validation and risk stratification datasets, some of which can identify individual patients. The agreement allows the data to be used to check that provider invoices are correct and payable, to identify patients at high risk of health deterioration, and to plan and redesign local health services. The main intended benefit is that providers are paid accurately and care is better targeted to the needs of the local population.

DARS-NIC-803751-Z3B5K.summary: The University of Liverpool's agreement covers national NHS England screening data from the newborn and infant physical examination (NIPE) programme. The agreement allows a service evaluation of developmental dysplasia of the hip in babies. The evaluation will describe how often the condition is found, how screening results compare, and how treatment varies between providers. It aims to show unwarranted variation and support safer, better-quality care.

DARS-NIC-804158-C1F4R.summary: NHS Essex Integrated Care Board's agreement covers commissioning, invoice validation and risk stratification datasets, some of which can identify patients by NHS number. The data is for checking provider invoices before payment, identifying patients at high risk of health deterioration, and planning health services for the local population. The main intended benefit is more effective commissioning of services, leading to better patient experience and health outcomes.

DARS-NIC-804235-N1Y0J.summary: NHS Central East Integrated Care Board's agreement covers commissioning, invoice validation and risk stratification datasets, which include pseudonymised and some identifiable patient data. The agreement allows the data to be used to check provider invoices before payment, identify patients at high risk of health deterioration, and plan health services for the local population. The main intended benefit is more effective commissioning of services, leading to better patient experience and health outcomes.

DARS-NIC-804237-Y2H9C.summary: NHS Norfolk and Suffolk Integrated Care Board's agreement covers invoice, risk stratification and commissioning datasets, some of which can identify patients and some of which are pseudonymised. The agreement allows the data to be used to check that providers' invoices are correct and payable, to identify patients at risk of poor health so GPs can target care, and to plan and monitor health services for the local population. The main intended benefit is more effective commissioning, leading to better patient experience and health outcomes.

DARS-NIC-804238-Q6H7C.summary: NHS Thames Valley Integrated Care Board's agreement, jointly with Oxfordshire County Council for the commissioning part, covers commissioning data (clinical and financial, pseudonymised) and invoice validation data. The agreement allows the commissioning data to be used to plan health services around the needs of the local population, including population health management and service redesign. The agreement allows the invoice validation data to be used to check that provider invoices are correct and that the patient is the ICB's responsibility. The main intended benefit is that providers are paid accurately and services are better planned.

DARS-NIC-804239-H4X6K.summary: NHS Surrey and Sussex Integrated Care Board's agreement covers commissioning data, which includes clinical and financial information with personal identifiers removed, and invoice validation data. The data is for checking that care providers' invoices are correct and that patients are its responsibility, and for planning and commissioning health services for the local population. The main intended benefit is that providers are paid accurately and services are better planned to meet local needs.

DARS-NIC-806125-J8B8J.summary: BCP Council (Bournemouth, Christchurch and Poole) uses pseudonymised hospital and emergency care data, including Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set. It uses them for its public health duties, such as needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, the Director of Public Health's annual report and advice to NHS commissioners. The main intended benefit is locally focused analysis of health inequalities, so that the needs of disadvantaged groups are identified and responded to.
DARS-NIC-806125-J8B8J.retense_draft: BCP Council's agreement covers the use of pseudonymised hospital and emergency care data, including Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set. The data is for its public health duties, such as needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, the Director of Public Health's annual report and advice to NHS commissioners. The main intended benefit is locally focused analysis of health inequalities, so that the needs of disadvantaged groups are identified and responded to.

DARS-NIC-80632-R9D6T.summary: East Riding of Yorkshire Council's agreement covers the use of hospital and emergency care records (Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set) for its public health work. The agreement allows aggregated analyses to support needs assessments, health strategies, service commissioning and advice to NHS commissioners. The aim is to show local health inequalities more clearly. The data has been used to show higher emergency admission rates in deprived areas and to review outpatient travel distances for local hospitals.

DARS-NIC-808477-T8P0S.summary: The Children's Commissioner's Office's agreement covers the use of hospital, emergency care and mental health services data about children detained under the Mental Health Act. The data is for understanding how many children are detained, which children are most affected and the nature of their stays, including details such as age, ethnic group and diagnosis. The findings will go into a policy report, briefings and press releases. They are intended to help ensure that policy on children in mental health inpatient care is evidence based.

DARS-NIC-81103-S1W0G.summary: Warrington Borough Council's agreement covers the use of hospital and emergency care records (Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set) for its public health work. The data is for analysing local health needs and inequalities, supporting needs assessments, health strategies, annual reports and advice to NHS commissioners. Reported results so far include adult social care health profiles and a self-harm analysis that informed the Joint Strategic Needs Assessment.

DARS-NIC-812033-W7R8C.summary: The London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine's agreement covers hospital admission records and civil death registration data for a research project called ELATE. The data is for comparing local with general anaesthesia for endovascular repair of ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysms, looking at clinical and cost effectiveness for different patient subgroups, such as age, sex and frailty. The aim is to give clinicians and policymakers stronger evidence to guide anaesthetic choices in this emergency surgery.

DARS-NIC-81417-R1V4C.summary: NHS North East London ICB (a sub-ICB location, covering the former Redbridge CCG area) has an agreement that allows it to use pseudonymised hospital, ambulance, community and emergency care activity data. The data is for supporting the commissioning of health services and for linking NHS 111 calls to what happened to callers afterwards. This allows evaluation of the NHS 111 Patient Relationship Manager system and the accuracy of call recommendations. The main intended benefit is better planning of urgent care patient flows.

DARS-NIC-81519-G1T5F.summary: The University of Birmingham holds hospital records (A&E, inpatient, outpatient and critical care) and death registration data for about 75,000 primary care patients at risk of COPD (chronic obstructive pulmonary disease). The agreement only allows the data to be securely kept, not used further. It supports the TargetCOPD2 study, which looked at whether finding COPD earlier reduces hospital admissions and deaths. The text reports no benefit yet from the study's results.

DARS-NIC-81831-Y2N8H.summary: NHS Thurrock Clinical Commissioning Group (CCG) uses pseudonymised hospital, ambulance, community, mental health, maternity and other health service datasets. It uses them to produce intelligence for commissioning health services, including population health management, data quality checks and reports on provider activity and finance. The main intended benefit is more effective commissioning of services, leading to a better patient experience.
DARS-NIC-81831-Y2N8H.retense_draft: NHS Thurrock Clinical Commissioning Group's agreement covers pseudonymised hospital, ambulance, community, mental health, maternity and other health service datasets. The agreement allows the data to produce intelligence for commissioning health services, including population health management, data quality checks and reports on provider activity and finance. The main intended benefit is more effective commissioning of services, leading to a better patient experience.

DARS-NIC-82373-G0D9K.summary: NHS Corby CCG's agreement covers hospital activity data from the Secondary Uses Service (SUS), including accident and emergency, admitted patient care and outpatient records, including NHS numbers. The agreement allows the data to be used to check invoices for payment and to identify patients at high risk of needing future care, so GPs and commissioners can plan support. The main intended benefit is better-targeted care and more effective commissioning of services.

DARS-NIC-82378-M2B6C.summary: NHS Coventry and Warwickshire ICB (a sub-ICB location) agreement covers use of Secondary User Services (SUS+) data for commissioners, identifiable by NHS number. The data is for checking provider invoices so that only activity the ICB is responsible for is paid, and for risk stratification, which links the data with GP records to identify patients at high risk of health deterioration. The main intended benefits are accurate payment for care and better targeted, more effective care.

DARS-NIC-82384-W1T6C.summary: NHS Southern Derbyshire CCG's agreement covers pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other health service data, which includes clinical and financial information. The data is for planning and commissioning health services, including analysing population needs, monitoring contracts and redesigning services. The main intended benefit is better planning of services and patient flow to meet the needs of the local population.

DARS-NIC-82396-W4F5T.summary: NHS Coventry and Warwickshire ICB's agreement, covering the former NHS Warwickshire North CCG area, allows use of Secondary Uses Service (SUS+) data for commissioners, which can be identified by NHS number. The data is for checking invoices from care providers, so the commissioner pays only for activity it is responsible for. The main intended benefit is accurate payment to providers and appropriate use of public funds.

DARS-NIC-82404-V2S5B.summary: NHS Coventry and Warwickshire Integrated Care Board (ICB) uses Secondary User Services (SUS+) data, which can be identified by NHS number, to check invoices from care providers. The aim is to confirm that the activity claimed is the responsibility of the former South Warwickshire Clinical Commissioning Group, and to review past payments for overcharges. The main intended benefit is that providers are paid accurately and money that would otherwise be lost is recovered.
DARS-NIC-82404-V2S5B.retense_draft: NHS Coventry and Warwickshire Integrated Care Board's agreement covers the use of Secondary User Services (SUS+) data, which can be identified by NHS number, to check invoices from care providers. The data is for confirming that the activity claimed is the responsibility of the former South Warwickshire Clinical Commissioning Group, and for reviewing past payments for overcharges. The main intended benefit is that providers are paid accurately and money that would otherwise be lost is recovered.

DARS-NIC-82493-P8Y3N.summary: The University of Essex's agreement allows it to use school-level, pseudonymised National Child Measurement Programme data on children's weight and body mass index (BMI). The data is for studying how free lunches for all infant school children in England affect weight in reception class. The aim is to show whether the policy leads to fewer overweight or obese children, helping policy makers decide on funding. Reported findings include a presentation at conferences, a draft report and press coverage.

DARS-NIC-82980-V6D4Q.summary: University Hospitals Dorset NHS Foundation Trust's agreement covers the use of Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care data on behalf of the British Society for Gynaecological Endoscopy. The agreement allows the data to be used to count hysterectomies each year and show whether they were abdominal, vaginal or laparoscopic, to describe national practice and variation. The aim is to target surgeon training and inform national guidance. Early findings have already helped focus the society's laparoscopic hysterectomy training project.

DARS-NIC-83772-T4M1V.summary: NHS Calderdale CCG's agreement covers the use of pseudonymised hospital activity data (accident and emergency, admitted patient care and outpatient records) and local provider data for the Calderdale area. The data is for linking with GP data to group the local population by health need and resource use, and for modelling the combined effect of two service reconfiguration programmes on patient flows, bed numbers and travel times. The aim is to help prioritise and design new models of care closer to home.

DARS-NIC-84254-J2G1Q.summary: The University of York's Centre for Health Economics agreement covers the use of pseudonymised, record-level hospital, emergency care, mental health, death registration and patient-reported outcome data. The data is for studying NHS efficiency, provider performance, policy impacts and inequalities in access. The aim is to inform health and social care policy and the use of NHS funding. Published studies have already examined drivers of health care spending and inequalities in waiting times, and an online tool helps patients and GPs discuss surgery outcomes.

DARS-NIC-84763-L9X2G.summary: Leicester City Council's agreement covers its use of hospital and emergency care data (Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set) for public health work. The agreement allows the data to be analysed to understand local health needs and inequalities, and to support needs assessments, strategies and commissioning. The data is for identifying and responding to local health challenges, particularly for the most disadvantaged. Results have already fed into Joint Strategic Needs Assessments and neighbourhood profiles.

DARS-NIC-85465-H1W9F.summary: The University of Sheffield's agreement covers holding pseudonymised Improving Access to Psychological Therapies (IAPT) data on patients who received high intensity therapy. The data is for comparing how well Cognitive Behaviour Therapy, Counselling for Depression and other high intensity therapies treat depression. The aim is to help patients, practitioners and commissioners understand how the therapies compare. Early findings were presented at a Society for Psychotherapy Research conference in July 2022.

DARS-NIC-86054-Q4Y8W.summary: NHS North West London ICB, acting for the former NHS Brent CCG, is permitted to use Secondary User Services (SUS+) data for commissioners, identifiable by NHS number. The agreement allows the data to be used to check provider invoices are correct and the CCG's responsibility, and to run risk stratification, which links the data with GP records to score patients' risk. The main intended benefit is accurate payment of providers and better targeted care, helping reduce avoidable emergency admissions.

DARS-NIC-86183-K1Q2W.summary: Hackney Council's agreement covers Personal Demographics Service (PDS) data, which holds NHS Numbers and basic details such as name, address, date of birth, date of death and registered GP practice. The agreement allows the council to find or confirm the NHS Number of adults receiving social care and to record it on its case management system. The data is for helping social care and health staff coordinate care, including hospital discharge, and to identify the same person reliably.

DARS-NIC-86202-N8J7S.summary: Tameside Metropolitan Borough Council's adult social care service agreement covers basic personal details from the Personal Demographics Service (PDS): NHS Number, name, address, date of birth, date of death and registered GP practice. The agreement allows these details to confirm or find each client's NHS Number and record it on its case management system. This lets social care and health staff refer to the same person and coordinate care, including hospital discharge. The main intended benefit is better joined-up, safer care.

DARS-NIC-86244-P6Y1N.summary: NHS Nottingham and Nottinghamshire ICB's agreement allows it to use hospital activity data (SUS for Commissioners), identifiable by NHS number, for invoice validation and risk stratification. Invoice validation checks that providers are paid correctly for patients the commissioner is responsible for. Risk stratification links this data with GP data to identify patients at high risk, so care can be planned and targeted. The reported benefits so far include improved data quality, financial savings and identifying higher-risk patients to prioritise GP work.

DARS-NIC-86246-M3T5X.summary: NHS Nottingham and Nottinghamshire ICB's agreement allows it to use hospital activity data (SUS for Commissioners), identifiable by NHS number, for two purposes. The first is checking provider invoices so the right commissioner pays for each patient's care. The second is risk stratification, which links the data with GP data to identify patients at high risk of hospital admission so care can be planned and targeted. Reported benefits include improved data quality, financial savings and better prioritisation of GP and community care work.

DARS-NIC-86250-T2M6F.summary: NHS Nottingham and Nottinghamshire ICB (formerly Rushcliffe CCG)'s agreement allows it to use hospital activity data from Secondary User Services, identifiable by NHS number, to check provider invoices and to identify patients at high risk of hospital admission. The work is to be carried out by Nottinghamshire Health Informatics Service. The aim is to make sure payments are accurate and to help GPs and commissioners plan and target care. Reported benefits include improved data quality, financial savings and better identification of higher-risk patients.

DARS-NIC-86260-S0V2F.summary: NHS Nottingham and Nottinghamshire ICB (Mansfield and Ashfield area)'s agreement allows it to use Secondary User Services (SUS+) hospital activity data, identifiable by NHS number, for invoice validation and risk stratification. Invoice validation checks that providers' invoices are for patients the commissioner is responsible for. Risk stratification links the data with GP data to identify patients at high risk, so care can be planned and targeted. Reported benefits include improved data quality and financial savings.

DARS-NIC-86349-M3B9V.summary: NHS Nottingham and Nottinghamshire ICB's agreement allows it to use hospital activity data (SUS for Commissioners) to check provider invoices are valid and to identify patients at high risk of health deterioration. The aim is to make sure payments are accurate and to help GPs and commissioners target care, reduce avoidable admissions and plan services. Reported benefits so far include improved data quality, financial savings, and identifying higher-risk patients so GP practices and community teams can prioritise their work.

DARS-NIC-86409-C4S9S.summary: NHS Nottingham and Nottinghamshire ICB (Nottingham West area)'s agreement allows hospital activity data from Secondary Uses Service (SUS+), which is identifiable by NHS number, to be used to check provider invoices before payment and to identify patients at high risk of health deterioration by linking it with GP data. The main intended benefits are accurate payment for care and earlier, better targeted care for vulnerable patients.

DARS-NIC-86623-P4F4D.summary: The Nuffield Trust, an independent research organisation, has an agreement covering hospital records of accident and emergency visits, admitted patient care and outpatient appointments. The data is for evaluating the Royal Voluntary Service "Home from Hospital" scheme in Leicestershire by comparing hospital use by people who received the service with a matched group who did not. The aim is to give commissioners an independent assessment of whether such schemes affect older people's use of hospital services.

DARS-NIC-86666-V7Z1L.summary: University College London (UCL) is keeping hospital records (admissions and A&E attendances) and linked death registration data for a study of hospital discharge for homeless people in England. The study compares readmissions and deaths between homeless people who used specialist discharge services, those who did not, and non-homeless people in the most deprived areas. It aims to help commissioners and policy makers target services better and reduce readmissions and avoidable deaths. Analysis of the main outcomes has already enabled an economic analysis of the discharge schemes.
DARS-NIC-86666-V7Z1L.retense_draft: University College London's agreement covers holding hospital records (admissions and A&E attendances) and linked death registration data for a study of hospital discharge for homeless people in England. The study compares readmissions and deaths between homeless people who used specialist discharge services, those who did not, and non-homeless people in the most deprived areas. It aims to help commissioners and policy makers target services better and reduce readmissions and avoidable deaths. Analysis of the main outcomes has already enabled an economic analysis of the discharge schemes.

DARS-NIC-86861-K1L1N.summary: NHS South Yorkshire ICB, covering the former NHS Doncaster CCG area, is permitted under the agreement to use identifiable hospital activity data to check invoices from care providers, and pseudonymised health, social care and population datasets to support commissioning. The data is for validating payments, planning and redesigning services, assessing local health needs and identifying patients at risk. The stated aim is to ensure providers are paid accurately and services meet the population's needs. The CCG has published an annual report on its developments and achievements, supported by this data.

DARS-NIC-86954-Y0R2N.summary: University College London's agreement covers linked NHS England hospital, mortality, cancer registration and demographic data on members of the 1946 National Survey of Health and Development birth cohort. The data is for updating study records, re-contacting members lost to follow-up, and researching how factors across life affect ageing and diseases such as cardiovascular disease. The aim is to show when in life interventions might prevent disease. Published papers include one linking early childhood respiratory infection to premature adult death from respiratory disease.

DARS-NIC-87225-T1V3B.summary: London Borough of Lewisham, a local authority, is permitted to use hospital and emergency care records (Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set). The data is for its public health duties, including needs assessments, health strategies, the annual public health report and advice to NHS commissioners. The aim is locally focused analysis of health and inequalities. So far, the data has fed analyses of self-harm admissions, children's asthma admissions for an air quality briefing, and an alcohol harm dashboard.

DARS-NIC-88045-R0G8D.summary: Durham County Council's agreement covers the use of hospital and emergency care records (Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set) for its public health work. The data is for needs assessments, health strategies, the annual public health report and advice to NHS commissioners. The aim is locally focused analysis of health and inequalities. The data informed an updated Serious Violence Needs Assessment and supported work towards a new Dementia Strategy for County Durham.

DARS-NIC-88542-J1S6S.summary: NHS Dartford, Gravesham and Swanley CCG's agreement covers hospital activity data (SUS), local provider data and mental health, maternity and other national datasets, some identifiable by NHS number and some pseudonymised. The agreement allows the data to be used to validate invoices, identify high-risk patients through risk stratification, and support the commissioning of health services. The main intended benefit is better-planned services and earlier, more targeted care for patients.

DARS-NIC-88562-G4W4K.summary: NHS Medway CCG's agreement covers hospital, ambulance, community, mental health, maternity and other health service data, some identifiable by NHS number and some pseudonymised. The agreement allows the data to be used to check invoices, identify patients at high risk of needing care, and analyse local health services to support commissioning. The main intended benefit is better planning and quality of services, and more effective use of public money.

DARS-NIC-88562-J4W4K.summary: NHS Medway CCG's agreement covers hospital, mental health, community, primary care and other health service data, some identifiable by NHS number and some pseudonymised. The agreement allows the data to be used to validate invoices, identify patients at high risk of future service use, and analyse local care to support commissioning. The main intended benefit is more effective commissioning of services, leading to better patient experience.

DARS-NIC-88564-W3R5K.summary: NHS Swale CCG's agreement covers hospital, mental health, maternity, community and other local health service data, some identifiable by NHS number and some pseudonymised. The agreement allows the data to be used to validate invoices, identify patients at high risk for GPs through risk stratification, and support commissioning of health services for its local population. The main intended benefit is more effective commissioning, with better planning, quality and patient experience.

DARS-NIC-88623-F2H1Q.summary: The Royal College of Anaesthetists's agreement covers hospital admission, critical care and death registration records for patients who had inpatient surgery in the UK in one week in March 2017. The data is for studying how critical care admission after surgery relates to complications and longer-term outcomes, aiming to improve care for surgical patients. Work so far has been published as a PhD thesis and has influenced national policy on critical care provision and perioperative care services.

DARS-NIC-88740-G2Y9Q.summary: Worcestershire County Council's agreement covers hospital records for emergency care, admitted patients, critical care and outpatients. The agreement allows the data to support the council's public health duties, including needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, the annual public health report and advice to NHS commissioners. The aim is locally focused analysis of health outcomes and inequalities. The data helped the council target populations and work with the Integrated Care Board on inequalities and strategic plans.

DARS-NIC-88788-M6F3S.summary: NHS Surrey Heartlands ICB's agreement, acting for the former Guildford and Waverley CCG area, covers pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, maternity, cancer waiting times, births and deaths data. The agreement allows the data to be used to plan and monitor commissioned health services, assess local needs and identify patients at risk. Processing is carried out by NHS South, Central and West Commissioning Support Unit. The main intended benefit is better planning and quality of services for the local population.

DARS-NIC-88834-Y3L8B.summary: NHS North East Hampshire and Farnham CCG's agreement covers hospital activity data (the Secondary Uses Service), local provider flows and mental health, maternity, children's and diagnostic datasets. The data is for validating invoices, identifying patients at high risk through risk stratification, and supporting commissioning of health services. The main intended benefit is more effective commissioning, with better-targeted care and improved patient experience.

DARS-NIC-89613-L9D8C.summary: NHS South Yorkshire ICB, acting for the former Sheffield clinical commissioning group (CCG), has an agreement covering hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other health activity data, some identifiable by NHS number and some pseudonymised. The agreement allows the data to be used to check provider invoices, identify patients at high risk of poor health, and plan and commission services for the local population. The main intended benefit is accurate payment and better-targeted care. The register reports that the data has helped services match population needs and has supported monitoring of in-year projects.

DARS-NIC-90019-Q8P9K.summary: The Health Foundation, a charity, is permitted to use Hospital Episode Statistics data on hospital admissions, outpatient appointments and A&E attendances. The agreement allows it to analyse health inequality in NHS hospital services, A&E waiting times and maternity care by area, deprivation and ethnicity. The aim is to give policymakers and commissioners evidence to target areas for reducing inequality. So far, only preliminary results exist and none have been published.

DARS-NIC-90049-D5S8M.summary: NHS Greater Manchester ICB, acting for the former NHS Heywood, Middleton and Rochdale CCG, is covered by an agreement allowing it to hold hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other health and social care data, some identifiable by NHS number and some pseudonymised. The agreement allows the data to be used to check provider invoices, identify patients at high risk of poor health, and support planning and buying of health services. The main intended benefit is that providers are paid accurately and care is better targeted and commissioned.

DARS-NIC-90070-F3K4Z.summary: The Health Foundation's agreement covers the use of Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care data to study the Any Qualified Provider scheme, which lets patients choose between NHS and private providers. DARS-NIC-95909-K7G6V.summary: NHS City & Hackney CCG's agreement covers hospital, mental health, community and other health service data, some identifiable by NHS number and most pseudonymised. The agreement allows the data to be used to validate invoices, identify patients at high risk of needing services, and analyse health care provision to support commissioning. The stated aim is more effective commissioning of services, leading to a better patient experience.

DARS-NIC-96444-N2B7K.summary: The Intensive Care National Audit & Research Centre (ICNARC) agreement covers the use of NHS Digital's patient status and date of death information to support the 65 Trial. The trial tests whether keeping blood pressure lower while patients receive vasopressor drugs benefits critically ill people aged 65 or over. The data is for providing 90-day mortality and survival outcomes and avoiding contact with families of participants who have died. The trial results have been published in a medical journal and a national report, and the intervention has been included in guidelines.

DARS-NIC-96472-W0K5S.summary: The Royal College of Surgeons of England's agreement, which runs the National Prostate Cancer Audit, covers a Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) list cleaning report. It covers men in the audit's survey group in England who have not raised type 2 objections. The report is for checking for deaths and finding current addresses before a patient survey on outcomes after prostate cancer is posted. The aim is to avoid distressing bereaved families and to assess and improve the quality of prostate cancer care.

DARS-NIC-96550-Z8N7V.summary: Cornwall Council, a local authority, has an agreement covering Hospital Episode Statistics and Emergency Care Data Set records, covering hospital admissions, outpatients, critical care and A&E. The agreement allows the data to be used in its public health work, such as Joint Strategic Needs Assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, advice to NHS commissioners and the Director of Public Health's annual report. The data is for locally focused analysis of health and health inequalities. Between 2023 and 2026, the data were used in the statutory Joint Strategic Needs Assessment reporting.

DARS-NIC-97202-W2L3P.summary: Portsmouth City Council's agreement covers the use of hospital and emergency care records (Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set) for its public health work. The agreement allows the council to produce aggregated reports such as needs assessments, health strategies and advice to NHS commissioners, aiming to target local health needs and inequalities more effectively. Analysis of heart failure admissions informed discussions with NHS partners, and neighbourhood health profiles support local planning.

DARS-NIC-99077-Q0K6Z.summary: University College London (UCL) is using identifiable hospital admissions, death registration, demographic and mortality tracking data for 69 participants in the SABRE cohort study, who declined cancer record linkage. It is studying why heart, metabolic and cognitive health differ by ethnicity and sex in older age, to help shape prevention and treatment. Reported benefits include publications, and findings on diabetes in South Asian and African Caribbean people that informed NICE's BMI thresholds.

DARS-NIC-99094-L3H5G.summary: NHS Islington CCG's agreement covers pseudonymised data, where identifying details are removed, from hospital, ambulance, community, mental health, maternity and other NHS datasets. The data is for analysing the health needs of the local population and supporting commissioning (planning and buying) of health services, including service redesign and identifying patients at risk. The main intended benefit is more effective commissioning, leading to improved patient experience.

DARS-NIC-99319-F0R8C.summary: NHS City and Hackney Clinical Commissioning Group (CCG)'s agreement covers hospital, mental health, community, ambulance and other patient activity data, including some identifiable by NHS number. The data is for validating provider invoices, identifying patients at high risk so their care can be planned, and analysing services for commissioning. The stated aim is better planning, more effective commissioning and improved patient experience.

DARS-NIC-99675-X5S7X.summary: NHS South, Central and West Commissioning Support Unit's agreement allows it to use Hospital Episode Statistics covering accident and emergency, admitted patient care, critical care and outpatients. The agreement allows it to produce aggregated reports, with small numbers suppressed, that let NHS and local authority customers benchmark against similar organisations nationally. The aim is to improve patient pathways and make better use of resources. The unit's analysis identified savings opportunities for NEW Devon CCG and for Surrey Heath CCG's hip and knee pathways.
